Extensive mucosal involvement (40-60% of cases): xanthomatous papules and plaques infiltrating the upper aerodigestive tract (oral cavity, tongue, pharynx, epiglottis, larynx, vocal cords, trachea, bronchi), leading to progressive hoarseness, dysphonia, dysphagia, stridor, and potentially fatal upper airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy

Pituitary-hypothalamic axis involvement (~40% of cases): transient or permanent central diabetes insipidus resulting in polyuria and polydipsia, forming the classic Montgomery triad (flexural xanthomas, mucosal lesions, and diabetes insipidus)
Ocular involvement: xanthomatous infiltration of conjunctiva, cornea, sclera, and orbits causing visual impairment
Normal serum lipid and cholesterol profile (normolipemic xanthomatosis), distinguishing it from hyperlipidemic xanthomatosis
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Pituitary MRI (High-Resolution T1, T2, T1+C): Nodular thickening and avid, homogeneous gadolinium enhancement of the pituitary stalk (infundibulum) and hypothalamus; absence of the normal hyperintense 'bright spot' of the posterior pituitary on unenhanced T1-weighted images (hallmark of central diabetes insipidus); meningeal thickening and xanthomatous dural plaques

CT of Neck and Soft Tissues / Virtual Endoscopy: Extensive irregular nodular soft tissue mucosal thickening causing luminal narrowing of the glottis, subglottis, pyriform sinuses, and upper trachea without destruction of underlying laryngeal cartilage
Chest CT: Nodular xanthomatous deposits along tracheobronchial tree, pulmonary interstitial infiltrates, and subpleural micronodules
Orbital MRI / CT: Well-defined, non-calcified soft tissue masses within the epibulbar space, cornea, and retrobulbar orbit with variable T2 hypointensity and contrast enhancement

Skeletal Radiography / Whole-Body Low-Dose CT: Complete absence of osteolytic skeletal bone lesions, which is crucial for distinguishing xanthoma disseminatum from Langerhans cell histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester disease
pathology_manifestations: Non-Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis: Dense, sheets-like, nodular inflammatory infiltrate occupying the upper and mid dermis without extending into the epidermis (clear Grenz zone)

Cellular Composition: Predominance of large, lipid-laden foamy histiocytes (xanthoma cells) admixed with pathognomonic Touton-type multinucleated giant cells (characterized by a central wreath of nuclei surrounded by a rim of foamy, lipid-rich cytoplasm)
Admixed Infiltrate: Interspersed mature lymphocytes, plasma cells, neutrophils, and eosinophils; older lesions show progressive storiform interstitial fibrosis

Immunohistochemistry (IHC): Histiocytes are strongly positive for CD68, CD163, and Factor XIIIa; negative for CD1a and Langerin (CD207) (ruling out Langerhans cell histiocytosis); S100 protein is typically negative or only weakly and focally positive
Electron Microscopy: Absence of Birbeck granules (pentalaminar tennis-racket organelles), confirming non-Langerhans lineage
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive normolipemic non-Langerhans cell histiocytic dermatosis characterized by widespread flexural xanthomas and upper airway lesions, imaged on brain MRI by infundibular stalk thickening with loss of the posterior pituitary T1 bright spot, on neck CT by laryngeal/tracheal airway narrowing, and confirmed histologically by CD68+/CD1a- foamy histiocytes and Touton giant cells.

Dermatology.name: Mycosis Fungoides
clinical_manifestations: Patch stage: bathing-suit distribution of scaly, atrophic, wrinkled patches
Plaque and tumor stage: infiltrated arcuate plaques and ulcerated nodules
Poikiloderma and a wrinkled epidermis in long-standing patches
radiological_manifestations: CT or PET only when staging nodes or viscera; the diagnostic images are clinical and histologic
pathology_manifestations: Epidermotropic atypical CD4 lymphocytes, Pautrier microabscesses, and a band-like dermal infiltrate
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Cutaneous lymphoma whose stage photographs and skin biopsy are the image library, not a single rash type.

Dermatology.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Pearly rolled-border papule with telangiectasias on sun-exposed skin
Ulcerated rodent ulcer and the scar-like morpheaform plaque
Pigmented and superficial variants on dermoscopy
radiological_manifestations: Imaging is reserved for neglected perineural or orbital invasion and is not required for the usual gallery
pathology_manifestations: Basaloid tumor islands with peripheral palisading and retraction artifact
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: The most photographed cutaneous malignancy, with clinical, dermoscopic, and histologic images.

Dermatology.name: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma
synonyms: Marjolin ulcer when arising in a scar
clinical_manifestations: Hyperkeratotic, crateriform nodule on sun-damaged skin
Marjolin ulcer in a burn scar or chronic osteomyelitis sinus
Keratoacanthoma-like dome with a central keratin plug
radiological_manifestations: Regional nodal ultrasound or CT when a high-risk tumor is staged
pathology_manifestations: Invasive atypical keratinocytes, keratin pearls, and solar elastosis in the adjacent dermis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Keratinocyte cancer with ulcer and keratosis photographs plus a standard histologic image.

Dermatology.name: Darier Disease
clinical_manifestations: Greasy hyperkeratotic papules in seborrheic areas, coalescing into plaques
Nail dystrophy with red and white longitudinal bands and V-shaped nicks
Palmar pits and cobblestone oral papules
radiological_manifestations: No disease-specific radiology; nail and oral photographs carry the non-skin sites
pathology_manifestations: Acantholytic dyskeratosis with corps ronds and grains
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Genodermatosis identified by the seborrheic papules, pathognomonic nails, and acantholytic histology.

Dermatology.name: Hailey-Hailey Disease
clinical_manifestations: Macerated, fissured plaques in the neck, axillae, and groin with a soggy scale crust
Flare photographs after friction, heat, or secondary infection
radiological_manifestations: No radiology; intertriginous photographs and histology define the topic
pathology_manifestations: Dilapidated brick wall full-thickness acantholysis, distinguishing it from pemphigus vulgaris
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Inherited blistering disease with a recognizable intertriginous photograph and a named histologic pattern.

Dermatology.name: Lamellar Ichthyosis
clinical_manifestations: Collodion membrane in the newborn, then large plate-like brown scales
Ectropion and eclabium photographs
Palmoplantar keratoderma
radiological_manifestations: No diagnostic radiology; the neonatal and scale photographs are the gallery
pathology_manifestations: Compact orthohyperkeratosis without the epidermolytic change of epidermolytic ichthyosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Congenital ichthyosis with unmistakable neonatal and plate-scale photographs, distinct from epidermolytic ichthyosis already indexed.

Dermatology.name: Xeroderma Pigmentosum
clinical_manifestations: Lentigines and poikiloderma on sun-exposed skin of a child
Multiple basal and squamous cell carcinomas and melanoma on the face
Photophobia and conjunctival injection or ocular surface tumors
radiological_manifestations: Neuroimaging only in the De Sanctis-Cacchione neurologic subset
pathology_manifestations: Early keratinocyte atypia and the specific skin cancers that arise in the poikiloderma
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: DNA-repair genodermatosis whose childhood pigmentary photographs and skin cancers are the image set.

Dermatology.name: Cutaneous Mastocytosis
clinical_manifestations: Red-brown macules and papules on the trunk of a child
Darier sign: wheal and flare photographed after stroking a lesion
Mastocytoma: a solitary yellow-orange plaque that blisters when rubbed
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal survey or abdominal imaging only if systemic mastocytosis is being separated from the cutaneous disease
pathology_manifestations: Dermal mast-cell aggregates highlighted by tryptase and CD117
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Mast-cell skin disease with a photographable Darier sign, kept separate from systemic mastocytosis.

Dermatology.name: Lichen Planus
clinical_manifestations: Flat-topped violaceous polygonal papules with Wickham striae on the wrists and ankles
Lacy white buccal network
Nail pterygium and scarring alopecia in lichen planopilaris, filed as sites of the same disease rather than separate topics
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: Band-like lymphocytic interface dermatitis, sawtooth acanthosis, and cytoid bodies
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Interface dermatosis with skin, mouth, and nail photographs plus a standard biopsy image.

Dermatology.name: Vitiligo
clinical_manifestations: Depigmented macules with convex borders on the face, hands, and genitals
Wood lamp accentuation of chalk-white patches
Segmental vitiligo stopping at the midline
radiological_manifestations: No radiology; Wood lamp is the imaging adjunct
pathology_manifestations: Absent melanocytes on melan-A or Fontana stain, distinguishing vitiligo from post-inflammatory hypopigmentation
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Pigmentary disease whose clinical and Wood-lamp photographs are the library. It is a disease, not a manifestation of another indexed topic.

Dermatology.name: Lichen Sclerosus
clinical_manifestations: Ivory-white atrophic figure-of-eight plaques on the vulva or a sclerotic prepuce
Purpura, fissures, and architectural loss in chronic anogenital disease
Extragenital crinkled porcelain papules on the trunk
radiological_manifestations: No radiology unless urethral stricture is imaged in male disease
pathology_manifestations: Homogenized papillary dermal collagen, follicular plugging, and a lichenoid lymphocytic band
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Sclerotic dermatosis with characteristic anogenital photographs and histology.

Dermatology.name: Infantile Hemangioma
clinical_manifestations: Precursor pallor or telangiectatic patch, then a bright red lobulated plaque in infancy
Deep bluish subcutaneous component and later gray involution
Beard distribution and segmental facial lesions that prompt airway or PHACE evaluation, without making those complications separate topics
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound of a deep component; MRI when a segmental facial lesion is assessed for PHACE
pathology_manifestations: GLUT1-positive capillary lobules, distinguishing infantile hemangioma from vascular malformations
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Infantile vascular tumor with a predictable photographic life cycle and a confirming immunostain.

Dermatology.name: Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Blue rubbery compressible skin blebs, including palms and soles
Endoscopy: similar venous malformations that bleed
radiological_manifestations: No required radiology unless a deep lesion is mapped with MRI
pathology_manifestations: Venous malformations, unlike GLUT1-positive infantile hemangioma
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Venous malformation syndrome with skin and endoscopic photographs.

Dermatology.name: Acrodermatitis Enteropathica
clinical_manifestations: Erosive, scaly plaques around the mouth, anus, and acral sites in a weanling infant
Alopecia and diarrhea
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: Pale upper epidermis; low serum zinc and SLC39A4 confirm
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Zinc dermatosis with a periorificial photograph. Ordinary nutritional deficiency without this pattern stays out.

Dermatology.name: Pellagra
clinical_manifestations: Casal necklace and a photosensitive dermatitis on the hands and feet
Beefy red tongue
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: No specific biopsy; the distribution photograph is the diagnosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Niacin deficiency with a named photosensitive photograph. Included as a visual deficiency disease, not as generic malnutrition.

Dermatology.name: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: A rapidly growing red-violet nodule on sun-exposed skin of an older adult
radiological_manifestations: Regional nodal ultrasound or PET when staging
pathology_manifestations: Trabecular neuroendocrine tumor, CK20 perinuclear dot, Merkel-cell polyomavirus in most
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma with a nodule photograph and a CK20 immunostain.

Dermatology.name: Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
clinical_manifestations: Discoid plaques with follicular plugging, scarring, and pigment change
Polycyclic photosensitive plaques of subacute disease
Malar erythema of acute disease is a site of lupus, and systemic lupus remains the systemic topic
radiological_manifestations: No routine radiology
pathology_manifestations: Interface dermatitis, basement-membrane thickening, and a lupus band on immunofluorescence
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Skin-limited lupus phenotypes with scar and annular photographs. Systemic lupus stays the systemic topic; a malar rash alone is not a topic.

Dermatology.name: Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly spreading confluent salmon-colored or orange-red erythroderma displaying pathognomonic sharply demarcated islands of completely normal, uninvolved skin ("islands of sparing")

Follicular hyperkeratotic papules topped by central horny plugs distributed on the dorsal aspects of the fingers (proximal phalanges), hands, wrists, and elbows, imparting a coarse "nutmeg-grater" texture on palpation
Distinctive thick, waxy, orange-yellow palmoplantar keratoderma extending onto the lateral margins of the hands and feet ("PRP sandals" and "PRP gloves") with deep painful fissures
Facial erythema with thick branny scale, severe ectropion, conjunctival injection, and thick yellow-brown subungual hyperkeratosis with longitudinal nail splintering
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound: Diffuse hyperechoic thickening of the stratum corneum and epidermal acoustic shadow corresponding to hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis
Chest Radiography / CT: Utilized in atypical erythroderma workup to exclude underlying solid-organ malignancies or paraneoplastic triggers
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic Histology): Alternating orthokeratosis and parakeratosis oriented both vertically and horizontally across the stratum corneum, creating a characteristic "checkerboard pattern"

Folliculotropic features: Follicular infundibular plugging with shoulder parakeratosis surrounding hair follicular ostia; broad suprapapillary plates and thick hypergranulosis without significant epidermotropism
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal visual papulosquamous disease entity featuring unmistakable clinical images (orange-red erythroderma with islands of normal skin, nutmeg-grater dorsal finger papules, and waxy palmoplantar keratoderma) confirmed by checkerboard parakeratosis on histology.

Dermatology.name: Erythema Multiforme Major
clinical_manifestations: Abrupt onset of pathognomonic symmetric three-concentric-zone "target" or "iris" lesions: dark dusky purpuric or vesicular center, surrounding pale edematous intermediate zone, and an outer sharply defined erythematous halo
Acral and extensor predilection: initial appearance on the dorsa of hands, feet, palms, soles, forearms, and shins, spreading centripetally to limbs and trunk

Severe painful mucosal erosions involving at least one mucosal site (most commonly vermilion border of the lips and oral labial mucosa) with hemorrhagic lip crusting, shallow oral aphthoid erosions, and pseudomembrane formation

Ocular and genital mucosal involvement: bilateral non-purulent conjunctival injection, chemosis, and painful genital erosions (frequently triggered by recurrent Herpes simplex virus infection or Mycoplasma pneumoniae)
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / High-Resolution Chest CT: Indicated when triggered by Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection, demonstrating patchy reticular-nodular interstitial opacities or ground-glass bronchointerstitial infiltrates
Slit Lamp Biomicroscopy: Direct visualization of tarsal and bulbar conjunctival erosions, pseudomembranes, and punctate corneal epithelial erosions
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy: Prototypic cytotoxic cell-mediated interface dermatitis characterized by hydropic degenerating basal keratinocytes and necrotic apoptotic individual keratinocytes (Civatte bodies) throughout the stratum spinosum

Subepidermal separation: Dermal-epidermal detachment leading to subepidermal clefting with papillary dermal edema and dense perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate; direct immunofluorescence is negative for intercellular or basement membrane immune complexes
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield dermatologic disease defined by unmistakable physical clinical photographs of concentric three-zone target iris lesions on the palms and soles and bloody crusted lip erosions.

Dermatology.name: Epidermodysplasia Verruciformis
clinical_manifestations: Lifelong genetic vulnerability to beta-human papillomavirus (beta-HPV, especially types 5 and 8) presenting in early childhood with widespread, polymorphic verrucous and lichenoid cutaneous eruptions
Multiple flat, smooth-topped, flesh-colored, pink, or light-brown papules resembling flat warts (verruca plana) on the dorsa of hands, fingers, forehead, neck, and forearms
Large confluent reddish-brown, pink, or hypopigmented macules and plaques with fine scale resembling tinea versicolor (pityriasis versicolor-like lesions) on the trunk, abdomen, and limbs

Extremely high malignant transformation rate: 30-60% of patients develop multiple primary actinic keratoses, Bowenoid carcinoma in situ, and invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas (cutaneous SCC) starting in the third to fourth decade, strictly concentrated on sun-exposed head, neck, and hands
radiological_manifestations: Cutaneous High-Resolution Ultrasound: Measurement of tumor thickness, depth of invasion, and dermal penetration of transformation lesions into subcutaneous fat
Head and Neck CT / MRI: Staging of metastatic or deeply invasive squamous cell carcinomas, delineating cortical bone erosion of the calvarium or facial skeleton and cervical nodal metastasis
pathology_manifestations: Cutaneous Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic Cytopathic Effect): Marked epidermal acanthosis with swollen, enlarged keratinocytes in the granular and upper spinous layers possessing pathognomonic pale blue-gray or slate-colored cytoplasm and clear perinuclear halos

Nuclear alterations: Large, round, hyperchromatic or pyknotic nuclei with clumped chromatin; electron microscopy and in situ hybridization confirm intranuclear crystalline arrays of beta-HPV viral particles

Molecular Genetics: Inactivating biallelic mutations in EVER1 (TMC6) or EVER2 (TMC8) genes leading to impaired intracellular zinc homeostasis and selective inability of cutaneous keratinocytes to restrict beta-papillomaviruses
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic genodermatosis with indelible clinical photographs of extensive flat-wart plaques, pityriasis-like trunk macules, and hyperkeratotic cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas, verified by pathognomonic swollen blue-gray keratinocytes on biopsy.

Dermatology.name: Granuloma Faciale
clinical_manifestations: Solitary or multiple smooth, soft-to-firm, asymptomatic, well-circumscribed plaques, nodules, or macules measuring 1 to 5 cm, localized almost exclusively to the face (bridge of the nose, malar eminences, cheeks, and forehead)
Distinctive coloration ranging from reddish-brown to violaceous, purplish, or bronze, often with an oily or glistening sheen
Accentuated, prominent, gaping follicular orifices giving the surface an "orange-peel" (peau d'orange) appearance, studded with fine arborizing superficial telangiectasias
Absence of ulceration or epidermal atrophy; lesions run a chronic, persistent, relapsing course without spontaneous involution
radiological_manifestations: Facial Soft-Tissue MRI / Ultrasound: Well-demarcated dermal soft-tissue thickening confined strictly to the cutaneous compartment, without invasion into underlying facial musculature, cartilaginous nasal framework, or periosteum
Dermoscopy: Pinkish-red homogeneous background with prominent linear branching vessels and conspicuous white follicular circles surrounded by halo-like follicular sparing
pathology_manifestations: Skin Biopsy (Pathognomonic Grenz Zone): Unmistakable subepidermal "Grenz zone"—a distinct band of uninvolved, completely normal collagen in the upper papillary dermis separating the flattened epidermis from the dense inflammatory infiltrate beneath

Dense polymorphous dermal infiltrate: Massive infiltration of the mid and deep reticular dermis composed of an intimate mixture of abundant eosinophils, neutrophils with prominent leukocytoclasia (nuclear dust), lymphocytes, histiocytes, and plasma cells

Periadnexal sparing: The dense infiltrate completely surrounds but spares hair follicles and eccrine sweat ducts; vascular endothelial swelling with extravasated erythrocytes and hemosiderin deposition without true fibrinoid necrosis of blood vessel walls
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Visually classic facial dermatologic disease featuring soft violaceous plaques with accentuated follicular openings (peau d'orange) on the nose and cheeks, diagnosed by the pathognomonic subepidermal Grenz zone and eosinophil-rich infiltrate on biopsy.

Dermatology.name: Pityriasis Lichenoides et Varioliformis Acuta
clinical_manifestations: Abrupt, recurrent crops of polymorphic cutaneous lesions erupting in symmetric waves over the trunk, flexural extremities, and proximal limbs
Rapid morphological evolution of lesions: initial discrete erythematous macules and edematous papules evolving into central vesicles, hemorrhagic pustules, and dark necrotic crusted ulcers
Pathognomonic healing phase: lesions resolve leaving depressed, varioliform ("chickenpox-like") pitted atrophic scars accompanied by post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation

Constitutional symptoms: low-grade fever, malaise, burning or pruritus; severe cases can progress to febrile ulceronecrotic Mucha-Habermann disease (FUMHD) with confluent necrotizing ulcers and septic-like systemic collapse
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Skin Ultrasound: Acoustic demarcation of epidermal necrosis, intraepidermal fluid collections, and dermal edema beneath active necrotic eschars
Abdominal / Chest CT (in severe FUMHD variant): Evaluation of hepatosplenomegaly, interstitial pneumonitis, and systemic lymphadenopathy
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic Wedge-Shaped Infiltrate): Dense, wedge-shaped (V-shaped) perivascular and interstitial lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis with the base at the dermal-epidermal junction and apex in the deep reticular dermis
Epidermal Necrosis & Interface Changes: Extensive vacuolar interface alteration with prominent confluent keratinocyte necrosis, dyskeratosis, and ballooning degeneration

Vascular and RBC findings: Extensive extravasation of red blood cells throughout the dermis and extending up into the necrotic stratum corneum; CD8+ T-cell predominant clonal infiltrate with endothelial swelling without true necrotizing vasculitis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield distinct clinical disease with unmistakable polymorphic photographs (crops of papulonecrotic lesions, black hemorrhagic crusts, and varioliform pox-like scars) and pathognomonic wedge-shaped lymphocytic histology.

Dermatology.name: Keratoacanthoma
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly growing, solitary, symmetric, dome-shaped cutaneous nodule appearing on sun-exposed skin (face, nose, cheeks, dorsum of hands, and forearms) in middle-aged and elderly individuals

Pathognomonic crateriform "volcano-like" silhouette: elevated, smooth, firm, flesh-colored to erythematous rolled border surrounding a prominent central crater packed with a hard, dark-brown or yellow, hyperkeratotic horn plug

Distinct triphasic biological progression: rapid growth phase over 4 to 8 weeks, static plateau phase lasting 2 to 8 weeks, followed in classic cases by spontaneous involution over 6 months leaving a depressed puckered scar (or persistent aggressive malignant behavior)
Clinical differentiation from nodular BCC/SCC: explosive growth velocity (growing from a tiny macule to 1-2.5 cm within weeks) and absence of central bleeding or ulcerated floor
radiological_manifestations: Dermoscopy: Central amorphous yellowish-white or brownish keratin mass surrounded by a peripheral white collar and radial, linear-irregular "hairpin" or "crown" vessels
High-Resolution Cutaneous Ultrasound: Well-circumscribed hypoechoic dermal nodule with a central hyperreflective crateriform cone corresponding to the dense keratin plug
Soft-Tissue MRI: Used for large or giant keratoacanthomas of the central face (nose, lip) to exclude infiltration of facial cartilage or deep muscle compartments
pathology_manifestations: Excisional Biopsy Silhouette (Low-Power Hallmark): Exo-endophytic, symmetric, cup-shaped or crateriform architectural configuration filled with an enormous plug of lamellar parakeratotic and orthokeratotic keratin
Epidermal 'Lip' / Shoulder: Lateral margins of normal epidermis form a distinctive overhanging "lip" or "collar" capping the peripheral borders of the crater

Cytology: Proliferating islands and sheets of highly differentiated squamous epithelium composed of voluminous, glassy, eosinophilic keratinocytes with minimal nuclear pleomorphism, sharp borders, and prominent neutrophil-containing intraepithelial microabscesses
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal visual cutaneous neoplasm featuring a pathognomonic volcano-shaped clinical photograph (central hyperkeratotic keratin horn plug and rolled border) and a classic cup-shaped low-power histological silhouette.

Dermatology.name: Pemphigus Foliaceus
clinical_manifestations: Superficial autoimmune blistering disease characterized by extremely fragile, superficial, flaccid bullae that rupture almost immediately upon formation, rarely seen intact by examiners
Striking clinical picture of widespread, shallow, erythematous erosions covered by greasy, scaly, cornflake-like adherent crusts ("cornflake sign")

Predilection for seborrheic anatomical zones: initial appearance on the face (often in a malar "butterfly" distribution), scalp, upper chest, and interscapular back, progressing to generalized exfoliative erythroderma
Positive Nikolsky sign: gentle lateral shearing friction on perilesional normal skin induces instant superficial epidermal detachment

Strict absence of mucosal lesions: oral cavity, pharynx, and genital mucosal membranes are completely spared (unlike Pemphigus vulgaris), reflecting tissue distribution of desmoglein 1 versus desmoglein 3
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound: Subcorneal micro-cleavages and intraepidermal acoustic disorganization confined to the superficial upper third of the epidermis, contrasting with deep suprabasal detachment in pemphigus vulgaris
Dermoscopy: Yellowish greasy scales, circular white scaling collarettes, and linear-irregular vessels on an erythematous base
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic Clefting Level): Subcorneal or intragranular acantholysis resulting in a cleft situated immediately beneath the stratum corneum or within the granular cell layer; individual detached rounded acantholytic keratinocytes float within the subcorneal space

Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF - Diagnostic Standard): Deposition of IgG (specifically IgG4 subclass) and complement C3 in an intercellular, honeycomb, or "chicken-wire" net pattern restricted strictly to the upper superficial spinous and granular layers of the epidermis
Serology (ELISA): High circulating titers of autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 (anti-Dsg1 IgG), with negative anti-desmoglein 3 (anti-Dsg3) titers
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic autoimmune bullous disease presenting with unique physical examination images (greasy cornflake-like crusts on seborrheic areas with complete mucosal sparing) and pathognomonic subcorneal acantholysis on DIF.

Dermatology.name: Erythema Annulare Centrifugum
clinical_manifestations: Prototypic reactive figurate erythema presenting with slowly expanding annular, arcuate, polycyclic, or circinate erythematous plaques that advance outward at 2 to 5 mm per day with central clearing
Pathognomonic "trailing scale" (in the superficial form): a fine, delicate collarette of scale situated along the inner margin of the advancing indurated erythematous border, behind the leading edge
Deep variant presentation: firm, non-scaly, cord-like elevated erythematous border with a smooth surface and central hyperpigmentation or clearing
Predilection for the trunk, buttocks, hips, and thighs, typically sparing the face, palms, and soles; lesions can coalesce into vast intricate polycyclic, festooned, or "wood-grain" patterns
Chronic relapsing course triggered by dermatophyte infections (tinea pedis), candidiasis, arthropod bites, medications, or occult hematologic/solid malignancies
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / Abdominal Ultrasound: Used as part of the systemic clinical workup to exclude occult pulmonary infections, sarcoidosis, or intra-abdominal neoplasms in refractory elderly presentations
Dermoscopy: Delicate inner collarette of white scale clinging to the internal border of the erythematous ring with dotted or linear irregular vessels
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic "Coat-Sleeve" Pattern): Tight, dense, sharply demarcated lymphohistiocytic infiltrate concentrated around blood vessels in the upper and middle dermis, producing a classic "coat-sleeve" perivascular cuffing appearance
Epidermal alterations (Superficial Form): Focal spongiosis, parakeratosis coinciding with the trailing scale, and mild basilar vacuolization without significant individual necrotic keratinocytes
Absence of true vasculitis: Vascular lumens remain patent, and there is an absence of fibrinoid necrosis, leukocytoclasia, or vascular thrombosis
Dermatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic figurate dermatologic disease displaying unmistakable clinical photographs (expanding polycyclic rings with a pathognomonic trailing scale) and distinctive 'coat-sleeve' perivascular lymphocytic cuffs on histology.

Endocrinology.name: Acromegaly
clinical_manifestations: Acral overgrowth: progressive enlargement of hands and feet (tightening of rings and shoes), broad 'spade-like' hands with blunt fingers
Coarsening of facial features: prominent frontal bossing, severe prognathism (macrognathia with underbite and dental diastema / widened interdental spaces)
Macroglossia with scalloped borders and deep voice
Hyperhidrosis, oily skin, and skin tags (molluscum fibrosum)
Carpal tunnel syndrome and proximal myopathy
radiological_manifestations: Sella Turcica / Pituitary MRI: Pituitary adenoma (macroadenoma >10 mm or microadenoma), suprasellar extension compressing the optic chiasm, invasion of cavernous sinuses
Hand Radiographs: Prominent arrow-like or tufted bony exostoses ('spade-like phalanges'), widening of the joint spaces due to articular cartilage hypertrophy, thickening of soft tissues
Foot Radiographs: Pathognomonic heel-pad thickness (>25 mm on lateral X-ray)
Skull Radiographs: Enlargement of the sella turcica, hyperostosis frontalis, marked enlargement of frontal and paranasal sinuses, prognathism
pathology_manifestations: Transsphenoidal pituitary resection: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET) composed of sheets or cords of acidophilic or chromophobic adenoma cells; strong immunohistochemical cytoplasmic positivity for Growth Hormone (GH); PIT-1 lineage transcription factor expression
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Classic endocrine condition with unmistakable physical appearance (spade-like hands, prognathism, macroglossia) paired with pituitary macroadenoma on MRI and heel-pad thickening >25 mm on X-ray.

Endocrinology.name: Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1 (APECED)
clinical_manifestations: Diagnostic Whittaker Triad: Presence of at least two of the three classic components (or one if an affected sibling): (1) Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC), (2) Primary hypoparathyroidism, and (3) Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease)

Chronic Mucocutaneous Candidiasis (CMC): Earliest manifestation typically presenting before age 5; persistent, recurrent Candida albicans infection manifesting as thick hyperkeratotic, dystrophic nail plates (onychomycosis with subungual crumbling), chronic pseudomembranous oral thrush, angular cheilitis, and painful esophageal or genital candidiasis refractory to topical antifungals

Hypocalcemic Neuromuscular Tetany: Symptomatic hypoparathyroidism presenting with paresthesias of the perioral region and fingertips, painful muscle cramps, carpopedal spasm (Trousseau sign elicited upon sphygmomanometer cuff inflation), facial nerve irritability (Chvostek sign on periauricular percussion), laryngeal stridor, and generalized hypocalcemic seizures

Addisonian Cutaneous and Mucosal Hyperpigmentation: Diffuse bronze-brown cutaneous hyperpigmentation accentuating sun-exposed areas, friction zones (elbows, knees, knuckles), palmar creases, and blue-gray macules along the buccal mucosa, driven by proopiomelanocortin (POMC) peptides secondary to lack of cortisol negative feedback; accompanied by hypotension and salt-craving

Ectodermal Dystrophic Features: Pitted enamel hypoplasia with transverse ridges and microdontia; chronic keratoconjunctivitis with photophobia and corneal scarring; patchy or universal alopecia (alopecia areata/universalis); and depigmented patches of vitiligo
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Head CT: Striking, dense, bilateral symmetric calcifications within the basal ganglia (globus pallidus, putamen, and caudate nuclei), thalami, centrum semiovale, and cerebellar dentate nuclei (Fahr syndrome pattern), resulting from chronic profound hypocalcemia and elevated calcium-phosphate product in untreated hypoparathyroidism

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Bilateral, symmetrical, marked adrenal gland atrophy with extreme thinning of the medial and lateral limbs (<2 mm), preservation of smooth adreniform shape, and complete absence of nodular masses or adrenal calcifications (distinguishing autoimmune adrenalitis from tuberculosis or histoplasmosis)

Plain Skeletal Radiography: Diffuse, marked increase in bone mineral density (osteosclerosis) with cortical thickening, prominent metaphyseal sclerotic bands in growing long bones, and dental panoramic radiographs showing blunted, shortened dental roots and deficient enamel caps

Renal Ultrasound: Medullary nephrocalcinosis and recurrent nephrolithiasis appearing as bilateral hyperechoic renal pyramids with posterior acoustic shadowing, frequently precipitated by vitamin D and calcium replacement therapy
pathology_manifestations: Organ-Specific Endocrine Histopathology: Massive autoimmune lymphocytic infiltration (predominantly CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes and plasma cells) of the adrenal cortex and parathyroid glands, leading to follicular/parenchymal cell apoptosis, destruction of steroidogenic cortical zones, and progressive dense fibrocollagenous replacement atrophy

Molecular Genetics and Serology: Monogenic autosomal recessive loss-of-function mutations in the AIRE (Autoimmune Regulator) gene located on chromosome 21q22.3, impairing medullary thymic epithelial expression of peripheral tissue antigens and disrupting central immune tolerance; presence of pathognomonic, high-titer neutralising autoantibodies against Type I interferons (interferon-omega and interferon-alpha) present in >95% of patients, alongside antibodies against 21-hydroxylase, 17-alpha-hydroxylase, side-chain cleavage enzyme (CYP11A1), and NALP5
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Classic monogenic autoimmune endocrine triad of refractory mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroid tetany, and Addisonian bronze skin, matched with dense basal ganglia Fahr calcifications on head CT and AIRE gene mutations.

Endocrinology.name: Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 2 (Schmidt Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Syndromic Pairing: Mandatory presence of autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) combined with autoimmune thyroid disease (Hashimoto's thyroiditis in 70% or Graves' disease in 30%) and/or Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus; adult onset typically in the third or fourth decade with strong female preponderance (3:1)

Addisonian Cutaneous and Mucosal Hyperpigmentation: Generalized bronze-brown skin hyperpigmentation, intensely pronounced in sun-exposed zones, palmar creases, pressure points (elbows, knees, knuckles), areolae, perineum, and fresh scars, accompanied by slate-grey or bluish-black longitudinal melanotic streaks and macules along the buccal mucosa, tongue, and gingival margins

High-Contrast Coexisting Autoimmune Vitiligo: Sharply demarcated, milky-white chalky depigmented cutaneous macules and patches (most frequently periocular, perioral, hand, and genital) providing a dramatic, high-contrast visual juxtaposition directly against the surrounding generalized Addisonian bronze skin

Thyroid and Pancreatic Stigmata: Palpable firm, rubbery, lobulated Hashimoto's goiter or exophthalmic Graves' ocular signs, accompanied by acute ketoacidotic or polyuric symptoms of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus

Associated Autoimmune Manifestations: Patchy alopecia areata, premature ovarian insufficiency with secondary amenorrhea, autoimmune atrophic gastritis with pernicious anemia (pallor, atrophic smooth red tongue), and celiac disease
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Bilateral, marked, symmetrical adrenal gland atrophy with severe reduction in adrenal limb thickness (<2 mm), preservation of smooth adreniform shape, and total absence of nodular expansion or calcifications (critically excluding granulomatous/tuberculous adrenalitis)

High-Resolution Thyroid Ultrasound: Diffusely heterogeneous, markedly hypoechoic thyroid parenchyma with micronodular 'pseudonodular' architecture, thick hyperechoic fibrous septa traversing the parenchyma ('giraffe-skin' appearance), and variable vascularity characteristic of chronic autoimmune thyroiditis

Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) / Skeletal X-Ray: Generalized reduction in bone mineral density (osteopenia/osteoporosis) resulting from chronic glucocorticoid replacement, hypogonadism, or unrecognized celiac-induced calcium malabsorption
pathology_manifestations: Adrenal Gland Histopathology: Severe autoimmune lymphocytic adrenalitis characterized by dense infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes, plasma cells, and histiocytes causing progressive destruction and disappearance of cells across the zona glomerulosa, fasciculata, and reticularis; sparing of the central chromaffin adrenal medulla; and dense capsular and parenchymal fibrous replacement

Thyroid and Pancreatic Histopathology: Thyroid tissue reveals extensive lymphocytic infiltration with lymphoid germinal centers, destruction of thyroid follicles, and oxyphilic metaplasia (Hürthle / Askanazy cells); pancreatic histology shows autoimmune insulitis with selective T-cell mediated destruction of insulin-producing beta cells within the islets of Langerhans

Serologic and Immunogenetic Profile: Polygenic HLA-DR3/DR4-DQ2/DQ8 haplotype association; circulating high-titer autoantibodies against steroidogenic 21-hydroxylase (CYP21A2), thyroid peroxidase (TPO), thyroglobulin (Tg), glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD65), and IA-2
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Classic polygenic autoimmune syndrome manifesting as a high-contrast visual pairing of chalky-white vitiligo against bronze Addisonian hyperpigmentation, verified by bilateral adrenal atrophy on CT and 21-hydroxylase antibodies.

Endocrinology.name: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia
Endocrinology.subspecialty: Pediatric Endocrinology & Inborn Errors of Steroidogenesis
clinical_manifestations: 46,XX Neonatal Females: Severe ambiguous genitalia (female pseudohermaphroditism) present at birth: clitoromegaly (phallus-like enlargement), complete or partial labial fusion with scrotalization, and single urogenital sinus opening (Prader stages 1-5); internal female reproductive organs (uterus, tubes, ovaries) are normal
46,XY Neonatal Males: Normal or slightly enlarged phallus, hyperpigmentation of the scrotum, with subtle presentation leading to delayed recognition
Cutaneous Hyperpigmentation: Striking bronze pigmentation of the nipples, areolae, genitalia, and skin creases due to uninhibited ACTH/alpha-MSH hypersecretion
Adrenal Salt-Wasting Crisis (Days 7-21 of life): Life-threatening shock, severe dehydration, projectile vomiting, profound hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis

Post-infancy: Precocious pseudopuberty (axillary and pubic hair, adult body odor, muscular build), rapid early somatic growth velocity but premature epiphyseal fusion resulting in severe adult short stature
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Adrenal Ultrasound and CT: Bilateral marked symmetrical adrenomegaly with pathognomonic 'cerebroid' (brain-like undulating gyral) folded surface pattern; preservation of normal adrenal triangular/crescent shape

Pelvic Ultrasound and MRI: Confirms presence of normal female pelvic internal organs (anteverted uterus, normal ovaries) and identifies the level of urogenital sinus confluence; confirms absence of male testicular tissue in labia
Bone Age Plain Radiography: Significant advance in skeletal maturation (bone age >> chronological age) with premature fusion of epiphyseal plates
pathology_manifestations: Adrenal Cortex Histopathology: Marked diffuse cortical hyperplasia, predominantly involving the zona fasciculata and zona reticularis, which are expanded by lipid-depleted, compact, eosinophilic cells with round uniform nuclei; medullary tissue is compressed but morphologically normal; testicular adrenal rest tumors (TART) composed of sheets of polygonal steroid-producing cells resembling Leydig cells

Biochemical and Molecular Genetics: Autosomal recessive CYP21A2 gene deletions or mutations causing enzymatic blockade, accumulation of serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP), and deficient cortisol and aldosterone synthesis
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Classic pediatric endocrine emergency featuring neonatal ambiguous genitalia and cutaneous hyperpigmentation, matched with cerebroid adrenomegaly on US and advanced bone age.

Endocrinology.name: Craniopharyngioma
clinical_manifestations: Bimodal age distribution: Peak 1 in childhood (5-14 years); Peak 2 in older adults (50-75 years)

Endocrine Deficiencies (Anterior & Posterior Hypopituitarism): Growth failure and severe short stature in children (Growth Hormone deficiency); delayed puberty; secondary adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism; central diabetes insipidus (polyuria, polydipsia, hypernatremia) due to pituitary stalk compression
Neuro-Ophthalmic Manifestations: Progressive visual field loss (classic bitemporal hemianopsia from chiasmal compression), optic disc atrophy, or papilledema
Raised Intracranial Pressure: Morning headaches, projectile vomiting, and obstructive hydrocephalus
radiological_manifestations: Sella and Brain Contrast MRI: Heterogeneous solid and multicystic sellar/suprasellar mass with vivid enhancement of solid components and cyst capsules; cystic components contain high protein, cholesterol crystals, and methemoglobin, creating pathognomonic high signal intensity on T1-weighted images ('machinery oil' fluid) and high signal on T2; upward displacement of the optic chiasm and compression of the third ventricle
Non-Contrast Brain CT: Pathognomonic dense, clumpy, nodular, or rim calcification in >90% of adamantinomatous variants (rare in papillary variant)
pathology_manifestations: Adamantinomatous Craniopharyngioma Histopathology: Reticular and anastomosing sheets of stratified squamous epithelium with peripheral nuclear palisading; stellate reticulum (loose spongy meshwork); pathognomonic 'Wet Keratin' (compact, rounded nodular masses of anucleate squames); cystic cavities filled with dark 'machinery oil' fluid teeming with birefringent cholesterol crystals; nuclear accumulation of beta-catenin driven by somatic CTNNB1 mutations
Papillary Craniopharyngioma (Adults): Well-differentiated non-keratinizing squamous papillomas without wet keratin or calcification, harboring BRAF V600E mutations
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal sellar-suprasellar tumor displaying bitemporal hemianopsia, growth failure, pathognomonic CT calcifications, T1-hyperintense 'machinery oil' cysts, and wet keratin histology.

Endocrinology.name: Cushing's Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: 'Moon facies': rounded, plethoric, facial fullness with telangiectasias
Centripetal obesity with supraclavicular fat pads and dorsocervical fat pad ('buffalo hump')
Wide (>1 cm), prominent, violaceous or purple abdominal striae (flanks, thighs, breasts)
Severe cutaneous fragility, easy bruising, ecchymoses following minimal pressure, and paper-thin skin
Proximal muscle wasting (thin limbs contrasting with obese trunk)
radiological_manifestations: Adrenal CT / MRI: Bilateral adrenal cortical hyperplasia in ACTH-dependent Cushing's; unilateral adrenal cortical adenoma or large heterogeneous adrenal carcinoma in primary adrenal Cushing's
Pituitary MRI with Dynamic Contrast: ACTH-secreting microadenoma (<10 mm) in Cushing disease (hypoenhancing lesion on early dynamic T1)
Thoracic/Lumbar Spine Radiographs and DXA: Severe osteopenia, multiple asymptomatic vertebral compression fractures with biconcave codfish vertebrae
pathology_manifestations: Adrenal resection: In adenoma: well-circumscribed golden-yellow cortical tumor composed of lipid-rich clear cells and compact eosinophilic cells; in Cushing disease: Crooke's hyaline change within normal non-neoplastic pituitary corticotrope cells (accumulation of cytokeratin filaments due to high circulating cortisol)
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Textbook physical phenotype (moon facies, buffalo hump, wide violaceous striae) coupled with adrenal CT adenoma/hyperplasia, dynamic pituitary MRI, and osteoporotic vertebral collapse.

Endocrinology.name: Gastrinoma (Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome)
Endocrinology.subspecialty: Gastrointestinal Neuroendocrine Tumors & Acid Peptic Syndromes
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Refractory Peptic Ulcer Disease: Severe, recurrent, debilitating peptic ulcerations refractory to standard proton-pump inhibitor therapy, characteristically found in atypical anatomic sites—the post-bulbar duodenum (second and third portions) or proximal jejunum—predisposing to recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding, hematemesis, melena, and visceral perforation
Stomal and Anastomotic Ulceration: Rapid, aggressive, recurring ulceration at surgical gastrojejunal anastomotic sites following previous ulcer surgery or vagotomy

Profuse Watery Secretory Diarrhea and Steatorrhea: High-volume watery diarrhea (often >2–3 liters/day) that improves or completely resolves upon high-dose PPI or gastric acid aspiration; accompanied by foul-smelling steatorrhea caused by massive hydrochloric acid secretion (basal acid output >15 mEq/h) overwhelming duodenal bicarbonate, lowering intestinal pH below 4.5, and irreversibly inactivating pancreatic lipase

Endoscopic Photography Signs: Striking, massive hypertrophy and tortuosity of gastric mucosal rugal folds ('giant gastric folds' resembling cerebral gyri) in the fundus and corpus, accompanied by extensive erosive duodenitis, mucosal cobblestoning, and active distal ulcerations

Associated MEN1 Stigmata: In 25% of cases occurring in the context of MEN1, coexisting signs of primary hyperparathyroidism (nephrolithiasis, hypercalcemia) and pituitary adenomas (visual disturbance, galactorrhea)
radiological_manifestations: Upper Gastrointestinal Barium Examination: Massive enlargement and tortuosity of gastric rugal folds; multiple post-bulbar duodenal and proximal jejunal ulcer craters; marked thickening and edema of duodenal mucosal folds; and dilution of barium contrast by massive volumes of hypersecreted acidic fluid ('dilution sign')

68Ga-DOTATATE / 68Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT: Premier imaging technique with exceptional sensitivity (>90%) demonstrating intense, focal somatostatin receptor-avid radiotracer uptake within the 'Gastrinoma Triangle' (Passaro's triangle: superiorly cystic/common bile duct junction, inferiorly junction of second and third duodenum, medially neck and body of pancreas), detecting tiny occult primary submucosal duodenal and peripancreatic tumors (<5–10 mm)

High-Resolution Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS): Exquisite visualization of tiny, submucosal hypoechoic duodenal wall nodules and periduodenal/peripancreatic lymph node metastases with real-time EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration

Dynamic Multiphasic Pancreas CT / Contrast MRI: Visualizes hypervascular, intensely arterial-enhancing duodenal or pancreatic head tumors with persistent contrast enhancement, alongside evaluation of liver metastases with characteristic arterial ring-enhancement
pathology_manifestations: Gastric Mucosa Histopathology: Striking parietal cell hyperplasia and hypertrophy causing profound expansion of the oxyntic mucosal thickness (2–3 times normal depth); accompanied by diffuse, linear, and micronodular enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cell hyperplasia within fundic glands driven by chronic severe hypergastrinemia, with risk of ECL neuroendocrine dysplasia

Gastrinoma Tumor Histopathology: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasm (NET G1 or G2) displaying solid nests, trabeculae, ribbons, or pseudo-acini of uniform, monomorphic polygonal cells with central round nuclei exhibiting classic finely stippled 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin and pale eosinophilic cytoplasm

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for synaptophysin and chromogranin A, with specific intense positivity for gastrin; high membrane expression of somatostatin receptor subtype 2A (SSTR2A)
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Severe neuroendocrine acid-hypersecretory syndrome featuring atypical post-bulbar peptic ulcers, giant gastric rugal hypertrophy, and tiny hypervascular duodenal/pancreatic gastrinomas localized by 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.

Endocrinology.name: Glucagonoma Syndrome (Necrolytic Migratory Erythema)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Cutaneous Eruption (Necrolytic Migratory Erythema - NME): Intensely pruritic, painful, migratory, cyclic erythematous patches and papules that rapidly develop flaccid vesicles and bullae, undergoing superficial epidermal necrosis, central erosion, and crusting with centrifugal spread, leaving behind scarred, bronze-brown hyperpigmented patches; lesions cycle dynamically over 1 to 2 weeks

Characteristic Anatomic Distribution of NME: Marked predilection for regions of mechanical friction, pressure, and intertriginous skin—specifically the perineum, perianal region, groin, buttocks, inner thighs, lower abdomen, ankles, and perioral skin (sparing trunk)

Prominent Mucosal Lesions: Bright red, painful, atrophic, depapillated 'beefy red' glossitis; severe angular cheilitis with painful rhagades at oral commissures; stomatitis; and brittle, dystrophic, ridged fingernails

Systemic Wasting and Cachexia: Severe, unprovoked weight loss and generalized skeletal muscle wasting despite normal or increased appetite; new-onset mild, non-ketotic diabetes mellitus or glucose intolerance; and frequent normochromic normocytic anemia

Thromboembolic Diathesis and Neuropsychiatric Signs: Markedly elevated incidence of unprovoked deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) secondary to tumor-induced hypercoagulability; accompanied by depression, insomnia, and proximal muscle weakness
radiological_manifestations: Multiphasic Pancreatic Protocol CT: Large (typically >3–6 cm at clinical presentation), well-demarcated, solitary hypervascular neuroendocrine tumor located in the body or tail of the pancreas, showing avid, intense, heterogeneous contrast enhancement during the late arterial/pancreatic parenchymal phase with rapid washout on portal venous phases

68Ga-DOTATATE / 68Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT: Exceptional diagnostic sensitivity showing intense, avid, focal somatostatin receptor (SSTR) radiotracer uptake (SUVmax typically >25–50) in the primary pancreatic tail mass and identifying occult regional lymph node or hepatic metastases

Abdominal MRI (with Dynamic Gadolinium): Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor demonstrating hypointensity on T1-weighted images, marked hyperintensity on T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) with restricted diffusion; depicts multiple hyperenhancing hypervascular liver metastases with ring-like peripheral enhancement
Venous Doppler Ultrasound / CT Pulmonary Angiography: Confirms lower extremity deep vein thrombosis and segmental/lobar pulmonary emboli stemming from paraneoplastic prothrombotic state
pathology_manifestations: Skin Lesion Punch Biopsy (Advancing Edge of NME): Pathognomonic superficial necrolysis—pale, vacuolated, ballooning degeneration of keratinocytes in the upper spinous layer (stratum spinosum) with intercellular edema, abrupt full-thickness necrosis of the upper epidermis, intraepidermal clefting, and subcorneal pustules, while the basal cell layer remains viable and intact

Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor Histology: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasm (PanNET G1 or G2) displaying solid nests, trabecular ribbons, or insular arrangements of monomorphic polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic or amphophilic cytoplasm and central round nuclei featuring classic stippled 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for neuroendocrine markers chromogranin A and synaptophysin, and intense specific immunoreactivity for glucagon; typically low Ki-67 proliferative index (<5–10%) in well-differentiated tumors
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Definitive paraneoplastic endocrine syndrome featuring pathognomonic necrolytic migratory erythema (NME), beefy glossitis, and a solitary hypervascular pancreatic tail neuroendocrine tumor on multiphasic CT and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.

Endocrinology.name: Graves' Disease (Thyroid Eye Disease & Dermopathy)
clinical_manifestations: Graves' orbitopathy / ophthalmopathy: bilateral or asymmetric proptosis (exophthalmos), lid retraction (Dalrymple sign), lid lag on downward gaze (von Graefe sign), chemosis, conjunctival injection, periorbital edema
Pretibial myxedema (thyroid dermopathy): non-pitting, indurated, violaceous, orange-peel ('peau d'orange') plaques and nodules over the anterior lower shins
Thyroid acropachy: digital clubbing, soft-tissue swelling of hands and feet, periosteal new bone formation
Diffuse, symmetrical, smooth, vascular thyroid enlargement with audible systolic bruit
radiological_manifestations: Orbital CT / MRI: Pathognomonic spindle-shaped enlargement of extraocular muscle bellies (inferior rectus, medial rectus, superior rectus, lateral rectus: 'I'M SLOw') with characteristic sparing of the anterior tendinous insertions; increased retro-orbital fat volume; optic nerve compression at the orbital apex
Thyroid Doppler Ultrasound: Diffuse thyroid enlargement, heterogeneous hypoechogenicity, and pathognomonic marked hypervascularity on color Doppler ('thyroid inferno')
Hand Radiographs (Thyroid Acropachy): Characteristic fluffy, spicular, symmetric periosteal new bone formation along the diaphyses of metacarpals and proximal phalanges
pathology_manifestations: Thyroid fine-needle aspiration / histology: Diffuse follicular hyperplasia with columnar epithelial cells forming papillary projections into the colloid; scalloping of colloid at the apical margins of follicular cells ('moth-eaten colloid')
Pretibial dermopathy biopsy: Abundant glycosaminoglycan (mucin/hyaluronic acid) accumulation splitting collagen bundles in the reticular dermis, demonstrated by Alcian blue stain
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict criteria: possesses hallmark physical manifestations (proptosis, pretibial myxedema, thyroid acropachy) and pathognomonic extraocular muscle belly enlargement on orbit CT/MRI and 'thyroid inferno' on Doppler.

Endocrinology.name: McCune-Albright Syndrome
Endocrinology.subspecialty: Metabolic Bone Disease & Genetic Endocrine Syndromes
synonyms: polyostotic fibrous dysplasia with precocious puberty
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Cutaneous Macules: Large, unilateral, flat hyperpigmented café-au-lait skin macules featuring jagged, irregular margins classically described as resembling the 'coast of Maine' ('coast-of-Maine' sign), distinct from smooth regular Neurofibromatosis type 1 patches; typically respect the dorsal or ventral midline of the body and are concentrated over the sacrum, buttocks, posterior thorax, nape of the neck, and forehead

Peripheral Autonomous Precocious Puberty: In young girls, recurrent painless vaginal bleeding and breast budding occurring as early as infancy to toddler age, driven by autonomous hyperestrogenemia produced by recurrent luteinized follicular ovarian cysts that fluctuate independently of hypothalamic GnRH; in boys, macroorchidism with bilateral or asymmetric testicular enlargement due to autonomous Leydig and Sertoli cell hyperplasia with or without autonomous testosterone production

Craniofacial Bony Asymmetry and Deformity: Painless, progressive asymmetric enlargement and bossing of the skull, maxilla, mandible, and orbital roof ('leontiasis ossea' appearance), leading to facial asymmetry, proptosis, vision loss from bony impingement of the optic canal, and conductive/sensorineural hearing impairment from internal auditory canal stenosis

Multifocal Autonomous Endocrine Hyperfunction: Autonomous thyrotoxicosis with nodular goiter (diffuse toxic or multinodular goiter resistant to antithyroid drug withdrawal), growth hormone / prolactin hypersecretion causing gigantism or coarse acromegalic facial features, autonomous ACTH-independent neonatal hypercortisolism (Cushing syndrome), and FGF23-mediated renal phosphate wasting resulting in hypophosphatemic osteomalacia/rickets with muscle weakness
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Radiography: Expansile, intramedullary diaphyseal and metaphyseal polyostotic lesions displaying a pathognomonic homogeneous, hazy, radiolucent 'ground-glass' matrix lacking normal trabecular bone markings; associated with smooth endosteal scalloping, cortical thinning, and a well-defined narrow sclerotic rim

Femoral Radiograph ('Shepherd's Crook' Deformity): Marked, progressive varus angulation and bowing of the proximal femur secondary to repeated microfractures and mechanical weight-bearing on diseased fibrous bone, creating the classic 'shepherd's crook' (coxa vara) deformity with cortical thickening and pseudoarthrosis risk

High-Resolution Craniofacial CT (Bone Window): Diffuse expansile ground-glass thickening and sclerosis replacing normal diploic bone across the sphenoid wing, orbital roofs, clivus, maxilla, and ethmoids; accurately details severe concentric narrowing of the optic canals and superior orbital fissures

Pelvic and Scrotal Ultrasound: Pelvic US reveals large, solitary or bilateral, thick-walled, autonomous cystic ovarian lesions that fluctuate in diameter over serial examinations; scrotal US in males reveals heterogeneous testicular parenchyma with hyperechoic microlithiasis, discrete hyperechoic nodular Leydig/Sertoli cell lesions, and enlarged testicular volume
pathology_manifestations: Bone Histopathology: Disorganized curvilinear, C-shaped, or fishhook-shaped trabeculae of immature woven bone resembling Chinese ideograms or 'alphabet soup' patterns, characteristically lacking osteoblastic rimming, embedded within a cellular to hypocellular fibrous stroma composed of benign, uniform, spindle-shaped fibroblastic cells lacking atypia or mitotic activity

Molecular Genetic Correlate: Postzygotic mosaic gain-of-function missense mutations in codon 201 of the GNAS gene (most commonly p.Arg201Cys or p.Arg201His on chromosome 20q13.3) leading to constitutive GTPase inhibition, persistent activation of the Gs-alpha subunit, and uncoupled hyperactivation of adenylate cyclase with elevated intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP) across affected osteoblasts, melanocytes, and endocrine cell lineages
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic mosaic endocrine-skeletal disorder exhibiting pathognomonic 'coast-of-Maine' café-au-lait skin lesions, autonomous precocious puberty, and plain radiographic 'ground-glass' expansile bone lesions with shepherd's crook femoral deformity.

Endocrinology.name: Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Palpable Thyroid Nodule: Hard, firm, non-tender solitary thyroid nodule located characteristically in the upper to middle third of the thyroid lobes (where C-cell concentration is highest), moving with deglutition and showing fixity in advanced stages

Bulky Cervical Lymphadenopathy: Early, prominent, firm or rock-hard cervical lymphadenopathy in the central (level VI) and ipsilateral/contralateral lateral neck (levels II–V), present in >50% of patients at initial clinical presentation

Systemic Neuroendocrine Flushing and Diarrhea: Paroxysmal erythematous cutaneous flushing of the face and upper torso, combined with intractable secretory watery diarrhea and abdominal cramps, triggered by massive tumor hypersecretion of calcitonin, VIP, prostaglandins, and serotonin in metastatic disease

Invasive Local Aerodigestive Signs: Hoarseness, dysphonia, and vocal cord paralysis from recurrent laryngeal nerve invasion; stridor, hemoptysis, and dysphagia from tracheal and esophageal infiltration

Associated Syndromic Phenotypes: In hereditary forms (MEN2A/MEN2B), presence of bilateral pheochromocytomas, primary hyperparathyroidism (MEN2A), or pathognomonic mucosal neuromas on tongue/lips, bumpy eyelids, marfanoid habitus, and medullated corneal nerve fibers (MEN2B)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Neck Ultrasound: Distinctive, suspicious thyroid nodule demonstrating marked hypoechogenicity, taller-than-wide morphology, irregular or lobulated margins, chaotic intranodular vascularity on color Doppler, and pathognomonic coarse, dense, irregular intrathyroidal microcalcifications or punctate echogenic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing

Cervical Lymph Node Ultrasound: Rounded, plump, enlarged metastatic cervical lymph nodes with loss of normal echogenic fatty hilum, internal cystic necrosis, peripheral vascularity, and distinctive coarse internal microcalcifications identical to the primary tumor

Contrast-Enhanced Neck and Chest CT: Dense, heterogeneously enhancing thyroid mass with invasive margins abutted against the trachea and esophagus, coupled with heavily calcified cervical and superior mediastinal lymphadenopathy

68Ga-DOTATATE, 18F-DOPA, or 18F-FDG PET/CT: Excellent sensitivity for detecting occult liver metastases (which often appear hypervascular with central necrosis) and diffuse osteoblastic / osteolytic skeletal metastases in patients with postoperative calcitonin doubling
pathology_manifestations: Thyroid Histopathology: Proliferation of uniform to mildly pleomorphic polygonal, round, or spindle-shaped parafoveolar C-cells growing in solid sheets, nests, cords, or pseudo-follicles, separated by an abundant, characteristic fibrovascular stroma

Pathognomonic Amyloid Deposition: Amorphous, dense, eosinophilic extracellular amyloid stroma derived from altered polymerized procalcitonin fibrils, demonstrating bright salmon-pink staining with Congo red dye and pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light microscopy

Immunohistochemistry: Universal, diffuse, intense cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for calcitonin, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), chromogranin A, and synaptophysin; characteristically negative for thyroglobulin (excluding follicular-derived thyroid carcinomas)
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Neuroendocrine thyroid neoplasm featuring firm thyroid nodularity, bulky calcified lymphadenopathy, flushing, and diagnostic coarse intranodal calcifications on neck US paired with apple-green birefringent amyloid on Congo red.

Endocrinology.name: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1
clinical_manifestations: Classic '3 Ps' Tumors: 1) Parathyroid: Multi-gland parathyroid hyperplasia/adenomas presenting with primary hyperparathyroidism, recurrent calcium nephrolithiasis, fatigue, and osteopenia; 2) Pancreatic Neuroendocrine: Gastrinomas (Zollinger-Ellison syndrome with severe, refractory peptic ulcerations, gastroesophageal reflux, and watery secretory diarrhea), insulinomas (recurrent fasting hypoglycemia with neuroglycopenic symptoms), or nonfunctioning pNETs; 3) Pituitary: Prolactinomas (galactorrhea, amenorrhea, bitemporal hemianopsia), growth hormone-secreting adenomas (acromegalic features), or non-functioning macroadenomas
Characteristic Cutaneous Markers: Multiple facial angiofibromas (flesh-colored papules), collagenomas, subcutaneous lipomas, and café-au-lait macules
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Multi-Phase Contrast CT and MRI: Hypervascular, avidly arterial-enhancing neuroendocrine tumors of the pancreas and duodenum; small ring-enhancing liver metastases
68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT: Extremely high sensitivity and spatial resolution for detecting primary and metastatic somatostatin receptor-expressing enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
Neck 4D-CT / 99mTc-Sestamibi SPECT-CT: Multi-gland enlargement demonstrating asymmetric 4-gland parathyroid hyperplasia
Pituitary Contrast MRI: Pituitary microadenoma or expansile macroadenoma with suprasellar extension and optic chiasm displacement
pathology_manifestations: Neuroendocrine Tumor Histopathology: Organoid nested ('Zellballen-like'), trabecular, or insular arrangements of uniform polygonal cells with finely granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and pathognomonic 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin with absent nucleoli; diffuse immunoreactivity for synaptophysin and chromogranin A
Parathyroid Histopathology: Multi-gland chief cell hyperplasia with complete depletion of stromal fat cells
Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant germline loss-of-function mutations in the MEN1 tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 11q13, encoding the nuclear scaffold protein menin
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Core endocrine neoplasia syndrome combining the '3 Ps', facial angiofibromas, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT somatostatin avidity, multi-gland parathyroid imaging, and menin loss pathology.

Endocrinology.name: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2B
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Mucosal Neuromas: Multiple, soft, flesh-colored or pink nodules clustering conspicuously on the vermilion border of the lips, dorsal and lateral surfaces of the tongue ('bumpy tongue'), buccal mucosa, and palate
'Bumpy, Blubbery Lips': Prominent diffuse hypertrophy of the upper and lower lips; eyelid neuromas with thickened, everted tarsal plates
Slit-Lamp Biomicroscopy: Hypertrophied, prominent, thickened corneal nerve fibers traversing the clear corneal stroma

Marfanoid Habitus: Asthenic, tall, slender build with arachnodactyly, joint hypermobility, pectus excavatum, and high-arched palate (without lens dislocation or aortic root aneurysm); severe intestinal ganglioneuromatosis presenting with megacolon
Extremely aggressive, virulent early-onset Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma (MTC) developing in the first year of life; bilateral pheochromocytomas (~50%)
radiological_manifestations: Neck Ultrasound and Contrast-Enhanced CT: Bulky, multifocal, infiltrative medullary thyroid carcinoma nodules with dense punctate echogenic foci (microcalcifications); extensive metastatic cervical lymphadenopathy
Abdominal Contrast CT and MRI: Bilateral, heterogeneous, hypervascular adrenal masses with central necrosis (pheochromocytomas); T2-hyperintense 'lightbulb' adrenal lesions
Abdominal Plain Radiographs / Fluoroscopy: Severe colonic dilation, megacolon, and delayed intestinal transit from diffuse ganglioneuromatosis
pathology_manifestations: Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma Histopathology: Sheets, cords, and nests of polygonal or spindle-shaped neuroendocrine cells surrounded by fibrovascular stroma containing Congo-red-positive amyloid deposits (derived from procalcitonin) exhibiting pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light; positive immunohistochemistry for calcitonin, CEA, and chromogranin
Mucosal Neuroma / Ganglioneuromatosis: Hyperplasia and tortuous proliferation of enlarged, unencapsulated nerve bundles and Schwann cells intermingled with ganglion cells
Molecular Genetics: Specific heterozygous germline point mutation in the RET proto-oncogene kinase domain at codon 918 (p.Met918Thr / M918T) in >95% of patients
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Unmatched clinical exam constellation (mucosal tongue/lip neuromas, marfanoid habitus, prominent corneal nerves) accompanied by lethal early medullary thyroid carcinoma and amyloid histology.

Endocrinology.name: Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma
clinical_manifestations: Classic Symptomatic '5 Ps' Paroxysm: 1) Paroxysmal severe hypertension (or sustained hypertension with paroxysmal spikes); 2) Pounding headache (sudden, severe, bifrontal/occipital); 3) Profuse diaphoresis (drenching generalized sweating); 4) Palpitations and tachycardia; 5) Pallor: Striking blanching/pallor of the face and extremities during paroxysms due to intense alpha-1-adrenergic peripheral vasoconstriction
Tremor, extreme anxiety/sense of impending doom ('spells'), orthostatic hypotension due to contracted plasma volume, and episodic nausea
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT: Large, well-defined, heterogeneous adrenal mass with non-contrast attenuation >10 Hounsfield Units (HU), avid heterogeneous arterial phase enhancement, and delayed contrast washout (<50% absolute washout)

Abdominal MRI (Gold Standard for Soft Tissue Characterization): Pathognomonic 'Lightbulb Bright' Sign: Extremely high signal intensity on T2-weighted MRI sequences; areas of internal cystic necrosis, hemorrhage, and prominent serpiginous flow voids

Nuclear Medicine / Molecular Functional Imaging: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT demonstrates exceptional sensitivity for paragangliomas and metastatic disease; 123I-MIBG Scintigraphy / SPECT-CT shows intense tracer avidity within chromaffin tissue reflecting catecholamine uptake via the norepinephrine transporter
pathology_manifestations: Tumor Histopathology: Classic 'Zellballen' (cell balls / nests) architecture: well-defined nests of round-to-polygonal chromaffin cells surrounded by a delicate, rich capillary network lined by S100-positive sustentacular cells; abundant granular, amphophilic-to-basophilic cytoplasm and pleomorphic nuclei

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong cytoplasmic positivity for chromogranin A and synaptophysin; peripheral rimming of nests by S100-positive sustentacular cells; GAPP and PASS histopathological scoring systems evaluate malignant potential
Molecular Genetics: Germline mutations in >15 susceptibility genes including SDHB, SDHD, VHL, RET, and NF1
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Classic endocrine hypertensive tumor where episodic facial pallor and sweating correlate with pathognomonic MRI 'lightbulb bright' T2 adrenal lesions, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT, and Zellballen architecture.

Endocrinology.name: Primary Hyperparathyroidism and Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica
clinical_manifestations: Classic multisystem mnemonic: 'Stones, bones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans': Stones (recurrent calcium nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis); Bones (severe diffuse bone pain, pathological fractures, focal jaw swellings / epulis); Groans (constipation, pancreatitis, peptic ulcer); Moans (depression, fatigue, muscle weakness)
Band Keratopathy: Horizontal grayish-white superficial corneal opacity in the interpalpebral fissure due to calcium phosphate deposition in Bowman layer
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Radiography Hallmark Signs: 1) Subperiosteal Bone Resorption (Pathognomonic): Best visualized along the radial aspect of the middle phalanges of the 2nd and 3rd digits, giving a finely lace-like, scalloped cortical border; 2) 'Salt-and-Pepper' Skull: Granular, mottled loss of calvarial trabecular architecture with blurred inner and outer skull tables; 3) Brown Tumors (Osteoclastomas): Well-circumscribed, expansile, geographic lytic lesions in the mandible, ribs, pelvis, and long bones with thinned cortices; 4) Distal Clavicular Osteolysis: Tapering, resorption, and pencil-pointing of the distal acromial ends of the clavicles
Neck 4D-CT and 99mTc-Sestamibi SPECT-CT: Hypervascular, early-enhancing, rapidly washing-out enlarged parathyroid adenoma (typically inferior gland)
Renal Ultrasound / CT: Bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis and staghorn calculi
pathology_manifestations: Parathyroid Adenoma Histopathology: Encapsulated nodule composed almost exclusively of densely packed chief cells with absent intrastromal adipocytes, surrounded by a compressed rim of normal parathyroid tissue containing fat

Brown Tumor / Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica Bone Histopathology: Intense osteoclastic bone resorption with peritrabecular fibrosis; proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells intermixed with spindle-shaped fibroblastic stroma; abundant hemosiderin pigment accumulation from repetitive microhemorrhages giving the classic gross brown appearance
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Celebrated metabolic bone catastrophe combining band keratopathy, pathognomonic subperiosteal finger resorption on X-ray, brown tumors, and parathyroid adenoma sestamibi imaging.

Endocrinology.name: Pseudohypoparathyroidism Type 1A
Endocrinology.subspecialty: Metabolic Bone Disease & Albright Hereditary Osteodystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Albright Hereditary Osteodystrophy (AHO) Physical Habitus: Short stature, stocky habitus, and early-onset central obesity; rounded moon facies with flattened nasal bridge

Pathognomonic Brachydactyly: Shortening of the 4th and 5th metacarpals and metatarsals, producing dimples in place of knuckles when making a clenched fist (Archibald sign / 'knuckle, knuckle, dimple, dimple' sign)
Subcutaneous Ossifications / Osteoma Cutis: Hard, palpable, plaque-like or nodular heterotopic bone formations within the dermis and subcutaneous tissues

Hypocalcemic Tetany Signs: Positive Chvostek sign (facial twitch on tapping facial nerve) and Trousseau sign (carpopedal spasm upon inflation of blood pressure cuff); paresthesias, seizures, and prolonged QT interval
Multi-hormone end-organ resistance (PTH, TSH [subclinical hypothyroidism], LH/FSH, and GHRH)
radiological_manifestations: Hand and Foot Radiographs (Plain Films): Pathognomonic shortening of the 4th and 5th metacarpal and metatarsal bones; short broad phalanges with cone-shaped epiphyses; short distal phalanx of the thumb ('murderer's thumb')
Soft-Tissue Radiography and CT: Extensive subcutaneous heterotopic ossification and osteoma cutis in the extremities and abdominal wall without muscle involvement

Non-Contrast Brain CT: Striking, extensive, symmetrical calcification of the basal ganglia (caudate nucleus, globus pallidus, putamen), thalami, and subcortical white matter (Fahr syndrome pattern) due to chronic hyperphosphatemia and hypocalcemia
pathology_manifestations: Osteoma Cutis Histopathology: True mature lamellar bone islands containing osteocytes, osteoblasts, and bone marrow elements residing entirely within the reticular dermis and subcutaneous adipose tissue

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the GNAS gene on chromosome 20q13.3 (encoding the alpha subunit of the stimulatory G-protein, Gs-alpha) inherited maternally, causing tissue-specific resistance to PTH in renal proximal tubules despite marked compensatory elevation of serum PTH
Endocrinology.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive endocrine-dysmorphic condition presenting with Archibald knuckle sign, osteoma cutis, Fahr basal ganglia calcification on CT, and maternal GNAS-mediated PTH resistance.

Endocrinology.name: Riedel Thyroiditis (Invasive Fibrous Thyroiditis)
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Palpable Neck Mass: Slowly or subacutely expanding, stony 'iron-hard', 'woody', or 'ligneous' anterior cervical mass that is completely fixed to surrounding anatomical structures (pretracheal fascia, sternocleidomastoid and strap muscles, trachea, and carotid sheaths) and fails to ascend upon deglutition

Severe Tracheoesophageal Compressive Symptoms: Progressive, severe inspiratory stridor, choking sensation, orthopnea, and suffocating dyspnea secondary to rigid circumferential tracheal encasement and luminal narrowing; progressive solid-food dysphagia from esophageal compression

Invasive Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Palsy: Early hoarseness, dysphonia, and fixed vocal cord paralysis documented on flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy, frequently mimicking invasive anaplastic thyroid carcinoma

Vascular and Extrathyroidal Infiltration: Encasement of carotid sheaths causing diminished unilateral or bilateral carotid pulsations, cervical venous engorgement from internal jugular compression, and hard woody induration extending diffusely beyond the thyroid bed into the anterior chest and supraclavicular fossae

Coexisting Systemic Fibrosing Disorders (IgG4-RD): Extrathyroidal manifestation of systemic IgG4-related disease in approximately one-third of patients, including retroperitoneal fibrosis (flank/back pain, ureteral obstruction, hydronephrosis), sclerosing mediastinitis, sclerosing cholangitis, or orbital pseudotumor
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Neck CT: Ill-defined, infiltrative, markedly hypoattenuating neck mass replacing thyroid parenchyma with direct, aggressive contiguous invasion through the thyroid capsule into adjacent strap muscles, carotid sheaths, and prevertebral space; demonstrates circumferential encasement, displacement, and caliber reduction ('saber-sheath' narrowing) of the cervical trachea

Neck MRI ('Black Thyroid' Sign): Striking, pathognomonic profound hypointensity of the entire mass on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted sequences ('black thyroid' appearance) caused by dense, avascular, hyalinized fibrous collagen, with negligible or faint heterogeneous post-gadolinium enhancement

High-Frequency Neck Ultrasound: Diffuse, intensely hypoechoic, markedly heterogeneous replacement of the thyroid gland with loss of normal architecture and indistinct capsule; demonstrates absence of vascularity on color Doppler ('cold thyroid') and direct acoustic continuity between the thyroid mass and adjacent strap muscles

Abdominal and Thoracic CT/MRI: Evaluates systemic fibrosing correlates, revealing periaortic soft-tissue mantling and medial ureteral deviation characteristic of retroperitoneal fibrosis, fibrosing mediastinitis with superior vena cava narrowing, or tumefactive autoimmune pancreatitis
