Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Marked parenchymal atrophy of the pancreatic body and tail with replacement by fibrofatty tissue; severe, irregular, beaded main pancreatic duct dilatation ('chain of lakes' or 'string of pearls' appearance, duct caliber >10-15 mm) with alternating segments of tight inflammatory strictures and cystic sacculations; intraductal filling defects corresponding to dense calcified stones; associated pseudocysts and common bile duct compression

Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP): High-resolution delineation of the entire ductal architecture showing marked main pancreatic duct ectasia, ectatic side branches, intraductal signal voids (stones), and distal smooth tapering stricture of the intrapancreatic common bile duct ('double-duct' appearance if head mass develops)

Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS): Rosemont and Milwaukee criteria for chronic pancreatitis: hyperechoic parenchymal foci with shadowing (calculi), parenchymal lobularity with honeycombing, thickened hyperechoic duct margins, and main duct irregular dilatation with intraductal calculi
pathology_manifestations: Pancreatectomy / surgical biopsy: Gross specimen shows a shrunken, rock-hard, densely fibrotic pancreas with a prominently dilated main pancreatic duct containing numerous white-to-chalky, hard, jagged or rounded intraductal stones composed primarily of calcium carbonate (calcite) precipitate over a proteinaceous nidus

Histology: Advanced chronic pancreatitis with extensive intralobular and perilobular collagenous sclerosis and fibrosis; severe, near-total loss and atrophy of acinar lobules; residual hyperplastic or metaplastic ductules (mucinous and squamous metaplasia); relative preservation of endocrine islets of Langerhans early, progressing to islet aggregation and sclerosis late; chronic inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and activated pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs)

Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant gain-of-function mutation in the PRSS1 gene on chromosome 7q35 encoding cationic trypsinogen (predominantly p.R122H or p.N29I, which disrupt the autolytic cleavage site preventing protective trypsin autodegradation), or autosomal recessive/modifier mutations in SPINK1 (p.N34S), CTRC, or CFTR
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic monogenic pancreatobiliary disease with childhood onset of agonizing back-radiating pain, steatorrhea, and brittle type 3c diabetes, paired with pathognomonic massive rounded 'bull's eye' intraductal stones and 'chain of lakes' ductal dilatation on CT/radiographs, driven by PRSS1 mutations.

Gastroenterology.name: Ménétrier Disease (Hypertrophic Protein-Losing Gastropathy)
clinical_manifestations: Massive, severe peripheral pitting edema (anasarca, periorbital edema, scrotal/labial edema, ascites, and pleural effusions) resulting from profound hypoalbuminemia and systemic hypoproteinemia secondary to enteric protein loss across the hyperplastic gastric mucosa (protein-losing gastropathy)
Severe postprandial epigastric pain, persistent nausea, projectile or copious vomiting, early satiety, and anorexia accompanied by profound involuntary weight loss and muscle wasting (cachexia)
Epigastric fullness or ill-defined soft epigastric tenderness to deep palpation without focal peritoneal signs, often accompanied by an audible gastric succession splash

Microcytic hypochromic anemia stigmata (pallor, conjunctival rim pallor, fatigue, angular cheilitis, brittle spoon-shaped nails / koilonychia) secondary to chronic, occult, microscopic mucosal bleeding from friable gastric rugae

Pediatric acute self-limiting variant (frequently triggered by acute cytomegalovirus / CMV infection or Helicobacter pylori) manifesting with abrupt-onset facial edema, periorbital puffiness, lethargy, and severe hypoalbuminemia
radiological_manifestations: Upper Gastrointestinal Barium Series (Barium Meal / Double-Contrast Fluoroscopy): Striking, pathognomonic giant, tortuous, thickened gastric rugal folds resembling cerebral gyri ('brain-like' or 'convoluted cerebriform' appearance) predominantly involving the fundus and greater curvature of the gastric body, with absolute or relative sparing of the gastric antrum; broad, polypoid-like filling defects coated by thick, hypersecreted mucus that separates barium particles

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Marked, diffuse, scalloped mural thickening of the gastric fundus and body (often >10 mm, up to 20-30 mm; normal gastric wall <3-5 mm) with preservation of mural stratification; prominent, undulating giant mucosal folds projecting deeply into the gastric lumen; classic abrupt transition sparing the gastric antrum; secondary imaging signs include diffuse ascites, bilateral pleural effusions, and anasarca (diffuse subcutaneous edema)

Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS): Dramatic thickening of the mucosal layer (layer 2: deep hypoechoic mucosa) representing massive foveolar hyperplasia, while the underlying submucosa (layer 3) and muscularis propria (layer 4) remain preserved, distinct, intact, and non-invaded, crucially distinguishing Ménétrier disease from infiltrating gastric malignancy (linitis plastica) or gastric lymphoma
Abdominal Ultrasound: Marked gastric wall thickening with giant, undulating rugal folds and associated ascites; Doppler reveals preserved layered mural architecture without invasive disruption
pathology_manifestations: Full-thickness gastric mucosal / snare biopsy: Pathognomonic massive foveolar hyperplasia with striking elongation, tortuosity, and cystic dilation of the gastric surface and pit epithelium (corkscrew-like foveolar glands lined by mature mucin-secreting cells), resulting in dramatic expansion of the mucosal thickness; marked atrophy and numeric reduction of parietal (oxyntic) and chief cells leading to profound hypochlorhydria or absolute achlorhydria and decreased pepsinogen; diffuse chronic lamina propria edema, smooth muscle hyperplasia extending between glands, and patchy plasma cell / eosinophil infiltrates; marked overexpression of transforming growth factor-alpha (TGF-alpha) acting via epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling; pediatric cases show characteristic CMV intranuclear inclusion bodies (owl-eye appearance) or positive CMV immunohistochemistry (IHC)
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic protein-losing hypertrophic gastropathy with striking clinical anasarca from profound hypoalbuminemia, pathognomonic cerebral-like giant gastric folds sparing the antrum on barium and CT, and diagnostic foveolar hyperplasia with parietal cell drop-out on histology.

Gastroenterology.name: Primary Biliary Cholangitis
clinical_manifestations: Extensive periorbital xanthelasma (soft, yellowish, cholesterol-rich plaques on inner eyelids)
Tuberous and planar xanthomas over palms, extensor tendons, and buttocks
Diffuse cutaneous hyperpigmentation (melanoderma) sparing oral mucosa
Severe linear excoriations from intractable cholestatic itching
Signs of advanced cirrhosis (spider nevi, palmar erythema, jaundice)
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal MRI / Ultrasound: 'Periportal halo sign' on T2-weighted MRI (round hypointense areas surrounding portal tracts due to fibrosis and inflammation); prominent lymphadenopathy at the gastrohepatic ligament and porta hepatis; cirrhotic morphology (hypertrophied caudate lobe, nodular liver surface)
Transient Elastography (FibroScan): Objective non-invasive measurement of advanced hepatic fibrosis
pathology_manifestations: Liver needle biopsy: Pathognomonic 'florid duct lesion' consisting of chronic non-suppurative destructive cholangitis; focal granulomatous destruction of medium and small interlobular septal bile ducts by lymphocytes, plasma cells, and epithelioid histiocytes; copper-associated protein accumulation
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Classic cholestatic entity with dramatic physical signs (palmar xanthomas, xanthelasma, melanoderma) matched with the 'periportal halo sign' and hilar lymphadenopathy on liver MRI.

Gastroenterology.name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
clinical_manifestations: Severe scleral icterus and generalized jaundice
Extensive excoriations and prurigo nodularis from unremitting cholestatic pruritus
Cutaneous xanthomas and xanthelasma around the eyelids
Hepatosplenomegaly and signs of portal hypertension (caput medusae, spider angiomas)
Frequent clinical coexistence with ulcerative colitis (~70-80%)
radiological_manifestations: Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP): Gold standard diagnostic imaging demonstrating the pathognomonic 'beaded' appearance of the biliary tree (multifocal, short, annular strictures alternating with normal or mildly dilated segments involving both intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts); 'pruned-tree' appearance from obliteration of small peripheral ducts
Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Segmental biliary duct dilation, gallbladder wall thickening, nodular cirrhotic liver contour, splenomegaly, and portal venous collaterals
pathology_manifestations: Liver needle / wedge biopsy: Periductal concentric 'onion-skin' fibrosis surrounding medium and small interlobular bile ducts, progressive ductopenia (vanishing bile duct syndrome), portal tract lymphocytic inflammation, and biliary piecemeal necrosis
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Core hepatobiliary disease with striking deep jaundice, pruritic excoriations, and xanthelasma, diagnosed by the pathognomonic 'beaded' biliary tree on MRCP.

Gastroenterology.name: Pyogenic Liver Abscess (Klebsiella / Enteric Hepatic Abscess)
clinical_manifestations: Severe, potentially lethal suppurative infection of hepatic parenchyma, most frequently caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae (especially hypervirulent K1/K2 hypermucoviscous strains), Escherichia coli, Streptococcus anginosus (milleri) group, or enteric anaerobes (Bacteroides fragilis), originating from ascending cholangitis (biliary), pylephlebitis (portal vein drainage from diverticulitis/appendicitis), or cryptogenic sources (strongly linked to diabetes mellitus and occult colorectal neoplasia)

Classic clinical presentation: high spiking, hectic fevers accompanied by severe shaking chills (rigors), drenching night sweats, and persistent dull, aching right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the right shoulder or scapula

Bedside physical examination: exquisite tenderness to palpation in the right hypochondrium; positive Murphy punch sign (exquisite fist-percussion tenderness over the right lower intercostal spaces and liver bed); palpable, tender, smooth hepatomegaly; deep scleral icterus and cutaneous jaundice in ~25-30% of cases; secondary right-sided pleural effusion with dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds at the right lung base

Invasive Klebsiella pneumoniae liver abscess syndrome (IKPLAS / septic metastasis): hypermucoviscous K1/K2 serotype strains cause rapid metastatic septic embolization presenting with acute endogenous endophthalmitis (sudden painful visual loss, severe conjunctival and ciliary injection, hypopyon, vitritis), septic pulmonary emboli with cavitation, and suppurative meningitis/brain abscess
Signs of septic shock: profound hypotension, tachycardia, tachypnea, oliguria, altered mental status, and warm flushed or mottled peripheries requiring aggressive resuscitation
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Diagnostic Modality of Choice): Single or multilocular, well-circumscribed, round-to-oval hypodense fluid collections (attenuation typically 10-30 HU); pathognomonic 'double-target sign' on contrast-enhanced scans: a central hypodense non-enhancing fluid cavity surrounded by an inner hyperenhancing hyperemic rim (granulation tissue/capillary proliferation) and an outer hypoattenuating halo of parenchymal edema; 'cluster sign': multiple small hypodense locules coalescing into a single larger multilocular abscess cavity (highly specific for pyogenic etiology rather than amebic or fungal); internal gas bubbles or air-fluid levels (pathognomonic for gas-forming organisms like K. pneumoniae, E. coli, or Clostridium species)

Abdominal Ultrasound: Round or oval hypoechoic to mixed echogenic mass with irregular, thickened, shaggy walls and internal acoustic enhancement; presence of internal low-level echoes, thick mobile debris, and multiple internal septations; microbubbles of gas produce hyperechoic foci with 'dirty' acoustic shadowing or comet-tail / ring-down artifacts

Abdominal MRI: Markedly hypointense on T1-weighted images with high signal intensity on T2-weighted images; restricted diffusion on Diffusion-Weighted Imaging (DWI) with profoundly low Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC) values within the central purulent cavity (representing viscous, hypercellular, necrotic pus, clearly differentiating abscess from necrotic tumor or simple cyst); thick, irregular peripheral rim enhancement on post-gadolinium sequences
pathology_manifestations: Diagnostic percutaneous aspiration: Thick, copious, opaque, creamy yellow-green or tan purulent exudate (pus) with a foul or sweet odor; positive 'string test' (>5 mm viscous string when colonies are stretched with an inoculation loop) pathognomonic for the hypermucoviscous phenotype of Klebsiella pneumoniae (encoded by rmpA and magA virulence genes)

Microscopic examination of aspirate: Dense, confluent sheets of degenerating and necrotic polymorphonuclear leukocytes (neutrophils), proteinaceous debris, fragmented nuclear debris (karyorrhexis), and abundant intra- and extracellular Gram-negative bacilli or Gram-positive cocci; positive bacterial cultures

Liver resection / core biopsy (at perimeter): Confluent liquefactive necrosis of hepatic parenchyma; central cavity filled with neutrophilic exudate and necrotic debris, bordered by an active rim of vascular granulation tissue, proliferating fibroblasts, and capillary neoangiogenesis; adjacent hepatic parenchyma displays sinusoidal congestion, microvascular thrombosis, hepatocyte hydropic degeneration, and prominent intracanalicular cholestasis
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Critical hepatobiliary infection characterized by the triad of spiking fevers, RUQ punch tenderness, and septic metastases (endophthalmitis in hypervirulent Klebsiella), paired with CT 'double-target sign', 'cluster sign', and gas formation, and purulent neutrophilic liquefactive necrosis.

Gastroenterology.name: Trichobezoar and Rapunzel Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Dermatological hallmark: Patchy, irregular, non-scarring alopecia with hairs of varying lengths, broken shafts, and twisted stubs across the scalp (trichotillomania) in a young girl or adolescent female, often concealed by hairstyles or scarves
Palpable, extremely firm, mobile, non-tender or mildly tender, indentable epigastric mass that precisely contours to the shape of the stomach (stomach-shaped epigastric abdominal mass)
Severe, offensive, putrid halitosis (fetor oris) caused by the fermentation, bacterial putrefaction, and entrapment of lipids and food debris within the tangled, insoluble hairball
Chronic epigastric discomfort, early satiety, severe postprandial nausea, bilious vomiting, profound anorexia, and massive involuntary weight loss (severe malnutrition and cachexia)

Rapunzel syndrome: Distal extension of a long, coiled hair tail past the pylorus through the entire duodenum into the jejunum or ileocolic junction, manifesting with complete mechanical small bowel obstruction, intestinal intussusception, or transmural pressure necrosis and bowel perforation
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Imaging Modality of Choice): Pathognomonic, well-defined, non-enhancing intraluminal soft-tissue mass filling and conforming precisely to the gastric lumen, containing hundreds of tiny, trapped, mottled air bubbles resembling a coarse 'spongiform' or 'bread-crumb' pattern; in Rapunzel syndrome, the mass shows a continuous elongated, high-density tail extending through the pyloric canal, sweeping through the duodenal C-loop, and entering the proximal small bowel; non-adherence to the gastric mucosa with a rim of oral contrast coating the outer surface of the hairball

Upper Gastrointestinal Barium Series (Barium Meal): Classic large, mobile, mottled, inhomogeneous intraluminal filling defect in the stomach that retains contrast within its interstices long after the stomach has emptied; free-floating appearance within the barium pool without attachment to the gastric wall

Plain Abdominal Radiographs: Non-specific soft-tissue density outlined by gastric gas; mottled air-density pattern in the upper abdomen simulating feculent material inside the stomach; distended loops of small bowel with multiple air-fluid levels if complicated by distal small bowel obstruction
Abdominal Ultrasound: Broad, highly reflective hyperechoic arc-like anterior band with dense acoustic shadowing, obscuring visualization of deeper gastric structures
pathology_manifestations: Surgical gastrotomy / enterotomy extraction specimen: Dramatic, single, foul-smelling, solid, heavy, dark-green-to-black mass consisting of a densely compacted felt-like meshwork of thousands of swallowed hairs, fibers, and mucus concretions, taking the exact cast of the entire gastric cavity (gastric mold), with an elongated, twisted string-like tail measuring up to 50-100 cm in length (Rapunzel syndrome); microscopic examination of concretions reveals densely packed, keratinized hair shafts, amorphous mucinous material, food detritus, calcium soaps, and colonies of putrefactive bacteria and fungi; gastric wall biopsy reveals pressure-induced mucosal ischemic ulceration, marked chronic inflammatory infiltration, granulation tissue, and reactive epithelial hyperplasia
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Bizarre, clinically arresting neuropsychiatric-gastrointestinal disorder pairing compulsive trichotillomania alopecia with an indentable epigastric mass, foul halitosis, and pathognomonic spongiform air-mottled gastric cast extending into the small bowel on CT.

Gastroenterology.name: Ulcerative Colitis
clinical_manifestations: Tense, distended, exquisitely tender abdomen in acute fulminant colitis and toxic megacolon
Extraintestinal skin manifestations: severe pyoderma gangrenosum, erythema nodosum
Ocular: episcleritis, anterior uveitis
Peripheral asymmetric inflammatory arthritis, clubbing
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Radiography: Toxic megacolon demonstrated by marked transverse colon dilation (>6 cm) with loss of normal colonic haustral pattern and pseudopolyp mucosal projections; thumbprinting (submucosal edema)

Abdominal / Pelvic CT: Continuous, symmetrical colonic wall thickening starting at the rectum and extending proximally without skip lesions; 'mural stratification' (target or halo sign with submucosal edema); 'lead-pipe' colon (rigid, featureless, foreshortened colon with complete loss of haustra in chronic UC)
pathology_manifestations: Colonoscopic mucosal biopsy: Inflammation strictly limited to the mucosa and submucosa (sparing muscularis propria and serosa); diffuse, continuous crypt architectural distortion (branched, shortened crypts), cryptitis and neutrophilic crypt abscesses, goblet cell mucin depletion, and absence of transmural lymphoid aggregates or granulomas
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: High-impact visual colitis with toxic megacolon abdominal distension and pyoderma gangrenosum, verified by classic plain film colonic dilation >6 cm and the 'lead-pipe' colon on CT.

Gastroenterology.name: Whipple's Disease (Tropheryma whipplei Infection)
clinical_manifestations: Diffuse, slate-gray or brownish cutaneous hyperpigmentation of sun-exposed areas (face, neck, dorsum of hands), resembling Addisonian pigmentation (without adrenal insufficiency)
Severe cachexia, profound temporal wasting, anorexia, and intractable chronic watery diarrhea with steatorrhea and abdominal distension

Pathognomonic neuro-ophthalmologic sign: Oculomasticatory or oculofacial-skeletal myorhythmia (continuous, rhythmic, pendular, slow [1 Hz] convergent/divergent nystagmus synchronized with rhythmic contractions of masticatory, facial, and limb muscles; pathognomonic of CNS Whipple disease)
Supranuclear vertical gaze palsy, progressive dementia, ataxia, memory impairment, and hypothalamic symptoms (insomnia, hyperphagia, polydipsia)

Chronic, migratory, seronegative, non-deforming, episodic oligo- or polyarthritis (affecting knees, ankles, wrists) often preceding gastrointestinal symptoms by years; generalized painless peripheral lymphadenopathy and heart murmurs from culture-negative endocarditis
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI: Massive, confluent retroperitoneal and mesenteric lymphadenopathy with characteristic low attenuation (near water or fat density, 10-25 Hounsfield units) due to massive accumulation of emulsified lipids and PAS-positive foamy macrophages; diffuse, irregular, marked thickening of the duodenum and proximal jejunal mucosal folds (>4 mm) with a coarse, nodular mucosal surface ('sand-like' appearance); small bowel dilatation without mechanical obstruction; retroperitoneal lymph node conglomerate mimicking lymphoma
Small Bowel Barium Series: Coarse, thickened, nodular, distorted mucosal fold pattern in the duodenum and jejunum with mucosal speckling and flocculation of barium
Brain MRI (in CNS Whipple): Multifocal, nodular or ring-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions within the hypothalamus, uncus, mammillary bodies, tectum, thalamus, and periaqueductal gray matter
pathology_manifestations: Small bowel (duodenum/jejunum) mucosal biopsy: Massive infiltration and expansion of the lamina propria by sheets of large, foamy, rounded macrophages that are densely packed with coarse cytoplasmic granules that stain intensely magenta/purplish with Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS) and are strictly resistant to diastase digestion (PAS-D positive); acid-fast (Ziehl-Neelsen) stain is negative (excluding Mycobacterium avium complex); Transmission Electron Microscopy demonstrates innumerable intact and degenerating rod-shaped bacillary organisms (Tropheryma whipplei) within macrophage phagolysosomes and the interstitium; confirmatory PCR testing for T. whipplei 16S rRNA gene
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Rare systemic bacterial enteropathy featuring slate-gray cutaneous hyperpigmentation, arthritis, and pathognomonic oculomasticatory myorhythmia, paired with unique low-attenuation mesenteric lymphadenopathy on CT and diastase-resistant PAS+ macrophage infiltration on small bowel biopsy.

Gastroenterology.name: Zenker Diverticulum (Pharyngoesophageal Pouch)
clinical_manifestations: Visible, soft, compressible, fluctuant swelling or mass in the left anterior cervical triangle of the neck (or occasionally right side), especially noticeable after eating or drinking

Boyce's sign: Pathognomonic elicitation of an audible squelching, gurgling sound (borborygmi) upon manual compression or palpation of the left lower cervical neck mass, accompanied by spontaneous regurgitation of foul fluids into the pharynx
Severe, intolerable fetor oris (putrid halitosis) caused by the chronic decomposition, stagnation, and bacterial putrefaction of retained food particles trapped within the dependent diverticular sac
Regurgitation of undigested, non-acidic, foul-smelling food ingested hours or even days earlier, typically occurring when the patient lies supine at night or bends forward

High cervical dysphagia ('sticking' of solids and liquids at the level of the suprasternal notch), chronic nocturnal coughing spells, choking, recurrent aspiration pneumonia, hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve irritation, and progressive involuntary weight loss
radiological_manifestations: Dynamic Barium Swallow / Barium Esophagram (Imaging Modality of Choice and Definitive Gold Standard): Performed in lateral and oblique fluoroscopic projections: striking demonstration of a smooth, sac-like, pouch-shaped contrast collection arising posteriorly from the midline hypopharynx precisely at the pharyngoesophageal junction, immediately above a prominent transverse posterior indentation caused by the hypertonic cricopharyngeus muscle ('cricopharyngeal bar'); dependent retention and pooling of barium within the pouch with an air-fluid level; anterior compression and displacement of the cervical esophagus; dynamic fluoroscopy demonstrates failure of cricopharyngeal relaxation during swallowing and frequent tracheal / bronchial contrast aspiration

Contrast-Enhanced Neck and Chest CT: Well-circumscribed, thin-walled, air- and fluid-filled pouch located posteriorly and to the left of the esophagus, in the retrovisceral / retropharyngeal space at the C5-C6 vertebral level; demonstrates absence of invasive soft-tissue extension or cervical lymphadenopathy unless malignant transformation (squamous cell carcinoma) has developed within the chronic diverticulum
pathology_manifestations: Surgical diverticulectomy / endoscopic myotomy specimen: Classic false diverticulum (pulsion pseudodiverticulum) consisting of an outpouching of mucosal and submucosal layers herniating through Killian's triangle (Killian's dehiscence, an anatomically weak triangular muscular defect between the oblique fibers of the thyropharyngeus muscle and the transverse fibers of the cricopharyngeus muscle of the inferior pharyngeal constrictor); histopathology confirms pouch wall composed exclusively of squamous epithelium and fibroadipose submucosa, completely devoid of a true muscularis propria layer (only fragmented or absent muscular fibers); chronic mucosal inflammation, retention cyst changes, superficial ulceration, and in 0.5-1% of long-standing cases, invasive squamous cell carcinoma arising from the chronic stasis and irritation
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Premier structural-motility lesion of the upper digestive tract presenting with palpable cervical mass and pathognomonic Boyce's sign, putrid halitosis, textbook fluoroscopic posterior barium pouch above the cricopharyngeal bar, and true pulsion pseudodiverticulum histology through Killian's triangle.

Gastroenterology.name: Eosinophilic Esophagitis
clinical_manifestations: Food impaction history is clinical; the image is endoscopic, not an external photograph
Endoscopy: trachealization, longitudinal furrows, white exudates, and a narrow esophagus
radiological_manifestations: Barium esophagram: a long narrow-caliber esophagus or a ringed feline esophagus
pathology_manifestations: Esophageal eosinophilia at least 15 per high-power field with eosinophil microabscesses, after excluding reflux as the sole cause
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Esophageal disease defined by endoscopic and barium images plus a biopsy threshold. Not a manifestation of a broader indexed disease.

Gastroenterology.name: Intestinal Amebiasis
clinical_manifestations: Colonoscopy: flask-shaped ulcers with intervening normal mucosa
Ameboma as a cecal mass mimic; fulminant colitis with a toxic appearance is the severe end, not a separate topic
radiological_manifestations: CT: right-sided colitis or a cecal ameboma; liver abscess is not re-listed here because amebic liver abscess is already a topic
pathology_manifestations: Trophozoites with ingested erythrocytes on stool or ulcer biopsy, PAS-positive
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Endoscopic ulcerative colitis look-alike with a specific parasite image. Liver abscess stays its own indexed topic because the image set is different.

Gastroenterology.name: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: A hard irregular liver, sometimes with a bruit
Paraneoplastic photographs when present: pityriasis rotunda or sudden porphyria-like skin fragility are uncommon and not required
The usual gallery is arterial-phase imaging rather than an external photo
radiological_manifestations: Multiphase CT or MRI: arterial hyperenhancement and portal venous washout
LI-RADS features in a cirrhotic liver
pathology_manifestations: Trabecular hepatocyte tumor, bile production, and a glypican-3 immunostain
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Hepatic malignancy with a pathognomonic enhancement pattern and a histologic image. Decompensated cirrhosis remains a separate topic.

Gastroenterology.name: Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Endoscopy: multiple juvenile polyps in the colon or stomach
Rectal bleeding and protein-losing edema when the burden is high
radiological_manifestations: No specific radiology unless intussusception complicates a polyp; that event is not a separate topic
pathology_manifestations: Juvenile polyps with dilated cystic glands and inflamed lamina propria; SMAD4 or BMPR1A confirms
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Polyposis with an endoscopic gallery, distinct from familial adenomatous polyposis.

Gastroenterology.name: Howel-Evans Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Focal palmoplantar keratoderma from late childhood
Endoscopy or barium study of the associated esophageal squamous carcinoma
radiological_manifestations: Barium esophagram or PET when a carcinoma has declared itself
pathology_manifestations: Callus-like keratoderma; RHBDF2 confirms the syndrome
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Keratoderma-plus-esophageal-cancer syndrome with palm photographs and an esophageal image.

Gastroenterology.name: Primary Intestinal Lymphangiectasia
clinical_manifestations: Edema, chylous effusions, and a child who looks malnourished despite intake
Endoscopy: snowflake white duodenal villi
radiological_manifestations: Lymphoscintigraphy or MR lymphangiography shows intestinal lymphatic leak
pathology_manifestations: Dilated mucosal lymphatics on duodenal biopsy
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Lymphatic enteropathy with edema photographs, white-villus endoscopy, and dilated lymphatics on biopsy.

Gastroenterology.name: Eosinophilic Gastroenteritis
clinical_manifestations: Endoscopy: thickened folds, erythema, and erosions
Ascites when the serosal layer is involved
radiological_manifestations: CT: thickened gastric or small-bowel wall and ascites
pathology_manifestations: Dense eosinophilic infiltration of mucosa, muscle, or serosa, after excluding parasite infection
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Eosinophilic gut disease with endoscopic and CT images. Esophagitis remains a separate topic because the image set differs.

Gastroenterology.name: Solitary Rectal Ulcer Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Rectal bleeding and mucus
Endoscopy: a solitary anterior rectal ulcer or a polypoid prolapsing fold
radiological_manifestations: Defecography: internal intussusception or prolapse
pathology_manifestations: Fibromuscular obliteration of the lamina propria
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Rectal prolapse disorder with an endoscopic ulcer photograph and a defecography image.

Gastroenterology.name: Pseudomembranous Colitis
clinical_manifestations: Endoscopy: raised yellow-white plaques on an erythematous mucosa
A toxic, distended abdomen in fulminant disease
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal radiograph or CT: accordion-sign colonic thickening and megacolon
pathology_manifestations: Summit lesions of pseudomembrane over necrotic epithelium; toxin assay confirms
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Colitis with a pathognomonic endoscopic photograph and an accordion-sign CT.

Gastroenterology.name: Acute Graft-versus-Host Disease
clinical_manifestations: Maculopapular rash on the palms, soles, and trunk after transplant
Endoscopy: denuded mucosa and bile-stained exudate in gut GVHD
radiological_manifestations: CT: diffuse small-bowel wall thickening when the gut is involved
pathology_manifestations: Satellite-cell necrosis and apoptotic crypt cells; skin shows interface dermatitis with satellite necrosis
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Transplant disease with skin photographs and endoscopic or histologic crypt apoptosis. The rash is a site, not a separate topic.

Gastroenterology.name: Plummer-Vinson Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Koilonychia, angular cheilitis, and glossitis
Dysphagia to solids
radiological_manifestations: Barium esophagram: a proximal esophageal web
pathology_manifestations: The web is a thin mucosal shelf; iron deficiency explains the nails and mucosa
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Web syndrome with nail and tongue photographs plus a barium web.

Gastroenterology.name: Alagille Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Broad forehead, deep-set eyes, and a pointed chin
Chronic cholestasis with xanthomas
radiological_manifestations: Spine radiograph: butterfly vertebrae
Echocardiography: peripheral pulmonary stenosis
pathology_manifestations: Paucity of intrahepatic bile ducts; JAG1 or NOTCH2 confirms
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Cholestatic syndrome with a face photograph, xanthomas, butterfly vertebrae, and bile-duct paucity.

Gastroenterology.name: Abetalipoproteinemia
clinical_manifestations: Failure to thrive and steatorrhea in infancy
Retinitis pigmentosa and ataxia later; the smear is the early image
radiological_manifestations: Not primarily radiologic; the acanthocyte smear and the retinal photograph are the gallery
pathology_manifestations: Enterocyte lipid vacuolization and absent apoB-containing lipoproteins
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Malabsorption with acanthocytes, a lipid-filled biopsy, and later retinal photographs.

Gastroenterology.name: Barrett Esophagus
clinical_manifestations: Longstanding history of chronic gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) with retrosternal pyrosis, acid regurgitation, and nocturnal cough
Paradoxical improvement in heartburn symptoms as acid-sensitive squamous mucosa is replaced by less sensitive metaplastic columnar epithelium
Progressive dysphagia for solids, odynophagia, and involuntary weight loss heralding neoplastic progression to esophageal adenocarcinoma
radiological_manifestations: Barium Esophagram: Reticular mucosal pattern, distal esophageal stricture, or high esophageal ulcer (Barrett ulcer) proximal to the hiatus hernia
Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS): Used for staging when dysplasia or nodularity is detected; demonstrates thickening of mucosal layer with disruption of muscularis mucosae in invasive malignancy
pathology_manifestations: Upper Endoscopy (EGD): Salmon-pink, velvety columnar mucosa extending proximally from the gastroesophageal junction into the tubular esophagus, contrasting sharply with the pale, pearly squamous epithelium; categorized by Prague Criteria (Circumferential 'C' and Maximal 'M' extent in cm); narrow-band imaging (NBI) reveals irregular mucosal pit patterns and abnormal microvasculature

Histopathology (Biopsy): Definitive diagnosis requires specialized intestinal metaplasia characterized by columnar epithelium containing distinct, mucin-rich goblet cells (staining brilliant blue with Alcian blue at pH 2.5); progressive architectural and cytologic atypia defining low-grade dysplasia, high-grade dysplasia, and intramucosal adenocarcinoma
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic premalignant gastrointestinal condition defined by salmon-pink tongues of columnar mucosa on endoscopy and pathognomonic Alcian-blue positive goblet cells on biopsy.

Gastroenterology.name: Mallory-Weiss Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Classic history of non-bloody forceful retching or vomiting, followed immediately by bright red acute hematemesis or coffee-ground emesis
Epigastric or retrosternal pain radiating to the back following repetitive emetic paroxysms
Melena, orthostatic lightheadedness, tachycardia, and hypotension in massive arterial bleeding (often associated with heavy binge alcohol consumption or bulimia)
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT / Angiography: Performed if active arterial extravasation persists; demonstrates active contrast blush originating from branches of the left gastric artery at the gastroesophageal junction without extraluminal gas (rules out transmural Boerhaave rupture)
pathology_manifestations: Upper Endoscopy (EGD - Diagnostic Gold Standard): Single or multiple longitudinal, linear, non-transmural mucosal and submucosal lacerations characteristically situated across the gastroesophageal junction or gastric cardia, typically measuring 1–4 cm in length, with active arterial spurting, oozing, fresh adherent clot, or a fibrinous base

Histopathology: Linear disruption extending through the mucosal epithelium and muscularis mucosae into the submucosal vascular plexus, accompanied by acute hemorrhage, fibrin deposition, and neutrophilic infiltration, with the muscularis propria remaining strictly intact
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Classic cause of upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage diagnosed immediately by the pathognomonic longitudinal linear mucosal tear across the gastroesophageal junction on upper endoscopy.

Gastroenterology.name: Dieulafoy Lesion
clinical_manifestations: Sudden, catastrophic, recurrent, and painless upper gastrointestinal bleeding presenting with massive hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia
Severe hemodynamic instability and hemorrhagic shock in an otherwise healthy patient without prior peptic ulcer symptoms or liver disease
Typically located in the proximal stomach along the lesser curvature within 6 cm of the gastroesophageal junction, but can occur ectopically in duodenum, colon, or rectum
radiological_manifestations: Catheter Angiography (Digital Subtraction Angiography): Contrast extravasation from an abnormally tortuous, non-tapering, wide-caliber submucosal artery arising from the left gastric artery without evidence of vascular malformation or tumor blush
pathology_manifestations: Upper Endoscopy (EGD - Primary Modality): Minute mucosal defect (typically 2–5 mm) with an actively arterial jet/spurting vessel or protruding pigmented vessel plug, surrounded by normal-appearing, smooth background mucosa without surrounding ulceration, mass, or inflammatory changes

Histopathology: Aberrantly large, tortuous, caliber-persistent artery (1–3 mm in diameter, 10 times normal mucosal capillary size) that fails to branch normally as it enters the submucosa and protrudes through a pinpoint mucosal erosion; normal arterial wall histology with internal elastic lamina preservation without vasculitis or atheroma
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct cause of catastrophic gastrointestinal hemorrhage identified by a solitary caliber-persistent arterial vessel spurting directly through normal mucosa without an ulcer crater.

Gastroenterology.name: Gastrointestinal Angiodysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent, painless lower gastrointestinal bleeding (hematochezia or maroon stools) or occult gastrointestinal bleeding presenting with iron deficiency anemia in elderly patients
Frequent association with severe aortic stenosis (Heyde syndrome: acquired von Willebrand syndrome type 2A from sheer stress destruction of vWF multimers by stenotic valve)
Chronic fatigue, pallor, and orthostatic dizziness requiring repeated blood transfusions
radiological_manifestations: Mesenteric Catheter Angiography: Early-filling, densely opacified, slowly emptying draining vein with an abnormal cluster of ectatic vessels in the cecal/ascending colon wall (pathognomonic vascular tuft)
CT Angiography: Hyperdense, tiny contrast blushes within the mucosal and submucosal layers of the cecum or right colon in arterial and venous phases
pathology_manifestations: Colonoscopy / Capsule Endoscopy: Distinct, flat or slightly raised, bright red, fern-like, stellate, or arborizing mucosal ectasias (typically 2–10 mm in diameter) composed of radiating tortuous microvessels emanating from a central feeding vessel, most frequently clustered in the cecum and ascending colon

Histopathology: Marked dilation and tortuosity of submucosal and mucosal veins and capillaries lined by a thin endothelial monolayer with little or no smooth muscle or elastic tissue, directly abutting the surface epithelium
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield vascular source of gastrointestinal bleeding in older adults displaying the classic arborizing coral-red fern-like vascular ectasias on colonoscopy.

Gastroenterology.name: Pneumatosis Cystoides Intestinalis
clinical_manifestations: Often asymptomatic and discovered incidentally; symptomatic cases feature abdominal cramping, diarrhea, excessive flatulence, and tenesmus
Painless hematochezia or passage of mucus when mucosal cysts erode
Benign pneumoperitoneum presenting without peritonitis or peritoneal signs when subserosal cysts rupture spontaneously into the abdominal cavity
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal CT (Imaging Modality of Choice): Pathognomonic clusters of multiple round, bubbly, or linear gas collections entirely confined within the bowel wall (submucosa or subserosa) without mucosal wall thickening or portal venous gas; concurrent pneumoperitoneum without inflammatory ascites confirms benign rupture
Plain Abdominal Radiography: Multiple radiolucent round gas-filled bubbles lining the bowel contours mimicking polyps ('ring around the bowel' or double-lumen appearance)
pathology_manifestations: Colonoscopy: Multiple soft, compressible, sessile, pale or bluish submucosal blebs/nodules resembling polyps that characteristically deflate with an audible 'pop' upon endoscopic biopsy forceps puncture

Histopathology: Multilocular, gas-filled cystic spaces situated within the submucosa or subserosa lined by attenuated endothelial-like cells or foreign body giant cells, accompanied by surrounding mild fibrosis and histiocytic reaction without neoplastic elements
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Unmistakable radiographic and endoscopic condition characterized by bubbly intramural air cysts that pop upon biopsy and can create dramatic non-surgical benign pneumoperitoneum.

Gastroenterology.name: Ischemic Colitis
clinical_manifestations: Sudden onset of crampy, mild-to-moderate left lower quadrant abdominal pain followed within 24 hours by an urgent desire to defecate and bloody diarrhea or bright red rectal bleeding
Preferential targeting of anatomical watershed regions: Griffiths point (splenic flexure) and Sudeck point (rectosigmoid junction)
Peritoneal signs (guarding, rigidity, rebound tenderness) heralding full-thickness colonic gangrene and perforation requiring emergent laparotomy
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Circumferential bowel wall thickening with the 'target sign' or 'halo sign' (inner and outer hyperdense rings sandwiching hypodense submucosal edema); pericolic fat stranding along the splenic flexure or descending colon; absence of wall enhancement or pneumatosis in gangrenous colitis
Barium Enema (Historical): Classic 'thumbprinting' sign produced by submucosal hemorrhage and severe edema projecting into the contrast column
pathology_manifestations: Colonoscopy (Diagnostic Modality of Choice): Sharply demarcated transition between diseased and normal mucosa; pale, edematous, dusky mucosa with petechial hemorrhages, friability, and linear ulcerations along the longitudinal axis of the colon ('single-stripe sign'); dark purple or black necrotic mucosa indicates irreversible transmural infarction

Histopathology: Mucosal necrosis, loss of surface epithelium with crypt 'withering' (atrophic, ghost-like microcrypts), extensive submucosal edema, hemorrhage, and microvascular fibrin thrombi in the lamina propria capillaries
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Most common intestinal vascular disorder, classically diagnosed by the endoscopic 'single-stripe sign' in watershed territories and radiographic thumbprinting.

Gastroenterology.name: Collagenous Colitis
clinical_manifestations: Chronic, watery, non-bloody diarrhea (typically 4–10 watery bowel movements per day), nocturnal diarrhea, and fecal urgency
Significant involuntary weight loss, abdominal cramping, and fatigue primarily affecting middle-aged and elderly females
Frequent association with autoimmune diseases (celiac disease, Hashimoto thyroiditis, rheumatoid arthritis) and offending medications (NSAIDs, PPIs, SSRIs)
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal CT: Typically completely normal, confirming absence of gross transmural inflammation or wall thickening, which aids in ruling out conventional Crohn's or ulcerative colitis
pathology_manifestations: Colonoscopy: Colonic mucosa appears endoscopically normal in the vast majority; occasionally reveals subtle mucosal lacerations, linear tears, or mucosal fractures provoked by air insufflation ('cat-scratch colon')

Histopathology (Biopsy - Diagnostic Gold Standard): Thick, continuous subepithelial collagen band >10 µm in thickness (normal <3 µm) immediately underlying the surface basement membrane, highlighted brilliantly on Masson trichrome stain; accompanied by surface epithelial detachment/sloughing, increased lamina propria lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, and intraepithelial lymphocytosis
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct form of microscopic colitis featuring the dramatic endoscopic 'cat-scratch' mucosa and the pathognomonic thickened subepithelial collagen band on Masson trichrome staining.

Gastroenterology.name: Acute Colonic Pseudo-Obstruction
clinical_manifestations: Massive, painless or mildly tender abdominal distension evolving over several days in hospitalized or postoperative patients (orthopedic, pelvic, or cardiac surgery)
Nausea, obstipation, and vomiting with tympanic abdominal percussion and hyperactive or absent bowel sounds
Localized right lower quadrant peritonitis, fever, and leukocytosis signaling impending or actual cecal perforation (imminent when cecal diameter exceeds 10–12 cm)
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Plain Radiograph (Kidney-Ureter-Bladder / KUB): Massive, continuous gaseous dilation of the colon, with the cecum typically dilated >9–12 cm, preserved haustrations, and smooth cutoff near the splenic flexure

Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Massive dilation of the cecum, ascending colon, and transverse colon with a distinct anatomical transition zone near the splenic flexure in the strict absence of any mechanical obstructing intraluminal mass, stricture, or volvulus; demonstrates bowel wall thinning, pneumatosis, and free air if perforation occurs
pathology_manifestations: Colonoscopy (Diagnostic and Decompressive): Striking dilation of the colonic lumen with thin, stretched mucosal folds and absence of obstructing neoplasm, stricture, or extrinsic compression; direct visualization of mucosal viability (ischemia seen as dusky bluish discoloration requiring emergent cessation of air insufflation)

Histopathology (when resected for perforation): Thinning and ischemic necrosis of the muscularis propria and mucosa with microvascular thrombosis and mucosal sloughing, without underlying mechanical luminal obstruction
Gastroenterology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield functional emergency characterized by monstrous gaseous colonic dilation without mechanical obstruction, visually diagnostic on abdominal plain films and CT.

Hematology.name: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia
clinical_manifestations: Catastrophic disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) / hyperfibrinolysis: Massive, diffuse, spontaneous ecchymoses, extensive deep hematomas, cutaneous purpura fulminans, and persistent oozing from all venipuncture, intravenous catheter, and mucosal sites

Mucosal hemorrhages: Profuse, recurrent, life-threatening epistaxis, extensive bleeding of the gingiva and oral mucosa, subconjunctival hemorrhages, and gastrointestinal / genitourinary bleeding (gross hematuria, menorrhagia)

Acute intracranial hemorrhage signs: Sudden catastrophic neurological deterioration (lethargy, severe headache, focal hemispheric deficits, decerebrate posturing) resulting from multifocal intraparenchymal or subarachnoid hemorrhage

Differentiation syndrome (ATRA/ATO syndrome): High fever, acute respiratory distress with hypoxia, diffuse episodic weight gain, generalized peripheral edema, and episodic hypotension occurring during targeted induction therapy
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Head CT: Acute, high-attenuation, multifocal intracranial hemorrhages (intraparenchymal, subdural, and subarachnoid hemorrhages) with prominent surrounding vasogenic edema, mass effect, midline shift, and herniation risk

High-Resolution Chest CT / Radiography: In Differentiation Syndrome: bilateral diffuse reticulonodular ground-glass opacities, alveolar consolidation with air bronchograms, peribronchovascular cuffing, bilateral pleural effusions, and cardiomegaly/pericardial effusion; pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage presenting as diffuse bilateral perihilar ground-glass haziness
Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Mild-to-moderate splenomegaly and hepatomegaly without bulky lymphadenopathy; renal cortical hemorrhages or retroperitoneal hematomas
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral blood and bone marrow aspirate (Pathognomonic Gold Standard): Predominance (>=20-30%) of abnormal, heavily granulated, atypical promyelocytes with reniform, bilobed, or folded nuclei and abundant dense, dark pink-to-purple azurophilic granules obscuring the nuclear-cytoplasmic junction; pathognomonic 'faggot cells': promyelocytes containing multiple, bundled Auer rods stacked in parallel like a bundle of twigs/firewood (faggot); microgranular (hypogranular) variant (AML M3v) displays characteristic bilobed or butterfly-shaped 'spectacle' nuclei with fine, dust-like granules; Cytochemistry: Intensely, diffusely positive for myeloperoxidase (MPO) and Sudan Black B; IHC: CD33+, CD117+, CD13+, with characteristic negativity for CD34 and HLA-DR (aberrant immature myeloid phenotype); Molecular / Cytogenetics: Obligate balanced reciprocal translocation t(15;17)(q24;q21), generating the oncogenic PML::RARA fusion gene detectable by rapid reverse transcription-PCR (RT-PCR) or fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal hematologic emergency defined by dramatic clinical DIC purpura fulminans and mucosal hemorrhages, life-threatening intracranial hemorrhage on emergent head CT, and pathognomonic 'faggot cells' packed with stacked Auer rods harboring t(15;17) PML-RARA.

Hematology.name: Beta-Thalassemia Major
clinical_manifestations: Classic 'Chipmunk' / 'Cooley' Facies: Striking craniofacial distortion caused by extreme, ineffective erythropoiesis and compensatory marrow expansion in the skull and facial bones: prominent frontal and parietal bossing, depression of the nasal bridge (saddle nose), marked bilateral maxillary hyperplasia leading to protruding cheekbones, overgrowth of the upper jaw, and severe dental malocclusion with prominent protruding incisors

Massive hepatosplenomegaly & abdominal distension: Immense, protuberant abdomen contrasting with thin, wasted limbs; hard, massive splenomegaly reaching the iliac crest and crossing the midline; firm hepatomegaly resulting from chronic extramedullary hematopoiesis and progressive transfusion-related hemosiderosis

Cutaneous pigmentary changes & leg ulcers: Characteristic muddy-bronze, greenish-brown, or yellow-brown skin discoloration resulting from the combination of chronic jaundice (unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia) and diffuse melanin/hemosiderin deposition; chronic, painful, non-healing indolent ulcers over the medial and lateral malleoli of the ankles

Severe growth failure & hypogonadism: Marked short stature, failure to thrive in infancy, delayed puberty, primary amenorrhea, and absent secondary sexual characteristics resulting from iron-overload-induced anterior hypopituitarism
radiological_manifestations: Skull Plain Radiography (Pathognomonic 'Hair-on-End' Sign): Striking widening of the diploic space with marked thinning or disappearance of the outer table of the calvarium, accompanied by fine, vertical, needle-like bony spicules radiating outward perpendicular to the inner table, creating the classic 'crew-cut' or 'hair-on-end' appearance

Hand / Extremity Plain Radiographs: Marked expansion of medullary cavities in metacarpals and proximal phalanges, with severe cortical thinning, loss of normal diaphyseal concavity, and coarsened, thinned trabecular pattern creating a 'lace-like' or 'honeycomb' mosaic appearance

Thoracic & Spinal MRI / CT (Extramedullary Hematopoietic Pseudotumors): Well-demarcated, lobulated, homogeneous soft-tissue masses in the posterior mediastinum and bilateral paraspinal gutters, with intermediate-to-high signal on T1 and T2, without bony erosion, potentially compressing the spinal cord; cardiac and liver T2* MRI demonstrates profound signal drop and shortening (T2* <10-20 ms) indicating life-threatening myocardial and hepatic iron overload
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear: Severe microcytic hypochromic anemia (hemoglobin often <6-7 g/dL without transfusion, MCV <65 fL); striking anisopoikilocytosis; abundant target cells (codocytes) with 'bull's-eye' hemoglobin distribution; numerous nucleated red blood cells (erythroblasts); coarse basophilic stippling, Pappenheimer bodies (iron granules), and teardrop cells (dacrocytes)

Bone Marrow Aspirate & Biopsy: Dramatic erythroid hyperplasia with complete reversal of the normal myeloid-to-erythroid (M:E) ratio (from normal 3:1 to 1:10 or 1:20); intense dyserythropoiesis characterized by nuclear-cytoplasmic dyssynchrony, nuclear budding, multinucleation, and premature erythroblast apoptosis (ineffective erythropoiesis); Prussian blue staining reveals marked ring sideroblasts and heavily laden reticuloendothelial macrophages

Hemoglobin Electrophoresis / High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC): Diagnostic profile showing near-total or complete absence of adult hemoglobin (HbA: 0-10%), markedly elevated fetal hemoglobin (HbF: 70-95%), and variable or slightly elevated hemoglobin A2 (HbA2); molecular genetics identifies homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the HBB gene on chromosome 11 (e.g., codon 39 nonsense, IVS-I-110, or IVS-I-1 splice-site mutations)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic severe congenital hemoglobinopathy defined physically by classic 'chipmunk facies' and muddy-bronze skin, immortalized radiologically by the calvarial 'hair-on-end' sign and paraspinal extramedullary pseudotumors, and confirmed by target cells on smear and HbF predominance on electrophoresis.

Hematology.name: Burkitt Lymphoma
clinical_manifestations: Endemic (African) variant: Rapidly enlarging, massive, disfiguring painless tumor of the jaw, mandible, maxilla, or orbit; loosening and gross displacement of teeth with alveolar ridge expansion; severe facial asymmetry, unilateral exophthalmos/proptosis, and distortion of facial architecture

Sporadic (non-endemic) variant: Massive palpable, firm, non-tender abdominal or pelvic mass; rapid abdominal distension with gross ascites; ileocecal mass presenting as acute abdomen or bowel obstruction / intussusception in children or young adults

Constitutional symptoms: High-grade fever, drenching night sweats, profound weight loss (B symptoms); extreme rapid tumor growth (shortest doubling time of any human tumor, ~24-48 hours) resulting in early tumor lysis syndrome signs
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI of Head and Neck: Massive soft-tissue mass centered in the mandible or maxilla causing extensive osteolytic bone destruction, aggressive periosteal reaction, cortical breakthrough, tooth displacement ('floating teeth' in jaw mass), and expansion into maxillary antrum, nasal cavity, and orbit

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal/Pelvic CT: Bulky, homogeneous or heterogeneous soft-tissue masses originating in the ileocecal region, mesentery, retroperitoneum, or ovaries; frequent ileocolic intussusception with classic 'target' or 'doughnut' sign on cross-sectional imaging; massive low-attenuation ascites, peritoneal carcinomatosis/nodularity, and organ displacement without significant biliary or vascular invasion ('sandwich sign' of mesenteric vessels)

Whole-Body 18F-FDG PET/CT: Intensely, homogeneously hypermetabolic masses with extraordinarily elevated maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax often >25-30), readily differentiating viable lymphoma from necrosis and mapping rapid systemic dissemination
pathology_manifestations: Tissue biopsy / touch imprint: Highly cellular diffuse proliferation of medium-sized, monotonous, non-cleaved B lymphocytes with round nuclei, clumped coarse chromatin, multiple (2-5) prominent basophilic nucleoli, and deeply basophilic cytoplasm containing fine lipid-filled vacuoles (visible on Oil Red O or Giemsa); pathognomonic 'starry-sky' low-power appearance created by numerous tingible-body macrophages containing ingested apoptotic nuclear debris scattered amongst the dark sheets of proliferating tumor cells; extremely high mitotic and apoptotic rate with Ki-67 proliferation index virtually 100%; IHC: CD20+, CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2 negative, c-MYC strong uniform nuclear positivity; Cytogenetics: pathognomonic reciprocal translocation t(8;14)(q24;q32) placing the MYC proto-oncogene under the control of the immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) promoter, or less commonly t(2;8) or t(8;22)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic ultra-high-grade hematologic malignancy presenting with grotesque facial jaw distortion (endemic) or massive abdominal intussusception masses (sporadic), paired with bulky retroperitoneal/ileocecal CT masses, extreme PET hypermetabolism (Ki-67 ~100%), and pathognomonic 'starry-sky' c-MYC-driven histology.

Hematology.name: Castleman Disease
clinical_manifestations: Unicentric Castleman Disease (UCD): Asymptomatic, large, firm, non-tender, slow-growing, solitary palpable mass in the neck, axilla, or groin; compressive symptoms from mediastinal or pelvic retroperitoneal masses (stridor, cough, hydronephrosis)

Idiopathic Multicentric Castleman Disease (iMCD): Widespread, symmetric, generalized palpable lymphadenopathy; massive extravascular fluid overload with generalized anasarca, tense ascites, and severe peripheral pitting edema; TAFRO syndrome: Thrombocytopenia, Anasarca, Fever, Reticulin myelofibrosis, and Organomegaly (hepatosplenomegaly); multiple violaceous cherry angiomas, violaceous papules, and hyperpigmentation; systemic inflammatory symptoms (fever, night sweats, wasting)
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Chest / Abdominal CT (Unicentric / Hyaline-Vascular Type): Solitary, sharply marginated, rounded or lobulated nodal mass exhibiting intense, brilliant, homogeneous arterial-phase contrast enhancement (mimicking a hypervascular neuroendocrine tumor or paraganglioma); characteristic internal branching or radiating low-attenuation fibrous bands producing a 'spoke-wheel' vascular pattern; discrete, coarse, punctate or arborizing central calcifications in 5-10% of cases

Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI (Multicentric Type): Extensive, diffuse, bilateral, multi-station lymphadenopathy (cervical, axillary, mediastinal, mesenteric, retroperitoneal, pelvic) with moderate-to-marked enhancement; profound polyserositis (massive bilateral pleural effusions, pericardial effusion, high-volume ascites), hepatosplenomegaly, and retroperitoneal perinephric fat stranding
18F-FDG PET/CT: Moderate-to-high FDG uptake (SUVmax 3-8) throughout involved nodal basins, reflecting polyclonal lymphoid proliferation and hypervascularity
pathology_manifestations: Excisional lymph node biopsy: (1) Hyaline-Vascular Variant (90% of UCD): Expanded mantle zones composed of concentric, onion-skin-like rings of small, mature mantle zone lymphocytes surrounding depleted, atrophic, regressively transformed germinal centers; pathognomonic 'lollipop lesion': penetrating, radially directed, hyalinized, thick-walled capillaries entering atrophic germinal centers, accompanied by follicular dendritic cell (FDC) hyperplasia and expanded CD21+/CD35+ meshworks; twin or multiple germinal centers within a single mantle zone; (2) Plasma Cell Variant (dominant in MCD): Hyperplastic, enlarged germinal centers surrounded by massive sheets of mature, polyclonal plasma cells expanding the interfollicular and medullary cords; absence of light chain restriction (polyclonal kappa and lambda by in situ hybridization); HHV-8 latency-associated nuclear antigen (LANA-1) staining differentiates HHV-8-associated MCD from HHV-8-negative iMCD; elevated serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) drives systemic inflammation and vascular proliferation
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive lymphoproliferative entity exhibiting prominent palpable nodal masses and severe TAFRO anasarca, diagnosed on CT by brilliant hypervascular enhancement with 'spoke-wheel' architecture, and by 'onion-skin' mantle zones with 'lollipop' hyalinized penetrating vessels on histology.

Hematology.name: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma
clinical_manifestations: Superficial lymphadenopathy: Visible, palpable, asymmetric, painless, firm, rubbery, discrete, non-tender enlargement of lymph nodes in the anterior cervical chain (60-70%) and supraclavicular fossae ('sentinel nodes' / Virchow's node); nodes feel like 'rubbery pencil erasers' and move freely without overlying skin erythema

Superior Vena Cava (SVC) Syndrome: Visible engorgement and tortuosity of superficial collateral veins across the anterior chest wall and neck, facial and periorbital edema, conjunctival suffusion, and facial plethora accentuated by forward bending or raising arms above the head (Pemberton sign)

Constitutional & sensory signs: Pel-Ebstein fever (cyclical, high-grade spikes lasting 1-2 weeks separated by afebrile intervals); alcohol-induced nodal pain (severe, aching pain localized to involved lymph nodes within minutes of drinking alcohol); intractable generalized pruritus with prominent excoriations and prurigo nodularis
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT: Bulky anterior mediastinal and prevascular nodal mass (>10 cm maximum transverse diameter or >1/3 of the internal transverse thoracic diameter), with smooth or lobulated contours, displacing the trachea and compressing the superior vena cava; retrosternal space obliteration; continuous contiguous lymphatic spread involving subcarinal, hilar, and internal mammary stations

Whole-Body 18F-FDG PET/CT (Deauville Criteria Gold Standard): Intense, avid glucose uptake (SUVmax typically 10-25) in contiguous nodal groups above and below the diaphragm and in the spleen; essential for baseline Ann Arbor staging and interim/end-of-treatment metabolic response assessment
Abdominal/Pelvic CT: Multiple enlarged, homogeneous retroperitoneal (para-aortic, interaortocaval) and iliac lymph nodes; focal hypodense splenic nodules or diffuse homogeneous splenomegaly
pathology_manifestations: Excisional lymph node biopsy: Classical nodular sclerosis subtype (70-80% of cases) characterized by broad collagenous, birefringent fibrous bands that extend from the thickened lymph node capsule and subdivide the lymphoid parenchyma into discrete cellular nodules; pathognomonic diagnostic Reed-Sternberg (RS) cells: gigantic binucleated or multinucleated neoplastic cells with abundant amphophilic cytoplasm, mirror-image ('owl-eyed') lobulated nuclei, each containing a gigantic, inclusion-like eosinophilic nucleolus surrounded by a clear halo; classic lacunar variants (RS cells with retraction artifacts creating empty spaces around the cell) prominent in formalin-fixed tissue; RS cells constitute only 1-2% of the tissue, embedded in an abundant, non-neoplastic reactive inflammatory background composed of small T-lymphocytes (rosetting around RS cells), eosinophils, plasma cells, and histiocytes; IHC: Reed-Sternberg cells are intensely positive for CD30 (membrane and Golgi dot pattern) and CD15 (>80%), weak/variable nuclear positivity for PAX5, negative for CD45 (LCA), and negative or weak for CD20
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal hematologic neoplasm presenting with visible rubbery cervical adenopathy, alcohol-induced nodal pain, and SVC collaterals, imaged as massive 'bulky' anterior mediastinal masses on CT, and confirmed by 'owl-eyed' Reed-Sternberg cells within nodular collagen bands on CD30+ histology.

Hematology.name: Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma
clinical_manifestations: Mycosis fungoides sequential stages: (1) Patch stage: flat, erythematous, cigarette-paper-wrinkled scaling macules in sun-protected 'bathing-suit' areas; (2) Plaque stage: infiltrated, well-demarcated, violaceous or indurated annular plaques; (3) Tumor stage: large, exophytic, ulcerated, mushroom-like red-brown nodules and tumors
Sézary syndrome: generalized intense exfoliative erythroderma ('red man syndrome'), palmoplantar keratoderma with painful fissuring, diffuse alopecia, severe ectropion, and intractable pruritus
Facies leontina in advanced facial plaque infiltration
radiological_manifestations: Whole-Body 18F-FDG PET/CT: Staging of extracutaneous nodal and visceral dissemination (hypermetabolic axillary/inguinal lymphadenopathy, visceral organ involvement in advanced stages)
Chest and Abdominopelvic CT: Assessment of deep retroperitoneal lymph node architecture and hepatosplenomegaly
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy: Epidermotropism of atypical, hyperchromatic CD4+ T lymphocytes without spongiosis; lymphocytes aligning along the basal layer with haloed clear borders; pathognomonic intraepidermal collections of atypical lymphocytes ('Pautrier microabscesses'); cerebriform (brain-like) indented nuclei (Sézary-Lutzner cells); peripheral blood smear in Sézary syndrome shows circulating atypical lymphocytes with convoluted cerebriform nuclei
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Classic malignant dermatologic-hematologic condition with iconic patch/plaque/mushroom tumor progression, erythroderma, and ectropion paired with whole-body PET/CT staging.

Hematology.name: Diamond-Blackfan Anemia
Hematology.subspecialty: Inherited Bone Marrow Failure Syndromes / Pure Red Cell Aplasias
clinical_manifestations: Severe infantile pallor & lethargy: Profound normocytic or macrocytic anemia presenting typically within the first 2-6 months of life (frequently with hemoglobin <5-6 g/dL) manifesting as porcelain-white skin pallor, tachypnea, tachycardia, poor feeding, and lethargy, in the absence of jaundice or organomegaly

Craniofacial dysmorphism ('Cathie facies'): Distinctive dysmorphic facial features in ~50% of patients, including hypertelorism, broad flat nasal bridge, micrognathia, high-arched or cleft palate, microcephaly, and low-set ears
Upper extremity malformations: Triphalangeal thumbs (pathognomonic visual phenotypic feature), subluxated or bifid thumbs, hypoplastic thenar eminences, or duplication of thumb phalanges
Webbed neck & short stature: Pterygium colli (prominent lateral skin folds of the neck resembling Turner syndrome), short neck, low posterior hairline, and post-natal growth retardation
radiological_manifestations: Hand and Wrist Radiographs: Bilateral or unilateral triphalangeal thumbs containing three phalanges rather than two, with an extra trapezoidal or rectangular ossification center in the proximal or middle phalanx; hypoplasia of thenar soft tissues; occasionally radial hypoplasia or duplicated phalanges
Echocardiography: Congenital heart defects in ~30% of patients, prominently ventricular septal defect (VSD), atrial septal defect (ASD), coarctation of the aorta, or tetralogy of Fallot
Renal Ultrasound: Structural urinary tract malformations including horseshoe kidney, duplicated collecting systems, or absent single kidney
pathology_manifestations: Bone Marrow Aspirate / Biopsy (Gold-Standard Pathological Hallmark): Profound, selective erythroid hypoplasia or near-total absence of erythroid precursors (erythroblastopenia, typically erythroid precursors <1-5% of total nucleated cells), with normal cellularity and normal maturation of myeloid (granulocytic) and megakaryocytic lineages; absence of dysplastic ring sideroblasts or megaloblastoid changes

Laboratory & Biochemical Markers: Markedly elevated erythrocyte adenosine deaminase (eADA) activity present in >80-85% of affected individuals; significantly elevated fetal hemoglobin (HbF) and persistent i-antigen expression on red cells; isolated macrocytic anemia (elevated MCV) with severe reticulocytopenia (<0.5%)

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous loss-of-function pathogenic mutations or large deletions in ribosomal protein genes affecting the small (40S) or large (60S) ribosomal subunits, most commonly RPS19 (~25% of cases), RPL5, RPL11 (frequently associated with cleft palate and thumb anomalies), RPS26, or RPL35A
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal congenital pure red cell aplasia marked by severe infantile pallor, Cathie facies, webbed neck, and triphalangeal thumbs on physical inspection and hand radiographs, pathologically characterized by isolated marrow erythroblastopenia with preserved myeloid/megakaryocytic lines and elevated erythrocyte ADA.

Hematology.name: Dyskeratosis Congenita
Hematology.subspecialty: Inherited Bone Marrow Failure Syndromes / Telomeropathies
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Mucocutaneous Diagnostic Triad (Present in >85-90%): (1) Reticulated, lacy, mottled, grayish-brown cutaneous hyperpigmentation predominantly distributed across the neck, upper chest, shoulders, and face, often producing a classic 'dirty neck' appearance with interspersed hypopigmented atrophic macules; (2) Severe progressive nail dystrophy: progressive longitudinal ridging, splitting, thinning, and brittleness of fingernails and toenails, evolving into pterygium unguis (inward growth of proximal nail fold) and eventual complete loss of nail plates (anonychia); (3) Premalignant oral mucosal leukoplakia: thickened, painless, persistent, adherent white patches and plaques on the dorsal and lateral surfaces of the tongue, buccal mucosa, and gingiva, carrying a high lifetime risk of transformation into aggressive squamous cell carcinoma

Additional phenotypic features: Premature canities (early graying of hair in childhood or adolescence), androgenic alopecia, continuous tearing (epiphora) resulting from nasolacrimal duct stenosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, and loss of dermatoglyphics

Bone Marrow Failure & Bleeding: Progressive pancytopenia emerging typically in late childhood or young adulthood causing mucosal bleeding, petechiae, ecchymoses, severe fatigue, and opportunistic infections
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT (HRCT): Progressive pulmonary fibrosis (a primary cause of mortality): bilateral subpleural and basilar reticular opacities, traction bronchiectasis, interlobular septal thickening, and subpleural honeycombing resembling idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) or fibrotic non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP)

Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Signs of cryptogenic cirrhosis, hepatic fibrosis, and portal hypertension, including nodular shrunken liver contour, splenomegaly, ascites, and portosystemic collaterals; pulmonary arteriovenous malformations or hepatopulmonary syndrome signs

Skeletal Plain Radiography / MRI: Severe premature osteopenia and osteoporosis in children or young adults; recurrent avascular necrosis / osteonecrosis of the femoral and humeral heads with subchondral collapse; skeletal hypoplasia and scoliosis
pathology_manifestations: Diagnostic Telomere Length Flow-FISH: Quantitative fluorescence in situ hybridization coupled with flow cytometry (flow-FISH) of peripheral blood leukocytes (lymphocytes and granulocytes) demonstrates pathognomonic, profound telomere shortening (<1st percentile for age-matched controls, the diagnostic gold standard)

Bone Marrow Trephine Biopsy: Progressive hypocellular bone marrow failure: marked loss of hematopoietic elements with replacement by mature adipocytes (fat marrow) without dysplastic blasts or clonal cytogenetic markers, indistinguishable morphologically from idiopathic severe aplastic anemia

Oral Leukoplakia & Skin Biopsy: Biopsy of mucosal leukoplakic plaques reveals prominent hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, acanthosis, chronic subepithelial inflammation, and progressive cellular atypia / epithelial dysplasia (mild to severe) requiring serial surveillance for malignant transformation; skin biopsy shows basal layer hyperpigmentation with pigmentary incontinence and dermal melanophages

Molecular Genetics: Identification of pathogenic germline mutations in telomere maintenance and telomerase complex genes: X-linked recessive DKC1 (dyskerin, ~30% of cases), autosomal dominant or recessive TERC (telomerase RNA component), TERT (telomerase reverse transcriptase), TINF2 (shelterin component), RTEL1, NOP10, or NHP2
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Premier inherited telomeropathy diagnosed clinically by the unmistakable mucocutaneous triad ('dirty neck' lacy pigmentation, nail pterygium/anonychia, oral leukoplakia), evidenced radiologically by basal honeycombing pulmonary fibrosis and avascular necrosis, and proven by flow-FISH telomeres <1st percentile.

Hematology.name: Erdheim-Chester Disease
clinical_manifestations: Ophthalmic and facial signs: Bilateral, symmetric, yellowish plaques on eyelids and periorbital regions (periorbital xanthelasma); progressive, bilateral, painless, non-pulsatile exophthalmos (proptosis) with retro-orbital fullness and diplopia
Cutaneous findings: Yellowish-brown, lipid-rich xanthomatous macules, papules, and indurated plaques over the face, neck, and flexural areas
Musculoskeletal complaints: Chronic, dull, deep, aching bone pain affecting the lower extremities (knees, shins, thighs), worsened by ambulation

Neuroendocrine manifestations: Central diabetes insipidus (polyuria, polydipsia), cerebellar ataxia, dysarthria, and pyramidal signs due to infratentorial brainstem/cerebellar histiocytic infiltration
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography / Skeletal CT (Pathognomonic Hallmark): Bilateral, symmetrical, diametaphyseal cortical osteosclerosis of the long tubular bones (distal femur, proximal and distal tibia, fibula), with characteristic sparing of the epiphyses; thick, irregular, endosteal and periosteal cortical hyperostosis narrowing the medullary cavity

99mTc Bone Scintigraphy (Pathognomonic 'Hot Knees'): Striking, symmetric, intensely increased radiotracer uptake in the diaphyses and metaphyses of the distal femora and proximal/distal tibiae ('hot knees' and 'hot ankles')

Abdominal CT / MRI (Pathognomonic 'Hairy Kidney' and 'Coated Aorta'): Symmetrical, infiltrating, homogeneous soft-tissue rind encasing the perirenal spaces and renal fascial boundaries ('hairy kidney' sign); circumferential, continuous periaortic soft-tissue infiltration extending from thoracic to abdominal aorta ('coated aorta' sign); soft-tissue infiltration of the right atrium ('pseudotumor' of the right atrial wall/sulcus)
pathology_manifestations: Bone / perinephric / skin biopsy: Xanthogranulomatous infiltration characterized by sheets of large, lipid-laden, foamy histiocytes (xanthoma cells) surrounded by dense, lamellar fibrosis, sparse Touton-type multinucleated giant cells, and mixed lymphocytes and plasma cells; IHC: Histiocytes strongly positive for CD68 and CD163; negative for CD1a and Langerin (CD207); S100 negative or only weakly/focally positive; Molecular: BRAF V600E somatic activating mutation identified in >55-65% of patients (responsive to BRAF/MEK inhibitors); alternate MAP kinase pathway mutations (MAP2K1, KRAS, NRAS) in remaining cases
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Premier visual multisystem histiocytosis featuring bilateral xanthelasma and exophthalmos matched with three world-famous radiological hallmarks: symmetric long bone diametaphyseal sclerosis ('hot knees'), 'hairy kidney' perirenal infiltration, and the 'coated aorta'.

Hematology.name: Fanconi Anemia
clinical_manifestations: Radial ray defects & upper limb anomalies (pathognomonic visual signs): Unilateral or bilateral absent thumbs, hypoplastic or bifid ('floating') thumbs, triphalangeal thumbs, rudimentary thenar eminences, or complete absence/hypoplasia of the radius causing acute radial deviation of the hand and wrist ('radial club hand')

Cutaneous pigmentary changes: Generalized patchy cutaneous hyperpigmentation ('rain-drop' pigmentation on trunk, neck, and flexures) and multiple, well-circumscribed café-au-lait macules (>3-5 macules) scattered across the trunk, abdomen, and groin

Craniofacial and growth abnormalities: Striking proportionate microcephaly, characteristic triangular 'bird-like' facies, microphthalmia, epicanthal folds, low-set ears, deafness, and profound pre- and post-natal short stature (<3rd percentile)
Urogenital abnormalities: Micropenis, undescended testes (cryptorchidism), and hypospadias in males; bicornuate uterus or vaginal atresia in females

Marrow failure signs: Severe pallor, generalized petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, epistaxis, and recurring bacterial/fungal infections emerging typically between 5 and 10 years of age due to progressive trilineage marrow failure
radiological_manifestations: Upper Extremity Plain Radiographs: Complete absence or hypoplasia of the radius; absent, hypoplastic, or bifid first metacarpal and thumb phalanges; hypoplasia of carpal bones (particularly scaphoid and trapezium); synostosis of forearm bones

Renal Ultrasound / CT: Structural congenital urinary tract anomalies in 25-30% of patients, including horseshoe kidney, unilateral renal agenesis, ectopic/pelvic kidney, duplicated collecting systems, or severe hydronephrosis
Skeletal / Pelvic Radiographs: Congenital hip dislocation, hypoplastic pelvis, vertebral anomalies (hemivertebrae, butterfly vertebrae, scoliosis), and rib synostosis
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood & Bone Marrow: Macrocytic red blood cells with markedly elevated mean corpuscular volume (MCV >100-110 fL) preceding cytopenias; elevated fetal hemoglobin (HbF); progressive bone marrow hypocellularity evolving into complete marrow aplasia, where hematopoietic tissue is replaced almost entirely by mature adipocytes (fat marrow) without dysplasia initially

Diagnostic Gold-Standard Chromosome Breakage Analysis: Peripheral blood lymphocytes cultured with DNA interstrand cross-linking agents—diepoxybutane (DEB) or mitomycin C (MMC)—demonstrate striking, pathognomonic chromosomal breakage, chromatid gaps, exchanges, multiradial chromosomes (tri- and quadriradial figures), and end-to-end fusions

Molecular Genetics: Biallelic (or X-linked in FANCB / autosomal dominant in RAD51) pathogenic mutations in FA/BRCA DNA repair pathway genes (FANCA responsible for ~60-65% of cases, followed by FANCC, FANCG, and BRCA2/FANCD1)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Premier inherited chromosomal instability and bone marrow failure syndrome defined bedside by striking radial ray deformities (radial club hand, absent thumbs) and café-au-lait spots, confirmed radiologically by absent radii and horseshoe kidneys, and definitively proven by pathognomonic diepoxybutane (DEB) chromosomal breakage multiradials.

Hematology.name: Gaucher Disease Type 1
clinical_manifestations: Colossal protuberant hepatosplenomegaly: Massive abdominal distension driven by tremendous, firm, non-tender splenomegaly (often 15 to 20 times normal volume, crossing the abdominal midline and descending into the left lower quadrant and true pelvis), causing early satiety, mechanical abdominal discomfort, and secondary hypersplenism; moderate-to-severe firm hepatomegaly
