Bleeding diathesis and cutaneous manifestations: Widespread petechial rash, spontaneous purpuric lesions, extensive ecchymoses, and recurrent mucocutaneous hemorrhage (profuse epistaxis, gingival bleeding, menorrhagia) directly caused by severe hypersplenism-induced thrombocytopenia; diffuse yellow-brown or bronze hyperpigmentation of the facial skin and pretibial anterior lower legs; yellowish-brown, triangular/wedge-shaped bulbar conjunctival deposits (pingueculae) adjacent to the medial or lateral corneal limbus

Debilitating skeletal crises: Acute, agonizing, localized bone crises characterized by excruciating deep bone pain, localized soft-tissue erythema, warmth, and exquisite periosteal tenderness (frequently mimicking acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis), predominantly targeting the distal femur, proximal tibia, or vertebrae; accompanied by low-grade fever, chronic debilitating arthralgias, and stunted growth in children
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Radiography: Pathognomonic 'Erlenmeyer flask' deformity (tubulation defect characterized by abnormal flaring and failure of normal remodeling/constriction of the distal femoral metaphyses and distal tibiae, with cortical thinning); generalized skeletal osteopenia, endosteal scalloping, cortical thinning, and punched-out focal osteolytic lesions

Skeletal MRI (T1, T2, and Short Tau Inversion Recovery [STIR]): Marked diffuse loss of bone marrow signal intensity on both T1- and T2-weighted sequences due to extensive replacement of normal fat-containing marrow by glucocerebroside-laden Gaucher cells ('dark marrow' pattern); ischemic complications including avascular necrosis / osteonecrosis of femoral heads (crescent sign, subchondral collapse, and secondary osteoarthritis), acute bone infarcts with serpiginous sclerotic borders, and diffuse periostitis with marrow edema during acute crises

Abdominal Ultrasound / CT / MRI: Colossal splenomegaly with homogeneous or heterogeneous parenchyma, containing discrete hypoechoic or hypoattenuating nodular aggregates ('Gaucheromas' or splenomas) and wedge-shaped non-enhancing splenic infarcts; diffuse hepatomegaly with perivascular low attenuation and frequent cholelithiasis in young adults
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow aspirate and core biopsy: Diagnostic hallmark 'Gaucher cells' (lipid-engorged histiocytes/macrophages measuring 20 to 100 micrometers in diameter) possessing small, eccentrically placed, round nuclei and abundant, pale, basophilic-to-pink cytoplasm characterized by a pathognomonic fibrillar, striated texture resembling 'wrinkled tissue paper' or 'crumpled silk' (produced by electron-dense parallel arrays of tubular glucocerebroside aggregates within dilated lysosomes)

Cytochemical and special stains: Gaucher cells stain intensely positive with Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and remain resistant to diastase digestion; strongly positive for Tartrate-Resistant Acid Phosphatase (TRAP); positive with Prussian blue staining for intracellular iron deposits

Biochemical and Molecular Genetics: Severely deficient beta-glucocerebrosidase (acid beta-glucosidase) enzymatic activity in peripheral blood leukocytes or cultured skin fibroblasts (<15% of normal control activity); markedly elevated serum chitotriosidase, chemokine ligand 18 (CCL18/PARC), and glucosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb1, the primary monitoring biomarker); definitive diagnosis confirmed by biallelic pathogenic mutations in the GBA1 gene (most commonly N370S / p.Asn409Ser in Ashkenazi Jewish kindreds, alongside L444P / p.Leu483Pro)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic lysosomal storage disease presenting with massive, protuberant organomegaly, severe cytopenias, and excruciating bone pain crises, paired with pathognomonic skeletal 'Erlenmeyer flask' metadiaphyseal flaring on plain radiography, dark T1 marrow replacement on MRI, and diagnostic bone marrow Gaucher cells with 'wrinkled tissue paper' fibrillar cytoplasm.

Hematology.name: Hairy Cell Leukemia
clinical_manifestations: Massive splenomegaly: Enormous, firm, non-tender spleen palpable deep into the left lower quadrant or pelvis, producing a visible left-sided abdominal bulge, marked early satiety, dragging abdominal fullness, and left flank pain

Severe pancytopenia findings: Striking waxy pallor of skin and mucous membranes (normocytic normochromic anemia); petechiae, purpura, and easy bruising across lower extremities (severe thrombocytopenia); frequent opportunistic infections (disseminated atypical mycobacteria, Legionella, fungi) due to profound monocytopenia and neutropenia
Cutaneous manifestations: Cutaneous leukemic infiltrates (red-violaceous papules and plaques) and secondary immune-mediated cutaneous vasculitis (erythema nodosum or leukocytoclastic vasculitis)
Conspicuous absence of peripheral lymphadenopathy: Normal-sized cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes despite massive visceral splenomegaly
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT / Ultrasound: Gigantic, homogeneous splenomegaly (frequently exceeding 20-25 cm in craniocaudal dimension and weighing >1-3 kg), often displacing the left kidney and descending colon across the midline; moderate hepatomegaly; characteristic absence of bulky retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy (differentiating HCL from other B-cell lymphomas)

Musculoskeletal MRI / Plain Radiography: High incidence of avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) of the femoral heads and bone marrow replacement displaying diffuse low signal intensity on T1-weighted images and elevated signal on T2/STIR; occasional discrete osteolytic bone lesions with cortical destruction
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral blood smear: Mononuclear cells (medium-sized mature B cells) with abundant pale-blue cytoplasm featuring circumferential, fine, delicate, hair-like or ruffle-like cytoplasmic projections ('hairy cells'), with round, oval, or kidney-shaped nuclei and spongy, ground-glass chromatin

Bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy: Invariably yields a 'dry tap' (punctio sicca) on aspiration due to extensive pericellular reticulin fibrosis (collagen/reticulin meshwork); core trephine biopsy reveals a pathognomonic 'fried-egg' appearance (abundant clear cytoplasm creating wide, distinct halos around widely spaced, uniform round-to-oval nuclei); diffuse or interstitial marrow infiltration with effacement of normal fat and hematopoietic spaces; pseudosinuses lined by hairy cells and filled with red blood cells ('blood lakes' in red pulp of spleen); Cytochemistry: Tartrate-Resistant Acid Phosphatase (TRAP) intensely positive (inhibited poorly by tartaric acid); IHC: Clonal mature B-cells strongly positive for CD19, CD20, CD22, CD11c, CD25, CD103 (integrin alpha E), CD123, and Annexin A1 (highly specific marker); Molecular Genetics: Pathognomonic somatic activating BRAF V600E point mutation present in virtually 100% of classic HCL cases
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Classic mature B-cell leukemia featuring gargantuan clinical and CT splenomegaly without adenopathy, bone marrow 'dry tap' with pathognomonic 'fried-egg' histology and fine cytoplasmic hair-like projections, verified by TRAP positivity and universal BRAF V600E mutations.

Hematology.name: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis
clinical_manifestations: Prolonged unremitting high spiking fever: Sustained daily fevers (>38.5°C) refractory to broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, accompanied by rigors and diaphoresis
Massive hepatosplenomegaly: Prominent palpable, firm, tender enlargement of the spleen and liver causing marked abdominal distension
Cutaneous & mucosal purpura: Generalized erythematous maculopapular or morbilliform eruption, widespread petechiae, ecchymoses, mucosal bleeding, and progressive scleral icterus / jaundice
Neurological signs: Irritability, encephalopathy, altered mental status, neck stiffness / meningismus, seizures, cranial nerve palsies, and ataxia in secondary CNS involvement

Extreme laboratory biomarkers: Astoundingly high serum ferritin (often >10,000-50,000 ng/mL, occasionally >100,000 ng/mL, which is >90% sensitive and specific), severe hypertriglyceridemia, and hypofibrinogenemia
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Massive, homogeneous hepatosplenomegaly; marked diffuse gallbladder wall thickening (edema without gallstones); periportal cuffing / hypoechogenicity; retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy; moderate-to-gross peritoneal ascites

Contrast-Enhanced Brain MRI (CNS-HLH): Multifocal, symmetric, T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions involving the deep periventricular white matter, brainstem, and cerebellum; leptomeningeal and perivascular parenchymal gadolinium enhancement; diffuse cerebral volume loss, subdural collections, and diffuse restriction on DWI during acute cytotoxic edema

Chest CT / Radiography: Bilateral diffuse interstitial or alveolar ground-glass infiltrates, interlobular septal thickening, pulmonary edema pattern from capillary leak, and bilateral pleural effusions
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow, spleen, liver, or lymph node biopsy: Pathognomonic hemophagocytosis: morphologically mature, activated histiocytes/macrophages with abundant vacuolated cytoplasm containing intact or fragmented engulfed hematopoietic cells, including erythrocytes, erythroblasts, mature neutrophils, lymphocytes, platelets, and nuclear debris; absence of cytologic atypia or malignant cytologic features in the macrophages; liver biopsy demonstrates marked sinusoidal lymphohistiocytic infiltration and Kupffer cell hyperplasia with erythrophagocytosis; Laboratory/Immunology Criteria (HLH-2004): Profound hyperferritinemia (>500-10,000 ng/mL), low or absent NK-cell cytotoxic activity, dramatically elevated soluble interleukin-2 receptor (soluble CD25 / sIL-2R >2400 U/mL), hypertriglyceridemia (fasting triglycerides >=265 mg/dL), hypofibrinogenemia (fibrinogen <=150 mg/dL), and cytopenias affecting >=2 lineages; Genetics: Mutations in PRF1 (perforin), UNC13D (Munc13-4), STX11 (syntaxin 11), or STXBP2 in primary familial HLH
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening hyperinflammatory cytokine storm syndrome marked by unremitting fever, purpura, and massive hepatosplenomegaly on bedside and abdominal ultrasound, leptomeningeal brain MRI enhancement, extreme hyperferritinemia, and pathognomonic histiocytic hemophagocytosis on bone marrow biopsy.

Hematology.name: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
clinical_manifestations: Seborrheic dermatitis-like rash: scaling, crusted, erythematous, or purpuric papules refractory to topical therapy on scalp, groin, and retroauricular areas (infants)
Ulcerative mucosal lesions in the oral cavity and gingival retraction with loose, mobile, 'floating teeth'
Classic Hand-Schüller-Christian triad: lytic bone lesions, exophthalmos (proptosis), and diabetes insipidus (polyuria/polydipsia)
Localized painful bone swelling (skull, femur, ribs)
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal Radiography / CT: Punched-out lytic bone lesions with pathognomonic 'beveled edges' (due to unequal destruction of inner and outer cortical tables of the skull); complete collapse of a vertebral body into a thin, wafer-like plate ('vertebra plana'); mandibular alveolar bone resorption causing teeth to appear suspended in air ('floating teeth')

Chest HRCT (Pulmonary LCH in young smokers): Bilateral centrilobular micronodules and bizarrely shaped, bilobed or clover-leaf thin-walled cysts with upper- and mid-lung zone predominance and sparing of the costophrenic angles
Brain / Pituitary MRI: Thickening of the pituitary stalk (>3 mm) with loss of the normal posterior pituitary T1 bright spot in central diabetes insipidus
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy: Proliferation of clonal Langerhans cells with characteristic grooved, folded, elongated nuclei ('coffee-bean' nuclei) admixed with eosinophils, histiocytes, and multinucleated giant cells; strong immunohistochemical positivity for CD1a, Langerin (CD207), and S100; electron microscopy historically demonstrates rod- or tennis-racket-shaped Birbeck granules
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield multisystem entity showing refractory scalp crusted rashes, loose 'floating teeth', and proptosis paired with beveled-edge skull lesions and vertebra plana on plain film/CT.

Hematology.name: Multiple Myeloma
clinical_manifestations: Pallor from severe normocytic anemia
Macroglossia and waxy periorbital purpura ('raccoon eyes') in secondary AL amyloidosis
Cutaneous and subcutaneous extramedullary plasmacytomas (violaceous nodules)
Severe localized bone pain and tenderness, vertebral collapse kyphosis
Hyperviscosity syndrome (engorged, sausage-like retinal veins on fundoscopy, mucosal bleeding)
radiological_manifestations: Whole-Body Low-Dose CT (WBLDCT) / Skeletal Survey: Pathognomonic discrete, sharply marginated, punched-out lytic 'cookie-cutter' bone lesions without reactive osteosclerotic rims (skull, pelvis, ribs, proximal humerus/femur); vertebral compression fractures; diffuse osteopenia

Whole-Body MRI: Highest sensitivity for bone marrow infiltration (diffuse, focal, or salt-and-pepper marrow replacement, hypointense on T1, hyperintense on STIR); assessment of spinal cord and root compression
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy: Clonal bone marrow plasma cell infiltration >=10%; atypical plasma cells displaying clock-face (cartwheel) chromatin, eccentric nuclei, prominent nucleoli, Mott cells (grape-like clusters of Russell bodies containing immunoglobulins), and flame cells; monoclonality confirmed by kappa/lambda light chain restriction on flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry; CD138+, CD38+, CD56+
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal hematologic malignancy with clinical macroglossia and cutaneous plasmacytomas matched with pathognomonic punched-out lytic bone lesions ('cookie-cutter' skull) on skeletal CT and MRI.

Hematology.name: Myeloid Sarcoma
Hematology.subspecialty: Acute Myeloid Leukemias and Related Neoplasms
clinical_manifestations: Gross subcutaneous / soft tissue masses: Solitary or multiple, rapidly enlarging, firm-to-rubbery, non-tender, painless or tender, violaceous, bluish, or greenish subcutaneous nodules and exophytic tumor masses (termed 'chloroma' because fresh, unstained surgical specimens exhibit a vivid emerald-green coloration that rapidly fades upon exposure to air)

Ophthalmic / Craniofacial manifestations: Unilateral or bilateral severe exophthalmos (proptosis), chemosis, eyelid swelling, and visual impairment caused by retro-bulbar or intra-orbital chloroma (most frequent presentation in pediatric AML); massive, boggy, violaceous gingival hypertrophy and ulceration with spontaneous bleeding (frequent in acute monocytic leukemia, FAB M4/M5)
Neurologic deficits: Rapidly evolving motor weakness, sensory loss, radicular pain, and paraplegia due to epidural myeloid sarcoma with spinal cord compression
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Brain / Orbital MRI: Well-defined, lobulated, homogeneous soft-tissue masses in the retro-orbital space, extra-axial intracranial space, or paranasal sinuses; isointense to hypointense on T1-weighted images, isointense to hyperintense on T2-weighted images, with uniform, intense gadolinium enhancement; adjacent bony remodeling or cortical erosion without frank osteolytic permeation

Contrast-Enhanced Spine MRI: Epidural soft-tissue mass encircling the thecal sac, extending through neural foramina, causing spinal cord compression and obliteration of the epidural fat pad, with strong homogeneous enhancement

Whole-Body 18F-FDG PET/CT: Avid, intensely hypermetabolic soft-tissue masses throughout nodal, visceral, and musculoskeletal sites, localizing occult chloromas in non-leukemic or post-transplant relapse settings
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy of extramedullary mass: Sheets of monotonous, medium-to-large, immature myeloid precursor cells (myeloblasts, monoblasts, or promyelocytes) with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, round or indented nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, and variable nucleoli, effacing the normal tissue architecture; pathognomonic green hue in fresh gross tissue caused by high concentrations of endogenous myeloperoxidase (MPO); IHC (Confirmatory): Positive for myeloperoxidase (MPO), lysozyme, CD43, CD68, CD33, CD117 (c-kit), and CD34; monoblastic differentiation highlighted by CD68 (PG-M1) and non-specific esterase (NSE); terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) typically negative; Molecular / Cytogenetics: Frequently associated with AML-defining chromosomal aberrations, notably t(8;21)(q22;q22) [RUNX1::RUNX1T1] and inv(16)(p13.1q22) / t(16;16) [CBFB::MYH11]
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic extramedullary manifestation of acute myeloid leukemia featuring vivid greenish subcutaneous tumors ('chloroma'), prominent orbital proptosis, and florid gingival hypertrophy, verified by homogeneous enhancing retro-orbital/epidural MRI masses and myeloperoxidase-rich (MPO+) myeloid blast histology.

Hematology.name: Niemann-Pick Disease
clinical_manifestations: Colossal hepatosplenomegaly & abdominal distension: Striking, rock-firm splenomegaly and massive hepatomegaly presenting in infancy or childhood with marked protuberant abdomen, cachexia, feeding difficulties, and failure to thrive (infantile neurovisceral ASMD / Type A); insidious progressive organomegaly in chronic visceral ASMD (Type B)

Ocular fundoscopic hallmark: Pathognomonic 'cherry-red spot' at the fovea centralis of the macula on dilated ophthalmologic examination in ~50-90% of severe infantile neurovisceral cases (Type A) and a subset of Type C cases, caused by lipid storage within retinal ganglion cells that contrast against and accentuate the transparent central fovea showing underlying hypervascular choroid

Neurological manifestations: Progressive vertical supranuclear gaze palsy (VSGP, pathognomonic clinical sign of Niemann-Pick type C, initially affecting downward vertical saccades), progressive cerebellar ataxia, dysarthria, dystonia, gelastic cataplexy (sudden loss of muscle tone triggered by laughter), and rapid neurodegenerative cognitive decline

Cutaneous & mucosal signs: Eruptive or planar xanthomatous lipid deposits in skin and tendons in older patients, facial dysmorphic features in severe infantile cases, jaundice in neonatal cholestatic presentation, and bleeding purpura secondary to severe hypersplenism
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT (HRCT): Diagnostic diffuse interstitial lung disease characterized by uniform ground-glass opacities, fine reticulonodular infiltrates, and prominent thickening of interlobular septa producing a 'crazy-paving' pattern throughout both lung fields (due to alveolar and interstitial accumulation of lipid-laden foamy histiocytes), predominantly in lower lung zones

Abdominal Ultrasound / CT / MRI: Massive hepatomegaly with smooth, rounded contours and diffuse fatty/lipid-like infiltration; colossal splenomegaly with multiple hypoechoic or low-attenuation nodular aggregates ('storage nodules' or foam cell granulomas), portal vein enlargement, and prominent retroperitoneal and perihilar lymphadenopathy

Brain MRI (Type C): Progressive bilateral symmetrical cerebellar and cortical atrophy, particularly affecting the cerebellar vermis; midbrain atrophy with thinning of the corpus callosum; hypointensity of the thalami and globus pallidus on T2-weighted and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) reflecting abnormal metal or lipid accretion
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow aspirate / trephine biopsy: Diagnostic Niemann-Pick foam cells (histiocytes measuring 20-50 micrometers) featuring small eccentric nuclei and abundant cytoplasm uniformly packed with numerous fine, tiny lipid droplets giving a distinct 'foamy', 'honeycomb', or 'mulberry' vacuolated appearance; Giemsa and Wright stains demonstrate classic 'sea-blue histiocytes' (macrophages filled with blue-green ceroid and sphingomyelin pigment)

Histochemical and fluorescent staining: Cytoplasmic vacuoles stain positive with Oil Red O and Sudan Black B; in Niemann-Pick Type C, cultured skin fibroblasts demonstrate diagnostic intense punctate perinuclear cholesterol accumulation upon Filipin fluorescent staining

Biochemical and Molecular confirmation: Markedly deficient acid sphingomyelinase (ASM) activity in leukocytes or cultured fibroblasts (for SMPD1-related ASMD Type A/B) or identification of biallelic pathogenic mutations in SMPD1 (Type A/B), NPC1 (95% of Type C), or NPC2; elevated plasma cholestane-3beta,5alpha,6beta-triol and lysosphingomyelin-509
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Hallmark multi-organ sphingolipidosis combining colossal hepato-splenic abdominal enlargement and fundoscopic 'cherry-red spots' with chest HRCT 'crazy-paving' interstitial lipidosis, progressive vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, and pathognomonic sea-blue histiocytic foamy 'mulberry' bone marrow infiltration.

Hematology.name: POEMS Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous lesions (pathognomonic visual signs): Glomeruloid hemangiomas (small, red-to-violaceous cutaneous vascular papules resembling renal glomeruli on microscopy), diffuse cutaneous hyperpigmentation (often mistaken for Addison disease), hypertrichosis (coarse, dark hair overgrowth on face, chest, and limbs), sclerodermoid skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, and leukonychia (white nails / Terry nails)

Peripheral neuropathy: Severe, progressive, symmetrical, sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy beginning distally in lower limbs with profound muscle atrophy ('stork leg' appearance), foot drop, and loss of deep tendon reflexes

Organomegaly and volume overload: Pronounced hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and non-tender peripheral lymphadenopathy; massive extravascular volume overload presenting as severe dependent peripheral pitting edema, abdominal ascites, pleural effusions, and pericardial effusion
Endocrinopathy: Gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, and erectile dysfunction in men; amenorrhea and galactorrhea in women; primary hypothyroidism and adrenal insufficiency
Papilledema: Bilateral optic disc swelling on fundoscopy in >50% of patients without intracranial mass lesion
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal CT / Plain Radiography (Mandatory Hallmark): Solitary or multiple well-demarcated osteosclerotic or mixed sclerotic/lytic bone lesions without cortical destruction, predominantly in pelvis, spine, ribs, and proximal long bones; pathognomonic ivory-like, dense osteoblastic lesions with a central radiolucent nidus encircled by a prominent sclerotic border ('soap bubble' or sunburst-like hyperostosis); absence of generalized osteolysis (distinguishing POEMS from multiple myeloma)

Body CT (Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis): Diffuse polyserositis (pleural, pericardial effusions, gross ascites), generalized organomegaly (massive hepatosplenomegaly), and retroperitoneal/axillary lymphadenopathy
Brain/Orbital MRI: Optic disc elevation with perineural subarachnoid space dilation and tortuosity of the optic nerve sheath corresponding to intracranial hypertension and bilateral papilledema
pathology_manifestations: Bone lesion / bone marrow biopsy: Monoclonal plasma cell proliferation (restricted lambda light chain in virtually 100% of cases); hyperplastic bone trabeculae lined by active osteoblasts with intertrabecular fibrosis surrounding atypical clonal plasma cells expressing CD138, CD38, and lambda light chains (kappa-negative); absence of high-grade marrow infiltration (often <5-10% plasma cells on random marrow aspirate)

Skin biopsy of vascular lesions: Pathognomonic glomeruloid hemangioma composed of dilated ectatic vascular spaces containing aggregates of coiled, capillary-sized loops resembling renal glomeruli, lined by endothelial cells and enclosed by pericytes

Sural nerve biopsy: Severe loss of myelinated nerve fibers with evidence of both axonal degeneration and demyelination, accompanied by prominent endoneurial microvascular proliferation and thickening of basement membranes driven by massively elevated serum Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF >1000-2000 pg/mL)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Vivid multisystem paraneoplastic syndrome showcasing pathognomonic glomeruloid hemangiomas, hypertrichosis, and papilledema, definitively recognized radiologically by dense osteosclerotic bone lesions without osteolysis on skeletal CT and surging serum VEGF.

Hematology.name: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria
Hematology.subspecialty: Complement-Mediated Hemolytic Anemias / Bone Marrow Disorders
synonyms: acquired hemolytic anemia with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Gross Hemoglobinuria: Intermittent, startling passage of dark burgundy, reddish-brown, mahogany, or 'cola-colored' / 'tea-colored' urine passed upon awakening in the morning, which progressively lightens throughout subsequent daytime voids (resulting from overnight intravascular hemolysis triggered by mild sleep-induced hypoventilation, respiratory acidosis, and complement activation)

Severe Visual Pallor & Jaundice: Concomitant pale-lemon skin coloration and brilliant yellow scleral icterus from rapid, continuous complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis and elevated indirect bilirubin

Visceral & Extremity Pain Crises: Episodes of agonizing, severe central abdominal pain, back pain, and intractable dysphagia (esophageal spasms / 'food getting stuck') caused by acute depletion and scavenging of endogenous nitric oxide (NO) by massive quantities of free cell-free plasma hemoglobin

Cutaneous & Thromboembolic Signs: Sudden development of severe abdominal distension with rapid ascites and jaundice (acute Budd-Chiari syndrome), lower extremity asymmetrical swelling and violaceous discoloration (deep vein thrombosis), or extensive cutaneous purpura fulminans / hemorrhagic skin necrosis from dermal microvascular thrombosis; priapism and erectile dysfunction in men
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Doppler Ultrasound / Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI: High-yield evaluation for Budd-Chiari syndrome (the leading cause of mortality in PNH): absence of flow, non-visualization, or intraluminal filling defects in hepatic veins; marked hypertrophy of the caudate lobe (which has independent venous drainage into IVC); patchy, heterogeneous mosaic parenchymal enhancement during early arterial phase; severe ascites, splenomegaly, and portal/mesenteric vein thrombosis

Renal MRI (Pathognomonic Renal Hemosiderosis): Striking, uniform, bilateral darkening of the renal cortex on T1- and T2-weighted sequences, with marked signal loss ('black renal cortex') on gradient-echo / susceptibility-weighted T2* sequences due to massive reabsorption and intracellular deposition of hemosiderin in renal proximal tubular epithelial cells, sparing the renal medulla

Brain CT / MRI & MR Venography: High-risk detection of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST): superior sagittal or transverse sinus dense clot sign on non-contrast CT, 'empty delta sign' on contrast-enhanced CT, and loss of normal flow void on MRI
pathology_manifestations: Flow Cytometry (Gold-Standard Diagnostic Test): Multiparameter flow cytometry demonstrating complete absence (Type III cells) or partial deficiency (Type II cells) of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored regulatory proteins—specifically CD55 (decay-accelerating factor / DAF) and CD59 (membrane inhibitor of reactive lysis / MIRL / MAC-inhibitory protein)—on erythrocytes and granulocytes/monocytes using fluorescent aerolysin (FLAIR); identification of a distinct PNH clone size

Peripheral Blood & Urine Analysis: Normocytic or macrocytic anemia with prominent polychromasia and elevated reticulocyte count, with notable absence of spherocytes or mechanical schistocytes (distinguishing complement-mediated from mechanical hemolysis); markedly elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH often >5-10 times upper limit of normal) and undetectable haptoglobin; urinalysis demonstrates positive dipstick for blood with absence of intact red blood cells on microscopy, and pathognomonic Prussian blue staining of urinary sediment demonstrates massive blue hemosiderin granules within desquamated tubular cells (hemosiderinuria)

Bone Marrow Aspirate & Trephine Biopsy: Normocellular or hypercellular marrow showing prominent erythroid hyperplasia responding to peripheral hemolysis, or varying degrees of hypocellularity if presenting in the context of an aplastic anemia/PNH overlap syndrome

Molecular Genetics: Acquired somatic loss-of-function mutations in the X-linked PIGA (phosphatidylinositol glycan class A) gene in one or more hematopoietic stem cell clones, preventing the initial enzymatic step in GPI anchor biosynthesis
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic complement-mediated hematologic disorder displaying striking morning mahogany-colored hemoglobinuria and scleral icterus, imaged via pathognomonic 'black renal cortex' hemosiderosis on T2* MRI and Budd-Chiari hepatic thrombosis, and definitively confirmed by flow cytometric loss of CD55/CD59/FLAER.

Hematology.name: Polycythemia Vera
clinical_manifestations: Facial plethora ('ruddy cyanosis'): Deeply flushed, red-purple engorgement of the face, cheeks, ears, lips, and neck, contrasting with suffused, brick-red, congested conjunctival vessels ('bloodshot eyes') without inflammation

Aquagenic pruritus: Intense, intractable, prickling or stinging cutaneous itch devoid of rash, classically triggered within minutes of contact with warm water (taking a warm bath or shower), lasting 15-60 minutes and resistant to antihistamines

Erythromelalgia: Paroxysmal, intense burning pain, bright erythema, and increased skin temperature affecting the extremities (principally soles of feet and toes, occasionally palms), exacerbated by warmth and dramatically relieved by elevating the limbs or taking a single dose of aspirin
Retinal changes: Marked engorgement, tortuosity, and dark purple coloration of retinal veins on fundoscopy ('fundus polycythaemicus') with occasional retinal hemorrhages
Splenomegaly: Palpable, firm, non-tender spleen extending well below the left costal margin (in >70% of patients), sometimes crossing the midline and causing visible left upper quadrant fullness
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Doppler Ultrasound / Contrast-Enhanced CT: Massive, homogeneous splenomegaly (craniocaudal length often >16-20 cm); direct visualization of hepatic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari syndrome) or extrahepatic portal vein thrombosis, demonstrating non-visualized or truncated hepatic veins, intrahepatic comma-shaped collateral veins, patchy caudate lobe hypertrophy, and reduced peripheral hepatic perfusion; mesenteric and splenic vein thrombosis

Skeletal MRI: Marked diffuse conversion of fatty yellow marrow to cellular red marrow throughout the appendicular skeleton (proximal and distal femur and humerus), demonstrating diffuse low signal intensity on T1-weighted images and elevated signal on STIR
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow trephine core biopsy (WHO Major Criterion): Marked hypercellularity (often 90-100% cellularity) with panmyelosis (trilineage proliferation: prominent erythroid hyperplasia, granulocytic hyperplasia, and megakaryocytic hyperplasia); megakaryocytes form loose clusters, vary in size, and display hyperlobulated, pleomorphic nuclei without significant dysplasia; minimal reticulin fibrosis in early stages (grade 0-1/3), advancing to dense reticulin/collagen fibrosis in post-PV myelofibrosis

Peripheral blood smear: Striking polycythemia with packed red blood cells, mild leukocytosis (predominance of mature neutrophils), and thrombocytosis (large, hypergranulated platelets); absence of leucoerythroblastic features unless transformed to myelofibrosis

Molecular genetic testing: Pathognomonic somatic gain-of-function mutation in the JAK2 gene: JAK2 V617F (exon 14) detected in >95-97% of patients; JAK2 exon 12 mutations identified in 2-3% of remaining JAK2 V617F-negative cases; Serum erythropoietin (EPO) subnormal/suppressed
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic myeloproliferative disorder defined by bedside ruddy plethoric facies, suffused conjunctivae, aquagenic pruritus, and burning erythromelalgia, coupled with massive ultrasound splenomegaly, splanchnic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari), and panmyeloid hypercellular marrow harboring JAK2 V617F.

Hematology.name: Primary Myelofibrosis
clinical_manifestations: Colossal, rock-hard splenomegaly: Massive, non-tender or tender, firm splenomegaly frequently crossing the abdominal midline and descending into the right lower quadrant or pelvis; colossal abdominal asymmetry, early satiety, severe left upper quadrant pain (from splenic infarction or perisplenitis with friction rubs), and progressive moderate hepatomegaly

Extreme constitutional symptoms & cachexia: Severe profound unintentional weight loss, temporal and thenar muscle wasting ('bitemporal hollows'), sunken cheeks, drenching night sweats, low-grade fevers, and disabling generalized pruritus

Cutaneous & extramedullary hematopoietic signs: Extramedullary hematopoietic skin deposits (eruptive red-to-violaceous cutaneous plaques, nodules, or tumors), petechiae, ecchymoses, and mucosal purpura; diffuse pallor, resting tachycardia, and lower-extremity dependent pitting edema from portal hypertension and inferior vena cava compression by the massive spleen
Bone pain & arthropathies: Severe, deep, aching bone pain (especially in long bones and axial skeleton), exquisite localized sternal tenderness, and secondary gouty arthritis from purine turnover
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT / MRI: Giant, colossal splenomegaly (craniocaudal length often >25-35 cm) displacing stomach, bowel loops, and left kidney into the right hemiabdomen; frequent wedge-shaped, sharply demarcated, non-enhancing peripheral areas of splenic infarction; portal hypertension signs including dilated splenic vein, ascites, and splenorenal collaterals; marked hepatomegaly

Plain Skeletal Radiography / Skeletal CT: Diffuse, uniform or patchy osteosclerosis presenting in ~40-60% of advanced cases as increased bone density, coarsened thickened trabeculae, and cortical thickening without osteolysis, prominently involving the axial skeleton (spine, ribs, pelvis, proximal humeri, and femora); characteristic 'sandwich vertebrae' (dense sclerotic bands parallel to vertebral endplates)

18F-FDG PET/CT & Bone Scintigraphy: Diffuse, intense FDG uptake throughout the entire axial and appendicular skeletal marrow, extending down into distal extremities (distal tibiae and forearms) corresponding to peripheral expansion of active extramedullary and intramedullary hematopoiesis; bone scintigraphy reveals a 'super-scan' appearance with intense axial uptake and faint or absent renal visualization
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear (Pathognomonic Leukoerythroblastic Picture): Striking, classical tear-drop poikilocytes (dacrocytes) formed during mechanical extrusion through distorted, fibrotic marrow sinusoids; circulating immature myeloid cells (myelocytes, metamyelocytes, myeloblasts <10%) and nucleated red blood cells (normoblasts); anisopoikilocytosis; giant, hypogranular, dysplastic platelets and circulating megakaryocytic nuclei

Bone Marrow Aspirate & Trephine Core Biopsy (WHO Major Criterion): Marrow aspirate characteristically yields a 'dry tap' (punctio sicca) due to dense fibrosis. Trephine biopsy reveals marked hypercellularity with prominent megakaryocytic proliferation and atypia: tightly clustered, abnormally large megakaryocytes with hyperchromatic, bulbous, or 'cloud-like' nuclei with abnormal maturation (high N:C ratio); dense reticulin fibrosis (MF-2 or MF-3 on Silver Gomori stain) and extensive collagen fibrosis (blue on Masson trichrome stain); progressive osteosclerosis with neo-osteogenesis and dilated sinusoids containing intraluminal hematopoiesis

Molecular Genetics: Mutually exclusive driver mutations identifying constitutively active JAK-STAT signaling: JAK2 V617F (exon 14, in ~50-60% of patients), CALR (calreticulin exon 9 indels, in ~25-30%), or MPL (thrombopoietin receptor W515K/L, in ~5-10%); ~10% are 'triple-negative'
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic myeloproliferative neoplasm manifesting bedside with colossal spleen crossing the midline and profound cachectic muscle wasting, recognized radiologically by diffuse patchy osteosclerosis on CT and splenic infarcts, and diagnosed by blood smear dacrocytes (tear-drop cells) and marrow dry tap with dense silver-stained reticulin/collagen fibrosis.

Hematology.name: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
clinical_manifestations: Massive cervical lymphadenopathy ('bull neck'): Rapid, painless, bilateral, symmetric, grotesque enlargement of cervical lymph nodes forming huge, matted, confluent lobulated masses that obscure the angle of the jaw and sternocleidomastoid contours

Extranodal cutaneous lesions: Asymptomatic, firm, indurated, yellow-red, brownish, or violaceous papules, plaques, and solitary or grouped subcutaneous nodules (often xanthomatous in appearance), frequently on the face, nasal bridge, and trunk

Extranodal upper respiratory tract involvement: Exophytic mucosal masses and polypoid swelling of the nasal septum, turbinates, and paranasal sinuses causing chronic nasal obstruction, epistaxis, and 'saddle-nose' deformity
Extranodal orbital involvement: Painless, progressive, unilateral or bilateral exophthalmos (proptosis), eyelid edema, and periorbital soft tissue fullness from retro-orbital histiocytic deposition
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Neck and Chest CT: Massive, extensive, bilateral cervical, submandibular, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy with homogeneous soft-tissue density and moderate contrast enhancement, frequently coalescing into giant confluent lobulated nodal conglomerations; absence of central caseous necrosis or macroscopic calcification (distinguishing RDD from tuberculosis and necrotic metastatic carcinoma)

Contrast-Enhanced Brain / Spine MRI: Dural-based, intensely and homogeneously enhancing extra-axial masses with prominent 'dural tail' sign, closely mimicking meningioma, causing compressive myelopathy or mass effect on adjacent brain parenchyma
Sinonasal CT: Soft-tissue opacification of the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses with extensive remodeling and thinning of adjacent bony walls without frank aggressive bony destruction
Whole-Body 18F-FDG PET/CT: Symmetrical, intense hypermetabolism (SUVmax 5-15) throughout the cervical and mediastinal lymph node stations and extranodal skeletal/soft-tissue sites
pathology_manifestations: Lymph node / extranodal tissue biopsy: Massive sinus expansion and distension by large, pale, polygonal histiocytes possessing abundant clear-to-eosinophilic cytoplasm, round vesicular nuclei, and single prominent nucleoli; pathognomonic emperipolesis: intact, viable, non-degraded lymphocytes, plasma cells, and occasional erythrocytes traversing the cytoplasm of intact viable histiocytes; background interfollicular stroma exhibits marked sclerosis, polyclonal plasma cell infiltrate, and prominent lymphoid follicles; IHC: Histiocytes are intensely and diffusely positive for S100 protein and CD68 / CD163; negative for CD1a and Langerin (CD207) (distinguishing RDD from Langerhans cell histiocytosis)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Striking histiocytic disorder characterized by grotesque 'bull neck' cervical adenopathy and orbital exophthalmos, diagnosed by massive non-necrotic matted nodal conglomerations on CT and pathognomonic emperipolesis within S100-positive histiocytes.

Hematology.name: Sickle Cell Disease
clinical_manifestations: Dactylitis ('hand-foot syndrome'): Acute, exquisite, symmetric, painful, tender, tense, non-pitting soft tissue swelling of the dorsum of hands and feet in infants and young children (6-24 months) secondary to bone marrow infarction of the metacarpals and metatarsals

Craniofacial deformity ('chipmunk facies'): Prominent frontal and parietal bossing, maxillary hypertrophy, gnathopathy, malocclusion, and widening of the dental arch caused by profound extramedullary and intramedullary erythroid hyperplasia

Chronic lower extremity skin ulcers: Deep, sharply marginated, punched-out, painful, indolent ulcers with necrotic yellow fibrinous bases located over the medial and lateral malleoli, often surrounded by hyperpigmentation and atrophic skin

Ocular and systemic signs: Marked scleral icterus (conjugated/unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia from chronic hemolysis); pallor of conjunctivae and palmar creases; priapism; acute chest syndrome (tachypnea, chest pain, fever, hypoxia)
radiological_manifestations: Skull Radiography / CT: Marked widening and thickening of the diploic space with complete thinning of the outer cortical table, accompanied by vertical, fine, perpendicular trabecular striations producing the pathognomonic 'hair-on-end' (crew-cut) appearance of the calvarium

Spine Radiography / CT: Pathognomonic 'H-shaped vertebrae' (Reynolds sign): sharp, square, step-like central endplate depression of lumbar and thoracic vertebral bodies caused by microvascular ischemia and growth inhibition of the central growth plates with preserved peripheral vascular supply; 'fish-mouth' biconcave vertebrae

Musculoskeletal Radiography / MRI: Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) of the femoral and humeral heads demonstrating subchondral radiolucent crescent sign, structural flattening, sclerosis, and joint collapse; bone-within-bone appearance (endosteal bone formation following infarction); acute dactylitis showing initial soft-tissue swelling followed by patchy periosteal reaction and cortical resorption

Abdominal CT / Ultrasound: Progressive splenic autosplenectomy: childhood splenomegaly progressing to an exceedingly small, densely calcified, shrunken, non-functional fibrous splenic remnant; cholelithiasis (multiple radiopaque calcium bilirubinate gallstones)
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral blood smear: Striking red blood cell morphology featuring elongated, crescentic, sickle-shaped erythrocytes with pointed ends (drepanocytes / irreversible sickle cells); target cells (codocytes), Howell-Jolly bodies and Pappenheimer bodies (reflecting functional asplenia/autosplenectomy), polychromasia, nucleated red blood cells, and marked anisopoikilocytosis

Hemoglobin electrophoresis / High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC): Homozygous sickle cell disease (HbSS) demonstrates absent adult Hemoglobin A (HbA 0%), predominant Hemoglobin S (HbS 80-95%), elevated Hemoglobin F (HbF 5-20%), and normal/mildly elevated HbA2

Bone marrow aspirate/biopsy: Massive normoblastic erythroid hyperplasia (myeloid:erythroid ratio reversed to 1:1 or 1:2) with trabecular bone thinning, vascular engorgement, and prominent hemosiderin iron accumulation in reticuloendothelial macrophages
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential hemoglobinopathy with dramatic clinical phenotypes (infantile hand-foot dactylitis, malleolar leg ulcers, chipmunk facies) and unmistakable skeletal radiology: 'hair-on-end' skull, Reynolds 'H-shaped' vertebrae, and dense calcified autosplenectomy.

Hematology.name: Solitary Plasmacytoma
clinical_manifestations: Solitary Plasmacytoma of Bone (SPB): Severe, localized, persistent, deep bone pain corresponding to a focal skeletal site (most commonly thoracic/lumbar spine, pelvis, ribs, or proximal femur); localized palpable bony swelling or tenderness; neurologic deficits (radiculopathy, lower extremity weakness, sensory loss, or acute paraplegia) from epidural cord compression in vertebral lesions

Extramedullary Plasmacytoma (EMP): Solitary, fleshy, smooth, sessile or pedunculated, highly vascular, red-to-violaceous polypoid mass protruding from the mucosal surfaces of the upper aerodigestive tract (nasopharynx, nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses, or tonsils); symptoms of persistent unilateral nasal obstruction, epistaxis, hoarseness, dysphagia, or proptosis; subcutaneous extramedullary violaceous tumors
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography / Skeletal CT: Solitary, sharply demarcated, expansile osteolytic lesion with cortical thinning, ballooning, or frank cortical breach, typically devoid of sclerotic margins or periosteal reaction; in vertebral bodies, produces a classic 'mini-brain' appearance on axial CT (thickened cortical and trabecular struts radiating from the periphery resembling cerebral sulci/gyri) or vertebral collapse ('vertebra plana')

Contrast-Enhanced MRI: Essential modality demonstrating a single focal mass hypointense on T1, hyperintense on T2/STIR, with brisk homogeneous contrast enhancement; delineates epidural extension and spinal cord compression in SPB; confirms complete absence of occult lesions in the remainder of the spine and pelvis

Whole-Body 18F-FDG PET/CT (Mandatory Exclusionary Modality): Single, solitary intensely hypermetabolic focus (SUVmax typically >4-8) with definitive negative whole-body survey proving the strict solitary nature of the disease and ruling out systemic Multiple Myeloma
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy of solitary lesion: Monomorphic, sheet-like infiltration of mature or immature atypical plasma cells with eccentric, cartwheel ('clock-face') nuclear chromatin, abundant basophilic cytoplasm, and perinuclear pale hof; monoclonality confirmed by light chain restriction (kappa or lambda) on in situ hybridization or immunohistochemistry; CD138+, CD38+, CD56+ (often in SPB) or CD56- (often in EMP); absence of high-grade marrow plasma cell infiltration on blind bone marrow biopsy (<5% plasma cells) and absence of CRAB end-organ damage (hypercalcemia, renal failure, anemia) attributable to multiple myeloma
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Focal plasma cell neoplasm presenting with localized violaceous mucosal nasopharyngeal masses or solitary destructive spine tumors, confirmed by unique 'mini-brain' expansile lytic lesions on CT/MRI and solitary PET avidity without disseminated myeloma.

Hematology.name: Systemic Mastocytosis
clinical_manifestations: Urticaria pigmentosa (maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis): Fixed, non-blanching, reddish-brown to hyperpigmented round or oval macules and papules scattered symmetrically across the trunk and extremities, sparing the face, palms, and soles

Pathognomonic Darier sign: Stroking, rubbing, or scratching a cutaneous lesion results within minutes in localized urtication, erythema, edema, and intense surrounding wheal-and-flare reaction due to local histamine and mast cell mediator degranulation

Systemic mediator flush: Sudden episodic intense fiery-red flushing of face, neck, and upper chest accompanied by tachycardia, hypotension/syncope, throbbing headache, and explosive diarrhea/abdominal cramping

Dermatographism: Exaggerated linear wheal formation after light blunt stroking of normal-appearing skin; telangiectasia macularis eruptiva perstans (TMEP) in older adults showing persistent telangiectatic brownish macules
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal Radiography / CT: Diffuse or focal osteosclerosis alternating with osteolytic lesions, producing a classic mottled 'peppered' or 'pagetoid' bone appearance, predominantly in axial skeleton (spine, pelvis, ribs, and proximal femora); thickened, sclerotic vertebral trabeculae with cortical thickening; pathological compression fractures and progressive generalized osteopenia/osteoporosis in young individuals

Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Marked diffuse hepatomegaly and splenomegaly (frequent hypersplenism), extensive mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, diffuse bowel wall thickening (mast cell enteropathy), and ascites

99mTc Bone Scintigraphy: Heterogeneous, patchy, diffuse skeletal uptake ('super-scan'-like pattern in severe bone marrow mastocytosis) reflecting intense osteoblastic reaction adjacent to mast cell aggregates
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow trephine core biopsy (Major WHO Diagnostic Criterion): Multifocal, dense, compact aggregates of >=15 mast cells per infiltrate located in perivascular, paratrabecular, or intertrabecular marrow spaces; abnormal mast cells display elongated, spindle-shaped morphology with hypogranular cytoplasm, oval or bilobed nuclei (atypical mast cells type I and II); metachromatic cytoplasmic granules highlighted on Giemsa, toluidine blue, or Astra blue stains; IHC (Minor Criteria): Aberrant co-expression of CD25 and/or CD2 on neoplastic mast cells (alongside constitutive CD117/KIT and tryptase); Molecular: Activating KIT point mutation at codon 816 (most commonly KIT D816V, exon 17) present in >90% of cases; Serum total tryptase persistently elevated >20 ng/mL in absence of anaphylaxis
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Classic systemic mediator and infiltration disorder recognized clinically by Darier sign (urtication upon stroking reddish-brown papules) and episodic flushing, diagnosed on imaging by mottled diffuse osteosclerosis/osteolysis on CT and confirmed by spindle mast cell bone marrow aggregates with CD117/CD25 positivity and KIT D816V.

Hematology.name: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous & mucosal bleeding manifestations: Florid spontaneous purpuric eruption, extensive petechiae over extremities and torso, ecchymoses, subconjunctival hemorrhages, brisk epistaxis, and wet purpura of the buccal mucosa due to profound, consumptive peripheral thrombocytopenia (often platelet count <10,000-20,000/microL)

Severe, fluctuating neurological deficits: Strikingly waxing and waning neurological alterations ranging from acute confusion, agitation, expressive aphasia, transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), fluctuating hemiparesis, dysarthria, and headache to visual disturbances, seizures, stupor, and deep coma, reflecting transient microvascular platelet thrombi in the cerebral microcirculation

Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia signs: Marked porcelain-to-lemon-yellow skin pallor combined with vivid scleral icterus (unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia from intravascular mechanical erythrocyte fragmentation), dark cola-colored or tea-colored urine (hemoglobinuria)

Classic Diagnostic Pentad: The complete pentad—(1) thrombocytopenia with bleeding, (2) microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), (3) fluctuating neurologic deficits, (4) low-grade to high-grade fever, and (5) acute renal impairment—though present concurrently in only ~20-30% of patients, represents the iconic clinical hallmark
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (T2/FLAIR, DWI, and ADC): Multifocal, punctate or patchy hyperintensities in the subcortical white matter, basal ganglia, and cortex corresponding to acute microvascular platelet-rich ischemic microinfarctions; classic imaging pattern of Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES) with bilateral, symmetrical parieto-occipital subcortical hyperintensity on T2/FLAIR and elevated ADC representing reversible vasogenic edema

Abdominal / Renal Doppler Ultrasound: Kidneys usually appear normal in size with preserved parenchymal thickness but demonstrate increased cortical echogenicity and elevated resistive indices (RI >0.70-0.75) due to microvascular occlusion in the intrarenal arteriolar beds

CT Angiography / Brain MRA: Typically demonstrates normal large intracranial vessels (no major arterial trunk occlusion), highlighting that ischemic deficits are entirely microvascular and downstream of major bifurcations
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear (Cornerstone Microscopic Diagnosis): Marked microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with abundant red cell fragmentation: striking presence of schistocytes (helmet cells, triangular fragments, keratocytes, and microspherocytes) typically exceeding 1-2% of red blood cells (often 5-10+ per high-power field); marked polychromasia, nucleated red blood cells (normoblasts), severe thrombocytopenia with rare, giant stress platelets, and absence of platelet clumping

Histopathology (Skin, Gingival, or Organ Biopsy): Diagnostic disseminated platelet-rich, fibrin-poor microthrombi completely occluding arterioles and capillaries throughout multiple organs (brain, kidneys, heart, adrenals), with associated endothelial swelling and subendothelial hyaline deposition, without transmural inflammation, vessel wall necrosis, or leukocytoclasia (non-inflammatory microthrombosis)

Specialized Laboratory Hallmark: Severe deficiency of plasma ADAMTS13 metalloprotease activity (<10% of normal activity); detection of high-titer inhibitory anti-ADAMTS13 IgG autoantibodies in acquired immune TTP (or biallelic ADAMTS13 gene mutations in congenital Upshaw-Schulman syndrome); normal coagulation parameters (PT, aPTT, and fibrinogen normal, distinguishing TTP from disseminated intravascular coagulation)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening medical emergency recognized clinically by the classic pentad of petechiae/purpura, fluctuating focal aphasia/delirium, fever, and jaundice, verified radiologically by cerebral microvascular ischemic/PRES hyperintensities on brain MRI, and proved microscopically by sheets of schistocytes on blood smear and severe ADAMTS13 deficiency (<10%).

Hematology.name: Waldenström Macroglobulinemia
Hematology.subspecialty: Mature B-Cell Neoplasms / Plasma Cell Dyscrasias
clinical_manifestations: Hyperviscosity Retinopathy ('Fundus Macroglobulinemicus'): Dilated, hugely engorged, tortuous, segmented retinal veins displaying alternating narrowings and bulges resembling a string of sausages ('link-sausage' or 'boxcar' veins) on dilated fundoscopic examination; accompanied by diffuse flame-shaped retinal hemorrhages, soft exudates, microaneurysms, and bilateral papilledema, culminating in sudden painless visual loss

Mucocutaneous bleeding: Recurrent, profuse spontaneous epistaxis, persistent gingival bleeding, and prolonged oozing from minor trauma or surgical procedures caused by IgM coating of platelets and clotting factors

Cold-induced cutaneous changes: Acrocyanosis, Raynaud phenomenon, livedo reticularis, purpura, and cold urticaria affecting the fingertips, ears, and nose tip in patients with concomitant Type I IgM cryoglobulinemia or cold agglutinin disease

Neurologic & lymphoproliferative signs: Symmetrical, slowly progressive, distal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy ('numb feet' and ataxia); moderate non-tender peripheral lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT / Ultrasound: Moderate-to-marked homogeneous splenomegaly (in 30-40% of cases) and diffuse, smooth retroperitoneal, mesenteric, and celiac lymphadenopathy; absence of bulky conglomerations or necrotic nodal centers

Whole-Body Skeletal Radiography / CT: Absence of discrete punched-out osteolytic bone lesions (a critical negative radiological sign distinguishing Waldenström from Multiple Myeloma); diffuse osteopenia and mild vertebral demineralization without focal cortical destruction

Whole-Body MRI: Diffuse, homogenous or patchy bone marrow infiltration of the spine, pelvis, and proximal long bones, showing low signal on T1-weighted sequences and hyperintensity on T2/STIR, reflecting extensive lymphoplasmacytic marrow replacement
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow trephine core biopsy & aspirate (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Intertrabecular infiltration (diffuse, interstitial, or nodular) by a clonal mixture of small B-lymphocytes, plasmacytoid lymphocytes, and mature plasma cells (lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, LPL); pathognomonic Dutcher bodies: intranuclear, Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive pseudoinclusions composed of invaginated cytoplasmic immunoglobulin (IgM); presence of cytoplasmic Russell bodies and increased background mast cells intimately admixed with the neoplastic lymphoid cells; IHC: Neoplastic B-cells are positive for CD19, CD20, CD22, and CD79a; plasma cells are CD138+ and CD38+; surface and cytoplasmic IgM monoclonal light chain restriction (predominantly kappa); negative for CD5, CD10, and CD23 (distinguishing from CLL and mantle cell lymphoma); Molecular Genetics: Pathognomonic somatic activating MYD88 L265P mutation detected in >90-95% of cases; CXCR4 mutations present in 30-40% of patients
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Classic lymphoplasmacytic IgM hyperviscosity neoplasm displaying striking 'sausage-link' retinal vein engorgement and cryoglobulinemic acrocyanosis, supported by diffuse marrow replacement without lytic bone lesions on MRI/CT, and Dutcher-body lymphoplasmacytic histology with MYD88 L265P.

Hematology.name: Hemophilia A
clinical_manifestations: Acute hemarthrosis: a warm swollen knee or elbow photographed before chronic arthropathy
Intramuscular hematoma and prolonged bleeding after minor trauma
Chronic arthropathy is a complication and is not a separate topic
radiological_manifestations: Joint radiographs or MRI once hemophilic arthropathy develops; ultrasound of an acute hemarthrosis
pathology_manifestations: No diagnostic tissue pattern; the factor VIII assay is the laboratory image companion, and synovium shows hemosiderin only late
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Bleeding disease with acute joint and soft-tissue photographs. The arthropathy manifestation was removed as its own topic.

Hematology.name: Immune Thrombocytopenia
clinical_manifestations: Dependent petechiae and wet purpura on the buccal mucosa
Scattered ecchymoses without the retiform pattern of vasculitis
radiological_manifestations: No diagnostic radiology; splenic size is normal, which separates it from infiltrative splenomegaly on ultrasound
pathology_manifestations: Increased marrow megakaryocytes if biopsied; skin biopsy is not diagnostic and is used only to exclude vasculitis
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Platelet disorder whose petechial and mucosal photographs are the clinical image, distinct from TTP.

Hematology.name: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
clinical_manifestations: Massive splenomegaly presenting with left upper quadrant fullness, early satiety, and palpable splenic notch descending into the lower quadrant or pelvis
Constitutional B-symptoms including hypermetabolic night sweats, low-grade fevers, and unexplained weight loss
Symptomatic anemia manifesting as pallor, exertional dyspnea, and lethargy
Leukostasis syndrome with priapism, blurred vision, retinal hemorrhages, and dyspnea when leukocyte counts exceed 100,000–300,000/uL
Extramedullary blast proliferation (myeloid sarcoma/chloroma) presenting as green-tinged soft tissue masses during accelerated or blast phase
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasonography: Massive homogeneous splenomegaly measuring >20 cm in craniocaudal length, occasionally displaying triangular hypoechoic peripheral wedges indicative of splenic infarction

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Striking splenic enlargement displacing the left kidney and stomach medialward, with well-demarcated non-enhancing peripheral wedge defects from acute splenic infarctions
Chest Radiography: Severe elevation of the left hemidiaphragm with secondary compression atelectasis of the left lung base
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear: Marked leukocytosis (often >100,000/uL) with the complete differential spectrum of myeloid maturation (myeloblasts, promyelocytes, myelocytes, metamyelocytes, bands, segmented neutrophils); characteristic 'myelocyte bulge' where myelocytes exceed metamyelocytes; absolute basophilia and eosinophilia

Bone Marrow Biopsy: Striking hypercellularity (90–100%) with dominant granulocytic and megakaryocytic hyperplasia, marked reduction in erythroid elements (M:E ratio 10:1 to 30:1), and sea-blue histiocytes (pseudo-Gaucher cells) with lipid-laden cytoplasmic sheets
Cytogenetics / Molecular: Reciprocal translocation t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2) generating the Philadelphia chromosome, with BCR::ABL1 fusion gene identified via FISH or quantitative RT-PCR
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield hematologic neoplasm with pathognomonic peripheral blood smear displaying the complete spectrum of myeloid maturation and classic physical exam findings of massive splenomegaly.

Hematology.name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
clinical_manifestations: Symmetric, painless, rubbery generalized lymphadenopathy involving cervical, supraclavicular, axillary, and inguinal nodal chains
Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly causing abdominal fullness and early satiety
Constitutional symptoms including unintentional weight loss >10% over 6 months, drenching night sweats, and persistent fevers
Exaggerated hypersensitivity reactions to insect/mosquito bites (leukemia cutis or vesicular papular eruption)
Autoimmune cytopenias including autoimmune hemolytic anemia (jaundice, dark urine) and immune thrombocytopenia (petechiae, purpura)
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Neck/Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis CT: Diffuse, symmetric, non-matted, homogeneous lymphadenopathy across mediastinal, retroperitoneal, mesenteric, and iliac chains, accompanied by marked homogeneous splenomegaly
PET/CT: Typically low-grade fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) avidity; intense focal SUV uptake (>5–10) signals histologic transformation into diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Richter transformation)
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear: Absolute clonal B-cell lymphocytosis (>5,000/uL) composed of small, mature-appearing lymphocytes with scant cytoplasm, dense clumped chromatin ('soccer-ball' or 'cracked-mud' appearance), and abundant pathognomonic smudge cells (Gumprecht shadows)
Bone Marrow Biopsy: Diffuse, nodular, or interstitial infiltration of small, mature CD5+/CD19+/CD20+(dim)/CD23+/surface-Ig(dim) monoclonal B lymphocytes with proliferation centers (pseudofollicles)
Flow Cytometry: Co-expression of CD5 and CD23, weak CD20 and surface immunoglobulin expression, light chain restriction (kappa or lambda), and CD200 positivity
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Most common adult leukemia characterized by unmistakable smudge cells (Gumprecht shadows) on blood smear, generalized rubbery lymphadenopathy, and high propensity for Richter transformation.

Hematology.name: Hereditary Spherocytosis
Hematology.subspecialty: Hemolytic Anemias & Red Cell Membrane Disorders
clinical_manifestations: Triad of fluctuating scleral icterus/jaundice, normocytic/microcytic anemia, and splenomegaly
Symptomatic pigmented cholelithiasis presenting in children and young adults with recurrent biliary colic or cholecystitis
Aplastic crisis triggered by Parvovirus B19 infection presenting with sudden profound pallor, lethargy, and absent reticulocytes
Poorly healing chronic pretibial ulcers and delayed growth in severe untreated phenotypes
radiological_manifestations: Right Upper Quadrant Abdominal Ultrasound: Multiple strongly echogenic, mobile gallstones with acoustic shadowing (black pigment/calcium bilirubinate calculi) in a young patient, along with smooth splenomegaly (>13 cm)
Abdominal CT / MRI: Splenomegaly with homogeneous enhancement; calcified radiopaque pigment gallstones within the gallbladder lumen and extrahepatic biliary ducts
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear: Abundant microspherocytes (small, round, darkly staining red cells lacking central pallor), polychromasia, anisopoikilocytosis, and elevated mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC >36 g/dL); Howell-Jolly bodies post-splenectomy
Eosin-5-Maleimide (EMA) Binding Test: Decreased EMA fluorescence by flow cytometry due to deficiency of band 3, spectrin, or ankyrin
Acidified Glycerol Lysis and Osmotic Fragility: Markedly shifted osmotic fragility curve with premature red cell hemolysis in hypotonic saline solutions
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Classic congenital red cell membrane disorder producing pathognomonic dense microspherocytes lacking central pallor on peripheral blood smear and premature pigment cholelithiasis in youth.

Hematology.name: Purpura Fulminans
synonyms: congenital protein C deficiency purpura fulminans
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly progressing, well-demarcated cutaneous ecchymoses that evolve into painful, retiform, stellate purpura with central hemorrhagic bullae and black eschars
Symmetric peripheral gangrene of digits, ears, nose, and extremities requiring limb amputations
Acute hemodynamic collapse, septic shock, and multi-organ failure commonly following Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, or neonatal protein C/S deficiency
Adrenal crisis secondary to acute bilateral hemorrhagic necrosis of the adrenal glands (Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome)
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT: Bilateral enlarged, non-enhancing, or hyperdense adrenal glands indicative of hemorrhagic adrenal infarction (Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome)
Vascular Duplex Ultrasonography: Extensive microvascular and macrovascular thrombosis with absent flow in digital and pedal arteries and deep venous systems
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch/Incisional Biopsy: Extensive microvascular occlusion by dense fibrin thrombi within small dermal and subcutaneous blood vessels, marked endothelial necrosis, red blood cell extravasation, and absence of true leukocytoclastic vasculitis

Peripheral Blood Smear: Consumptive coagulopathy showing marked thrombocytopenia, frequent schistocytes (helmet cells and fragmented red cells indicative of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia), and polychromasia
Coagulation Profile: Profound depletion of fibrinogen, extreme D-dimer elevation, prolonged PT/PTT, and severe reduction in protein C, protein S, or antithrombin activity
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Catastrophic thrombotic emergency presenting with unforgettable retiform purpuric maps and peripheral digital gangrene driven by microvascular fibrin thrombosis and consumable anticoagulants.

Hematology.name: Chédiak-Higashi Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Oculocutaneous albinism with striking metallic silver/silvery-gray hair, pale skin, and ocular hypopigmentation with photophobia and horizontal nystagmus
Severe recurrent pyogenic cutaneous and sinopulmonary infections (Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus) due to defective granulocyte chemotaxis and degranulation
Bleeding diathesis with easy bruising and mucosal oozing secondary to platelet dense granule deficiency (storage pool defect)
Accelerated phase (hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis transformation) characterized by sustained fever, jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, and pancytopenia
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasonography / CT: Massive hepatosplenomegaly and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy developing rapidly during the accelerated hemophagocytic phase
Chest Radiography and CT: Recurrent dense consolidations, bronchiectasis, and cavitation from repeated necrotizing pyogenic bacterial pneumonias
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear: Pathognomonic enormous, peroxidase-positive azurophilic giant lysosomal granules inside neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, and monocytes; giant granules in circulating lymphocytes

Bone Marrow Aspirate / Biopsy: Abundant myeloid precursors packed with colossal giant cytoplasmic granules; hemophagocytic histiocytes engulfing red cells, platelets, and leukocytes during the accelerated phase
Hair Shaft Microscopy: Clumped, regularly spaced, giant melanin granules distributed evenly along the hair shaft under polarized light (distinct from Griscelli or Elejalde syndrome)
Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic biallelic mutations in the LYST (lysosomal trafficking regulator) gene
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Rare autosomal recessive disorder instantly recognized by silvery hair and pathognomonic giant lysosomal granules across all granulocyte lineages on light microscopy.

Hematology.name: Cold Agglutinin Disease
clinical_manifestations: Acrocyanosis: Painful, dark violet/blue discoloration and mottled erythema of digits, nose tip, ears, and cheeks triggered by cold temperatures, reversing upon warming
Livedo reticularis of extremities and peripheral cutaneous necrosis or ulceration in severe cold exposure
Episodic intravascular hemolysis manifesting with dark brown/cola-colored morning hemoglobinuria, jaundice, fatigue, and lower back/abdominal pain
Exacerbation after hypothermic cardiopulmonary bypass surgery or cold ambient environments
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasonography: Mild to moderate splenomegaly; calcium bilirubinate gallstones developing from chronic intravascular and extravascular hemolysis
Peripheral Vascular Doppler: Normal large-caliber arterial anatomy with reversible microvascular flow stagnation and sluggish venous return precipitated by local cold challenge
pathology_manifestations: Gross Blood Sample Inspection: Visible gross red blood cell autoagglutination ('sand-like' clumping) on the glass walls of EDTA collection tubes at room temperature that disperses upon warming to 37°C

Peripheral Blood Smear: Massive, dense aggregates and clumps of erythrocytes at room temperature resembling clusters of grapes, pseudo-macrocytosis (artifactually elevated MCV >120 fL), spherocytes, and reticulocytosis
Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT / Coombs): Strongly positive for complement C3d alone; negative for IgG
Immunohematology: High-titer cold-reactive monoclonal IgM autoantibodies (typically IgM kappa targeting the red blood cell surface I/i antigen)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct autoimmune hemolytic anemia featuring unmistakable physical exam acrocyanosis and macroscopic tube agglutination that dissolves only upon heating to body temperature.

Hematology.name: Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Deficiency
clinical_manifestations: Acute episodic hemolytic crisis occurring 24–72 hours following oxidative triggers (fava beans, rasburicase, primaquine, dapsone, cotrimoxazole, or severe infection)
Sudden onset of dark, red-to-cola colored urine (gross hemoglobinuria) accompanied by acute lumbar/abdominal flank pain
Rapidly progressive scleral icterus, pallor, tachypnea, and hemodynamic instability due to precipitate drop in hemoglobin
Severe neonatal hyperbilirubinemia with high risk of acute bilirubin encephalopathy (kernicterus)
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound: Normal to mildly enlarged spleen during acute crises; gallbladder sludge or radiopaque pigment gallstones in patients with chronic hemolysis (Class I G6PD variants)
Brain MRI (Neonatal Kernicterus Sequelae): Bilateral symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the globus pallidus and subthalamic nuclei
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear (Acute Crisis): Pathognomonic 'bite cells' (degmacytes with semicircular marginal defect excavated by splenic macrophages) and 'blister cells' (erythrocytes with hemoglobin retracted to one pole beneath a thin membrane); polychromasia, nucleated red cells
Supravital Stain (Brilliant Cresyl Blue / Crystal Violet): Distinct round Heinz bodies (precipitated oxidized denatured hemoglobin globules adhering to the inner cell membrane)
Enzymatic Assay: Decreased quantitative G6PD enzyme activity (measured accurately weeks after the hemolytic episode resolves to avoid false-normal reticulocyte readings)
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield X-linked red cell enzymopathy that displays iconic bite cells, blister cells, and Heinz bodies on supravital peripheral smears during oxidative hemolytic crises.

Hematology.name: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia
clinical_manifestations: Unexplained thrombocytopenia (drop in platelet count by >50% from baseline) occurring typically 5–10 days after heparin initiation (or <24 hours with recent heparin exposure)
Paradoxical extensive venous thromboembolism (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism) and arterial thrombosis (stroke, limb ischemia, acute myocardial infarction)
Erythematous, indurated plaques progressing to painful cutaneous skin necrosis at subcutaneous heparin injection sites
Phlegmasia cerulea dolens (massive limb swelling, severe pain, cyanosis, and threatened limb viability) from complete venous outflow occlusion
Acute systemic reactions following IV heparin bolus (chills, diaphoresis, hypertension, tachycardia, transient global amnesia)
radiological_manifestations: Venous Duplex Ultrasound: Acute, occlusive, hypoechoic intraluminal thrombi throughout femoral, popliteal, or upper-extremity deep venous systems

CT Angiography of Chest / Abdomen / Extremities: Massive pulmonary embolism with saddle emboli, bilateral adrenal enlargement with hypodense hemorrhage (adrenal infarction), or abrupt arterial cutoff in peripheral vessels
Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT: Bilateral adrenal hemorrhage secondary to adrenal vein thrombosis, a known life-threatening complication of HIT
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear: Significant thrombocytopenia without schistocytes or red cell fragmentation (rules out TTP/HUS); normal red cell morphology with activated platelet clumps
Skin Biopsy (from injection site necrosis): Extensive intraluminal platelet-rich microvascular fibrin thrombosis in the dermal and subcutaneous vasculature without true vasculitic infiltrate

Functional and Immunoassays: Positive anti-platelet factor 4 (PF4)/heparin ELISA antibodies; confirmatory Serotonin Release Assay (SRA) or heparin-induced platelet aggregation (HIPA) demonstrating high-percentage platelet activation at therapeutic heparin concentrations
Hematology.inclusion_rationale: Crucial immunohematologic complication characterized by paradoxical widespread thromboses, injection site skin necrosis, and limb gangrene provoked by pathogenic PF4-heparin complexes.

Infectious Diseases.name: Actinomycosis
clinical_manifestations: Cervicofacial 'lumpy jaw': extremely hard, indurated, painless, dark-red or purplish 'wooden' swelling over the angle of the jaw or submandibular region
Multiple chronic draining cutaneous sinus tracts that erupt through the skin
Discharge containing macroscopic, gritty, yellowish-white particles known as 'sulfur granules'
Thoracic and abdominopelvic wall fistulous masses
radiological_manifestations: Head/Neck/Chest/Abdominal CT: Aggressive, infiltrative, expansile soft-tissue mass that ignores anatomical tissue planes and fascial boundaries, central areas of low-attenuation necrosis, prominent peripheral rim enhancement, adjacent bone periostitis or osteolysis (mandibular erosion)
Chest CT: Non-segmental airspace consolidation with multiple microcavities and chest wall invasion with rib periostitis
pathology_manifestations: Exudate / surgical biopsy: Characteristic 'sulfur granules' consisting of basophilic masses of tangled branching filamentous Gram-positive bacteria surrounded by an eosinophilic, radiating, club-like Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon; surrounding dense suppurative and xanthogranulomatous inflammation
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Iconic 'lumpy jaw' presentation with woody induration and sulfur granule sinus drainage, matching infiltrative CT masses crossing tissue planes with adjacent bone periostitis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Alveolar Echinococcosis
clinical_manifestations: Hepatic Pseudomalignancy Presentation: Highly aggressive, chronically progressive, tumor-like invasive behavior resembling intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma or hepatocellular carcinoma; right upper quadrant heaviness, epigastric fullness, and hepatomegaly with a hard, irregular, rock-like liver mass

Biliary and Vascular Obstruction: Progressive obstructive jaundice, pruritus, dark urine, and pale stools from direct infiltration into the biliary confluence; secondary biliary cirrhosis and portal hypertension with ascites and bleeding esophageal varices from portal vein invasion (Budd-Chiari-like syndrome)
Distal Metastatic Dissemination: Infiltrative metastases to the lungs, brain, and regional retroperitoneal lymph nodes in advanced, untreated stages
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal CT (Diagnostic Hallmark): Large, ill-defined, infiltrative, heterogeneous hypoattenuating hepatic mass featuring an irregular, lobulated contour and a characteristic 'honeycomb' or multivesicular pattern composed of innumerable microcysts (1-10 mm); scattered amorphous, punctate, micronodular, or ring-like calcifications throughout the lesion ('geographic calcification' or 'stormy sky' appearance) with a central non-enhancing hypodense necrotic core and no peripheral vascular rim enhancement on contrast CT

Abdominal MRI: Heterogeneous mass with hypointense matrix on T1, heterogeneous T2 with innumerable hyperintense tiny microcysts ('bunch of grapes' microvesicles) embedded in a hypointense fibro-inflammatory background; direct invasion into the inferior vena cava, portal vein, and hepatic veins

PET/CT (18F-FDG): Distinct rim of intense metabolic activity surrounding the central cold necrotic cavity, corresponding to the active proliferating germinative metacestode layer at the outer advancing border (essential for monitoring response to albendazole)
pathology_manifestations: Gross Pathology of Hepatic Resection: Extremely firm, gritty, fibrous mass resembling scirrhous carcinoma, displaying a multivesicular spongy, honeycomb architecture with a central, ragged, yellowish-white necrotic liquefactive cavity

Histopathology of Cyst Wall: Microvesicles lined by a thin, folded, acellular, eosinophilic, Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive laminated layer enveloped by an outer proliferative germinal membrane; absence of a thick host fibrous pericyst (unlike Echinococcus granulosus), permitting unrestricted exogenous budding and aggressive contiguous tissue invasion into surrounding hepatic sinusoids

Surrounding Granulomatous Host Reaction: Dense necrotizing epithelioid granulomas, palisading histiocytes, foreign-body multinucleated giant cells, and extensive scirrhous collagenous fibrosis with dystrophic calcification; protoscolices are rarely observed in human tissue (sterile larvae)
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Lethal parasitic pseudomalignancy of the liver characterized by the pathognomonic multivesicular honeycomb mass with 'stormy sky' calcifications on CT/MRI, metabolic rim on PET/CT, and invasively budding PAS-positive laminated microcysts on histology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Amebic Liver Abscess
clinical_manifestations: Hepatic Signs: Constant, dull, aching right upper quadrant (RUQ) abdominal pain, exquisite point tenderness over liver margins and lower right intercostal spaces (positive Murphy's percussion sign), and tender, firm, smooth hepatomegaly
Systemic Signs: High-spiking fevers, rigors, profuse nocturnal diaphoresis, malaise, weight loss, anorexia, and mild jaundice in large or multiple abscesses
Referred Diaphragmatic Pain: Dull aching pain referred to the right shoulder or neck from diaphragmatic irritation

Pathognomonic Pus Aspirate: Thick, odorless, reddish-brown or chocolate-colored viscous fluid traditionally described as 'anchovy paste' or chocolate sauce (consisting of liquefied necrotic hepatocytes rather than viable neutrophils)

Rupture Complications: Peritonitis from intraperitoneal rupture, empyema or hepatobronchial fistula with coughing of 'anchovy paste' sputum from transdiaphragmatic rupture, and pericardial tamponade from left-lobe abscess rupture
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound: Solitary, round or oval, well-defined hypoechoic mass located predominantly (70-80%) in the right hepatic lobe (subcapsular, posterosuperior aspect near the dome), with fine, low-level internal homogeneous echoes without wall calcification, and posterior acoustic enhancement
