Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Major helminthic infection characterized by terminal hematuria, the pathognomonic 'fetal head' calcification of the bladder on radiography, Symmers pipe-stem periportal fibrosis on ultrasound, and definitive terminal/lateral spine egg morphology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Scrub Typhus
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic inoculation eschar ('tache noire'): Begins as a small erythematous papule at the chigger mite bite site, ulcerates, and forms a painless, punched-out ulcer covered by a central dark black necrotic crust surrounded by an erythematous, indurated inflammatory halo (frequently located in intertriginous skin folds: groin, axilla, perineum, under waistband)
Cutaneous rash: Transient, macular or maculopapular, non-pruritic, pink-to-erythematous rash developing around day 5-7, spreading centrifugally from trunk to extremities
Bilateral bulbar conjunctival injection / suffusion without purulent discharge
Painful, tender regional lymphadenopathy draining the eschar site, rapidly evolving into generalized lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT: Bilateral interstitial infiltrates, diffuse ground-glass opacities (GGOs), interlobular septal thickening, bronchial wall thickening, centrilobular nodules, and dependent airspace consolidations; bilateral pleural effusions; signs of acute lung injury / acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
Abdominal Ultrasound / Contrast CT: Hepatosplenomegaly, gallbladder wall thickening with pericholecystic edema, and generalized mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy
Brain Contrast MRI (Scrub Typhus Meningoencephalitis): Leptomeningeal enhancement, multifocal punctate T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in cerebral white matter, and microvascular microbleeds
pathology_manifestations: Skin eschar punch biopsy: Acute, systemic, infective microvascular endothelitis and perivasculitis: swelling and proliferation of vascular endothelial cells, transmural infiltration of mononuclear leukocytes (predominantly CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes and histiocytes), microvascular thrombosis, erythrocyte extravasation, and full-thickness epidermal coagulative necrosis overlying dermal necrosis

Immunohistochemistry (IHC) / PCR: Specific identification of Orientia tsutsugamushi bacterial antigens localized within the cytoplasm of vascular endothelial cells and perivascular mononuclear phagocytes
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential chigger-borne rickettsial illness recognized by the pathognomonic black 'tache noire' inoculation eschar, bilateral ground-glass pneumonitis on chest CT, and systemic endothelial vasculitis on histopathology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Severe Generalized Tetanus
clinical_manifestations: Trismus ('lockjaw'): Severe, painful tonic contraction and involuntary spasm of the masseter and temporalis muscles, preventing the patient from opening the mouth; elicited by the spatula test (touching the posterior pharyngeal wall with a tongue spatula causes reflex spasm of the masseters and biting down, rather than the normal gag reflex)

Risus sardonicus ('sardonic grin'): Pathognomonic grotesque facial grimace caused by continuous, sustained tonic contraction of the facial expression muscles (frontalis, orbicularis oris, and risorius), resulting in sustained elevation of the eyebrows, deep horizontal forehead furrowing, and retraction of the oral commissures exposing clenched teeth

Opisthotonos and board-like abdominal rigidity: Extreme, violent hyper-extension of the entire axial skeleton where the spine, neck, and lower extremities arch backward into a rigid bridge supported only by the back of the head and the heels; accompanied by stony 'board-like' involuntary rigidity of the abdominal wall and chest

Stimulus-induced reflex tetanic spasms: Excruciatingly painful, generalized paroxysmal muscle spasms triggered by minimal auditory, visual, or tactile stimuli (sudden noise, turning on lights, touching the bed, drafts of air), during which the patient remains fully conscious and alert, with flexed fists held tightly against the chest and extended lower limbs

Autonomic storm / sympathetic hyperactivity: Severe cardiovascular instability beginning several days into the illness, characterized by fluctuating malignant hypertension alternating with profound hypotension, persistent resting tachycardia, cardiac arrhythmias, profuse drenching diaphoresis, hyperpyrexia, and peripheral vasoconstriction due to disinhibition of preganglionic sympathetic neurons in the brainstem and spinal cord
radiological_manifestations: Thoracic and Lumbar Spine Plain Radiographs / CT: Classic, pathognomonic mid-thoracic vertebral compression fractures (typically T4-T8) resulting from the violent, unremitting force of paraspinous and paraspinal muscle contractions against the bony skeleton in conscious patients; often accompanied by compression deformities of anterior vertebral bodies

Skeletal Plain Films and CT: Heterotopic ossification of periarticular soft tissues (particularly around hips and elbows) developing secondary to sustained immobility, muscle hypertonicity, and tissue hypoxia; fractures of the femoral neck, humeral head, or avulsion of muscular insertions

Soft Tissue Radiography and Wound CT: Identification of radiopaque foreign bodies (soil, wood splinters, rusted metal fragments) or pockets of gas within devitalized, necrotic soft tissue tracking from the primary inoculation puncture site
pathology_manifestations: Pathophysiology and Toxin Mechanism: Infection of devitalized, anaerobic puncture wounds by spores of Clostridium tetani, which germinate and elaborate tetanospasmin (tetanus neurotoxin, TeNT), a 150-kDa zinc-dependent endopeptidase; TeNT undergoes retrograde intra-axonal transport along peripheral motor neurons to the central nervous system, where it enters inhibitory interneurons (Renshaw cells) and selectively cleaves synaptobrevin-2 (VAMP-2), abolishing the presynaptic exocytosis of glycine and GABA, producing unchecked motor neuron disinhibition, continuous resting tone, and reflex spasms

Microbiology: Gram stain of wound tissue or debrided exudate demonstrating slender, Gram-positive (or Gram-variable in older cultures) rod with a spherical, terminal spore yielding a pathognomonic 'drumstick' or 'tennis racket' morphology; strict obligate anaerobe; diagnosis is fundamentally clinical as blood cultures are uniformly negative and wound cultures are positive in only ~30% of cases
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Unforgettable neurotoxic disease presenting with unmistakable photographic physical signs—risus sardonicus, trismus, and opisthotonos—sparing consciousness during excruciating reflex spasms, complicated radiologically by thoracic compression fractures from pure muscular force.

Infectious Diseases.name: Severe Leptospirosis (Weil's Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic physical examination sign: Dramatic bilateral conjunctival suffusion (deep ciliary and scleral erythema/vascular injection without purulent discharge or chemosis) appearing within the first 48-72 hours

Severe triad of Weil's syndrome: (1) deep, intense, orange-yellow jaundice / icterus with hepatomegaly, (2) acute oliguric renal failure with azotemia, and (3) generalized hemorrhagic diathesis (petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, epistaxis, pulmonary hemorrhage)
Severe, exquisite muscle tenderness and hyperesthesia, characteristically concentrated in the calves, thighs, and paraspinal/lumbar musculature
Severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome (SPHS): Acute hemoptysis, cyanosis, and catastrophic respiratory arrest
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / High-Resolution CT: Classic diffuse, bilateral, patchy ground-glass opacities, alveolar consolidations, and a coarse 'snowstorm' appearance representing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, predominantly involving the lower and middle lobes; resolution or rapid migration over 24-48 hours

Abdominal Ultrasound: Hepatomegaly with patent bile ducts, acute acalculous cholecystitis (marked gallbladder wall thickening, mucosal striation, pericholecystic fluid halo), and bilaterally enlarged, swollen kidneys with hyperechoic cortex and loss of corticomedullary differentiation
pathology_manifestations: Lung histopathology: Massive intra-alveolar and interstitial hemorrhage, disruption of capillary endothelial basement membranes, extensive fibrin thrombi in alveolar capillaries, without significant inflammatory infiltrate (bystander capillary damage)

Liver and Kidney histology: Liver demonstrates disarray of hepatic cords, marked intracellular and canalicular cholestasis, and Kupffer cell hyperplasia without massive hepatocellular necrosis; kidneys exhibit acute tubular injury, interstitial edema, and dense interstitial mononuclear nephritis

Warthin-Starry / Steiner silver impregnation stain: Slender, tightly coiled, flexible spirochetes (6-20 um long, 0.1 um wide) with characteristic hooked or bent ends (resembling a question mark or umbrella handle) visible within renal tubular lumens, interstitial tissue, and hepatic sinusoids
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Iconic severe spirochetal zoonosis featuring pathognomonic non-purulent conjunctival suffusion, Weil's jaundice-renal failure triad, 'snowstorm' pulmonary hemorrhage on chest CT, and hooked spirochetes on silver stain.

Infectious Diseases.name: Sporotrichosis
clinical_manifestations: Classic lymphocutaneous presentation ('sporotrichoid spread'): Initial painless erythematous subcutaneous nodule at the site of minor skin trauma ('sporotrichotic chancre'), which ulcerates into an indolent violaceous ulcer with a ragged undermined edge

Subsequent eruption of a linear, ascending chain of painless, firm, nodular subcutaneous lesions along proximal draining lymphatics ('sporotrichoid cord'), which progressively soften, fluctuate, ulcerate, and discharge serosanguinous/purulent fluid
Fixed cutaneous form: Solitary, indurated, verrucous, vegetative, or ulcerated plaque without lymphatic dissemination
Extracutaneous osteoarticular sporotrichosis: Chronic asymmetric monoarthritis (knee, wrist) with chronic joint effusion, soft tissue swelling, and periarticular sinus tract formation
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal Radiography / MRI (Osteoarticular Sporotrichosis): Asymmetric periarticular osteopenia, marginal bone erosions, joint space narrowing, and cortical lytic lesions; contrast MRI reveals pronounced synovial hypertrophy, nodular pannus formation, and extensive soft-tissue abscesses tracking along tendon sheaths

Chest CT (Pulmonary Sporotrichosis): Chronic upper-lobe predominant cavitary infiltrates with irregular thick walls, surrounding parenchymal fibrosis, and architectural distortion, frequently mimicking secondary tuberculosis; ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch / synovial biopsy (H&E, GMS, PAS stains): Suppurative granulomatous dermatitis and panniculitis featuring central microabscesses dominated by neutrophils, encircled by a granulomatous mantle of epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans multinucleated giant cells, and dense plasma cells

Microscopic fungal morphology: Pleomorphic, round, oval, and classic elongated 'cigar-shaped' budding yeast cells (2-6 um in length); pathognomonic 'asteroid body' (Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon) displaying a central round basophilic yeast cell encircled by radiating, club-like, brightly eosinophilic spicules
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Definitive prototype of ascending nodular lymphocutaneous infection ('sporotrichoid spread') with classic rose-gardener/feline contact history, tuberculous-like upper lobe cavities on chest CT, and cigar-shaped yeasts with asteroid bodies on pathology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Strongyloidiasis Hyperinfection Syndrome and Disseminated Strongyloidiasis
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Larva Currens: Rapidly progressing, pruritic, raised, serpiginous, urticarial linear cutaneous eruption moving at astonishing speed (5 to 10 cm per hour - the fastest migrating parasitic lesion in medicine), predominantly distributed over the buttocks, perianal region, groin, thighs, and trunk

Thumbprint Purpura: Characteristic scattered, purpuric, petechial macules and ecchymoses across the lower periumbilical abdomen and thighs caused by larval extravasation and dermal microvascular rupture

Hyperinfection Gastrointestinal and Pulmonary Syndrome: Severe watery diarrhea, paralytic ileus, severe abdominal distension, intestinal obstruction, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage with hemoptysis, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) triggered by immunosuppressive therapy (especially high-dose systemic corticosteroids or HTLV-1 co-infection)

Recurrent Polymicrobial Sepsis and Meningitis: Gram-negative bacteremia (E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus) and bacterial meningitis caused by enteric bacteria carried on the cuticle or in the gut lumen of hyper-migrating filariform larvae piercing the bowel wall
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT: Extensive bilateral ground-glass opacities, focal or confluent consolidations, and interlobular septal thickening representing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema; multifocal patchy infiltrates and 'tree-in-bud' nodular opacities corresponding to larval migration through bronchovascular bundles

Abdominal Plain Radiograph and CT: Marked dilation of small bowel loops with loss of normal mucosal fold architecture ('pipestem' or 'featureless' rigid duodenum and jejunum), severe paralytic ileus, duodenal wall thickening, and pneumatosis intestinalis in transmural necrosis
pathology_manifestations: Direct Sputum, Stool, and Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) Wet Prep: Massive swarms of active, wriggling rhabditiform and infectious filariform larvae; filariform larvae measure 500-600 um in length, have a long esophagus extending half the length of the body, and possess a pathognomonic notched, bifurcated tail (forked tail tip)

Duodenal and Jejunal Biopsy Histopathology: Profound infiltration of the lamina propria with eosinophils and plasma cells, villous blunting, crypt hyperplasia, and cross-sections of adult female worms, rhabditiform larvae, and embryonated eggs directly embedded within mucosal crypts of Lieberkuhn

Extraintestinal Organ Histopathology: In disseminated disease, filariform larvae identified in tissue sections of the lung alveoli, myocardium, kidneys, brain, and skin alongside extravasated erythrocytes and mixed inflammatory cells
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Catastrophic parasitic emergency featuring the lightning-fast migrating 'larva currens' and periumbilical 'thumbprint purpura' on physical exam, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage on chest CT, and notched-tail filariform larvae on sputum/BAL microscopy.

Infectious Diseases.name: Syphilis
clinical_manifestations: Primary: painless, indurated, clean-based ulcer (chancre) with raised borders and painless regional lymphadenopathy

Secondary: symmetrical non-pruritic copper-red ('raw ham') papulosquamous eruption predominantly on palms and soles (syphilitic collarette of Biett); condylomata lata (flat, moist, highly infectious whitish papules in anogenital folds); mucosal mucous patches; moth-eaten alopecia
Tertiary: destructive noduloulcerative gummas (face, palate, extremities), Charcot joints, Argyll Robertson pupils (accommodate but do not react to light)
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT Angiography / MRA: Cardiovascular syphilis: ascending aortic aneurysm with pathognomonic linear calcification of the ascending aorta ('tree-bark calcification'), aortic valve insufficiency, ostial coronary stenosis

Brain MRI: Meningovascular syphilis: basal leptomeningeal enhancement, arteritis with cerebral ischemic strokes; parenchymal syphilitic gummas (ring-enhancing dural-based lesions mimicking meningiomas); tabes dorsalis (dorsal column atrophy and hyperintensity)
Skeletal Radiography: Gummatous osteitis and periostitis with mixed lytic and sclerotic bone remodeling
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy: Dense perivascular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate rich in plasma cells; marked endothelial cell swelling and proliferation leading to obliterative endarteritis ('onion-peel' intimal fibrosis); gummas display central coagulative gummatous necrosis surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes and plasma cells; spirochetes demonstrated by Warthin-Starry stain or Treponema immunohistochemistry
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: 'The Great Imitator' featuring pathognomonic palmoplantar copper collarettes and condylomata lata paired with linear ascending aortic calcification on chest CT and cerebral gummas on brain MRI.

Infectious Diseases.name: Talaromycosis
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark skin manifestation: Generalized, widespread, painless umbilicated papules with central necrotic crusts or ulcerations resembling molluscum contagiosum (predominantly involving the face, ears, neck, chest, and upper extremities)
Infiltrated plaques, pustules, subcutaneous nodules, and necrotic mucosal ulcers of the palate and tongue
High remittent fever, profound constitutional wasting/cachexia, and severe anemia
Marked generalized lymphadenopathy and progressive hepatosplenomegaly (in patients with advanced HIV/CD4 < 100 or non-HIV immunocompromise in Southeast Asia)
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / High-Resolution CT: Diffuse, bilateral interstitial reticulonodular opacities; patchy multifocal alveolar consolidations with air bronchograms; thin- and thick-walled cavitary nodules; extensive necrotic mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy; pleural effusions

Abdominal CT / Ultrasound: Marked hepatosplenomegaly with multiple discrete, round, hypodense/hypoechoic microabscesses scattered in the splenic parenchyma; extensive retroperitoneal and mesenteric necrotic lymphadenopathy
Musculoskeletal CT / MRI: Multifocal osteolytic bone lesions involving the ribs, skull, and appendicular skeleton, associated with overlying soft-tissue cold abscesses
pathology_manifestations: Wright-Giemsa / GMS / PAS stains of skin scraping, bone marrow, or lymph node biopsy: Innumerable small (2-8 um), round, oval, or sausage-shaped yeast-like cells situated intracellularly within histiocytes and extracellularly; pathognomonic finding is a distinctive internal transverse cross-wall (binary fission septum) rather than budding, distinguishing it from Histoplasma

Fungal culture morphology: Characteristic thermal dimorphism producing a distinctive water-soluble, diffusible deep-red/wine-colored pigment that stains Sabouraud dextrose agar at 25 deg C, with conversion to a yeast form at 37 deg C
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Key Southeast Asian dimorphic endemic mycosis featuring hallmark molluscum-like umbilicated necrotic facial papules, cavitary bronchopneumonia with necrotic lymphadenopathy on CT, and intracellular fission yeasts on cytology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Trichinellosis (Trichinosis)
clinical_manifestations: Classical Diagnostic Clinical Tetrad: (1) Sudden-onset, symmetrical, non-pitting bilateral periorbital and facial edema (classically accompanied by prominent chemosis, subconjunctival hemorrhages, and photophobia); (2) Severe muscle pain and tenderness (myalgia) with wooden induration exacerbated by muscle contraction, predominantly involving extraocular muscles, masseters (causing trismus and difficulty chewing), diaphragm, intercostals, and proximal limb muscles; (3) High persistent fever (39-40 C) with rigors and profuse diaphoresis; (4) Subungual splinter hemorrhages (characteristic linear, dark reddish-brown hemorrhages beneath fingernails and toenails)

Extreme Laboratory Marker: Striking, profound leukocytosis with marked peripheral eosinophilia (often 30-70%, reaching absolute counts >5,000/uL) and massive serum creatine kinase (CK) and aldolase elevation
Severe Complications: Lethal acute myocarditis (arrhythmias, congestive heart failure) and neurotrichinellosis (encephalopathy, stroke-like focal deficits)
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal MRI: Bilateral, symmetrical, diffuse or patchy areas of high signal intensity on T2-weighted and STIR sequences within affected skeletal muscles (deltoids, biceps, quadriceps, gastrocnemius), accompanied by intense heterogeneous intramuscular contrast enhancement on T1-gadolinium images, reflecting active acute infectious myositis

High-Frequency Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Diffuse hypoechoic thickening and swelling of skeletal muscle bundles with loss of normal fibrillar pennate architecture and localized intramuscular fluid collections

Soft Tissue Plain Radiography: In remote, longstanding cases (years later), fine, minute, punctate or oval calcifications (0.5-1.0 mm) oriented parallel to muscle fibers representing calcified nurse cell-larva complexes
pathology_manifestations: Skeletal Muscle Biopsy (Diagnostic Gold Standard - Deltoid or Gastrocnemius, performed 3-4 weeks post-infection): Fresh muscle crush preparation (compressorium technique) or histopathologic examination: pathognomonic coiled, spiral nematode larva (Trichinella spiralis, measuring ~1 mm long) encysted within an altered skeletal muscle cell known as a 'Nurse Cell'

Nurse Cell Complex Histology: The infected myofiber loses its transverse striations, undergoes basophilic transformation, develops multiple enlarged vesicular nuclei, and becomes enveloped by a thick, eosinophilic collagenous capsule (0.3-0.5 mm) with a surrounding network of newly formed capillaries (hyperangiogenesis)

Surrounding Tissue Reaction: Intense interstitial myositis with a prominent infiltrate composed primarily of eosinophils, histiocytes, lymphocytes, and occasional multinucleated giant cells; late stages demonstrate complete larva necrosis and dystrophic shell-like calcification of the nurse cell complex
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Classic foodborne parasitic myositis presenting with the hallmark bedside tetrad of periorbital edema, trismus/myalgia, high fever, and subungual splinter hemorrhages, symmetrical muscle inflammation on MRI, and pathognomonic coiled larvae in nurse cells on muscle biopsy.

Infectious Diseases.name: Tuberculosis
clinical_manifestations: Scrofula (scrofuloderma): massive cervical lymphadenitis forming firm, cold, matted masses that break down into chronic draining sinus tracts with bluish undermined borders
Lupus vulgaris: reddish-brown gelatinous plaques on face/neck demonstrating classic 'apple-jelly' nodules upon glass diascopy
Erythema induratum of Bazin: painful, violaceous nodules on the posterior lower calves that ulcerate
Pott disease physical gibbus deformity (sharp angular kyphosis of the spine due to anterior vertebral collapse)
Miliary TB: choroidal tubercles on fundoscopy
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / CT: Apical and posterior segment upper lobe cavitary lesions with thick irregular walls; 'tree-in-bud' branching centrilobular opacities (endobronchial spread); miliary mottling (1-3 mm diffuse uniform micronodules); Ghon focus and calcified Ranke complex
Spine MRI / CT (Pott Disease): Destruction of adjacent anterior vertebral bodies and intervening intervertebral disc; prevertebral and paraspinal 'cold abscess' with thick peripheral rim enhancement
Brain MRI: Intense basilar meningeal enhancement, tuberculomas (ring-enhancing lesions with central T2 hypointensity), vasculitic infarcts
pathology_manifestations: Histology: Caseating (necrotizing) granulomas with central amorphous eosinophilic caseous necrosis surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans multinucleated giant cells (horseshoe-shaped nuclei), and lymphocytes; positive Ziehl-Neelsen (acid-fast) or auramine-rhodamine fluorescence staining
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: The supreme visual infectious disease with iconic bedside lesions (scrofula, lupus vulgaris, Pott gibbus) and landmark radiology (cavitary upper lobe CT, miliary TB, spinal Pott cold abscesses).

Infectious Diseases.name: Tularemia
clinical_manifestations: Ulceroglandular tularemia (most common clinical form, ~75-85%): Punched-out, painful, indurated cutaneous ulcer with sharply circumscribed, raised, erythematous borders and a deep, necrotic or yellow-slough base at the arthropod bite or animal handling site

Disproportionate, massive, tender regional lymphadenopathy (epitrochlear, axillary, cervical, or inguinal) that rapidly enlarges, becomes fluctuant ('bubo-like'), and may spontaneously suppurate and drain

Oculoglandular tularemia (Parinaud oculoglandular syndrome): Severe, unilateral, painful conjunctivitis with yellowish chemotic granulomatous ulcers on the palpebral conjunctiva, periorbital edema, and massive ipsilateral preauricular/submandibular lymphadenopathy
Oropharyngeal tularemia: Severe membranous pharyngotonsillitis with deep tonsillar ulcers and painful cervical lymphadenopathy
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT / Ultrasound of Lymph Nodes: Markedly enlarged, matted, conglomerate regional lymph node complexes with prominent peripheral rim enhancement and central low-attenuation cystic liquefactive necrosis (suppurative lymphadenitis) with extensive surrounding soft-tissue edema

Chest CT (Pneumonic / Systemic Tularemia): Patchy lobar, segmental, or subsegmental consolidation with air bronchograms, cavitary pulmonary nodules, pleural effusion, and prominent, asymmetric, necrotic hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Abdominal Contrast CT: Multiple small, round, low-attenuation microabscesses or granulomas scattered throughout the spleen and liver parenchyma
pathology_manifestations: Lymph node excision / core biopsy (H&E stain): Classic progression of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation: central confluent caseous-like or coagulative suppurative necrosis surrounded by an inner palisade of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated Langhans giant cells, encased within a dense outer cuff of lymphocytes and plasma cells (closely resembling tuberculosis or cat scratch disease)

Microbiologic staining: Francisella tularensis are extremely tiny (0.2 x 0.7 um), poorly staining, pleomorphic, non-motile Gram-negative coccobacilli; rarely visualized on standard Gram stain; definitive identification by direct immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, or real-time PCR
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-consequence zoonotic pathogen presenting with punched-out inoculation ulcers, massive suppurative regional lymphadenopathy, cavitary bronchopneumonia with necrotic hilar nodes on CT, and stellate necrotizing granulomas on biopsy.

Infectious Diseases.name: Visceral Leishmaniasis (Kala-Azar)
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Clinical Pentad: (1) Massive, progressive, non-tender splenomegaly (splenic edge frequently descending below the umbilicus into the right lower quadrant/pelvis); (2) Moderate, smooth, non-tender hepatomegaly; (3) Prolonged, irregular, undulating high fever with double daily peaks (dromedary curve); (4) Profound cachexia, temporal wasting, and severe emaciation contrasting with the protuberant belly; (5) Characteristic gray-black or ashen hyperpigmentation of the face, hands, feet, and abdominal midline ('kala-azar' = black sickness)
Pancytopenia Manifestations: Mucosal bleeding, epistaxis, petechiae, severe pallor from anemia, and secondary bacterial infections (noma/cancrum oris, pneumonia)

Post-Kala-Azar Dermal Leishmaniasis (PKDL): Chronic dermatologic complication arising months to years after successful visceral cure, characterized by hypopigmented macules evolving into erythematous butterfly-distribution facial plaques and nodular granulomas resembling lepromatous leprosy
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound: Massive, homogeneous splenomegaly (frequently >20 cm in craniocaudal dimension) with normal or mildly hypoechoic architecture, occasional focal hypoechoic splenic microabscesses or infarctions, hepatomegaly with smooth contours, and generalized intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy (porta hepatis, retroperitoneum, and mesentery)

Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT: Huge splenomegaly displacing the stomach and left kidney, patent portal and splenic veins without cirrhotic distortion, and retroperitoneal/peripancreatic lymphadenopathy
Chest Radiography: Secondary opportunistic bronchopneumonia and basilar atelectasis from marked diaphragmatic splinting by the enlarged spleen
pathology_manifestations: Bone Marrow, Splenic, or Lymph Node Aspirate: Giemsa- or Leishman-stained smears demonstrate abundant intracellular and extracellular Leishman-Donovan (LD) Bodies (Amastigotes); amastigotes are tiny (2-4 um), round-to-oval organisms lacking a free flagellum, containing a prominent spherical nucleus and a distinct, pathognomonic, rod-shaped or bar-shaped organelle termed the kinetoplast (oriented perpendicularly or obliquely to the nucleus)

Reticuloendothelial Hyperplasia: Marked proliferation of macrophages and histiocytes engorged with hundreds of amastigotes throughout the red pulp of the spleen, hepatic Kupffer cells, and bone marrow cords; marked bone marrow erythroid, myeloid, and megakaryocytic hypoplasia with pronounced reactive polyclonal plasmacytosis

Immunodiagnostics: Recombinant rK39 immunochromatographic rapid strip test positive for anti-leishmanial antibodies; kinetoplast DNA (kDNA) real-time PCR demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Neglected tropical protozoan disease featuring massive splenomegaly, characteristic skin hyperpigmentation ('black fever'), ultrasound documentation of organomegaly, and pathognomonic amastigotes with rod-shaped kinetoplasts on bone marrow/splenic aspirate.

Infectious Diseases.name: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis
clinical_manifestations: A chronic crateriform ulcer with a rolled edge on an exposed site
Mucocutaneous disease: destructive nasal and lip ulcers, filed as the mucosal site of the same infection
radiological_manifestations: No routine radiology; facial CT only for destructive mucocutaneous bone loss
pathology_manifestations: Dermal amastigotes in macrophages on Giemsa or biopsy
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Protozoal ulcer with a classic clinical photograph and a visible parasite.

Infectious Diseases.name: Herpes Zoster
clinical_manifestations: Dermatomal vesicles on an erythematous base that do not cross the midline
Herpes zoster ophthalmicus with a Hutchinson sign on the nose
Disseminated zoster in an immunocompromised patient remains the same disease
radiological_manifestations: MRI only for the rare zoster myelitis or vasculopathy complication, which is not a separate topic
pathology_manifestations: Multinucleated keratinocytes and acantholysis; PCR of vesicle fluid confirms VZV
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Reactivation infection with a dermatomal photograph. Postherpetic neuralgia is a symptom and is not a topic.

Infectious Diseases.name: Mpox
clinical_manifestations: Firm deep-seated umbilicated pustules in the same stage across a region
Anogenital and oral mucosal lesions in the 2022 clade pattern
Palmar and plantar pustules
radiological_manifestations: No routine imaging; proctitis MRI is a complication, not the topic
pathology_manifestations: Orthopox viral cytopathic effect; PCR distinguishes mpox from varicella
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Poxvirus whose umbilicated pustule photographs are the diagnostic image.

Infectious Diseases.name: Measles
clinical_manifestations: Koplik spots on the buccal mucosa opposite the molars
Cephalocaudal morbilliform eruption that becomes confluent on the face
Conjunctivitis and a toxic febrile appearance
radiological_manifestations: Chest radiograph only if pneumonia complicates the illness; the gallery is the spots and rash
pathology_manifestations: Warthin-Finkeldey giant cells in lymphoid tissue when biopsied, which is uncommon
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Viral exanthem with two photographable hallmarks, Koplik spots and the confluent rash.

Infectious Diseases.name: Respiratory Diphtheria
clinical_manifestations: Adherent gray pharyngeal pseudomembrane that bleeds when lifted
Bull neck from cervical edema
Cutaneous diphtheria ulcers are a site of the same infection, not a separate topic
radiological_manifestations: Neck soft-tissue radiograph or endoscopy images of airway membrane when intubation is considered
pathology_manifestations: Toxin-producing Corynebacterium diphtheriae on culture; the membrane is necrotic epithelium and fibrin
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Toxin disease with a membrane photograph and a bull-neck photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Yaws
clinical_manifestations: Primary mother yaw: a papillomatous raspberry lesion
Secondary disseminated papillomas and palmoplantar keratoderma
Late gangosa nasal destruction and saber tibia, kept as late sites of yaws rather than new topics
radiological_manifestations: Tibial radiograph: periosteal new bone in late osteoperiostitis
pathology_manifestations: Epidermal hyperplasia with treponemes on silver stain; serology crosses with syphilis, so geography and the photograph matter
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Endemic treponematosis with papilloma photographs and a late bone film, distinct from venereal syphilis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Orf
clinical_manifestations: A targetoid nodule on a finger after sheep or goat exposure, evolving through macule, target, weeping nodule, and crust
Usually a single lesion on the hand
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: Ballooning keratinocytes and eosinophilic inclusions; parapoxvirus PCR confirms
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Zoonotic poxvirus with a staged hand photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease
clinical_manifestations: Oval gray vesicles on the palms, soles, and buttocks
Painful oral vesicles and shallow ulcers
Onychomadesis weeks later is a sequela, not a separate topic
radiological_manifestations: No radiology
pathology_manifestations: Reticular degeneration of the epidermis; enterovirus PCR when needed
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Enteroviral illness with a distribution-specific vesicle photograph.

Infectious Diseases.name: Cutaneous Larva Migrans
clinical_manifestations: Intensely pruritic, erythematous, elevated, serpiginous, winding, snake-like burrowing cutaneous tracks ("creeping eruption") advancing millimeters to centimeters per day

Acral and dependent anatomical distribution: predilection for barefoot-exposed surfaces including the dorsum and soles of the feet, interdigital web spaces, buttocks, thighs, and hands following contact with tropical beach sand or moist soil contaminated with animal feces

Progression of lesions: initial erythematous pruritic papule at the larval penetration site evolving into a tortuous, raised, red or pink linear track (1-3 mm wide) with localized vesicular or bullous formation along the burrow

Excoriation, secondary impetiginization (Staphylococcus aureus / Streptococcus pyogenes superinfection), and severe sleep-disrupting nocturnal pruritus caused by trapped non-human hookworm larvae (Ancylostoma braziliense, Ancylostoma caninum)
radiological_manifestations: Dermoscopy (Epiluminescence Microscopy): Direct non-invasive visualization of the translucent nematode larva within the advancing terminus of the burrow; demonstrates brownish-yellow translucent oval structures with red dots and empty winding tracks with white scales
Reflectance Confocal Microscopy (RCM): In vivo visualization of round-to-oval refractile structures corresponding to hookworm larvae within the stratum spinosum and stratum basale
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology (rarely required for diagnosis): Biopsy of the advancing edge demonstrates an intraepidermal or subepidermal burrow with marked epidermal spongiosis, necrotic keratinocytes, and intraepidermal eosinophilic microabscesses

Inflammatory infiltrate: Dense dermal perivascular and interstitial infiltrate packed with eosinophils, mast cells, and mononuclear cells; the migrating larva is rarely caught on single sections due to its location 1-2 cm ahead of the visible inflammatory erythema
Peripheral Blood Laboratory: Peripheral eosinophilia (>500 cells/mcL) in 20-30% of extensive or disseminated cases
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-yield parasitic tropical infection with indelible, pathognomonic clinical photographs of winding, serpiginous creeping eruption tracks across bare feet and buttocks.

Infectious Diseases.name: Rhinoscleroma
clinical_manifestations: Chronic, progressive granulomatous bacterial infection of the upper respiratory tract caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae subsp. rhinoscleromatis
Triphasic clinical evolution: 1) Catarrhal/atrophic phase with persistent purulent rhinorrhea and crusting mimicking ozena; 2) Granulomatous/hypertrophic phase; 3) Cicatricial/sclerotic phase
Granulomatous phase physical findings: progressive development of woody, rock-hard, non-tender, reddish-blue nodular infiltrates in the nasal mucosa and vestibule

Pathognomonic facial deformity: "Hebra nose" or tapir snout deformity—striking widening, bulbous expansion, and woody induration of the lower half of the external nose with complete obliteration of the anterior nares
Extension into upper airway: infiltration and destruction of the nasal septum, hard/soft palate, uvula, and subglottic larynx leading to stridor, airway compromise, and hoarseness
radiological_manifestations: Maxillofacial & Neck CT: Soft-tissue masses with homogeneous or heterogeneous contrast enhancement occupying the nasal cavity, maxillary sinuses, and nasopharynx, with destruction and remodeling of the nasal septum and turbinates without regional lymphadenopathy
Laryngeal & Neck CT: Circumferential subglottic soft-tissue stenosis and concentric tracheal narrowing ("hour-glass" trachea)

Head & Neck MRI: Soft-tissue masses demonstrating intermediate signal on T1-weighted images and markedly hypointense signal on T2-weighted images corresponding to dense fibrosis and hypercellular granulomatous tissue
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy of Nasal Mass (Pathognomonic Histology): Diagnostic "Mikulicz cells"—massively distended, pale, foamy or vacuolated macrophages (20-100 μm) with reticulated cytoplasm and eccentric nuclei
Special Staining: Warthin-Starry silver, Giemsa, and Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stains directly reveal intracellular Gram-negative bacilli packed inside the cytoplasm of Mikulicz cells

Plasma Cell Inclusions: Abundant surrounding plasma cells with prominent Russell bodies (eosinophilic globular proteinaceous immunoglobulin inclusions) and dense interlacing collagen fibrosis in the cicatricial stage
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Striking infectious disease featuring unmistakable photographic facial deformities (woody Hebra nose / tapir snout obliterating the nares) and diagnostic Mikulicz cells on histology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Rhinosporidiosis
clinical_manifestations: Chronic granulomatous mucocutaneous infection caused by the aquatic mesomycetozoan protoctist Rhinosporidium seeberi (acquired from bathing in stagnant pond water in South Asia and tropical regions)

Pathognomonic fleshy mucocutaneous lesions: friable, vascular, sessile or pedunculated, mulberry-like or "strawberry-like" polypoid masses protruding from the nasal cavity (septum, inferior turbinate) or conjunctiva

Characteristic surface appearance: bright red, glistening, vascular masses covered with visible tiny white, yellowish, or greyish pinhead-sized dots representing mature subepithelial sporangia ready to rupture

Ocular presentation (Oculosporidiosis): bright red polypoid vascular mass originating from the palpebral conjunctiva, caruncle, or lacrimal sac with foreign body sensation, bloody epiphora, and eversion of the eyelid
Associated signs: recurrent unilateral epistaxis, partial or total nasal obstruction, serosanguinous discharge, and visible mass hanging from the anterior nares or dangling into the oropharynx
radiological_manifestations: Paranasal Sinus CT: Well-defined, hyperattenuating, polypoid soft-tissue mass filling the nasal cavity with focal remodeling or thinning of adjacent bony sinus walls without frank osseous invasion

Facial MRI: Intensely enhancing lobulated nasal mass showing heterogeneous intermediate T1 signal and hypointense to isointense T2 signal with punctate hyperintense foci corresponding to cystic sporangia
CT Angiography: Conspicuous hypervascularity with rich arterial feeder vessels (typically from sphenopalatine and facial arteries) requiring preoperative consideration of embolization
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy / Surgical Excision (Diagnostic Hallmark): Enormous, thick-walled, globular sporangia (100 to 450 μm in diameter) embedded within hyperplastic, vascularized mucosal stroma
Sporangiospores: Mature sporangia are packed with thousands (up to 12,000) of round, basophilic endospores (6-7 μm), seen in various stages of maturation with an apical operculum / germ pore

Histochemical Stains: Sporangial walls stain intensely with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS), Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS), and Mucicarmine; surrounded by a chronic granulomatous reaction with histiocytes, foreign-body giant cells, and vascular granulation tissue
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Visually unmistakable tropical infectious entity featuring classic clinical photographs of friable strawberry-like bleeding nasal polyps studded with white dots, verified by giant mature sporangia on histology.

Infectious Diseases.name: Clostridial Myonecrosis
clinical_manifestations: Hyperacute, rapidly fatal necrotizing soft-tissue and deep muscular infection occurring post-trauma, post-surgery, or spontaneously (Clostridium septicum in occult colon cancer)
Excruciating, out-of-proportion, sudden pain at the injury site followed rapidly by systemic toxic shock, tachycardia disproportionate to fever, and mental apathy
Cutaneous physical hallmarks: skin overlying the infected muscle rapidly turns from pale to tense, shiny, bronze or copper-colored, progressing to dark purple, black, and frank cutaneous necrosis
Large, tense hemorrhagic bullae containing thin, dark, reddish-brown, sweet-foul-smelling "dishwater" fluid

Palpable soft-tissue crepitus extending rapidly along anatomical fascial planes; infected muscle exposed at surgery appears pale, edematous, fails to bleed on incision, and does not contract upon electrical stimulation ("cooked meat" appearance)
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography: Pathognomonic feathery, branching, linear lucencies of extensive gas dissecting longitudinally along muscle fibers and fascial planes far beyond the clinical borders of trauma

Computed Tomography (CT of Involved Extremity / Body Region): Extensive intramuscular gas pockets (subcutaneous emphysema and myonecrosis), fascial fluid collections, and absence of muscular contrast enhancement indicating complete muscular devitalization

Emergency Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS): "Cobblestoning" of subcutaneous tissues with bright, hyperechoic foci of gas producing dirty acoustic shadowing and reverberation artifacts within muscle bellies
pathology_manifestations: Emergency Exudate / Muscle Gram Stain (Immediate Diagnostic Clue): Abundant, large, thick, blunt-ended, rectangular Gram-positive bacilli ("boxcar-shaped" rods) accompanied by a dramatic, striking *absence of polymorphonuclear leukocytes* (leukocytes are rapidly lysed by clostridial alpha-toxin and theta-toxin)

Surgical Muscle Histopathology: Extensive coagulative necrosis of skeletal muscle bundles with loss of nuclear staining (ghost myocytes); gas bubbles dissecting myofibrillar architecture; marked intravascular thrombosis and capillary destruction without inflammatory infiltrate
Microbiology: Rapid double zone of beta-hemolysis on anaerobic sheep blood agar produced by Clostridium perfringens
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic emergency surgical infection defined by dramatic bedside physical images (bronze skin discoloration, hemorrhagic dishwater bullae, exposed cooked-meat muscle) and pathognomonic feathery gas patterns on plain radiography and CT.

Infectious Diseases.name: Acute Fulminant Meningococcemia and Purpura Fulminans
clinical_manifestations: Catastrophic, hyperacute invasive bacterial sepsis caused by Neisseria meningitidis with rapid progression from mild febrile illness to septic shock and death within hours
Initial rash: faint, discrete, pink-to-red maculopapular or petechial eruption concentrated on the trunk, lower extremities, and conjunctiva

Rapid evolution to purpura fulminans: explosive coalescence of petechiae into extensive, jagged, angular, stellate ecchymoses and large purpuric plaques with central dusky, gunmetal-gray or black cutaneous ischemic infarction

Symmetrical peripheral gangrene: acute ischemic dry gangrene of the digits, hands, feet, nose, and earlobes resulting from widespread microvascular thrombosis and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)

Endocrine collapse (Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome): acute fulminant adrenal crisis caused by bilateral massive adrenal hemorrhage, manifesting with profound refractory hypotension, hypoglycemia, and vascular collapse
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal CT / Ultrasound (Emergency Diagnostic Clue): Bilaterally enlarged, round or oval adrenal glands demonstrating high-attenuation intraparenchymal hematoma on non-contrast CT and absence of normal post-contrast adrenal enhancement (pathognomonic Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome)
Extremity Doppler Ultrasound: Extensive occlusion of distal peripheral arterial and venous microvasculature with preservation of proximal major conduit vessels
Chest Radiography: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) with bilateral confluent fluffy alveolar infiltrates and cardiomegaly
pathology_manifestations: Skin Biopsy / Tzanck-like Slit-Skin Smear: Extensive occlusive microvascular thrombosis of dermal capillaries and arterioles by dense fibrin thrombi; marked extravasation of erythrocytes into the dermis with ischemic necrosis of the overlying epidermis
Pathognomonic Gram Stain of Skin Lesion: Gram-negative coffee-bean-shaped diplococci directly visualized within the cytoplasm of endothelial cells and neutrophils lining thrombosed dermal vessels
Autopsy Pathology: Bilateral hemorrhagic destruction of the adrenal cortex with diffuse petechial hemorrhages into epicardium, pleura, and peritoneum
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-yield critical care infectious disease featuring undeniable, unforgettable photographs of stellate purpura fulminans lesions and peripheral acral gangrene, paired with bilateral adrenal hemorrhage on CT.

Infectious Diseases.name: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
clinical_manifestations: Systemic bacteremic complication of mucosal Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection (frequently asymptomatic primary urogenital, anorectal, or pharyngeal colonization)
Classic clinical triad of the Arthritis-Dermatitis Syndrome: migratory polyarthralgias, acute tenosynovitis, and distinctive cutaneous pustular lesions
Pathognomonic skin lesions: sparse (typically 2 to 10 lesions total), painless, discrete lesions located on the distal extremities, fingers, palms, toes, and over joints

Morphological progression of cutaneous lesions: initial erythematous or purpuric macules evolving rapidly into tender hemorrhagic vesicles or necrotic, gray-centered, gunmetal-colored pustules on an erythematous base

Acute severe tenosynovitis: simultaneous, dramatic, visible swelling and exquisite tenderness along multiple tendon sheaths (predominantly wrist extensors, dorsum of hands, ankles, and Achilles tendons)
Second phase: localized purulent monoarthritis or oligoarthritis (most frequently the knee, ankle, or wrist) with hot, tense, swollen joint effusion
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Dramatic thickening and distension of tendon sheaths with anechoic/hypoechoic fluid collections, synovial proliferation, and intense hypervascularity on Power Doppler (tenosynovitis of extensor pollicis, extensor digitorum, or tibialis anterior)
Joint MRI: Marked synovial enhancement, joint effusion, and periarticular soft-tissue and tenosynovial contrast enhancement without initial subchondral bony erosions
Plain Radiography of Involved Joints: Soft-tissue swelling and periarticular osteopenia; joint space preservation in acute presentation
pathology_manifestations: Synovial Fluid Analysis: Markedly purulent synovial fluid with leukocytosis (typically 30,000 to 100,000 WBC/mcL, >90% polymorphonuclear neutrophils); low glucose level

Microbiology: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci identified inside polymorphonuclear neutrophils on synovial fluid or skin lesion smear; high diagnostic yield on NAAT (nucleic acid amplification testing) from mucosal and synovial sites; chocolate agar / Thayer-Martin medium culture
Skin Biopsy: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis or microvascular thrombosis in the upper dermis with subepidermal pustule formation packed with neutrophils
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-yield infectious disease defined by a classic physical exam triad: sparse gunmetal-gray necrotic pustules on the extremities, severe visible wrist/ankle tenosynovitis, and acute purulent arthritis.

Infectious Diseases.name: Human African Trypanosomiasis
clinical_manifestations: Vector-borne protozoan infection transmitted by the bite of the tsetse fly (Glossina species) in sub-Saharan Africa, occurring in West African form (Trypanosoma brucei gambiense) and acute East African form (T. b. rhodesiense)
Primary inoculation lesion (Trypanosomal chancre): painful, indurated, fiery-red nodule or ulcer (2-5 cm) at the bite site appearing within 5-15 days, exuding serous fluid teeming with parasites
Stage 1 (Hemolymphatic stage) hallmark: Winterbottom sign—pathognomonic painless, rubbery, firm, mobile enlargement of the posterior cervical lymph nodes along the posterior triangle of the neck
Systemic signs: undulating recurrent fevers, striking pruritus, transient circinate or annular erythema ("trypanids"), and progressive facial and periorbital edema

Stage 2 (Meningoencephalitic stage): inversion of the circadian sleep-wake cycle (daytime somnolence and nighttime insomnia), progressive choreiform movements, ataxia, tremors, personality deterioration, and terminal coma
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Stage 2 Encephalitic Phase): Bilateral, symmetrical, patchy or confluent T2/FLAIR hyperintensities within the basal ganglia, internal capsules, brainstem tegmentum, and periventricular deep cerebral white matter
Post-Contrast T1 MRI: Punctate or diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement reflecting chronic lymphoplasmacytic meningoencephalitis
Neck Soft-Tissue Ultrasound: Multiple discrete, round, hypoechoic lymph nodes in the posterior cervical chains with prominent central hilar vascularity
pathology_manifestations: Microscopy (Diagnostic Hallmark): Direct microscopic identification of motile, slender, flagellated trypomastigotes (15-30 μm) with an undulating membrane and anterior flagellum in Giemsa-stained thin/thick blood films, lymph node aspirate, or chancre exudate

CSF Examination (Staging Hallmark): Elevated CSF WBC count (>5 WBC/mcL) or direct visualization of trypanosomes; presence of pathognomonic "Mott cells" (morula cells of Mott)—plasma cells distended with multiple spherical Russell-body-like eosinophilic IgM inclusions
Lymph Node Biopsy: Follicular hyperplasia with sinus histiocytosis, marked plasma cell infiltration, and high concentrations of IgM
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal visual tropical disease featuring unmistakable photographic signs (primary trypanosomal chancre, pathognomonic Winterbottom posterior cervical adenopathy) and diagnostic flagellated trypomastigotes on Giemsa smear.

Infectious Diseases.name: Crusted Scabies
clinical_manifestations: Highly contagious, severe, exuberant hyperinfestation by Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis occurring in individuals with impaired cell-mediated immunity (HIV, HTLV-1, organ transplant, systemic corticosteroids) or sensory/neurological deficits (Down syndrome, leprosy, dementia)
Striking physical examination: massive, thick, adherent, chalky white-to-yellow-gray, hyperkeratotic, warty, fissured crusts resembling severe psoriasis, Darier disease, or pachyonychia congenita
Extensive anatomical distribution: predilection for the palms, soles, scalp, face, ears, elbows, knees, and beneath deformed subungual nail beds; can progress to generalized exfoliative erythroderma
Severely deformed, dystrophic, thickened nails with massive subungual hyperkeratotic debris ("oyster-shell" appearance) harboring millions of mites

Paradoxical absence or minimal degree of pruritus despite teeming millions of mites (due to deficient host cell-mediated immune response), contributing to delayed diagnosis and explosive institutional outbreaks
radiological_manifestations: Dermoscopy (Diagnostic Bedside Hallmark): Pathognomonic "delta-wing jet" or "delta-glider" sign—dark, pigmented triangular structure (representing the anterior body, head, and anterior legs of the mite) located at the end of a whitish, tortuous, S-shaped burrow
High-Frequency Skin Ultrasound: Massive hyperechoic thickening of the stratum corneum with multiple acoustic micro-discontinuities corresponding to intra-stratum burrows
pathology_manifestations: Microscopic Examination of Skin Scrapings (Immediate Diagnostic Gold Standard): Direct potassium hydroxide (KOH) or mineral oil mount of superficial crust scrapings reveals an astonishing horde of hundreds to thousands of live, eight-legged adult mites, six-legged larvae, oval translucent eggs, and brownish-black oval fecal pellets (scybala)
Skin Punch Biopsy: Enormous compact hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis of the stratum corneum completely riddled with hundreds of round-to-oval tunnels and cross-sections of Sarcoptes scabiei mites
Dermal changes: Marked epidermal acanthosis, papillomatosis, and a dense mixed dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of eosinophils, histiocytes, and lymphocytes
Infectious Diseases.inclusion_rationale: High-yield contagious parasitic dermatosis with dramatic, unmistakable clinical photographs (massive hyperkeratotic chalky crusts over palms/soles and oyster-shell dystrophic nails) and millions of mites visible on direct KOH microscopy.

Nephrology.name: Alport Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Anterior lenticonus: conical protrusion of the anterior pole of the lens into the anterior chamber on slit-lamp examination (pathognomonic hallmark)
Macular and mid-peripheral dot-and-fleck retinopathy (innumerable pale yellow or whitish flecks sparing the fovea)
Posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy
Bilateral progressive high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss
Persistent microscopic or gross recurrent hematuria from childhood
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasound: Progressive bilateral increase in renal cortical echogenicity, loss of normal corticomedullary differentiation, and symmetric reduction in kidney size in late-stage renal failure
Temporal Bone CT / Audiometry: Sensorineural cochlear hearing loss documentation
pathology_manifestations: Renal biopsy electron microscopy (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic 'basket-weave' appearance of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) characterized by irregular alternating areas of thinning and thickening, multi-layering, and longitudinal splitting of the lamina densa; immunohistochemistry demonstrates complete absence of collagen alpha-3, alpha-4, and alpha-5 (IV) chains in X-linked disease
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Unmistakable syndromic nephropathy pairing ocular anterior lenticonus and dot-and-fleck retinopathy on slit lamp with bilateral shrunken echogenic kidneys on ultrasound and basket-weave GBM on electron microscopy.

Nephrology.name: Atheroembolic Renal Disease
clinical_manifestations:
Classic cutaneous triad following recent vascular instrumentation, angiography, cardiac catheterization, aortic surgery, or anticoagulation:
1) Livedo reticularis: prominent, mottled, violaceous, lace-like or reticular net-like erythema over the thighs, abdomen, and buttocks that does not blanch completely
2) 'Blue toe syndrome' (purple toe syndrome): exquisitely painful, cold, cyanotic or purplish discoloration and ulceration of the toes and forefeet, in the presence of intact, palpable, bounding peripheral pedal (dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial) pulses (hallmark of microvascular embolic occlusion)
3) Digital gangrene, cutaneous infarction, and tender subcutaneous purpuric nodules

Ophthalmoscopic pathognomonic sign: Hollenhorst plaques: bright, highly refractile, glistening orange-yellow, copper-hued cholesterol crystals lodged at the arterial bifurcations of retinal arterioles on funduscopy
Subacute, stuttering, stepwise deterioration in renal function with oliguria, marked refractory hypertension, fever, and weight loss
Abdominal signs: severe ischemic abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, and pancreatitis from concurrent visceral mesenteric atheroembolization
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT Angiography (CTA) / MR Angiography (MRA) of the Aorta: Pathognomonic 'shaggy aorta' sign: extensive, severe, diffuse, protruding, ulcerated, irregular atheromatous plaques (>4 mm thickness) and mobile, pedunculated thrombi lining the thoracic and abdominal aorta, particularly at and proximal to the origins of the renal arteries

Renal Doppler Ultrasound: Symmetrically normal or mildly reduced renal size with elevated renal arterial resistive indices (RI >0.75-0.80), patchy cortical perfusion defects, and absence of main renal artery occlusion
Fundus Photography: High-resolution photographic documentation of glistening, yellow refractile intravascular crystals at branching bifurcations of the retinal arterial tree
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic 'cholesterol clefts': biconvex, needle-shaped, or spindle-shaped optically clear ghost clefts inside the lumens of medium- and small-sized arcuate and interlobular renal arteries and arterioles (formed by the chemical dissolution of cholesterol crystals during routine alcohol and paraffin histological processing)

Associated Vascular Inflammatory Reaction: Acute stage reveals occlusive luminal thrombi containing fibrin, platelets, and entrapped cholesterol crystals; followed rapidly by a vigorous foreign-body giant cell reaction, surrounding histiocytes, endothelial proliferation, concentric 'onion-skin' intimal fibrous hyperplasia, and perivascular mononuclear and eosinophilic inflammation leading to complete luminal obliteration and downstream ischemic glomerulosclerosis and tubular atrophy
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Definitive systemic vascular nephropathy linking recent endovascular manipulation to livedo reticularis, blue toe syndrome with bounding pulses, and retinal Hollenhorst plaques, alongside a 'shaggy aorta' on CTA and pathognomonic biconvex biconcave needle-shaped cholesterol clefts on renal biopsy.

Nephrology.name: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
clinical_manifestations: Massively enlarged, palpable, nodular, ballotable bilateral flank masses extending into the lower abdomen
Protruding, distended abdomen with flank fullness
Gross macroscopic hematuria and acute flank pain from cyst rupture or hemorrhage
Signs of intracranial aneurysm (severe sudden headache / third nerve palsy)
Mitral valve prolapse click and murmur
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasound / CT / MRI: Bilateral, massively enlarged kidneys completely filled with innumerable, round, thin-walled fluid-filled cysts; high attenuation/hyperintensity in cysts with recent hemorrhage or infection; total kidney volume (TKV) calculation for Mayo prognostic classification; concurrent hepatic polycystic disease (cysts scattered throughout liver parenchyma) and pancreatic cysts
Brain MRA: Screening detection of unruptured intracranial saccular (berry) aneurysms in the Circle of Willis
pathology_manifestations: Nephrectomy gross and histology: Gigantic kidneys weighing up to several kilograms each; external surface resembles a bunch of grapes; cysts lined by flattened or cuboidal tubular epithelium; intervening normal renal parenchyma completely atrophied and compressed by progressive cystic expansion
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield genetic renal disorder with gigantic ballotable abdominal masses and distension, matched with unmistakable innumerable bilateral renal and hepatic cysts on ultrasound, CT, and MRI.

Nephrology.name: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease
clinical_manifestations: Classic Potter sequence physical phenotype at birth: flattened, compressed facial features (flattened nose, prominent infraorbital folds, micrognathia), low-set and flattened floppy ears, clubbed feet (talipes equinovarus), and severe pulmonary hypoplasia leading to neonatal respiratory failure
Enormous, bilateral, symmetrical, ballotable flank masses palpated in the newborn, producing a dramatically distended, protuberant abdomen that may impede spontaneous vaginal delivery
Early severe systemic arterial hypertension appearing in the first weeks of life, often refractory to multi-drug therapy

Manifestations of progressive congenital hepatic fibrosis in older children: massive, firm, non-tender hepatosplenomegaly, bleeding esophageal varices (hematemesis/melena), hypersplenism (thrombocytopenia, leukopenia), and caput medusae from portal hypertension
Failure to thrive and oliguria/anuria in the immediate perinatal period
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Neonatal / Prenatal Renal Ultrasound (Diagnostic Hallmark): Bilateral, symmetrically enlarged, kidney silhouettes (often 4 to 10 times normal volume) that retain their reniform shape, exhibiting diffuse, homogeneous hyperechogenicity ('white kidneys') with complete loss of corticomedullary differentiation; the bright echogenicity is caused by sound reflection from millions of microscopic acoustic interfaces between tiny, cylindrical (1-2 mm) radially arranged microcysts and fluid

Abdominal CT / MRI: Massively enlarged kidneys packed with radial microcysts, displaying high T2 signal intensity throughout the entire parenchyma; liver imaging demonstrates congenital hepatic fibrosis with periportal cuffing, dilation of intrahepatic biliary ducts (Caroli disease pattern), and prominent signs of portal hypertension (dilated portal vein, splenomegaly, gastroesophageal collateral veins)

High-Resolution Contrast Urography (Historical Classic): 'Sunburst' or 'spoke-wheel' striated nephrogram resulting from linear puddling and retention of contrast agent within elongated, fusiform dilated collecting ducts extending from the papillae outwards to the capsule
pathology_manifestations: Gross Pathology: Symmetrically gigantic kidneys retaining a smooth external surface (unlike the bosselated 'bunch-of-grapes' appearance of ADPKD); cut surface reveals countless uniform, tiny cylindrical, radially arranged fusiform cysts oriented perpendicular to the renal capsule, extending uninterrupted through the cortex and medulla

Histopathology (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Diffuse, non-branching, uniform fusiform or cylindrical dilatation of 100% of the collecting ducts lined by simple cuboidal or columnar epithelium; normal intervening glomeruli and proximal tubules are compressed into spaces between the dilated ducts; liver histology invariably demonstrates ductal plate malformation characterized by extensive concentric periportal fibrosis and bizarrely branching, dilated intrahepatic bile ductules (congenital hepatic fibrosis)

Genetics / Molecular: Biallelic pathogenic loss-of-function variants in the *PKHD1* gene on chromosome 6p21, encoding fibrocystin/polyductin, an integral membrane protein essential for primary cilia/basal body signaling in renal collecting tubules and biliary epithelial cells
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Premier recessive ciliopathy presenting with neonatal Potter facies, massive symmetric flank masses, and hepatosplenomegaly, corroborated by pathognomonic echogenic 'white kidneys' packed with radial microcysts on ultrasound and diffuse cylindrical collecting duct ectasia with congenital hepatic fibrosis on pathology.

Nephrology.name: Dense Deposit Disease
synonyms: complement factor H-related dense deposit disease
clinical_manifestations: Barraquer-Simons syndrome (acquired partial lipodystrophy): striking, symmetrical, progressive, irreversible loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue beginning in the face ('gaunt, hollow-cheeked, aged facies'), neck, shoulders, thoracic cage, and arms, with absolute sparing or compensatory hypertrophy of hips, buttocks, and lower extremities

Juvenile Ocular Drusen: Bilateral, symmetrical, yellow-white nodular subretinal deposits densely clustered across the macula and posterior pole on slit-lamp fundoscopy (identical to age-related macular degeneration but manifesting in adolescents and young adults), complicated by choroidal neovascular membranes and visual blurring
Nephritic-nephrotic syndrome: macroscopic cola-colored hematuria, heavy proteinuria, periorbital and peripheral pitting edema, and accelerated hypertension in children or young adults

Persistent profound hypocomplementemia: marked depression of serum C3 with characteristically normal C4 levels, driven by circulating C3 nephritic factor (C3NeF—an IgG autoantibody stabilizing the alternative pathway C3 convertase C3bBb)
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasonography: Bilaterally enlarged, echogenic kidneys with increased cortical reflectivity that matches or exceeds adjacent liver parenchyma; prominent accentuation of corticomedullary contrast during acute phases, followed by progressive parenchymal thinning and symmetric cortical atrophy in chronic stages

Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Distinct dome-shaped, hyperreflective nodular elevations located between the basal lamina of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and the inner collagenous layer of Bruch's membrane, with focal RPE atrophy and subretinal fluid accumulation

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) & Fluorescein Angiography: Confluent areas of focal hypo-autofluorescence surrounded by hyper-autofluorescent halos at drusen sites, with early hyperfluorescence ('starry sky' appearance) on fluorescein angiography
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy Electron Microscopy (Pathognomonic Gold Standard): Continuous, ribbon-like, extremely osmiophilic, electron-dense transformation of the lamina densa of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), creating a wavy, sausage-like, dark, highly electron-dense band replacing the normal lamina densa; identical dense transformation frequently involves Bowman's capsule and tubular basement membranes

Immunofluorescence Microscopy: Intense, dominant, bright staining for C3 alone along the glomerular capillary loops in a distinctive pseudolinear, patchy, or granular 'double-contour' / 'ring-and-saucer' pattern, along with bright mesangial C3 rings; characteristically negative for IgG, IgM, IgA, C1q, and C4

Light Microscopy: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) pattern with marked lobular accentuation of the glomerular tuft, mesangial and endocapillary hypercellularity, and basement membrane duplication ('tram-track' or double-contour appearance on Jones silver and PAS stains)
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Benchmark complement alternative pathway disorder linking Barraquer-Simons partial lipodystrophy (facial wasting) and juvenile ocular drusen to pathognomonic ribbon-like osmiophilic GBM transformation on EM and isolated bright C3 immunofluorescence.

Nephrology.name: Malakoplakia of the Urinary Tract
clinical_manifestations: Chronic, relentless, recurrent urinary tract infections refractory to conventional antibiotic regimens, classically occurring in immunocompromised, diabetic, or renal transplant patients
Gross painless hematuria, foul-smelling urine, and chronic dysuria
Palpable, tender, firm unilateral or bilateral flank mass mimicking a renal neoplasm, frequently accompanied by low-grade fever and weight loss
Acute or subacute obstructive renal failure (hydronephrosis) from ureteral or bladder neck lesions

Cystoscopic / Endoscopic Photographic Hallmark: Pathognomonic direct visualization of soft, friable, yellowish to yellowish-brown, umbilicated plaques or raised nodules (ranging from millimeters to several centimeters) surrounded by an intensely erythematous, hyperemic mucosal halo lining the urinary bladder (trigone) and ureter
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal/Pelvic CT: Multiple, poorly circumscribed, solid, hypoattenuating (20-40 HU) cortical and corticomedullary renal masses or diffuse enlargement of the entire kidney ('pseudotumor' pattern) with patchy, heterogeneous enhancement; pronounced perinephric fat stranding; thickened bladder wall with multiple discrete, intraluminal enhancing nodular mucosal plaques
Renal Ultrasound: Solitary or multifocal ill-defined, hypoechoic or heterogeneous parenchymal masses with distortion of the central renal sinus complex, accompanied by hydroureteronephrosis
Fluoroscopic Retrograde / Antegrade Ureteropyelography: Irregular filling defects, strictures, and luminal nodularity in the distal ureters mimicking multifocal urothelial carcinoma
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Dense, confluent, chronic histiocytic infiltrate composed of sheets of large, polygonal macrophages with abundant, eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm known as von Hansemann cells

Pathognomonic Pathologic Structure: Michaelis-Gutmann bodies: round to oval, targetoid, basophilic, concentrically laminated, calcified intracytoplasmic (or extracellular) inclusion bodies; they represent defective phagolysosomes containing incompletely digested, calcified bacterial fragments (Escherichia coli)

Special Stains: Michaelis-Gutmann bodies are strongly positive for von Kossa stain (black, demonstrating calcium phosphate), Prussian blue stain (bright blue, demonstrating ferric iron), and Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) with diastase resistance; CD68 positive, confirming histiocytic lineage
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive chronic granulomatous infection featuring cystoscopic yellowish-brown mucosal plaques with hyperemic halos, CT renal pseudotumors with hydronephrosis, and pathognomonic basophilic targetoid Michaelis-Gutmann bodies within von Hansemann histiocytes on pathology.

Nephrology.name: Nail-Patella Syndrome
clinical_manifestations:
Tetrad of classic physical examination dysmorphic findings:
1) Dystrophic fingernails (pathognomonic bedside hallmark): Bilateral, symmetrical nail hypoplasia, aplasia, longitudinal ridging, spooning (koilonychia), triangular lunulae (pathognomonic sign where lunulae point distally like an arrowhead), most severe on the thumbs and progressively milder towards the fifth digit
2) Absent, hypoplastic, or dislocated patellae: easily palpated small, rudimentary, or absent kneecaps, associated with habitual recurrent patellar dislocations, genu valgum, and gait disturbances
3) Elbow dysplasias: prominent limitation of full extension, pronation, and supination of the forearms, with visible antecubital pterygia (webbing) and prominence of the radial head
4) Palpable posterior iliac horns: symmetric, firm, bony prominences palpated along the posterolateral surface of the iliac crests
Lester's sign: cloverleaf-shaped or irregular dark hyperpigmentation of the inner pupillary margin of the iris on slit-lamp ophthalmic examination

Renal manifestations: early asymptomatic microscopic hematuria and persistent, progressive non-nephrotic or nephrotic proteinuria developing in childhood or adolescence, progressing to end-stage kidney disease in 30-50%
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic Radiography (Pathognomonic Skeletal Hallmark): Pathognomonic bilateral, symmetrical, horn-like bony spurs or exostoses projecting posterolaterally from the posterior aspect of the iliac bones, known as iliac horns or Fong's sign (present in >80% of patients and pathognomonic for the syndrome)
Knee Radiography / MRI: Hypoplastic, small, asymmetrical, or completely absent patellae; lateral displacement/subluxation of the patella; hypoplastic lateral femoral condyle
Elbow Radiography: Hypoplasia of the capitellum, asymmetric enlargement of the medial epicondyle, and posterolateral subluxation or dislocation of the radial head
Renal Ultrasound: Non-specific findings of progressive glomerulopathy: bilateral normal-to-small kidneys with increased cortical echogenicity and loss of corticomedullary differentiation
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy Electron Microscopy (Diagnostic Gold Standard & Pathognomonic Hallmark): Pathognomonic 'moth-eaten' appearance of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) with diffuse irregular lucent areas throughout the lamina densa, containing embedded bundles of banded collagen fibrils showing characteristic 64 nm periodic striations (Type III collagen fibers, which are normally entirely absent from the glomerular basement membrane); accompanied by podocyte foot process effacement
Light Microscopy: Variable, non-specific changes ranging from mild mesangial matrix expansion to progressive focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and tubular atrophy

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous pathogenic loss-of-function mutations in the *LMX1B* gene on chromosome 9q34.1, encoding the LIM homeobox transcription factor 1-beta, critical for dorsoventral limb patterning, podocyte differentiation, and glomerular basement membrane collagen regulation
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Premier hereditary pleiotropic nephropathy combining bedside triangular fingernail lunulae and absent patellae with pathognomonic bilateral iliac horns on pelvic radiography and pathognomonic banded collagen fibrils within a 'moth-eaten' GBM on electron microscopy.

Nephrology.name: Nephropathic Cystinosis
Nephrology.subspecialty: Metabolic and Lysosomal Storage Kidney Diseases
clinical_manifestations: Onset in early infancy (6-12 months) with complete renal Fanconi syndrome: extreme polyuria, polydipsia, recurrent episodes of severe dehydration, vomiting, failure to thrive, and growth arrest below the 3rd percentile

Hypophosphatemic Fanconi rickets: prominent rachitic rosary (beading of costochondral junctions), widening of wrists and ankles, severe lower limb bowing (genu varum/valgum), and craniotabes resistant to physiologic vitamin D

Pathognomonic ocular findings: severe photophobia, chronic blepharospasm, and eye rubbing; slit-lamp biomicroscopy reveals innumerable glistening, tinsel-like, needle-shaped and hexagonal cystine crystals deposited throughout the corneal stroma (appearing after 1 year of age, 100% pathognomonic)
Cutaneous pigmentary dilution: characteristic fair complexion, blond hair, and blue eyes (distinct hypopigmentation compared to unaffected family members due to altered melanogenesis)

Extrarenal storage manifestations in late childhood/adolescence: primary hypothyroidism (thyroid follicular atrophy), distal vacuolar myopathy, pancreatic exocrine and endocrine insufficiency (diabetes mellitus), and swallowing dysfunction
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Radiography: Severe, active hypophosphatemic rickets demonstrating pathognomonic cupping, widening, splaying, and ragged fraying of the metaphyseal margins at the distal radius, ulna, and tibia; wide, radiolucent growth plates (physes); severe generalized osteopenia and pseudofractures (Looser zones)

Renal Ultrasonography: Progressive bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis characterized by intensely hyperechoic renal pyramids with acoustic shadowing, loss of corticomedullary differentiation, and progressive symmetric renal volume loss leading to small, shrunken, echogenic kidneys
In Vivo Corneal Confocal Microscopy: Quantitative visualization of high-density hyperreflective, needle-shaped and fusiform crystal deposits in the anterior, middle, and posterior corneal stroma
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy Light Microscopy & Microdissection: Pathognomonic 'swan-neck' deformity of the proximal convoluted tubule (extreme atrophy and narrowing of the initial proximal tubule segment directly originating from the glomerulus, lined by flattened, atrophic epithelium); marked multinucleated podocytes; progressive focal segmental and global glomerulosclerosis with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy

Polarized Light Microscopy (Alcohol-Fixed Tissue): Innumerable iridescent, birefringent, hexagonal, rectangular, and needle-shaped cystine crystals packed within the lysosomes of interstitial histiocytes, mesangial cells, and proximal tubular cells (crystals dissolve in routine aqueous formalin fixation and require absolute ethanol fixation)

Electron Microscopy & Genetics: Intralysosomal crystalline voids within podocytes and interstitial macrophages; molecular testing demonstrates biallelic pathogenic loss-of-function variants in CTNS (such as the common 57-kb European founder deletion), resulting in defective lysosomal cystinosin transporter
Nephrology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic lysosomal storage ciliopathy pairing infantile Fanconi rickets, blond hypopigmentation, and slit-lamp corneal crystals with metaphyseal fraying on X-ray, medullary nephrocalcinosis, and pathognomonic proximal tubular 'swan-neck' deformity on histology.

Nephrology.name: Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1
Nephrology.subspecialty: Metabolic and Genetic Renal Storage Diseases
clinical_manifestations: Early infantile or childhood presentation with recurrent, refractory calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis and urolithiasis, passing gravel or large calculi, leading to obstructive uropathy, renal colic, and rapid progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD)
Oxalate osteopathy: severe bone pain, joint deformities, pathological fractures of long bones, and painful swollen metaphyses mimicking intractable rickets

Cutaneous oxalosis (calciphylaxis-like ischemic necrosis): livedo reticularis, painful violaceous plaques, peripheral digital gangrene, Raynaud phenomenon, and ischemic acral ulcerations from systemic microvascular oxalate precipitation

Ocular oxalosis: pathognomonic 'crystalline retinopathy' characterized by white-to-yellow glistening birefringent flecks and crystalline deposits densely scattered across the posterior pole, macula, and retinal pigment epithelium on fundoscopy

Cardiac oxalosis: high-grade atrioventricular conduction blocks, bundle branch blocks, intractable ventricular arrhythmias, and restrictive cardiomyopathy resulting from diffuse myocardial oxalate crystal infiltration
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Abdominal CT / KUB Plain Radiography: Dense, diffuse, bilateral medullary and cortical nephrocalcinosis ('chalky-white kidneys') accompanied by bilateral radiopaque staghorn or multiple branched dendritic renal calculi (pure calcium oxalate monohydrate, >1200-1500 HU)

Renal Ultrasonography: Strikingly hyperechoic kidneys ('bright kidneys') with complete loss of corticomedullary differentiation and dense posterior acoustic shadowing caused by diffuse parenchymal crystal aggregation
