Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and MR Angiography (MRA): High-resolution T2/FLAIR demonstrating pathognomonic 'ivy sign' (prominent leptomeningeal high signal intensity along cortical sulci reflecting slow retrograde collateral blood flow through pial anastomoses); multiple flow voids at the basal ganglia and perimesencephalic cisterns on T1/T2; multiple acute and chronic watershed infarctions in deep white matter and borderzones; MRA shows marked flow attenuation/disappearance of terminal ICAs and proximal MCAs/ACAs

Perfusion Imaging (CT Perfusion / Dynamic Susceptibility Contrast MRI / SPECT / PET): Striking hemodynamic compromise characterized by markedly prolonged time to peak (TTP) and mean transit time (MTT), reduced cerebral blood flow (CBF), and exhausted cerebrovascular reserve capacity following acetazolamide (Diamox) challenge, confirming severe vascular steal and tissue at risk
pathology_manifestations: Arterial Histopathology and Genetics: Non-inflammatory, non-atherosclerotic fibrocellular intimal thickening and smooth muscle hyperplasia leading to marked luminal stenosis of the terminal internal carotid arteries; marked tortuosity, fragmentation, disruption, or duplication of the internal elastic lamina; thinning and attenuation of the muscular media with adventitial preservation; prominent proliferation and microaneurysmal dilation of fragile basal perforating collateral vessels with mural microthrombi and fibrinoid degeneration; strong genetic association with loss-of-function or missense variants in the ring finger protein 213 (RNF213) gene, particularly the p.R4810K founder variant in East Asian populations
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic cerebrovascular disease marked by hyperventilation-induced TIAs in children and catastrophic intraventricular hemorrhages in adults, defined radiologically by the pathognomonic catheter angiographic 'puff of smoke' basal collaterals and MRI 'ivy sign', underpinned by non-inflammatory intimal fibroplasia and RNF213 genetic mutations.

Neurology.name: Multiple Sclerosis
clinical_manifestations: Optic neuritis: unilateral painful loss of vision, afferent pupillary defect (Marcus Gunn pupil), swollen or pale optic disc on fundoscopy
Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO): impaired adduction of the ipsilateral eye with horizontal nystagmus of the abducting contralateral eye (damage to medial longitudinal fasciculus)
Lhermitte sign: electric-shock-like sensation shooting down the spine into the limbs upon neck flexion
Uhthoff phenomenon (transient worsening of neurologic symptoms with elevated body temperature)
Spastic paraparesis, intention tremor, scanning speech, and ataxia (Charcot neurologic triad)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Oval/ellipsoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense demyelinating plaques perpendicular to the lateral ventricles ('Dawson's fingers' along medullary veins); juxtacortical, infratentorial (pons/cerebellum), and periventricular lesions; T1 hypointense 'black holes' (permanent axonal loss); active lesions display incomplete 'open-ring' or nodular gadolinium enhancement
Spine MRI: Focal, peripherally located demyelinating lesions spanning <2 vertebral segments in length, occupying <50% of cord cross-section
pathology_manifestations: Brain autopsy / biopsy: Sharply demarcated, hypocellular demyelinating plaques with destruction of myelin sheaths and relative axonal sparing; abundant lipid-laden foamy macrophages (luxol fast blue myelin degradation products), perivenular cuffs of T lymphocytes and B cells, reactive astrogliosis
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Core neurologic disorder with physical exam hallmarks (INO, optic disc pallor, Lhermitte sign) matching textbook 'Dawson's fingers' and open-ring enhancing lesions on brain/spine MRI.

Neurology.name: Multiple System Atrophy
clinical_manifestations: Profound, symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension (blood pressure drop >30 mmHg systolic or >15 mmHg diastolic without compensatory heart rate increase), often causing recurrent syncope
Nocturnal inspiratory stridor (high-pitched, harsh breathing during sleep caused by laryngeal abductor dystonia and vocal cord adductor paralysis), an ominous harbinger of sudden nocturnal death
Antecollis (severe, disproportionate flexion dystonia of the neck / 'dropped head' syndrome)

Severe, poorly levodopa-responsive parkinsonian rigidity and akinesia (MSA-P subtype) or progressive cerebellar ataxia with intention tremor, scanning dysarthria, and wide-based staggering gait (MSA-C subtype)

Disproportionate hand/foot posturing (striatal hands/toes), cold dusky violaceous extremities with impaired peripheral thermoregulation (autonomic circulatory dysfunction), and severe urinary urge incontinence or retention
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial T2 and FLAIR): Pathognomonic 'hot cross bun sign'—a striking cruciform T2 hyperintensity in the pontine tegmentum caused by selective degeneration and gliosis of transverse pontocerebellar fibers and the median pontine raphe

Brain MRI (Axial T2/SWI): 'Putaminal rim sign'—a distinct linear T2-hyperintense rim along the dorsolateral border of the putamen, accompanied by marked putaminal hypointensity (excessive iron deposition) and significant putaminal volume loss in MSA-P

Posterior Fossa MRI: Pronounced atrophy of the middle cerebellar peduncles (MCP) with bilateral T2/FLAIR hyperintensity ('MCP sign'), accompanied by severe olivopontocerebellar atrophy and marked enlargement of the fourth ventricle and prepontine cistern

Cardiovascular Autonomic Testing / 123I-MIBG Myocardial Scintigraphy: Normal or minimally decreased myocardial MIBG uptake (reflecting preserved postganglionic sympathetic fibers, unlike Lewy body Parkinson disease where MIBG uptake is profoundly reduced)
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology Histopathology: Alpha-synucleinopathy characterized by pathognomonic, widespread Glial Cytoplasmic Inclusions (GCIs, also known as Papp-Lantos bodies) located within the cytoplasm of oligodendrocytes, strongly positive for alpha-synuclein and ubiquitin; accompanied by severe neuronal loss, myelin pallor, and dense microglial activation in the striatonigral and olivopontocerebellar networks
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Classic neurodegenerative synucleinopathy displaying hallmark clinical autonomic collapse, laryngeal stridor, and antecollis, anchored by the iconic 'hot cross bun sign' on pontine MRI and putaminal rim hyperintensity.

Neurology.name: Myasthenia Gravis
clinical_manifestations: Asymmetric, fatigable ptosis worsening upon sustained upward gaze (>60 seconds)
Diplopia that changes with fatigue
'Myasthenic snarl' (retraction of the corners of the mouth without tooth exposure due to facial muscle weakness)
Dropped head syndrome (weakness of neck extensor muscles)
Bulbar fatigue with chewing and talking (dysphonia, nasal voice), proximal limb weakness
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT / MRI with Contrast: Anterior mediastinal mass demonstrating a thymoma (smooth or lobulated soft-tissue mass, calcification, cystic changes) or diffuse symmetric thymic hyperplasia
Orbit MRI: Useful to rule out structural compressive orbital/cavernous sinus lesions mimicking ocular MG
pathology_manifestations: Thymectomy surgical histology: Thymoma (WHO types A, AB, B1, B2, B3) showing neoplastic epithelial cells admixed with non-neoplastic immature T lymphocytes, or thymic follicular lymphoid hyperplasia with prominent ectopic germinal centers
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Textbook neuromuscular disorder with visible fatigable ptosis and the 'myasthenic snarl' paired with diagnostic mediastinal thymoma imaging on chest CT.

Neurology.name: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease
clinical_manifestations: Severe acute bilateral optic neuritis: Profound decrease in visual acuity accompanied by excruciating orbital pain with eye movements; direct fundoscopy demonstrates marked, florid optic disc edema (papillitis) and peripapillary hemorrhages in >80% of eyes, with rapid steroid responsiveness

Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM)-like presentation: Common in children and adolescents, presenting with fever, encephalopathy, lethargy, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and multifocal cranial nerve palsies

Transverse myelitis and conus syndrome: Flaccid paraparesis, sensory ataxia, saddle anesthesia, early severe neurogenic bladder dysfunction (urinary retention), and erectile dysfunction due to preferential conus medullaris targeting
Steroid dependency and rapid remission: Dramatic, rapid clinical improvement following high-dose corticosteroids, with high risk of rebound relapses during tapering
radiological_manifestations: Orbital MRI (Coronal and Axial T1+Gd with Fat Suppression, T2/STIR): Longitudinally extensive optic nerve hyperintensity involving anterior optic nerve segments with marked swelling; pathognomonic prominent peri-optic nerve sheath and orbital fat enhancement (orbital perineuritis), extending along the sheath

Spine MRI: Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) often involving the lower thoracic cord and conus medullaris; axial T2-weighted MRI demonstrates the pathognomonic 'H-sign' (confined hyperintensity strictly mapped to the central spinal gray matter resembling the letter 'H', sparing surrounding white matter)

Brain MRI: Large, bilateral, hazy, fluffy, cloud-like, poorly demarcated T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions distributed in the deep white matter, brainstem, cerebellar peduncles, and cortical-subcortical junctions; cortical/subcortical FLAIR hyperintense lesions with seizures (FLICE pattern)
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology: Perivenular demyelination mediated by anti-MOG IgG1 autoantibodies targeting the extracellular domain of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein; distinct histopathologic preservation of oligodendrocytes and relative axonal sparing; macrophage-dominated inflammation with CD4+ T-cell infiltration and complement deposition, strictly lacking the astrocytic necrosis, AQP4 loss, and thick perivascular rosettes seen in NMOSD
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct antibody-mediated demyelinating syndrome featuring florid optic papillitis, pathognomonic orbital fat/nerve sheath perineuritis and conus spinal 'H-sign' on MRI, and perivenular demyelination with oligodendrocyte preservation on histology.

Neurology.name: Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1
clinical_manifestations: Distinctive 'hatchet' facies: long, narrow, haggard facial appearance caused by marked bilateral temporalis and masseter muscle wasting, facial diplegia, sagging jaw, and drooping lips
Premature frontal balding (androgenic alopecia) in both men and women, often initiating before age 30
Bilateral, symmetrical ptosis with hollowed temples, nasal speech, and swan-neck deformity of the cervical spine from severe sternocleidomastoid muscle atrophy

Active grip myotonia (dramatic inability to rapidly release hand grip after clenching) and percussion myotonia (percussion of thenar eminence with a reflex hammer elicits persistent abduction/flexion of thumb with slow relaxation)
Ophthalmic hallmark: polychromatic, iridescent 'Christmas tree' cataracts visible on slit-lamp biomicroscopy, and endocrine abnormalities (testicular atrophy, diabetes mellitus, hypogonadism)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial T2 and FLAIR): Highly characteristic, bilateral symmetrical white matter hyperintensities preferentially concentrated in the anterior temporal lobes and poles (a rare and specific distribution), along with diffuse white matter hyperintensities and ventriculomegaly

Lower Extremity Muscle MRI: Selective fatty degeneration and muscular atrophy demonstrating predilection for the anterior compartment of the lower leg (tibialis anterior, extensor digitorum longus) and medial gastrocnemius, with relative preservation of the posterior deep compartment

Chest Radiography and Fluoroscopy: Elevated hemidiaphragm (bilateral or unilateral) due to severe diaphragmatic weakness/myotonia, accompanied by basal atelectasis and chronic alveolar hypoventilation

Electrocardiography and Cardiac MRI: PR interval prolongation (first-degree AV block), intraventricular conduction delays (bundle branch block), and myocardial interstitial fibrosis on late gadolinium enhancement predisposing to sudden cardiac death
pathology_manifestations: Muscle Biopsy Histopathology: Striking, diagnostic profusion of internalized central nuclei forming long chains along the longitudinal axis of fibers (>20-50% of fibers contain central nuclei); severe selective atrophy of type 1 muscle fibers; presence of ring fibers (Ringbinden) with peripheral encircling myofibrils, sarcoplasmic masses, and pyknotic nuclear clumps

Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic expansion of unstable (CTG)n trinucleotide repeats in the 3'-UTR of the DMPK gene on chromosome 19q13.3 (>50 to thousands of repeats), triggering toxic RNA foci that sequester MBNL1 splicing regulators
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential multisystem trinucleotide repeat disorder displaying the unmistakable 'hatchet' facies, frontal balding, and percussion myotonia, correlated with temporal pole white matter lesions on brain MRI and internal nuclear chains on muscle biopsy.

Neurology.name: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
clinical_manifestations: Café-au-lait macules: flat, uniform, light-brown patches with smooth borders (>=6 lesions >=5 mm prepubertal or >=15 mm postpubertal)
Axillary and inguinal freckling (Crowe sign)
Multiple cutaneous and subcutaneous neurofibromas (soft, flesh-colored, violaceous dome-shaped papules with 'buttonhole sign')
Plexiform neurofibromas: large, infiltrative, drooping, baggy subcutaneous masses feeling like a 'bag of worms'
Lisch nodules: pigmented, yellow-brown, raised melanocytic iris hamartomas on slit-lamp exam
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Orbit MRI: Optic pathway gliomas (thickening, tortuosity, and hyperintensity of optic nerves and chiasm); focal areas of signal intensity (FASI / unidentified bright objects [UBOs]) on T2/FLAIR in basal ganglia and cerebellum

Spine and Body MRI: Plexiform neurofibromas showing characteristic 'target sign' (central low T2 signal fibrocollagenous tissue rimmed by hyperintense myxoid tissue); dural ectasia with vertebral scalloping
Skeletal Radiographs: Sphenoid wing dysplasia (causing pulsating exophthalmos), congenital anterolateral bowing and pseudarthrosis of the tibia
pathology_manifestations: Neurofibroma biopsy: Benign, unencapsulated nerve sheath tumor composed of wavy Schwann cells with elongated comma-shaped nuclei, fibroblasts, perineurial-like cells, and mast cells embedded in an abundant myxoid and collagenous extracellular matrix
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Classic phakomatosis with distinct skin findings (café-au-lait, Crowe sign, Lisch nodules, plexiform neurofibromas) matched with MRI optic pathway gliomas and tibial pseudarthrosis on X-ray.

Neurology.name: Neurofibromatosis Type 2
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and vestibular dysfunction: Progressive, asymmetric hearing loss, tinnitus, and unsteadiness/disequilibrium in young adults (second to third decade) resulting from bilateral vestibulocochlear nerve schwannomas

Ocular abnormalities: Juvenile posterior subcapsular lenticular cataracts (early presenile cataracts) and combined hamartomas of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium (CRHRPE) visible on slit-lamp and dilated fundoscopy
Cutaneous schwannomas: Discrete, slightly raised, intracutaneous or subcutaneous plaque-like or nodular tumors along peripheral nerve courses, often hyperesthetic

Absence of NF1 hallmarks: Diagnostic absence of Lisch iris nodules, rarity or low number (<6) of pale cafe-au-lait macules, and lack of axillary/inguinal freckling (Crowe sign), distinguishing NF2 from NF1
Multiple cranial neuropathies: Facial weakness (CN VII), hoarseness and dysphagia (CN IX/X), and tongue atrophy (CN XII) from non-vestibular cranial nerve schwannomas
radiological_manifestations: Brain Contrast-Enhanced MRI: Pathognomonic bilateral vestibular schwannomas (acoustic neuromas) originating within the internal auditory canals (IAC) with 'ice cream cone' extension into the cerebellopontine angles (CPA), exhibiting intense, heterogeneous gadolinium enhancement and internal cystic changes; multiple intracranial meningiomas presenting as hyperostotic, intensely enhancing extra-axial masses with dural tails

Spine MRI (Sagittal and Axial T1+Gd and T2): Multiple intramedullary ependymomas (particularly in the cervical and upper thoracic cord) with central cystic components and hemosiderin 'cap sign'; multiple intradural extramedullary spinal schwannomas producing classic 'dumbbell' or 'hourglass' expansion through the neural exit foramina
CT of Temporal Bones: Symmetrical funnel-shaped widening and bony erosion of the internal acoustic canals bilaterally
pathology_manifestations: Schwannoma histopathology: Classic biphasic Antoni A and Antoni B architecture: Antoni A consists of dense, compact spindle-shaped cells with elongated nuclei aligned in parallel palisades around eosinophilic fibrillary zones (Verocay bodies); Antoni B consists of loose, hypocellular, microcystic myxoid stroma; strong, uniform, diffuse cytoplasmic and nuclear positivity for S100 and SOX10; molecular pathology demonstrates biallelic inactivating mutations in the NF2 gene on chromosome 22q12.2 encoding the tumor suppressor protein merlin (schwannomin)
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic genetic phakomatosis with juvenile posterior subcapsular cataract, pathognomonic bilateral internal auditory canal 'ice cream cone' vestibular schwannomas on MRI, and classic Antoni A/B Verocay body histology.

Neurology.name: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
clinical_manifestations: Severe acute optic neuritis: Typically bilateral or rapidly sequential unilateral profound vision loss (frequently counting fingers or light perception only), severe ocular retrobulbar pain exacerbated by eye movement, and marked optic disc swelling (papillitis) on direct ophthalmoscopy evolving to chalky white optic atrophy

Area postrema syndrome: Intractable, persistent nausea, projectile vomiting, and continuous hiccups (singultus) lasting days to weeks, refractory to antiemetics, caused by medullary floor inflammation

Acute transverse myelitis: Sudden flaccid paraplegia or quadriplegia with a sharp, well-demarcated sensory level on the trunk, accompanied by painful paroxysmal tonic limb spasms, Lhermitte sign, and acute urinary retention/neurogenic bladder
Relative sparing of cognitive function: Unlike progressive forms of multiple sclerosis, cortical and cognitive functions are preserved in the majority of episodes
radiological_manifestations: Spine MRI (Sagittal and Axial T2/STIR and T1+Gd): Pathognomonic Longitudinally Extensive Transverse Myelitis (LETM) displaying continuous, uninterrupted T2 hyperintensity extending across >=3 contiguous vertebral segments; axial T2 images demonstrate central cord involvement occupying >50% of the cross-sectional spinal cord area, marked cord swelling, and heterogeneous patchy or ring gadolinium enhancement; late scans show central cord cavitation and atrophy

Brain MRI (FLAIR and T1+Gd): Distinctive non-MS lesions localized to aquaporin-4 (AQP4)-rich periependymal regions lining the ventricles: dorsal medulla/area postrema T2 hyperintensity, periaqueductal gray and third ventricle/hypothalamic lesions, and extensive splenium 'bridge-like' corpus callosum hyperintensities; absence of typical MS Dawson fingers

Orbital MRI: Longitudinally extensive T2 hyperintensity and marked gadolinium enhancement of the optic nerve, extending posteriorly into the optic chiasm and optic tracts over >50% of the optic nerve length
pathology_manifestations: CNS histopathology / autopsy: Vasocentric (perivascular) deposition of immunoglobulins (IgG and IgM) and activated complement components (membrane attack complex C9neo) forming characteristic perivascular rosettes around hyalinized vessels; profound, selective destruction of astrocytic foot processes with loss of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) immunoreactivity; secondary demyelination with extensive axonal injury, necrosis, and prominent perivascular infiltrates rich in neutrophils and eosinophils
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Definitive neuroimmunologic entity with classic clinical area postrema hiccups/vomiting and profound optic neuritis, pathognomonic >=3 segment longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) on spine MRI, and AQP4 astrocytopathic complement rosette pathology.

Neurology.name: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus
clinical_manifestations: Classic Hakim-Adams clinical triad: gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and progressive cognitive impairment
Characteristic 'magnetic' gait: slow, wide-based, short-stepped, shuffling gait with feet appearing glued or magnetized to the floor; impaired postural reflexes and difficulty initiating steps
Significant immediate improvement in gait velocity and stride length following large-volume lumbar puncture (Miller Fisher CSF tap test)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI / CT: Marked symmetric ventriculomegaly out of proportion to high-convexity sulcal enlargement; Evans index >0.30; DESH sign (Disproportionately Enlarged Subarachnoid Space Hydrocephalus: tight high-convexity sulci with enlarged sylvian fissures); acute callosal angle (<90 degrees on coronal MRI); bulging of the lateral ventricular third ventricle into the chiasm; periventricular T2/FLAIR transependymal edema
pathology_manifestations: Brain biopsy / post-mortem: Patchy loss and disruption of ependymal lining along ventricular margins, periventricular subcortical interstitial edema, reactive subependymal astrogliosis, and absence of extensive primary cortical neuronal degeneration
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Reversible neurological condition featuring the visible shuffling magnetic gait triad confirmed by pathognomonic DESH pattern, acute callosal angle, and Evans index >0.3 on coronal brain MRI.

Neurology.name: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral, symmetrical, slowly progressive ptosis causing drooping eyelids that obstruct the visual axis, eliciting chronic compensatory contraction of the frontalis muscle (deep horizontal forehead furrows)
Characteristic 'astronomer posture' (retrocollis / head-tilt-back compensation to gaze beneath drooping ptotic eyelids)
Severe progressive pharyngeal dysphagia: early difficulty swallowing dry solid foods, progressing to liquids, with choking episodes, coughing during meals, and frequent nasal regurgitation
Progressive extraocular ophthalmoparesis with restricted upward and lateral gaze, typically without diplopia
Tongue atrophy, furrowing, and weakness with severe difficulty manipulating boluses within the oral cavity, leading to malnutrition, aspiration pneumonia, and weight loss
radiological_manifestations: Videofluoroscopic Swallowing Study (VFSS) / Barium Swallow: Severe pooling and stasis of barium contrast in the valleculae and pyriform sinuses, delayed trigger of pharyngeal swallow, prominent cricopharyngeal bar (achalasia of the upper esophageal sphincter failure to relax), and frequent laryngeal penetration or tracheal aspiration

Head and Neck Muscle MRI (T1-weighted and STIR): Advanced, symmetrical fatty infiltration and severe atrophy of the intrinsic and extrinsic tongue musculature (genioglossus, lingual muscles), pharyngeal constrictors, and masseters, with relative sparing of masticatory temporalis muscles

Pelvis and Thigh Muscle MRI: Late-stage selective fatty replacement in the lower limbs preferentially involving the adductor magnus, semimembranosus, and hamstrings, with relative preservation of rectus femoris
pathology_manifestations: Muscle Biopsy Histopathology and Electron Microscopy: Pathognomonic intranuclear tubulofilamentous inclusions (8.5 nm outer diameter filaments arranged in straight or tangled arrays within muscle fiber nuclei on transmission electron microscopy); light microscopy shows rimmed vacuoles (autophagic vacuoles rimmed by basophilic granular material on modified Gomori trichrome staining), muscle fiber size variation, and endomysial fibrosis

Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant or recessive (GCG)7-13 trinucleotide repeat expansion in the PABPN1 gene on chromosome 14q11.2, causing nuclear aggregation of mutant polyadenylate-binding protein nuclear 1
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive late-onset myopathy presenting with the hallmark 'astronomer' tilted-head posture, bilateral ptosis, and cricopharyngeal bar on barium swallow, confirmed by pathognomonic 8.5 nm intranuclear tubulofilamentous inclusions.

Neurology.name: Pantothenate Kinase-Associated Neurodegeneration
synonyms: neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation type 1
clinical_manifestations: Severe progressive extrapyramidal movement disorder: striking cranial-orofacial dystonia characterized by blepharospasm, grimacing, forceful involuntary tongue protrusion, and severe jaw-opening dystonia that often leads to self-mutilating tongue and lip biting
Severe generalized limb dystonia: fixed equinovarus posturing of the feet, dystonic clenched fists with hyperextension of fingers, torticollis, and opisthotonic posturing of trunk
Progressive parkinsonian rigidity, bradykinesia, freezing of gait, and loss of postural reflexes leading to premature loss of independent walking
Corticospinal tract signs: spasticity, hyperreflexia, and bilateral extensor plantar responses (Babinski signs)
Ophthalmic hallmark: pigmentary retinopathy ('bone-spicule' retinal pigmentation / atypical retinitis pigmentosa) and optic atrophy causing progressive visual field constriction
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial T2-weighted and T2* / Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging SWI): Pathognomonic 'Eye of the Tiger' sign—marked, symmetrical, profound T2 hypointensity (striking signal loss due to massive iron deposition) throughout the globus pallidus, surrounding a well-circumscribed, central oval focus of hyperintensity (representing severe localized tissue necrosis, gliosis, and vacuolation)
Substantia Nigra MRI: Concomitant marked T2 hypointensity in the substantia nigra pars reticulata due to progressive iron accumulation, with sparing of the red nucleus and cerebral cortex

Gradient Echo / Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM): Markedly increased magnetic susceptibility confirming excessive ferrihydrite and non-heme iron load in the medial and lateral globus pallidus
pathology_manifestations: Brain Autopsy Gross Pathology: Striking rust-brown or dark chocolate-brown discoloration of the globus pallidus and substantia nigra caused by massive localized non-heme iron deposition (strongly positive on Perls Prussian blue stain)

Microscopic Histopathology: Abundant swollen, eosinophilic, degenerating axon spheroids (neuroaxonal dystrophy) throughout the pallidonigral system; marked loss of pallidal and nigral neurons accompanied by reactive astrocytic gliosis and macrophage infiltration with iron and ceroid-lipofuscin pigments; caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in PANK2 gene on chromosome 20p13
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic brain iron accumulation disorder featuring dramatic self-mutilating orofacial dystonia and equinovarus posturing, anchored by the pathognomonic MRI 'eye of the tiger' sign and rust-brown pallidonigral iron accumulation.

Neurology.name: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System
clinical_manifestations: Subacute progressive encephalopathy and intractable headache: Insidious, severe, unrelenting headache refractory to standard analgesics, accompanied by progressive cognitive deterioration, memory impairment, and personality changes in middle-aged adults

Recurrent multifocal cerebrovascular events: Multiple transient ischemic attacks and completed ischemic or hemorrhagic strokes in disparate vascular territories, producing fluctuating hemiparesis, aphasia, visual field cuts, and cerebellar ataxia
Absence of systemic vasculitis signs: Distinct lack of systemic symptoms (no rash, fever, weight loss, arthritis, or peripheral neuropathy) and normal or mildly elevated ESR/CRP
Intractable partial or generalized seizures: Refractory epileptic seizures resulting from cortical microvascular ischemia and leptomeningeal inflammation
radiological_manifestations: Catheter Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA): Classical pathognomonic 'string-of-beads' or 'beading' sign: multifocal, alternating areas of smooth arterial constriction (stenosis) and post-stenotic ectasia/dilatation across small and medium-sized intracranial arteries (anterior, middle, and posterior cerebral branches), associated with abrupt vascular tapering, occlusions, and collateral vessel development

High-Resolution Vessel Wall MRI (HR-VWMRI): Pathognomonic concentric, smooth, circumferential vessel wall thickening and vivid gadolinium enhancement of affected intracranial arterial segments, differentiating vasculitis from the eccentric, irregular enhancement of atherosclerosis or non-enhancing reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (RCVS)

Brain MRI (DWI, T2/FLAIR, SWI, T1+Gd): Multiple bilateral ischemic infarcts of differing ages involving both cortical gray and subcortical white matter territories; punctate microbleeds and superficial siderosis on SWI; linear and nodular leptomeningeal gadolinium enhancement in ~15-20% of cases
pathology_manifestations: Brain and Leptomeningeal Biopsy (Gold Standard): Transmural segmental inflammatory infiltration of small-to-medium-sized leptomeningeal and cortical arteries with destruction and fragmentation of the internal elastic lamina; three recognized histologic subtypes: 1) Granulomatous vasculitis (~60%): epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated Langerhans-type giant cells with vascular wall necrosis; 2) Lymphocytic vasculitis: dense CD3+ T-lymphocyte cuffs; 3) Necrotizing vasculitis: transmural fibrinoid necrosis mimicking polyarteritis nodosa; exclusion of infection, amyloid, and lymphoma
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic isolated neurovascular inflammatory entity presenting with multi-territorial strokes, pathognomonic angiographic arterial 'beading' and vessel-wall MRI enhancement, and transmural elastic lamina granulomatous pathology on brain biopsy.

Neurology.name: Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
clinical_manifestations: Staring, unblinking facial appearance with widened palpebral fissures, infrequent blinking, and deep vertical/horizontal forehead furrowing ('astonished' or 'reptilian' facies)

Vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, characteristically affecting downward voluntary saccades early and selectively, with preservation of reflexive vertical eye movements during the doll's head maneuver (oculocephalic reflex)
Procerus sign: persistent contraction of the procerus muscle producing transverse wrinkling over the bridge of the nose and a worried/perplexed stare
Early severe postural instability with unexplained, precipitate backward falls within the first year of symptoms ('rocket sign' when attempting to stand)

Severe axial rigidity in extension with prominent retrocollis (neck extension dystonia), dysarthria (growling, spastic-hypokinetic speech), and applause sign (inability to stop clapping after three claps)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Midsagittal T1-weighted): Pathognomonic 'hummingbird sign' (also called 'penguin sign') created by severe selective midbrain tegmental atrophy with concavity of the superior midbrain contour, contrasting against a preserved, rounded pontine base

Brain MRI (Axial T2/T1-weighted): Marked midbrain tegmental atrophy producing the 'Mickey Mouse sign' (or 'morning glory flower sign') due to concavity of the lateral margins of the midbrain tegmentum; midbrain anteroposterior diameter reduced to <14 mm

Quantitative Magnetic Resonance Parkinsonism Index (MRPI): Midbrain area to pons area ratio multiplied by middle cerebellar peduncle (MCP) width to superior cerebellar peduncle (SCP) width ratio (MRPI > 13.5 reliably distinguishes PSP from Parkinson disease and MSA)
Tau-PET and FDG-PET: Symmetrical hyperaccumulation of 4-repeat tau tracers and hypometabolism in the midbrain tegmentum, subthalamic nucleus, thalamus, and medial frontal cortex
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology Histopathology: 4-repeat (4R) tauopathy defined by pathognomonic 'tufted astrocytes' (dense starburst-like radiating arrays of phosphorylated tau-immunoreactive filaments in proximal astrocytic processes) in motor cortex and striatum; globose neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) and neuropil threads in subthalamic nucleus, substantia nigra, globus pallidus, locus coeruleus, and oculomotor motor complex; severe neuronal loss and gliosis in substantia nigra and superior cerebellar peduncle
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Exemplar neurodegenerative movement disorder defined clinically by the astonished facies, procerus sign, and downward gaze palsy, paired with the iconic 'hummingbird sign' and 'Mickey Mouse sign' of midbrain atrophy on brain MRI.

Neurology.name: Septic Cavernous Sinus Thrombosis
clinical_manifestations: Acute toxic febrile onset with severe periorbital and frontal headache: High spiking fevers, chills, severe retro-orbital and frontal cephalalgia, photophobia, and rapidly escalating toxic encephalopathy, typically following a mid-facial furuncle in the 'danger triangle of the face', sphenoid/ethmoid sinusitis, or dental infection

Severe chemosis and progressive proptosis: Striking, dramatic periorbital edema with violaceous discoloration, conjunctival chemosis (conjunctiva swelling and prolapsing between the eyelids), and prominent exophthalmos (proptosis) driven by obstructed venous return through the superior and inferior ophthalmic veins

Complete ophthalmoplegia and ptosis: Early abducens nerve (CN VI) palsy presenting as lateral rectus weakness and diplopia, rapidly followed by complete external and internal ophthalmoplegia involving oculomotor (CN III) and trochlear (CN IV) nerves, producing complete immobility of the eye, profound ptosis, and a dilated, sluggish or unreactive pupil

Trigeminal sensory loss and absent corneal reflex: Hyperesthesia or hypoesthesia in the ophthalmic (V1) and maxillary (V2) distribution of the trigeminal nerve, accompanied by an early loss of the ipsilateral corneal reflex

Rapid contralateral eye involvement: Hallmark pathognomonic progression of the periorbital edema, proptosis, and ophthalmoplegia to the contralateral eye within 24 to 48 hours, transmitted via the circular intercavernous sinuses across the midline
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Brain and Orbit MRI / Magnetic Resonance Venography (MRV): Pathognomonic asymmetric enlargement of the cavernous sinus with non-enhancing intraluminal filling defects (hypointense on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images) representing septic thrombus; pronounced lateral convexity of the normally concave or straight lateral wall of the cavernous sinus; dramatic dilatation, tortuosity, and thrombosis of the superior ophthalmic vein; narrowing or irregular contour of the intracavernous internal carotid artery; associated T2 hyperintensity and mucosal thickening in the adjacent sphenoid and ethmoid air cells

Contrast-Enhanced Orbit and Cranial CT / CT Venography (CTV): Demonstrates non-enhancing low-attenuation filling defects within an expanded cavernous sinus, lateral bulging of the lateral cavernous sinus margin, marked proptosis, marked enlargement of the superior ophthalmic vein, and fat stranding in the retrobulbar orbit, alongside frank opacification of the sphenoid/ethmoid sinuses

Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA): Used when carotico-cavernous fistula or internal carotid artery pseudoaneurysm / narrowing / occlusion is suspected; demonstrates non-filling of the cavernous sinus, delayed transit through the cavernous sinus tributaries, and segmental irregular stenosis or spasm of the cavernous ICA
pathology_manifestations: Vascular Histopathology and Microbiology: Acute suppurative thrombophlebitis within the trabeculated, endothelial-lined venous channels of the cavernous sinus; intraluminal septic thrombus densely packed with fibrin, necrotic debris, degenerate polymorphonuclear neutrophils, and clusters of bacteria; transmural inflammatory infiltration of the dural sinus wall extending into adjacent cranial nerves (CN III, IV, V1, V2, VI); potential adventitial and media necrosis of the internal carotid artery (septic arteritis) predisposing to catastrophic carotid rupture or mycotic aneurysm formation; Staphylococcus aureus is the predominant pathogen (>70% of cases, including methicillin-resistant S. aureus / MRSA), followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus pyogenes, Streptococcus anginosus group, Gram-negative bacilli, and anaerobes
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening neuro-ophthalmologic infection marked by photographic bilateral chemosis, proptosis, and ophthalmoplegia rapidly crossing the midline, matched radiologically by contrast CT/MRI cavernous sinus filling defects and superior ophthalmic vein thrombosis.

Neurology.name: Spinal Muscular Atrophy
clinical_manifestations: Severe generalized hypotonia in infants ('floppy infant' syndrome) with characteristic 'frog-leg' resting posture of the lower extremities (hips abducted and externally rotated, knees flexed, resting flat against the examination table)

Bell-shaped thoracic deformity: narrow, constricted upper chest wall with flared lower ribs, accompanied by prominent paradoxical (see-saw) abdominal breathing due to severe intercostal muscle paralysis with preserved diaphragmatic strength
Continuous, fine, rippling fasciculations of the tongue, accompanied by progressive tongue atrophy
Profound, symmetric, flaccid proximal muscle weakness (lower limbs affected earlier and more severely than upper limbs) with complete loss of deep tendon reflexes (areflexia)
Alert, expressive, cognitively intact facial appearance ('bright, engaging eyes') contrasting starkly with an immobile, flaccid body; weakness of cry, weak suck, and progressive bulbar palsy
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (Plain X-ray): Pathognomonic 'bell-shaped thorax' characterized by narrow apex, widening of the basal thoracic cage, thin slender ribs ('pencil ribs') due to severe intercostal muscle hypoplasia, and pectus excavatum

Whole-Body and Lower Extremity Muscle MRI: Severe, symmetric, widespread muscular atrophy and advanced fibrofatty replacement of pelvic girdle and thigh musculature (striking fatty degeneration of gluteus maximus, quadriceps, and hamstrings), with characteristic relative preservation of the diaphragm, rectus abdominis, and facial muscles
High-Resolution Spinal Cord Ultrasound and MRI: Marked volumetric thinning and caliber reduction of the cervical and lumbosacral anterior spinal cord, reflecting loss of anterior horn motor columns
Pelvic Radiography: Bilateral paralytic hip subluxation or dislocation and severe progressive neuromuscular C-shaped scoliosis
pathology_manifestations: Skeletal Muscle Biopsy Histopathology: Classic pan-fascicular / large group neurogenic atrophy: entire muscle fascicles are composed of small, rounded, atrophic myofibers with scattered or clustered massively hypertrophic type 1 muscle fibers (compensatory collateral reinnervation); endomysial connective tissue is preserved without active necrosis or inflammatory infiltration

Spinal Cord Neuropathology: Massive, selective loss and ballooning of large alpha-motor neurons in the anterior horns of the spinal cord and motor cranial nerve nuclei (CN VII, IX, X, XII); remaining neurons show central chromatolysis and neurofilament accumulation
Molecular Genetics: Biallelic homozygous deletion or loss-of-function mutation of exon 7 and/or 8 in the SMN1 gene on chromosome 5q13.2, with disease severity modulated by SMN2 copy number
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Preeminent pediatric motor neuron disease displaying the unforgettable bell-shaped chest, frog-leg posture, and tongue fasciculations, confirmed by pencil-ribs on chest X-ray, pan-fascicular neurogenic atrophy on biopsy, and SMN1 deletions.

Neurology.name: Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy
synonyms: X-linked spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy
clinical_manifestations: Prominent perioral and chin fasciculations: rhythmic, involuntary flickering quivering of the chin and perioral muscles, dramatically exacerbated by speech, pursing lips, or swallowing
Marked tongue muscle atrophy with deep longitudinal furrowing ('scrotal tongue') and relentless, coarse, continuous tongue fasciculations
Systemic signs of partial androgen insensitivity in adult males: prominent, often tender, bilateral gynecomastia; testicular atrophy; reduced fertility; and early erectile dysfunction
Postural hand tremor (often fine, fast kinetic and postural tremor mimicking essential tremor) preceding overt proximal muscle weakness by decades
Slowly progressive proximal lower limb weakness (difficulty rising from chairs, climbing stairs), muscle cramping, diminished deep tendon reflexes, and preserved longevity
radiological_manifestations: Head and Neck Muscle MRI (T1-weighted): Advanced, symmetrical fatty infiltration and volumetric atrophy of intrinsic and extrinsic tongue musculature (genioglossus, vertical and longitudinal tongue muscles), producing a hollowed, fatty appearance on axial and coronal views
Pelvic and Thigh Muscle MRI: Symmetrical fatty infiltration and atrophy of the iliopsoas, gluteus maximus, and quadriceps muscles, with relative preservation of pelvic adductors
Spinal Cord and Brainstem MRI: Progressive volumetric thinning and atrophy of the cervical anterior spinal cord and anterior motor nuclei of the lower brainstem (hypoglossal and facial nuclei)
Breast and Scrotal Ultrasound: True gynecomastia with glandular ductal proliferation (subareolar hypoechoic tissue) and bilateral testicular volume reduction
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology of Spinal Cord and Brainstem: Severe, selective loss of lower motor neurons in the anterior horns of the spinal cord and motor cranial nerve nuclei (especially CN VII, IX, X, and XII); surviving motor neurons demonstrate diffuse cytoplasmic and pathognomonic nuclear inclusions containing mutant truncated androgen receptor protein

Skeletal Muscle Biopsy: Neurogenic muscular atrophy characterized by massive grouped atrophy of myofibers (large clusters of small, angulated fibers) interspersed with reinnervated, hypertrophic fibers displaying fiber type grouping and targetoid fibers
Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion (>38 repeats) in exon 1 of the androgen receptor (AR) gene on chromosome Xq12
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Unique X-linked motor neuropathy combining lower motor neuron signs (quivering chin, scrotal tongue, fasciculations) with systemic androgen insensitivity (gynecomastia, testicular atrophy) and striking tongue MRI fatty replacement.

Neurology.name: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic facial appearance: prominent, bulging, staring unblinking eyes with upper eyelid retraction and apparent exophthalmos ('Machado-Joseph staring facies')
Continuous, visible facial, perioral, and lingual fasciculations or undulating myokymia
Progressive cerebellar ataxia with severe broad-based staggering gait, dysmetria, intention tremor, and explosive scanning dysarthria
External ophthalmoplegia: progressive restriction of voluntary saccades, gaze-evoked horizontal and vertical nystagmus, and slow saccadic velocities
Pyramidal and extrapyramidal signs: lower limb spasticity, brisk hyperreflexia, extensor plantar responses (Babinski signs), and prominent dystonic limb posturing (equinovarus foot deformities)
Peripheral amyotrophy with distal wasting and sensory loss in the lower extremities
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Sagittal and Axial T1/T2-weighted): Severe, progressive olivopontocerebellar and brainstem atrophy: striking thinning of the basis pontis, severe atrophy of the superior cerebellar peduncles (SCP) and dentate nuclei, with marked enlargement of the fourth ventricle and prepontine cistern
Diffusion MRI: Microstructural degeneration with increased mean diffusivity and decreased fractional anisotropy in the cerebellar white matter, cerebellar peduncles, and spinocerebellar tracts

Proton MR Spectroscopy (1H-MRS): Significant reduction in N-acetylaspartate/creatine (NAA/Cr) ratio within the pontine tegmentum, cerebellar vermis, and cerebellar hemispheres, signifying neuronal loss
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology Histopathology: Autosomal dominant polyglutamine (polyQ) neurodegeneration characterized by pathognomonic, widespread ubiquitin- and ataxin-3-positive neuronal intranuclear inclusions (NIIs) within degenerating neurons of the dentate nucleus, substantia nigra, subthalamic nucleus, and motor cranial nerve nuclei (CN III, IV, VI, VII, X, XII); striking loss of neurons in dentate nuclei and anterior horns of the spinal cord, with relative sparing of the inferior olive and Purkinje cells (distinguishing SCA3 from olivopontocerebellar atrophy)
Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion (>60-87 repeats) in exon 10 of the ATXN3 gene on chromosome 14q32.1
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Most prevalent autosomal dominant ataxia globally, presenting with the unmistakable staring proptotic facies, facial fasciculations, and severe gait ataxia, supported by marked pontine/superior cerebellar peduncle atrophy on MRI and intranuclear polyQ ataxin-3 inclusions.

Neurology.name: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Port-wine stain (nevus flammeus): unilateral, flat, pink, dark-red or violaceous vascular birthmark covering the ophthalmic (V1) and maxillary (V2) dermatomes of the trigeminal nerve, including upper eyelid
Congenital buphthalmos ('ox eye': enlarged cornea/globe from infantile glaucoma)
Contralateral focal motor seizures, hemiparesis, and hemianopia
Choroidal hemangioma on ophthalmoscopic exam ('tomato catsup' fundus)
radiological_manifestations: Brain CT (Non-contrast): Pathognomonic gyriform, serpentine, cortical calcification under the leptomeningeal angioma ('tram-track' or 'railroad-track' cortical calcification), ipsilateral calvarial thickening and hyperpneumatization of sinuses
Brain MRI with Contrast: Leptomeningeal capillary-venous angiomatosis with avid pial gadolinium enhancement, ipsilateral cerebral hemiatrophy, enlarged and hypervascular ipsilateral choroid plexus
pathology_manifestations: Brain/meningeal biopsy: Thin-walled, tortuous, dilated, non-neoplastic venous and capillary blood vessels packing the leptomeninges (pia-arachnoid); underlying cerebral cortex shows severe neuronal loss, marked astrogliosis, and extensive pericapillary calcification of cortical layers II and III
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Classic neurocutaneous disorder pairing the vivid facial port-wine stain and buphthalmos with pathognomonic gyriform 'tram-track' cortical calcifications on brain CT.

Neurology.name: Susac Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic clinical triad: 1) Subacute encephalopathy (cognitive dysfunction, confusion, severe memory loss, behavioral alterations, paranoia, and severe migraine-like headache); 2) Branch retinal artery occlusions (BRAO) presenting as dark scotomas, visual field cuts, or metamorphopsia; 3) Acute-onset bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, typically asymmetric with low-to-mid frequency loss, accompanied by tinnitus and severe vertigo

Fundoscopic Gass plaques: Direct ophthalmoscopy / fundus photography reveals characteristic small, discrete, yellow-white refractile or non-refractile atheromatous-like plaques (Gass plaques) located in retinal arterioles distant from bifurcations, accompanied by boxcar segmentation and localized retinal pallor/edema

Psychiatric and cognitive disturbances: Fluctuating abulia, confabulation, emotional lability, and catatonic-like states in young female patients, often misattributed to atypical psychosis or primary demyelinating disease
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial and Sagittal T2/FLAIR, DWI, T1+Gd): Pathognomonic 'snowball' lesions—small (3-7 mm), round, well-demarcated hyperintense lesions with restricted diffusion centered in the central fibers of the corpus callosum with strict sparing of the callosal-septal interface; sagittal T1-weighted images show evolution into 'punched-out' hypointense callosal holes ('Swiss cheese' or 'black holes'); 'spoke-wheel' lesions radiating perpendicularly through the callosum; leptomeningeal enhancement in up to 33% of patients

Retinal Fluorescein Angiography (FFA): Gold standard ophthalmologic modality: reveals multifocal branch retinal artery occlusions, delayed arterial filling, and pathognomonic segmental Arteriolar Wall Hyperfluorescence (AWH) affecting arteriolar segments remote from the actual occlusion sites

Pure Tone Audiometry: Diagnostic bilateral, asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss characteristically affecting the low-to-medium frequencies (250-2000 Hz), reflecting microinfarction of the apical turn of the cochlea
pathology_manifestations: Brain / leptomeningeal histopathology: CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell-mediated autoimmune endotheliopathy directed against endothelial cells of the precapillary arterioles; microvascular endothelial cell swelling, microvascular occlusion, and microinfarcts in the corpus callosum, cerebral white matter, and deep gray matter; absence of transmural necrotizing vasculitis, absence of fibrinoid necrosis, and absence of prominent perivascular lymphocytic cuffs
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Visually striking neurovascular triad of encephalopathy, Gass plaques and BRAO, pathognomonic corpus callosum 'snowball' and 'punched-out hole' lesions on MRI, and diagnostic fluorescein arteriolar wall hyperfluorescence.

Neurology.name: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
clinical_manifestations: Hypomelanotic macules: polygonal or lanceolate ash-leaf spots (>=3 lesions highlighted by Wood's lamp) and confetti macules
Facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum): symmetrical, red-brown, telangiectatic papules over the nose, nasolabial folds, and cheeks in a butterfly distribution
Shagreen patch: leathery, pebbled, flesh-colored plaque (connective tissue nevus) on lumbosacral region
Periungual and subungual fibromas (Koenen tumors): smooth, firm nodules arising from nail folds
Dental enamel pits and gingival fibromas
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI / CT: Cortical and subcortical tubers (flair hyperintense widened gyri); subependymal nodules (calcified 'candle guttering' lining the ventricles on CT); Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytoma (SEGA: avidly enhancing mass at the Foramen of Monro causing hydrocephalus)
Abdominal CT / MRI: Multiple bilateral renal angiomyolipomas (AMLs) containing macroscopic fat density (<-20 HU)
Chest HRCT: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (thin-walled cystic lung disease in females)
Echocardiography: Cardiac rhabdomyomas (intracardiac tumors projecting into ventricles)
pathology_manifestations: Tissue biopsy: Cortical tubers display disordered cortical lamination, bizarre multinucleated giant cells, and balloon cells; angiofibromas display dermal vascular proliferation with perivascular fibrosis; renal AMLs exhibit triphasic histology (mature adipose tissue, thick-walled dysplastic blood vessels, and smooth muscle spindles)
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Renowned visual triad (epilepsy, adenoma sebaceum, intellectual disability) with ash-leaf spots, Koenen tumors, and shagreen patches paired with ventricular 'candle-guttering' nodules, SEGA, and renal AMLs on imaging.

Neurology.name: Von Hippel-Lindau Disease
clinical_manifestations: Retinal capillary hemangioblastomas (von Hippel angiomas): Direct fundoscopy and color fundus photography demonstrate bright reddish-orange or pink spherical vascular lesions located in the peripheral or peripapillary retina, supplied by a conspicuously dilated, tortuous retinal feeder artery and drained by an engorged, tortuous vein, frequently surrounded by hard lipid exudates and macular star formation

Polycythemic ruddy cyanosis / plethora: Striking facial rubor, flushing, and conjunctival suffusion caused by secondary polycythemia resulting from tumor-driven ectopic erythropoietin (EPO) secretion by renal cell carcinomas or cerebellar hemangioblastomas

Pheochromocytoma paroxysms: Episodic severe hypertension accompanied by the classic symptomatic triad of profuse diaphoresis, headache, and episodic pallor/flushing, with postural orthostatic hypotension

Cerebellar and vestibular signs: Subacute truncal ataxia, appendicular intention tremor, dysmetria, past-pointing, and coarse horizontal/gaze-evoked nystagmus resulting from posterior fossa hemangioblastomas and obstructive hydrocephalus
Palpable scrotal or epididymal masses: Painless, firm, nodular scrotal swellings due to papillary cystadenomas of the epididymis in males or broad ligament cystadenomas in females
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Spinal Cord Contrast-Enhanced MRI: Pathognomonic hemangioblastomas appearing as well-demarcated cystic lesions with an intensely enhancing, vascular mural nodule abutting the pial surface; prominent serpiginous flow voids from dilated feeding vessels; characteristic predilection for the cerebellar hemispheres, vermis, medulla, and dorsal spinal cord; avid nodular enhancement on post-gadolinium T1-weighted images with high T2 signal in surrounding cystic fluid

Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT and MRI: Multicentric bilateral clear cell renal cell carcinomas (RCC) manifesting as heterogeneous enhancing cortical lesions with necrotic cystic components; innumerable simple pancreatic cysts, serous microcystic cystadenomas, and hypervascular pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNET); bilateral adrenal pheochromocytomas with intense arterial phase enhancement, heterogeneous central necrosis, and delayed wash-out

Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Immediate, intense hyperfluorescence of retinal capillary hemangioblastomas in the early arterial phase with late profuse fluorescein leakage into the vitreous and surrounding subretinal exudation
pathology_manifestations: Hemangioblastoma histopathology: Highly vascular neoplasm composed of an intricate meshwork of thin-walled, arborizing capillary blood vessels lined by normal endothelial cells, interspersed with abundant, distinctive vacuolated stromal cells containing lipid-rich, clear, lipid-laden cytoplasm; immunohistochemistry shows positive staining for inhibin-A, S100, neuron-specific enolase (NSE), and carbonic anhydrase IX (CA-IX); genetic confirmation demonstrates germline loss-of-function mutation or deletion of the VHL tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 3p25-26
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Classic multi-system phakomatosis combining unmistakable fundoscopic retinal angiomas and polycythemic facies with pathognomonic MRI cystic lesions with enhancing mural nodules, abdominal CT renal cell carcinomas and pheochromocytomas, and characteristic lipid-laden stromal pathology.

Neurology.name: Wilson's Disease
clinical_manifestations: Kayser-Fleischer (KF) rings: golden-brown or greenish copper rings at the periphery of the cornea in Descemet's membrane on slit-lamp biomicroscopy
Sunflower cataracts (anterior subcapsular copper deposition)
Facial dystonia creating an involuntary fixed vacant smile ('risus sardonicus')
'Wing-beating' tremor (coarse, slow, high-amplitude postural tremor upon arm abduction)
Dysarthria, dystonia, choreoathetosis, and parkinsonian rigidity
Stigmata of chronic liver disease (spider angiomas, palmar erythema, jaundice)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Pathognomonic 'face of the giant panda' sign in the midbrain (normal red nuclei as 'eyes', normal substantia nigra as 'ears', and hypointense superior colliculus as 'chin' set against hyperintense tegmentum on T2); 'face of the miniature panda' in the pons; bilateral symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in lentiform and caudate nuclei, thalami, and brainstem
Abdominal Ultrasound / MRI: Micronodular or macronodular cirrhosis, splenomegaly, ascites
pathology_manifestations: Liver needle biopsy: Steatosis, glycogenated nuclei, chronic active hepatitis progressing to micronodular cirrhosis; marked elevation of hepatic copper concentration (>250 ug/g dry weight); rhodanine or rubeanic acid staining demonstrates coarse copper granules in periportal hepatocytes
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield neuro-metabolic entity with the unmistakable corneal Kayser-Fleischer ring paired with the textbook 'face of the giant panda' sign on brain MRI.

Neurology.name: X-Linked Adrenoleukodystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Bronze hyperpigmentation when adrenal failure accompanies the cerebral disease
Behavioral change and school failure are not images; the photograph is the pigment plus the MRI
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: posterior white-matter demyelination with a leading edge of contrast enhancement, scored by the Loes pattern
pathology_manifestations: Adrenal cortical atrophy; very-long-chain fatty acids and ABCD1 sequencing confirm
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Leukodystrophy with a named MRI pattern and, often, Addisonian photographs.

Neurology.name: Melkersson-Rosenthal Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent non-pitting lip or facial swelling
Fissured lingua plicata
Recurrent facial palsy, photographed during an attack
radiological_manifestations: MRI may show facial-nerve enhancement during palsy; it is supportive, not defining
pathology_manifestations: Non-caseating granulomas in the lip, overlapping orofacial granulomatosis
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Triad with three photographable findings: lip edema, fissured tongue, and facial palsy.

Neurology.name: Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy
clinical_manifestations: Acute painless central vision loss in a young adult, often sequential
Fundus in the acute phase: disc hyperemia and peripapillary telangiectatic microangiopathy
radiological_manifestations: Optical coherence tomography: early retinal-nerve-fiber swelling, then atrophy; MRI excludes compressive and demyelinating mimics
pathology_manifestations: Mitochondrial DNA mutation, most often m.11778G>A; there is no useful nerve biopsy
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Mitochondrial optic neuropathy with an acute fundus photograph and OCT, distinct from demyelinating optic neuritis.

Neurology.name: Cockayne Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cachectic dwarfism, sunken eyes, and photosensitivity
Disproportionately small head
radiological_manifestations: CT or MRI: basal-ganglia calcification and white-matter hypomyelination
pathology_manifestations: Transcription-coupled repair defect; a skin biopsy is not routinely diagnostic
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: DNA-repair progeria with a face photograph and basal-ganglia calcification.

Neurology.name: Niemann-Pick Disease Type C
clinical_manifestations: Vertical supranuclear gaze palsy
Gelastic cataplexy and school-age cognitive loss
Neonatal cholestasis in the early-onset form
radiological_manifestations: MRI is often normal early, then shows cerebellar atrophy
pathology_manifestations: Filipin staining of unesterified cholesterol in fibroblasts; NPC1 or NPC2 confirms
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Neurovisceral lipid disease whose gaze palsy and, in infants, cholestasis are the clinical images.

Neurology.name: LGI1-Antibody Encephalitis
clinical_manifestations: Very brief ipsilateral face and arm dystonic spasms, often filmed
Later memory loss
radiological_manifestations: MRI: temporal T2 hyperintensity or a normal scan
Hyponatremia is laboratory, not an image
pathology_manifestations: LGI1 antibodies; brain biopsy is not required
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Autoimmune encephalitis identified by a filmed faciobrachial seizure and antibody testing.

Neurology.name: Canavan Disease
clinical_manifestations: Macrocephaly and hypotonia in early infancy
radiological_manifestations: MRI: diffuse white-matter T2 hyperintensity including the subcortical U fibers, with an elevated NAA peak on spectroscopy
pathology_manifestations: Spongy myelin vacuolization; elevated urine NAA
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Leukodystrophy with macrocephaly photographs and a spectroscopy-confirmed MRI pattern.

Neurology.name: Zellweger Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: High forehead, large fontanelle, and severe hypotonia
Hepatomegaly and neonatal seizures
radiological_manifestations: MRI: germinolytic cysts and neuronal-migration abnormalities
Patellar and acetabular stippling on radiographs
pathology_manifestations: Absent peroxisomes and elevated very-long-chain fatty acids
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Peroxisomal syndrome with a face photograph, stippled epiphyses, and a neuronal-migration MRI.

Neurology.name: Parry-Romberg Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Progressive unilateral atrophy of the skin, subcutaneous adipose tissue, underlying facial musculature, and osteocartilaginous structures of the face, typically starting in the first or second decade of life

Characteristic sharply demarcated linear vertical furrow or scar-like depression on the frontoparietal paramedian scalp and forehead ("en coup de sabre" depression) accompanied by focal cicatricial alopecia
Severe enophthalmos and dystopia from atrophy of the retrobulbar and periorbital adipose tissue, accompanied by eyelid retraction, lagophthalmos, or Horner syndrome
Deviation of the mouth, philtrum, and nose toward the affected atrophic side with hemiatrophy of the tongue, gingiva, and unilateral jaw malocclusion
Neurological sequelae including intractable focal motor or sensory seizures (epilepsia partialis continua), migraine-like hemiplegic headaches, and trigeminal neuralgia
radiological_manifestations: Brain & Orbital MRI: Striking asymmetry of extracranial soft tissues with marked loss of facial and orbital fat; ipsilateral cerebral white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities, subcortical leukoencephalopathy, focal ipsilateral cerebral cortical atrophy, ventricular dilatation, and leptomeningeal gadolinium enhancement

Non-Contrast Head & Maxillofacial CT: Marked bony hypoplasia and thinning of the ipsilateral mandible, maxilla, zygoma, and frontal bone with prominent intracranial intraparenchymal or cortical calcifications

Magnetic Resonance Angiography (MRA) / CTA: Intracranial vascular dysplasias, aneurysmal dilatation, focal vessel caliber stenosis, and vascular malformations involving ipsilateral internal carotid or middle cerebral artery branches
pathology_manifestations: Skin and soft tissue biopsy: Severe dermal sclerosis and hyalinization with progressive disappearance of the subcutaneous fat architecture; atrophy of hair follicles and sweat glands; perivascular and perineural chronic lymphocytic infiltrates
Histopathology: Endothelial swelling and perivascular elastosis in the reticular dermis with condensation and homogenization of collagen bundles resembling localized scleroderma/morphea
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Classic neurocutaneous entity featuring profound unilateral facial and craniofacial atrophy, en coup de sabre deformity, and enophthalmos paired with ipsilateral cerebral white matter lesions and cortical calcifications.

Neurology.name: Kearns-Sayre Syndrome
synonyms: Chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia with ragged red fibers
clinical_manifestations: Classic clinical triad presenting before age 20: progressive external ophthalmoplegia (PEO), atypical pigmentary retinopathy, and cardiac conduction block
Bilateral, symmetric, slowly progressive severe ptosis with compensatory contraction of the frontalis muscle and backward head tilt (retroflexion of neck) to visualize objects in the field of view
Progressive ophthalmoparesis culminating in complete bilateral external ophthalmoplegia with fixed globes, sparing pupillary light and near reflexes

Ophthalmoscopic fundus examination demonstrating diffuse "salt-and-pepper" pigmentary retinopathy and chorioretinal atrophy, most prominent at the posterior pole and mid-periphery (unlike bone-spicule deposits in retinitis pigmentosa)
Systemic manifestations: progressive cerebellar ataxia, sensorineural hearing loss, proximal limb myopathy, endocrine abnormalities (diabetes mellitus, hypoparathyroidism), and short stature
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Symmetric T2-weighted and FLAIR hyperintensities within the subcortical cerebral white matter, globus pallidus, caudate nuclei, thalami, brainstem tegmentum, and cerebellar dentate nuclei, with sparing of deep cerebral white matter
Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (1H-MRS): Prominent lactate resonance doublet peak at 1.33 ppm in affected brain parenchyma and CSF, indicative of defective mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
Electrocardiogram / Transthoracic Echocardiogram: High-grade atrioventricular block (bifascicular or complete third-degree AV block) requiring urgent pacemaker placement; progressive cardiomyopathy
pathology_manifestations: Skeletal Muscle Biopsy (Diagnostic Hallmark): Modified Gomori trichrome staining reveals pathognomonic "ragged-red fibers" (RRFs) caused by massive subsarcolemmal accumulations of abnormal mitochondria; cytochrome c oxidase (COX) histochemistry displays mosaic pattern of COX-negative muscle fibers
Electron Microscopy: Disorganized myofibrillar architecture with dramatically enlarged mitochondria containing paracrystalline "parking-lot" inclusions and disrupted cristae
Molecular Genetics: Large-scale single heteroplasmic deletions of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), commonly a 4.97-kb "common deletion" spanning multiple tRNA and respiratory chain genes
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic visual mitochondrial disorder combining striking bedside facial photographs (extreme bilateral ptosis and compensatory chin-up posture), salt-and-pepper pigmentary fundus photography, and pathognomonic Gomori trichrome ragged-red fibers.

Neurology.name: Rasmussen Encephalitis
clinical_manifestations: Triphasic clinical progression in children or young adults: prodromal non-specific phase, acute progressive phase, and late residual stable phase characterized by severe neurological deficits

Epilepsia partialis continua (EPC): pathognomonic relentless, continuous, focal rhythmic clonic muscle jerks confined to one side of the body (typically face, hand, or thumb) persisting for days, months, or years without impairment of consciousness
Progressive unilateral motor loss resulting in dense hemiparesis and hemiplegia on the side affected by focal motor seizures
Progressive cognitive decline, homonymous hemianopia, and prominent receptive/expressive aphasia when the dominant cerebral hemisphere is affected
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Pathognomonic Progressive Unilateral Atrophy): Serial imaging demonstrates progressive, irreversible unilateral cortical atrophy with enlargement of the ipsilateral lateral ventricle (especially frontal and temporal horns) and widening of hemispheric sulci/Sylvian fissure; contralateral hemisphere remains completely unaffected

T2-weighted and FLAIR MRI: Hyperintense signal abnormality in the cortex and subcortical white matter of the affected hemisphere during active inflammatory stages, with focal caudate and putaminal atrophy

Fluorodeoxyglucose PET (18F-FDG-PET): Marked unilateral hemispheric hypometabolism during interictal phases, contrasting with hypermetabolic focal seizure foci during active epilepsia partialis continua
pathology_manifestations: Brain Biopsy / Hemispherectomy Neuropathology: Patchy multifocal chronic cortical inflammation driven by cytotoxic CD8+ T lymphocytes forming perivascular cuffs and infiltrating the neuropil in close apposition to apoptotic neurons

Microglial activation: Prominent microglial nodules (babès nodules) throughout cerebral cortex and white matter, accompanied by reactive astrogliosis, neuronal loss, and spongiosis confined entirely to the affected hemisphere
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Exceptional clinical-radiological neurological entity featuring continuous bedside focal motor twitches (epilepsia partialis continua) and dramatic, unmistakable progressive unilateral hemispheric cortical atrophy on serial brain MRI.

Neurology.name: Miller Fisher Syndrome
synonyms: Acute ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and areflexia syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Classic acute post-infectious clinical triad (often preceded 1-3 weeks by Campylobacter jejuni or viral gastroenteritis/URI): acute external ophthalmoplegia, sensory ataxia, and generalized areflexia

Acute bilateral external ophthalmoparesis: dramatic limitation of conjugate eye movements starting in vertical or lateral gaze and rapidly progressing to complete symmetric or asymmetric bilateral external ophthalmoplegia
Bilateral ptosis, pupillary sluggishness or light-near dissociation, and fixed dilated pupils (internal ophthalmoplegia in severe cases)
Profound sensory ataxia with broad-based unsteadiness of gait and prominent dysmetria disproportionate to any motor weakness; preserved limb strength is a core feature
Loss of all deep tendon reflexes (universal generalized areflexia or hyporeflexia) with preserved sensation or minimal distal paresthesias
radiological_manifestations: Brain & Spine MRI with Gadolinium: High-resolution contrast-enhanced T1 sequences frequently show smooth enhancement of cranial nerves (CN III, IV, and VI) and dorsal spinal roots/cauda equina due to autoimmune disruption of the blood-nerve barrier
Orbital MRI: Excludes structural mass lesions, orbital apex syndrome, thyroid eye disease, or cavernous sinus thrombosis

Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS / EMG): Sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitude reduction or absence with normal or minimally slowed motor conduction velocities; absent H-reflexes confirming sensory afferent pathway disruption
pathology_manifestations: Serology (Diagnostic Hallmark): Exceptionally high titers (>90-95% sensitivity and specificity) of serum IgG antibodies directed against GQ1b ganglioside, which is highly enriched in the paranodal myelin of human oculomotor, trochlear, abducens cranial nerves and muscle spindle primary afferents
CSF Analysis: Albuminocytologic dissociation (markedly elevated CSF protein with normal white blood cell count, <5 WBC/mcL)
Nerve Pathology: Acute antibody- and complement-mediated attack on the nodes of Ranvier of cranial and peripheral nerves with localized paranodal demyelination and microvascular inflammation
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic acute neuro-ophthalmologic disease entity with distinct visual ocular motility signs (bilateral external ophthalmoplegia and ptosis), gait ataxia, pathognomonic anti-GQ1b ganglioside serology, and cranial nerve enhancement on MRI.

Neurology.name: Wernicke Encephalopathy
clinical_manifestations: Classic clinical triad caused by acute thiamine (vitamin B1) depletion (seen in chronic alcoholism, hyperemesis gravidarum, prolonged fasting, bariatric surgery, or TPN without vitamins): acute encephalopathy, gait ataxia, and prominent ocular motor signs

Ocular motor abnormalities: pathognomonic bilateral abducens (CN VI) nerve palsies causing horizontal diplopia; prominent horizontal, vertical, and rotary nystagmus (especially gaze-evoked horizontal nystagmus); bilateral conjugate gaze palsies progressing to complete external ophthalmoplegia in advanced stages
Truncal and gait ataxia: broad-based, unsteady, cerebellar gait with prominent postural instability and inability to perform tandem gait, often necessitating wheelchair assistance

Acute confusional state: profound apathy, spatial disorientation, drowsiness, inattention, progressing without thiamine repletion to stupor, coma, or permanent anterograde Korsakoff amnesic confabulatory psychosis
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Pathognomonic Pattern): Highly characteristic symmetric hyperintensity on T2-weighted, FLAIR, and DWI sequences localized to the mammillary bodies, periaqueductal gray matter of the midbrain, medial thalami, tectal plate, and third ventricle margins
Post-Contrast T1 MRI: Intense avid enhancement of the mammillary bodies (virtually pathognomonic sign of active thiamine deficiency)
Gradient Recalled Echo (GRE) / Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging (SWI): Petechial microhemorrhages and hemosiderin staining within the mammillary bodies and paraventricular thalamic regions
pathology_manifestations: Gross Brain Pathology: Petechial hemorrhages, discoloration, and softening specifically confined to the mammillary bodies, periaqueductal gray, and floor of the fourth ventricle; chronic atrophy of the mammillary bodies

Histopathology: Endothelial swelling and capillary proliferation with microvascular remodeling; localized petechial extravasation of erythrocytes, microglial proliferation, and spongiform neuropil vacuolation with relative preservation of neuronal perikarya (non-infarctive cytotoxic edema)
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Critical neurological emergency featuring overt physical ocular motor signs (bilateral lateral rectus palsies and multidirectional nystagmus) combined with pathognomonic symmetrical mammillary body and periaqueductal T2/FLAIR hyperintensity and enhancement on MRI.

Neurology.name: Stiff-Person Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Insidious progressive fluctuating symmetric rigidity and stiffness of axial, paraspinal, abdominal, and proximal limb muscles, causing a rigid, robotic, "tin soldier" or "statue-like" gait

Pathognomonic fixed hyperlordosis of the lumbar spine caused by persistent simultaneous contraction of the thoracolumbar paraspinal and abdominal rectus muscles, persisting even when the patient lies recumbent or attempts relaxation

Violent, excruciating, episodic reflex muscle spasms triggered by unexpected acoustic stimuli (doorbell, loud noise), light emotional stress, cold temperature, or sudden touch, causing catastrophic stiff falls ("like a felled log") without protective outstretched arms
Severe task-specific phobias (agoraphobia, task-freeze when crossing open unassisted spaces), muscle hypertrophy, and board-like palpably rock-hard abdominal and paraspinal musculature
radiological_manifestations: Spine Radiography & CT: Exaggerated lumbar hyperlordosis with rigid paraspinal alignment without intrinsic destructive vertebral lesions or primary ankylosing spinal disease
Brain & Spinal Cord MRI: Usually normal or non-specific; essential for excluding compressive cervical or thoracic myelopathy, structural tumors, and demyelinating lesions

Electromyography (EMG - Diagnostic Hallmark): Pathognomonic continuous motor unit action potential (CMUAP) activity firing at rest in agonist and antagonist muscles simultaneously, which completely abolishes following intravenous diazepam administration
pathology_manifestations: Serology and CSF Biomarkers: Extremely high titers of autoantibodies targeting glutamic acid decarboxylase (anti-GAD65) in serum and CSF (>10,000 IU/mL; >80% of patients), or anti-amphiphysin antibodies in paraneoplastic cases associated with breast or small-cell lung cancer

Pathophysiology: Autoimmune loss of GABAergic inhibition in the spinal cord and motor cortex leading to unchecked tonic motor neuron firing and lack of reciprocal inhibition between opposing muscle groups
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Visually striking neurological condition featuring unforgettable bedside physical exam postures (rigid robot-like gait, rock-hard abdomen, persistent hyperlordosis) and pathognomonic continuous motor unit activity on EMG confirmed by anti-GAD65 autoantibodies.

Neurology.name: Möbius Syndrome
synonyms: Congenital facial diplegia and abducens nerve palsy
clinical_manifestations: Congenital non-progressive bilateral facial (CN VII) and abducens (CN VI) nerve palsies resulting in a completely mask-like, unexpressive, impassive facies ("frozen face") with complete inability to smile, frown, puff the cheeks, or whistle

Bilateral lagophthalmos: incomplete eyelid closure during blinking and sleep, leading to exposure keratitis and nocturnal corneal dryness; upward deviation of the eyes during attempts to close lids (intact Bell phenomenon)

Complete or near-complete inability to abduct either eye past midline with preservation of vertical gaze (supranuclear and third-nerve vertical pathways spared); cross-eyed appearance (convergent strabismus / esotropia)
Feeding difficulties and drooling in neonates due to weak orbicularis oris and hypoglossal (CN XII) nerve involvement, causing a furrowed, atrophic, or microglossic tongue

Associated musculoskeletal anomalies in 50-60%: clubfoot (talipes equinovarus), syndactyly, brachydactyly, or Poland syndrome (unilateral absence of the pectoralis major muscle and ipsilateral symbrachydactyly)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Brainstem MRI (3D CISS / FIESTA): Complete absence or profound hypoplasia of the facial (CN VII) and abducens (CN VI) cranial nerve rootlets as they exit the pons; hypoplasia of the facial colliculus and dorsal brainstem tegmentum
Brainstem CT: Focal punctate calcifications within the dorsal pontine tegmentum at the floor of the fourth ventricle corresponding to the abducens nuclei
Orbital MRI: Marked muscular atrophy or hypoplasia of the lateral rectus muscles bilaterally with normal superior, inferior, and medial recti
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology: Agenesis, hypoplasia, or degeneration of the motor nuclei of the sixth and seventh cranial nerves within the pontine tegmentum; absence of motor rootlet axons in the peripheral facial and abducens nerve trunks

Etiology: Disruption of early embryonic vascular supply to the subclavian artery branches and basilar vertebral arterial arcade (subclavian artery supply disruption sequence) during weeks 4-7 of gestation
Neurology.inclusion_rationale: Congenital neuro-ophthalmologic entity defined by an instantly recognizable facial photographic phenotype (expressionless mask-like face, bilateral lagophthalmos, abducens palsy) coupled with brainstem cranial nerve agenesis on high-resolution MRI.

Neurology.name: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Severe, excruciating, deep, boring, lancinating retro-orbital and periorbital unilateral head pain centered around the brow and temple

Ipsilateral painful ophthalmoplegia developing within days of pain onset: paresis or paralysis of the oculomotor (CN III), trochlear (CN IV), and/or abducens (CN VI) nerves, manifesting with diplopia and limitation of ocular excursion in multiple directions
Ptosis and pupillary abnormalities (dilated non-reactive pupil due to parasympathetic CN III involvement or Horner syndrome due to sympathetic plexus involvement around the internal carotid artery)
Sensory loss and hyperesthesia over the ipsilateral forehead, brow, and cornea (involvement of the ophthalmic V1 division, and occasionally maxillary V2 division, of the trigeminal nerve)
Dramatic, rapid relief of severe pain within 24-72 hours following systemic high-dose corticosteroid administration (diagnostic criterion)
radiological_manifestations: Brain & Orbital MRI with Contrast (Diagnostic Modality of Choice): Pathognomonic focal soft-tissue thickening, enlargement, and avid homogeneous gadolinium enhancement filling the ipsilateral cavernous sinus, superior orbital fissure, and/or orbital apex, with isointense to hypointense signal on T1/T2-weighted images
