Severe feeding difficulties and failure to thrive: Disrupted suck-swallow-breathe coordination due to the posterior tongue occluding the oropharynx, leading to prolonged feeding sessions, fatigue, nasal regurgitation, recurrent microaspiration, and aspiration pneumonia

Secondary pectus excavatum: Progressive inward sternal depression resulting from chronic, severe intrathoracic negative pressure generated against the obstructed upper airway during inspiratory efforts in infancy

Associated syndromic features (in syndromic PRS): High myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration, and retinal detachment in Stickler syndrome (the most common syndromic cause, ~25-35%); conotruncal cardiac defects in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome; downward-slanting palpebral fissures and zygomatic hypoplasia in Treacher Collins syndrome
radiological_manifestations: 3D Reconstructed Craniofacial CT: Exquisite visualization of the hypoplastic, shortened mandibular body and ramus with acute mandibular angles; demonstrates severe posterior displacement of the genial tubercles and tongue base tightly abutted against the posterior pharyngeal wall, producing critical slit-like narrowing or complete obliteration of the retroglossal airway lumen; wide U-shaped cleft of the secondary palate with widely separated palatine shelves

Dynamic Airway Fluoroscopy / Cine MRI: Demonstrates dynamic inspiratory collapse of the tongue base into the hypopharynx (glossoptosis) acting as a ball-valve or piston-like total airway occlusion during tidal breathing; objectively demonstrates restoration of oropharyngeal airway dimensions during prone positioning, nasopharyngeal airway stenting, or surgical mandibular distraction osteogenesis (MDO)

Lateral Cephalometry / Skull Radiographs: Markedly decreased sella-nasion-B point (SNB) angle and increased ANB angle reflecting severe skeletal Class II retrognathia; foreshortened mandibular effective length (condylion to gnathion); hypoplasia of the mandibular symphysis
pathology_manifestations: Pathogenetic Sequence Mechanism: Primary intrauterine developmental arrest or mechanical hypoplasia of the mandible occurring prior to week 9 of gestation prevents the normal caudal descent of the embryonic tongue; the persistently high, interposed tongue mechanically prevents the bilateral lateral palatine shelves from elevating above the tongue dorsum and fusing in the midline, creating the pathognomonic rounded, wide U-shaped cleft palate (distinct from the typical V-shaped cleft palate resulting from intrinsic palatal shelf failure)

Molecular Genetics & Cytogenetics: Heterozygous disruption or translocation of non-coding upstream cis-regulatory enhancer elements of the SOX9 gene on chromosome 17q24.3 in isolated non-syndromic PRS; syndromic forms verified by targeted genetic testing: heterozygous mutations in COL2A1, COL11A1, or COL11A2 in Stickler syndrome; 22q11.2 microdeletion (TBX1) in velocardiofacial syndrome; TCOF1, POLR1D, or POLR1C mutations in Treacher Collins syndrome
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Classic textbook pediatric craniofacial malformation sequence where the bedside photographic finding of retrognathia and glossoptosis correlates with cross-sectional airway CT imaging demonstrating physical airway occlusion, and elucidates a fundamental paradigm of embryological mechanical cascades.

Pediatrics.name: Prader-Willi Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Biphasic clinical course: Phase 1 (neonatal/infancy) presents with severe central hypotonia ('floppy infant'), lethargy, weak cry, absent suck reflex, and failure to thrive requiring tube feeding
Phase 2 (early childhood): Insatiable voracious appetite (hyperphagia) due to lack of satiety leading to rapid development of massive central obesity

Characteristic dysmorphic craniofacial features: narrow bifrontal diameter (dolichocephaly), almond-shaped palpebral fissures, thin upper vermilion border with downturned corners of mouth ('fish-like' mouth), hypopigmentation of hair, skin, and irises
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: micropenis, cryptorchidism, and hypoplastic scrotal sac in males; hypoplastic labia minora/clitoris in females
Acromicria: disproportionately small hands and feet with straight ulnar borders
radiological_manifestations: Bone Age Radiographs (Left Hand/Wrist): Significant delay in skeletal maturation throughout childhood, followed by accelerated epiphyseal fusion and resultant adult short stature
Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA): Markedly elevated total body fat mass percentage with significant reduction in lean muscle mass and generalized osteopenia/osteoporosis
Spine Radiography: High prevalence of progressive scoliosis and kyphosis (>40-80% of adolescents)
Brain and Sella MRI: Hypoplasia of the pituitary gland, decreased pituitary height, or small sella turcica; normal posterior pituitary bright spot
pathology_manifestations: Hypothalamic Neurohistopathology: Marked reduction in the number and volume of oxytocinergic neurons within the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus; testicular biopsy reveals prepubertal seminiferous tubules with germ cell depletion and absent mature Leydig cells

Molecular Genetics: Absence of paternal expression in the 15q11.2-q13 imprinted region, caused by paternal 15q11-q13 deletion (65-75%), maternal uniparental disomy 15 (20-30%), or imprinting center defects (1-3%)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal biphasic pediatric syndrome evolving from the floppy infant to hyperphagic morbid obesity, small hands/feet, almond eyes, delayed bone age, and hypothalamic neuroendocrine disruption.

Pediatrics.name: Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic broad, spatulate thumbs and great toes (halluces), often with persistent radial deviation (angulation)

Highly characteristic facial dysmorphism: prominent beaked or aquiline nose with the nasal columella extending conspicuously below the lower margin of the alae nasi; heavy, arched eyebrows with long eyelashes; downslanting palpebral fissures; high-arched palate; talon cusps on incisors
Grimacing or 'pursing' smile with eyes closing almost completely during smiling
Microcephaly, post-natal growth retardation, severe intellectual disability, and excessive propensity to spontaneous keloid and hypertrophic scar formation
radiological_manifestations: Hand and Foot Radiographs: Broad, short, spatulate distal phalanges of the first digits (thumbs and great toes); pathognomonic abnormal triangular or trapezoidal proximal phalanx causing radial deviation (delta phalanx); partial or complete duplication of the distal phalanx of the thumb
Cranial Radiographs and Brain MRI: Delayed closure of fontanelles, persistent parietal foramina, corpus callosum hypoplasia/agenesis, and Chiari I malformation
Pelvic and Spine Radiographs: Vertebral segmentation abnormalities, spina bifida occulta, and kyphoscoliosis
pathology_manifestations: Keloid and Skin Histopathology: Abundant haphazard bundles of thick, hyalinized, hypocellular collagen fibers (keloidal collagen) within the reticular dermis with absence of normal adnexal structures

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous mutations or microdeletions at 16p13.3 disrupting CREBBP (CREB-binding protein, ~60%) or at 22q13.2 disrupting EP300 (~10%), resulting in deficient histone acetyltransferase activity
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Immediate bedside visual recognition from broad deviated thumbs/toes, low-hanging columella, characteristic grimacing smile, delta phalanges on plain film, and CREBBP histone acetylation defect.

Pediatrics.name: Saethre-Chotzen Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Asymmetric craniosynostosis and cranial vault deformity: Coronal suture synostosis (frequently unicoronal, causing prominent anterior plagiocephaly with marked facial asymmetry, or bicoronal causing brachycephaly/turricephaly); low anterior hairline with prominent frontal bossing

Characteristic facial gestalt and ocular signs: Unilateral or bilateral eyelid ptosis (a major diagnostic hallmark differentiating it from other syndromic craniosynostoses); hypertelorism; tear-duct stenosis; prominent, sharp nasal bridge with beaked nasal tip; facial asymmetry

Pathognomonic ear anomalies: Small, low-set ears with a prominent horizontal crus of the helix extending across the concha (divided or prominent crus cymbae), folded upper helix, and narrow external auditory canals

Extremity and digital anomalies: Partial cutaneous soft-tissue syndactyly, classically involving the second and third fingers (syndactyly II-III) and third and fourth toes; broad, bifid, or duplicated hallux; clinodactyly of the fifth finger
radiological_manifestations: 3D Reconstructed Craniofacial CT: Demonstrates premature synostosis of the coronal suture (unilateral in anterior plagiocephaly or bilateral in brachycephaly); ipsilateral elevation of the superior orbital margin and sphenoid ridge ('harlequin eye' deformity on plain AP radiograph and CT scout view); contralateral compensatory frontal bossing; deviation of the nasal septum and chin point

Skeletal Radiographs of Hands and Feet: Soft-tissue syndactyly between digits 2 and 3; duplicated or bifid distal phalanx of the hallux; carpal/tarsal bone coalitions or radioulnar synostosis in severe variants

Cranial MRI: Parietal foramina (large symmetric calvarial defects in the parietal bones along the sagittal suture in cases with contiguous 7p21.1 microdeletions); low risk of Chiari I or hydrocephalus compared to FGFR-related craniosynostoses
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology of Sutures: Eburnation and premature bony bridging across coronal suture margins with fibrous disorganization of the pericranium and dura mater

Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant loss-of-function heterozygous mutations, intragenic deletions, or whole-gene microdeletions of TWIST1 on chromosome 7p21.1 (a basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor that acts as a negative regulator of osteogenic differentiation during calvarial development); haploinsufficiency of TWIST1 results in unrestrained RUNX2 and FGFR signaling, driving premature suture ossification
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: The leading basic helix-loop-helix craniosynostosis syndrome, recognized by bedside low hairline, eyelid ptosis, and ear crus crus cymbae alongside pathognomonic 3D CT unicoronal synostosis with 'harlequin eye' orbitopathy and TWIST1 haploinsufficiency.

Pediatrics.name: Sotos Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cardinal facial gestalt: Striking macrocephaly with dolichocephalic skull shape, prominent high forehead with frontotemporal bossing, receding frontotemporal hairline (parietotemporal alopecia/hair sparsity), downslanting palpebral fissures, hypertelorism, long narrow triangular face, and a prominent, pointed, square chin; prominent facial flushing across the cheeks

Pre- and postnatal somatic overgrowth: Height and head circumference typically >=2 standard deviations above the mean (>97th percentile) throughout infancy and childhood; disproportionately large hands and feet with broad digits, pes planus, and accelerated linear velocity that stabilizes toward normal adult height in late adolescence

Neurological and behavioral manifestations: Marked neonatal hypotonia with feeding difficulties, gross and fine motor coordination delay, severe expressive language delay, mild-to-severe intellectual disability, and characteristic behavioral features (autism spectrum traits, impulsivity, temper tantrums, and attention deficit)

Systemic associations: Neonatal jaundice, hypoglycemia, maternal/fetal polyhydramnios, congenital cardiac anomalies (ASD, VSD, patent ductus arteriosus), vesicoureteral reflux, and small increased risk of pediatric embryonal tumors (sacrococcygeal teratoma, neuroblastoma, Wilms tumor)
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Survey / Left Hand-Wrist Radiography: Marked advancement of bone age (carpal and epiphyseal ossification advanced by >=2 to 4 years ahead of chronological age) observed in 75–85% of affected pediatric patients; elongation of metacarpals and phalanges

Brain MRI: Prominent non-progressive cerebral ventriculomegaly (prominence of the lateral ventricles, especially trigones and occipital horns); persistence of cavum septum pellucidum and cavum vergae; hypoplasia of the corpus callosum; hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis and prominent cisterna magna; enlarged perivascular spaces and macrocrania

Abdominal Ultrasonography: Demonstrates renal structural anomalies (vesicoureteral reflux, hydronephrosis, duplex collecting systems, or unilateral renal agenesis) and screens for occult abdominal embryonal neoplasms
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Genetics & Epigenetics: Heterozygous de novo loss-of-function mutation or 5q35 microdeletion spanning the NSD1 gene (Nuclear Receptor Binding SET Domain Protein 1), encoding a histone methyltransferase specific for histone H3 lysine 36 (H3K36me2); 5q35 microdeletions account for ~50% of Japanese cases and ~10-15% of European/American cases, whereas NSD1 intragenic truncating/missense mutations account for 75-80% of Western cohorts; pathognomonic peripheral blood genome-wide DNA hypomethylation episignature differentiates Sotos syndrome from other overgrowth conditions
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Premier pediatric overgrowth syndrome demonstrating pathognomonic photographic facial morphology (high prominent bossed forehead, inverted pear/triangular chin) corroborated by radiological advanced skeletal bone age and ventriculomegaly, governed by NSD1 epigenetic histone dysregulation.

Pediatrics.name: Thanatophoric Dysplasia
clinical_manifestations: Most common lethal neonatal skeletal dysplasia ('thanatophoric' = death-bearing); infants present at birth with severe, extreme micromelia (profound rhizomelic, mesomelic, and acromelic shortening of all four limbs)
Severe bell-shaped, narrow, constricted thorax with short ribs, leading to immediate respiratory failure at birth

Distinctive craniofacial features: prominent macrocephaly, heavy frontal bossing, depressed nasal bridge, marked hypertelorism, low-set ears; in Type 2 TD, severe cloverleaf skull deformity (kleeblattschädel)
Redundant skin folds ('doughy rolls') along all four shortened extremities; hypotonia and absent Moro reflex
radiological_manifestations: Infant Babygram (Whole-Body Skeletal Radiographs): Type 1 TD demonstrates extremely short, curved, bowed long bones with pathognomonic curved 'telephone-receiver' femora, flared irregular metaphyses, and prominent medial bone spurs; Type 2 TD demonstrates straight femora with pathognomonic cloverleaf skull (kleeblattschädel); axial skeleton reveals severe generalized platyspondyly with flattened 'H-shaped' or 'wafer-thin' vertebral bodies and wide intervertebral disc spaces; narrow thoracic cage with extremely short horizontal ribs
Brain CT/MRI: Severe foramen magnum stenosis, temporal lobe dysplasia with deep transverse fissuring and polymicrogyria, and obstructive hydrocephalus
pathology_manifestations: Growth Plate Chondro-osseous Histopathology: Disastrous disruption of endochondral ossification; growth plates display completely disorganized, short, hypocellular chondrocyte columns with loss of the normal proliferative and hypertrophic zones; abundant vascular mesenchyme and fibrous tissue encroaching into the physeal-metaphyseal junction

Molecular Genetics: Constitutively active gain-of-function missense mutations in FGFR3 (fibroblast growth factor receptor 3) on chromosome 4p16.3; Type 1 is caused by mutations such as p.Arg248Cys or p.Tyr373Cys, whereas Type 2 is universally caused by the specific p.Lys650Glu substitution
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Unforgettable neonatal presentation featuring extreme micromelia, telephone-receiver femora, wafer-thin platyspondyly, and cloverleaf skull driven by FGFR3 gain-of-function.

Pediatrics.name: Treacher Collins Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Striking downward-slanting (antimongoloid) palpebral fissures
Coloboma of the outer third of the lower eyelid (notching) with partial-to-complete absence of eyelashes medial to the coloboma
Severe hypoplasia of the zygomatic arches and malar bones resulting in hollow, sunken cheekbones
Micrognathia and retrognathia with steep mandibular angle and Class II malocclusion
External ear anomalies: microtia, anotia, or severely crumpled pinnae, meatal atresia, and preauricular hair displacement anterior to the ear
Bilateral conductive hearing loss due to middle ear ossicular chain dysgenesis; intact intellect
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Maxillofacial CT: Bilateral symmetrical hypoplasia or complete bony absence (cleft) of the zygomatic arches and malar complexes; hypoplasia of the mandibular ramus, condyle, and coronoid process; acute gonial angle; severely constricted pharyngeal airway

Temporal Bone High-Resolution CT: Complete bony atresia or stenosis of external auditory canals; malformed, hypoplastic, or ankylosed ossicular chains (malleus-incus fusion); hypoplastic middle ear cavities and mastoid pneumatization; normal inner ear (cochlea and vestibule typically preserved)
pathology_manifestations: Pathogenesis & Histopathology: Defective biogenesis of ribosomal RNA causing p53-dependent nucleolar stress and extensive apoptosis of migratory neural crest cells of the first and second pharyngeal arches; hypoplastic branchial bone architecture
Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant heterozygous mutations in TCOF1 (encoding Treacle, >90% of cases), POLR1D, or autosomal recessive mutations in POLR1C
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Classic bedside facial phenotype (antimongoloid slant, lower lid colobomas, sunken malar cheeks, microtia) with pathognomonic CT absence of zygomatic arches and middle ear atresia.

Pediatrics.name: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder
clinical_manifestations: Short palpebral fissures, smooth philtrum, and a thin upper lip
Growth restriction and microcephaly
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: corpus callosum hypoplasia or migration anomalies in the severe end
pathology_manifestations: No diagnostic biopsy; the lip-philtrum guide photograph is the clinical standard
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Teratogenic syndrome with a standardized facial photograph.

Pediatrics.name: 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Hooded eyelids, a bulbous nose tip, small ears, and a small mouth
Overt or submucous cleft palate and nasal regurgitation
Neonatal hypocalcemic tetany is not the image
radiological_manifestations: Echocardiography: conotruncal anomalies, especially tetralogy or interrupted aortic arch
Absent thymic shadow on the newborn chest radiograph when the T-cell defect is severe
pathology_manifestations: Thymic hypoplasia if tissue is examined; chromosomal microarray is the confirming test
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Microdeletion with a facial photograph, a palate photograph, and a conotruncal imaging set.

Pediatrics.name: Stickler Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Flat midface, Pierre Robin sequence, and a small jaw
High myopia and vitreous changes; retinal detachment is a complication, not a separate topic
radiological_manifestations: Spine and joint radiographs: mild epiphyseal dysplasia and platyspondyly
pathology_manifestations: Vitreous photography and COL2A1-spectrum testing; cleft-palate histology is not specific
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Collagenopathy with a midface photograph, vitreous findings, and mild skeletal films.

Pediatrics.name: Proteus Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Progressive, asymmetric, distorting overgrowth of a limb or digit after birth
Cerebriform connective-tissue nevus of the sole
Epidermal nevi and lipomas in the same mosaic distribution
radiological_manifestations: Radiographs of the affected limb: irregular bony overgrowth; MRI of soft-tissue asymmetry
pathology_manifestations: AKT1 activating mosaic variant; the sole nevus shows collagenous overgrowth
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Mosaic overgrowth with a progressive limb photograph and a cerebriform sole.

Pediatrics.name: Edwards Syndrome (Trisomy 18)
clinical_manifestations: Severe intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), microcephaly with a prominent, elongated occiput, and narrow bifrontal diameter
Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism: micrognathia, low-set, malformed 'faun-like' ears with pointed tops, short palpebral fissures, and high-arched palate
Pathognomonic clenched fists with overlapping digits: index finger overlapping the third finger, and fifth finger overlapping the fourth finger
Rocker-bottom feet (prominent calcaneus and convex rounded soles), hypoplastic or absent halluces, and hypoplastic fingernails
Severe congenital heart disease (VSD, PDA, ASD, polyvalvular dysplasia) and early infant lethality
radiological_manifestations: Prenatal Obstetric Ultrasound: Choroid plexus cysts, 'strawberry-shaped' cranium, clenched hands, persistent single umbilical artery, polyhydramnios, and severe growth restriction

Postnatal Skeletal Radiography: Hypoplastic thin ribs, short sternum with premature closure of sternal ossification centers, small pelvis with anteriorly rotated ilia, and rocker-bottom foot alignment (dorsiflexed talus with plantarflexed calcaneus)
Echocardiography: Ventricular septal defect (90%), patent ductus arteriosus, and coarctation of aorta
pathology_manifestations: Cytogenetics / Karyotype: Free trisomy 18 (47,XX,+18 or 47,XY,+18) in >95% of cases; mosaicism in remainder
Autopsy Pathology: Meckel diverticulum, horseshoe kidney, diaphragmatic hernia, malrotation, and polyvalvular cardiac dysplasia with nodular thickening of all four valves
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic chromosomal aneuploidy syndrome featuring the classic clenched hands with overlapping digits, rocker-bottom feet, and prominent occiput.

Pediatrics.name: Patau Syndrome (Trisomy 13)
clinical_manifestations: Prototypic triad: Holoprosencephaly with severe midline facial defects, microphthalmia/anophthalmia, and postaxial polydactyly of hands and feet
Midline craniofacial defects: Bilateral cleft lip and palate, cyclopia or ethmocephaly, hypotelorism, and low-set malformed ears
Cutis aplasia: Punched-out circular skin and scalp defects over the parieto-occipital vertex displaying glistening underlying dura or thin transparent membrane
Omphalocele, cryptorchidism, ambiguous genitalia, and profound neurodevelopmental arrest with high neonatal mortality
radiological_manifestations: Prenatal Ultrasound / Neuroimaging: Holoprosencephaly (alobar or semilobar failure of forebrain cleavage into hemispheres, monoventricle, fused thalami), facial clefts, and polycystic kidneys
Skeletal Radiography: Postaxial polydactyly with fully formed or pedunculated supernumerary digits, sloping forehead, and hypoplastic pelvic bones
Echocardiography: Complex cardiac malformations including hypoplastic left heart syndrome, double outlet right ventricle, and tetralogy of Fallot
pathology_manifestations: Cytogenetics / Karyotype: Full trisomy 13 (47,XX,+13 or 47,XY,+13) in 80%; Robertsonian translocation t(13;14) in 20%

Autopsy / Histopathology: Persistence of embryonic hemoglobin (Hb Gower), nuclear projections in circulating neutrophils (sessile nuclear tags), cystic renal dysplasia, and incomplete lobation of lungs and liver
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic chromosomal disorder presenting with the pathognomonic triad of holoprosencephaly, midline clefting, postaxial polydactyly, and scalp cutis aplasia.

Pediatrics.name: Wolf-Hirschhorn Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic 'Greek warrior helmet' facies: Broad, flat bridge of the nose continuing directly into a prominent glabella, high forehead, hypertelorism, and arched eyebrows
Microcephaly, micrognathia, downturned corners of the mouth ('carp mouth'), short philtrum, and prominent low-set ears with preauricular tags/pits
Iris coloboma, strabismus, and cleft lip/palate
Severe prenatal and postnatal growth retardation, intractable early-onset seizures (atypical absence and myoclonic seizures), profound intellectual disability, and hypotonia
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Diffuse microcephaly with corpus callosum hypogenesis or agenesis, delayed myelination, simplified gyral pattern, and cerebellar hypoplasia
Skeletal Radiography: Delayed bone age, kyphoscoliosis, asymmetric pelvic development, clubfoot, and supernumerary ribs
pathology_manifestations: Chromosomal Microarray / FISH: Terminal deletion of chromosome 4p16.3 (involving LETM1 and WHSC1/NSD2 genes); identified on standard high-resolution karyotyping or array CGH
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield deletion syndrome instantly identifiable by the striking pathognomonic 'Greek warrior helmet' facial profile.

Pediatrics.name: Cri-du-Chat Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic high-pitched, monochromatic, kitten-like crying (cri du chat) in infancy caused by structural laryngeal hypoplasia and abnormal vocal cord anatomy
Characteristic infant facies: Moon-shaped round face, hypertelorism, epicanthal folds, downward-slanting (antimongoloid) palpebral fissures, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Microcephaly, low-set ears, single transverse palmar creases (simian crease), severe hypotonia, and profound cognitive impairment
radiological_manifestations: Laryngoscopy: Small, narrow, diamond-shaped larynx with small, flaccid vocal cords and asymmetric epiglottis accounting for acoustic characteristics of the cat-like cry
Brain MRI: Brainstem hypoplasia with disproportionately small pontine and cerebellar vermian volume, enlarged lateral ventricles, and microcephaly
pathology_manifestations: Cytogenetics / FISH: Deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5 (terminal or interstitial deletion spanning 5p15.2-p15.3, the cri-du-chat critical region)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic cytogenetic deletion syndrome characterized by the unmistakable high-pitched cat-like cry and distinctive round moon-like facies with epicanthal folds.

Pediatrics.name: Angelman Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic behavioral phenotype: Inappropriately happy demeanor with frequent paroxysms of unprovoked laughter, smiling, and excitability, accompanied by hand-flapping movements
Severe motor delay and ataxia with jerky, puppet-like, stiff-legged uncoordinated gait
Severe speech impairment (complete absence of expressive speech or fewer than six words)

Dysmorphic craniofacial features: Microbrachycephaly, prominent pointed chin (prognathia), wide mouth (macrostomia) with widely spaced teeth, tongue protrusion, and fair skin with light eyes (hypopigmentation)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Generally structurally normal or mild non-specific white matter volume reduction and mild delayed myelination, ruling out destructive structural malformations

Electroencephalography (EEG - Diagnostic Hallmark): Striking, highly characteristic patterns including runs of high-amplitude rhythmic slow waves (2–3 Hz) with frontally dominant sharp waves, often appearing before clinical symptoms manifest
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Genetics: Loss of maternal UBE3A expression at chromosome 15q11.2-q13 due to: (1) maternal deletion (70%), (2) paternal uniparental disomy 15 (2–5%), (3) imprinting defect (2–4%), or (4) maternal UBE3A point mutation (10%); confirmed via methylation-specific PCR (MS-PCR)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic genomic imprinting disorder characterized by the 'happy puppet' behavioral phenotype with joyful affect, ataxic hand-flapping gait, and prominent chin.

Pediatrics.name: Meckel-Gruber Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Lethal autosomal recessive ciliopathy defined by the classic triad: (1) Occipital encephalocele, (2) Large bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys, and (3) Postaxial polydactyly
Profound oligohydramnios resulting in severe Potter sequence: Pulmonary hypoplasia, compressed squashed facies, and talipes equinovarus deformities
Microcephaly, microphthalmia, cleft palate, and genital ambiguities
Uniformly fatal in the perinatal period or early neonatal hours
radiological_manifestations: Prenatal Ultrasonography / Fetal MRI: Large herniated occipital encephalocele containing brain parenchyma and meninges through an occipital skull defect; massive bilateral enlarged echogenic multicystic kidneys causing severe abdominal distension; postaxial polydactyly on hands and feet; severe anhydramnios
pathology_manifestations: Autopsy Pathology: Bilateral symmetrically enlarged kidneys replaced by sponge-like macroscopic cysts; pathognomonic hepatic ductal plate malformation characterized by profuse proliferation and dilation of intrahepatic bile ducts with portal fibrosis; complete pulmonary hypoplasia
Molecular Genetics: Biallelic pathogenic variants in cilia genes (MKS1, TMEM216, TMEM67/MKS3, RPGRIP1L, CC2D2A)
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield lethal ciliopathy defined by the classic triad of occipital encephalocele, bilateral multicystic kidneys, and postaxial polydactyly on prenatal imaging and gross exam.

Pediatrics.name: Smith-Lemli-Opitz Syndrome
Pediatrics.subspecialty: Inborn Errors of Metabolism and Dysmorphology
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism: Microcephaly, ptosis, epicanthal folds, broad anteverted nostrils, and micrognathia
Pathognomonic skeletal anomaly: 2-3 toe syndactyly (Y-shaped cutaneous fusion of the second and third toes), postaxial polydactyly, and single palmar crease
Genital anomalies in 46,XY males ranging from hypospadias and cryptorchidism to complete sex reversal (female external genitalia)
Severe feeding intolerance, failure to thrive, photosensitivity, autistic behavioral stereotypies, and intellectual disability
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Hypoplasia or agenesis of the corpus callosum, frontotemporal atrophy, and ventriculomegaly
Echocardiography: Atrioventricular canal defects, anomalous pulmonary venous return, and coarctation of aorta
Skeletal Radiographs: 2nd and 3rd toe syndactyly with postaxial hexadactyly and osteopenia
pathology_manifestations: Biochemical Diagnostics: Elevated serum 7-dehydrocholesterol (7-DHC) and markedly decreased total cholesterol levels (pathognomonic hallmark reflecting defective conversion to cholesterol)
Molecular Genetics: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the DHCR7 (7-dehydrocholesterol reductase) gene
Pathology: Bilateral adrenal cortical hypoplasia, Hirschsprung disease, and renal cystic dysplasia on autopsy
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic inborn error of cholesterol synthesis featuring the pathognomonic Y-shaped 2-3 syndactyly of toes, ambiguous genitalia, and elevated 7-dehydrocholesterol.

Pediatrics.name: Kabuki Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic facial features resembling the makeup worn by actors in traditional Japanese Kabuki theatre: Elongated palpebral fissures with eversion of the lateral third of the lower eyelid, arched high eyebrows with lateral sparseness, broad depressed nasal tip, and prominent large earlobes
Persistent prominent fetal fingertip pads (fleshy pads on digital pulps persisting throughout life)
Skeletal anomalies including brachydactyly V, clinodactyly, scoliosis, and sagittal clefting of vertebrae
Congenital heart disease (coarctation of aorta, VSD, ASD), hypermobility of joints, frequent otitis media with hearing impairment, and mild-to-moderate intellectual disability
radiological_manifestations: Spinal Radiographs: Sagittal cleft vertebrae (butterfly vertebrae), scoliosis, rib anomalies, and hip dysplasia
Hand Radiographs: Short fourth and fifth metacarpals, brachydactyly, and pseudoepiphyses
Brain MRI: Non-specific enlargement of ventricles, Chiari I malformation, and microcephaly
pathology_manifestations: Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic variants in KMT2D (MLL2) in type 1 (~75%) or KDM6A in type 2 (~5%), encoding histone methyltransferases involved in chromatin remodeling
Pediatrics.inclusion_rationale: Instantly recognizable dysmorphic syndrome named after traditional Japanese theatre makeup with everted lateral lower eyelids and persistent fetal fingertip pads.

Pulmonology.name: Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis
clinical_manifestations: Expectoration of pathognomonic firm, rubbery, branching, golden-brown, dark brown, or black mucus plugs and bronchial casts ('mucus plug expectoration')
Severe, refractory, poorly controlled wheezing and asthmatic paroxysms accompanied by low-grade fever, malaise, and pleuritic chest pain
Recurrent episodes of hemoptysis (from blood-streaked sputum to moderate hemoptysis secondary to bronchiectatic vessel erosion)
Prominent digital clubbing in patients with advanced, chronic, stage V fibrotic ABPA
Visible immediate cutaneous wheal-and-flare reactivity and late erythematous induration on Aspergillus fumigatus skin prick testing
Gross bronchoscopic visual findings of dilated central bronchi occluded by viscous, dark brown, tenacious mucus plugs forming complete bronchial casts
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT (Imaging Hallmarks): Central, proximal, varicose and cystic bronchiectasis predominantly involving the upper and middle lung lobes with characteristically normal, tapering peripheral bronchi; pathognomonic 'high-attenuation mucus' (HAM sign: mucoid impaction that is hyperdense relative to paraspinal skeletal muscle, caused by precipitated calcium salts and manganese/iron chelates concentrated by fungal elements); extensive branching tubular, Y-shaped, or V-shaped opacities radiating from the hilum ('finger-in-glove sign' or 'gloved-finger sign'); signet-ring sign and bronchial wall thickening; centrilobular tree-in-bud opacities and mosaic attenuation on expiratory scans
Chest Radiography: Transient or migratory pulmonary consolidations, fleeting infiltrates, toothpaste sign, gloved-finger opacities radiating from the hilum, and upper lobe volume loss
pathology_manifestations: Bronchial mucus plug / lung biopsy: Bronchocentric granulomatosis and allergic mucin comprising laminated, degenerating, compact eosinophils, necrotic debris, and abundant hexagonal bipyramidal Charcot-Leyden crystals; silver stains (GMS / Grocott methenamine silver) reveal non-invasive, dichotomously 45-degree branching, septate hyphae of Aspergillus within the mucus plugs; complete absence of fungal invasion into the bronchial wall or adjacent pulmonary parenchyma (strictly differentiating ABPA from invasive or semi-invasive aspergillosis)
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Features the iconic physical sign of expectorated golden-brown bronchial mucus casts paired with the pathognomonic high-attenuation mucus (HAM) and central 'finger-in-glove' bronchiectasis on chest HRCT, confirmed by Charcot-Leyden crystals and non-invasive hyphae.

Pulmonology.name: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency
clinical_manifestations: Premature, severe barrel chest deformity with marked increase in anteroposterior thoracic diameter and widening of the intercostal spaces in non-smokers or young adults (30–40s)

Severe, painful, necrotizing panniculitis (pathognomonic cutaneous manifestation): recurrent, indurated, tender, violaceous-to-erythematous subcutaneous nodules and plaques localized to the lower abdomen, buttocks, and thighs, which ulcerate discharging sterile, oily, serosanguinous fluid and heal with atrophic scarring
Prominent digital clubbing of fingers and toes in patients with advanced panacinar emphysema and secondary bronchiectasis
Signs of liver cirrhosis and portal hypertension: scleral icterus, palmar erythema, spider telangiectasias, abdominal caput medusae, and firm splenomegaly
Severe central cyanosis, pursed-lip breathing, tripod sitting posture, and Hoover's sign (paradoxical inward movement of the lower lateral ribcage during inspiration)
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT (Pathognomonic Panacinar Emphysema): Severe, diffuse, bilateral panacinar (panlobular) emphysema characterized by uniform, extensive destruction of entire secondary pulmonary lobules with marked predilection for the lower lobes and lung bases; severe attenuation of pulmonary vessels ('vascular pruning') and diffuse basal hyperlucency contrasting with relatively spared lung apices; secondary cylindrical and varicose bronchiectasis; large basilar bullae and flattened diaphragms

Chest Radiography: Hyperinflated, hyperexpanded lungs (>10 posterior ribs visible), marked flattening and depression of the diaphragmatic domes, increased retrosternal clear space (>2.5 cm on lateral film), and marked attenuation/scarcity of peripheral basal vascular markings
Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Nodular, shrunken, cirrhotic liver contour, splenomegaly, recanalized umbilical vein, and ascites
pathology_manifestations: Liver biopsy (Pathognomonic hallmark): Hepatocytes contain numerous round-to-oval, eosinophilic, intracytoplasmic inclusions and globules concentrated predominantly in the periportal zone (Zone 1); inclusions stain brilliantly positive with Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS) and are completely resistant to diastase digestion (PAS-D positive), representing insoluble polymers of mutant Z protein (PiZZ) trapped inside the endoplasmic reticulum

Lung explant / surgical specimen: Panacinar emphysema characterized by uniform, non-selective simplification and destruction of all alveolar structures originating from the respiratory bronchioles through to the alveolar sacs, leaving large coalescent airspaces devoid of normal elastica; diffuse loss of alveolar capillary networks without prominent peribronchiolar anthracotic pigment (differentiating from smoking-induced centrilobular emphysema)
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Combines hallmark clinical necrotizing panniculitis (oily-draining nodules) and premature barrel chest with pathognomonic basal-predominant panacinar emphysema on chest HRCT and PAS-D positive hepatic globules.

Pulmonology.name: Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia
clinical_manifestations: Subacute flu-like illness persisting for weeks to months with low-grade fever, malaise, persistent dry hacking cough, and progressive exertional dyspnea unresponsive to empiric antibiotic regimens
Localized or diffuse inspiratory fine, crackling rales (crackles) on lung auscultation, particularly over the lung bases and areas of consolidation
Absence of digital clubbing (a critical bedside negative finding that strongly helps distinguish COP from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, where clubbing is prevalent)
Resting tachypnea, mild central cyanosis, and mild weight loss in progressive disease
Dramatic, near-miraculous clinical resolution within 48–72 hours following the initiation of systemic corticosteroid therapy ('steroid responsiveness')
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT (Pathognomonic Reverse Halo / Atoll Sign): Central area of ground-glass opacity encircled by a complete or crescentic ring-like rim of dense consolidation (≥2 mm in thickness); bilateral, patchy, non-segmental subpleural and peribronchovascular consolidations with prominent patent air bronchograms; lower lung zone predominance; characteristic migratory pattern (lesions spontaneously regress in one area while newly erupting in another across serial CT scans)
Chest Radiography: Bilateral, patchy, multi-focal alveolar consolidations ('pneumonia-like' opacities) with peripheral, subpleural distribution and preserved lung volumes
Chest HRCT (Secondary signs): Nodular pattern (peribronchovascular micronodules), band-like parenchymal opacities parallel to the pleural surface, and mild bronchocentric ground-glass attenuation
pathology_manifestations: Transbronchial / video-assisted thoracoscopic (VATS) lung biopsy: Diagnostic intra-alveolar and intraluminal polypoid plugs of loose, immature, myxoid connective tissue composed of proliferating fibroblasts and myofibroblasts embedded in a pale, basophilic, glycosaminoglycan-rich extracellular matrix ('Masson bodies'); Masson bodies extend in a serpentine branching pattern through alveolar ducts, alveolar spaces, and respiratory bronchioles; patchy distribution with temporal uniformity (all lesions appear to be at the same stage of evolution); background preservation of the underlying alveolar architecture and elastic lamina (unlike UIP), with mild chronic interstitial inflammation
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Distinguished by the pathognomonic 'reverse halo sign' (atoll sign) and migratory consolidations with air bronchograms on chest HRCT, correlated with the absence of clubbing at the bedside and diagnostic fibroblastic Masson bodies on lung biopsy.

Pulmonology.name: Cystic Fibrosis
clinical_manifestations: Severe digital clubbing of all fingers and toes
Barrel chest deformity with increased anteroposterior thoracic diameter
Nasal polyposis and chronic purulent rhinosinusitis with bridge widening
Failure to thrive, thin cachectic habitus, protuberant abdomen
Salty sweat taste (salt frost on forehead)
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT: Severe, diffuse cylindrical, varicose, and cystic bronchiectasis with upper lobe predominance; 'signet-ring' sign (bronchial diameter > adjacent pulmonary artery), extensive mucoid impaction ('finger-in-glove' opacities), bronchial wall thickening, mosaic perfusion and air trapping on expiration
Paranasal Sinus CT: Pansinusitis with complete sinus opacification, extensive mucosal polyposis, hypoplasia or absence of frontal and sphenoid sinuses
Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Pancreatic atrophy with fatty replacement (fibrocystic changes), biliary cirrhosis, microgallbladder
pathology_manifestations: Lung tissue/bronchial biopsy: Severe chronic peribronchial inflammation, goblet cell hyperplasia, squamous metaplasia of respiratory epithelium, plugging of airway lumens with inspissated hyperviscous mucus loaded with degenerated neutrophils and Pseudomonas biofilm
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield multisystem genetic disease with profound digital clubbing, barrel chest, and nasal polyps matched with pathognomonic cystic bronchiectasis and 'finger-in-glove' mucus plugging on chest HRCT.

Pulmonology.name: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis
clinical_manifestations: Acute episodes: abrupt onset of fever, chills, non-productive cough, chest tightness, and tachypnea developing 4–8 hours following antigen inhalation
Bilateral diffuse inspiratory fine crackles ('squeaks') heard during chest auscultation, often accompanied by high-pitched mid-inspiratory squawks indicative of bronchiolar involvement
Prominent digital clubbing in chronic, fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (loss of Lovibond angle, bulbous enlargement of distal nail beds)
Central cyanosis, resting tachypnea, and accessory respiratory muscle use in progressive advanced fibrotic disease
Marked weight loss, asthenic habitus, and respiratory cachexia in chronic exposure settings
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT (Non-fibrotic HP): Pathognomonic 'headcheese sign' (three-density sign: coexistence of ground-glass opacity, normal lung parenchyma, and sharply demarcated mosaic low-attenuation air-trapping on inspiratory scans accentuated on end-expiratory imaging); ill-defined centrilobular ground-glass micronodules (<5 mm) distributed diffusely across mid-to-upper lung zones

Chest HRCT (Fibrotic HP): Mid-lung and upper-to-mid lung predominant reticulation, traction bronchiectasis and bronchiolectasis, honeycombing with characteristic relative basilar sparing (unlike IPF), accompanied by mosaic perfusion and lobular air trapping on expiratory HRCT
Chest Radiography: Diffuse, hazy ground-glass opacification or fine reticulonodular opacities with upper-to-middle lobe predominance, sparing the extreme costophrenic angles
pathology_manifestations: Transbronchial / surgical lung biopsy: Classical histologic triad consisting of (1) cellular interstitial pneumonia with prominent lymphocytic alveolitis (predominantly CD8+ T cells), (2) marked cellular bronchiolitis with peribronchiolar lymphocytic cuffing, and (3) loose, poorly formed, non-caseating (non-necrotizing) epithelioid cell granulomas or multinucleated giant cells containing cholesterol clefts or Schaumann bodies localized in the peribronchiolar interstitium
Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL): Striking marked lymphocytic alveolitis (>40-50% lymphocytes), with an inverted CD4+/CD8+ T-cell ratio (<1.0) characteristic of active exposure
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Combines hallmark bedside signs (inspiratory squeaks/squawks, digital clubbing, and cyanosis) with the pathognomonic 'headcheese sign' (three-density pattern) and centrilobular ground-glass nodules on chest HRCT, confirmed by peribronchiolar granulomatous histology.

Pulmonology.name: Idiopathic Pleuroparenchymal Fibroelastosis
clinical_manifestations: Platythorax (pathognomonic visual thoracic deformity): severe 'flat chest cage' characterized by a markedly reduced anteroposterior thoracic diameter and widening of the transverse diameter, resulting in an exceptionally low AP-to-transverse thoracic ratio
Prominent deep inspiratory suprasternal notch, supraclavicular, and intercostal muscular retractions visible during quiet and deep breathing
Severe thoracic cachexia and slender, asthenic habitus with marked involuntary weight loss and loss of subcutaneous fat over the upper chest
Persistent, dry, hacking cough and progressive exertional dyspnea
Spontaneous recurrent pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum resulting from rupture of subpleural apical blebs or stiff fibroelastotic lung tissue
Notable absence of digital clubbing (distinguishing PPFE from typical IPF)
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT (Pathognomonic Criteria): Dense, bilateral, subpleural consolidations and pleural thickening concentrated strictly in the apical and upper lung zones; marked traction bronchiectasis and bronchiolectasis within areas of fibroelastosis; severe upper-lobe volume loss resulting in dramatic upward retraction of both pulmonary hila ('tenting' or upward displacement of hilar structures); abrupt transition between dense subpleural fibroelastotic consolidation and normal underlying lung parenchyma; secondary pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, and apical bullae; coexisting co-occurring lower-lobe UIP or NSIP pattern in a subset of advanced patients

Chest Radiography: Bilateral dense apical pleural thickening resembling apical caps, progressive upper zone volume reduction, elevated hilar vessels, and a visibly narrowed anteroposterior thoracic cage on lateral radiographs
pathology_manifestations: Surgical lung biopsy / explanted lung (Pathognomonic Histology): Profound intra-alveolar collagenous fibrosis with alveolar obliteration, accompanied by prominent, dense accumulation of elastic fibers (elastosis) filling the alveolar spaces; highlighted by elastic stains such as Verhoeff-Van Gieson (VVG) or elastica van Gieson (EVG) showing dense bundles of black/dark purple elastic fibers; prominent visceral pleural fibrosis; characteristic abrupt, sharp demarcation between the subpleural fibroelastotic zone and the adjacent histologically normal or minimally affected lung parenchyma; absence of active fibroblastic foci or granulomas
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Exceptional interstitial disorder presenting with the pathognomonic visual signs of platythorax ('flat chest') and deep suprasternal retractions, alongside textbook apical subpleural fibroelastosis, traction bronchiectasis, and upward hilar retraction on chest HRCT.

Pulmonology.name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
clinical_manifestations: Digital clubbing (Hippocratic fingers: bulbous enlargement of distal digits with loss of Lovibond angle)
Bilateral dry, fine, end-inspiratory Velcro crackles on lung auscultation
Cyanosis of lips and nail beds on exertion
Progressive tachypnea and respiratory accessory muscle use
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT (Definite UIP pattern): Subpleural, basal-predominant reticulation, clustered layered honeycombing (cystic spaces 3-10 mm with shared walls), traction bronchiectasis and bronchiolectasis, absolute absence of features inconsistent with UIP (such as prominent ground-glass, mosaic attenuation, or cysts away from honeycombing)
Chest Radiography: Reduced lung volumes, bilateral peripheral basal reticular opacities
pathology_manifestations: Surgical lung biopsy: Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP) pattern characterized by spatial and temporal heterogeneity, patchy dense parenchymal fibrosis alternating with preserved normal lung architecture, active fibroblast foci (proliferating myxoid connective tissue), and honeycomb remodeling
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal fibrotic lung disease combining classic digital clubbing and cyanosis with the definitive subpleural basal honeycombing UIP pattern on chest HRCT.

Pulmonology.name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Hemosiderosis
synonyms: Lane-Hamilton syndrome (when associated with celiac disease)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic clinical triad: (1) recurrent episodes of hemoptysis (ranging from microscopic blood streaking to sudden life-threatening alveolar hemorrhage), (2) profound, refractory iron-deficiency anemia, and (3) transient, diffuse bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on chest imaging
Severe bedside signs of chronic iron deficiency: profound cutaneous and conjunctival pallor, severe fatigue, lethargy, angular cheilitis, atrophic glossitis, and spoon-shaped nails (koilonychia)
Acute respiratory crisis during active intra-alveolar hemorrhage: acute dyspnea, tachypnea, cyanosis, tachycardia, and diffuse bilateral fine inspiratory crackles (crepitations) on chest auscultation
Hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy seen in up to 25% of pediatric cases
Digital clubbing and failure to thrive / growth retardation in children with chronic, unremitting occult alveolar hemorrhage
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT (Acute Hemorrhagic Phase): Diffuse, bilateral, relatively symmetrical ground-glass opacities (GGO) and airspace consolidations with perihilar and bibasilar predilection, typically sparing the subpleural rind and apices; crazy-paving pattern (superimposed interlobular and intralobular septal thickening over ground-glass attenuation) resulting from alveolar and interstitial red blood cell extravasation

Chest HRCT (Chronic / Interictal Phase): Resolution of alveolar consolidations within 10–14 days, replaced by fine diffuse centrilobular micronodules (representing clustered hemosiderin-laden macrophages) and delicate reticular opacities; long-standing disease shows progressive basal interstitial fibrosis with traction bronchiectasis and honeycombing
Chest Radiography: Patchy or confluent bilateral flocculent alveolar opacities during acute bleeding that clear remarkably over several days, leaving a fine reticulonodular pattern

Carbon Monoxide Diffusing Capacity (DLCO): Striking acute elevation of DLCO (>100–130% of predicted) during active alveolar bleeding due to high affinity of intra-alveolar erythrocytes for carbon monoxide, followed by chronic reduction as fibrosis ensues
pathology_manifestations: Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL): Sequentially bloodier aliquots from the same bronchopulmonary segment; Prussian blue (Perls' acid ferrocyanide) staining demonstrates overwhelming presence of iron-laden alveolar macrophages (siderophages), with a Golde score >100 indicating diffuse alveolar hemorrhage

Lung Biopsy Histology: Alveolar spaces packed with siderophages, free erythrocytes, and fibrin; extensive interstitial hemosiderin deposition along alveolar septa, elastic fibers, and vascular walls, accompanied by type II pneumocyte hyperplasia and secondary interstitial fibrosis; absence of capillaritis, neutrophilic infiltration, or microvascular necrosis (distinguishing IPH from granulomatosis with polyangiitis and microscopic polyangiitis)

Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Completely negative for immune complex deposition, anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) linear IgG staining, or antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), definitively excluding Goodpasture syndrome and systemic vasculitides
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential alveolar hemorrhage disorder characterized by the classic triad of hemoptysis, severe iron-deficiency anemia, and diffuse infiltrates, confirmed by siderophage-rich BAL (Golde score >100), ground-glass crazy-paving on HRCT, and absence of immune complexes on DIF.

Pulmonology.name: Kartagener Syndrome (Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia with Situs Inversus)
synonyms: immotile cilia syndrome with situs inversus
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Siewert-Kartagener clinical triad: (1) Situs inversus totalis (complete mirror-image visceral transposition), (2) chronic sinusitis and bronchiectasis, and (3) male subfertility/infertility due to immotile spermatozoa (and increased ectopic pregnancy risk in females)

Bedside Cardiovascular Signs: Dextrocardia: Point of maximal impulse (apical cardiac impulse) palpated in the right fifth intercostal space along the right midclavicular line; heart sounds louder over the right hemithorax than the left
Neonatal History: Unexplained neonatal respiratory distress in term infants with mild hypoxemia and tachypnea, often requiring supplemental oxygen

Upper Airway Signs: Chronic refractory purulent rhinorrhea beginning in early infancy, severe chronic pansinusitis, nasal polyposis (pale, edematous glistening mucosal polyps obstructing the nasal cavity), and conductive hearing loss from recurrent serous otitis media
Lower Airway Signs: Chronic productive cough with copious purulent sputum, coarse crackles and expiratory wheezes, and pronounced digital clubbing (Hippocratic fingers) of the hands and feet
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (CXR - Mirror-Image Anatomy): Dextrocardia with the cardiac apex pointing toward the right; right aortic arch; liver shadow located in the left upper quadrant and gastric air bubble situated beneath the right hemidiaphragm (situs inversus totalis); bilateral lower-zone peribronchial cuffing, tram-track opacities, and cystic radiolucencies indicative of bronchiectasis

Chest HRCT: Extensive, bilateral cylindrical, varicose, and saccular bronchiectasis with severe bronchial wall thickening, predominantly affecting the middle and lower lobes (anatomically, the left middle-equivalent and lower lobes); diffuse centrilobular tree-in-bud nodular opacities representing bronchiolar impaction, accompanied by mucoid impaction ('finger-in-glove' sign) and mosaic attenuation on expiratory scans

CT Paranasal Sinuses: Complete pansinusitis with mucosal thickening and opacification of the maxillary, ethmoid, and sphenoid sinuses; characteristic aplasia or severe hypoplasia of the frontal and sphenoid sinuses

Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Complete mirror-image transposition of all abdominal viscera: spleen on the right, trilobed liver and gallbladder on the left, stomach and duodenal sweep on the right, and reversed mesenteric vessel orientation
pathology_manifestations: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM - Gold Standard on Endobronchial / Nasal Brush Biopsy): Cross-sections of respiratory cilia reveal pathognomonic axonemal ultrastructural defects: Complete or partial absence of outer dynein arms (ODA, most common defect, ~40%), absence of inner dynein arms (IDA), combined ODA/IDA absence, central pair microtubule absence (9+0 arrangement), or radial spoke defects
High-Speed Video Microscopy Analysis (HSVA): Demonstrates immotile cilia or stiff, erratic, dyskinetic ciliary beating patterns lacking normal coordinated metachronal waves
Immunofluorescence Microscopy: Direct absence of ciliary axonemal proteins, including DNAH5, DNAH11 (outer dynein arm heavy chains), and DNALI1 (inner dynein arm light chain)
Genetic Confirmation: Autosomal recessive mutations in over 45 identified ciliary structural genes (most frequently DNAH5, DNAI1, CCDC39, CCDC40)
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Seminal genetic ciliopathy characterized by the legendary triad of situs inversus, pansinusitis/bronchiectasis, and infertility, proven by right-sided apical impulse, complete mirror-image transposition on CXR/CT, and absent dynein arms on TEM.

Pulmonology.name: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis
clinical_manifestations: Almost exclusively affects women of reproductive age
Spontaneous recurrent pneumothorax with acute chest pain and dyspnea
Chylothorax (milky lymphatic pleural fluid on thoracentesis)
Chylous ascites, chylohemoptysis, and chyluria
Cutaneous signs of Tuberous Sclerosis in TSC-LAM: facial angiofibromas, ungual fibromas, shagreen patches
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT: Pathognomonic diffuse, bilateral, thin-walled (typically <2 mm), round, well-circumscribed, air-filled cysts uniformly distributed throughout both lungs with completely normal intervening lung parenchyma
Abdominal / Pelvic CT and MRI: Multiple bilateral fat-containing renal angiomyolipomas (AMLs), retroperitoneal cystic lymphangiomyomas showing progressive fluid accumulation
pathology_manifestations: Lung biopsy / cell block: Proliferation of atypical, immature smooth muscle-like spindle and epithelioid cells (LAM cells) lining pulmonary cyst walls and tracking along lymphatic channels; immunohistochemistry positive for smooth muscle actin (SMA), desmin, and estrogen/progesterone receptors, and specifically reactive for HMB-45
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield cystic lung disease presenting with milky chylothorax, pneumothorax, and TSC skin signs, alongside diagnostic uniform thin-walled lung cysts and renal angiomyolipomas on CT.

Pulmonology.name: Plastic Bronchitis
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic bedside finding: Expectoration (vomica) or bronchoscopic extraction of large, intact, cohesive, branching, tree-like, rubbery bronchial casts that form an astonishingly exact anatomical three-dimensional replication of the tracheobronchial tree arborization

Acute life-threatening asphyxiation: Sudden-onset severe dyspnea, choking, intractable coughing fits, stridor, and central cyanosis caused by complete mainstem or lobar bronchial airway occlusion by impacted casts

Clinical context: Most frequently develops in children and adolescents who have undergone single-ventricle palliation (Fontan procedure, 1–4% incidence) due to elevated systemic venous pressures and lymphatic hypertension, or in patients with congenital pulmonary lymphangiectasia, severe asthma, cystic fibrosis, or sickle cell acute chest syndrome

Bedside physical examination: Asymmetric, completely absent breath sounds over an entire hemithorax or lobe ('silent chest') alternating with high-pitched wheezing; paradoxical 'flapping' or 'thudding' sound (bruit de drapeau) audible over the trachea during inspiration as the cast mobilizes
Transient relief: Immediate, dramatic clinical improvement and clearing of breath sounds immediately following the expectoration or bronchoscopic removal of an obstructive bronchial cast
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (CXR): Sudden complete or lobar atelectasis (homogeneous opacification with volume loss and ipsilateral mediastinal shift) that rapidly and dramatically resolves or shifts to another lobe following cast expectoration; compensatory hyperinflation of adjacent unobstructed segments

High-Resolution Chest CT: Directly demonstrates dense, branching, intraluminal, soft-tissue-attenuation casts filling and expanding the lumen of large and segmental bronchi, creating the 'finger-in-glove' appearance or extensive branching endobronchial plugging without underlying airway wall destruction

Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced Magnetic Resonance Lymphangiography (DCMRL - Definitive Diagnostic Imaging): Visualizes the underlying pathophysiological lymphatic mechanism: demonstrates abnormal dilated, tortuous retroperitoneal and thoracic lymphatic channels, dilated and congested thoracic duct, and pathognomonic retrograde lymphatic perfusion into the pulmonary parenchyma and peribronchial sheaths ('lymphatic pulmonary perfusion syndrome') weeping chyle/lymph directly into the bronchial lumen
pathology_manifestations: Gross Pathology: Remarkable branching, arborizing, white, cream-colored, or tan rubbery cylindrical casts measuring up to 10–15 cm in length, conforming exactly to the branching bifurcations of the lobar, segmental, and subsegmental bronchi

Histopathology (Seear Classification): Type 1 (Inflammatory / Cellular Casts - 25%): Dense, eosinophilic, laminated fibrin network heavily infiltrated with inflammatory cells (abundant neutrophils, eosinophils, Charcot-Leyden crystals, and desquamated respiratory epithelial cells; typically seen in severe asthma, ABPA, or respiratory infections); Type 2 (Acellular / Lymphatic Casts - 75%): Composed almost entirely of amorphous mucin and proteinaceous fibrin matrix with scattered mononuclear lymphocytes, devoid of cellular inflammatory infiltrates; contains chylomicrons and fat droplets that stain positive with Oil Red O or Sudan black (characteristic of post-Fontan and lymphatic disorders)
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Unforgettable pulmonary entity distinguished by dramatic bedside expectoration of arborizing, tree-like bronchial casts causing acute asphyxia, with DCMRL demonstrating peribronchial lymphatic weeping and histology categorizing Type 1 vs Type 2 casts.

Pulmonology.name: Pulmonary Alveolar Microlithiasis
clinical_manifestations: Striking clinical-radiological dissociation in early and moderate stages: patients often present with surprisingly mild exertional dyspnea or near-normal bedside examination despite astonishingly dense, near-total opacification of both lungs on imaging
Progressive exertional dyspnea developing into profound respiratory failure in late-stage disease
Marked digital clubbing (Hippocratic fingers) of hands and feet in advanced stages
Central cyanosis, tachypnea, and prominent end-inspiratory crackles on chest auscultation

Signs of severe pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale: elevated jugular venous pressure with prominent 'v' wave, right ventricular heave, loud P2 heart sound, tricuspid regurgitation murmur, and peripheral lower extremity pitting edema
Expectoration of gritty, stony, calcific sand-like microliths (microlithoptysis) during severe coughing paroxysms
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (Pathognomonic 'Sandstorm' Appearance): Bilateral, diffuse, extraordinarily dense, sand-like calcific micronodules (<1 mm) involving every lung field with middle-to-lower zone and posterior predominance; 'white-out' of the lungs obscuring the cardiac borders and diaphragmatic silhouettes (shaggy heart sign); pathognomonic subpleural radiolucent line ('black pleural line') along the inner thoracic cage due to relative preservation of subpleural tissue against the densely calcified lung

Chest HRCT: Diffuse, high-attenuation, calcium-density micronodules distributed along bronchovascular bundles, subpleural surfaces, and interlobular septa ('calcified crazy-paving'); dense calcification of the interlobular septa and subpleural calcific bands ('flame-shaped calcifications'); pleural calcification and small subpleural bullae; hyperdense calcific consolidation of the lung bases ('stony lungs')

99mTc-Bone Scintigraphy (MDP SPECT/CT): Intense, diffuse, symmetrical radiotracer uptake across both lung fields ('hot lungs') matching or exceeding skeletal uptake, definitively demonstrating active calcium phosphate accumulation
pathology_manifestations: Surgical / transbronchial lung biopsy: Intra-alveolar spaces packed with dense, spherical, concentric, laminated calcospherites (microliths) measuring 50–1000 µm in diameter, composed of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite); strongly positive with Von Kossa calcium stain (intense black) and Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS); underlying alveolar septa initially intact and morphologically normal, later showing secondary interstitial fibrosis and giant cell reaction around displaced microliths; genetic confirmation via SLC34A2 mutation
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Legendary pulmonary condition characterized by the textbook 'sandstorm' bilateral lung calcification and 'black pleural line' on chest CT and X-ray, matched with clinical microlithoptysis, digital clubbing, and pathognomonic calcospherite histology.

Pulmonology.name: Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis
clinical_manifestations: Cyanosis and tachypnea disproportionate to physical examination findings
Digital clubbing of fingers and toes
Cough productive of gelatinous, chunky, or milky sputum
Milky, opaque, lipid-rich bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid on direct visual inspection
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT: Pathognomonic 'crazy-paving' pattern consisting of patchy, bilateral ground-glass opacities with sharply demarcated geographic borders and superimposed smooth interlobular and intralobular septal thickening
Chest Radiography: Symmetrical bilateral perihilar alveolar infiltrates resembling pulmonary edema ('bat-wing' or 'butterfly' distribution) with normal cardiac size
pathology_manifestations: Transbronchial / surgical lung biopsy: Alveolar spaces packed and distended with granular, eosinophilic, amorphous, lipoproteinaceous material derived from surfactant, which stains intensely positive with Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS) and resists diastase digestion; preservation of underlying alveolar wall architecture without marked interstitial inflammation
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Displays gross milky BAL fluid and digital clubbing matching the textbook, pathognomonic 'crazy-paving' pattern on chest HRCT.

Pulmonology.name: Pulmonary Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
clinical_manifestations: Patient demographic profile: Almost exclusively affects young adults (20–40 years of age) with a heavy current or past cigarette smoking history (>90–95% smokers)

Acute spontaneous pneumothorax: Presents in 15–20% of patients as sudden-onset sharp pleuritic chest pain, acute dyspnea, asymmetric diminished breath sounds, and hyperresonance (recurrent pneumothoraces are frequent and may be bilateral)
Insidious onset of non-productive cough, progressive exertional breathlessness, tachypnea, fatigue, and constitutional weight loss

Bedside physical signs: Nicotine-stained fingers and teeth, asthenic habitus, tachypnea; chest auscultation is frequently normal or reveals subtle mid-to-upper lung fine crackles or end-expiratory squeaks
Extrapulmonary physical findings in systemic disease: localized bone tenderness/swelling (osteolytic lesions), central diabetes insipidus (polyuria, polydipsia), or crusted papular scalp rash
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT (Pathognomonic Chronological Evolution): Early phase: Multiple, small (1–10 mm), poorly defined centrilobular nodules and peribronchiolar cavitary nodules; Intermediate to Late phase: Nodules cavitate and evolve into bizarrely shaped, bilobed, branched, cloverleaf-like, or coalescent thick- and thin-walled air-filled cysts (<2 cm in diameter)

Spatial Distribution (Crucial Diagnostic Rule): Striking predilection for the upper and middle lung zones with absolute or relative sparing of the extreme lung bases (costophrenic angles) — a key feature differentiating PLCH from lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM), where cysts are uniformly round and distributed throughout the entire lung including the bases
Preserved Lung Volume: Normal or increased total lung capacity (hyperinflation) despite diffuse cystic disease, without significant traction bronchiectasis or honeycombing

Chest Radiography: Bilateral reticulonodular and cystic opacities predominantly affecting the upper and middle zones, sparing the bases, with normal or increased lung volumes and visible pneumothorax line
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology: Bronchiolocentric, cellular, stellate or star-shaped interstitial granulomatous nodules that infiltrate and destroy the walls of distal respiratory bronchioles, followed by central cavitation leading to cystic enlargement

Cellular Composition: Proliferation of clonal, dendritic Langerhans cells characterized by abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and highly characteristic folded, grooved, indented, lobulated nuclei ('coffee-bean' or twisted nuclei); accompanied by an intense inflammatory infiltrate rich in eosinophils, lymphocytes, histiocytes, and pigment-laden 'smoker's macrophages'

Immunohistochemistry: Langerhans cells are strongly and specifically positive for CD1a, Langerin (CD207), and S100 protein; negative for HMB-45, smooth muscle actin (SMA), and cytokeratins (definitively ruling out LAM and carcinoma); high frequency of somatic BRAF V600E (50%) or MAP2K1 mutations
Transmission Electron Microscopy: Identifies classic intracytoplasmic Birbeck granules (pentalaminar rod-shaped or tennis-racket-shaped organelles with central striated line)
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Flagship smoking-related cystic lung disease characterized by sudden pneumothorax in young smokers, paired with pathognomonic bizarre/cloverleaf-shaped cysts sparing the lung bases on HRCT, and CD1a+/Langerin+ coffee-bean histiocytic nodules.

Pulmonology.name: Sarcoidosis
clinical_manifestations: Lupus pernio: indurated, violaceous, blue-red plaques and nodules on the nose, cheeks, ears, and lips
Erythema nodosum (painful red nodules on shins in Löfgren syndrome: fever, bilateral hilar adenopathy, erythema nodosum, polyarthritis)
Maculopapular sarcoidosis (waxy, translucent yellow-brown 'apple-jelly' papules on diascopy)
Scar sarcoidosis (sudden erythema and induration of preexisting tattoo marks or cutaneous scars)
Heerfordt syndrome (uveoparotid fever: parotid gland enlargement, anterior uveitis, facial palsy)
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (Stages 0-IV): Symmetrical bilateral hilar and right paratracheal lymphadenopathy ('Garland triad' / '1-2-3 sign'), progressive mid-to-upper lung zone reticulonodular opacities, upper lobe fibrocystic distortion

Chest HRCT: Perilymphatic nodular distribution (micronodules along bronchovascular bundles, subpleural regions, and interlobular septa), galaxy sign (central coalescence surrounded by satellite micronodules), traction bronchiectasis
Cardiac MRI: Patchy, non-ischemic mid-myocardial or subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) representing cardiac granulomatous involvement
18F-FDG PET/CT: Marked metabolic avidity in mediastinal/hilar lymph nodes, cardiac myocardium, and extrapulmonary organs
pathology_manifestations: Transbronchial / skin / lymph node biopsy: Well-formed, discrete, tightly packed, non-caseating (non-necrotizing) epithelioid granulomas rimmed by CD4+ T lymphocytes and fibroblasts; multinucleated giant cells containing Schaumann bodies (concentric laminations of calcium and protein) and Asteroid bodies (stellate starburst inclusions); negative stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungi
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Classic multisystem disease with textbook skin manifestations (lupus pernio, erythema nodosum, scar sarcoid) paired with the pathognomonic '1-2-3 sign' and perilymphatic micronodules on chest HRCT, PET, and cardiac MRI.

Pulmonology.name: Thoracic Empyema Necessitans
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark physical exam finding: A distinct, palpable, tender or non-tender, fluctuant subcutaneous chest wall mass or swelling, most commonly located on the anterior or anterolateral chest wall between the 2nd and 6th intercostal spaces, parasternal region, or mid-axillary line
Spontaneous cutaneous draining sinus or fistula tract discharging purulent, foul-smelling, or caseous necrotic exudate through the thoracic skin
Dullness to percussion and absent or severely diminished tactile vocal fremitus and vesicular breath sounds over the affected hemithorax
Systemic constitutional signs: low-grade or swinging fever, drenching night sweats, severe cachexia, unintentional weight loss, and chronic productive cough
Overlying skin changes: erythema, warm induration, purpuric discoloration, or necrotic cutaneous ulceration with visible granulation tissue at the fistula orifice
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic direct visualization of a continuous, fluid-attenuation (10–30 HU) collection extending from the pleural space, breaching the parietal pleura and costal intercostal space, and dissecting into the chest wall musculature (pectoralis major, serratus anterior, intercostal muscles) and subcutaneous soft tissues ('collar-button' or dumbbell-shaped abscess)
'Split Pleura Sign': Prominent thickening and avid contrast enhancement of both the separated visceral and parietal pleura surrounding the loculated pleural collection, diagnostic of true empyema
Rib and Skeletal Involvement: Irregular cortical erosion, osteolytic destruction, periosteal reaction, or sequestrum formation of the adjacent ribs or sternum (secondary osteomyelitis)

Chest Radiography: Large, lenticular or D-shaped peripheral pleural-based opacity with obtuse angles to the chest wall, often accompanied by an adjacent soft-tissue bulge projecting beyond the lateral thoracic rib cage shadow

Thoracic Ultrasound: Complex, septated, hypoechoic or heterogeneous fluid collection in the pleural space with real-time demonstration of a transcostal defect and communicating subcutaneous fluid pocket
pathology_manifestations: Microbiological and Histological Etiology: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is the causative agent in ~73% of cases worldwide; Actinomyces israelii accounts for ~20%; pyogenic bacterial pathogens (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus) account for the remainder

Tuberculous Pathology: Abundant caseous necrosis with multinucleated Langhans giant cells, epithelioid histiocytes, and peripheral lymphocytic cuffing; positive Ziehl-Neelsen (acid-fast) or auramine-rhodamine fluorochrome staining, confirmed by Mycobacterium tuberculosis PCR (GeneXpert MTB/RIF)

Actinomycotic Pathology: Suppurative microabscesses containing pathognomonic 'sulfur granules' (round/lobulated basophilic colonies of branching filamentous bacteria with radiating, club-like eosinophilic peripheral Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon); Gram-positive and silver methenamine (GMS) positive branching filaments

Pleural Fluid Analysis: Frank purulence, exudative criteria (pleural protein >3 g/dL, pleural/serum LDH >0.6), profound acidosis (pH <7.20), low glucose (<40 mg/dL), and markedly elevated WBC count with polymorphonuclear or lymphocytic predominance
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive, high-yield complication of untreated pleural infection featuring a palpable, fluctuant chest wall mass or draining fistula, uniquely visualized on CT as an empyema breaching the intercostal space with the 'split pleura sign'.

Pulmonology.name: Tracheobronchial Amyloidosis
clinical_manifestations: Progressive, harsh inspiratory and expiratory stridor refractory to conventional bronchodilators, frequently misdiagnosed for years as adult-onset refractory asthma or severe COPD
Intractable hoarseness and dysphonia resulting from amyloid infiltration and rigid fixation of the vocal cords and subglottic mucosa
Episodic, recurrent hemoptysis ranging from mild blood-tinged sputum to life-threatening bleeding triggered by mucosal fragility and erosion of submucosal amyloid plaques
Recurrent post-obstructive lobar atelectasis and pneumonia, presenting with fever, localized wheezing, pleuritic chest pain, and foul-smelling purulent sputum

Bedside physical examination: audible monophonic tracheal wheeze or rhonchus over the anterior neck and sternal notch, marked suprasternal and intercostal retractions during forced inspiration, and localized reduction in air entry
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT with Tracheobronchial Multiplanar Reformats (MPR) and Virtual Bronchoscopy: Pathognomonic circumferential, nodular, or plaque-like thickening of the tracheal and proximal bronchial walls that characteristically INVOLVES the posterior membranous wall (trachealis muscle) — a critical distinguishing radiological feature that differentiates amyloidosis from relapsing polychondritis and tracheobronchopathia osteochondroplastica (TBO), both of which strictly spare the posterior membrane
Airway Calcification: Coarse, punctate, or dense nodular mural calcifications and ossifications embedded within the thickened airway wall lining the tracheal lumen
Dynamic Expiratory CT: Fixed, rigid central airway luminal narrowing without the dynamic excessive collapse seen in tracheobronchomalacia

Thoracic MRI: Amyloid airway deposits display characteristic intermediate-to-low signal intensity on T1-weighted images and marked hypointensity on T2-weighted images due to high proteinaceous fibril content and calcification, with variable enhancement post-gadolinium
Chest Radiography: Tracheal luminal irregularity, narrowing, scalloping, and secondary downstream lobar collapse or hyperinflation
pathology_manifestations: Endobronchial Biopsy: Submucosa expanded and replaced by extensive, dense, acellular, amorphous, glassy, eosinophilic hyaline protein deposits that efface normal glandular and vascular structures

Congo Red Histochemistry: Pathognomonic bright apple-green birefringence under polarized light microscopy, confirming β-pleated sheet amyloid fibril conformation; displays distinctive metachromasia with methyl violet or crystal violet

Immunohistochemistry and Typing: Predominantly AL amyloidosis (localized immunoglobulin light chain amyloid, positive for monoclonal kappa [κ] or lambda [λ] light chains secreted by localized clonal plasma cells); occasionally AA amyloidosis (amyloid A protein positive); negative for transthyretin (ATTR)
Electron Microscopy: Identifies rigid, non-branching, randomly oriented fibrils measuring 7.5 to 10 nm in diameter infiltrating the submucosa and encircling tracheal microvessels
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Essential non-malignant central airway disorder presenting with intractable stridor and hoarseness, marked on CT by pathognomonic circumferential airway thickening involving the posterior membranous wall with mural calcification, confirmed by Congo red apple-green birefringence.

Pulmonology.name: Tracheobronchopathia Osteochondroplastica
clinical_manifestations: Inspiratory or biphasic stridor, progressive hoarseness, and persistent coarse 'croupy' cough that is refractory to bronchodilators and corticosteroids
Recurrent lower respiratory tract infections, post-obstructive pneumonia, and chronic purulent sputum production
Recurrent episodes of hemoptysis triggered by mechanical trauma and ulceration of airway nodules

Dramatic bronchoscopic visual exam (pathognomonic visual hallmark): striking 'cobblestone', 'rock garden', or 'stalactite/stalagmite' appearance of multiple sessile, hard, white-to-yellow osteocartilaginous nodules (1–3 mm) projecting into the lumen along the anterior and lateral walls of the trachea and main bronchi, with characteristic, absolute sparing of the posterior membranous trachea
Grating sensation or difficult/impossible endotracheal intubation ('gritty resistance' during tube passage)
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT / Virtual Bronchoscopy (Imaging Gold Standard): Characteristic, pathognomonic nodular, irregular, beaded ossified and calcified submucosal projections (1–5 mm) protruding into the tracheal and major bronchial lumen arising exclusively from the cartilaginous anterior and lateral walls; absolute and strict sparing of the soft posterior membranous tracheal wall; luminal narrowing and tracheal wall deformity; absence of extrinsic compression or lymphadenopathy
Neck and Chest Radiography: Undulating, irregular, scalloped, calcified lining of the inner tracheal wall with luminal narrowing
