Coronal / 3D CT Airway Reconstructions: Extensive 'beaded' or corrugated inner tracheal lumen extending from the subglottic space to the carinal and proximal bronchial bifurcations
pathology_manifestations: Bronchoscopic mucosal biopsy / surgical specimen: Submucosal islands of mature lamellar bone, osteoid tissue, mature hyaline cartilage, and focal hematopoietic or fatty bone marrow elements situated directly within the lamina propria and submucosa of the airway wall; continuous or in direct contact with the underlying perichondrium of native tracheal cartilaginous rings; overlying pseudostratified ciliated columnar respiratory epithelium showing squamous metaplasia, erosion, or ulceration without cytologic atypia
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Exceptional airway disease with a pathognomonic bronchoscopic 'rock garden' visual sign and diagnostic chest CT demonstrating calcified nodular projections along the anterior/lateral tracheal wall with absolute posterior membrane sparing.

Pulmonology.name: Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis
clinical_manifestations: Hoarse child with warty lesions on the vocal cords at laryngoscopy
Stridor when the glottis is obstructed
radiological_manifestations: CT: tracheal or pulmonary cystic papillomas if disease spreads below the larynx
pathology_manifestations: HPV-driven squamous papillomas with koilocytes, usually types 6 and 11
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Airway HPV disease whose laryngoscopic photographs are the gallery.

Pulmonology.name: Diffuse Panbronchiolitis
clinical_manifestations: Chronic sinusitis with nasal polyps plus productive cough
The external image is the sinus disease; the defining image is the chest CT
radiological_manifestations: HRCT: diffuse centrilobular nodules and tree-in-bud with later bronchiolectasis
pathology_manifestations: Transbronchial biopsy: foamy interstitial macrophages in respiratory bronchioles
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: East-Asian small-airway disease with sinus photographs, a tree-in-bud CT, and a foamy-macrophage biopsy.

Pulmonology.name: Pulmonary Arteriovenous Malformation
clinical_manifestations: Cyanosis, clubbing, and orthodeoxia when shunts are large
Telangiectasias if hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia is the cause; HHT stays a dermatology topic and this is the lung lesion
radiological_manifestations: CT angiography: a peripheral nodule with a feeding artery and draining vein; bubble echo shows intrapulmonary shunt
pathology_manifestations: Dilated vascular channels without a capillary bed on resected lesions
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Shunt lesion with clubbing photographs and a feeding-vessel CT sign.

Pulmonology.name: Exogenous Lipoid Pneumonia
clinical_manifestations: Chronic cough after mineral-oil laxative or oil-based nasal drops
The history is clinical; the image is CT
radiological_manifestations: CT: consolidation or a mass-like lesion with fat attenuation
pathology_manifestations: Lipid-laden macrophages on BAL or biopsy, oil-red-O positive
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Aspiration disease with fat-attenuation CT and lipid-laden macrophages.

Pulmonology.name: Thoracic Endometriosis
clinical_manifestations: Pneumothorax or hemoptysis within 72 hours of menses
radiological_manifestations: Chest radiograph or CT: right-sided pneumothorax, diaphragmatic holes, or ground-glass hemorrhage
pathology_manifestations: Endometrial stroma and glands on pleural or diaphragmatic biopsy, often with CD10
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Catamenial lung disease with a timed pneumothorax film and ectopic endometrial histology.

Pulmonology.name: Yellow Nail Syndrome
synonyms: yellow nail, lymphedema, and pleural effusion
clinical_manifestations: Slow-growing thick yellow nails
Lymphedema of the legs
radiological_manifestations: Chest radiograph: recurrent pleural effusions, often exudative and lymphocytic
pathology_manifestations: No specific nail histology is required; dilated lymphatics may be shown
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Triad with nail and lymphedema photographs plus a pleural effusion film.

Pulmonology.name: Chronic Eosinophilic Pneumonia
clinical_manifestations: Subacute cough, fever, and wheeze in a middle-aged adult, often a woman
The photograph of the disease is the chest film
radiological_manifestations: Chest radiograph: peripheral photographic-negative-of-pulmonary-edema infiltrates
CT: upper-lobe peripheral consolidation
pathology_manifestations: BAL eosinophilia and organizing eosinophilic pneumonia on biopsy if performed
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Eosinophilic pneumonia with a named radiographic pattern. Asthma alone stays excluded.

Pulmonology.name: Diffuse Pulmonary Lymphangiomatosis
clinical_manifestations: Chylous pleural effusion and chyloptysis
Wheeze from infiltrated airways
radiological_manifestations: CT: septal thickening, mediastinal infiltration, and pleural fluid
MR lymphangiography shows the leak
pathology_manifestations: Anastomosing lymphatic channels along bronchovascular bundles
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Lymphatic lung disease with chylous fluid photographs and septal-thickening CT.

Pulmonology.name: Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease
clinical_manifestations: Nasal polyps that recur after polypectomy
Aspirin-induced wheeze is a provocation, not a separate topic
radiological_manifestations: Sinus CT: expansile bilateral polyps filling the ethmoid and maxillary sinuses
pathology_manifestations: Edematous eosinophilic polyps
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Airway disease with polyp photographs and a packed-sinus CT. Asthma alone stays excluded.

Pulmonology.name: Pulmonary Hyalinizing Granuloma
clinical_manifestations: Often found on a film; clubbing is uncommon
Included for the nodule photograph on CT and the histologic lamellae
radiological_manifestations: CT: bilateral well-circumscribed nodules, sometimes with calcification
pathology_manifestations: Lamellar collagen whorls, after excluding infection, vasculitis, and IgG4 disease
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Nodular fibrosing lung disease with a CT gallery and a lamellar histologic image.

Pulmonology.name: Acute Eosinophilic Pneumonia
clinical_manifestations: Acute febrile hypoxic respiratory failure, often after new smoking or dust exposure
radiological_manifestations: CT: bilateral ground-glass opacity, septal lines, and pleural fluid
pathology_manifestations: BAL eosinophils above 25 percent without infection
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Acute eosinophilic lung injury with a CT pattern and a BAL image. Distinct from the chronic photographic-negative form.

Pulmonology.name: Hermansky-Pudlak Syndrome
synonyms: albinism with pulmonary fibrosis and bleeding diathesis
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic oculocutaneous albinism in clinical photographs: creamy-white to light sandy skin, white-to-light blond or brown hair, horizontal nystagmus, and reduced visual acuity
Ophthalmologic examination: iris transillumination on slit-lamp photography and markedly reduced retinal pigmentation with foveal hypoplasia on funduscopy
Bleeding diathesis: lifelong easy bruising, prolonged epistaxis, and gingival hemorrhage from platelet dense granule deficiency
Progressive dyspnea on exertion and intractable dry cough developing in the 3rd to 5th decade heralds fatal fibrosing lung disease
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT (HRCT): Progressive usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) or fibrosing non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) pattern with peripheral and basilar reticulation, subpleural honeycombing, and extensive traction bronchiectasis
HRCT Ground-Glass Opacities: Bilateral symmetrical patchy ground-glass attenuations indicating intra-alveolar ceroid accumulation
Chest Radiography: Progressive volume loss, basilar reticulonodular opacities, and elevated hemidiaphragms
pathology_manifestations: Surgical Lung Biopsy: Patchy interstitial collagenous fibrosis with fibroblastic foci, accompanied by striking intra-alveolar and interstitial accumulation of foamy macrophages containing brown, PAS-positive, diastase-resistant ceroid pigment
Platelet Electron Microscopy: Complete absence of electron-dense delta granules (dense granules), confirming platelet storage pool deficiency
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield pulmonary-genetic syndrome where fatal fibrosing alveolitis (pulmonary fibrosis) is immediately linked to clinical photographs of oculocutaneous albinism, iris transillumination, and platelet bleeding.

Pulmonology.name: Poland Syndrome
synonyms: unilateral pectoralis major agenesis with symbrachydactyly
clinical_manifestations: Striking anterior chest wall photograph: unilateral absence of the sternocostal head of the pectoralis major muscle, resulting in flattening/depression of the anterior chest, hypoplasia or amastia of the ipsilateral breast and nipple-areola complex, and absent axillary hair
Dynamic clinical sign: visible lung herniation (paradoxical bulging of the lung through anterior intercostal rib defects during coughing or forced expiration)
Ipsilateral hand deformity: symbrachydactyly (short, webbed fingers with hypoplasia or aplasia of middle phalanges) visible on clinical extremity photographs
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT with 3D Volume Rendering: Unilateral total absence of the sternocostal head of pectoralis major muscle, anterior rib defects (absence/hypoplasia of ribs 2-4), lung herniation, and ipsilateral thoracic volume reduction
Chest Radiography: Unilateral hyperlucency of the involved hemithorax (mimicking Swyer-James or pneumothorax) caused by absence of the overlying pectoral soft tissue shadow
Hand Radiography: Symbrachydactyly with hypoplasia/aplasia of middle phalanges and soft tissue syndactyly
pathology_manifestations: Embryological Etiology: Subclavian artery supply disruption sequence (interruption of the embryonic proximal subclavian branches during the 6th week of gestation)
Gross Muscle Pathology: Total agenesis of the sternocostal portion of the pectoralis major, with variable absence of pectoralis minor, serratus anterior, and latissimus dorsi
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Classic thoracic cage disease presenting with unmistakable clinical photographs of unilateral chest depression, absent pectoralis major, lung herniation, and ipsilateral symbrachydactyly.

Pulmonology.name: Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma
clinical_manifestations: Asymmetric thoracic constriction on clinical photos: noticeable contraction and flattening of the affected hemithorax with ipsilateral shoulder drooping and restricted chest excursion
Cutaneous / chest wall seeding: palpable, firm subcutaneous tumor nodules erupting along previous thoracentesis, chest tube, or biopsy tract sites
Auscultation and percussion: stony dullness to percussion and complete absence of breath sounds over the encased hemithorax with severe dull non-pleuritic chest pain
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT: Pathognomonic diffuse, circumferential, nodular, rind-like pleural thickening (>1 cm) encasing the hemithorax, extending into mediastinal pleura and interlobar fissures, with ipsilateral volume loss and mediastinal shift toward the tumor
18F-FDG PET/CT: Intense, continuous hypermetabolic tracer uptake (SUVmax typically >6-12) outlining the entire thickened pleural rind and identifying chest wall or transdiaphragmatic invasion
Chest Radiography: Large unilateral pleural effusion with nodular pleural contours, contracted hemithorax, and blunted costophrenic angles
pathology_manifestations: Thoracoscopic / VATS Visual Inspection: Thick, grayish-white, fibrous cobblestone or gelatinous neoplastic rind studding both parietal and visceral pleurae, with thick hemorrhagic pleural effusion

Histopathology & Immunohistochemistry: Tubulopapillary, solid, or spindle-cell (sarcomatoid) growth pattern; positive for calretinin, WT1, cytokeratin 5/6, and D2-40 (podoplanin), with diagnostic loss of nuclear BAP1 expression and MTAP deletion
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield pleural malignancy with distinct thoracoscopic photography of cobblestone tumor rind, CT demonstration of circumferential pleural encasement, and visible biopsy tract tumor seeding.

Pulmonology.name: Bronchial Carcinoid Tumor
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent unilateral hemoptysis (from cough-induced bleeding of the hypervascular endobronchial tumor surface)
Persistent, localized, monophonic musical wheezing on thoracic auscultation, unresponsive to bronchodilators, frequently misdiagnosed as adult-onset refractory asthma
Recurrent post-obstructive pneumonias, fever, and purulent sputum occurring repeatedly in the exact same pulmonary lobe or segment
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT: Well-circumscribed, round or oval central endobronchial mass showing intense intravenous contrast enhancement (due to rich capillary vascularity), post-obstructive atelectasis, mucus plugging (bronchocele), and distal air-trapping
68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT: Intense somatostatin receptor-avid radiotracer uptake (high SUVmax) localized to the endobronchial lesion and regional hilar lymph nodes
Chest Radiography: Sharply demarcated hilar nodule or persistent lobar collapse/consolidation with volume loss
pathology_manifestations: Flexible / Rigid Bronchoscopy Photography: Pathognomonic appearance of a smooth, spherical, highly vascular, bright cherry-red to pink polypoid fleshy mass protruding into and occluding the bronchial lumen ('iceberg' tumor)

Histopathology: Monomorphic, round-to-polygonal neuroendocrine cells with moderate eosinophilic cytoplasm and uniform round nuclei with classic 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin, arranged in organoid nests and trabeculae; strongly positive for synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and CD56
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal endobronchial neoplasm with unmistakable bronchoscopic photographs of a bright cherry-red vascular polypoid mass, intense enhancement on CT, and classic neuroendocrine organoid architecture.

Pulmonology.name: Endobronchial Hamartoma
clinical_manifestations: Severe progressive dyspnea, persistent intractable cough, and intermittent hemoptysis resulting from dynamic large airway obstruction
Recurrent, unresolving post-obstructive atelectasis and pneumonia distal to the obstructing airway mass
Unilateral localized wheeze or stridor audible over the central chest that changes intensity with posture
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT: Well-circumscribed, round endobronchial lesion displaying pathognomonic areas of low CT attenuation (-40 to -120 HU) indicative of fat tissue, interspersed with coarse, punctate 'popcorn' calcifications
Virtual Bronchoscopy CT Reconstructions: Clear demonstration of a pedunculated intraluminal tumor projecting from the bronchial wall with distal complete lobar collapse and bronchial dilation
Chest Radiography: Complete lobar or segmental atelectasis with triangular wedge-shaped opacity and compensatory hyperinflation of adjacent lobes
pathology_manifestations: Bronchoscopic Photography: Distinctive smooth, lobulated, yellowish-white to pinkish, glistening, firm, mobile pedunculated or sessile polypoid mass projecting directly into the tracheobronchial lumen

Histopathology: Benign mesenchymal mixture of mature hyaline cartilage lobules, mature adipose tissue, fibrous myxoid connective tissue, and entrapped clefts lined by normal pseudostratified ciliated respiratory epithelium
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: A benign airway neoplasm presenting with distinctive bronchoscopic photographs of a yellowish lobulated polypoid mass, pathognomonic CT fat and popcorn calcification, and post-obstructive atelectasis.

Pulmonology.name: Vanishing Lung Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Young, tall, thin male tobacco or marijuana smoker presenting with progressive, severe dyspnea, chest tightness, and sudden-onset pleuritic pain from secondary pneumothorax
Physical examination: dramatic asymmetry of chest wall expansion with marked hyperresonance to percussion and total absence of breath sounds across the upper half of the involved hemithorax
Severe exercise intolerance with resting hypoxemia and hypercapnia out of proportion to patient age
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Giant, coalescent, paper-thin walled bullae occupying at least one-third of the hemithorax (often >50-70%), predominantly in the upper lobes, compressing the adjacent normal lung parenchyma into a dense atelectatic crescent

Chest Radiography: Avital, hyperlucent lung zones with absent bronchovascular markings occupying the upper chest, mimicking a tension pneumothorax, with downward displacement of the diaphragm and contralateral mediastinal shift
Expiratory HRCT: Marked air-trapping within the giant bullae without volume reduction during expiration, confirming absence of effective ventilation
pathology_manifestations: VATS / Thoracoscopy Operative Photography: Spectacular view of massive, transparent, tense, glistening, paper-thin subpleural air sacs ballooning out and herniating from the apical chest cavity

Surgical Pathology: Resected bullous wall consists of attenuated, paper-thin fibrous connective tissue with compressed subpleural elastic fibers and scattered anthracotic pigment, devoid of functioning alveolar capillary beds
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct clinical and radiologic disease defined by giant upper-lobe bullae occupying >1/3 of a hemithorax, with breathtaking thoracoscopic surgical photography of transparent ballooning air sacs.

Pulmonology.name: Middle Lobe Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Chronic, intractable, hacking cough with copious purulent sputum and recurrent bouts of right-sided pleuritic chest pain and fever
Recurrent, refractory episodes of pneumonia localized exclusively to the right middle lobe occurring over months to years
Hemoptysis (streaky or brisk) originating from chronic middle lobe bronchiectasis and recurrent bacterial colonization
radiological_manifestations: Posteroanterior & Lateral Chest Radiography: Classic triangular or wedge-shaped dense band extending anteroinferiorly from the hilum toward the anterior costophrenic angle on the lateral view, with blurring of the right heart border (positive silhouette sign) on the PA view

High-Resolution Chest CT: Complete or partial collapse of the right middle lobe, severe cylindrical or cystic bronchiectasis confined to middle lobe segments, with extrinsic compression from enlarged calcified hilar lymph nodes or intrinsic mucus plugging
Sagittal CT Reconstructions: Narrow, compressed wedge of collapsed middle lobe sandwiched tightly between the major and minor fissures
pathology_manifestations: Bronchoscopic Photography: Dramatic view of slit-like concentric stenosis, fish-mouth narrowing, or complete purulent inflammatory occlusion of the right middle lobe bronchus orifice

Surgical Lobectomy Pathology: Extensive follicular bronchiectasis with chronic suppurative bronchitis, dense peribronchial lymphadenitis, parenchymal fibrosis, and lipid-laden foamy macrophages ('foam cell pneumonia')
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Classic clinicopathologic entity characterized by recurrent atelectasis of the right middle lobe, marked by the classic radiological lateral wedge and silhouette sign, and bronchoscopic slit-like orifice stenosis.

Pulmonology.name: Pulmonary Veno-Occlusive Disease
clinical_manifestations: Severe, rapidly progressive exertional dyspnea, fatigue, syncope, and resting hypoxemia mimicking idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension
Physical examination: loud, booming second heart sound (P2), right ventricular heave, elevated jugular venous distension with prominent 'v' waves, and peripheral cyanosis
Catastrophic acute clinical event: sudden, severe flash pulmonary edema occurring rapidly after administration of pulmonary vasodilator therapy (e.g., prostacyclin, PDE5 inhibitors)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT (Diagnostic Gold Standard Triad): Concomitant presence of: (1) smooth interlobular septal thickening (Kerley B lines), (2) diffuse centrilobular ground-glass opacities, and (3) mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy in the setting of severe pulmonary arterial hypertension
CT Pulmonary Angiography: Normal large pulmonary arteries without thromboembolism, but with massive main pulmonary artery dilatation (>29 mm) and normal left atrial dimensions
Right Heart Catheterization: Markedly elevated pulmonary arterial pressure with characteristically normal pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP)
pathology_manifestations: Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) Cytology (Diagnostic Clue): Striking, diffuse presence of hemosiderin-laden alveolar macrophages highlighted by Prussian blue (Perls) stain (Golde score typically >100), reflecting occult intra-alveolar hemorrhage

Lung Histopathology: Extensive, fibrous, intimal loose-to-dense obliteration of small pulmonary veins and post-capillary venules with prominent pulmonary capillary engorgement and secondary medial arterial hypertrophy
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield pulmonary vascular disease distinguished by the pathognomonic HRCT triad (septal thickening, ground-glass nodules, adenopathy), Prussian blue-positive BAL cytology, and vasodilator-induced pulmonary edema.

Pulmonology.name: Pulmonary Capillary Hemangiomatosis
clinical_manifestations: Progressive, refractory exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, and severe fatigue in young-to-middle-aged adults
Recurrent, life-threatening hemoptysis resulting from pulmonary capillary rupture into alveolar spaces
Rapidly progressive right heart failure with massive peripheral edema, hepatomegaly, ascites, and digital clubbing
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT: Diffuse, ill-defined, centrilobular ground-glass nodules (<1 cm) distributed symmetrically throughout both lungs, without significant interlobular septal thickening or pleural effusion
Contrast-Enhanced CT / MR: Enormous dilatation of the main pulmonary artery trunk, marked right ventricular enlargement, and normal pulmonary venous anatomy
Ventilation-Perfusion (V/Q) Scan: Multiple, non-segmental, patchy, subsegmental perfusion defects mimicking chronic thromboembolic disease
pathology_manifestations: Surgical Lung Biopsy / Explant Histopathology (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Infiltrative, patch-like proliferation of thin-walled capillary channels arranged in 2 or 3 layers within thickened alveolar septa, directly invading and occluding adjacent pulmonary venules and bronchiolar walls
Immunohistochemistry: Proliferating capillary endothelial cells strongly express CD31, CD34, and ERG, and are negative for D2-40 and GLUT-1, distinguishing them from vascular sarcomas
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Severe pulmonary vascular disorder presenting with diffuse centrilobular nodules on HRCT and recurrent hemoptysis, with diagnostic histopathology of multiple-layered capillary proliferation invading alveolar walls.

Pulmonology.name: Lymphocytic Interstitial Pneumonia
synonyms: diffuse lymphoid hyperplasia of the lung
clinical_manifestations: Progressive exertional dyspnea, dry cough, and constitutional signs (weight loss, low-grade fevers, night sweats) in patients with Sjögren syndrome, HIV, or common variable immunodeficiency

Striking physical examination photos: massive, bilateral, painless parotid and submandibular salivary gland enlargement ('chipmunk cheeks'), marked keratoconjunctivitis sicca, and diffuse cervical lymphadenopathy
Thoracic exam: bilateral fine inspiratory velcro crackles audible across lung bases without digital clubbing
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT (Diagnostic Hallmark): Bilateral, thin-walled, well-circumscribed, round pulmonary cysts (typically 1-30 mm) distributed along peribronchovascular bundles and interlobular septa, superimposed on diffuse ground-glass attenuation
HRCT Nodular Features: Centrilobular and subpleural micronodules, bronchovascular bundle thickening, and mild mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Chest Radiography: Diffuse, symmetric reticulonodular opacities predominantly affecting the lower lung zones
pathology_manifestations: Surgical Lung Biopsy / Transbronchial Cryobiopsy: Dense, continuous, polyclonal lymphocytic infiltrate composed of mature T and B cells, plasma cells, and histiocytes expanding the alveolar septa and peribronchiolar interstitium without alveolar destruction
Immunohistochemistry: Polyclonal light chain expression (kappa and lambda positivity) and reactive germinal centers, distinguishing LIP from low-grade pulmonary MALT lymphoma
Pulmonology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct benign lymphoproliferative pulmonary disease defined by thin-walled peribronchovascular cysts on HRCT, dense polyclonal interstitial lymphocytic infiltration, and massive parotid enlargement on clinical photography.

Rheumatology.name: Adult-Onset Still's Disease
clinical_manifestations: Evanescent, salmon-pink, non-pruritic, macular or maculopapular rash (predominantly trunk and proximal extremities, transiently appearing during daily high-spiking quotidian fevers)
Persistent inflammatory polyarthritis and arthralgia (wrists, knees, ankles)
Severe sore throat (non-suppurative exudative pharyngitis)
Generalized lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly
radiological_manifestations: Wrist/Hand Radiographs: Non-erosive carpal joint space narrowing rapidly progressing to characteristic pericarpal and intercarpal bony ankylosis (carpometacarpal and intercarpal fusion sparing MCPs)
Abdominal CT/Ultrasound: Hepatosplenomegaly and retroperitoneal/mesenteric lymphadenopathy
Chest CT: Pleural and pericardial effusions, transient transient pulmonary parenchymal infiltrates
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy: Non-specific mild perivascular neutrophilic and lymphocytic infiltrate in the upper dermis without epidermal changes or true leukocytoclastic vasculitis
Lymph node biopsy: Marked benign follicular and paracortical hyperplasia, intense vascular proliferation with histiocytic sinus histiocytosis mimicking lymphoma
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Features the hallmark salmon-pink fever-dependent rash alongside progressive intercarpal bony fusion on wrist X-rays and systemic lymphadenopathy on CT.

Rheumatology.name: Ankylosing Spondylitis
clinical_manifestations: Kyphotic spinal deformity ('question mark' posture) with loss of normal lumbar lordosis and thoracic hyperkyphosis
Enthesitis (Achilles tendon swelling/tenderness, plantar fascial insertion pain)
Dactylitis ('sausage digits')
Acute anterior uveitis (erythematous ciliary flush, irregular pupil, hypopyon)
Restricted chest wall expansion (<2.5 cm at 4th intercostal space)
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic Radiographs/CT: Bilateral symmetric sacroiliitis (Grade I-IV: subchondral blurring, erosions, reactive sclerosis, complete bony ankylosis)
Sacroiliac Joint MRI: Active subchondral bone marrow edema on STIR sequences, periarticular fat metaplasia, capsulitis
Spine Radiographs/CT: Squaring of vertebral bodies, shiny corner sign (Romanus lesions), Andersson lesions, delicate vertical syndesmophytes, classical 'bamboo spine', dagger sign, trolley-track sign
Chest HRCT: Apical fibrobullous disease, secondary aspergilloma colonization
pathology_manifestations: Entheseal and sacroiliac joint histology: Mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate at the fibrocartilage-bone interface, osteoclast-mediated bone resorption followed by endochondral ossification and new woven bone formation
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Premier axial spondyloarthritis featuring severe structural postural changes and uveitis coupled with the pathognomonic 'bamboo spine' and sacroiliac erosion/ankylosis on plain film, CT, and MRI.

Rheumatology.name: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
Rheumatology.subspecialty: Systemic Autoimmune Thrombophilia & Connective Tissue Diseases
clinical_manifestations: Livedo reticularis / livedo racemosa: irregular, broken, asymmetric, violaceous branching net-like or circular cutaneous erythema over the thighs, trunk, and arms that does not resolve with warming

Digital ischemia and peripheral gangrene: acute onset of cyanotic, exquisitely painful, cold digits with rapid progression to dry gangrene, splinter hemorrhages beneath nail beds, and periungual necrotic infarcts

Atrophie blanche and livedoid vasculopathy: exquisitely painful, purpuric, crusted papules and stellate ulcers on the lower legs and ankles that heal with porcelain-white, stellate, atrophic scars bordered by hyperpigmentation and telangiectasias
Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and superficial thrombophlebitis: unilateral leg swelling, warmth, erythema, and tenderness, occasionally progressing to phlegmasia cerulea dolens

Catastrophic Antiphospholipid Syndrome (CAPS): acute, life-threatening multiorgan failure resulting from simultaneous disseminated microvascular thromboses in renal, pulmonary, cardiac, adrenal, and central nervous systems
radiological_manifestations: Duplex Doppler Ultrasonography of Peripheral Vessels: Intraluminal non-compressible, echogenic or hypoechoic thrombotic masses with loss of venous flow augmentation in femoral, popliteal, and deep calf veins, or acute occlusive arterial thrombosis

Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) (Chest, Abdomen, Pelvis): Pulmonary embolism manifesting as acute intraluminal filling defects in main, lobar, or segmental pulmonary arteries; bilateral adrenal gland enlargement and hypoenhancement (adrenal infarction/hemorrhage); wedge-shaped renal cortical infarcts; and mesenteric or aortic thrombi

Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and MRV: Multiple acute wedge-shaped cortical infarctions, multiple subcortical and deep white matter hyperintensities on T2/FLAIR representing chronic microvascular ischemic injury, and dural venous sinus thrombosis (superior sagittal or transverse sinus filling defects)

Transthoracic / Transesophageal Echocardiography: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (pathognomonic non-bacterial verrucous vegetations, characteristically sessile, irregular, 2-10 mm in size, adhering to the atrial surface of the mitral valve leaflets or aortic valve, with valvular thickening and regurgitation)
pathology_manifestations: Tissue Biopsy (Skin, Kidney, Heart, or other affected viscera): Non-inflammatory, bland occlusive thrombosis of small to medium-sized arterioles, capillaries, and venules filled with fibrin and platelet thrombi; striking absence of significant transmural inflammatory infiltrates or leukocytoclasia in the vessel wall, definitively differentiating APS from systemic necrotizing vasculitis

Renal Biopsy (APS Nephropathy): Acute thrombotic microangiopathy (fibrin thrombi occluding glomerular capillaries and afferent arterioles) and chronic vascular lesions including fibrous intimal hyperplasia ('onion-skin' arteriopathy), focal cortical atrophy, and organized recanalized arterial thrombi
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal systemic autoimmune thrombophilia with unmistakable physical manifestations (livedo racemosa, atrophie blanche, digital gangrene), multi-system radiologic thrombi (Doppler DVT, CT pulmonary emboli, echocardiographic Libman-Sacks vegetations), and definitive histology of bland non-inflammatory vascular thrombosis.

Rheumatology.name: Antisynthetase Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: 'Mechanic's hands' and 'hiker's feet' (pathognomonic hallmark): rough, hyperkeratotic, hyperpigmented, fissured, and scaling erythema along the lateral and palmar surfaces of the fingers, thumbs, and soles of the feet, resembling the dirty cracked hands of manual laborers
Proximal symmetric muscle weakness: insidious or acute-onset weakness of deltoids, hip flexors, and neck flexors, with marked myalgias, muscle tenderness, and elevated serum creatine kinase

Symmetrical non-erosive polyarthritis: inflammatory arthritis involving small joints of the hands (metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints) and wrists, causing morning stiffness and boggy periarticular swelling
Constitutional symptoms and Raynaud phenomenon: recurrent unexplained spiking fevers, profound fatigue, involuntary weight loss, and cold-induced triphasic digital color changes
Dyspnea and dry cough: rapidly progressive or insidious exertion-limiting dyspnea resulting from acute or chronic interstitial pulmonary parenchymal involvement
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of the Chest (Primary Diagnostic Modality): Rapidly evolving organizing pneumonia (OP) pattern, non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) pattern, or mixed OP/NSIP overlap; key findings include peripheral and peribronchovascular consolidations, lower-lobe predominant ground-glass opacities, the 'reversed halo' or 'atoll' sign (central ground-glass surrounded by a crescentic or complete ring of consolidation), fine reticulation, and traction bronchiectasis

Pelvic Girdle and Thigh MRI: Short tau inversion recovery (STIR) and T2-weighted fat-suppressed sequences demonstrate intense, symmetrical, patchy or diffuse hyperintensity indicating active muscle edema (myositis) and prominent high-signal fluid cuffs along fascial planes (myofasciitis and perimuscular edema)

Plain Radiography of Hands and Wrists: Periarticular soft tissue swelling and juxta-articular demineralization; distinctive preservation of cortical bone margins without severe marginal erosions, occasionally demonstrating periarticular calcification
pathology_manifestations: Skeletal Muscle Biopsy: Distinctive perimysial pathology featuring prominent perimysial connective tissue fragmentation and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) positivity; inflammatory infiltrates (macrophages, CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells) primarily clustered in the perimysium with perifascicular myofiber necrosis, atrophy, and regeneration, characteristically lacking the primary endomysial capillary drop-out seen in dermatomyositis

Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgical (VATS) Lung Biopsy: Organizing pneumonia (intra-alveolar loose fibroblastic plugs known as Masson bodies within alveolar ducts and spaces) accompanied by interstitial lymphocytic infiltration and alveolar septal thickening (NSIP pattern)
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic autoimmune multi-organ syndrome combining the pathognomonic physical finding of 'mechanic's hands' with life-threatening interstitial lung disease readily visualized on chest HRCT (atoll sign, NSIP/OP overlap), muscle STIR MRI hyperintensity, and distinctive perimysial myofiber necrosis on biopsy.

Rheumatology.name: Behçet's Disease
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent painful oral aphthous stomatitis (round/oval punched-out ulcers with yellow necrotic base and red halo)
Recurrent painful genital aphthous ulcerations (scrotal, penile, vulvar scarring ulcers)
Pathergy reaction (pustule or papule formation 24-48 hours after sterile needle puncture of the skin)
Cutaneous lesions: erythema nodosum-like nodules, pseudofolliculitis, acneiform pustules
Ocular disease: acute hypopyon uveitis, panuveitis, retinal vasculitis with vitreous haze
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Brainstem/mesodiencephalic junction T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions extending to thalamus and basal ganglia in Neuro-Behçet; cerebral venous sinus thrombosis on MRV
Chest CT Angiography: Pulmonary artery aneurysms (pathognomonic vascular hallmark; saccular or fusiform), pulmonary thromboembolism, in situ pulmonary artery thrombosis
Abdominal/Peripheral Doppler & CT: Deep venous thrombosis (lower limbs, IVC thrombosis), peripheral arterial pseudoaneurysms
pathology_manifestations: Skin/mucosal biopsy: Neutrophilic vascular reaction, leukocytoclastic vasculitis of venules and arterioles with endothelial cell swelling, fibrinoid necrosis, and dense neutrophilic infiltrates without granulomas
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic presentation of oral/genital ulcers, hypopyon, and positive skin pathergy combined with diagnostic pulmonary artery aneurysms on chest CTA and brainstem lesions on MRI.

Rheumatology.name: Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition Disease
clinical_manifestations: Acute pseudogout arthritis: sudden onset of severe pain, warmth, erythema, and marked swelling of a single joint (most commonly the knee, wrist, shoulder, or ankle)
Chronic CPPD inflammatory polyarthritis mimicking rheumatoid arthritis (symmetric MCP and wrist swelling)
Severe joint degeneration mimicking destructive osteoarthritis with prominent crepitus and joint deformities
Crowned dens syndrome (severe acute neck pain and rigidity with fever)
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography: Chondrocalcinosis (thin, linear or punctate radiopaque calcifications within fibrocartilage, such as the knee menisci, triangular fibrocartilage complex [TFCC] of the wrist, and symphysis pubis, or hyaline cartilage)
Radiography of Hand/Wrist: Radiocarpal joint space narrowing, subchondral cyst formation, scaphoid-lunate dissociation
Cervical Spine CT: Calcification surrounding the odontoid process in crowned dens syndrome ('halo-like' calcification)
Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Hyperechoic punctate bands parallel to the bone contour within the hyaline cartilage layer, twinkling artifact on color Doppler
pathology_manifestations: Synovial fluid compensated polarized microscopy: Rhomboid-shaped or rod-shaped calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystals demonstrating weak positive birefringence (blue when parallel to the compensator axis, yellow when perpendicular)
Cartilage/synovial histology: Basophilic, granular microcrystalline deposits embedded within cartilage matrix surrounded by variable histiocytic and giant cell response
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield acute and chronic arthropathy featuring severe inflammatory joint swelling alongside hallmark radiographic chondrocalcinosis of knee menisci and TFCC on plain X-rays and crowned dens calcification on cervical CT.

Rheumatology.name: Cogan Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Ocular manifestations (interstitial keratitis): Sudden onset of bilateral eye pain, severe photophobia, lacrimation, blurred vision, and deep ciliary injection ('ciliary flush'); slit-lamp biomicroscopy reveals patchy, deep stromal corneal infiltrates, corneal stromal edema, and deep corneal neovascularization ('ghost vessels' in quiescent stages); atypical forms may present with episcleritis, scleritis, or anterior uveitis

Vestibuloauditory dysfunction: Abrupt, recurrent Ménière-like attacks with severe rotatory vertigo, ataxia, nausea, vomiting, and loud tinnitus, progressing rapidly within days to months to profound, irreversible bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (frequently resulting in total deafness)

Large- and medium-vessel vasculitis: Aortitis occurring in 10–15% of patients, presenting with severe substernal chest or back pain, high-pitched early diastolic murmur of aortic insufficiency, bounding pulses, widened pulse pressure, and acute heart failure from rapid aortic root dilation; upper-extremity pulse deficits, claudication, and carotid bruits
Systemic constitutional symptoms: Low-grade fever, weight loss, myalgias, arthralgias, and abdominal angina from mesenteric vasculitis
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Contrast-Enhanced Temporal Bone MRI (3D T1-weighted, 3D FLAIR, and 3D CISS/FIESTA): Pathognomonic intralabyrinthine findings: marked enhancement of the membranous labyrinth (cochlea, vestibule, and semicircular canals) on post-gadolinium T1-weighted images during active labyrinthitis; loss of normal high fluid signal intensity within the perilymphatic spaces on high-resolution T2/CISS sequences, reflecting fibro-osseous obliteration (labyrinthitis ossificans)

Contrast-Enhanced CT / MR Angiography of the Chest and Aorta: Concentric, smooth, circumferential wall thickening (>3 mm) with mural enhancement of the ascending aorta, aortic root, and aortic arch (aortitis); aneurysmal dilation of the aortic root and sinuses of Valsalva causing aortic valve annulus dilation and severe aortic regurgitation; ostial stenosis or occlusion of the coronary arteries, innominate, carotid, and subclavian arteries

Temporal Bone High-Resolution CT: Sclerosis and new bone formation within the basal turn of the cochlea, vestibule, and lateral semicircular canal (labyrinthitis ossificans) in advanced/chronic disease
Echocardiography: Marked dilation of the aortic valve annulus and ascending aorta with severe, eccentric, wide aortic regurgitation jet and valve cusp prolapse
pathology_manifestations: Corneal histopathology: Deep corneal stroma infiltrated by lymphocytes, plasma cells, and histiocytes with extensive neovascularization (ingrowth of capillaries into the substantia propria), destruction of collagen lamellae, focal degeneration of keratocytes, and wrinkling or breaks in Descemet's membrane without granuloma formation

Inner ear pathology: Severe endolymphatic hydrops, extensive degeneration and atrophy of the organ of Corti, marked loss of spiral ganglion neurons in the cochlea, atrophy of the stria vascularis, and proliferation of fibrous connective tissue and osteoid trabeculae completely obliterating the fluid-filled spaces of the labyrinth

Aortic and arterial histopathology: Transmural necrotizing or lymphoplasmacytic aortitis; dense infiltration of the adventitia and media by lymphocytes, macrophages, and plasma cells; prominent adventitial vasa vasorum proliferation; disruption and fragmentation of elastic fibers with focal medial necrosis and prominent reactive fibrous intimal hyperplasia; multinucleated giant cells may be scarce or absent (distinguishing from classic giant cell arteritis)
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Features the distinctive pairing of slit-lamp interstitial keratitis and vestibular ataxia with temporal bone MRI labyrinthitis enhancement, CTA aortitis with aortic root dilation, and transmural necrotizing aortitis pathology.

Rheumatology.name: Cryoglobulinemic Vasculitis
clinical_manifestations: Classic Meltzer triad: Recurrent palpable purpura, profound generalized fatigue (asthenia), and diffuse symmetric arthralgias/myalgias without chronic joint deformities

Palpable purpura: Recurrent crops of non-blanching, violaceous, palpable petechiae and purpuric macules/papules distributed symmetrically across gravity-dependent areas (predominantly lower extremities, ankles, pretibial regions, and buttocks), often precipitated by prolonged standing or cold exposure, which heal leaving residual brown hemosiderin hyperpigmentation
Cutaneous ischemia and chronic leg ulcers: Deep, punched-out, exquisitely painful malleolar and pretibial ulcers, digital cyanosis, Raynaud phenomenon, and acral gangrene

Peripheral neuropathy: Severe sensory or sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy, classically presenting as painful asymmetric mononeuritis multiplex (foot drop, wrist drop) or progressive distal symmetrical stocking-glove sensorimotor polyneuropathy with burning dysesthesias

Nephritic/Nephrotic features and systemic involvement: Hypertension, gross or microscopic hematuria, severe peripheral edema (nephrotic syndrome), low-grade fever, and postprandial abdominal angina resulting from mesenteric vasculitis
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasonography: Bilaterally enlarged or normal-sized kidneys with increased parenchymal cortical echogenicity and accentuated corticomedullary differentiation during acute cryoglobulinemic membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN); progressive cortical thinning, parenchymal atrophy, and loss of corticomedullary differentiation in chronic end-stage renal involvement

High-Resolution Chest CT (HRCT): Bilateral, multifocal, dependent ground-glass opacities, air-space consolidations, and interlobular septal thickening indicative of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) or pulmonary capillaritis; bibasilar reticular opacities, traction bronchiectasis, and architectural distortion in chronic cryoglobulinemia-associated interstitial lung disease

Lower Extremity Arterial Duplex Ultrasound and CT/MR Angiography: Segmental, smooth, non-atherosclerotic stenoses and abrupt occlusions of distal infrapopliteal, tibial, peroneal, and pedal arteries with prominent collateral vessel formation

Magnetic Resonance Neurography (MRN) / Brain MRI: T2/STIR hyperintensity, enlargement, and fascicular swelling of affected peripheral nerves (sciatic, tibial, common peroneal) in mononeuritis multiplex; brain MRI demonstrates punctate or confluent subcortical and deep white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities reflecting small-vessel cerebral ischemia or CNS vasculitis
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy: Classic leukocytoclastic vasculitis (LCV) affecting dermal postcapillary venules and small arterioles; transmural infiltration of vessel walls by polymorphonuclear neutrophils with prominent leukocytoclasia (karyorrhexis / neutrophilic nuclear dust), extensive fibrinoid necrosis of vessel walls, erythrocyte extravasation, and pathognomonic periodic acid–Schiff (PAS)-positive, eosinophilic intraluminal cryoglobulin precipitates and hyaline thrombi. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) demonstrates intense granular deposition of IgM, IgG, and C3 within and around dermal vessel walls

Renal biopsy: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN Type 1) pattern; marked endocapillary and mesangial hypercellularity with prominent monocyte/macrophage infiltration creating a lobular accentuation of glomerular tufts; characteristic duplication ('tram-tracking' or double contours) of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) on Jones silver methenamine stain; pathognomonic massive intraluminal PAS-positive, eosinophilic, Congo red-negative 'pseudothrombi' (crystallized cryoglobulin immune complexes) occluding glomerular capillary loops; electron microscopy demonstrates diagnostic organized microtubular, curved tubular, or fibrillar subendothelial electron-dense immune deposits (10–30 nm diameter)
Sural nerve biopsy: Axonal degeneration with perivascular inflammatory cuffs around epineurial arterioles and transmural necrotizing vasculitis of the vasa nervorum
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Features the hallmark Meltzer triad with dependent palpable purpura and ischemic malleolar ulcers, paired with renal US of MPGN, HRCT findings of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, and pathognomonic PAS-positive cryoglobulin thrombi on renal and skin pathology.

Rheumatology.name: Cryopyrin-Associated Periodic Syndromes (CAPS / NOMID)
synonyms: chronic infantile neurological cutaneous and articular syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous eruption: Persistent or recurrent, non-pruritic, migratory, maculopapular or urticaria-like erythematous rash present continuously from birth or early infancy, characteristically worsening with cold exposure or evening fatigue, without true wheals or angioedema

Dysmorphic facial and cranial features: Striking macrocephaly, prominent frontal bossing, flattened nasal bridge (saddle-nose deformity), protruding eyes with hypertelorism, and delayed anterior fontanelle closure

Severe articular deformities and patellar overgrowth: Gross, grotesque, painless or painful symmetrical joint enlargement predominantly involving the knees, with massive, palpable, bony-hard enlargement of the patellae and distal femoral/proximal tibial metaphyses, resulting in severe flexion contractures, knock-knees (genu valgum), and short-limbed dwarfism

Neurological impairment: Chronic aseptic meningitis presenting with persistent headache, vomiting, progressive bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, bilateral optic disc edema (chronic papilledema evolving to optic atrophy and blindness), and developmental delay

Chronic systemic inflammation: Unremitting low-grade fevers, marked elevations of acute phase reactants (ESR, CRP, serum amyloid A), hepatosplenomegaly, and high risk of secondary systemic AA amyloidosis
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography of the Knees and Long Bones (Pathognomonic hallmark in NOMID/CINCA): Massive, bizarre, irregular cartilaginous overgrowth and premature, disorganized endochondral ossification of the patella ('giant patella'); severe epiphyseal and metaphyseal flaring with marked radiolucency, irregular calcified specks, and coarse trabeculation resembling intra-articular tumors; accelerated bone maturation with premature epiphyseal fusion leading to limb shortening

Brain and Spine MRI (T2/FLAIR and post-gadolinium T1): Chronic, diffuse leptomeningeal thickening and prominent enhancement over the cerebral convexities, basal cisterns, and spinal cord; progressive communicating ventriculomegaly / hydrocephalus; generalized cerebral and cerebellar cortical atrophy; retrobulbar optic nerve sheath dilation and enhancement

Temporal Bone CT / MRI: High-resolution CT demonstrates cochlear dysplasia and sclerosis; MRI demonstrates labyrinthine fluid attenuation and cochlear post-contrast enhancement reflecting chronic labyrinthine inflammation
Plain Radiography of Skull: Thickened calvarium, wide cranial sutures, prominent frontal bossing, and basilar invagination
pathology_manifestations: Bone and Epiphyseal Cartilage Biopsy: Disorganized endochondral ossification characterized by massive, chaotic proliferation of chondrocytes with loss of the normal columnar cartilage architecture; extensive irregular vascular invasion, abnormal matrix calcification, and patchy areas of osteonecrosis without neoplastic cells; confirmation via genetic sequencing demonstrating gain-of-function missense mutations in the NLRP3 (CIAS1) gene on chromosome 1q44 encoding cryopyrin

Skin punch biopsy: Non-specific perivascular and interstitial inflammatory infiltrate in the upper and mid-dermis composed predominantly of polymorphonuclear neutrophils, with absence of mast cell degranulation, dermal eosinophilia, or true leukocytoclastic vasculitis (pseudourticarial neutrophilic dermatosis)
Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis: Chronic sterile neutrophilic and lymphocytic pleocytosis (10–100 WBCs/μL), markedly elevated CSF opening pressure, and elevated total protein
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Pediatric autoinflammatory disorder exhibiting the triad of neonatal pseudo-urticaria, frontal bossing with saddle-nose, and pathognomonic massive patellar/epiphyseal overgrowth on knee radiographs, alongside diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement on brain MRI.

Rheumatology.name: Dermatomyositis
clinical_manifestations: Heliotrope rash: violaceous periorbital erythema often accompanied by periorbital edema
Gottron papules: violaceous or erythematous papules and plaques over the dorsal MCP and IP joints
Gottron sign: macular violaceous erythema over elbows, knees, or medial malleoli
V-sign rash: macular violaceous erythema over the anterior neck and upper chest
Shawl sign: confluent violaceous poikiloderma across posterior shoulders, upper back, and neck
Mechanic's hands: hyperkeratotic fissuring and scaling along the radial aspects of digits
Holster sign: poikiloderma over the lateral thighs
Calcinosis cutis (common in juvenile dermatomyositis)
radiological_manifestations: Proximal Muscle MRI (Thigh/Pelvis): Symmetrical muscle and fascial edema with bright STIR/T2-FS hyperintensity in active myositis; T1 muscle atrophy and fatty replacement in chronic disease
Chest HRCT: Rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease in anti-MDA5 DM; organizing pneumonia (OP) or NSIP patterns with bilateral basal ground-glass and consolidations
Soft Tissue Radiographs/CT: Extensive subcutaneous, fascial, and intermuscular sheet-like calcifications (calcinosis universalis) in juvenile DM
pathology_manifestations: Muscle biopsy: Perifascicular atrophy (selective atrophy of muscle fibers at the periphery of fascicles), microinfarcts, perivascular and perimysial inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of CD4+ T cells and B cells; endothelial tubuloreticular inclusions; MAC (C5b-9) deposition on endomysial capillaries
Skin punch biopsy: Vacuolar interface dermatitis, subepidermal edema, necrotic basal keratinocytes, abundant dermal mucin
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Contains quintessential dermatologic hallmarks (heliotrope rash, Gottron papules, shawl sign) paired with prominent STIR muscle edema on MRI and calcinosis on soft-tissue imaging.

Rheumatology.name: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
clinical_manifestations: Acute to subacute symmetric woody induration, thickening, and non-pitting edema of the extremities (forearms, calves, thighs, arms), typically beginning following strenuous physical exertion and strictly sparing the digits, face, and acral areas

'Groove sign' (pathognomonic clinical sign): linear subcutaneous depression or guttering along the anatomic course of superficial superficial veins (such as cephalic or basilic veins), prominently accentuated upon arm elevation due to adherence of fibrosed deep fascia to overlying skin while veins collapse
'Peau d'orange' cutaneous appearance: coarse puckering, dimpling, and follicular prominence of the skin overlying the indurated fascia, giving the skin the appearance of an orange peel

Severe flexion contractures: rapid development of flexion contractures across the elbows, wrists, knees, and ankles due to fascial fibrosis, resulting in the inability to flatten the palms together ('prayer sign' positivity)
Marked peripheral blood hypereosinophilia and hypergammaglobulinemia during the acute inflammatory phase
radiological_manifestations: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of Affected Limbs (Gold Standard Imaging Modality): T2-weighted fat-saturated and Short Tau Inversion Recovery (STIR) sequences demonstrate marked, symmetrical or asymmetrical thickening and intense hyperintensity of the deep muscular fascia and superficial fascial layers; T1-weighted post-gadolinium sequences show intense fascial contrast enhancement; the underlying muscle parenchyma and superficial dermis are characteristically spared

High-Frequency Musculoskeletal Ultrasonography: Marked hyperechoic thickening of the deep muscular fascia (often measuring 2-4 times normal reference thickness), with loss of the normal thin, fibrillar fascial architecture, fascial blurring, and fluid tracking along the myofascial interface
pathology_manifestations: Full-Thickness En Bloc Skin-to-Muscle Incisional Biopsy (Pathognomonic Gold Standard): Markedly thickened deep fascia (often up to 10 to 20 times normal thickness, measuring several millimeters) comprising dense, packed collagen bundles; dense inflammatory infiltrate within the deep fascia, epimysium, and lower subcutis consisting of lymphocytes, plasma cells, histiocytes, and numerous eosinophils (prominent in early acute stages); marked sclerosis and hyalinization of fascial connective tissue with progressive entrapment of adipocytes; characteristic absence of primary epidermal or upper dermal sclerosis (distinguishing EF from systemic sclerosis)
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Unmistakable deep fibrosing autoimmune entity exhibiting the pathognomonic 'groove sign' and woody extremity induration on physical exam, striking fascial STIR hyperintensity and thickening on limb MRI, and dramatic fascial eosinophilic sclerosis on full-thickness biopsy.

Rheumatology.name: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis
clinical_manifestations: Palpable purpura and petechiae predominantly on lower extremities
Subcutaneous tender nodules (especially on scalp and limbs)
Nasal polyposis and allergic fungal-like rhinosinusitis
Mononeuritis multiplex (asymmetric foot drop or wrist drop)
Urticarial or erythematous maculopapular eruptions
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT: Transient, non-segmental, migratory patchy ground-glass opacities and consolidations with peripheral/subpleural predominance; bronchial wall thickening, centrilobular nodules, interlobular septal thickening
Cardiac MRI: Subendocardial or transmural late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) representing eosinophilic myocarditis or myocardial fibrosis, biventricular thrombi
Paranasal Sinus CT: Pansinusitis with extensive polypoid soft-tissue thickening
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy: Dense tissue eosinophilic infiltration, necrotizing vasculitis of small vessels, and extravascular necrotizing eosinophilic granulomas with central core of necrotic eosinophils surrounded by histiocytes
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Features cutaneous palpable purpura, subcutaneous nodules, and nasal polyps alongside distinctive migratory pulmonary infiltrates on chest CT and eosinophilic myocarditis on cardiac MRI.

Rheumatology.name: Familial Mediterranean Fever
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent, self-limited febrile attacks: High fever (38–40°C) lasting 12 to 72 hours, recurring irregularly and resolving spontaneously

Erysipelas-like erythema (ELE): Highly characteristic, warm, tender, well-demarcated, raised erythematous plaque (10–15 cm in diameter) classically located over the lower leg, ankle, or dorsum of the foot, accompanied by marked local non-pitting edema

Acute sterile peritonitis: Severe, diffuse abdominal pain with board-like muscular rigidity, guarding, absent bowel sounds, and rebound tenderness mimicking an acute surgical abdomen, often leading to negative exploratory laparotomies
Acute sterile pleuritis: Sudden unilateral, sharp pleuritic chest pain, shallow tachypnea, pleural friction rub, and transient pleural effusion

Acute monoarthritis: Abrupt, severe inflammatory arthritis predominantly affecting a single large lower-extremity joint (knee, ankle, or hip), with hot, red, tense joint effusion preventing weight-bearing
Acute scrotal attacks: Unilateral, excruciating scrotal pain and erythema from acute sterile inflammation of the tunica vaginalis (acute periorchitis) in young boys
Systemic AA Amyloidosis (late/untreated complication): Massive proteinuria progressing to nephrotic syndrome (anasarca, periorbital edema, ascites) and end-stage renal disease
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound and CT (during acute attack): Moderate-to-large volume free peritoneal fluid (ascites) in the pelvis and Morrison pouch; diffuse peritoneal thickening and contrast enhancement; transient segmental small-bowel wall thickening (mural edema); reactive mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy; absence of appendiceal dilation or surgical pathology

Chest Radiography and CT: Small-to-moderate unilateral pleural effusion (characteristically resolving completely within 48–72 hours post-attack); basilar compressive atelectasis; transient pericardial effusion

Musculoskeletal Ultrasound and MRI: Large joint effusion with pronounced synovial thickening and hypervascularity on Power Doppler during attacks, which resolves without erosive destruction; absence of pannus or permanent cartilage loss

Renal Ultrasound (in AA amyloidosis): Bilaterally enlarged, smoothly contoured, hyperechoic kidneys with loss of corticomedullary differentiation during the nephrotic phase, progressing to shrunken, echogenic, atrophic kidneys in end-stage renal disease
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy of Erysipelas-Like Erythema: Massive edema of the papillary and upper reticular dermis; dense perivascular and interstitial inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of mature neutrophils and histiocytes; prominent leukocytoclasia (nuclear debris) but absence of true fibrinoid necrosis of blood vessel walls (differentiating ELE from true leukocytoclastic vasculitis)

Peritoneal and pleural serosal histopathology: Intense acute serositis characterized by hyperemic dilated capillaries, superficial fibrin exudate, and massive transmural infiltration of the serosal mesothelium by polymorphonuclear leukocytes without granulomas or microbial growth

Renal / Rectal biopsy (AA Amyloidosis): Extracellular amorphous, eosinophilic, hyaline deposits expanding the mesangium, capillary walls, and interlobular arterioles; pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light microscopy following Congo red staining; strong immunohistochemical reactivity for Serum Amyloid A (SAA) protein; loss of Congo red affinity following potassium permanganate incubation (pre-treatment sensitivity test distinguishing secondary AA amyloid from AL amyloid)
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Exhibits hallmark erysipelas-like erythema over the dorsum of the foot alongside board-like abdominal peritonitis, confirmed by CT/US ascites and peritoneal thickening during attacks, and Congo red-positive AA amyloidosis.

Rheumatology.name: Giant Cell Arteritis
clinical_manifestations: Prominent, nodular, tender, tortuous, thickened, and pulseless superficial temporal artery
Scalp necrosis and ulceration (ischaemic complication)
Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (AION) on fundoscopy: chalky-white swollen optic disc with splinter hemorrhages
Tongue claudication, tongue infarction/necrosis
Jaw claudication during mastication
radiological_manifestations: Temporal and Axillary Artery Color Doppler Ultrasound: 'Halo sign' (hypoechoic, non-compressible vessel wall thickening surrounding the lumen), 'compression sign' (vessel wall remains visible upon probe pressure)
CTA / MRA of Aorta and Neck Vessels: Concentric mural thickening, wall enhancement, luminal stenosis, or aneurysmal dilation of the thoracic aorta and its major branches (subclavian, axillary)
18F-FDG PET/CT: Linear, smooth, circumferential increased metabolic uptake along the thoracic aorta, subclavian, axillary, and carotid arteries
pathology_manifestations: Temporal artery biopsy: Transmural granulomatous inflammation of the arterial wall with disruption/fragmentation of the internal elastic lamina (Verhoeff-Van Gieson stain), infiltration by CD4+ T lymphocytes, macrophages, and multi-nucleated foreign-body or Langhans giant cells; intimal hyperplasia
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Presents striking superficial temporal artery tortuosity, scalp necrosis, and ischemic fundoscopy findings paired with the pathognomonic ultrasound 'halo sign' and large-vessel FDG-PET/CTA aortitis.

Rheumatology.name: Gout
clinical_manifestations: Podagra: acute, exquisite, intensely erythematous and warm monoarticular swelling of the first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint
Subcutaneous tophi: firm, nodular, non-tender, chalky-yellow or white monosodium urate deposits on the helix of the ear, olecranon bursa, prepatellar bursa, Achilles tendon, and digit joints
Ulcerated tophi with extrusion of paste-like or chalky white urate material
Acute monoarthritis of the ankle, knee, or wrist
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiographs: Punched-out juxta-articular bony erosions with sclerotic margins and overhanging edges ('rat-bite' or 'Martel sign'), preservation of joint space until late, eccentric soft tissue topheaceous masses
Dual-Energy CT (DECT): Color-coded identification and 3D volumetric mapping of monosodium urate (MSU) crystal deposits around articular and periarticular structures (typically displayed in green)

Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: 'Double-contour sign' (hyperechoic line on the superficial margin of hyaline cartilage created by crystal deposition), tophi (heterogeneous hyperechoic masses with anechoic halo), acoustic shadowing
pathology_manifestations: Synovial fluid polarized light microscopy: Strongly negatively birefringent, needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals (bright yellow when parallel to the slow axis of the red compensator, blue when perpendicular)
Tophi histology: Amorphous or crystalline urate cores surrounded by a granulomatous foreign-body reaction comprising multi-nucleated giant cells, histiocytes, and fibroblasts
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential crystal arthropathy featuring unmistakable bedside findings (podagra, ulcerated chalky tophi) alongside definitive DECT color mapping, ultrasound double-contour signs, and plain-film rat-bite erosions.

Rheumatology.name: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis
clinical_manifestations: Saddle nose deformity (collapse of the nasal bridge from cartilage chondritis)
Strawberry gingivitis (hyperplastic, granular, erythematous gingival enlargement with petechial hemorrhages)
Orbital pseudotumor causing unilateral or bilateral proptosis, ptosis, and diplopia
Palpable purpura, pyoderma gangrenosum-like necrotic ulcers, and digital gangrene
Severe nasal crusting, epistaxis, and nasal septal perforation
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT: Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and masses, frequently with central cavitation (thick, irregular walls), patchy ground-glass opacities representing alveolar hemorrhage, subglottic tracheal stenosis
Facial/Sinus CT: Mucosal opacification, destruction of nasal turbinates, nasal septal erosion, bony remodeling, sinus osteoneogenesis
Orbit CT/MRI: Infiltrative soft-tissue mass in the retro-orbital space (pseudotumor) encasing the optic nerve and extraocular muscles
pathology_manifestations: Tissue biopsy (lung, sinus, or skin): Triad of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, geographic basophilic necrosis, and necrotizing leukocytoclastic vasculitis of small to medium vessels; multi-nucleated giant cells
Renal biopsy: Pauci-immune crescentic necrotizing glomerulonephritis
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Features iconic facial physical signs (saddle nose, strawberry gingivitis, proptosis) alongside classic radiologic cavitary pulmonary nodules and destructive sinus lesions on CT.

Rheumatology.name: IgA Vasculitis
clinical_manifestations: Palpable, non-thrombocytopenic purpura and petechiae distributed symmetrically over the buttocks, lower extremities, and extensor surfaces
Targetoid or bullous hemorrhagic lesions (in severe pediatric cases)
Subcutaneous dependent non-pitting edema (dorsum of hands, feet, periorbital, scrotum)
Oligoarticular inflammatory periarthritis of knees and ankles without joint destruction
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Concentric small bowel wall thickening (jejunum/ileum), intramural hematoma, prominent mesenteric lymphadenopathy, 'target sign' or 'doughnut sign' of ileoileal or ileocolic intussusception
Joint Ultrasound: Periarticular soft tissue swelling and small sterile joint effusions
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis of dermal post-capillary venules with neutrophilic infiltration, nuclear dusting (leukocytoclasia), and extravasated red blood cells
Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Predominant granular vascular wall deposition of IgA and C3 within superficial dermal vessels
Renal biopsy: Mesangial proliferative glomerulonephritis with strong mesangial IgA and C3 deposition
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinguished by dependent palpable purpura and buttocks rash in concert with bowel wall hematoma and intussusception ('target sign') on abdominal ultrasound and CT.

Rheumatology.name: IgG4-Related Disease
clinical_manifestations: Mikulicz disease (lacrimal and salivary tumefaction): bilateral, indolent, painless, symmetrical, firm and rubbery enlargement of lacrimal glands causing characteristic 'S-shaped' ptosis of the upper eyelids, and massive enlargement of the submandibular and parotid glands
Riedel thyroiditis: extremely hard, 'stony' or 'woody', non-tender, fixed thyroid goiter extending into adjacent cervical soft tissues, causing compressive dysphagia, stridor, and hoarseness

Orbital pseudotumor: unilateral or bilateral retro-orbital fibroinflammatory masses producing painless progressive proptosis, diplopia, extraocular muscle restriction, and compressive optic neuropathy

Abdominal and systemic mass effects: painless obstructive jaundice, dark urine, and acholic stools from autoimmune pancreatitis; flank pain and lower extremity edema from ureteral encasement in retroperitoneal fibrosis
Cutaneous lesions: indurated, erythematous to violaceous plaques or prurigo-like nodules distributed on the head, neck, and upper chest
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT and MRI of Abdomen (Autoimmune Pancreatitis Type 1): Diffuse, featureless 'sausage-shaped' enlargement of the pancreas with loss of the normal lobular clefts; characteristic peripheral hypoattenuating and hypointense rim ('capsule-like halo'); delayed, homogeneous parenchymal enhancement; Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) reveals diffuse, irregular narrowing of the main pancreatic duct without marked upstream dilatation

Abdominal / Pelvic CT and MRI (Retroperitoneal Fibrosis / Ormond Disease): Well-circumscribed, confluent soft-tissue mantle/mass encasing the anterior and lateral aspects of the infrarenal abdominal aorta and common iliac arteries; characteristically draws the ureters medially causing bilateral hydronephrosis; preserves the posterior aortic fat plane and does not displace the aorta anteriorly (crucial differential from retroperitoneal lymphoma)

Contrast-Enhanced Orbit and Neck MRI: Bilateral, symmetrical enlargement and intense enhancement of lacrimal glands, submandibular glands, and extraocular muscles (predominantly lateral rectus and levator palpebrae, with characteristic involvement of muscle bellies while sparing the tendinous insertions)

Chest CT: Peribronchovascular and interlobular septal interstitial thickening, mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy, paravertebral band-like soft-tissue masses, and central circumferential aortic wall thickening (periaortitis)
pathology_manifestations: Tissue Core or Incisional Biopsy (Consensus Diagnostic Criteria Triad): 1. Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate composed of abundant polyclonal plasma cells and small mature lymphocytes arranged in expansive sheets; 2. Storiform fibrosis: unique whirling, cartwheel, or woven-straw pattern of collagen bundles intermingled with proliferating spindle-shaped myofibroblasts; 3. Obliterative phlebitis: luminal obliteration and stenosis of medium and small venous channels caused by transmural infiltration of lymphoplasmacytic cells and collagen deposition, demonstrated by elastin Van Gieson stain
Immunohistochemistry: Marked abundance of IgG4-bearing plasma cells (>10-50 IgG4+ cells per high-power field, depending on the tissue source) and an IgG4-to-IgG positive plasma cell ratio >40%
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Multi-organ fibroinflammatory master-mimicker with unmistakable clinical mass lesions (Mikulicz dacryoadenitis, woody goiter), pathognomonic imaging signs ('sausage pancreas', periaortic mantle in retroperitoneal fibrosis), and consensus histopathologic triad (storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis, IgG4+ plasma cells >40%).

Rheumatology.name: Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy
clinical_manifestations: Acute or subacute, severe, symmetric proximal muscle weakness: profound weakness of the pelvic and shoulder girdle muscles (hip abductors, neck flexors, deltoids) developing over weeks to months, causing severe impairment in walking, stair climbing, and arm elevation
Severe muscle tenderness and progressive limb-girdle muscle wasting with loss of muscle bulk
Extremely high serum creatine kinase (CK) elevation: massive hyper-CK-emia, typically ranging from 10 to 50 times the upper limit of normal (often exceeding 10,000-20,000 IU/L)
Axial and bulbar involvement: 'dropped head syndrome' from severe neck extensor weakness, paraspinal muscle weakness causing camptocormia, and oropharyngeal dysphagia

Subtype-specific associations: history of statin exposure (in anti-HMG-CoA reductase [anti-HMGCR] myopathy, persisting after statin withdrawal) or severe aggressive disease with cardiac involvement and malignancy association (in anti-signal recognition particle [anti-SRP] myopathy)
radiological_manifestations: Whole-Body / Pelvic-Thigh Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): STIR and T2-weighted turbo inversion recovery magnitude (TIRM) sequences demonstrate massive, extensive, symmetrical, high-signal intensity (myoedema) throughout the gluteal muscles, thigh adductors, quadriceps, and hamstrings, directly reflecting widespread acute myofiber necrosis; T1-weighted sequences demonstrate early and rapid progression of confluent fatty infiltration, muscle atrophy, and architectural disruption if untreated; perimuscular fascial hyperintensity and fluid tracking without the extensive cutaneous/subcutaneous reticular panniculitis seen in dermatomyositis

Musculoskeletal Ultrasonography: Marked diffuse increased muscle echogenicity with complete loss of the normal architectural fibrillar pattern and acoustic shadowing of underlying bony acoustic interfaces
pathology_manifestations: Skeletal Muscle Biopsy (Pathognomonic Histopathologic Hallmark): Abundant, widespread, randomly distributed myofiber necrosis and vigorous myophagocytosis (macrophages engulfing necrotic fibers) accompanied by brisk myofiber regeneration (small basophilic fibers with enlarged, prominent vesicular nuclei); marked paucity or absence of primary lymphocytic infiltrates within the endomysium and perimysium, which definitively differentiates IMNM from polymyositis, inclusion body myositis, and classic dermatomyositis

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse and intense sarcolemmal expression of MHC Class I (HLA-ABC) on both non-necrotic and necrotic myofibers; sarcolemmal and endomysial capillary deposition of the complement membrane attack complex (MAC / C5b-9) with capillary enlargement and pipestem appearance
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive severe autoimmune myopathy characterized by massive CK elevations and disabling proximal weakness, extensive bilateral muscle edema on STIR MRI, and the definitive biopsy hallmark of prominent myofiber necrosis with pauci-immune lymphocytic infiltration and sarcolemmal MAC deposition.

Rheumatology.name: Juvenile Dermatomyositis
clinical_manifestations: Heliotrope rash: violaceous, purplish-red erythema and periorbital edema involving the upper eyelids and surrounding periorbital tissue, often accompanied by malar erythema

Gottron papules and Gottron sign: erythematous to violaceous lichenoid papules and plaques over the dorsal surface of the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints, and macules over extensor surfaces of elbows, knees, and medial malleoli

Calcinosis cutis et subsaliva (calcinosis universalis): rock-hard, chalky subcutaneous and fascial nodules, plaques, and extensive sheets of dystrophic calcium hydroxyapatite deposits that can ulcerate through the skin and extrude chalk-like material

Cutaneous ulcerations and vasculopathy: deep, punched-out ischemic ulcers over extensor joints, digital pulp necrosis, and dilated, tortuous nailfold capillary loops with bush-like arborization and avascular dropout areas on capillaroscopy

Gowers sign and proximal muscle weakness: symmetric, progressive proximal limb-girdle weakness (difficulty climbing stairs, rising from floor using hand-on-thigh maneuver [Gowers sign], and neck flexor weakness)
radiological_manifestations: Whole-Body / Thigh Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): T2-weighted fat-suppressed and STIR sequences reveal diffuse, symmetrical, intense high signal intensity (edema) involving proximal muscles (myositis), subcutaneous adipose tissues (panniculitis), and fascial envelopes (fasciitis); T1-weighted sequences delineate muscle atrophy and fatty replacement in chronic disease

Plain Radiography of Extremities and Trunk: Spectacular, extensive, sheet-like or tumor-like subcutaneous, fascial, and intermuscular radiopaque calcifications (calcinosis universalis) tracking along fascial planes and tendons
Barium Videofluoroscopy Swallow Examination: Oropharyngeal and upper esophageal dysmotility, pooling of contrast in pyriform sinuses, nasal regurgitation, and cricopharyngeal dysfunction
pathology_manifestations: Skeletal Muscle Biopsy (Pathognomonic Microvascular Hallmarks): Perifascicular atrophy (striking atrophy, degeneration, and regeneration of myofibers located at the periphery of the muscle fascicles); perivascular and perimysial inflammatory infiltrates (collections of CD4+ T-lymphocytes, B-lymphocytes, and plasmacytoid dendritic cells predominantly clustered around blood vessels and within the perimysium); endothelial microangiopathy (severe loss of endomysial capillaries, endothelial cell swelling, capillary thrombosis, and tubuloreticular inclusions within endothelial cells seen on transmission electron microscopy)

Immunohistochemistry: Robust deposition of the complement membrane attack complex (C5b-9) in the walls of intramuscular arterioles and capillaries, with overexpression of MHC Class I on perifascicular myofibers
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Pediatric autoimmune vascular-myopathic disorder showcasing hallmark heliotrope rash, Gottron papules, and dramatic calcinosis cutis on physical exam, striking plain radiograph sheet-like calcinosis universalis, and pathognomonic muscle biopsy perifascicular atrophy with microvascular MAC deposition.

Rheumatology.name: Microscopic Polyangiitis
clinical_manifestations: Palpable purpura and petechial eruptions on dependent lower limbs
Splinter hemorrhages of nailbeds, digital infarcts, and cutaneous ulcerations
Livedo reticularis / livedo racemosa
Hemoptysis and acute respiratory distress in pulmonary-renal syndrome
radiological_manifestations: Chest HRCT: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage with bilateral patchy or confluent ground-glass opacities and consolidation, interlobular septal thickening; fibrotic changes in chronic MPA (subpleural reticulation, traction bronchiectasis)
Abdominal/Renal Ultrasound: Normal-sized to enlarged echogenic kidneys in acute rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis
pathology_manifestations: Renal biopsy: Pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis with fibrinoid necrosis of capillary loops, absent or minimal immune complex deposition on immunofluorescence
Skin/lung biopsy: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis of post-capillary venules and small arterioles; neutrophilic capillaritis with alveolar hemorrhage and hemosiderin-laden macrophages without granulomas
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Combines prominent dermatologic vasculitic purpura and digital infarcts with life-threatening diffuse alveolar hemorrhage seen as bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest HRCT.

Rheumatology.name: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
synonyms: overlap connective tissue disease with high anti-U1-RNP
clinical_manifestations: 'Puffy hands' and sausage digits: diffuse, symmetrical, non-pitting tumefaction of the fingers and dorsum of hands that softens over time or evolves into mild sclerodactyly, preserving deep skin wrinkles initially

Severe Raynaud phenomenon: triphasic digital color changes (pallor, cyanosis, erythema) triggered by cold or emotional stress, frequently resulting in painful ischemic digital pulp ulcerations and pitted scars
Overlap cutaneous features: classic SLE-like malar erythema, photosensitive maculopapular rash, non-scarring alopecia, periungual erythema, telangiectasias, and cutaneous calcinosis

Inflammatory polyarthritis: symmetrical polyarticular hand arthritis with reducible joint deformities without significant bone erosion (Jaccoud-type arthropathy: ulnar deviation, swan-neck, and boutonnière deformities)
Proximal muscle weakness and myalgia: symmetric weakness of shoulder and pelvic girdle musculature reflecting an inflammatory myositis component
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of the Chest: Non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) pattern characterized by lower-lobe predominant ground-glass opacities, fine reticulation, and traction bronchiectasis with characteristic subpleural sparing; accompanying patulous, dilated thoracic esophagus (>10 mm luminal diameter) with air-fluid level reflecting esophageal dysmotility
