Transthoracic Echocardiography & Right Heart Catheterization (Evaluation of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension [PAH]): Right ventricular hypertrophy and dilatation, flattening or paradoxical motion of the interventricular septum, tricuspid regurgitation jet velocity >3.4 m/s, and right heart catheterization demonstrating mean pulmonary arterial pressure >20 mmHg with pulmonary vascular resistance >2 Wood units

Hand and Wrist Radiographs: Symmetrical soft tissue swelling of digits ('spindle digits'), periarticular osteopenia, distal phalangeal acro-osteolysis (resorption of the terminal digital tufts), soft tissue calcinosis, and non-erosive reducible joint subluxations

Barium Esophagogram: Markedly reduced or absent peristalsis in the smooth muscle portion (distal two-thirds) of the esophagus, dilated esophageal lumen, and open lower esophageal sphincter with free gastroesophageal reflux
pathology_manifestations: Nailfold Videocapillaroscopy: Classic 'scleroderma pattern' consisting of megacapillaries (giant dilated loops >50 um), microhemorrhages, capillary thrombosis, and focal avascular dropout areas

Skeletal Muscle Biopsy: Mixed myopathic changes combining perivascular and endomysial lymphocytic infiltrates, sporadic myofiber necrosis and regeneration, with perimysial connective tissue proliferation

Surgical Lung / Autopsy Pathology: Plexogenic pulmonary arteriopathy (concentric laminar intimal hyperplasia, medial hypertrophy, adventitial fibrosis, and plexiform lesions in small muscular pulmonary arteries) characteristic of severe pulmonary arterial hypertension, alongside interstitial lymphocytic infiltrates and collagen deposition
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct overlap autoimmune syndrome defined by high-titer anti-U1-RNP antibodies, pathognomonic physical exam features ('puffy sausage fingers', Raynaud scars), multi-organ imaging (HRCT fibrosing NSIP, patulous esophagus, echocardiographic PAH), and distinctive nailfold capillaroscopic patterns.

Rheumatology.name: Pachydermoperiostosis (Primary Hypertrophic Osteoarthropathy)
clinical_manifestations: Pachydermia: coarse, thickened, furrowed skin of the face and forehead ('leonine facies'), cutis verticis gyrata (thick cerebriform corrugated folds and furrows of the scalp), and severe ptosis caused by thickened eyelids (blepharoptosis)

Prominent digital clubbing: bilateral, symmetrical, severe bulbous clubbing of all fingers and toes ('drumstick fingers') with exaggerated curvature of nail plates ('watch-glass nails') and periungual erythema

Cylindrical limb enlargement and joint effusion: symmetrical 'tree-trunk' or 'columnar' thickening of distal legs, ankles, and forearms caused by subcutaneous edema and periostosis, accompanied by large non-inflammatory knee and ankle joint effusions
Seborrhea and palmoplantar hyperhidrosis: greasy skin, acne, seborrheic dermatitis, and profuse autonomic sweating of palms and soles
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography of Long Bones: Symmetrical, bilateral, irregular or smooth periosteal hyperostosis and cortical thickening along the diaphyses and metaphyses of tubular bones (radius, ulna, tibia, fibula, metacarpals, and proximal phalanges), with pathognomonic preservation and sparing of the epiphyses
Hand Radiographs: Severe soft tissue swelling of distal phalanges (clubbing), subperiosteal new bone formation along shafts of metacarpals and phalanges, and distal phalangeal tuft acro-osteolysis

Radionuclide 99mTc-Methylene Diphosphonate (MDP) Bone Scintigraphy: Symmetrical, diffuse, intense cortical tracer uptake ('double stripe' or 'parallel track' sign) along the periosteal margins of long tubular bones

Musculoskeletal MRI: Extensive periosteal thickening with intermediate-to-low signal on T1 and T2, high-signal subperiosteal and adjacent soft tissue edema on STIR, and prominent non-destructive joint effusions without synovial pannus
pathology_manifestations: Bone and Periosteal Histopathology: Dramatic subperiosteal new bone formation with active osteoblastic proliferation, marked cortical thickening, progressive incorporation of periosteal bone into cortex, and hypervascularity with fibrous tissue proliferation in the cambium layer of the periosteum

Skin Biopsy (Scalp/Face): Dermal hypertrophy characterized by marked accumulation of densely packed, thickened collagen fibers, abundant interstitial mucin (Alcian blue positive), prominent hypertrophy and hyperplasia of sebaceous glands and eccrine sweat glands, and mild perivascular lymphocytic infiltrates
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Spectacular multi-system osteo-dermato-rheumatologic disorder featuring cutis verticis gyrata and drumstick clubbing on physical exam, the pathognomonic symmetrical diaphyseal periostosis ('parallel track' sign) on skeletal imaging, and robust subperiosteal bone deposition on histology.

Rheumatology.name: Polyarteritis Nodosa
clinical_manifestations: Subcutaneous erythematous tender nodules along the course of medium arteries (lower limbs)
Livedo reticularis / livedo racemosa (violaceous net-like pattern)
Digital ischemia, ulceration, and peripheral acral gangrene
Mononeuritis multiplex (asymmetric peripheral neuropathy: wrist drop, foot drop)
Testicular pain, tenderness, and swelling
radiological_manifestations: Mesenteric and Renal Catheter Angiography / CTA: Multiple small saccular or fusiform microaneurysms (2-5 mm) in visceral arteries with alternating segmental stenoses ('string of beads' or 'beaded necklace' appearance)
Renal Doppler Ultrasound: Wedge-shaped cortical perfusion defects representing renal microinfarctions
Testicular Ultrasound: Heterogeneous testicular echotexture with focal ischemic hypoechoic areas
pathology_manifestations: Arterial biopsy (skin nodule, sural nerve, or testicle): Focal, segmental, transmural necrotizing inflammation of medium- or small-sized muscular arteries with fibrinoid necrosis of the vessel media, disruption of the internal elastic lamina, and neutrophilic/mononuclear infiltrate; absence of granulomas
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield medium-vessel vasculitis presenting with subcutaneous nodules, livedo, and digital gangrene, corroborated by pathognomonic renal and mesenteric microaneurysms ('string of beads') on angiography and CTA.

Rheumatology.name: Psoriatic Arthritis
clinical_manifestations: Dactylitis: diffuse, tender, non-pitting inflammatory swelling of an entire digit ('sausage digit')
Psoriatic nail disease: pitting, onycholysis, subungual hyperkeratosis, oil-drop/salmon patches, splinter hemorrhages
Cutaneous psoriatic plaques (extensor surfaces, scalp, umbilicus, gluteal cleft)
Arthritis mutilans: telescoping of digits ('opera-glass hands' / main en lorgnette) with redundant skin folds
Asymmetric oligoarthritis or DIP-predominant polyarthritis
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography: 'Pencil-in-cup' deformity (whittling of proximal phalanx with expansion/cupping of distal base), severe osteolysis, asymmetric joint space loss, exuberant bone proliferation (periostitis, bone whittling, ankylosis)
Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Enthesitis with thickening, hypoechogenicity, power Doppler vascularity at insertion sites (Achilles, patellar, triceps); flexor tenosynovitis
Hand/Foot MRI: Diffuse bone marrow edema, periarticular soft tissue edema ('capsulitis'), enthesitis, extensive synovitis
Spine Radiographs: Asymmetric non-marginal coarse syndesmophytes (paramarginal parasyndesmophytes)
pathology_manifestations: Synovium/enthesis histology: Prominent vascularity with tortuous, elongated vessels; infiltration by T cells (predominantly CD8+), neutrophils, and osteoclasts mediating aggressive bone resorption alongside bone proliferation
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Combines prominent cutaneous and nail psoriasis and dactylitis with pathognomonic plain film features such as the 'pencil-in-cup' deformity and periostitis.

Rheumatology.name: Reactive Arthritis
clinical_manifestations: Classic clinical triad: Urethritis/cervicitis (sterile dysuria, mucopurulent urethral or cervical discharge), non-infectious conjunctivitis or acute anterior uveitis (photophobia, ciliary flush, blurred vision), and acute asymmetric oligoarthritis ('can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree')

Keratoderma blennorrhagica: Highly characteristic hyperkeratotic, crusting, yellow-brown pustular or scaling macules, papules, and coalescing thick plaques located on the soles of the feet and palms of the hands, clinically and histologically indistinguishable from pustular psoriasis

Circinate balanitis: Painless, superficial, serpiginous, geographic erosions with slight erythematous, scaling borders on the glans penis and coronal sulcus in uncircumcised males, or dry hyperkeratotic, crusted, geographic plaques in circumcised males

Dactylitis ('sausage digits'): Striking, tender, diffuse, erythematous, fusiform swelling of entire toes (predominantly 2nd to 4th toes) or fingers, resulting from combined flexor tenosynovitis and adjacent joint synovitis

Enthesitis: Severe, localized pain and tenderness at tendon insertions, most characteristically causing severe retrocalcaneal or plantar heel pain at the Achilles tendon insertion and plantar fascia origin, accompanied by visible local erythema and swelling

Mucocutaneous erosions and nail changes: Painless, shallow, aphthous-like ulcers on the hard palate, tongue, and buccal mucosa; prominent subungual hyperkeratosis, brownish nail plate discoloration, and dystrophic onycholysis

Asymmetric oligoarthritis: Predominantly involving weight-bearing large joints of the lower extremities (knees, ankles, subtalar and metatarsophalangeal joints), characterized by marked warmth, tense joint effusions, and severe restriction of motion
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography of Feet and Calcaneus: Exuberant, fluffy, ill-defined periosteal new bone formation (periostitis / 'bone whiskering') along the metatarsal and phalangeal shafts; fluffy, ill-defined plantar and retrocalcaneal enthesophytes (calcaneal spurs with ragged, irregular margins); asymmetric marginal joint erosions with adjacent reactive bony sclerosis and soft-tissue swelling (dactylitis)

Plain Radiography of Pelvis and Sacroiliac Joints: Asymmetric or unilateral sacroiliitis (Grade 2 to 3 joint space blurring, subchondral sclerosis, and irregular erosions), distinctly differing from the strictly symmetric sacroiliitis of classic ankylosing spondylitis

Plain Radiography of Spine: Coarse, bulky, asymmetrical, non-marginal syndesmophytes (paramarginal bone bridges) that arise from the lateral or anterior mid-portion of vertebral bodies and bridge across intervertebral spaces while skipping intermediate vertebral levels, sparing the discovertebral corners

Musculoskeletal Ultrasound (with Power Doppler): Intense Doppler hypervascularity, hypoechoic entheseal thickening, and cortical bone irregularities at the insertion of the Achilles tendon and plantar fascia; distension of the retrocalcaneal bursa; marked soft-tissue subcutaneous edema and flexor tenosynovitis in dactylitic digits

MRI of Sacroiliac Joints and Lower Extremity Entheses: Unilateral or asymmetric subchondral bone marrow edema on T2 STIR and contrast-enhanced T1 sequences indicating active sacroiliitis; prominent entheseal bone marrow edema and peritendinous soft-tissue inflammation at the calcaneus
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy of Keratoderma Blennorrhagica: Histopathologically indistinguishable from pustular psoriasis: marked hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis with retained pyknotic nuclei, elongated, club-shaped epidermal rete ridges (acanthosis), marked thinning of the suprapapillary plates, and pathognomonic intraepidermal multilocular neutrophilic microabscesses (spongiform pustules of Kogoj in the stratum spinosum and microabscesses of Munro in the stratum corneum)

Synovial biopsy: Prominent synovial lining cell hyperplasia, intense neoangiogenesis with swollen endothelial cells, dense infiltration of the sublining stroma by polymorphonuclear neutrophils, CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes, and macrophages; absence of classic rheumatoid necrobiotic granulomas or crystal deposits

Synovial fluid analysis: Marked inflammatory exudate (leukocyte count 10,000–50,000/μL, >70% neutrophils), sterile bacterial cultures, negative polarized light microscopy for uric acid or calcium pyrophosphate crystals
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Combines classic physical bedside photographic findings (keratoderma blennorrhagica, circinate balanitis, dactylitis) with radiographic hallmarks of asymmetric sacroiliitis, fluffy periostitis ('bone whiskering'), and Kogoj spongiform pustules on pathology.

Rheumatology.name: Relapsing Febrile Nodular Panniculitis (Weber-Christian Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent crops of painful, tender, warm, erythematous subcutaneous nodules and plaques ranging from 1 to 10 cm in diameter, symmetrically distributed across the thighs, buttocks, calves, abdomen, and upper arms
Synchronous high-grade febrile episodes: systemic spiking fever, rigors, malaise, arthralgia, abdominal colic, and fatigue occurring concurrently with every new eruption of cutaneous nodules

Saucer-like lipodystrophic depressions: as acute inflammatory nodules resolve over weeks, they leave behind permanent, cup-shaped, atrophic subcutaneous hollows/dents and hyperpigmented scarring due to liquefactive fat necrosis

Visceral panniculitis involvement: severe systemic inflammation affecting mesenteric, retroperitoneal, pericardial, and perirenal fat depots, which may present as acute peritonitis, intestinal obstruction, or pericarditis
radiological_manifestations: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of Extremities / Trunk: T1-weighted images show patchy or nodular areas of decreased signal intensity within the subcutaneous fat; T2-weighted fat-suppressed and STIR sequences reveal intense, geographic hyperintensity with extensive surrounding subcutaneous reticular stranding reflecting acute fat necrosis and inflammatory edema; post-gadolinium T1 demonstrates thick peripheral or septal nodular enhancement

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal and Pelvic Computed Tomography (CT): Multiple soft-tissue attenuation nodules and extensive hazy infiltration ('misty mesentery') with stranding of the mesenteric, omental, and retroperitoneal adipose beds, reflecting visceral lobular panniculitis and fat saponification

High-Frequency Soft Tissue Ultrasonography: Ill-defined, mixed-echogenicity subcutaneous masses exhibiting central hypoechoic necrotic areas, peripheral hyperechoic rimming, and prominent peripheral hypervascularity on color Doppler interrogation
pathology_manifestations: Deep Incisional / Excisional Wedge Biopsy of Skin and Subcutis (Including Fascia): Primary lobular panniculitis without primary necrotizing vasculitis, progressing through three classical histopathologic stages: 1. Acute inflammatory stage: Dense, lobular infiltration of the fat lobules by neutrophils, lymphocytes, and histiocytes with early lipocyte degeneration; 2. Macrophagic / lipophagic stage (pathognomonic): Extensive fat necrosis with the replacement of adipocytes by sheets of lipid-laden, foamy histiocytes (lipophages) and multinucleated foreign-body giant cells engulfing lipid droplets; 3. Fibrotic / healing stage: Proliferation of fibroblasts, collagen deposition, and progressive dense fibrous scarring replacing the destroyed adipose lobules
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic systemic autoimmune adipose disorder presenting with hallmark febrile bouts, painful nodules, and saucer-like atrophic scars, imaged by limb MRI fascial/subcutaneous stranding and abdominal CT 'misty mesentery', confirmed by staged lobular panniculitis with foamy lipophages.

Rheumatology.name: Relapsing Polychondritis
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral or unilateral auricular chondritis: bright red, violaceous, intensely painful, swollen external ear with pathognomonic sparing of the non-cartilaginous ear lobule
Nasal chondritis causing acute nasal bridge pain and eventual collapse into a saddle nose deformity
Ocular inflammation: episcleritis, scleritis, uveitis, keratitis
Laryngotracheal tenderness, hoarseness, stridor, and respiratory distress from airway cartilage breakdown
Costochondritis with chest wall swelling and tenderness
radiological_manifestations: Dynamic Expiratory Chest CT: Diffuse tracheal and mainstem bronchial wall thickening with sparing of the non-cartilaginous posterior membranous wall; dynamic expiratory tracheobronchomalacia (airway collapse >50%), tracheal stenosis
Head/Neck MRI/CT: Auricular cartilage thickening and enhancement, nasal septal cartilage destruction
18F-FDG PET/CT: Marked FDG avidity in auricular, nasal, costochondral, and tracheobronchial cartilages
pathology_manifestations: Cartilage biopsy (ear/trachea): Loss of basophilic proteoglycan matrix staining, perichondrial inflammatory infiltrate composed of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and neutrophils, chondrocyte degeneration and pyknosis, fibrous tissue replacement
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield visual entity with the classic lobule-sparing red ear and saddle nose deformity paired with pathognomonic dynamic tracheal airway collapse and anterior tracheal wall thickening on chest CT.

Rheumatology.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
clinical_manifestations: Symmetric polyarthritis predominantly involving MCP, PIP, and wrist joints
Ulnar drift and volar subluxation of the MCP joints
Swan-neck deformities and Boutonnière deformities of the digits
Rheumatoid subcutaneous nodules (olecranon, extensor forearm, Achilles tendon)
Palmar erythema and cutaneous rheumatoid vasculitis (digital infarcts, splinter hemorrhages)
Episcleritis and scleromalacia perforans
radiological_manifestations: Hand and foot radiographs: Marginal osseous erosions, symmetric joint space narrowing, periarticular osteopenia, carpal coalescence
Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Synovial hypertrophy, power Doppler hyperemia (active pannus), extensor tenosynovitis, bone erosions
Hand/Wrist MRI: Synovial thickening, pannus enhancement, bone marrow edema (pre-erosive osteitis)
Cervical Spine X-ray/CT: Atlantoaxial subluxation (increased anterior atlantodental interval >3 mm), odontoid peg erosions
Chest HRCT: Rheumatoid ILD (UIP or NSIP patterns), rheumatoid pulmonary necrobiotic nodules
pathology_manifestations: Subcutaneous nodule histology: Central geographic fibrinoid necrosis surrounded by a palisade of CD68+ histiocytes and outer lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate
Synovial biopsy: Markedly hyperplastic synovial lining (synovial villi), dense sublining infiltration of lymphocytes (germinal center-like lymphoid follicles) and plasma cells
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic inflammatory joint disorder with landmark bedside joint deformities and subcutaneous nodules matching hallmark marginal erosions on plain radiographs, power Doppler synovitis on ultrasound, and atlantoaxial subluxation on spinal imaging.

Rheumatology.name: SAPHO Syndrome
synonyms: Synovitis, Acne, Pustulosis, Hyperostosis, Osteitis syndrome
chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis with cutaneous lesions
clinical_manifestations: Anterior chest wall syndrome: Severe, dull, aching pain, localized point tenderness, and prominent visible swelling and erythema over the sternoclavicular joints, manubriosternal junction, and upper costosternal synchondroses, causing marked limitation of shoulder girdle abduction and thorax expansion

Palmoplantar pustulosis (PPP): Recurrent crops of deep-seated, non-infectious, yellowish sterile pustules on erythematous bases located symmetrically on the palms and soles, evolving into brownish-yellow macules, peeling, and thick scaling hyperkeratotic plaques

Severe inflammatory dermatoses: Severe nodulocystic acne conglobata (deep burrowing inflammatory nodules with draining purulent sinus tracts and hypertrophic scarring), acne fulminans (abrupt ulcerating necrotic acne with fever), or hidradenitis suppurativa in inverse apocrine regions
Peripheral arthritis: Asymmetric non-erosive oligoarthritis predominantly involving large joints (knees, ankles, hips, wrists)
Axial involvement: Chronic inflammatory back pain, localized spinal tenderness, and stiffness involving the thoracolumbar spine or sacroiliac joints
radiological_manifestations: 99mTc-MDP Bone Scintigraphy: Pathognomonic 'bull's head' sign (intense, symmetric radiotracer hyperfixation at the manubriosternal joint representing the 'skull' and both sternoclavicular joints representing the 'horns' of a bull); multi-focal skeletal hot spots in the clavicles, spine, and long bones

High-Resolution CT of Anterior Chest Wall: Pathognomonic sternocostoclavicular hyperostosis: massive cortical thickening, diffuse osteosclerosis, and hyperostotic bony bridging fusing the medial clavicles, manubrium, and first rib synchondroses, with complete obliteration of the joint spaces; mottled osteolytic erosions interspersed with dense osteosclerosis producing a classic 'cotton-wool' appearance

MRI of Anterior Chest Wall and Spine: Extensive bone marrow edema (marked T2 STIR hyperintensity, low T1 signal) with avid gadolinium enhancement of the medial clavicle heads, manubrium, and adjacent pectoral soft tissues; spine involvement shows non-infectious anterior spondylodiscitis (corner inflammatory lesions, discovertebral erosions, vertebral squaring) and Romanus-like lesions
Plain Radiography: Hyperostosis and dense osteosclerosis of the medial third of the clavicles and sternal manubrium, periosteal cortical thickening, and sternomanubrial ankylosis
pathology_manifestations: Bone biopsy of hyperostotic lesion: Early phase shows acute non-specific osteitis with dense polymorphonuclear neutrophilic infiltration and active osteoclastic bone resorption; chronic phase shows dense medullary fibrosis replacing marrow adipocytes, chronic infiltrates of CD3+ T lymphocytes and plasma cells, prominent osteoblastic rimming, and irregular, thickened, sclerotic trabecular bone with disorganized mosaic cement lines (hyperostosis); routine microbiological cultures are sterile (or infrequently yield low-virulence Cutibacterium [Propionibacterium] acnes)

Skin punch biopsy of palmoplantar pustule: Large unilocular sterile subcorneal or intraepidermal pustules densely packed with viable and degenerate polymorphonuclear neutrophils (spongiform pustules of Kogoj), overlying an acanthotic epidermis with parakeratosis and a mild dermal perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Unites dramatic physical findings (sternoclavicular swelling, palmoplantar pustulosis, acne conglobata) with the pathognomonic 'bull's head' sign on bone scintigraphy, massive CT anterior chest wall hyperostosis, and sterile osteitic bone pathology.

Rheumatology.name: Scleromyxedema
clinical_manifestations: Widespread, dense, symmetrical eruption of closely spaced, 2-3 mm, waxy, firm, dome-shaped or flat-topped, flesh-colored to erythematous papules arranged in a linear or cobblestone pattern on indurated skin

Stereotypical anatomic distribution: striking involvement of the face, neck, retroauricular regions, upper trunk, forearms, and dorsum of hands, with characteristically spared scalp and oral mucous membranes
'Shar-Pei' sign / leonine facies: deep, exaggerated skin furrowing and massive thickened skin folds over the forehead, glabella, and posterior neck

'Doughnut sign' of the fingers (pathognomonic clinical sign): elevated annular rim of thick, infiltrated skin surrounding a central cup-like depression directly overlying the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints upon finger flexion

Sclerodermoid functional impairment: severe progressive limitation of joint mobility with flexion contractures of fingers ('sclerodactyly-like'), microstomia, reduced oral aperture, and proximal muscle weakness

Systemic paraproteinemia and Dermato-Neuro Syndrome: almost universal presence of a monoclonal IgG lambda paraproteinemia; life-threatening dermato-neuro syndrome characterized by fluctuating encephalopathy, stupor, seizures, high fever, and coma
radiological_manifestations: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of Hands and Limbs: Marked, diffuse thickening of the cutaneous and subcutaneous tissue layers with intermediate-to-high signal on T2-weighted and STIR sequences due to abundant hydrophilic mucin deposition; marked diffuse homogeneous enhancement on post-contrast T1 images; notable absence of deep fascial thickening or destructive synovial erosions

Brain MRI (during Dermato-Neuro Syndrome): Diffuse cerebral edema, T2/FLAIR hyperintensity within cortical and subcortical white matter, and diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement during acute neuro-encephalopathic crises

Transthoracic Echocardiography & Cardiac MRI: Diffuse myocardial thickening and delayed gadolinium enhancement caused by mucinous and fibrotic myocardial infiltration, leading to restrictive cardiomyopathy
pathology_manifestations: Full-Thickness Punch / Incisional Skin Biopsy (Diagnostic Pathognomonic Triad): 1. Abundant dermal mucin: Extensive, diffuse accumulation of mucopolysaccharide ground substance (mucin) throughout the upper and mid-reticular dermis, staining strongly positive with Alcian blue at pH 2.5 and colloidal iron, and digestible with hyaluronidase; 2. Proliferation of fibroblasts: Marked proliferation of irregularly arranged, plump, spindle-shaped and stellate fibroblasts dispersed between collagen bundles; 3. Sclerosis: Thickened, haphazardly organized, dense collagen fibers in the reticular dermis; absence of true vasculitis and preserved epidermis
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Rare but visually spectacular systemic fibromucinous disorder possessing pathognomonic physical signs ('Shar-Pei' facial furrowing, PIP 'doughnut sign'), soft-tissue mucin hyperintensity on MRI, and the definitive histological triad of dermal mucin, fibroblast proliferation, and collagen sclerosis with IgG lambda paraproteinemia.

Rheumatology.name: Sjögren's Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral or unilateral painless to mildly tender tumefaction/enlargement of major salivary glands (parotid and submandibular glands), often presenting with firm, rubbery lobulation on palpation

Severe xerostomia: dry, erythematous oral mucosa adhering tenaciously to wooden tongue depressors, dry parchment-like or lobulated 'cobblestone' tongue with total loss of filiform papillae, absence of salivary pooling in the floor of the mouth, and rampant cervical dental root caries

Keratoconjunctivitis sicca: severe ocular hyperemia, thick ropy mucus strands in the inferior fornix, abnormal Schirmer test (<=5 mm wetting at 5 minutes), and ocular surface staining with rose bengal or lissamine green demonstrating confluent punctate epithelial keratopathy and filamentary keratitis

Cutaneous manifestations: hypergammaglobulinemic purpura of Waldenström (crops of non-thrombocytopenic palpable petechiae and purpura over lower extremities triggered by prolonged standing), cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis, and annular erythema of Sjögren syndrome (wide polycyclic gyrate erythematous plaques with elevated border)
Extraglandular features: Raynaud phenomenon, non-erosive symmetrical polyarthralgias/polyarthritis, severe xerosis cutis, and dry vaginal mucosa
radiological_manifestations: Salivary Gland Ultrasonography (SGUS) (OMERACT/Hocevar score): Marked parenchymal heterogeneity within parotid and submandibular glands, characterized by multiple round-to-oval hypoechoic or anechoic areas (representing lymphocytic foci and ductectasias) surrounded by hyperechoic fibrous septa, blurred glandular borders, and posterior acoustic enhancement

Conventional / Digital Subtraction Sialography: Punctate (<1 mm), globular (1-2 mm), cavitary, or destructive contrast pools producing the classic pathognomonic 'cherry blossom tree' or 'fruit-laden branch' appearance, reflecting widespread peripheral sialectasis

Salivary Gland MRI: Inhomogeneous 'salt-and-pepper' or 'honeycomb' glandular architecture on T1- and T2-weighted sequences caused by punctate high-signal ectasias on T2, multiple microcysts, and diffuse fatty infiltration; hyperintense ductal dilation demonstrated on MR sialography

High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of the Chest: Lymphoid interstitial pneumonia (LIP) pattern characterized by bilateral thin-walled parenchymal lung cysts (2-30 mm), centrilobular ground-glass nodules, and interlobular septal thickening; or non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) pattern with bibasilar reticulation and traction bronchiectasis
pathology_manifestations: Minor Labial Salivary Gland Biopsy (Diagnostic gold standard, Greenspan / Chisholm-Mason focus score >=1 focus per 4 mm^2): Focal lymphocytic sialadenitis characterized by dense periductal aggregates of >=50 mononuclear inflammatory cells (predominantly CD4+ T-lymphocytes and plasma cells) adjacent to normal-appearing glandular acini, accompanied by progressive acinar atrophy, ductal epithelial hyperplasia, and periductal fibrosis

Major Salivary Gland Core/Incisional Biopsy: Epimyoepithelial islands (islands of ductal epithelial and myoepithelial cells obliterating salivary lumina), dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, with immunohistochemical light-chain restriction analysis to definitively rule out development of mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) B-cell lymphoma
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic systemic autoimmune exocrinopathy with hallmark physical exam findings (parotid tumefaction, cobblestone tongue, purpuric lesions), pathognomonic salivary ultrasound and sialographic 'cherry blossom' imaging, and standardized histological focus scoring on minor labial salivary gland biopsy.

Rheumatology.name: Sneddon Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Livedo racemosa: Widespread, persistent, violaceous, broken, asymmetrical, irregular, net-like (reticular) and branch-like cutaneous mottling on the trunk, buttocks, and upper and lower extremities; unlike physiological livedo reticularis, livedo racemosa lesions form incomplete, broken circular patterns, involve the trunk/abdomen, and never resolve upon warming

Recurrent ischemic cerebrovascular events: Transient ischemic attacks (TIAs) and multiple ischemic strokes in young patients (typically women aged 20–45 years), causing focal neurological deficits (hemiparesis, hemianopia, aphasia, ataxia)
Progressive cognitive and neuropsychiatric decline: Early-onset vascular dementia, memory loss, emotional lability, personality changes, depression, and severe recurrent migraine-like headaches
Peripheral vascular manifestations: Acrocyanosis, Raynaud phenomenon, and painful small ischemic cutaneous infarctions or ulcerations at the edges of the livedoid rings
Hypertension: Labile or renovascular-type hypertension due to renal arteriolar involvement
radiological_manifestations: Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI - DWI, FLAIR, T2-weighted, and T1 post-contrast): Multiple, bilateral, recurrent cortical and subcortical ischemic infarctions with predilection for watershed / borderzone territories and deep white matter; confluent periventricular hyperintensities (severe leukoaraiosis) and multiple chronic lacunar infarcts; subcortical microbleeds on gradient-echo (GRE) or susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI); generalized cerebral and cerebellar cortical atrophy disproportionate to the patient's young age

Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA) and High-Resolution MRA: Segmental stenoses, occlusions, and severe luminal irregularity of medium and small intracranial arteries (distal branches of middle and anterior cerebral arteries); secondary leptomeningeal and transdural collateral vessel network ('net-like' or 'cloud-like' neo-vascularization mimicking moyamoya collateral pattern); absence of large-vessel atherosclerosis or cardioembolic source
High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound: Focal dermal and subcutaneous microvascular irregularity, thickening of arteriolar walls, and localized dermal hypoechogenicity beneath the livedo racemosa rings
pathology_manifestations: Deep wedge skin biopsy (spanning both the pale central island and the peripheral violaceous ring down into subcutaneous fat): Pathognomonic non-inflammatory obliterative endotheliopathy: Subendothelial smooth muscle cell and myofibroblastic proliferation leading to eccentric or concentric intimal hyperplasia and progressive lumen stenosis/obliteration of medium-to-deep dermis and subcutaneous arterioles (at the dermal-subcutaneous border); strict absence of leukocytoclasia, transmural inflammatory infiltrates, or fibrinoid necrosis of vessel walls (distinguishing it from cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa and leukocytoclastic vasculitis); secondary microvascular luminal thrombosis and erythrocyte extravasation; duplication or fragmentation of the internal elastic lamina without true necrosis
Brain histopathology: Non-inflammatory obliterative arteriopathy of leptomeningeal and penetrating cortical arteries with intimal cushions, subtotal luminal occlusion, and microinfarcts
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Characterized by the striking clinical livedo racemosa rash and young-onset ischemic strokes, coupled with multi-territory watershed infarcts and moyamoya-like collateral networks on brain MRI/angiography, and non-inflammatory obliterative arteriopathy on deep skin biopsy.

Rheumatology.name: Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis
clinical_manifestations: Quotidian spiking fevers: characteristic high-spiking daily or twice-daily fevers (temperatures rapidly soaring to >=39°C, typically in the late afternoon/evening) that return rapidly to normal or subnormal levels, accompanied by chills and marked lethargy during spikes

Evanescent salmon-pink rash: transient, non-pruritic, macular or maculopapular salmon-pink erythematous rash that erupts strictly during febrile peaks and rapidly fades as body temperature normalizes; predominantly involves the trunk, neck, and proximal extremities; exhibits Koebner phenomenon (linear urticarial streaks elicited by light mechanical stroking of skin)

Symmetric polyarthritis: progressive inflammatory arthritis involving wrists, knees, ankles, cervical spine, and small joints of the hands and feet, leading to joint effusion, warm boggy swelling, and painful flexion contractures
Systemic reticuloendothelial enlargement: generalized non-tender lymphadenopathy (prominent axillary, cervical, and epitrochlear nodes) and marked hepatosplenomegaly

Severe systemic serositis and Macrophage Activation Syndrome (MAS): acute pleuropericarditis with audible pericardial friction rub; MAS manifests with unremitting fever, petechiae, ecchymoses, mucosal bleeding, jaundice, and central nervous system encephalopathy
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal Plain Radiography of Extremities: Early juxta-articular demineralization, accelerated osseous maturation (premature ossification and early closure of carpal and tarsal growth plates causing microdactyly/brachydactyly); progressive joint space narrowing, periosteal new bone formation, carpal ankylosis ('crowded carpus'), cervical spine apophyseal fusion (especially C2-C3/C3-C4), and mandibular hypoplasia (micrognathia resulting from temporomandibular joint ankylosis)

Musculoskeletal Ultrasonography and MRI: Marked synovial hypertrophy, extensive complex joint effusion with intense Power Doppler hypervascularity, thickened synovial pannus, subchondral bone marrow edema, and progressive articular cartilage erosions

Transthoracic Echocardiography & Chest CT: Pericardial thickening and effusion, bilateral pleural effusions, subsegmental pulmonary consolidations, and diffuse mediastinal/retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy
pathology_manifestations: Synovial Biopsy / Synovial Fluid Examination: Prominent villous hyperplasia of the synovial lining cells, intense sublining vascular proliferation, and dense infiltration by lymphocytes, plasma cells, and histiocytes; synovial fluid exhibits marked sterile inflammatory exudate with leukocytosis (>30,000-50,000/uL, predominantly neutrophils)

Bone Marrow / Lymph Node Aspirate and Biopsy (Pathognomonic in Macrophage Activation Syndrome): Marked hemophagocytosis characterized by activated CD163+/CD68+ mature tissue histiocytes actively engulfing erythrocytes, platelets, leukocytes, and nucleated precursor cells, accompanied by sinusoidal histiocytic hyperplasia and absence of cellular dysplasia
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal childhood autoinflammatory connective tissue disease defined by fever spikes, evanescent salmon-pink rash, and progressive polyarthritis, documented radiologically by cervical ankylosis and micrognathia, and pathologically by synovial pannus and life-threatening bone marrow hemophagocytosis in MAS.

Rheumatology.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
clinical_manifestations: Malar (butterfly) rash with nasolabial sparing
Discoid lupus erythematous (DLE) plaques with follicular plugging and central scarring
Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE: annular and papulosquamous forms)
Oral and nasopharyngeal mucosal ulcerations (typically painless, hard palate)
Non-scarring lupus alopecia and scarring discoid alopecia
Livedo reticularis and livedo racemosa
Jaccoud arthropathy (reducible non-erosive joint deformities)
Raynaud phenomenon and digital periungual erythema
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT: Lupus pneumonitis, pleural effusions, pericardial effusion, shrinking lung syndrome with diaphragmatic elevation
Brain MRI: T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in white matter, cerebral vasculitis, cortical infarcts, lupus cerebritis
MSK Plain X-ray: Reducible hand subluxations (ulnar deviation, swan-neck) without osseous erosions (Jaccoud arthropathy)
Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Synovitis, tenosynovitis without prominent marginal erosions
Renal Ultrasound: Increased cortical echogenicity in advanced lupus nephritis
pathology_manifestations: Renal biopsy (ISN/RPS lupus nephritis classes I-VI: mesangial, focal, diffuse proliferative, membranous, sclerosing)
Direct immunofluorescence (DIF): 'Full-house' granular deposition (IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q) along the glomerular basement membrane or dermo-epidermal junction (lupus band test)
Skin punch biopsy: Vacuolar interface dermatitis, basal layer hydropic degeneration, apoptotic keratinocytes (Civatte bodies), mucin deposition in the reticular dermis
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal systemic autoimmune disease with distinctive mucocutaneous lesions (malar, discoid, SCLE) paired with multi-organ radiological manifestations (CNS lupus on MRI, pleuropulmonary disease on CT, Jaccoud arthropathy on X-ray).

Rheumatology.name: Systemic Sclerosis
clinical_manifestations: Sclerodactyly (tightening and induration of the skin of the fingers distal to MCP joints)
Raynaud phenomenon with triphasic color changes (white pallor, blue cyanosis, red rubor)
Digital pitting scars and painful ischemic digital tip ulcers
Facial microstomia with radial perioral furrowing and beaked nose ('mauskopf' facies)
Mucocutaneous telangiectasias (face, lips, oral mucosa, hands)
Calcinosis cutis (chalky, firm subcutaneous nodular calcium deposits)
Tendon friction rubs (palpable or audible crepitus over wrists, ankles, knees)
Nailfold videocapillaroscopy: Enlarged giant capillaries, microhemorrhages, avascular areas
radiological_manifestations: Hand Radiographs: Acro-osteolysis (resorption of the distal tufts of phalanges), subcutaneous soft-tissue calcinosis

Chest HRCT: Non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) pattern with ground-glass opacities and fine reticulation, subpleural honeycombing (UIP pattern), dilated aperistaltic esophagus ('patulous esophagus')
Barium Esophagram: Esophageal dysmotility, dilated lower esophagus with patulous lower esophageal sphincter
Echocardiography: Elevated pulmonary artery systolic pressure, pericardial effusion, right ventricular hypertrophy
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy: Marked expansion and hyalinization of the dermis by thick, densely packed collagen bundles running parallel to the epidermis; entrapment of eccrine glands; loss of periadnexal fat; perivascular lymphocytic infiltrates
Vascular histology: Obliterative endarteropathy with concentric intimal proliferation ('onion-skinning') and adventitial fibrosis
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield multi-organ disease combining vivid bedside signs (sclerodactyly, microstomia, digital ulcers, calcinosis) with characteristic acro-osteolysis on hand X-rays and NSIP/patulous esophagus on chest HRCT.

Rheumatology.name: Takayasu Arteritis
clinical_manifestations: Asymmetric or absent peripheral pulses (especially radial and brachial pulses: 'pulseless disease')
Blood pressure discrepancy (>10 mmHg difference between arms)
Vascular bruits audible over carotid, subclavian, and abdominal aorta
Carotidynia (tenderness over the carotid bifurcations)
Upper extremity ischemic skin pallor, coldness, claudication, and digital gangrene
Erythema nodosum and pyoderma gangrenosum-like cutaneous lesions
radiological_manifestations: CT Angiography / MR Angiography: Circumferential mural thickening of the aorta and its primary branches ('macaroni sign'), smooth segmental tapered stenoses, occlusions, post-stenotic dilations, and saccular/fusiform aneurysms
18F-FDG PET/CT: Intense circumferential glucose uptake within the inflamed aortic arch and branch vessel walls
Color Doppler Ultrasound: Concentric, hypoechoic arterial wall thickening (macaroni sign) in the common carotid and subclavian arteries
pathology_manifestations: Aortic/arterial wall histology: Panarteritis with marked adventitial and medial infiltration of lymphocytes, plasma cells, histiocytes, and multinucleated giant cells; elastic fiber destruction, patchy medial necrosis, and extensive adventitial fibrosis; marked intimal fibrocellular hyperplasia
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Classic pulseless disease featuring asymmetric arm ischemia and vascular bruits alongside pathognomonic CTA/MRA concentric aortic wall thickening ('macaroni sign') and branch-vessel stenosis.

Rheumatology.name: Thromboangiitis Obliterans
clinical_manifestations: Almost exclusively affects young tobacco smokers (predominantly males under 45–50 years of age)
Severe ischemic rest pain and claudication: Intense burning or aching pain in the instep of the foot (foot claudication / arch pain) or hand, characteristically worsening at night and upon elevation

Digital ischemia, ulceration, and gangrene: Raynaud phenomenon, cold sensitivity, and painful, non-healing ischemic ulcers of the distal toes and fingertips, rapidly progressing to dry gangrene, mummification, and spontaneous autoamputation of phalanges

Superficial thrombophlebitis migrans: Recurrent crops of firm, tender, erythematous, cord-like subcutaneous nodules along the anatomical course of superficial veins in the feet, calves, or forearms that resolve spontaneously over weeks while new lesions appear elsewhere
Diminished or absent distal peripheral pulses (dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial, radial, ulnar) with completely normal and bounding proximal pulses (femoral, popliteal, brachial)
Positive Allen test demonstrating severe occlusion of the ulnar or radial arteries with compromised palmar arch microcirculation
radiological_manifestations: Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA) / CT Angiography / MR Angiography of Upper and Lower Extremities (Imaging Gold Standard): Pathognomonic 'corkscrew collaterals' (Martorell sign): Abundant, highly tortuous, coiled, helical collateral vessels that develop around the sites of arterial occlusion (hypertrophied vasa vasorum bridging occluded segments); segmental, smooth, tapering occlusions and severe luminal stenosis of small- and medium-sized arteries (tibial, peroneal, plantar, radial, ulnar, and digital arteries), with an abrupt cutoff ('tree root' or 'spider web' vascular pattern); striking absence of atherosclerotic plaques, calcifications, atheromatous ulcerations, or proximal aneurysms; proximal arterial tree (aorta, iliac, femoral, popliteal, subclavian, brachial) is entirely normal and widely patent

Arterial Duplex Ultrasonography: Multilevel segmental occlusion in distal arteries with triphasic normal waveforms proximally, flat monophasic or absent flow distally, hypoechoic intraluminal thrombus, and lack of arterial wall calcification

Plain Radiography of Hands and Feet: Resorption of terminal phalangeal tufts (acro-osteolysis), soft-tissue volume loss, bone erosion underlying chronic ischemic ulcers, and autoamputation of distal phalanges without vascular calcification
pathology_manifestations: Arterial and venous histopathology (Surgical resection or amputation specimen): Acute / Subacute phase (Pathognomonic): Highly cellular, occlusive, inflammatory intraluminal thrombus packed with polymorphonuclear leukocytes (often forming central microabscesses), multinucleated histiocytic giant cells, and proliferating endothelial cells; extensive panarteritis and panphlebitis involving all layers of the vessel wall (intima, media, adventitia)

Preserved vascular architecture: Pathognomonic preservation of the internal elastic lamina (intact, non-disrupted elastic lamina without fragmentation or transmural fibrinoid necrosis, distinguishing TAO from systemic necrotizing vasculitides such as polyarteritis nodosa)

Chronic phase: Fibrous organization and recanalization of the occlusive thrombi; dense perivascular adventitial fibrosis encasing and adhering the neurovascular bundle (artery, companion vein, and peripheral nerve) into a solid, unseparable fibrous sheath
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Iconic vascular condition in young smokers displaying visible digital gangrene, autoamputation, and thrombophlebitis migrans, verified by pathognomonic 'corkscrew collaterals' on angiography and cellular intraluminal microabscesses with preserved elastic lamina on histology.

Rheumatology.name: VEXAS Syndrome
synonyms: Vacuoles, E1 enzyme, X-linked, Autoinflammatory, Somatic syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Exclusively or predominantly affects older adult males (>50 years of age), driven by somatic mutations in the UBA1 gene

Relapsing chondritis: Severe, painful, erythematous swelling and tenderness of the auricular cartilage (auricular chondritis strictly sparing the non-cartilaginous earlobe, identical to relapsing polychondritis), nasal bridge chondritis (leading to saddle-nose deformity), and tracheobronchial cartilage inflammation

Cutaneous lesions: Neutrophilic dermatoses presenting as tender, violaceous, edematous plaques and nodules (Sweet syndrome-like eruptions), cutaneous vasculitis with palpable purpura, periorbital edema and erythema, and painful indurated injection-site reactions

Hematologic manifestations: Refractory macrocytic anemia (elevated MCV >100 fL), thrombocytopenia, myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), and severe systemic inflammation with marked elevations in ESR and CRP
Thromboembolic events: High incidence of recurrent deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in upper and lower extremities, pulmonary embolism, and superficial migratory thrombophlebitis
Systemic and ocular features: High spiking daily fevers, profound weight loss, scleritis, episcleritis, and periorbital edema
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT: Recurrent, bilateral pulmonary infiltrates: multifocal ground-glass opacities, dependent lung consolidations, interlobular septal thickening, 'crazy-paving' pattern, and tree-in-bud nodular opacities reflecting neutrophilic alveolitis; bilateral pleural effusions; mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy

Neck and Facial CT / MRI: Prominent soft-tissue thickening, edema, and intense contrast enhancement along the auricular cartilage and nasal septal cartilage; retro-orbital fat stranding and extraocular muscle thickening

Venous Duplex Ultrasonography: Extensive occlusive and non-occlusive deep vein thrombosis (femoral, popliteal, brachial, jugular veins) and superficial thrombophlebitis with luminal distension and lack of compressibility

Tracheobronchial CT / Dynamic Expiratory CT: Concentric thickening and enhancement of the anterior and lateral cartilaginous walls of the trachea and mainstem bronchi, with classic sparing of the posterior membranous wall, and dynamic tracheomalacia / airway narrowing
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy (Gold Standard Pathognomonic Hallmark): Characteristic cytoplasmic vacuoles: Striking, well-demarcated, spherical, clear cytoplasmic vacuoles in erythroid and myeloid precursor cells, most prominently in promyelocytes, myelocytes, metamyelocytes, and early erythroblasts (pronormoblasts); hypercellular marrow with dyserythropoiesis, ring sideroblasts on Prussian blue iron stain, megaloblastic changes, and atypical megakaryocytes; confirmation via Sanger sequencing or next-generation sequencing demonstrating somatic missense mutations in codon 41 (p.Met41Val, p.Met41Thr, p.Met41Leu) of the UBA1 gene on chromosome Xp11.3

Skin punch biopsy: Dense, band-like or diffuse infiltrate of mature neutrophils throughout the reticular dermis with marked papillary dermal edema (Sweet syndrome-like neutrophilic dermatosis pattern), or leukocytoclastic vasculitis with neutrophilic infiltration of small dermal vessels, karyorrhexis, and fibrin deposition, without evidence of bacterial or fungal infection
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Landmark modern autoinflammatory syndrome linking earlobe-sparing chondritis and neutrophilic cutaneous plaques with CT pulmonary infiltrates and pathognomonic cytoplasmic vacuoles in myeloid/erythroid precursors on bone marrow examination.

Rheumatology.name: Deficiency of Adenosine Deaminase 2
clinical_manifestations: Livedo racemosa and cutaneous nodules from small-vessel vasculitis
Early-onset lacunar strokes, kept as a site of DADA2 rather than a separate stroke topic
Hypogammaglobulinemia is laboratory, not an image
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: lacunar infarcts in a child; visceral angiography may mimic polyarteritis nodosa
pathology_manifestations: Non-granulomatous small- and medium-vessel vasculitis; plasma ADA2 activity is low
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Monogenic vasculitis with livedo photographs and childhood stroke imaging, distinct from polyarteritis nodosa.

Rheumatology.name: Blau Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Tan micropapular rash in an infant
Boggy polyarthritis and camptodactyly
Granulomatous uveitis
radiological_manifestations: Hand radiographs: expanded carpus and camptodactyly; chest imaging is clear, unlike sarcoidosis
pathology_manifestations: Non-caseating granulomas in skin; NOD2 mutation in the nucleotide-binding domain
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Infantile granulomatous triad with rash, joint, and eye photographs, separated from adult sarcoidosis by age and genotype.

Rheumatology.name: Schnitzler Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Chronic nonpruritic urticarial rash
Bone pain over the iliac crest or tibia
radiological_manifestations: Bone scintigraphy or radiographs: sclerotic bone lesions
pathology_manifestations: Neutrophilic dermal infiltrate without vasculitis; IgM monoclonal protein
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Autoinflammatory urticaria with a rash photograph and a sclerotic bone scan.

Rheumatology.name: Hypocomplementemic Urticarial Vasculitis
clinical_manifestations: Urticarial wheals that last more than 24 hours and leave purpura or pigment
Angioedema and eye redness from episcleritis or uveitis
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT if obstructive lung disease develops; it is a complication, not a required image
pathology_manifestations: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis on urticarial skin, low complements, and anti-C1q antibodies
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Urticarial vasculitis with timed clinical photographs and a vasculitis biopsy, distinct from ordinary urticaria.

Rheumatology.name: Alkaptonuria and Ochronotic Arthropathy
clinical_manifestations: Rare autosomal recessive inborn error of tyrosine catabolism caused by homogentisic acid oxidase (HGD) deficiency, leading to systemic accumulation and polymer deposition of homogentisic acid (HGA) in hyaline cartilage and connective tissues
Clinical triad: dark urine on standing/alkalinization, ochronotic cutaneous/scleral pigmentation, and severe early-onset degenerative arthropathy

Ochronotic pigmentation signs: slate-blue, brown, or brownish-black pigmentation of the sclera halfway between the cornea and outer canthus (Osler sign); bluish-black discoloration and rigid thickening of the ear cartilage (pinnae); dusky blue-grey pigmentation of the malar skin, nasal bridge, and palms
Urine abnormality: freshly voided urine darkens to brownish-black upon standing, alkalinization, or exposure to air due to HGA oxidation

Severe early-onset ochronotic spondyloarthropathy: loss of spinal flexibility, progressive lumbar flattening, thoracic kyphosis, and severe premature osteoarthritis of large weight-bearing joints (hips, knees, shoulders) with tendon ruptures (Achilles tendon)
radiological_manifestations: Spine Radiography (Pathognomonic Wafer Sign): Striking, universal, dense wafer-like calcification and ossification of intervertebral discs ("wafer sign" or "bamboo-like" appearance with wafer discs) throughout the lumbar and thoracic spine with multiple narrowed disc spaces

Pelvic & Knee Radiography: Severe symmetric joint space narrowing of hips and knees with dense subchondral sclerosis, osteophytosis, and intra-articular loose bodies (ochronotic chondromas), with conspicuous absence of subchondral cysts or primary bone erosions
Spine & Joint MRI: Disc calcifications displaying marked signal void on all sequences with vacuum phenomenon, disc degeneration, and loss of normal disc hydration
pathology_manifestations: Gross Surgical Pathology (Joint Arthroplasty Hallmark): Jet-black or dark brownish-black pigmentation of articular cartilage, intervertebral discs, meniscus, and synovial membranes ("coal-black cartilage")

Histopathology: Heavy intracellular and extracellular deposition of golden-brown or ochre-colored pigment granules within the chondrocytes and matrix of hyaline cartilage, turning black with silver stain (Fontana-Masson) or cresyl violet

Cartilage alterations: Ochronotic pigment encrustation makes cartilage brittle, leading to fissuring, fragmentation, and shedding of sharp pigmented shards into the synovium, inducing chronic foreign-body giant cell synovitis
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal visual metabolic rheumatology disorder featuring distinct external clinical photographs (blue-black ear cartilage, scleral Osler sign, black-turning urine) and pathognomonic wafer-like disc calcifications on spine radiographs.

Rheumatology.name: Diffuse Idiopathic Skeletal Hyperostosis
clinical_manifestations: Systemic non-inflammatory skeletal disorder of older adults (predominantly males >60 years) characterized by exuberant ossification of spinal anterior longitudinal ligaments and peripheral entheses
Physical examination: progressive spinal stiffness, reduced range of motion in the thoracic and cervical spine, and accentuated thoracic kyphosis with preserved lumbar lordosis

Oropharyngeal and airway complications: dysphagia (progressive difficulty swallowing solids) and stridor/airway obstruction resulting from massive anterior cervical osteophytes protruding into the posterior hypopharynx and esophagus
Peripheral enthesopathy signs: palpable, tender bony spurs and knobby enlargements at the patellae, Achilles tendon insertions, olecranon, and calcaneus
High susceptibility to unstable catastrophic spinal fractures following low-energy falls through brittle, ankylosed hyperostotic segments ("chalk-stick" fractures)
radiological_manifestations: Thoracic & Lumbar Spine Radiography (Pathognomonic Resnick Criteria): Flowing, continuous ossification and bony bridges along the anterolateral aspects of at least 4 contiguous vertebral bodies, creating a classic "dripping candle wax" or "flowing candle wax" appearance (predominantly right-sided due to aortic pulsation preventing left-sided ossification)
Intervertebral Disc Preservation: Relative preservation of intervertebral disc height without marked degenerative disc disease or vacuum phenomenon in the involved segments

Pelvic Radiography (Critical Distinction from Ankylosing Spondylitis): Complete absence of sacroiliac joint erosions, subchondral sclerosis, or intra-articular bony ankylosis of the SI joints (sacroiliac joint spaces remain completely open and normal)
Cervical CT / Barium Swallow: Enormous anterior flowing osteophytes protruding anteriorly from C3-C7, causing extrinsic impression and compression of the barium-filled esophagus
pathology_manifestations: Gross Bone Pathology: Exuberant flowing cortical bone bridging the anterior longitudinal ligament and periosteum, enveloping the anterior and lateral aspects of vertebral bodies while leaving the disc spaces intact

Histopathology: Progressive chondroid metaplasia and enchondral ossification within the deep layers of the anterior longitudinal ligament and fibrous entheseal attachment sites; normal lamellar bone formation with viable osteocytes and absent synovial or ligamentous inflammation
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield rheumatologic condition distinguished by pathognomonic spinal imaging (flowing anterior longitudinal ossification resembling dripping candle wax over ≥4 vertebrae with pristine sacroiliac joints) and external dysphagia-inducing cervical osteophytes.

Rheumatology.name: Tumor Necrosis Factor Receptor-Associated Periodic Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Autosomal dominant monogenic autoinflammatory disorder caused by missense mutations in the TNFRSF1A gene encoding the 55-kDa TNF receptor superfamily 1A
Characteristic prolonged febrile attacks: recurrent fever episodes typically lasting 1 to 3 weeks (significantly longer than the 1-3 day spikes of FMF)

Pathognomonic cutaneous hallmark: warm, tender, erythematous, edematous patches or plaques that migrate centrifugally down the extremities ("migratory centrifugal erythema") overlying intense deep myalgias
Ophthalmic signs (in up to 80%): dramatic unilateral or bilateral periorbital edema, conjunctival injection, periorbital erythema, and deep retro-orbital pain

Polyserositis and musculoskeletal findings: severe crampy abdominal pain mimicking an acute surgical abdomen, pleuritis, scrotal/testicular pain, and non-destructive oligoarthritis of the knees, ankles, and wrists
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal MRI of Affected Extremities: Marked hyperintense signal on T2-weighted and STIR sequences within the fascia and epimysium with diffuse fascial fluid and contrast enhancement, demonstrating that the migratory tenderness is a true *fasciitis* and *perimyositis* rather than an intrinsic myopathy
Abdominal CT / Ultrasound: Peritoneal thickening, ascites, and bowel wall edema during acute attacks; hepatosplenomegaly or renal enlargement in secondary AA amyloidosis
Renal Ultrasound: Increased cortical echogenicity in late-stage secondary AA amyloidosis (occurring in up to 25% of untreated patients)
pathology_manifestations: Skin Biopsy: Dense perivascular and interstitial mononuclear cell infiltrate in the reticular dermis and subcutaneous fat, composed primarily of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes and histiocytes without true leukocytoclastic vasculitis
Fascial / Muscle Biopsy: Prominent mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate expanding the deep muscular fascia with edema and sparing of muscle fibers themselves (fasciitis with perimyositis)

Renal / Rectal Biopsy (in chronic cases): Deposition of amorphous eosinophilic amyloid fibrils staining positive with Congo red and demonstrating apple-green birefringence under polarized light, confirmed as AA amyloid by immunohistochemistry
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Distinct monogenic autoinflammatory disease featuring prolonged multi-week fevers, striking clinical photographs of periorbital edema and migratory centrifugal erythematous plaques, with pathognomonic fascial STIR hyperintensity on MRI.

Rheumatology.name: Mevalonate Kinase Deficiency
clinical_manifestations: Autosomal recessive autoinflammatory disorder caused by mutations in the MVK gene, impairing the isoprenoid biosynthesis pathway and causing uninhibited IL-1beta release
Recurrent, abrupt febrile episodes lasting 3 to 7 days recurring every 4 to 6 weeks, frequently triggered by routine childhood vaccinations, minor infections, physical exertion, or emotional stress
Bedside physical hallmark: striking, massive, painful, tender bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy accompanying fever spikes
Cutaneous manifestations: polymorphic cutaneous eruption consisting of widespread maculopapular rashes, urticarial plaques, purpuric lesions on the limbs, or tender erythematous nodules

Mucocutaneous and joint signs: painful, recurrent aphthous oral ulcers and genital ulcers; symmetric, non-destructive, non-erosive polyarthritis or polyarthralgias involving predominantly the knees, ankles, and wrists; severe abdominal colic, vomiting, and diarrhea
radiological_manifestations: Cervical Soft-Tissue Ultrasound: Massive enlargement of cervical lymph node stations with preserved fatty hilum and intense hypervascularity on color Doppler without liquefactive necrosis
Musculoskeletal Ultrasound / Joint MRI: Marked joint effusion, synovial hypertrophy, and soft-tissue edema around large joints during attacks without cartilage loss or bony erosions
Abdominal Ultrasound: Splenomegaly and mesenteric lymphadenopathy during acute febrile crises
pathology_manifestations: Laboratory Biomarkers (Diagnostic Hallmark): Markedly elevated serum immunoglobulin D (IgD >100 IU/mL) in >80% of patients, commonly accompanied by elevated serum IgA, and massive urinary excretion of mevalonic acid during febrile attacks
Skin Biopsy: Superficial perivascular infiltrate of neutrophils, lymphocytes, and histiocytes with leukocytoclasia or neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis; negative direct immunofluorescence
Lymph Node Histopathology: Reactive follicular hyperplasia with marked interfollicular plasmacytosis and sinus histiocytosis
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Core pediatric and adult autoinflammatory syndrome presenting with vaccination-triggered fever attacks, dramatic photographs of massive tender cervical lymphadenopathy, aphthous stomatitis, and polymorphic erythematous eruptions.

Rheumatology.name: PAPA Syndrome
synonyms: Pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne syndrome
Familial recurrent arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne
clinical_manifestations: Rare autosomal dominant monogenic autoinflammatory syndrome caused by missense mutations in the PSTPIP1 (CD2BP1) gene on chromosome 15q24
Classic clinical triad spanning developmental ages: 1) Early-onset sterile pyogenic arthritis; 2) Pyoderma gangrenosum; 3) Severe cystic acne

Sterile Pyogenic Arthritis (Childhood Presentation): Recurrent, sudden, episodic flares of severe monoarthritis or oligoarthritis (knees, ankles, elbows) occurring after minor blunt trauma, presenting with tense, hot, red, swollen joints that mimic septic bacterial arthritis

Pyoderma Gangrenosum (Adolescence / Adulthood): Large, painful, rapidly expanding cutaneous ulcers with purplish, undermined, violaceous, ragged borders and necrotic purulent bases, predominantly on the lower extremities; exhibit marked pathergy
Severe Cystic Acne: Severe, intractable, nodulocystic acne conglobata covering the face, neck, and upper trunk, leaving extensive pitted and hypertrophic scarring
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography of Involved Joints: Repeated sterile pyogenic attacks result in rapid joint space narrowing, subchondral bone erosions, articular cartilage destruction, and secondary osteoarthritis in young patients
Joint MRI: Massive joint effusion, marked extensive synovial thickening with intense contrast enhancement, and adjacent bone marrow edema (osteitis)
Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Tense anechoic-to-hypoechoic articular effusion containing particulate debris and intense Power Doppler synovial hyperemia
pathology_manifestations: Synovial Fluid Aspiration (Key Negative Microbiology Hallmark): Markedly turbid or purulent "frankly purulent" synovial fluid with WBC counts frequently exceeding 50,000 to 100,000 neutrophils/mcL, but with *consistently negative bacterial Gram stains and cultures*
Cutaneous Biopsy of Pyoderma Gangrenosum: Massive dermal neutrophilic infiltration with tissue necrosis, ulceration, and microabscesses (neutrophilic dermatosis) without infectious microorganisms
Molecular Genetics: Mutations in PSTPIP1 lead to hyperphosphorylation, excessive binding to pyrin, and unchecked NLRP3 inflammasome activation with hypersecretion of IL-1beta and IL-18
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal visual monogenic rheumatologic triad featuring dramatic clinical photography (destructive sterile septic-like arthritis, violaceous undermined pyoderma gangrenosum ulcers, and disfiguring nodulocystic acne conglobata).

Rheumatology.name: Deficiency of the Interleukin-1 Receptor Antagonist
synonyms: Sterile multifocal osteomyelitis with periostitis and pustulosis
clinical_manifestations: Autosomal recessive life-threatening monogenic autoinflammatory disease caused by loss-of-function mutations in the IL1RN gene, leading to unopposed IL-1alpha and IL-1beta signaling
Perinatal or neonatal onset (birth to 2.5 weeks of life) characterized by the clinical triad of multifocal sterile osteomyelitis, extensive periostitis, and generalized pustular dermatosis

Cutaneous manifestations: crops of pinpoint-to-large sterile pustules on an erythematous base, generalized pustular psoriasis-like eruptions, severe palmoplantar pustulosis, ichthyosiform scaling, and severe oral mucosal ulcers
Nail changes: marked nail dystrophy with severe subungual pustules, onychomadesis, and pincer-like deformities

Musculoskeletal exam: prominent, painful, rock-hard bony swelling and exquisite tenderness over multiple skeletal sites, especially clavicles, anterior ribs, long bones of limbs, and digits (dactylitis); joint contractures and restricted mobility without high fever
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal Survey & Plain Radiographs (Pathognomonic Bony Features): Striking multifocal osteolytic bone lesions with profound, florid periosteal new bone formation ("ballooning" of clavicles, ribs, and long bones); pathognomonic massive cortical thickening and widening of the clavicles ("swollen clavicle sign")
Spinal Radiographs: Cervical and thoracic vertebral body collapse, flattening, and heterotopic ossification of anterior spinal ligaments

Whole-Body STIR MRI / Bone Scintigraphy: Intense multifocal signal hyperintensity and avid tracer uptake throughout the clavicles, proximal humeri, femora, ribs, and vertebral bodies demonstrating multifocal sterile osteitis and periostitis
pathology_manifestations: Bone Biopsy: Florid, intense osteomyelitis with extensive purulent infiltration by neutrophils and osteoclasts causing cortical bone resorption, surrounded by exuberant subperiosteal new bone formation, with completely sterile bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial cultures

Skin Punch Biopsy: Intraepidermal subcorneal pustules packed with neutrophils (spongiform pustules of Kogoj), marked acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, and papillary dermal edema with dense perivascular neutrophilic infiltration
Therapeutic Diagnostic Test: Instant, dramatic complete clinical and radiological remission upon administration of recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist (anakinra)
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: High-yield neonatal autoinflammatory disorder defined by striking visual clinical photos (widespread pustular rash, dystrophic nails, swollen tender joints) and unmistakable radiographic 'ballooned' clavicles and periosteal cloaks.

Rheumatology.name: Milwaukee Shoulder Syndrome
synonyms: Basic calcium phosphate crystal deposition disease of the shoulder
clinical_manifestations: Severe, rapidly progressive, highly destructive arthropathy occurring predominantly in elderly women (>70 years of age), caused by intra-articular deposition of basic calcium phosphate (BCP / hydroxyapatite) crystals
Physical examination: dramatic, massive, painless or moderately painful swelling and enlargement of the shoulder joint with complete loss of normal deltoid contour ("giant shoulder")
Pathognomonic fluid sign: large, tense, easily ballotable periarticular fluid collection extending into the subacromial/subdeltoid bursa and proximal arm with fluid wave
Prominent ecchymoses and cutaneous hematomas over the anterior chest wall and upper arm resulting from spontaneous capsular/synovial micro-ruptures
Profound loss of active glenohumeral motion with pseudoparalysis of the arm due to complete, catastrophic rupture of the rotator cuff, while passive range of motion remains preserved or hypermobile
radiological_manifestations: Shoulder Radiography (Pathognomonic Rapid Destruction): Striking superior migration of the humeral head with complete obliteration of the acromiohumeral distance (<5 mm), articulates directly against the under-surface of the acromion; rapid, severe resorption and flattening of the humeral head ("vanishing humeral head"); sclerosis and erosion of the acromion and glenoid

Shoulder MRI: Complete, massive tear of the rotator cuff tendons (supraspinatus, infraspinatus, subscapularis) with retraction, severe fatty atrophy of rotator cuff muscles, and enormous subacromial-subdeltoid bursal distension filled with complex debris

Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Massive anechoic-to-hypoechoic fluid collection in the glenohumeral joint and subdeltoid bursa, bare bone contact between humerus and acromion, and hyperechoic cloudy crystal aggregates
pathology_manifestations: Synovial Fluid Analysis (Pathognomonic Features): Hemorrhagic, dark red, or serosanguinous synovial fluid ("dishwater or port-wine fluid") with low leukocyte counts (<1,000-2,000 WBC/mcL, predominantly mononuclear cells); presence of amorphous shiny globular clumps on wet mount

Special Crystal Staining (Alizarin Red S): Intense bright red staining of rounded, amorphous basic calcium phosphate crystal clumps under light microscopy; crystals are non-birefringent under polarized light (distinguishing them from negatively birefringent MSU and positively birefringent CPPD)
Electron Microscopy (TEM / SEM): Spheroidal aggregates of rod-shaped hydroxyapatite crystals (needle-like individual crystals <0.1 μm)
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Visually arresting destructive crystal arthropathy featuring bedside photographs of giant bruised shoulders with rotator cuff pseudoparalysis and pathognomonic 'vanishing humeral head' on shoulder radiographs.

Rheumatology.name: CANDLE Syndrome
synonyms: Chronic atypical neutrophilic dermatosis with lipodystrophy and elevated temperature
clinical_manifestations: Rare autosomal recessive monogenic interferonopathy caused by loss-of-function mutations in proteasome subunit genes (predominantly PSMB8), leading to intracellular accumulation of ubiquitinated proteins and constitutive type I interferon signaling
Early infancy onset characterized by recurrent or continuous daily fevers, severe growth failure, microcytic anemia, and intellectual sparing
Pathognomonic facial appearance: striking, prominent violaceous periorbital edema and thick, swollen, violaceous eyelids ("monocle-like" facies), accompanied by thick, swollen, violaceous lips

Cutaneous plaques: recurrent, persistent, annular, violaceous to purpuric plaques with central fading and indurated borders distributed on the face, trunk, and extremities, lasting days to weeks and resolving with residual hyperpigmentation

Progressive lipodystrophy: dramatic, progressive loss of subcutaneous facial and upper-body adipose tissue, producing a gaunt, hollow-cheeked, aged facial contour contrasting with prominent hepatosplenomegaly, abdominal distension, and severe joint contractures
radiological_manifestations: Brain CT & MRI: Progressive, symmetric, punctate or coarse calcifications within the basal ganglia (globus pallidus, putamen, caudate nuclei) on non-contrast CT; cerebral atrophy with widened ventricles

Whole-Body MRI: Striking loss of subcutaneous fat in the face, neck, and upper trunk; hepatosplenomegaly; bone marrow signal alterations (osteopenia and diffuse subcortical hyperintensity on STIR sequences)
Echocardiogram: Progressive dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, pulmonary hypertension, and aortic root dilatation
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Pathognomonic Atypical Neutrophilic Infiltrate): Dense, diffuse interstitial and perivascular dermal infiltrate composed of atypical immature myeloid cells and mononuclear cells with convoluted or doughnut-shaped nuclei (atypical histiocytes/myelocytes), mixed with mature neutrophils, eosinophils, and lymphocytes
Panniculitis: Extension of the dense atypical infiltrate into subcutaneous adipose tissue causing lobular and septal panniculitis with progressive lipophagocytosis and adipocyte atrophy
Interferon Signature: Exceptionally high type I interferon gene expression score in peripheral blood mononuclear cells; marked elevation of interferon-inducible chemokines (CXCL9, CXCL10)
Rheumatology.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal monogenic interferonopathy presenting with unforgettable photographic facial features (violaceous periorbital monocle-like edema, swollen lips, progressive facial lipodystrophy) and basal ganglia calcifications on CT.

topics.name: Acute Aortic Dissection
synonyms: Stanford Type A / Type B dissection
clinical_manifestations: Sudden, catastrophic, tearing, ripping, or sharp chest/interscapular back pain
Asymmetric peripheral pulses (radial, femoral) with pulse deficit between arms (>20 mmHg)
Marfanoid habitus in younger patients (arachnodactyly, high-arched palate, pectus excavatum)
Horner syndrome (miosis, ptosis, anhidrosis from compression of sympathetic ganglion)
Acute murmur of aortic regurgitation and shock (cardiac tamponade)
radiological_manifestations: CT Angiography of Chest and Abdomen (Imaging Gold Standard): Pathognomonic intimal flap dividing the aorta into a true lumen and false lumen; differentiation between Stanford Type A (ascending aorta) and Type B (distal to left subclavian); identification of branch vessel compromise, hemopericardium, and intramural hematoma
Transesophageal Echocardiography (TEE): Mobile intimal flap in the ascending aorta, acute severe aortic regurgitation jet, pericardial tamponade
Chest Radiography: Widened superior mediastinum (>8 cm), obliteration of aortic knob, calcium sign (inward displacement of intimal calcification >10 mm from outer soft-tissue border)
pathology_manifestations: Surgical aortic resection: Cystic medial necrosis with fragmentation and loss of elastic fibers, basophilic pooling of ground substance (proteoglycans) within the media, cleavage plane within the outer third of the aortic media filled with fresh hematoma
topics.inclusion_rationale: Emergency vascular catastrophe with unmistakable physical exam pulse deficits, Marfan habitus, and Horner sign, diagnosed by the pathognomonic intimal flap separating true/false lumens on CTA.

topics.name: Anomalous Left Coronary Artery from the Pulmonary Artery
synonyms: Anomalous origin of left coronary artery from pulmonary trunk
clinical_manifestations: Infantile feeding angina ('episodic screaming'): Classic presentation between 4 and 12 weeks of age (coinciding with the physiological decline in pulmonary vascular resistance): recurrent paroxysms of acute irritability, vigorous crying, screaming, pallor, cold diaphoresis, and pulling up of the legs during or immediately following feeding or nursing, representing severe episodic myocardial ischemia / infantile angina pectoris

Severe congestive heart failure in infancy: Rapid development of tachypnea, intercostal grunting, wheezing, coughing, severe poor feeding, profound failure to thrive, listlessness, and cardiogenic shock
Precordial physical examination: Hyperdynamic, laterally and inferiorly displaced apical impulse; precordial heave; prominent third heart sound (S3) gallop

Cardiac auscultation: Harsh, high-pitched holosystolic regurgitant murmur best heard at the cardiac apex and radiating to the left axilla, resulting from ischemic mitral regurgitation due to papillary muscle necrosis/fibrosis and mitral annular dilatation; soft, continuous or mid-diastolic murmur audible over the upper left sternal border caused by extensive intercoronary collateral flow emptying into the pulmonary trunk

Electrocardiographic (ECG) hallmark: Characteristic anterolateral infantile myocardial infarction pattern: deep, wide, abnormal Q waves (> 30 ms and > 0.2 mV) with marked ST-segment elevation or T-wave inversion in leads I, aVL, and V4-V6, accompanied by loss of normal precordial R-wave progression
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic Echocardiography (TTE - Primary Diagnostic Modality): Direct anatomical visualization of the left main coronary artery arising anomalously from the posterolateral aspect of the main pulmonary artery trunk rather than the aortic sinus; Color and pulsed Doppler reveals pathognomonic retrograde, reversed flow from the left coronary artery into the pulmonary trunk ('coronary steal phenomenon'); markedly dilated and tortuous right coronary artery (RCA) originating normally from the aorta; extensive intercoronary collateral flow visualized as colorful mosaic color Doppler signals within the interventricular septum; severe left ventricular dilatation with global hypokinesia, depressed ejection fraction, and bright, hyperechogenic, scarred/calcified anterolateral papillary muscles with severe ischemic mitral regurgitation

Multidetector CT Angiography (MDCTA - Gold Standard 3D Vascular Mapping): Definitive non-invasive 3D volumetric depiction demonstrating the exact anomalous ostium of the left main coronary artery originating from the pulmonary artery, tracing the course of the dilated, tortuous RCA, mapping coronary collateral pathways, and providing preoperative anatomical roadmaps for surgical coronary transfer / aortic reimplantation

Cardiac MRI (CMR): Evaluates left ventricular volumes and systolic impairment; Late Gadolinium Enhancement (LGE) definitively delineates extensive subendocardial or transmural myocardial infarction involving the anterolateral LV free wall and papillary muscles; phase-contrast velocity mapping quantifies retrograde left coronary shunt volume
Chest Radiography: Marked, globular cardiomegaly with pronounced left ventricular configuration and prominent pulmonary venous congestion / interstitial pulmonary edema

Coronary Angiography (Catheterization): Aortic root or selective right coronary artery injection reveals an ectatic, giant RCA that retrogradely opacifies a dense network of septal and epicardial collaterals, which fill the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries retrogradely, finally emptying into the main pulmonary trunk
