Lipid Deposition: Extracellular lipid and cholesterol droplets within degenerate collagen bands demonstrated on oil red O or Sudan stains on frozen tissue
topics.inclusion_rationale: Hallmark pretibial granulomatous necrobiotic dermatosis presenting as waxy yellowish plaques with prominent arborizing telangiectasias, evaluated radiologically by high-frequency ultrasound demonstrating dermal thinning with horizontal hypoechoic bands, microvascular Doppler showing central hypoperfusion, and pathologically confirmed by the distinctive tiered 'layer-cake' granulomas with plasma cells and necrobiotic collagen.

topics.name: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma (NXG)
clinical_manifestations: Indurated, yellowish, red-orange to violaceous papules, plaques, and nodules that slowly enlarge, exhibiting a central atrophic, waxy yellowish depression with prominent arborizing telangiectasias, scar-like changes, and frequent painful, non-healing ulcerations

Pathognomonic periorbital predilection (>80% of patients): bilateral, symmetric yellowish plaques on upper and lower eyelids and periorbital skin, leading to severe ocular complications including cicatricial ectropion, ptosis, proptosis, lagophthalmos, scleritis, keratitis, and blindness
Extra-orbital involvement: trunk, extremities, and neck

Nearly universal association (>80-90% of cases) with monoclonal gammopathy, overwhelmingly an IgG kappa or lambda paraproteinemia; high risk of progression to multiple myeloma, smoldering myeloma, Waldenström macroglobulinemia, or lymphoproliferative disorders
Systemic internal organ xanthogranulomatous infiltrations: myocardium, pericardium, lungs, spleen, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system
radiological_manifestations: Orbital and Facial MRI / CT (High-Resolution T1, T2, T1+C): Extensive, bilateral, infiltrating, non-calcified soft tissue masses centered in the anterior and retrobulbar orbital spaces; masses are isointense to muscle on T1, heterogeneously hypointense to isointense on T2 (due to dense fibrosis and lipid), exhibiting avid, homogeneous post-contrast enhancement; frequently infiltrates extraocular muscles, lacrimal glands, and encases the optic nerve sheath without osseous destruction

Contrast-Enhanced Chest and Abdominal CT: Identifies systemic internal visceral lesions including solitary or multiple pulmonary nodules, pericardial thickening/effusion, myocardial xanthomatous masses, and retroperitoneal/mesenteric soft tissue infiltration

Skeletal Radiographic Survey / Low-Dose Whole-Body CT: Evaluates for osteolytic 'punched-out' bone lesions, severe osteoporosis, or pathologic fractures associated with underlying IgG monoclonal gammopathy and multiple myeloma
Cardiac MRI / Echocardiography: Detects myocardial nodular xanthogranulomas, pericardial infiltration, or restrictive cardiomyopathy secondary to systemic disease
pathology_manifestations: Massive Dermal and Subcutaneous Granulomatous Infiltrate: Broad, expansive granulomatous infiltrate replacing the entire reticular dermis and extending deep into the subcutaneous adipose tissue and skeletal muscle

Extensive Collagen Necrobiosis: Vast, irregular, geographic zones of degenerate, hypereosinophilic collagen necrobiosis with abundant cholesterol clefts (slit-like spaces where cholesterol crystals dissolved during processing)

Bizarre Multinucleated Giant Cells: Striking population of both classic Touton giant cells (wreath of nuclei with foamy periphery) and pathognomonic, enormous, bizarre foreign-body-type giant cells containing dozens to over a hundred hyperchromatic nuclei arranged irregularly or in florets
Infiltrate Components: Abundant lipid-laden foamy histiocytes, lymphocytes, plasma cells, and dense lymphoid aggregates with germinal centers
Immunohistochemistry: Histiocytes are intensely CD68+ and CD163+; negative for CD1a and Langerin (CD207)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Destructive paraproteinemia-associated granulomatous dermatosis characterized by periorbital xanthomatous plaques with ectropion, imaged on orbital MRI/CT by infiltrating retrobulbar masses, on skeletal CT by osteolytic myeloma lesions, and pathologically proven by extensive collagen necrobiosis with cholesterol clefts and bizarre Touton/foreign-body giant cells.

topics.name: Paraneoplastic Pemphigus
clinical_manifestations: Severe, intractable, excruciatingly painful mucosal ulcerations and hemorrhagic crusting involving the vermilion lip borders, tongue, buccal mucosa, palate, and oropharynx (stomatitis is the universal, earliest, and most recalcitrant clinical sign)
Severe bilateral erosive or pseudomembranous conjunctivitis, symblepharon formation, and progressive cicatricial ocular scarring that can lead to permanent visual impairment

Polymorphous cutaneous eruption displaying a spectrum of features: flaccid or tense bullae, necrotic erosions, targetoid erythema-multiforme-like lesions, dusky erythematous plaques, and lichenoid papules
Striking and excruciating palmoplantar sloughing, erosions, and painful erythema mimicking toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) or severe Stevens-Johnson syndrome

Life-threatening pulmonary involvement: progressive exertional dyspnea, non-productive cough, and severe hypoxemia secondary to acantholysis of bronchial and bronchiolar respiratory epithelium, progressing to irreversible, fatal bronchiolitis obliterans
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Computed Tomography (CECT) of Chest, Abdomen, and Pelvis: High-yield identification of occult lymphoproliferative neoplasms or hematologic malignancies; pathognomonic detection of Castleman disease (unicentric hyaline-vascular type presenting as a sharply demarcated, hypervascular retroperitoneal, pelvic, or mediastinal mass with avid homogeneous arterial enhancement and branching central calcifications), follicular non-Hodgkin lymphoma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), or thymoma

High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of Chest: In patients with respiratory symptoms, HRCT demonstrates hallmark findings of bronchiolitis obliterans: geographic mosaic attenuation with low-attenuation areas of air trapping accentuated on dynamic expiratory scans, central and peripheral bronchial wall thickening, peribronchial cuffing, and cylindrical bronchiectasis in the absence of mucous plugging
18F-FDG PET/CT: Differentiates indolent Castleman disease from aggressive transformed lymphomas, accurately staging occult disease and guiding percutaneous or surgical core needle biopsy
pathology_manifestations: Cutaneous and Mucosal Histopathology: Hallmark combination of intraepidermal suprabasal acantholysis (forming intraepidermal clefts, blisters, and tombstone-pattern basal layer retention) coexisting with interface dermatitis (vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer, apoptotic necrotic keratinocytes throughout the epidermis, and a lichenoid band-like mononuclear dermal infiltrate)

Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Demonstrates both cell surface (intercellular) IgG and/or C3 deposition within the epidermis ('fish-net' pattern) AND continuous granular or linear deposition of IgG and C3 along the epidermal basement membrane zone (BMZ)

Indirect Immunofluorescence (IIF) on Rat Bladder Epithelium: Highly specific (approaching 100% specificity for PNP), exhibiting intense intercellular IgG staining on transitional epithelium (which expresses high levels of plakin proteins but lacks desmoglein 1/3, thus distinguishing PNP from classical pemphigus vulgaris)

Immunoprecipitation and Immunoblotting: Demonstrates circulating autoantibodies targeting a complex of plakin family proteins: envoplakin (210 kDa), periplakin (190 kDa), desmoplakin I (250 kDa) and II (210 kDa), plectin (500 kDa), BP230, desmoglein 1 and 3, and alpha-2-macroglobulin-like-1 (A2ML1)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Landmark paraneoplastic autoimmune syndrome uniting intractable hemorrhagic stomatitis, polymorphous bullae, and fatal bronchiolitis obliterans with CT detection of occult retroperitoneal Castleman disease or lymphoma and rat-bladder IIF plakin autoimmunity.

topics.name: Pemphigus Vulgaris
clinical_manifestations: Painful, extensive, persistent oral mucosal ulcerations and erosions (buccal mucosa, palate, gingiva)
Flaccid, thin-walled, clear-fluid cutaneous bullae arising on normal or erythematous skin that rupture easily
Raw, painful, denuded, weeping erosions that bleed easily and fail to heal without therapy
Positive Nikolsky sign (detachment of superficial epidermis upon light rubbing of peri-lesional skin)
Scalp, face, neck, axillae, groin, and perineum predilection
radiological_manifestations: Barium Esophagram / Endoscopy / CT: Esophagitis dissecans superficialis (severe sloughing and peeling of the esophageal squamous epithelium, 'cast' formation)
Chest CT: Aspiration pneumonia secondary to severe dysphagia and pharyngeal denudation
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy: Intraepidermal suprabasal acantholysis with blister formation; 'row of tombstones' appearance of basal keratinocytes attached to the basement membrane
Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 in a net-like or 'fishnet' / chicken-wire pattern throughout the epidermis (targeting desmoglein 3 and 1)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic intraepidermal bullous disease with flaccid blisters, Nikolsky sign, and oral mucosal sloughing, alongside esophagrams demonstrating esophageal lining detachment (esophagitis dissecans superficialis).

topics.name: Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Striking, pathognomonic mucocutaneous pigmented macules (lentigines): discrete, flat, dark brown to black round or oval macules (1-5 mm) densely clustered around the vermilion border of the lips, perioral cutaneous margins, buccal mucosa, hard palate, tongue, nostrils, perianal skin, and volar fingertips
Pigmented macules typically appear in infancy or early childhood; mucosal macules characteristically persist throughout life, whereas facial cutaneous macules may fade in adulthood
Recurrent episodes of severe colicky abdominal pain, small bowel mechanical obstruction, and rectal bleeding/melena
Gynecomastia, accelerated bone age, and sexual precocity in prepubertal boys (due to estrogen-secreting testicular tumors)
radiological_manifestations: CT Enterography / MR Enterography: Multiple discrete, lobulated, pedunculated or sessile polyps throughout the gastrointestinal tract (predominantly jejunum, ileum, and duodenum); hallmark visualization of acute transient or fixed small bowel intussusceptions demonstrating classic 'target sign', 'donut sign', or sausage-shaped soft-tissue mass with lead-point polyps on ultrasound and CT
Pelvic Ultrasound / MRI: Sex cord tumors with annular tubules (SCTAT) of the ovary presenting as bilateral small, solid, calcified ovarian masses in females; adenoma malignum of the cervix
Scrotal Ultrasound: Bilateral, multifocal, bright intratesticular calcifications with acoustic shadowing diagnostic of Large Cell Calcifying Sertoli Cell Tumors (LCCSCT)
pathology_manifestations: Gastrointestinal Hamartomatous Polyp Histopathology: Pathognomonic architectural structure consisting of an extensive, arborizing, branching tree-like network of well-developed smooth muscle bundles (derived from the muscularis mucosae) that forms a structural core supporting hyperplastic, mature glandular mucosa with normal cellular differentiation

Mucocutaneous Macule Punch Biopsy: Marked increase in melanin pigmentation concentrated within keratinocytes of the epidermal basal layer and abundant melanophages nestled in the upper papillary dermis, without atypical melanocytic proliferation or significant increase in melanocyte numbers
topics.inclusion_rationale: Signature hamartomatous polyposis syndrome with pathognomonic perioral/mucosal melanocytic lentigines, matched with CT enterographic lead-point intussusceptions ('target sign'), testicular/ovarian sex-cord calcifications on ultrasound, and arborizing smooth muscle polyps on histology.

topics.name: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda
clinical_manifestations: Marked mechanical cutaneous fragility and photodistributed skin vulnerability confined to sun-exposed regions, most prominently the dorsal hands, extensor forearms, neck, and face
Tense subepidermal bullae and vesicles developing after trivial mechanical friction or sun exposure, rapidly rupturing into painful crusted erosions
Healing with characteristic tiny, firm, white inclusion cysts (milia), superficial atrophic scarring, and irregular mottled postinflammatory hyperpigmentation
Facial hypertrichosis featuring fine, dark, lanugo-like hairs developing over the malar prominences, temples, and periorbital margins
Sclerodermoid (morphea-like) induration with waxy yellowish thickened plaques on the chest, back, and face in longstanding disease
Dark reddish-brown or tea-colored urine exhibiting striking, brilliant coral-pink to red fluorescence under Wood's lamp examination (365 nm UVA)
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal MRI with Quantitative Iron Relaxometry (T2* / R2* Mapping): Marked diffuse loss of hepatic parenchymal signal intensity on T2-weighted and T2*-weighted gradient-echo sequences, directly quantifying hepatic iron overload (hemosiderosis) and guiding therapeutic phlebotomy

Multiphasic Liver CT / MRI: Assessment of underlying hepatic architectural changes (cirrhotic nodular surface, splenomegaly, ascites) and mandatory surveillance detection of hypervascular arterial-enhancing nodular lesions diagnostic of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
Abdominal Ultrasound: Diffuse coarse increase in hepatic parenchymal echogenicity secondary to hepatic steatosis, iron deposition, and progressive portal fibrosis
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy of Fresh Blister: Cell-poor, pauci-inflammatory subepidermal bulla with preserved, intact dermal papillae protruding upward into the blister lumen in an undulating, undulating pattern ('festooning of dermal papillae'); prominent eosinophilic PAS-positive, diastase-resistant hyaline cuffs encasing the superficial dermal microvasculature; intraepidermal eosinophilic globoid 'caterpillar bodies' representing degraded basement membrane components within the blister roof
Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Broad, homogeneous linear deposition of IgG and C3 (and to a lesser extent IgM) encircling upper dermal capillary walls and lining the dermo-epidermal junction

Liver Core Biopsy: Marked hemosiderin deposition primarily within periportal hepatocytes and Kupffer cells (confirmed with Perls' Prussian blue stain), accompanied by variable steatohepatitis; frozen unfixed liver tissue demonstrates needle-shaped birefringent uroporphyrin crystals showing bright red autofluorescence under fluorescence microscopy
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential photo-induced metabolic dermatosis combining dorsal hand mechanical blistering, milia, and facial hypertrichosis with tea-colored fluorescent urine, hepatic T2* MRI iron overload quantification, and festooned cell-poor subepidermal histology.

topics.name: Pseudoxanthoma Elasticum
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic yellowish, cobblestone-like or 'plucked-chicken skin' papules and confluent plaques primarily on the lateral neck and flexural folds (axillae, antecubital fossae, groin)
Progressive redundancy and laxity of skin in flexural creases forming prominent hanging folds

Angioid streaks on fundoscopic examination (breaks in calcified Bruch membrane radiating outward from the optic disc) with 'peau d'orange' mottling and subretinal choroidal neovascularization leading to retinal hemorrhages and central vision loss
Mucosal involvement with discrete yellowish submucosal papules on the inner aspect of the lower lip and buccal mucosa
Accelerated peripheral vascular insufficiency manifested by diminished or absent peripheral pulses, early-onset intermittent claudication, and cold extremities
Recurrent upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage from friable, calcified submucosal gastric vessels
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography of Extremities: Extensive, symmetric, fine linear 'tram-track' arterial wall calcifications along medium-sized muscular arteries (femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial, and radial arteries) in young adult patients

Non-Contrast Computed Tomography (CT): Extensive calcification of peripheral, visceral (mesenteric, renal), and cerebral arteries (particularly internal carotid siphon and vertebrobasilar arteries); premature coronary artery calcification on cardiac CT calcium scoring

Scrotal and Abdominal Ultrasound: Diffuse, fine, non-shadowing testicular microlithiasis ('snowstorm' pattern in bilateral testes); medullary nephrocalcinosis and acoustic shadowing along splenic and intrahepatic arterial branches
Screening Mammography: Distinctive linear and punctate microcalcifications tracing intramammary arterial walls with high specificity

Fundus Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) & Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): Angioid streaks appearing as irregular hyperfluorescent radial cracks, subretinal fluid, retinal pigment epithelium detachment, and choroidal neovascular membranes (CNVM)
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (Mid-to-Deep Reticular Dermis): Clumped, curled, fragmented, and swollen basophilic elastic fibers displaying a distinct 'ravelled wool' or 'ant-eaten' appearance on routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)

Special Histochemical Stains: von Kossa and Alizarin Red stains demonstrate dense calcium phosphate mineralization coating and encrusting the fragmented elastic fibers; Verhoeff-van Gieson (VVG) stain highlights irregular, fragmented, shortened black/blue elastic fibers

Arterial Wall Histology: Massive fragmentation and dense calcification concentrated within the internal elastic lamina of medium- and small-caliber muscular arteries, accompanied by secondary luminal narrowing and reactive intimal fibroplasia
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic heritable elastic tissue disorder marrying hallmark flexural 'plucked-chicken skin' and fundoscopic angioid streaks with striking peripheral 'tram-track' arterial calcifications on plain radiography/CT and von Kossa-positive fragmented dermal elastic fibers.

topics.name: Psoriasis Vulgaris
clinical_manifestations: Well-demarcated, erythematous plaques covered by thick, silvery-white micaceous scales (extensor elbows, knees, scalp, lumbosacral)
Auspitz sign: punctate bleeding points upon removal of scales
Koebner phenomenon (isomorphic response to epidermal trauma)
Psoriatic nail changes (pitting, oil-drop discoloration, subungual hyperkeratosis)
Guttate, inverse (intertriginous flexural), and generalized pustular (von Zumbusch) variants
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Ultrasound (HFUS) of Skin: Epidermal thickening, subepidermal hypoechoic band (dermal edema), hypervascularity on power Doppler
Joint and Entheseal Ultrasound: Subclinical enthesopathy (Achilles, plantar fascia) in cutaneous psoriasis patients
Plain Radiography / MRI (screening for concomitant PsA): Asymmetric periostitis and entheseal new bone formation
pathology_manifestations: Skin punch biopsy: Marked regular epidermal hyperplasia (acanthosis) with elongation of rete ridges ('test tubes in a rack'), hyperkeratosis with confluent parakeratosis, hypogranulosis, Munro microabscesses (neutrophils in stratum corneum), spongiform pustules of Kogoj, tortuous dilated capillary loops in dermal papillae
topics.inclusion_rationale: Core skin disease with unmistakable clinical plaques and nail changes paired with cutaneous high-frequency ultrasound and musculoskeletal imaging of concomitant enthesitis.

topics.name: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
clinical_manifestations: Rapidly progressive, agonizingly painful ulceration starting as an inflammatory pustule or furuncle
Pathognomonic undermined, violaceous, gunmetal-blue borders
Purulent, cribriform (sieve-like) necrotic ulcer base with foul exudate
Marked pathergy (ulcer enlargement or new lesion development following minor trauma, debridement, or venipuncture)
Heals with characteristic cribriform or 'cigarette paper' atrophic scarring
Peristomal pyoderma gangrenosum (around stomas in patients with inflammatory bowel disease)
radiological_manifestations: Soft Tissue Ultrasound / MRI: Marked subcutaneous edema, absence of necrotizing fascial fluid or gas (differentiating from necrotizing fasciitis)
CT / MR Enterography: Underlying inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease with transmural bowel thickening or Ulcerative Colitis)
Skeletal Radiography / CT: Underlying associated arthritis or hematologic malignancy (myelodysplastic syndrome bone marrow changes)
pathology_manifestations: Skin ulcer edge biopsy: Massive, dense, suppurative neutrophilic infiltration of the dermis with leukocytoclasia, tissue necrosis, and secondary endothelial swelling; lack of true primary vasculitis or infectious pathogens
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential neutrophilic ulcer with signature undermined violaceous borders and cribriform base, paired with abdominal CT enterography of associated IBD and soft-tissue MRI to rule out deep fascial infection.

topics.name: Reactive Perforating Collagenosis
clinical_manifestations: Eruption of multiple, intensely pruritic, discrete, umbilicated, dome-shaped erythematous to hyperpigmented papules and nodules (2 to 10 mm in diameter)
Pathognomonic firmly adherent, central, hard, dark brown-to-black hyperkeratotic crust or keratinous plug lodged in a central cup-shaped crater

Classic distribution over extensor surfaces of limbs (forearms, shins, thighs) and trunk, prominently demonstrating the Koebner phenomenon (linear arrays of eruptive papules induced by scratching or minor trauma)

Highly prevalent acquired association (>10% of patients with end-stage renal disease [ESRD] undergoing chronic hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis and patients with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus with microvascular complications)
Removal of the central plug causes pinpoint hemorrhage and is rapidly followed by reformation of the keratinous crater
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasound: Demonstrates bilateral, symmetrically small, shrunken, hyper-echogenic kidneys with severe cortical thinning (<1 cm) and loss of normal corticomedullary differentiation indicative of end-stage renal parenchymal disease (diabetic nephropathy or hypertensive nephrosclerosis); may show acquired cystic disease of uremia with multiple bilateral simple or complex cysts

Plain Radiography of Extremities: Extensive, symmetric, continuous 'pipe-stem' arterial wall calcifications along the femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial, and dorsalis pedis arteries characteristic of Mönckeberg medial calcific sclerosis; reveals severe renal osteodystrophy (subperiosteal cortical bone resorption along radial aspects of middle phalanges, terminal tuft acro-osteolysis, and 'salt-and-pepper' skull)

Plain Radiographs of Spine: Demonstrates pathognomonic 'rugger-jersey spine' (dense, sclerotic bands across the superior and inferior vertebral endplates with central lucency) reflecting secondary hyperparathyroidism in ESRD
Dermoscopy: Central yellow-brown to dark keratotic core surrounded by a structureless white or pink halo and a peripheral rim of dotted and hairpin vessels
pathology_manifestations: Cutaneous Biopsy (Including Central Crater and Underlying Dermis): Cup-shaped or saucer-shaped epidermal invagination filled with a massive, compact plug of parakeratin, orthokeratin, degenerated basophilic nuclear debris, and inflammatory cells

Transepidermal Elimination: Disruption and perforation of the epidermal basement membrane at the base of the invagination with vertically oriented, altered, degenerated basophilic collagen bundles streaming upward from the papillary dermis directly into the epidermal crater
Masson Trichrome Special Stain: Vividly stains the perforating degenerated collagen bundles blue/green, highlighting their vertical extrusion through the epidermal cleft
Verhoeff-van Gieson (VVG) Special Stain: Demonstrates that elastic fibers are fragmented and remain excluded from the crater, distinguishing RPC from elastosis perforans serpiginosa
von Kossa / Alizarin Red Stains: Negative for calcium deposits within the plug or collagen, differentiating from perforating calcinosis cutis
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic perforating dermatosis coupling hallmark umbilicated papules with central keratinous plugs in dialysis-dependent renal failure with renal ultrasound of shrunken kidneys, Mönckeberg calcifications, and Masson trichrome collagen elimination.

topics.name: Scleredema Adultorum of Buschke
clinical_manifestations: Insidious, symmetric, non-pitting, woody, indurated thickening and tightening of the skin characteristically beginning on the nape and lateral aspects of the neck and posterior upper back
Progressive spread over the shoulders, upper arms, chest wall, and occasionally the face, resulting in a mask-like facial appearance and restricted neck and shoulder range of motion
Characteristic 'peau d'orange' (orange peel) skin surface texture with prominent follicular ostia and complete loss of normal skin folds; skin cannot be pinched or wrinkled
Pathognomonic sparing of the hands and feet (absence of sclerodactyly, Raynaud phenomenon, or telangiectasias, cleanly distinguishing scleredema from systemic sclerosis/scleroderma)

Three recognized distinct clinical subsets: (1) Type 1: Post-infectious acute scleredema (typically preceded by streptococcal pharyngitis or viral infection in young females, often self-limiting); (2) Type 2: Paraproteinemia-associated chronic progressive scleredema (associated with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance [MGUS], multiple myeloma, or amyloidosis); (3) Type 3: Scleredema diabeticorum (occurring in middle-aged, obese individuals with longstanding, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus with severe insulin resistance and microvascular disease)
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Ultrasound (HFUS, 20-50 MHz) of Dermis: Demonstrates profound, diffuse thickening of the reticular dermis (often measuring 3 to 5 times thicker than unaffected skin) with marked hypoechogenicity reflecting abundant interstitial mucin and edema; demonstrates a sharply demarcated, intact dermal-subcutaneous boundary with complete sparing of subcutaneous fat and deep fascia

Soft Tissue Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of Neck and Upper Torso: Demonstrates marked diffuse thickening of the cutaneous and dermal layer; the expanded dermis is isointense to hypointense on T1-weighted images and markedly hyperintense on T2-weighted, STIR, and fat-suppressed sequences owing to high mucin (acid glycosaminoglycan) and free water content; crucially confirms normal appearance, signal, and absence of thickening or enhancement of the deep muscular fascia and skeletal muscle (distinguishing scleredema from eosinophilic fasciitis and dermatomyositis)

Whole-Body Low-Dose CT (WBLDCT) or Skeletal Survey: Evaluates patients with Type 2 scleredema for punched-out lytic bone lesions, osteosclerosis, or diffuse osteopenia indicative of underlying multiple myeloma or systemic plasma cell dyscrasias
Transthoracic Echocardiography: Assesses for diastolic dysfunction and restrictive cardiomyopathy in patients with paraproteinemia-associated deposition disease
pathology_manifestations: Full-Thickness Skin Incisional / Punch Biopsy (Extending into Subcutis): Demonstrates striking, massive thickening of the reticular dermis (up to 300-400% of normal dermal depth) characterized by markedly swollen, thickened, broad collagen bundles separated by wide, clear fenestrations and spaces (interstitial edema and mucin)

Preservation of Surrounding Structures: Unremarkable overlying epidermis, normal pilosebaceous and sweat gland adnexa, and absence of inflammatory infiltrate, cellular atypia, or vasculitis; subcutaneous fat lobules are normal, with broad collagen bands occasionally extending between fat cells

Alcian Blue (pH 2.5) & Colloidal Iron Special Stains: Strongly stain the clear fenestrations between collagen bundles bright turquoise/blue, confirming extensive extracellular deposition of non-sulfated acid mucopolysaccharides (hyaluronic acid)
Hyaluronidase Digestion: Completely abolishes the Alcian blue and colloidal iron staining, confirming hyaluronic acid as the principal accumulating glycosaminoglycan
Masson Trichrome & Verhoeff-van Gieson (VVG): Normal collagen and normal or slightly diminished elastic fibers without dermal fibrosis or elastorrhexis
topics.inclusion_rationale: Landmark deposition dermatosis characterized by woody neck/back induration with hand-sparing, where high-frequency ultrasound and soft-tissue MRI prove isolated dermal mucin thickening while sparing muscular fascia, and Alcian blue confirms hyaluronidase-sensitive mucin.

topics.name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
clinical_manifestations: Dusky, purpuric, atypical targetoid macules rapidly coalescing across the face, trunk, and extremities
Extensive flaccid epidermal bullae and sheet-like full-thickness sloughing of epidermis leaving raw, weeping, denuded dermis ('scalded skin')
Positive Nikolsky sign (shearing of epidermis upon gentle lateral digital pressure)
Positive Asboe-Hansen sign (lateral extension of bulla upon direct pressure)
Severe mucositis of >=2 surfaces: hemorrhagic crusting of vermilion lips, oral stomatitis, severe purulent conjunctivitis, pseudomembranes, genital/urethral erosions
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / CT: Acute pulmonary complications: tracheobronchial mucosal sloughing, non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, diffuse ground-glass infiltrates, chemical pneumonitis, bacterial superinfection
pathology_manifestations: Frozen section / Formalin-fixed biopsy: Full-thickness epidermal necrosis and detachment, subepidermal separation, extensive keratinocyte apoptosis, satellite cell necrosis, minimal superficial dermal perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate
topics.inclusion_rationale: Dramatic dermatologic emergency featuring full-thickness sheet sloughing and severe mucositis with chest imaging demonstrating tracheobronchial sloughing and ARDS.

topics.name: Subcorneal Pustular Dermatosis (Sneddon-Wilkinson Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Chronic, recurrent eruption of sterile, flaccid, pea-sized pustules grouped in annular, circinate, polycyclic, or serpiginous patterns

Pathognomonic 'Half-and-Half' Pustule Sign: pustules characteristically settle under the influence of gravity, such that purulent cellular debris forms a horizontal sediment in the lower half of the blister while clear serous fluid fills the upper half
Predilection for flexural aspects of the trunk and extremities: axillae, groins, submammary folds, inframammary regions, and lower abdomen; face, palms, and soles are characteristically spared

Pustules are extremely fragile and rupture rapidly within hours to days, leaving superficial circular or annular erythematous erosions with fine, collarette-like scaling and residual brown hyperpigmentation without scarring

Strong clinical association with monoclonal gammopathy, overwhelmingly an IgA paraproteinemia, which may herald or accompany multiple myeloma, smoldering myeloma, pyoderma gangrenosum, or inflammatory bowel disease
Remarkable and rapid clinical response to oral dapsone therapy, often within 48 to 72 hours
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS, 20-50 MHz): Identifies very superficial, subcorneal, anechoic to hypoechoic lenticular fluid pockets strictly localized to the uppermost stratum corneum and intraepidermal interface, with a thin roof and acoustic transmission; underlying dermis shows minimal, mild perivascular edema without deep subcutaneous expansion

Skeletal Radiographic Survey / Low-Dose Whole-Body CT: Essential screening for associated IgA multiple myeloma, identifying 'punched-out' osteolytic bone lesions of the calvarium, pelvis, spine, and long bones, or vertebral compression fractures
Chest CT and Abdominal CT: Evaluates for underlying systemic plasma cell neoplasms, solitary plasmacytomas, or occult lymphoproliferative disorders
Abdominal Ultrasound / Colonoscopy Imaging: Evaluates for concurrent inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis) in patients presenting with relapsing flexural pustulosis
pathology_manifestations: Subcorneal Cleavage: Large, unilocular pustules located directly beneath the stratum corneum, resting directly on the underlying stratum spinosum
Neutrophilic Content: The pustular cavity is filled overwhelmingly with mature, well-preserved polymorphonuclear neutrophils, with occasional eosinophils, and complete absence of acantholytic cells

Underlying Epidermis: The underlying spinous epidermis remains essentially intact, exhibiting minimal to mild intercellular edema (spongiosis) without acantholysis or significant spongiform pustule formation (distinguishing it from generalized pustular psoriasis)
Dermal Infiltrate: Superficial perivascular inflammatory infiltrate composed of neutrophils, lymphocytes, and histiocytes in the upper papillary dermis

Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF): Strictly negative for intercellular or basement membrane zone antibodies (negative for IgG, IgA, IgM, and C3), which is the essential diagnostic criteria ruling out subcorneal IgA pemphigus
topics.inclusion_rationale: Relapsing sterile pustular dermatosis with the pathognomonic 'half-and-half' gravity sign and IgA paraproteinemia association, monitored by high-frequency skin ultrasound showing superficial subcorneal fluid cavities, screened by skeletal radiography/CT for osteolytic myeloma lesions, and pathologically confirmed by subcorneal neutrophilic pustules without acantholysis or DIF positivity.

topics.name: Subcutaneous Granuloma Annulare (Deep Granuloma Annulare)
clinical_manifestations: Solitary or multiple, firm, non-tender, immobile or mobile deep dermal and subcutaneous nodules measuring 0.5 to 5 cm in diameter
Predominantly affects young children (peak age 2 to 6 years) who are otherwise healthy and lack systemic symptoms
Characteristic anatomic distribution: lower extremities (especially the anterior pretibial shins), dorsal hands and feet, fingers, buttocks, and scalp
Overlying skin typically appears completely normal, slightly violaceous, or flesh-colored, without epidermal scaling, ulceration, or ring-like surface morphology
Rapid initial growth over weeks often alarms clinicians and parents, raising concern for deep soft tissue sarcoma (epithelioid sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma) or rheumatoid nodules
Spontaneous regression occurs over months to several years without scar formation; recurrent lesions may develop at identical or distant sites
radiological_manifestations: Musculoskeletal MRI (Extremity / Soft Tissue): Infiltrative or well-demarcated nodular mass centered within the deep subcutaneous fat directly abutting or tracking along the deep muscular fascia; isointense to hypointense to muscle on T1-weighted images; heterogeneously hyperintense or target-like on T2-weighted and STIR images; demonstrates marked, avid, heterogeneous or thick peripheral nodular enhancement following intravenous gadolinium; absence of bone invasion or cortical breach

High-Frequency Soft Tissue Ultrasound: Well-defined or lobulated, uniformly hypoechoic subcutaneous mass abutting the underlying muscular fascia or periosteum without bony erosion; color Doppler shows minimal to moderate peripheral vascularity without high-velocity internal arteriovenous shunting (distinguishing it from vascular malformations or aggressive sarcomas)
Plain Radiography: Soft tissue nodular prominence without internal calcification (excluding phleboliths, calcinosis, or tumoral calcinosis) and completely normal underlying bone architecture
pathology_manifestations: Deep Subcutaneous Palisading Granulomas: Large, discrete or confluent granulomatous foci centered within the deep reticular dermis and extending broadly into subcutaneous adipose septa and lobules
Necrobiotic Core: Central expansive zones of pale, basophilic necrobiosis (altered, smudged collagen) containing abundant interstitial mucin (hyaluronic acid)

Colloidal Iron / Alcian Blue Stains: Intense, bright blue staining within the necrobiotic centers confirming abundant hyaluronic acid mucin, a key histological hallmark distinguishing SGA from rheumatoid nodules
Palisading Border: Palisade of activated CD68+ histiocytes, epithelioid macrophages, and multinucleated giant cells surrounding the necrobiotic mucinous cores

Differential Exclusions: Complete absence of neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells (differentiating from necrobiosis lipoidica); absence of central fibrinoid necrosis surrounded by CD3+ T-cells (differentiating from classic rheumatoid nodules); negative fungal and mycobacterial stains
topics.inclusion_rationale: Deep granulomatous condition of childhood presenting as firm non-tender subcutaneous nodules mimicking soft tissue sarcoma, characterized on extremity MRI by fascial-abutting hyperintense avidly enhancing masses, and pathologically defined by palisading granulomas surrounding mucin-rich (alcian blue+) necrobiotic collagen.

topics.name: Sweet Syndrome (Acute Febrile Neutrophilic Dermatosis)
clinical_manifestations: Sudden onset of painful, tender, sharply demarcated erythematous to violaceous succulent papules, plaques, and nodules with a characteristic mammillated or pseudovesicular/pustular surface caused by intense upper dermal edema
High spiking fevers (often >38.5°C) accompanying the eruption and dramatic peripheral neutrophilic leukocytosis (>10,000/µL with left shift)
Predilection for the upper extremities (dorsum of hands, forearms), head, neck, and upper trunk; lesions often exhibit an annular or arciform configuration with central clearing
Extracutaneous manifestations including severe arthralgias/arthritis (knees, wrists), ocular inflammation (conjunctivitis, episcleritis, iridocyclitis), and oral aphthous-like ulcerations

Association with hematologic neoplasms (acute myeloid leukemia, myelodysplastic syndrome in up to 20%), inflammatory bowel disease, infections, and medications (especially granulocyte colony-stimulating factor [G-CSF], all-trans retinoic acid [ATRA])
Rapid and dramatic therapeutic response to systemic corticosteroids (prompt defervescence within 48-72 hours)
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS, 20-50 MHz): Marked, pathognomonic hypoechoic band in the upper papillary dermis directly subjacent to an intact epidermis representing massive papillary dermal edema; absence of true fluid collections or abscess cavities (confirming pseudovesicular nature); increased dermal Doppler vascularity during acute flares

Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT: Multiple bilateral pulmonary opacities representing aseptic pulmonary Sweet syndrome / neutrophilic alveolitis, presenting as patchy peribronchovascular consolidations, ground-glass opacities, pleural effusions, and mediastinal/hilar lymphadenopathy that rapidly clear under systemic steroids

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal and Pelvic CT: Splenomegaly and multiple ill-defined, low-attenuation sterile splenic or hepatic lesions (neutrophilic microabscesses) that fail antibiotic therapy but resolve with steroids; mesenteric lymphadenopathy and screening for occult visceral malignancy or pelvic tumors

18F-FDG PET/CT: Intense focal hypermetabolism corresponding to active cutaneous plaques, splenic lesions, pulmonary infiltrates, and evaluation of underlying hematologic marrow involvement (diffuse hypermetabolism in AML/MDS transformation)
Musculoskeletal MRI: Periarticular soft tissue edema, joint effusion, and sterile tenosynovitis in symptomatic joints without underlying cortical erosions
pathology_manifestations: Skin Punch Biopsy (H&E): Striking, massive papillary dermal edema causing separation of collagen bundles and the clinical appearance of pseudovesicles, without intraepidermal blister formation

Dermal Infiltrate: Dense, band-like or nodular inflammatory infiltrate in the papillary and upper-to-mid reticular dermis composed overwhelmingly of mature, morphologically intact neutrophils with prominent leukocytoclasia (nuclear dust / karyorrhexis)

Absence of Primary Vasculitis: True leukocytoclastic vasculitis is absent (no primary fibrinoid necrosis of post-capillary venule walls, no erythrocyte extravasation into vessel walls); any minor vessel alteration is strictly secondary to bystander cytokine injury

Histiocytoid Sweet Syndrome Variant: Infiltrate composed predominantly of immature, myeloid-lineage mononuclear cells with histiocytoid reniform nuclei expressing myeloperoxidase (MPO), CD68, and CD43
Special Stains: Gram, PAS, and Fite/Grocott silver stains are strictly negative for bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial microorganisms; negative direct immunofluorescence (DIF)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic acute neutrophilic dermatosis characterized clinically by tender succulent pseudovesicular plaques and high fever, diagnostically evaluated radiologically by high-frequency skin ultrasound showing massive papillary dermal edema and chest/abdominal CT revealing aseptic pulmonary consolidations and splenic microabscesses, and pathologically confirmed by dense dermal neutrophilia with striking papillary edema without primary vasculitis.

topics.name: Wells Syndrome (Eosinophilic Cellulitis)
clinical_manifestations: Sudden, recurrent eruption of intensely itchy, stinging, or burning erythematous and edematous plaques that rapidly expand over 2-3 days to involve large cutaneous areas, clinically masquerading as severe bacterial cellulitis or erysipelas
Eruption frequently preceded by prodromal tingling, burning, or paresthesias; fails multiple courses of systemic antibacterial therapy
Evolution over several days into distinctive, indurated, firm, morphea-like or woody plaques with violaceous, dusky, or slate-blue/slate-gray advancing borders and central involution
Frequent formation of tense bullae, vesicles, or petechiae overlying the edematous plaques
Predilection for extremities, trunk, and face; resolves without scarring over 2-8 weeks, leaving temporary hyperpigmentation

Prominent peripheral blood eosinophilia (>50-60% of patients) during acute flares, accompanied by elevated serum eosinophil cationic protein (ECP) and total IgE; triggered by arthropod bites, viral/parasitic infections, medications, or hematologic disorders
radiological_manifestations: Soft Tissue MRI (T1, T2, STIR, T1+C): Extensive, diffuse cutaneous thickening and marked hyperintensity of the subcutaneous fat and superficial fascia on T2-weighted and STIR sequences (representing profound inflammatory edema); diffuse reticular enhancement post-contrast; crucial absence of discrete loculated fluid collections, drainable abscess cavities, intramuscular fluid, or soft tissue gas, radiologically excluding bacterial necrotizing fasciitis/cellulitis

High-Frequency Cutaneous Ultrasound (HFUS): Marked hypoechoic expansion of the dermis with a characteristic 'cobblestone' pattern in the subcutaneous tissue due to fluid tracking along fat lobules and septa; absence of hypoechoic liquefactive abscess pockets; power Doppler reveals diffuse hyperemia in acute phases
Plain Radiography: Excludes subcutaneous gas, radiopaque foreign bodies, or adjacent periosteal reaction
pathology_manifestations: Dynamic Triphasic Histological Evolution: Striking, diagnostic progression through acute, subacute, and resolution phases

Acute Phase: Massive dermal edema with an intense, diffuse inflammatory infiltrate dominated by mature eosinophils spreading through the reticular dermis and tracking along subcutaneous fibrous septa, without vasculitis

Subacute Phase (Pathognomonic): Formation of classic, diagnostic 'flame figures' (figures en flamme), composed of degenerate dermal collagen bundles coated with brightly eosinophilic granules of degranulated eosinophil major basic protein (MBP), surrounded by a palisade of CD68+ histiocytes and multinucleated foreign-body giant cells
Resolution Phase: Gradual phagocytosis of flame figures by histiocytic giant cells, disappearance of eosinophils, and mild dermal interstitial fibrosis
Immunohistochemistry: Extracellular granular deposition of eosinophil major basic protein (MBP) and eosinophil-derived neurotoxin (EDN) decorating the flame figures
topics.inclusion_rationale: Recurrent inflammatory dermatosis masquerading as severe bacterial cellulitis, imaged on soft tissue MRI and ultrasound by diffuse subcutaneous/fascial edema lacking drainable abscess or gas, and pathologically characterized by dramatic eosinophilic infiltrates with pathognomonic flame figures encrusted with eosinophil major basic protein.

topics.name: Xanthoma Disseminatum
synonyms: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis, xanthoma disseminatum type
clinical_manifestations: Eruption of hundreds to thousands of discrete, round, smooth, yellowish-red, orange-brown, or reddish-brown waxy papules and nodules (1-5 mm) that frequently coalesce into indurated, verrucous plaques

Characteristic pathognomonic flexural and intertriginous predilection: axillae, antecubital and popliteal fossae, groin, perineum, neck folds, and antecubital creases, as well as periorbital and perioral facial skin

Extensive mucosal involvement (40-60% of cases): xanthomatous papules and plaques infiltrating the upper aerodigestive tract (oral cavity, tongue, pharynx, epiglottis, larynx, vocal cords, trachea, bronchi), leading to progressive hoarseness, dysphonia, dysphagia, stridor, and potentially fatal upper airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy

Pituitary-hypothalamic axis involvement (~40% of cases): transient or permanent central diabetes insipidus resulting in polyuria and polydipsia, forming the classic Montgomery triad (flexural xanthomas, mucosal lesions, and diabetes insipidus)
Ocular involvement: xanthomatous infiltration of conjunctiva, cornea, sclera, and orbits causing visual impairment
Normal serum lipid and cholesterol profile (normolipemic xanthomatosis), distinguishing it from hyperlipidemic xanthomatosis
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Pituitary MRI (High-Resolution T1, T2, T1+C): Nodular thickening and avid, homogeneous gadolinium enhancement of the pituitary stalk (infundibulum) and hypothalamus; absence of the normal hyperintense 'bright spot' of the posterior pituitary on unenhanced T1-weighted images (hallmark of central diabetes insipidus); meningeal thickening and xanthomatous dural plaques

CT of Neck and Soft Tissues / Virtual Endoscopy: Extensive irregular nodular soft tissue mucosal thickening causing luminal narrowing of the glottis, subglottis, pyriform sinuses, and upper trachea without destruction of underlying laryngeal cartilage
Chest CT: Nodular xanthomatous deposits along tracheobronchial tree, pulmonary interstitial infiltrates, and subpleural micronodules
Orbital MRI / CT: Well-defined, non-calcified soft tissue masses within the epibulbar space, cornea, and retrobulbar orbit with variable T2 hypointensity and contrast enhancement

Skeletal Radiography / Whole-Body Low-Dose CT: Complete absence of osteolytic skeletal bone lesions, which is crucial for distinguishing xanthoma disseminatum from Langerhans cell histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester disease
pathology_manifestations: Non-Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis: Dense, sheets-like, nodular inflammatory infiltrate occupying the upper and mid dermis without extending into the epidermis (clear Grenz zone)

Cellular Composition: Predominance of large, lipid-laden foamy histiocytes (xanthoma cells) admixed with pathognomonic Touton-type multinucleated giant cells (characterized by a central wreath of nuclei surrounded by a rim of foamy, lipid-rich cytoplasm)
Admixed Infiltrate: Interspersed mature lymphocytes, plasma cells, neutrophils, and eosinophils; older lesions show progressive storiform interstitial fibrosis

Immunohistochemistry (IHC): Histiocytes are strongly positive for CD68, CD163, and Factor XIIIa; negative for CD1a and Langerin (CD207) (ruling out Langerhans cell histiocytosis); S100 protein is typically negative or only weakly and focally positive
Electron Microscopy: Absence of Birbeck granules (pentalaminar tennis-racket organelles), confirming non-Langerhans lineage
topics.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive normolipemic non-Langerhans cell histiocytic dermatosis characterized by widespread flexural xanthomas and upper airway lesions, imaged on brain MRI by infundibular stalk thickening with loss of the posterior pituitary T1 bright spot, on neck CT by laryngeal/tracheal airway narrowing, and confirmed histologically by CD68+/CD1a- foamy histiocytes and Touton giant cells.

topics.name: Acromegaly
clinical_manifestations: Acral overgrowth: progressive enlargement of hands and feet (tightening of rings and shoes), broad 'spade-like' hands with blunt fingers
Coarsening of facial features: prominent frontal bossing, severe prognathism (macrognathia with underbite and dental diastema / widened interdental spaces)
Macroglossia with scalloped borders and deep voice
Hyperhidrosis, oily skin, and skin tags (molluscum fibrosum)
Carpal tunnel syndrome and proximal myopathy
radiological_manifestations: Sella Turcica / Pituitary MRI: Pituitary adenoma (macroadenoma >10 mm or microadenoma), suprasellar extension compressing the optic chiasm, invasion of cavernous sinuses
Hand Radiographs: Prominent arrow-like or tufted bony exostoses ('spade-like phalanges'), widening of the joint spaces due to articular cartilage hypertrophy, thickening of soft tissues
Foot Radiographs: Pathognomonic heel-pad thickness (>25 mm on lateral X-ray)
Skull Radiographs: Enlargement of the sella turcica, hyperostosis frontalis, marked enlargement of frontal and paranasal sinuses, prognathism
pathology_manifestations: Transsphenoidal pituitary resection: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET) composed of sheets or cords of acidophilic or chromophobic adenoma cells; strong immunohistochemical cytoplasmic positivity for Growth Hormone (GH); PIT-1 lineage transcription factor expression
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic endocrine condition with unmistakable physical appearance (spade-like hands, prognathism, macroglossia) paired with pituitary macroadenoma on MRI and heel-pad thickening >25 mm on X-ray.

topics.name: Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 1 (APECED)
clinical_manifestations: Diagnostic Whittaker Triad: Presence of at least two of the three classic components (or one if an affected sibling): (1) Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC), (2) Primary hypoparathyroidism, and (3) Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease)

Chronic Mucocutaneous Candidiasis (CMC): Earliest manifestation typically presenting before age 5; persistent, recurrent Candida albicans infection manifesting as thick hyperkeratotic, dystrophic nail plates (onychomycosis with subungual crumbling), chronic pseudomembranous oral thrush, angular cheilitis, and painful esophageal or genital candidiasis refractory to topical antifungals

Hypocalcemic Neuromuscular Tetany: Symptomatic hypoparathyroidism presenting with paresthesias of the perioral region and fingertips, painful muscle cramps, carpopedal spasm (Trousseau sign elicited upon sphygmomanometer cuff inflation), facial nerve irritability (Chvostek sign on periauricular percussion), laryngeal stridor, and generalized hypocalcemic seizures

Addisonian Cutaneous and Mucosal Hyperpigmentation: Diffuse bronze-brown cutaneous hyperpigmentation accentuating sun-exposed areas, friction zones (elbows, knees, knuckles), palmar creases, and blue-gray macules along the buccal mucosa, driven by proopiomelanocortin (POMC) peptides secondary to lack of cortisol negative feedback; accompanied by hypotension and salt-craving

Ectodermal Dystrophic Features: Pitted enamel hypoplasia with transverse ridges and microdontia; chronic keratoconjunctivitis with photophobia and corneal scarring; patchy or universal alopecia (alopecia areata/universalis); and depigmented patches of vitiligo
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Head CT: Striking, dense, bilateral symmetric calcifications within the basal ganglia (globus pallidus, putamen, and caudate nuclei), thalami, centrum semiovale, and cerebellar dentate nuclei (Fahr syndrome pattern), resulting from chronic profound hypocalcemia and elevated calcium-phosphate product in untreated hypoparathyroidism

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Bilateral, symmetrical, marked adrenal gland atrophy with extreme thinning of the medial and lateral limbs (<2 mm), preservation of smooth adreniform shape, and complete absence of nodular masses or adrenal calcifications (distinguishing autoimmune adrenalitis from tuberculosis or histoplasmosis)

Plain Skeletal Radiography: Diffuse, marked increase in bone mineral density (osteosclerosis) with cortical thickening, prominent metaphyseal sclerotic bands in growing long bones, and dental panoramic radiographs showing blunted, shortened dental roots and deficient enamel caps

Renal Ultrasound: Medullary nephrocalcinosis and recurrent nephrolithiasis appearing as bilateral hyperechoic renal pyramids with posterior acoustic shadowing, frequently precipitated by vitamin D and calcium replacement therapy
pathology_manifestations: Organ-Specific Endocrine Histopathology: Massive autoimmune lymphocytic infiltration (predominantly CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes and plasma cells) of the adrenal cortex and parathyroid glands, leading to follicular/parenchymal cell apoptosis, destruction of steroidogenic cortical zones, and progressive dense fibrocollagenous replacement atrophy

Molecular Genetics and Serology: Monogenic autosomal recessive loss-of-function mutations in the AIRE (Autoimmune Regulator) gene located on chromosome 21q22.3, impairing medullary thymic epithelial expression of peripheral tissue antigens and disrupting central immune tolerance; presence of pathognomonic, high-titer neutralising autoantibodies against Type I interferons (interferon-omega and interferon-alpha) present in >95% of patients, alongside antibodies against 21-hydroxylase, 17-alpha-hydroxylase, side-chain cleavage enzyme (CYP11A1), and NALP5
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic monogenic autoimmune endocrine triad of refractory mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroid tetany, and Addisonian bronze skin, matched with dense basal ganglia Fahr calcifications on head CT and AIRE gene mutations.

topics.name: Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 2 (Schmidt Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Syndromic Pairing: Mandatory presence of autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) combined with autoimmune thyroid disease (Hashimoto's thyroiditis in 70% or Graves' disease in 30%) and/or Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus; adult onset typically in the third or fourth decade with strong female preponderance (3:1)

Addisonian Cutaneous and Mucosal Hyperpigmentation: Generalized bronze-brown skin hyperpigmentation, intensely pronounced in sun-exposed zones, palmar creases, pressure points (elbows, knees, knuckles), areolae, perineum, and fresh scars, accompanied by slate-grey or bluish-black longitudinal melanotic streaks and macules along the buccal mucosa, tongue, and gingival margins

High-Contrast Coexisting Autoimmune Vitiligo: Sharply demarcated, milky-white chalky depigmented cutaneous macules and patches (most frequently periocular, perioral, hand, and genital) providing a dramatic, high-contrast visual juxtaposition directly against the surrounding generalized Addisonian bronze skin

Thyroid and Pancreatic Stigmata: Palpable firm, rubbery, lobulated Hashimoto's goiter or exophthalmic Graves' ocular signs, accompanied by acute ketoacidotic or polyuric symptoms of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus

Associated Autoimmune Manifestations: Patchy alopecia areata, premature ovarian insufficiency with secondary amenorrhea, autoimmune atrophic gastritis with pernicious anemia (pallor, atrophic smooth red tongue), and celiac disease
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Bilateral, marked, symmetrical adrenal gland atrophy with severe reduction in adrenal limb thickness (<2 mm), preservation of smooth adreniform shape, and total absence of nodular expansion or calcifications (critically excluding granulomatous/tuberculous adrenalitis)

High-Resolution Thyroid Ultrasound: Diffusely heterogeneous, markedly hypoechoic thyroid parenchyma with micronodular 'pseudonodular' architecture, thick hyperechoic fibrous septa traversing the parenchyma ('giraffe-skin' appearance), and variable vascularity characteristic of chronic autoimmune thyroiditis

Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) / Skeletal X-Ray: Generalized reduction in bone mineral density (osteopenia/osteoporosis) resulting from chronic glucocorticoid replacement, hypogonadism, or unrecognized celiac-induced calcium malabsorption
pathology_manifestations: Adrenal Gland Histopathology: Severe autoimmune lymphocytic adrenalitis characterized by dense infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes, plasma cells, and histiocytes causing progressive destruction and disappearance of cells across the zona glomerulosa, fasciculata, and reticularis; sparing of the central chromaffin adrenal medulla; and dense capsular and parenchymal fibrous replacement

Thyroid and Pancreatic Histopathology: Thyroid tissue reveals extensive lymphocytic infiltration with lymphoid germinal centers, destruction of thyroid follicles, and oxyphilic metaplasia (Hürthle / Askanazy cells); pancreatic histology shows autoimmune insulitis with selective T-cell mediated destruction of insulin-producing beta cells within the islets of Langerhans

Serologic and Immunogenetic Profile: Polygenic HLA-DR3/DR4-DQ2/DQ8 haplotype association; circulating high-titer autoantibodies against steroidogenic 21-hydroxylase (CYP21A2), thyroid peroxidase (TPO), thyroglobulin (Tg), glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD65), and IA-2
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic polygenic autoimmune syndrome manifesting as a high-contrast visual pairing of chalky-white vitiligo against bronze Addisonian hyperpigmentation, verified by bilateral adrenal atrophy on CT and 21-hydroxylase antibodies.

topics.name: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia
topics.subspecialty: Pediatric Endocrinology & Inborn Errors of Steroidogenesis
clinical_manifestations: 46,XX Neonatal Females: Severe ambiguous genitalia (female pseudohermaphroditism) present at birth: clitoromegaly (phallus-like enlargement), complete or partial labial fusion with scrotalization, and single urogenital sinus opening (Prader stages 1-5); internal female reproductive organs (uterus, tubes, ovaries) are normal
46,XY Neonatal Males: Normal or slightly enlarged phallus, hyperpigmentation of the scrotum, with subtle presentation leading to delayed recognition
Cutaneous Hyperpigmentation: Striking bronze pigmentation of the nipples, areolae, genitalia, and skin creases due to uninhibited ACTH/alpha-MSH hypersecretion
Adrenal Salt-Wasting Crisis (Days 7-21 of life): Life-threatening shock, severe dehydration, projectile vomiting, profound hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis

Post-infancy: Precocious pseudopuberty (axillary and pubic hair, adult body odor, muscular build), rapid early somatic growth velocity but premature epiphyseal fusion resulting in severe adult short stature
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Adrenal Ultrasound and CT: Bilateral marked symmetrical adrenomegaly with pathognomonic 'cerebroid' (brain-like undulating gyral) folded surface pattern; preservation of normal adrenal triangular/crescent shape

Pelvic Ultrasound and MRI: Confirms presence of normal female pelvic internal organs (anteverted uterus, normal ovaries) and identifies the level of urogenital sinus confluence; confirms absence of male testicular tissue in labia
Bone Age Plain Radiography: Significant advance in skeletal maturation (bone age >> chronological age) with premature fusion of epiphyseal plates
pathology_manifestations: Adrenal Cortex Histopathology: Marked diffuse cortical hyperplasia, predominantly involving the zona fasciculata and zona reticularis, which are expanded by lipid-depleted, compact, eosinophilic cells with round uniform nuclei; medullary tissue is compressed but morphologically normal; testicular adrenal rest tumors (TART) composed of sheets of polygonal steroid-producing cells resembling Leydig cells

Biochemical and Molecular Genetics: Autosomal recessive CYP21A2 gene deletions or mutations causing enzymatic blockade, accumulation of serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP), and deficient cortisol and aldosterone synthesis
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic pediatric endocrine emergency featuring neonatal ambiguous genitalia and cutaneous hyperpigmentation, matched with cerebroid adrenomegaly on US and advanced bone age.

topics.name: Craniopharyngioma
clinical_manifestations: Bimodal age distribution: Peak 1 in childhood (5-14 years); Peak 2 in older adults (50-75 years)

Endocrine Deficiencies (Anterior & Posterior Hypopituitarism): Growth failure and severe short stature in children (Growth Hormone deficiency); delayed puberty; secondary adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism; central diabetes insipidus (polyuria, polydipsia, hypernatremia) due to pituitary stalk compression
Neuro-Ophthalmic Manifestations: Progressive visual field loss (classic bitemporal hemianopsia from chiasmal compression), optic disc atrophy, or papilledema
Raised Intracranial Pressure: Morning headaches, projectile vomiting, and obstructive hydrocephalus
radiological_manifestations: Sella and Brain Contrast MRI: Heterogeneous solid and multicystic sellar/suprasellar mass with vivid enhancement of solid components and cyst capsules; cystic components contain high protein, cholesterol crystals, and methemoglobin, creating pathognomonic high signal intensity on T1-weighted images ('machinery oil' fluid) and high signal on T2; upward displacement of the optic chiasm and compression of the third ventricle
Non-Contrast Brain CT: Pathognomonic dense, clumpy, nodular, or rim calcification in >90% of adamantinomatous variants (rare in papillary variant)
pathology_manifestations: Adamantinomatous Craniopharyngioma Histopathology: Reticular and anastomosing sheets of stratified squamous epithelium with peripheral nuclear palisading; stellate reticulum (loose spongy meshwork); pathognomonic 'Wet Keratin' (compact, rounded nodular masses of anucleate squames); cystic cavities filled with dark 'machinery oil' fluid teeming with birefringent cholesterol crystals; nuclear accumulation of beta-catenin driven by somatic CTNNB1 mutations
Papillary Craniopharyngioma (Adults): Well-differentiated non-keratinizing squamous papillomas without wet keratin or calcification, harboring BRAF V600E mutations
topics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal sellar-suprasellar tumor displaying bitemporal hemianopsia, growth failure, pathognomonic CT calcifications, T1-hyperintense 'machinery oil' cysts, and wet keratin histology.

topics.name: Cushing's Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: 'Moon facies': rounded, plethoric, facial fullness with telangiectasias
Centripetal obesity with supraclavicular fat pads and dorsocervical fat pad ('buffalo hump')
Wide (>1 cm), prominent, violaceous or purple abdominal striae (flanks, thighs, breasts)
Severe cutaneous fragility, easy bruising, ecchymoses following minimal pressure, and paper-thin skin
Proximal muscle wasting (thin limbs contrasting with obese trunk)
radiological_manifestations: Adrenal CT / MRI: Bilateral adrenal cortical hyperplasia in ACTH-dependent Cushing's; unilateral adrenal cortical adenoma or large heterogeneous adrenal carcinoma in primary adrenal Cushing's
Pituitary MRI with Dynamic Contrast: ACTH-secreting microadenoma (<10 mm) in Cushing disease (hypoenhancing lesion on early dynamic T1)
Thoracic/Lumbar Spine Radiographs and DXA: Severe osteopenia, multiple asymptomatic vertebral compression fractures with biconcave codfish vertebrae
pathology_manifestations: Adrenal resection: In adenoma: well-circumscribed golden-yellow cortical tumor composed of lipid-rich clear cells and compact eosinophilic cells; in Cushing disease: Crooke's hyaline change within normal non-neoplastic pituitary corticotrope cells (accumulation of cytokeratin filaments due to high circulating cortisol)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Textbook physical phenotype (moon facies, buffalo hump, wide violaceous striae) coupled with adrenal CT adenoma/hyperplasia, dynamic pituitary MRI, and osteoporotic vertebral collapse.

topics.name: Gastrinoma (Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome)
topics.subspecialty: Gastrointestinal Neuroendocrine Tumors & Acid Peptic Syndromes
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Refractory Peptic Ulcer Disease: Severe, recurrent, debilitating peptic ulcerations refractory to standard proton-pump inhibitor therapy, characteristically found in atypical anatomic sites—the post-bulbar duodenum (second and third portions) or proximal jejunum—predisposing to recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding, hematemesis, melena, and visceral perforation
Stomal and Anastomotic Ulceration: Rapid, aggressive, recurring ulceration at surgical gastrojejunal anastomotic sites following previous ulcer surgery or vagotomy

Profuse Watery Secretory Diarrhea and Steatorrhea: High-volume watery diarrhea (often >2–3 liters/day) that improves or completely resolves upon high-dose PPI or gastric acid aspiration; accompanied by foul-smelling steatorrhea caused by massive hydrochloric acid secretion (basal acid output >15 mEq/h) overwhelming duodenal bicarbonate, lowering intestinal pH below 4.5, and irreversibly inactivating pancreatic lipase

Endoscopic Photography Signs: Striking, massive hypertrophy and tortuosity of gastric mucosal rugal folds ('giant gastric folds' resembling cerebral gyri) in the fundus and corpus, accompanied by extensive erosive duodenitis, mucosal cobblestoning, and active distal ulcerations

Associated MEN1 Stigmata: In 25% of cases occurring in the context of MEN1, coexisting signs of primary hyperparathyroidism (nephrolithiasis, hypercalcemia) and pituitary adenomas (visual disturbance, galactorrhea)
radiological_manifestations: Upper Gastrointestinal Barium Examination: Massive enlargement and tortuosity of gastric rugal folds; multiple post-bulbar duodenal and proximal jejunal ulcer craters; marked thickening and edema of duodenal mucosal folds; and dilution of barium contrast by massive volumes of hypersecreted acidic fluid ('dilution sign')

68Ga-DOTATATE / 68Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT: Premier imaging technique with exceptional sensitivity (>90%) demonstrating intense, focal somatostatin receptor-avid radiotracer uptake within the 'Gastrinoma Triangle' (Passaro's triangle: superiorly cystic/common bile duct junction, inferiorly junction of second and third duodenum, medially neck and body of pancreas), detecting tiny occult primary submucosal duodenal and peripancreatic tumors (<5–10 mm)

High-Resolution Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS): Exquisite visualization of tiny, submucosal hypoechoic duodenal wall nodules and periduodenal/peripancreatic lymph node metastases with real-time EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration

Dynamic Multiphasic Pancreas CT / Contrast MRI: Visualizes hypervascular, intensely arterial-enhancing duodenal or pancreatic head tumors with persistent contrast enhancement, alongside evaluation of liver metastases with characteristic arterial ring-enhancement
pathology_manifestations: Gastric Mucosa Histopathology: Striking parietal cell hyperplasia and hypertrophy causing profound expansion of the oxyntic mucosal thickness (2–3 times normal depth); accompanied by diffuse, linear, and micronodular enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cell hyperplasia within fundic glands driven by chronic severe hypergastrinemia, with risk of ECL neuroendocrine dysplasia

Gastrinoma Tumor Histopathology: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasm (NET G1 or G2) displaying solid nests, trabeculae, ribbons, or pseudo-acini of uniform, monomorphic polygonal cells with central round nuclei exhibiting classic finely stippled 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin and pale eosinophilic cytoplasm

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for synaptophysin and chromogranin A, with specific intense positivity for gastrin; high membrane expression of somatostatin receptor subtype 2A (SSTR2A)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Severe neuroendocrine acid-hypersecretory syndrome featuring atypical post-bulbar peptic ulcers, giant gastric rugal hypertrophy, and tiny hypervascular duodenal/pancreatic gastrinomas localized by 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.

topics.name: Glucagonoma Syndrome (Necrolytic Migratory Erythema)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Cutaneous Eruption (Necrolytic Migratory Erythema - NME): Intensely pruritic, painful, migratory, cyclic erythematous patches and papules that rapidly develop flaccid vesicles and bullae, undergoing superficial epidermal necrosis, central erosion, and crusting with centrifugal spread, leaving behind scarred, bronze-brown hyperpigmented patches; lesions cycle dynamically over 1 to 2 weeks

Characteristic Anatomic Distribution of NME: Marked predilection for regions of mechanical friction, pressure, and intertriginous skin—specifically the perineum, perianal region, groin, buttocks, inner thighs, lower abdomen, ankles, and perioral skin (sparing trunk)

Prominent Mucosal Lesions: Bright red, painful, atrophic, depapillated 'beefy red' glossitis; severe angular cheilitis with painful rhagades at oral commissures; stomatitis; and brittle, dystrophic, ridged fingernails

Systemic Wasting and Cachexia: Severe, unprovoked weight loss and generalized skeletal muscle wasting despite normal or increased appetite; new-onset mild, non-ketotic diabetes mellitus or glucose intolerance; and frequent normochromic normocytic anemia

Thromboembolic Diathesis and Neuropsychiatric Signs: Markedly elevated incidence of unprovoked deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) secondary to tumor-induced hypercoagulability; accompanied by depression, insomnia, and proximal muscle weakness
radiological_manifestations: Multiphasic Pancreatic Protocol CT: Large (typically >3–6 cm at clinical presentation), well-demarcated, solitary hypervascular neuroendocrine tumor located in the body or tail of the pancreas, showing avid, intense, heterogeneous contrast enhancement during the late arterial/pancreatic parenchymal phase with rapid washout on portal venous phases

68Ga-DOTATATE / 68Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT: Exceptional diagnostic sensitivity showing intense, avid, focal somatostatin receptor (SSTR) radiotracer uptake (SUVmax typically >25–50) in the primary pancreatic tail mass and identifying occult regional lymph node or hepatic metastases

Abdominal MRI (with Dynamic Gadolinium): Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor demonstrating hypointensity on T1-weighted images, marked hyperintensity on T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) with restricted diffusion; depicts multiple hyperenhancing hypervascular liver metastases with ring-like peripheral enhancement
Venous Doppler Ultrasound / CT Pulmonary Angiography: Confirms lower extremity deep vein thrombosis and segmental/lobar pulmonary emboli stemming from paraneoplastic prothrombotic state
pathology_manifestations: Skin Lesion Punch Biopsy (Advancing Edge of NME): Pathognomonic superficial necrolysis—pale, vacuolated, ballooning degeneration of keratinocytes in the upper spinous layer (stratum spinosum) with intercellular edema, abrupt full-thickness necrosis of the upper epidermis, intraepidermal clefting, and subcorneal pustules, while the basal cell layer remains viable and intact

Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor Histology: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasm (PanNET G1 or G2) displaying solid nests, trabecular ribbons, or insular arrangements of monomorphic polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic or amphophilic cytoplasm and central round nuclei featuring classic stippled 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for neuroendocrine markers chromogranin A and synaptophysin, and intense specific immunoreactivity for glucagon; typically low Ki-67 proliferative index (<5–10%) in well-differentiated tumors
topics.inclusion_rationale: Definitive paraneoplastic endocrine syndrome featuring pathognomonic necrolytic migratory erythema (NME), beefy glossitis, and a solitary hypervascular pancreatic tail neuroendocrine tumor on multiphasic CT and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.

topics.name: Graves' Disease (Thyroid Eye Disease & Dermopathy)
clinical_manifestations: Graves' orbitopathy / ophthalmopathy: bilateral or asymmetric proptosis (exophthalmos), lid retraction (Dalrymple sign), lid lag on downward gaze (von Graefe sign), chemosis, conjunctival injection, periorbital edema
Pretibial myxedema (thyroid dermopathy): non-pitting, indurated, violaceous, orange-peel ('peau d'orange') plaques and nodules over the anterior lower shins
Thyroid acropachy: digital clubbing, soft-tissue swelling of hands and feet, periosteal new bone formation
Diffuse, symmetrical, smooth, vascular thyroid enlargement with audible systolic bruit
radiological_manifestations: Orbital CT / MRI: Pathognomonic spindle-shaped enlargement of extraocular muscle bellies (inferior rectus, medial rectus, superior rectus, lateral rectus: 'I'M SLOw') with characteristic sparing of the anterior tendinous insertions; increased retro-orbital fat volume; optic nerve compression at the orbital apex
Thyroid Doppler Ultrasound: Diffuse thyroid enlargement, heterogeneous hypoechogenicity, and pathognomonic marked hypervascularity on color Doppler ('thyroid inferno')
Hand Radiographs (Thyroid Acropachy): Characteristic fluffy, spicular, symmetric periosteal new bone formation along the diaphyses of metacarpals and proximal phalanges
pathology_manifestations: Thyroid fine-needle aspiration / histology: Diffuse follicular hyperplasia with columnar epithelial cells forming papillary projections into the colloid; scalloping of colloid at the apical margins of follicular cells ('moth-eaten colloid')
Pretibial dermopathy biopsy: Abundant glycosaminoglycan (mucin/hyaluronic acid) accumulation splitting collagen bundles in the reticular dermis, demonstrated by Alcian blue stain
topics.inclusion_rationale: Meets strict criteria: possesses hallmark physical manifestations (proptosis, pretibial myxedema, thyroid acropachy) and pathognomonic extraocular muscle belly enlargement on orbit CT/MRI and 'thyroid inferno' on Doppler.

topics.name: McCune-Albright Syndrome
topics.subspecialty: Metabolic Bone Disease & Genetic Endocrine Syndromes
synonyms: polyostotic fibrous dysplasia with precocious puberty
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Cutaneous Macules: Large, unilateral, flat hyperpigmented café-au-lait skin macules featuring jagged, irregular margins classically described as resembling the 'coast of Maine' ('coast-of-Maine' sign), distinct from smooth regular Neurofibromatosis type 1 patches; typically respect the dorsal or ventral midline of the body and are concentrated over the sacrum, buttocks, posterior thorax, nape of the neck, and forehead

Peripheral Autonomous Precocious Puberty: In young girls, recurrent painless vaginal bleeding and breast budding occurring as early as infancy to toddler age, driven by autonomous hyperestrogenemia produced by recurrent luteinized follicular ovarian cysts that fluctuate independently of hypothalamic GnRH; in boys, macroorchidism with bilateral or asymmetric testicular enlargement due to autonomous Leydig and Sertoli cell hyperplasia with or without autonomous testosterone production

Craniofacial Bony Asymmetry and Deformity: Painless, progressive asymmetric enlargement and bossing of the skull, maxilla, mandible, and orbital roof ('leontiasis ossea' appearance), leading to facial asymmetry, proptosis, vision loss from bony impingement of the optic canal, and conductive/sensorineural hearing impairment from internal auditory canal stenosis

Multifocal Autonomous Endocrine Hyperfunction: Autonomous thyrotoxicosis with nodular goiter (diffuse toxic or multinodular goiter resistant to antithyroid drug withdrawal), growth hormone / prolactin hypersecretion causing gigantism or coarse acromegalic facial features, autonomous ACTH-independent neonatal hypercortisolism (Cushing syndrome), and FGF23-mediated renal phosphate wasting resulting in hypophosphatemic osteomalacia/rickets with muscle weakness
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Radiography: Expansile, intramedullary diaphyseal and metaphyseal polyostotic lesions displaying a pathognomonic homogeneous, hazy, radiolucent 'ground-glass' matrix lacking normal trabecular bone markings; associated with smooth endosteal scalloping, cortical thinning, and a well-defined narrow sclerotic rim

Femoral Radiograph ('Shepherd's Crook' Deformity): Marked, progressive varus angulation and bowing of the proximal femur secondary to repeated microfractures and mechanical weight-bearing on diseased fibrous bone, creating the classic 'shepherd's crook' (coxa vara) deformity with cortical thickening and pseudoarthrosis risk

High-Resolution Craniofacial CT (Bone Window): Diffuse expansile ground-glass thickening and sclerosis replacing normal diploic bone across the sphenoid wing, orbital roofs, clivus, maxilla, and ethmoids; accurately details severe concentric narrowing of the optic canals and superior orbital fissures

Pelvic and Scrotal Ultrasound: Pelvic US reveals large, solitary or bilateral, thick-walled, autonomous cystic ovarian lesions that fluctuate in diameter over serial examinations; scrotal US in males reveals heterogeneous testicular parenchyma with hyperechoic microlithiasis, discrete hyperechoic nodular Leydig/Sertoli cell lesions, and enlarged testicular volume
pathology_manifestations: Bone Histopathology: Disorganized curvilinear, C-shaped, or fishhook-shaped trabeculae of immature woven bone resembling Chinese ideograms or 'alphabet soup' patterns, characteristically lacking osteoblastic rimming, embedded within a cellular to hypocellular fibrous stroma composed of benign, uniform, spindle-shaped fibroblastic cells lacking atypia or mitotic activity

Molecular Genetic Correlate: Postzygotic mosaic gain-of-function missense mutations in codon 201 of the GNAS gene (most commonly p.Arg201Cys or p.Arg201His on chromosome 20q13.3) leading to constitutive GTPase inhibition, persistent activation of the Gs-alpha subunit, and uncoupled hyperactivation of adenylate cyclase with elevated intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP) across affected osteoblasts, melanocytes, and endocrine cell lineages
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic mosaic endocrine-skeletal disorder exhibiting pathognomonic 'coast-of-Maine' café-au-lait skin lesions, autonomous precocious puberty, and plain radiographic 'ground-glass' expansile bone lesions with shepherd's crook femoral deformity.

topics.name: Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Palpable Thyroid Nodule: Hard, firm, non-tender solitary thyroid nodule located characteristically in the upper to middle third of the thyroid lobes (where C-cell concentration is highest), moving with deglutition and showing fixity in advanced stages

Bulky Cervical Lymphadenopathy: Early, prominent, firm or rock-hard cervical lymphadenopathy in the central (level VI) and ipsilateral/contralateral lateral neck (levels II–V), present in >50% of patients at initial clinical presentation
