Systemic Neuroendocrine Flushing and Diarrhea: Paroxysmal erythematous cutaneous flushing of the face and upper torso, combined with intractable secretory watery diarrhea and abdominal cramps, triggered by massive tumor hypersecretion of calcitonin, VIP, prostaglandins, and serotonin in metastatic disease

Invasive Local Aerodigestive Signs: Hoarseness, dysphonia, and vocal cord paralysis from recurrent laryngeal nerve invasion; stridor, hemoptysis, and dysphagia from tracheal and esophageal infiltration

Associated Syndromic Phenotypes: In hereditary forms (MEN2A/MEN2B), presence of bilateral pheochromocytomas, primary hyperparathyroidism (MEN2A), or pathognomonic mucosal neuromas on tongue/lips, bumpy eyelids, marfanoid habitus, and medullated corneal nerve fibers (MEN2B)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Neck Ultrasound: Distinctive, suspicious thyroid nodule demonstrating marked hypoechogenicity, taller-than-wide morphology, irregular or lobulated margins, chaotic intranodular vascularity on color Doppler, and pathognomonic coarse, dense, irregular intrathyroidal microcalcifications or punctate echogenic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing

Cervical Lymph Node Ultrasound: Rounded, plump, enlarged metastatic cervical lymph nodes with loss of normal echogenic fatty hilum, internal cystic necrosis, peripheral vascularity, and distinctive coarse internal microcalcifications identical to the primary tumor

Contrast-Enhanced Neck and Chest CT: Dense, heterogeneously enhancing thyroid mass with invasive margins abutted against the trachea and esophagus, coupled with heavily calcified cervical and superior mediastinal lymphadenopathy

68Ga-DOTATATE, 18F-DOPA, or 18F-FDG PET/CT: Excellent sensitivity for detecting occult liver metastases (which often appear hypervascular with central necrosis) and diffuse osteoblastic / osteolytic skeletal metastases in patients with postoperative calcitonin doubling
pathology_manifestations: Thyroid Histopathology: Proliferation of uniform to mildly pleomorphic polygonal, round, or spindle-shaped parafoveolar C-cells growing in solid sheets, nests, cords, or pseudo-follicles, separated by an abundant, characteristic fibrovascular stroma

Pathognomonic Amyloid Deposition: Amorphous, dense, eosinophilic extracellular amyloid stroma derived from altered polymerized procalcitonin fibrils, demonstrating bright salmon-pink staining with Congo red dye and pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light microscopy

Immunohistochemistry: Universal, diffuse, intense cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for calcitonin, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), chromogranin A, and synaptophysin; characteristically negative for thyroglobulin (excluding follicular-derived thyroid carcinomas)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Neuroendocrine thyroid neoplasm featuring firm thyroid nodularity, bulky calcified lymphadenopathy, flushing, and diagnostic coarse intranodal calcifications on neck US paired with apple-green birefringent amyloid on Congo red.

topics.name: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1
clinical_manifestations: Classic '3 Ps' Tumors: 1) Parathyroid: Multi-gland parathyroid hyperplasia/adenomas presenting with primary hyperparathyroidism, recurrent calcium nephrolithiasis, fatigue, and osteopenia; 2) Pancreatic Neuroendocrine: Gastrinomas (Zollinger-Ellison syndrome with severe, refractory peptic ulcerations, gastroesophageal reflux, and watery secretory diarrhea), insulinomas (recurrent fasting hypoglycemia with neuroglycopenic symptoms), or nonfunctioning pNETs; 3) Pituitary: Prolactinomas (galactorrhea, amenorrhea, bitemporal hemianopsia), growth hormone-secreting adenomas (acromegalic features), or non-functioning macroadenomas
Characteristic Cutaneous Markers: Multiple facial angiofibromas (flesh-colored papules), collagenomas, subcutaneous lipomas, and café-au-lait macules
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Multi-Phase Contrast CT and MRI: Hypervascular, avidly arterial-enhancing neuroendocrine tumors of the pancreas and duodenum; small ring-enhancing liver metastases
68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT: Extremely high sensitivity and spatial resolution for detecting primary and metastatic somatostatin receptor-expressing enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
Neck 4D-CT / 99mTc-Sestamibi SPECT-CT: Multi-gland enlargement demonstrating asymmetric 4-gland parathyroid hyperplasia
Pituitary Contrast MRI: Pituitary microadenoma or expansile macroadenoma with suprasellar extension and optic chiasm displacement
pathology_manifestations: Neuroendocrine Tumor Histopathology: Organoid nested ('Zellballen-like'), trabecular, or insular arrangements of uniform polygonal cells with finely granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and pathognomonic 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin with absent nucleoli; diffuse immunoreactivity for synaptophysin and chromogranin A
Parathyroid Histopathology: Multi-gland chief cell hyperplasia with complete depletion of stromal fat cells
Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant germline loss-of-function mutations in the MEN1 tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 11q13, encoding the nuclear scaffold protein menin
topics.inclusion_rationale: Core endocrine neoplasia syndrome combining the '3 Ps', facial angiofibromas, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT somatostatin avidity, multi-gland parathyroid imaging, and menin loss pathology.

topics.name: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2B
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Mucosal Neuromas: Multiple, soft, flesh-colored or pink nodules clustering conspicuously on the vermilion border of the lips, dorsal and lateral surfaces of the tongue ('bumpy tongue'), buccal mucosa, and palate
'Bumpy, Blubbery Lips': Prominent diffuse hypertrophy of the upper and lower lips; eyelid neuromas with thickened, everted tarsal plates
Slit-Lamp Biomicroscopy: Hypertrophied, prominent, thickened corneal nerve fibers traversing the clear corneal stroma

Marfanoid Habitus: Asthenic, tall, slender build with arachnodactyly, joint hypermobility, pectus excavatum, and high-arched palate (without lens dislocation or aortic root aneurysm); severe intestinal ganglioneuromatosis presenting with megacolon
Extremely aggressive, virulent early-onset Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma (MTC) developing in the first year of life; bilateral pheochromocytomas (~50%)
radiological_manifestations: Neck Ultrasound and Contrast-Enhanced CT: Bulky, multifocal, infiltrative medullary thyroid carcinoma nodules with dense punctate echogenic foci (microcalcifications); extensive metastatic cervical lymphadenopathy
Abdominal Contrast CT and MRI: Bilateral, heterogeneous, hypervascular adrenal masses with central necrosis (pheochromocytomas); T2-hyperintense 'lightbulb' adrenal lesions
Abdominal Plain Radiographs / Fluoroscopy: Severe colonic dilation, megacolon, and delayed intestinal transit from diffuse ganglioneuromatosis
pathology_manifestations: Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma Histopathology: Sheets, cords, and nests of polygonal or spindle-shaped neuroendocrine cells surrounded by fibrovascular stroma containing Congo-red-positive amyloid deposits (derived from procalcitonin) exhibiting pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light; positive immunohistochemistry for calcitonin, CEA, and chromogranin
Mucosal Neuroma / Ganglioneuromatosis: Hyperplasia and tortuous proliferation of enlarged, unencapsulated nerve bundles and Schwann cells intermingled with ganglion cells
Molecular Genetics: Specific heterozygous germline point mutation in the RET proto-oncogene kinase domain at codon 918 (p.Met918Thr / M918T) in >95% of patients
topics.inclusion_rationale: Unmatched clinical exam constellation (mucosal tongue/lip neuromas, marfanoid habitus, prominent corneal nerves) accompanied by lethal early medullary thyroid carcinoma and amyloid histology.

topics.name: Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma
clinical_manifestations: Classic Symptomatic '5 Ps' Paroxysm: 1) Paroxysmal severe hypertension (or sustained hypertension with paroxysmal spikes); 2) Pounding headache (sudden, severe, bifrontal/occipital); 3) Profuse diaphoresis (drenching generalized sweating); 4) Palpitations and tachycardia; 5) Pallor: Striking blanching/pallor of the face and extremities during paroxysms due to intense alpha-1-adrenergic peripheral vasoconstriction
Tremor, extreme anxiety/sense of impending doom ('spells'), orthostatic hypotension due to contracted plasma volume, and episodic nausea
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT: Large, well-defined, heterogeneous adrenal mass with non-contrast attenuation >10 Hounsfield Units (HU), avid heterogeneous arterial phase enhancement, and delayed contrast washout (<50% absolute washout)

Abdominal MRI (Gold Standard for Soft Tissue Characterization): Pathognomonic 'Lightbulb Bright' Sign: Extremely high signal intensity on T2-weighted MRI sequences; areas of internal cystic necrosis, hemorrhage, and prominent serpiginous flow voids

Nuclear Medicine / Molecular Functional Imaging: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT demonstrates exceptional sensitivity for paragangliomas and metastatic disease; 123I-MIBG Scintigraphy / SPECT-CT shows intense tracer avidity within chromaffin tissue reflecting catecholamine uptake via the norepinephrine transporter
pathology_manifestations: Tumor Histopathology: Classic 'Zellballen' (cell balls / nests) architecture: well-defined nests of round-to-polygonal chromaffin cells surrounded by a delicate, rich capillary network lined by S100-positive sustentacular cells; abundant granular, amphophilic-to-basophilic cytoplasm and pleomorphic nuclei

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong cytoplasmic positivity for chromogranin A and synaptophysin; peripheral rimming of nests by S100-positive sustentacular cells; GAPP and PASS histopathological scoring systems evaluate malignant potential
Molecular Genetics: Germline mutations in >15 susceptibility genes including SDHB, SDHD, VHL, RET, and NF1
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic endocrine hypertensive tumor where episodic facial pallor and sweating correlate with pathognomonic MRI 'lightbulb bright' T2 adrenal lesions, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT, and Zellballen architecture.

topics.name: Primary Hyperparathyroidism and Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica
clinical_manifestations: Classic multisystem mnemonic: 'Stones, bones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans': Stones (recurrent calcium nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis); Bones (severe diffuse bone pain, pathological fractures, focal jaw swellings / epulis); Groans (constipation, pancreatitis, peptic ulcer); Moans (depression, fatigue, muscle weakness)
Band Keratopathy: Horizontal grayish-white superficial corneal opacity in the interpalpebral fissure due to calcium phosphate deposition in Bowman layer
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Radiography Hallmark Signs: 1) Subperiosteal Bone Resorption (Pathognomonic): Best visualized along the radial aspect of the middle phalanges of the 2nd and 3rd digits, giving a finely lace-like, scalloped cortical border; 2) 'Salt-and-Pepper' Skull: Granular, mottled loss of calvarial trabecular architecture with blurred inner and outer skull tables; 3) Brown Tumors (Osteoclastomas): Well-circumscribed, expansile, geographic lytic lesions in the mandible, ribs, pelvis, and long bones with thinned cortices; 4) Distal Clavicular Osteolysis: Tapering, resorption, and pencil-pointing of the distal acromial ends of the clavicles
Neck 4D-CT and 99mTc-Sestamibi SPECT-CT: Hypervascular, early-enhancing, rapidly washing-out enlarged parathyroid adenoma (typically inferior gland)
Renal Ultrasound / CT: Bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis and staghorn calculi
pathology_manifestations: Parathyroid Adenoma Histopathology: Encapsulated nodule composed almost exclusively of densely packed chief cells with absent intrastromal adipocytes, surrounded by a compressed rim of normal parathyroid tissue containing fat

Brown Tumor / Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica Bone Histopathology: Intense osteoclastic bone resorption with peritrabecular fibrosis; proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells intermixed with spindle-shaped fibroblastic stroma; abundant hemosiderin pigment accumulation from repetitive microhemorrhages giving the classic gross brown appearance
topics.inclusion_rationale: Celebrated metabolic bone catastrophe combining band keratopathy, pathognomonic subperiosteal finger resorption on X-ray, brown tumors, and parathyroid adenoma sestamibi imaging.

topics.name: Pseudohypoparathyroidism Type 1A
topics.subspecialty: Metabolic Bone Disease & Albright Hereditary Osteodystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Albright Hereditary Osteodystrophy (AHO) Physical Habitus: Short stature, stocky habitus, and early-onset central obesity; rounded moon facies with flattened nasal bridge

Pathognomonic Brachydactyly: Shortening of the 4th and 5th metacarpals and metatarsals, producing dimples in place of knuckles when making a clenched fist (Archibald sign / 'knuckle, knuckle, dimple, dimple' sign)
Subcutaneous Ossifications / Osteoma Cutis: Hard, palpable, plaque-like or nodular heterotopic bone formations within the dermis and subcutaneous tissues

Hypocalcemic Tetany Signs: Positive Chvostek sign (facial twitch on tapping facial nerve) and Trousseau sign (carpopedal spasm upon inflation of blood pressure cuff); paresthesias, seizures, and prolonged QT interval
Multi-hormone end-organ resistance (PTH, TSH [subclinical hypothyroidism], LH/FSH, and GHRH)
radiological_manifestations: Hand and Foot Radiographs (Plain Films): Pathognomonic shortening of the 4th and 5th metacarpal and metatarsal bones; short broad phalanges with cone-shaped epiphyses; short distal phalanx of the thumb ('murderer's thumb')
Soft-Tissue Radiography and CT: Extensive subcutaneous heterotopic ossification and osteoma cutis in the extremities and abdominal wall without muscle involvement

Non-Contrast Brain CT: Striking, extensive, symmetrical calcification of the basal ganglia (caudate nucleus, globus pallidus, putamen), thalami, and subcortical white matter (Fahr syndrome pattern) due to chronic hyperphosphatemia and hypocalcemia
pathology_manifestations: Osteoma Cutis Histopathology: True mature lamellar bone islands containing osteocytes, osteoblasts, and bone marrow elements residing entirely within the reticular dermis and subcutaneous adipose tissue

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the GNAS gene on chromosome 20q13.3 (encoding the alpha subunit of the stimulatory G-protein, Gs-alpha) inherited maternally, causing tissue-specific resistance to PTH in renal proximal tubules despite marked compensatory elevation of serum PTH
topics.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive endocrine-dysmorphic condition presenting with Archibald knuckle sign, osteoma cutis, Fahr basal ganglia calcification on CT, and maternal GNAS-mediated PTH resistance.

topics.name: Riedel Thyroiditis (Invasive Fibrous Thyroiditis)
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Palpable Neck Mass: Slowly or subacutely expanding, stony 'iron-hard', 'woody', or 'ligneous' anterior cervical mass that is completely fixed to surrounding anatomical structures (pretracheal fascia, sternocleidomastoid and strap muscles, trachea, and carotid sheaths) and fails to ascend upon deglutition

Severe Tracheoesophageal Compressive Symptoms: Progressive, severe inspiratory stridor, choking sensation, orthopnea, and suffocating dyspnea secondary to rigid circumferential tracheal encasement and luminal narrowing; progressive solid-food dysphagia from esophageal compression

Invasive Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Palsy: Early hoarseness, dysphonia, and fixed vocal cord paralysis documented on flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy, frequently mimicking invasive anaplastic thyroid carcinoma

Vascular and Extrathyroidal Infiltration: Encasement of carotid sheaths causing diminished unilateral or bilateral carotid pulsations, cervical venous engorgement from internal jugular compression, and hard woody induration extending diffusely beyond the thyroid bed into the anterior chest and supraclavicular fossae

Coexisting Systemic Fibrosing Disorders (IgG4-RD): Extrathyroidal manifestation of systemic IgG4-related disease in approximately one-third of patients, including retroperitoneal fibrosis (flank/back pain, ureteral obstruction, hydronephrosis), sclerosing mediastinitis, sclerosing cholangitis, or orbital pseudotumor
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Neck CT: Ill-defined, infiltrative, markedly hypoattenuating neck mass replacing thyroid parenchyma with direct, aggressive contiguous invasion through the thyroid capsule into adjacent strap muscles, carotid sheaths, and prevertebral space; demonstrates circumferential encasement, displacement, and caliber reduction ('saber-sheath' narrowing) of the cervical trachea

Neck MRI ('Black Thyroid' Sign): Striking, pathognomonic profound hypointensity of the entire mass on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted sequences ('black thyroid' appearance) caused by dense, avascular, hyalinized fibrous collagen, with negligible or faint heterogeneous post-gadolinium enhancement

High-Frequency Neck Ultrasound: Diffuse, intensely hypoechoic, markedly heterogeneous replacement of the thyroid gland with loss of normal architecture and indistinct capsule; demonstrates absence of vascularity on color Doppler ('cold thyroid') and direct acoustic continuity between the thyroid mass and adjacent strap muscles

Abdominal and Thoracic CT/MRI: Evaluates systemic fibrosing correlates, revealing periaortic soft-tissue mantling and medial ureteral deviation characteristic of retroperitoneal fibrosis, fibrosing mediastinitis with superior vena cava narrowing, or tumefactive autoimmune pancreatitis
pathology_manifestations: Surgical Core / Open Biopsy Histopathology: Proliferation of dense, hyalinized, keloid-like fibrous tissue diffusely obliterating thyroid follicles and actively extending beyond the thyroid capsule into adjacent cervical adipose tissue and skeletal muscle fibers; complete absence of cellular atypia, necrosis, or high mitotic activity

Obliterative Phlebitis (Obliterative Venulitis): Endothelial infiltration and transmural invasion of cervical veins by a cellular fibroblastic and lymphoplasmacytic proliferation, leading to complete fibrous luminal occlusion—a definitive hallmark of IgG4-related fibrosclerosis

Immunohistochemistry: Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate displaying an abundant population of IgG4-positive plasma cells, with >30–50 IgG4-positive plasma cells per high-power field (HPF) and an IgG4/IgG plasma cell ratio exceeding 40%, confirming Riedel thyroiditis as the organ-specific manifestation of IgG4-related disease
topics.inclusion_rationale: Striking invasive endocrine disorder presenting as a stony 'iron-hard' neck mass with tracheal encasement, matched with characteristic T1/T2 hypointense 'black thyroid' on neck MRI and IgG4-rich obliterative venulitis on histology.

topics.name: Acute Necrotizing Pancreatitis with Retroperitoneal Hemorrhage
clinical_manifestations: Cullen's sign: Faint blue-purple or dirty yellowish-brown ecchymotic discoloration in the periumbilical region (resulting from retroperitoneal hemorrhage tracking through the gastrohepatic and falciform ligaments to the subcutaneous umbilical tissue)

Grey Turner's sign: Bluish-red to purplish-brown ecchymosis along the bilateral or unilateral flanks and costovertebral angles (caused by pancreatic enzymes and retroperitoneal blood dissecting along the posterior pararenal space and lateral abdominal wall)
Fox's sign: Ecchymosis over the upper anterior medial thigh just inferior to the inguinal ligament (blood tracking along the psoas fascia and femoral canal)

Severe epigastric peritoneal signs: Exquisite epigastric tenderness, marked abdominal guarding, board-like rigidity, absent bowel sounds (paralytic ileus), and rapid progression to systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), refractory septic/hypovolemic shock, and multi-organ failure
Subcutaneous fat necrosis (pancreatic panniculitis): Tender, erythematous, violaceous subcutaneous nodules on lower extremities that may ulcerate with discharge of oily brown viscous fluid
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Balthazar Classification / Modified CT Severity Index - Gold Standard): Non-enhancing or poorly enhancing regions of pancreatic parenchyma (>30% lack of enhancement indicates extensive parenchymal necrosis); extensive non-liquid, heterogeneous acute necrotic collections (ANC) in the peripancreatic, anterior/posterior pararenal spaces, and lesser sac; high-attenuation areas (>50-70 HU on unenhanced CT) reflecting acute retroperitoneal hematoma and hemorrhage; presence of gas bubbles within necrotic tissue indicating gas-forming infection / infected pancreatic necrosis; late-phase formation of walled-off necrosis (WON) with thick, fibrous capsule

Abdominal / Mesenteric CT Angiography: Pseudoaneurysms of peripancreatic arterial branches (splenic artery, gastroduodenal artery, superior pancreaticoduodenal artery) from enzymatic erosion; splenic vein thrombosis with left-sided (sinistral) portal hypertension and gastric varices

Abdominal Radiography: 'Sentinel loop' (focal isolated ileus of a dilated jejunal loop in the left upper quadrant) and 'colon cut-off sign' (abrupt cessation of colonic gas at the splenic flexure due to inflammatory spasm from retroperitoneal exudate spreading along the phrenicocolic ligament)
pathology_manifestations: Pancreatic necrosectomy / autopsy specimen: Extensive confluent parenchymal coagulative necrosis with complete loss of acinar and islet architecture; enzymatic fat necrosis (steatonecrosis) presenting grossly as opaque, chalky-white, yellowish-gray saponification plaques and deposits in peripancreatic fat, mesentery, and omentum (calcium salts precipitated by fatty acids liberated from triglyceride hydrolysis by pancreatic lipase); acute transmural necrotizing vasculitis with extensive thrombosis of arterioles and venules, marked erythrocyte extravasation and interstitial hemorrhage; dense neutrophilic demarcation at the borders of viable and nonviable tissue
topics.inclusion_rationale: Critical pancreatic emergency with legendary bedside hemorrhagic ecchymoses (Cullen, Grey Turner, and Fox signs) and pancreatic panniculitis, verified by diagnostic non-enhancing parenchymal necrosis and gas on contrast CT, and classic chalky enzymatic fat saponification.

topics.name: Biliary Atresia (Extrahepatic Biliary Atresia)
clinical_manifestations: Persistent, progressive neonatal cholestatic jaundice extending beyond the physiologic 2-week newborn window (deep scleral icterus and cutaneous bronze-yellow jaundice)

Hallmark visual bedside finding: persistent acholic, chalky, clay-colored, or pale putty-colored stools paired with dark golden-amber or tea-colored urine staining the diaper (due to elevated direct conjugated bilirubinuria)

Abdominal examination: progressive, firm-to-hard, smooth hepatomegaly with a sharp, prominent liver margin palpable several centimeters below the right costal margin, followed by early secondary splenomegaly due to rapid progression to biliary cirrhosis and portal hypertension

General infant physical examination: failure to thrive, progressive poor weight gain, irritability, pruritus-induced fretfulness, visible cutaneous ecchymoses or bleeding from vitamin K malabsorption, and caput medusae/ascites in late unrecognized presentations
Biliary Atresia Splenic Malformation (BASM) syndrome (~10-15% of cases): coexisting polysplenia, situs inversus, preduodenal portal vein, and congenital cardiac anomalies
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Abdominal Ultrasound (First-Line Diagnostic Tool): Pathognomonic 'triangular cord sign' (thickened, triangular or tubular echogenic fibrous tissue >4 mm in thickness located immediately anterior to the bifurcation of the portal vein at the porta hepatis, representing the obliterated common hepatic duct fibrous remnant); 'gallbladder ghost triad' (small, atretic gallbladder length <15 mm, irregular or lobular contour, and lack of a smooth mucosal echogenic lining); failure of the gallbladder to contract after feeding (<50% volume reduction); absence of common bile duct visualization; hepatic arterial hypertrophy with increased hepatic artery/portal vein diameter ratio

Hepatobiliary Scintigraphy (Technetium-99m DISIDA/HIDA Scan): Prompt and adequate hepatic parenchymal radiotracer extraction by hepatocytes, but complete failure of radiotracer excretion into the biliary tree and duodenum/small bowel on delayed imaging at 24 hours (100% sensitivity for biliary obstruction, though shared with severe neonatal hepatitis)

Intraoperative Cholangiography (Gold Standard for Definitive Confirmation): Direct cannulation of the gallbladder or fibrous ductal remnant demonstrates complete non-opacification of the extrahepatic biliary tree with absence of contrast flow into the intrahepatic bile ducts and duodenum
Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP): Non-visualization of the extrahepatic bile ducts (common hepatic duct and common bile duct) with an atrophic or absent gallbladder
pathology_manifestations: Percutaneous liver biopsy: Marked portal tract expansion with prominent, florid bile ductular proliferation (ductular reaction), dense portal stromal edema, bridging portal-to-portal fibrosis, and prominent intraluminal bile plugs in ductules; hepatocellular and canalicular cholestasis with multinucleated giant cell transformation of hepatocytes; intact interlobular bile ducts may be present early but become progressively obliterated

Kasai portoenterostomy / surgical explant: Gross fibrous cone or cord replacing the extrahepatic biliary ductal remnant; histological examination reveals dense obliterative fibroinflammatory sclerosis of the common hepatic and common bile ducts, complete luminal occlusion, chronic mononuclear inflammatory infiltration, and variable presence of minute, discontinuous epithelialized microscopic ductules (<150-300 μm) embedded within fibrous tissue
topics.inclusion_rationale: Premier pediatric surgical liver emergency characterized by neonatal acholic stools, dark amber urine, and firm hepatomegaly, confirmed by the pathognomonic ultrasound triangular cord sign and HIDA non-excretion, with florid portal ductular proliferation on histology requiring urgent Kasai portoenterostomy before 60 days of life.

topics.name: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Transmural Esophageal Rupture)
clinical_manifestations: Mackler's triad: Sudden forceful retching or vomiting followed by agonizing, tearing lower retrosternal/epigastric pain and progressive subcutaneous cervical emphysema
Subcutaneous emphysema: Massive soft-tissue swelling of the anterior neck, supraclavicular fossae, and upper chest with palpable crackling surgical crepitus upon light palpation

Hamman's sign (Hamman crunch): Pathognomonic crunching, rasping, or clicking precordial sound synchronized with the cardiac cycle on cardiac auscultation (due to heart beating against air-filled mediastinal tissue)
Rapidly developing septic and hypovolemic shock: Severe tachycardia, diaphoresis, tachypnea, cyanosis, hypotension, and board-like epigastric rigidity mimicking perforated peptic ulcer
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT with Oral Water-Soluble Contrast (Imaging Gold Standard): Extravasation of oral contrast into the posterior mediastinum, left pleural space, or peritoneal cavity; transmural defect in the left posterolateral wall of the distal esophagus (2-3 cm above the GE junction); extensive pneumomediastinum and mediastinal fluid collections; tension hydropneumothorax (predominantly left-sided in ~80-90% of cases); subcutaneous air dissecting into cervical fascial planes
Fluoroscopic Esophagography (Water-Soluble Gastrografin Swallow): Direct visualization of rapid contrast extravasation from the lower thoracic esophagus into the left pleural space

Chest Radiography: 'V sign of Naclerio' (pathognomonic V-shaped radiolucency of air in the lower mediastinum tracking along the left hemidiaphragm and retrocardiac mediastinal pleura); left pleural effusion/hydropneumothorax, widened mediastinum, and subcutaneous cervical emphysema
pathology_manifestations: Emergency thoracotomy / autopsy specimen: Full-thickness longitudinal transmural tear (typically 2-4 cm in length) located almost exclusively in the left posterolateral aspect of the distal third of the thoracic esophagus, cleaving all layers (mucosa, submucosa, circular and longitudinal muscularis propria, and adventitia); acute necrotizing, fibrinopurulent mediastinitis with massive neutrophilic infiltration, widespread tissue necrosis, and polymicrobial bacterial/fungal colonies dissecting the periesophageal fascial compartments
topics.inclusion_rationale: High-lethality gastrointestinal catastrophe featuring Mackler triad (vomiting, chest pain, cervical crepitus) and Hamman crunch, diagnosed by the pathognomonic Naclerio V sign and contrast extravasation on CT, with transmural distal esophageal rupture on surgical pathology.

topics.name: Budd-Chiari Syndrome (Hepatic Venous Outflow Tract Obstruction)
topics.subspecialty: Vascular Disorders of the Liver & Gut
clinical_manifestations: Classic clinical triad: Rapidly progressive tender hepatomegaly, intractable tense ascites, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain

Prominent, engorged subcutaneous collateral veins over the trunk, flanks, and back: Tortuous subcutaneous thoracoabdominal venous pathways with cephalad (upward) blood flow (indicating inferior vena cava obstruction and caval-caval collateralization)
Marked lower extremity bilateral pitting edema extending to the groin and lower abdominal wall from concomitant IVC compression or thrombosis
Mild scleral icterus and cutaneous jaundice, progressing to acute liver failure with asterixis and encephalopathy in fulminant cases
radiological_manifestations: Hepatic Doppler Ultrasound (First-Line Diagnostic Modality): Non-visualization, thrombosis, or luminal cord-like stenosis of the major hepatic veins (right, middle, left); absent or reversed (retrograde) flow; blunted or monophasic spectral waveforms lacking normal triphasic cardiac variations; pathognomonic 'spiderweb' or arcuate intrahepatic collateral veins connecting obstructed hepatic veins to patent accessory vessels; compressed, slit-like intrahepatic IVC

Multiphasic Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI: Markedly heterogeneous 'patchwork' or 'mosaic' hepatic parenchymal enhancement; dramatic 'flip-flop' enhancement pattern (intense early arterial enhancement of the centrally preserved caudate lobe and central liver parenchyma, with low attenuation and sluggish perfusion in the congested peripheral liver, reversing on delayed portal venous phases); profound caudate lobe hypertrophy (due to its autonomous venous drainage directly into the retrohepatic IVC via short emissary veins); intrahepatic and extrahepatic venous collaterals; massive peritoneal ascites

Direct Hepatic Venography and Cavography: Gold standard vascular imaging demonstrating the characteristic 'spiderweb' network of collateral veins with sluggish arborizing drainage and inability to catheterize the main hepatic vein ostia
pathology_manifestations: Liver needle or wedge biopsy: Severe, intense centrilobular (Zone 3) sinusoidal congestion and red blood cell engorgement with pooling of erythrocytes; atrophy and necrosis of centrilobular hepatocyte cords with preservation of periportal (Zone 1) hepatocytes (nutmeg liver pattern); in subacute and chronic stages, progressive centrilobular fibrosis bridging between adjacent central veins ('reversed lobular architecture' or veno-centric cirrhosis), with occluded, fibrosed terminal hepatic venules demonstrated on elastic stains; commonly associated with underlying myeloproliferative neoplasms (JAK2 V617F mutation), antiphospholipid syndrome, or paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria
topics.inclusion_rationale: High-acuity vascular hepatobiliary emergency characterized by rapid-onset tender hepatomegaly, refractory ascites, and flank collateral veins, diagnosed by pathognomonic 'spiderweb' collaterals and the 'flip-flop' central-peripheral enhancement pattern on CT/MRI.

topics.name: Carcinoid Syndrome and Gastrointestinal Neuroendocrine Tumors
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark paroxysmal cutaneous flushing: Sudden, dramatic, fiery red to purplish/violaceous erythema of the face, neck, and upper chest, provoked by emotional stress, alcohol, or tyramine-rich foods, accompanied by burning sensation, conjunctival injection, lacrimation, and tachycardia
Permanent cutaneous changes: Prominent facial telangiectasias (spider-like vascular webs over the nose, malar eminences, and cheeks) and cyanotic, violaceous facial plethora in long-standing disease

Pellagra-like dermatosis: Dry, scaly, hyperkeratotic, hyperpigmented, erythematous rash on sun-exposed areas (hands, neck [Casal necklace], face) due to preferential shunting of dietary tryptophan (>99%) away from niacin synthesis into serotonin production
Severe, explosive, non-bloody, secretory watery diarrhea (up to 10-20 stools daily) with abdominal cramps and borborygmi

Signs of carcinoid heart disease (Hedinger syndrome): Elevated jugular venous pressure with giant regurgitant 'v' waves, pulsatile liver, holosystolic murmur of tricuspid regurgitation (augmented by inspiration - Carvallo sign), right ventricular heave, and progressive refractory lower extremity edema
radiological_manifestations: 68Ga-DOTATATE / 64Cu-DOTATATE PET/CT (Imaging Gold Standard): Intense, focal somatostatin receptor-avid radiotracer uptake (SUVmax often >30-50) localized to the primary gastrointestinal tumor (most frequently in the distal ileum or appendix) and throughout hypervascular liver and mesenteric nodal metastases

Multiphasic Abdominal CT / MRI: Primary small bowel tumor appearing as a small enhancing mural lesion, with a prominent, classic 'spoke-wheel' stellate mesenteric soft-tissue mass containing coarse punctate calcifications and radiating linear fibrous stranding retracting and tethering adjacent small bowel loops (intense desmoplastic reaction); multiple hypervascular hepatic metastases demonstrating avid peripheral arterial-phase hyperenhancement with rapid venous washout

Transthoracic / Transesophageal Echocardiography: Pathognomonic carcinoid heart disease lesions: thickened, rigid, foreshortened, retracted tricuspid valve leaflets fixed in a semi-open position, failing to coapt in systole, leading to torrential tricuspid regurgitation; thickened and stenotic pulmonary valve leaflets; dilation of right atrium and right ventricle
pathology_manifestations: Surgical bowel resection / liver core biopsy: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (NET G1/G2) composed of highly monotonous, uniform polygonal cells arranged in tight nests, insular clusters, trabeculae, or pseudorosettes; uniform round central nuclei with pathognomonic finely stippled 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin and moderate eosinophilic granular cytoplasm; absent to rare mitoses; strong, diffuse cytoplasmic immunohistochemical positivity for Synaptophysin, Chromogranin A, and INSM1; serotonin production confirmed; primary or metastatic mesenteric mass showing dense, extensive elastotic fibroblastic stroma (desmoplasia); cardiac valves show subendocardial deposition of plaque-like fibrous tissue composed of smooth muscle cells and myofibroblasts rich in acid mucopolysaccharides, strictly sparing valve cusps and underlying architecture
topics.inclusion_rationale: The classic endocrine-GI neoplasia syndrome uniting dramatic bedside signs (fiery violaceous facial flushing, facial telangiectasias, pellagra rash, tricuspid murmur) with pathognomonic 68Ga-DOTATATE PET avidity, the 'spoke-wheel' mesenteric mass, and retracted rigid tricuspid valves on echo.

topics.name: Caroli Disease and Choledochal Malformations
synonyms: communicating cavernous ectasia of biliary tree
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent acute bacterial cholangitis with Charcot's triad: Spiking fevers with shaking chills (rigors), right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and fluctuating jaundice
Deep scleral icterus and generalized cutaneous excoriations from cholestasis
Smooth, tender right upper quadrant palpable hepatomegaly and palpable RUQ mass (in patients with associated extrahepatic choledochal cyst)

In Caroli syndrome (associated with congenital hepatic fibrosis): Stigmata of early, severe non-cirrhotic portal hypertension (massive splenomegaly, recurrent life-threatening hematemesis from bleeding esophageal varices, caput medusae, and ascites in children and young adults)
Associated bilateral palpable flank masses in patients with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD)
radiological_manifestations: Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP - Gold Standard): Multifocal, segmental, saccular or fusiform cystic dilatations of the intrahepatic bile ducts communicating directly with the normal or mildly dilated extrahepatic biliary tree (Todani Type V); multiple intrahepatic biliary calculi (hypointense signal voids within dilated bile ducts); exclusion of obstructive biliary dilatation

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT / MRI: Pathognomonic 'central dot sign': strongly enhancing, tiny round fibrovascular bundle (representing a branch of the portal vein and hepatic artery) located centrally or eccentrically within the low-attenuation, dilated cystic intrahepatic bile ducts; intrahepatic stone formation with high-attenuation ductal calculi; nodular liver, splenomegaly, and portosystemic collateral veins in Caroli syndrome

Abdominal Ultrasound: Saccular anechoic intrahepatic cystic spaces containing echogenic sludge or stones with acoustic shadowing, with color Doppler demonstrating flow within the central portal venous branch ('central dot sign')
pathology_manifestations: Liver resection / explant: Grossly dilated, ectatic intrahepatic bile ducts lined by columnar or cuboidal biliary epithelium, often eroded or ulcerated, with dense periductal chronic inflammation and fibrosis; conspicuous absence of the normal smooth muscle layer in the dilated duct wall; in Caroli syndrome, associated congenital hepatic fibrosis characterized by broad, mature fibrous bands bridging between portal tracts, containing an increased number of tortuous, irregularly branched bile ductules (ductal plate malformation) with preserved normal lobular hepatocyte architecture; markedly elevated lifetime risk of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (~7-15%)
topics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield congenital biliary ectasia characterized by Charcot triad cholangitis and portal hypertension signs, confirmed by the pathognomonic 'central dot sign' and communicating saccular intrahepatic bile ducts on MRCP/CT, with ductal plate malformation histology.

topics.name: Celiac Disease (Gluten-Sensitive Enteropathy) and Dermatitis Herpetiformis
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic skin finding: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring disease) presenting as intensely pruritic, stinging, burning, polymorphic grouped erythematous papules, urticarial plaques, and tense vesicles (resembling herpes clusters) symmetrically distributed on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees, buttocks, upper back, posterior scalp, and sacrum), with prominent excoriations and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation

Severe nutritional deficiency stigmata: Marked temporal and proximal muscle wasting, profound cachexia, protuberant distended abdomen ('potbelly' in children with thin extremities), and bilateral pedal edema from hypoalbuminemia

Mucocutaneous deficiency signs: Glossitis (beefy, smooth, painful red atrophic tongue from folate/B12 deficiency), angular cheilitis, recurrent painful aphthous stomatitis, and dental enamel hypoplasia (pitting and horizontal grooving of permanent teeth)
Digital clubbing, koilonychia (spoon nails from severe iron deficiency), ecchymoses and petechiae from vitamin K malabsorption, and bone pain/tetany from hypocalcemia and severe osteomalacia
radiological_manifestations: CT / MR Enterography: Pathognomonic 'reversal of the small bowel fold pattern' characterized by marked atrophy, flattening, and reduction in the number of mucosal folds in the jejunum (<3 folds per inch) accompanied by compensatory fold hypertrophy and crowding in the ileum (>4-5 folds per inch; 'jejunization of the ileum'); fluid-filled, dilated small bowel loops (luminal caliber >3 cm); transient, non-obstructive entero-enteric intussusception (due to mucosal edema and abnormal hyperperistalsis); 'moulage sign' (smooth, featureless, wax-like appearance of small bowel on barium fluoroscopy)

Abdominal CT: Cavitary mesenteric lymph node syndrome (enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes containing central fluid-fat levels / necrotic cystic low attenuation <10-20 HU); hyposplenism with small, atrophic spleen
Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA) / Skeletal Radiographs: Severe diffuse demineralization, Looser zones (pseudofractures) of osteomalacia, and pathologic insufficiency fractures
pathology_manifestations: Duodenal / jejunal endoscopic mucosal biopsy (Marsh-Oberhuber Classification - Marsh Type 3): Marked, diffuse blunting and complete or subtotal flattening of mucosal villi (villous atrophy), marked elongation and deepening of intestinal crypts (crypt hyperplasia), dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltration of the lamina propria, and marked intraepithelial lymphocytosis (>25-30 intraepithelial lymphocytes [IELs] per 100 enterocytes) with preferential infiltration of CD8+ T cells; Direct Immunofluorescence of perilesional skin punch biopsy (Dermatitis Herpetiformis): Pathognomonic continuous or granular IgA deposition clustered within the dermal papillae along the dermoepidermal junction; serum positivity for anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA (anti-tTG) and anti-endomysial IgA (EMA); strongly linked to HLA-DQ2 / HLA-DQ8
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic malabsorptive enteropathy linked to the intensely pruritic blistering extensor rash of dermatitis herpetiformis and dental hypoplasia, paired with the diagnostic 'reversal of fold pattern' on CT enterography and Marsh-3 villous atrophy.

topics.name: Choledochal Cysts (Todani Classification Types I-IV)
synonyms: multiple extrahepatic and intrahepatic biliary cysts (Todani type IVA)
clinical_manifestations: Classic clinical triad (present in ~10-20% of cases overall, most common in pediatric patients): intermittent right upper quadrant abdominal pain, fluctuating or progressive obstructive jaundice (scleral icterus, dark amber urine, acholic clay-colored stools), and a palpable, smooth, cystic, non-tender or tender right upper quadrant abdominal mass

In adult presentations: clinical picture dominated by recurrent acute cholangitis (Charcot's triad: spiking fevers with rigors, fluctuating jaundice, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain), recurrent biliary colic, acute gallstone or reflux pancreatitis, and secondary biliary cirrhosis

Bedside physical examination: visible or palpable right hypochondrial fullness or ballotable cystic mass in infants and young children; prominent cutaneous excoriations and prurigo from chronic cholestatic pruritus; deep scleral icterus and generalized jaundice

Acute surgical abdomen from spontaneous or traumatic cyst rupture: sudden-onset severe diffuse peritonitis with abdominal guarding, rebound tenderness, biliary ascites, and progressive hypovolemic or septic shock
radiological_manifestations: Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP - Diagnostic Gold Standard): Direct non-invasive visualization of the entire biliary tree defining the Todani classification: Type IA/IB/IC (cystic, focal segmental, or diffuse fusiform dilatation of the extrahepatic common bile duct), Type II (discrete saccular diverticulum protruding from the common bile duct wall), Type III (choledochocele: cystic dilatation of the intraduodenal segment of the distal common bile duct protruding into the duodenal lumen), or Type IVA (multiple cysts involving both extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts); pathognomonic demonstration of Anomalous Pancreaticobiliary Ductal Union (APBDU / APBDJ) characterized by an abnormally long common pancreatobiliary channel (>15 mm) situated outside the duodenal muscular wall beyond the sphincter of Oddi

Multidetector Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Well-circumscribed, fluid-attenuation (0-20 HU) cystic mass in the porta hepatis or hepatoduodenal ligament communicating directly with the biliary tree; absence of internal soft-tissue enhancement unless complicated by malignant transformation into cholangiocarcinoma; demonstrates intraductal biliary calculi (choledocholithiasis) and biliary sludge

High-Resolution Abdominal Ultrasound: Primary initial screening modality demonstrating a well-defined anechoic cystic structure in the right upper quadrant clearly distinct from the gallbladder, with direct communication to the dilated biliary ductal system; color Doppler confirms complete absence of internal vascularity within the cyst lumen, cleanly excluding portal vein aneurysm or vascular malformation

Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS) / Duodenoscopy: For Type III choledochoceles, EUS reveals an anechoic cystic lesion centered in the submucosal layer of the duodenal wall at the major papilla with characteristic smooth mucosal bulging into the duodenal lumen ('clubbed-finger' or 'cobra-head' appearance on fluoroscopy)
pathology_manifestations: Surgical resection specimen: Grossly dilated bile duct cyst with a thick, fibrous, leathery wall measuring 2 to 10 mm in thickness; microscopic examination shows dense concentric fibrous connective tissue with patchy interspersed elastosis, chronic lymphoplasmacytic inflammatory infiltrates, and severe absence or near-total absence of a normal smooth muscle layer

Mucosal lining is frequently denuded, ulcerated, or replaced by metaplastic intestinal or pyloric-type glandular epithelium exhibiting variable grades of biliary intraepithelial neoplasia (BilIN); dramatically elevated lifetime risk of cholangiocarcinoma (up to 20-30% if not surgically excised, driven by chronic mucosal damage from refluxed proteolytic and lipolytic pancreatic enzymes secondary to APBDU)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal congenital pancreatobiliary disease with the classic clinical triad of jaundice, RUQ mass, and pain, paired with MRCP-defined Todani classification (Types I-IV) and anomalous pancreaticobiliary ductal union (APBDU), and fibrous ductal elastosis with premalignant metaplasia.

topics.name: Crohn's Disease
clinical_manifestations: Perianal disease: complex draining perianal fistulae, perianal abscesses, and large edematous 'elephant-ear' skin tags
Aphthous stomatitis: deep linear oral mucosal ulcers ('snail-track' ulcers)
Erythema nodosum (tender red pretibial nodules) and pyoderma gangrenosum
Peristomal cutaneous ulcerations and fistulae
Episcleritis and anterior uveitis
radiological_manifestations: CT and MR Enterography: Segmental transmural bowel wall thickening (>3 mm), 'skip lesions' (discontinuous diseased segments separated by normal bowel), prominent engorgement of mesenteric vasa recta ('comb sign'), creeping fat (fibrofatty mesenteric proliferation), luminal strictures with proximal dilation ('string sign' of Kantor), enterocutaneous and enteroenteric fistulae
Pelvic MRI: High-resolution evaluation of perianal fistulous tracts (Parks classification: transsphincteric, intersphincteric, suprasphincteric), abscess cavities, and horseshoe tracts
pathology_manifestations: Endoscopic / surgical biopsy: Transmural inflammatory infiltrate spanning from mucosa to serosa, lymphoid aggregates across all bowel layers, knife-like fissuring ulcers, and discrete, non-caseating (non-necrotizing) epithelioid granulomas (pathognomonic hallmark in 50-60%)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal transmural IBD with prominent external perianal fistulae and skin tags matching hallmark CT/MRE features: 'comb sign', creeping fat, 'string sign', and pelvic fistula MRI.

topics.name: Cronkhite-Canada Syndrome
synonyms: polyposis, skin pigmentation, alopecia, and fingernail changes
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic ectodermal triad: (1) Diffuse cutaneous hyperpigmentation consisting of light brown, dark brown, or black lentiginous macules and patches clustering over the face, neck, dorsal hands, palms, and soles; (2) Rapid-onset, diffuse, severe alopecia resulting in near-total or complete loss of scalp hair, eyebrows, and eyelashes; (3) Severe onychodystrophy affecting all 20 fingernails and toenails (thinning, longitudinal ridging, splitting, dystrophic atrophy, and total onycholysis/shedding)
Severe malabsorptive cachexia, profound temporal wasting, watery diarrhea (5-10 bulky stools daily), protein-losing enteropathy with bilateral lower extremity pitting edema and ascites
Ageusia (complete loss of taste sensation) or dysgeusia and dry mouth (xerostomia), contributing to profound anorexia and rapid involuntary weight loss
radiological_manifestations: CT / MR Enterography: Innumerable, diffuse, generalized polypoid lesions studding the entire gastrointestinal tract (stomach, duodenum, jejunum, ileum, colon, and rectum) with conspicuous sparing of the esophagus; marked diffuse thickening of the gastric mucosal rugal folds with a 'giant cobblestone' or cerebriform appearance; small bowel loop dilation, extensive mesenteric lymphadenopathy, and peritoneal ascites from severe hypoalbuminemia

Barium Fluoroscopy (Upper GI Series & Small Bowel Follow-Through): Diffuse, uniform, innumerable round-to-oval filling defects ('carpet of polyps') throughout the gastric antrum, body, and small intestine; thickened, distorted, nodular mucosal folds with barium trapping

Endoscopic Examination: Hundreds of sessile, strawberry-like, erythematous, edematous hamartomatous polyps scattered from stomach to rectum with normal intervening mucosa replaced by edematous, hyperemic folds
pathology_manifestations: Endoscopic mucosal biopsy of gastric, small bowel, or colonic polyps: Characteristic inflammatory hamartomatous polyps characterized by markedly dilated, tortuous, cystic mucosal glands filled with inspissated neutral mucin, eosinophilic proteinaceous material, and cellular debris; prominent expansion and severe edema of the lamina propria with a dense inflammatory infiltrate composed of eosinophils, plasma cells, lymphocytes, and neutrophils; overlying non-dysplastic foveolar hyperplasia; non-familial etiology without identified germline mutations
topics.inclusion_rationale: Extraordinary non-inherited polyposis syndrome featuring the pathognomonic clinical tetrad of diffuse hyperpigmentation, alopecia, onychodystrophy, and diarrhea, matched with pan-GI hamartomatous polyposis on CT enterography and cystic mucin-filled dilated glands on histology.

topics.name: Decompensated Cirrhosis with Severe Portal Hypertension
synonyms: end-stage liver disease with portal hypertension
clinical_manifestations: Caput medusae: prominent, engorged, tortuous subcutaneous collateral veins radiating centrifugally outward from the umbilicus across the anterior abdominal wall (direction of blood flow away from the umbilicus, toward the systemic caval system)

Multiple spider angiomas (spider nevi): central pulsating arteriole surrounded by fine radiating spider-like capillary legs over the face, neck, anterior chest wall, and upper arms, which blanch completely on central pressure and refill from the center outward
Palmar erythema: prominent, mottled, symmetrical blotchy redness localized to the thenar and hypothenar eminences of the palms with central sparing
Tense, protuberant abdominal ascites with positive fluid wave and shifting dullness; severe eversion of the umbilicus (umbilical hernia)
Asterixis ('flapping tremor'): bilateral, asynchronous, arrhythmic interruption of sustained voluntary posture during wrist dorsiflexion indicating hepatic encephalopathy

Scleral icterus, deep cutaneous jaundice, bilateral Dupuytren contractures of the palmar fascia, white nails of Muehrcke or Terry, gynecomastia, and severe testicular atrophy with loss of secondary sexual hair
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI: Markedly shrunken, lobulated, nodular liver surface contour with selective volume redistribution (profound atrophy of the right hepatic lobe and medial segment of the left lobe, with compensatory hypertrophy of the caudate lobe [caudate-to-right-lobe ratio >0.65] and lateral segments II/III); wide fissures and expanded periportal spaces; massive splenomegaly (>13-16 cm longitudinal length); extensive peritoneal ascites

Doppler Ultrasound / CT Angiography: Recanalization of the ligamentum teres hepatis with a wide, patent paraumbilical vein (>3 mm) arising from the left branch of the portal vein and coursing through the anterior abdominal wall to the umbilicus (Cruveilhier-Baumgarten sign); massive tortuous gastroesophageal varices, splenorenal shunts, retroperitoneal collateral veins (Retzius veins), and inferior mesenteric vein collaterals; hepatofugal (reversed, away from liver) or sluggish hepatopetal portal venous flow; portal vein diameter >13 mm

Upper GI Endoscopy / Barium Swallow: Serpiginous, bluish, tortuous intraluminal columns of dilated submucosal veins protruding into the distal esophagus ('beaded cord' appearance) and gastric fundus, with 'red wale signs' or hematocystic spots indicating impending rupture
pathology_manifestations: Liver wedge / core needle biopsy or explant: Complete loss and disruption of normal hepatic lobular architecture; broad bands of dense collagenous fibrous septa (staining brilliant blue with Masson trichrome and black with reticulin) bridging between adjacent portal tracts and central veins, encircling rounded, circumscribed regenerative nodules of hepatocytes devoid of central veins (micronodular [<3 mm] or macronodular [>3 mm]); extensive capillarization of sinusoidal endothelial cells (loss of endothelial fenestrations and deposition of organized basement membrane collagen in the space of Disse); ductular reaction at the margins of fibrous septa
topics.inclusion_rationale: The quintessential syndrome in hepatology defined by legendary bedside signs (caput medusae, spider angiomas, asterixis, palmar erythema) coupled with unmistakable imaging signs (recanalized umbilical vein, esophageal varices, caudate hypertrophy, nodular contour) and bridging fibrous regenerative nodules on trichrome histology.

topics.name: Esophageal Achalasia and Megaesophagus
clinical_manifestations: Severe, progressive cachexia and involuntary wasting with hollow temporal fossae and sunken supraclavicular fossae due to long-standing dysphagia to both liquids and solids
Nocturnal regurgitation of large volumes of stagnant, undigested food and foul mucus onto the pillow, leading to chronic cough, wheezing, and recurrent chemical aspiration pneumonia
Severe halitosis (fetor oris) from fermentation and putrefaction of retained esophageal contents within the dilated esophagus

In Chagas disease achalasia: Associated Romaña's sign (unilateral painless palpebral edema and conjunctivitis) in early infection; megacolon with severe abdominal distension and fecal impaction; apical cardiac aneurysm, right bundle branch block, and congestive heart failure
radiological_manifestations: Barium Esophagram (Barium Swallow - Fluoroscopy Gold Standard): Pathognomonic 'bird's beak' or 'rat-tail' sign: smooth, symmetrical, tapered narrowing of the distal esophagus at the level of the gastroesophageal junction (persistent lower esophageal sphincter contraction); massive upstream dilatation of the esophageal body (>6-10 cm; 'megaesophagus') with tortuous, redundant, sigmoid-like elongation ('sigmoid esophagus'); absent primary progressive peristalsis, with non-propulsive tertiary contractions; persistent barium column and distinct air-fluid level of retained secretions and food debris

Chest Radiography (Plain Film): Markedly widened superior and posterior mediastinum with double right heart border; prominent air-fluid level in the mid-to-upper chest behind the trachea; absence of the normal gastric fundic air bubble ('airless stomach'); basilar infiltrates from recurrent aspiration pneumonitis

Chest CT: Markedly dilated, fluid- and debris-filled thoracic esophagus with thin, smooth walls and abrupt smooth caliber transition at the diaphragmatic hiatus; exclusion of pseudoachalasia (no eccentric mucosal mass or mediastinal invasion)
pathology_manifestations: Esophageal myectomy (Heller myotomy) / autopsy specimen: Marked, selective degeneration and near-total absence or loss of ganglion cells within the myenteric (Auerbach) plexus in the muscularis propria of the lower esophageal body and lower esophageal sphincter; pronounced chronic inflammatory infiltrate composed of cytotoxic CD8+ T lymphocytes and eosinophils localized within the myenteric plexus (ganglionitis); prominent perineural fibrosis and smooth muscle hypertrophy of the circular muscular layer; in Chagasic achalasia, intracellular pseudocysts containing amastigotes of Trypanosoma cruzi in smooth muscle cells and cardiac myocytes
topics.inclusion_rationale: Foremost esophageal motility disorder marked by profound nutritional wasting, foul halitosis, and nocturnal regurgitation, diagnosed by the pathognomonic 'bird's beak' distal narrowing and massive megaesophagus on barium swallow, and myenteric ganglion loss on pathology.

topics.name: Familial Adenomatous Polyposis / Gardner Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Extracolonic bony manifestations (Gardner variant): Palpable, stony-hard, non-tender osteomas of the mandible (causing mandibular asymmetry), angle of the jaw, and facial/cranial bones
Cutaneous lesions: Multiple epidermoid cysts, subcutaneous fibromas, and lipomas situated predominantly on the scalp, face, back, and extremities
Dental abnormalities: Unerupted and impacted permanent teeth, supernumerary teeth, complex compound odontomas, and delayed tooth eruption

Ophthalmologic hallmark: Congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium (CHRPE) on dilated indirect ophthalmoscopy (multiple [typically >3-4], bilateral, oval or round, flat, hyperpigmented dark-brown/black retinal lesions with sharp margins and surrounding depigmented halos; present in >80% of Gardner patients)

Desmoid tumors: Large, deep, rock-hard, non-metastasizing fibroblastic masses within the anterior abdominal wall (rectus sheath) or mesentery, causing palpable abdominal mass, bowel tethering, ischemia, or ureteral obstruction
radiological_manifestations: Double-Contrast Barium Enema / CT Colonography: Striking, dense, innumerable carpet-like filling defects (hundreds to thousands of small, 2-10 mm sessile and pedunculated adenomatous polyps) blanketing the entire mucosal surface of the colon from cecum to rectum ('carpet of polyps'); mucosal stippling and contour irregularity; synchronous annular apple-core filling defects if malignant transformation to adenocarcinoma has supervened

Abdominal / Pelvic Contrast CT / MRI: Large, infiltrative, well-defined or poorly marginated, homogeneous soft-tissue masses in the small bowel mesentery or anterior abdominal wall representing intra-abdominal desmoid fibromatosis; encasement and traction on mesenteric vasculature, loops of small bowel, and ureters with hydronephrosis

Mandibular / Skull Panoramic Radiographs (Orthopantomogram / CT): Dense, well-circumscribed, ivory-like radiopaque cortical bony masses (osteomas) projecting from the mandible and calvarium; impacted and unerupted supernumerary teeth
Upper Endoscopy / Duodenography: Concomitant carpet of duodenal adenomas clustering around the ampulla of Vater (Spigelman staging)
pathology_manifestations: Total colectomy specimen: Vast mucosal field studded with >100 (often 1,000 to 5,000) adenomatous polyps; histopathology confirms tubular, tubulovillous, or villous adenomas displaying low-grade to high-grade epithelial dysplasia with pencillate, hyperchromatic, stratified nuclei, loss of nuclear polarity, nuclear crowding, and loss of goblet cell mucin; Desmoid tumors: bland, hypocellular proliferation of elongated spindle-shaped fibroblasts/myofibroblasts embedded in abundant hyalinized collagen without cytological atypia or atypical mitotic figures, showing strong nuclear accumulation of beta-catenin; driven by germline pathogenic truncation mutations in the APC tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 5q21-q22
topics.inclusion_rationale: Landmark gastrointestinal polyposis syndrome with unmistakable syndromic markers (mandibular osteomas, epidermoid cysts, CHRPE fundus lesions, and desmoid tumors) corroborated by the breathtaking 'carpet of polyps' on barium enema/CT and diffuse adenomatous dysplasia with beta-catenin activation.

topics.name: Gastric Antral Vascular Ectasia (GAVE / Watermelon Stomach)
clinical_manifestations: Profound conjunctival and palmar pallor due to severe chronic, transfusion-dependent iron-deficiency anemia from persistent low-grade occult gastrointestinal bleeding

High clinical association with systemic sclerosis (scleroderma, ~30-60%): Sclerodactyly (tight, shiny skin over fingers with fixed flexion contractures), digital pitting scars, facial and mucosal telangiectasias, and Raynaud phenomenon
Concurrent stigmata of chronic cirrhosis in ~30% of cases (palmar erythema, spider angiomas, jaundice, mild splenomegaly)

Pathognomonic photographic endoscopic appearance: Distinctive erythematous stripes formed by tortuous, dilated, ectatic mucosal capillaries radiating longitudinally from the pylorus across the antrum toward the body, resembling the dark and light green stripes on the rind of a watermelon ('watermelon stomach'); or diffuse punctate 'honeycomb' red spots in cirrhosis
radiological_manifestations: Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS): Selective thickening of the gastric mucosal and submucosal layers strictly confined to the antrum (sparing the muscularis propria), with prominent tortuous, hypoechoic ectatic vascular structures within the submucosa; absence of large perigastric collaterals (distinguishing GAVE from portal hypertensive gastropathy)

Multidetector Abdominal CT / CT Gastrography: Symmetrical, hypervascular mucosal thickening of the gastric antrum displaying intense arterial and venous enhancement, with normal mural thickness in the gastric fundus and body; absence of ectopic varices

Technetium-99m Red Blood Cell Scintigraphy: Focal or diffuse persistent tracer accumulation localized to the gastric antrum, confirming chronic, non-variceal antral blood pooling and low-grade hemorrhage
pathology_manifestations: Endoscopic antral mucosal/submucosal biopsy: Pathognomonic diagnostic triad: (1) marked dilatation, tortuosity, and ectasia of mucosal and superficial submucosal capillaries and venules, (2) widespread intravascular microvascular fibrin thrombi in mucosal capillaries, and (3) prominent spindle cell fibromuscular hyperplasia of the lamina propria with smooth muscle fibers radiating between mucosal glands; CD31 and CD34 immunostains highlight the dense tangle of ectatic capillaries; lack of inflammatory infiltrate and lack of Helicobacter pylori colonization
topics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield mucosal vascular disorder presenting with transfusion-dependent pallor and systemic sclerosis stigmata, diagnosed by the pathognomonic 'watermelon stomach' radiating red stripes on endoscopy and the classic histopathologic triad of ectatic capillaries, microthrombi, and fibromuscular hyperplasia.

topics.name: Gastric Linitis Plastica (Diffuse-Type Gastric Carcinoma)
synonyms: signet ring cell carcinoma of stomach
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark metastatic bedside lymphadenopathy: Virchow's node (Troisier sign: hard, non-tender, enlarged, fixed left supraclavicular lymph node) and Irish's node (firm, palpable left anterior axillary lymph node)
Sister Mary Joseph nodule: Firm, indurated, irregular, ulcerated or violaceous metastatic cutaneous nodule at the umbilicus
Blumer's shelf: Hard, shelf-like, palpable nodular mass in the rectovesical or rectouterine pouch (pouch of Douglas) on digital rectal or pelvic examination
Krukenberg tumor: Palpable bilateral, firm, non-tender pelvic/lower abdominal masses with abdominal distension from metastatic ovarian enlargement in pre- or post-menopausal women

Paraneoplastic cutaneous signs: Leser-Trélat sign (sudden, explosive eruption of hundreds of intensely pruritic, hyperpigmented seborrheic keratoses over the trunk) and malignant acanthosis nigricans (velvety, hyperkeratotic, hyperpigmented plaques in intertriginous folds of neck and axillae)
Profound neoplastic cachexia: Severe temporal and skeletal muscle wasting, early satiety after only a few bites of food, and persistent epigastric fullness
radiological_manifestations: Barium Upper GI Fluoroscopy (Barium Meal): Pathognomonic 'leather bottle stomach' (linitis plastica): rigid, foreshortened, non-distensible stomach with complete loss of normal peristaltic contractions; diffuse, circumferential luminal narrowing; blunted, thickened, flattened, or completely obliterated mucosal rugal folds; rapid, unhindered transit of barium through a tubular, non-compliant stomach directly into the duodenum

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT / MRI: Marked, diffuse, circumferential, homogeneous mural thickening of the gastric wall (>10-15 mm) extending from fundus to pylorus with loss of the normal multilayered mural architecture; rigid, small-volume gastric lumen; necrotic left supraclavicular lymphadenopathy (Virchow node) and periumbilical soft-tissue infiltration; bilateral large, lobulated, solid-cystic ovarian masses with thick enhancing septa and central necrosis (Krukenberg tumors); peritoneal carcinomatosis with nodular omental caking and malignant ascites
pathology_manifestations: Gastric resection / endoscopic strip biopsy: Diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma (Lauren classification) / poorly cohesive carcinoma: highly infiltrative, discohesive malignant epithelial cells diffusely permeating the gastric wall without gland formation; pathognomonic 'signet-ring cell' morphology (cells containing a large, prominent intracytoplasmic mucin droplet that pushes, compresses, and indents the hyperchromatic nucleus into a crescent shape against the plasma membrane); mucin highlighted by mucicarmine and PAS-alcian blue stains; massive, dense desmoplastic fibrous stroma throughout the submucosa and muscularis propria; complete loss of membranous E-cadherin (CDH1) expression by immunohistochemistry; Krukenberg ovarian metastases demonstrate the identical signet-ring cell infiltration within an edematous cellular stroma
topics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal malignant GI entity marked by famous eponymous physical signs (Virchow node, Sister Mary Joseph nodule, Krukenberg tumor, Leser-Trélat sign) paired with the pathognomonic 'leather bottle' rigid non-distensible stomach on CT/barium meal and E-cadherin-negative signet-ring cell pathology.

topics.name: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST)
clinical_manifestations: Palpable, firm, non-tender, mobile or fixed large abdominal or epigastric mass, often incidentally detected or discovered during evaluation for chronic vague abdominal fullness and early satiety

Gastrointestinal hemorrhage stigmata: Recurrent episodes of dark tarry stools (melena), hematochezia, or brisk hematemesis resulting from central mucosal ulceration ('dell' or crater) overlying the submucosal exophytic tumor; chronic severe microcytic anemia with profound pallor, fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and resting tachycardia

Cutaneous and syndromic associations: Multiple neurofibromas, café-au-lait macules, and axillary freckling (Crowe sign) in Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1)-associated wild-type GIST; Carney triad (gastric GIST, extra-adrenal paraganglioma, and pulmonary chondroma) in young females; Carney-Stratakis syndrome (GIST and paraganglioma with germline succinate dehydrogenase / SDH mutations)
Acute abdomen: Sudden acute peritonitis and hemoperitoneum secondary to spontaneous rupture of a hypervascular exophytic subserosal tumor into the peritoneal cavity
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Primary Imaging Modality): Large (frequently >5 cm, up to 15-30 cm), well-circumscribed, lobulated, highly vascular, exophytic soft-tissue mass originating intramurally from the stomach (60%), jejunum/ileum (30%), duodenum (5%), or rectum (5%); characteristic heterogeneous enhancement with extensive internal low-attenuation areas of central cystic necrosis, hemorrhage, or liquefaction; central gas- or contrast-filled ulceration ('torus' or 'doughnut' sign) communicating directly with the gastrointestinal lumen; prominent, tortuous feeding tumor vessels; typically lacks significant regional lymphadenopathy (unlike gastric adenocarcinoma or lymphoma); hepatic and peritoneal metastases appear as hypervascular rim-enhancing target lesions

Contrast-Enhanced Abdomen MRI: Iso-to-hypointense on T1-weighted images, markedly hyperintense on T2-weighted images with prominent necrotic/cystic components and fluid-debris levels from intratumoral hemorrhage; intense, heterogeneous peripheral contrast enhancement; diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) showing restricted diffusion in solid cellular components

Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS): Well-demarcated hypoechoic mass arising distinctly within the fourth sonographic layer of the gastrointestinal wall (muscularis propria), occasionally third layer (submucosa); fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNA/FNB) provides diagnostic tissue core
pathology_manifestations: Resected tumor specimen / Core biopsy: Grossly fleshy, pink-tan, whorled or lobulated mass with focal cystic degeneration, hemorrhage, and necrosis; three distinct histologic architectural subtypes: (1) Spindle cell type (70%): Fascicles or whorls of uniform, elongated spindle cells with blunt-ended pale cigar-shaped nuclei, perinuclear vacuoles, and fibrillary eosinophilic cytoplasm; (2) Epithelioid type (20%): Sheets or nests of round-to-polygonal cells with abundant clear or eosinophilic cytoplasm and round vesicular nuclei; (3) Mixed spindle-epithelioid type (10%); Pathognomonic immunohistochemical profile: Strongly and diffusely positive for CD117 (c-KIT receptor tyrosine kinase, >95%) and DOG1 (Discovered on GIST-1 / Anoctamin-1, >98%); CD34 positive in 60-70%; positive for nestin; negative for S100 and desmin (distinguishing from schwannoma and leiomyoma/leiomyosarcoma); Molecular genetics: 75-80% harbor gain-of-function somatic activating mutations in KIT gene (exon 11, 9, 13, 17); 5-10% in PDGFRA gene (exon 18); remainder are SDH-deficient / quadruple wild-type
topics.inclusion_rationale: The archetypal mesenchymal neoplasm of the alimentary tract displaying striking exophytic CT masses with central cavitation, strong syndromic links to neurofibromatosis, and classic KIT/DOG1 immunohistochemical positivity driving targeted imatinib tyrosine-kinase inhibitor therapy.

topics.name: Hereditary Hemochromatosis
clinical_manifestations: 'Bronze diabetes': characteristic slate-gray, metallic, or bronze hyperpigmentation of the skin (predominantly face, neck, extensor hands, and genitals due to combined melanin and hemosiderin deposition)
Second and third MCP joint arthropathy with painful bony enlargement and fixed flexion deformities
Testicular atrophy and gynecomastia (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism from pituitary iron)
Stigmata of chronic cirrhosis and congestive heart failure
radiological_manifestations: Liver MRI (T2* Gradient-Echo / R2* Relaxometry): Severe, pathognomonic signal loss (black liver) within the hepatic parenchyma on T2 and T2* gradient-echo sequences due to magnetic susceptibility artifact from massive parenchymal iron deposition; pancreas also displays severe signal drop
Hand Radiographs: Characteristic 'hook-like' or drooping osteophytes on the radial margins of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpal heads, joint space narrowing, subchondral cysts, and chondrocalcinosis
Cardiac MRI: Myocardial T2* shortening (<20 ms) indicating life-threatening myocardial siderosis
pathology_manifestations: Liver core biopsy: Intense, golden-brown hemosiderin pigment granules accumulating within the cytoplasm of periportal hepatocytes; highlighted by brilliant blue staining with Perls' Prussian blue stain; quantitative hepatic iron index >1.9
topics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal iron overload disease with historic 'bronze diabetes' skin pigmentation and MCP arthropathy paired with the pathognomonic 'black liver' on T2* MRI and hook osteophytes on hand X-rays.

topics.name: Hereditary Pancreatitis (PRSS1 / SPINK1-Associated Chronic Pancreatitis)
clinical_manifestations: Early childhood onset (typically <10 years of age) of recurrent episodes of agonizing, severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating straight through to the mid-back, relieved characteristically by sitting upright and leaning forward (the 'pancreatic position'), accompanied by intractable nausea and vomiting

Progression to end-stage chronic pancreatitis by adolescence or early adulthood: severe exocrine pancreatic insufficiency manifested by chronic steatorrhea (voluminous, foul-smelling, pale, greasy, floating stools that produce an oily film or droplets in toilet water), chronic fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption (A, D, E, K), and significant failure to thrive / severe muscle wasting and cachexia

Endocrine pancreatic insufficiency: early development of pancreatogenic brittle diabetes mellitus (type 3c diabetes) with marked glycemic lability, frequent severe hypoglycemia (due to concomitant loss of islet alpha cells and glucagon secretion), and polyuria/polydipsia

Physical examination: marked temporal and proximal muscle wasting, profound cachexia, palmar erythema and scleral icterus from secondary common bile duct stricturing, and prominent abdominal epigastric tenderness during flare-ups
Extremely high lifetime risk (>40-50%) of developing pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), rising significantly after age 40, especially in tobacco smokers
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Plain Radiograph (KUB) & Non-Contrast Abdominal CT: Pathognomonic, striking, massive coarse intraductal calcifications and rounded 'bull's eye' or 'popcorn' calculi measuring up to 1-2 cm distributed throughout the entire head, body, and tail along the main pancreatic duct and secondary branches (much larger and more rounded than the fine speckled calcifications of alcoholic chronic pancreatitis)

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Marked parenchymal atrophy of the pancreatic body and tail with replacement by fibrofatty tissue; severe, irregular, beaded main pancreatic duct dilatation ('chain of lakes' or 'string of pearls' appearance, duct caliber >10-15 mm) with alternating segments of tight inflammatory strictures and cystic sacculations; intraductal filling defects corresponding to dense calcified stones; associated pseudocysts and common bile duct compression

Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP): High-resolution delineation of the entire ductal architecture showing marked main pancreatic duct ectasia, ectatic side branches, intraductal signal voids (stones), and distal smooth tapering stricture of the intrapancreatic common bile duct ('double-duct' appearance if head mass develops)

Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS): Rosemont and Milwaukee criteria for chronic pancreatitis: hyperechoic parenchymal foci with shadowing (calculi), parenchymal lobularity with honeycombing, thickened hyperechoic duct margins, and main duct irregular dilatation with intraductal calculi
pathology_manifestations: Pancreatectomy / surgical biopsy: Gross specimen shows a shrunken, rock-hard, densely fibrotic pancreas with a prominently dilated main pancreatic duct containing numerous white-to-chalky, hard, jagged or rounded intraductal stones composed primarily of calcium carbonate (calcite) precipitate over a proteinaceous nidus

Histology: Advanced chronic pancreatitis with extensive intralobular and perilobular collagenous sclerosis and fibrosis; severe, near-total loss and atrophy of acinar lobules; residual hyperplastic or metaplastic ductules (mucinous and squamous metaplasia); relative preservation of endocrine islets of Langerhans early, progressing to islet aggregation and sclerosis late; chronic inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and activated pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs)

Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant gain-of-function mutation in the PRSS1 gene on chromosome 7q35 encoding cationic trypsinogen (predominantly p.R122H or p.N29I, which disrupt the autolytic cleavage site preventing protective trypsin autodegradation), or autosomal recessive/modifier mutations in SPINK1 (p.N34S), CTRC, or CFTR
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic monogenic pancreatobiliary disease with childhood onset of agonizing back-radiating pain, steatorrhea, and brittle type 3c diabetes, paired with pathognomonic massive rounded 'bull's eye' intraductal stones and 'chain of lakes' ductal dilatation on CT/radiographs, driven by PRSS1 mutations.

topics.name: Ménétrier Disease (Hypertrophic Protein-Losing Gastropathy)
clinical_manifestations: Massive, severe peripheral pitting edema (anasarca, periorbital edema, scrotal/labial edema, ascites, and pleural effusions) resulting from profound hypoalbuminemia and systemic hypoproteinemia secondary to enteric protein loss across the hyperplastic gastric mucosa (protein-losing gastropathy)
Severe postprandial epigastric pain, persistent nausea, projectile or copious vomiting, early satiety, and anorexia accompanied by profound involuntary weight loss and muscle wasting (cachexia)
Epigastric fullness or ill-defined soft epigastric tenderness to deep palpation without focal peritoneal signs, often accompanied by an audible gastric succession splash

Microcytic hypochromic anemia stigmata (pallor, conjunctival rim pallor, fatigue, angular cheilitis, brittle spoon-shaped nails / koilonychia) secondary to chronic, occult, microscopic mucosal bleeding from friable gastric rugae

Pediatric acute self-limiting variant (frequently triggered by acute cytomegalovirus / CMV infection or Helicobacter pylori) manifesting with abrupt-onset facial edema, periorbital puffiness, lethargy, and severe hypoalbuminemia
radiological_manifestations: Upper Gastrointestinal Barium Series (Barium Meal / Double-Contrast Fluoroscopy): Striking, pathognomonic giant, tortuous, thickened gastric rugal folds resembling cerebral gyri ('brain-like' or 'convoluted cerebriform' appearance) predominantly involving the fundus and greater curvature of the gastric body, with absolute or relative sparing of the gastric antrum; broad, polypoid-like filling defects coated by thick, hypersecreted mucus that separates barium particles

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Marked, diffuse, scalloped mural thickening of the gastric fundus and body (often >10 mm, up to 20-30 mm; normal gastric wall <3-5 mm) with preservation of mural stratification; prominent, undulating giant mucosal folds projecting deeply into the gastric lumen; classic abrupt transition sparing the gastric antrum; secondary imaging signs include diffuse ascites, bilateral pleural effusions, and anasarca (diffuse subcutaneous edema)
