radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Doppler Ultrasound / Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI: High-yield evaluation for Budd-Chiari syndrome (the leading cause of mortality in PNH): absence of flow, non-visualization, or intraluminal filling defects in hepatic veins; marked hypertrophy of the caudate lobe (which has independent venous drainage into IVC); patchy, heterogeneous mosaic parenchymal enhancement during early arterial phase; severe ascites, splenomegaly, and portal/mesenteric vein thrombosis

Renal MRI (Pathognomonic Renal Hemosiderosis): Striking, uniform, bilateral darkening of the renal cortex on T1- and T2-weighted sequences, with marked signal loss ('black renal cortex') on gradient-echo / susceptibility-weighted T2* sequences due to massive reabsorption and intracellular deposition of hemosiderin in renal proximal tubular epithelial cells, sparing the renal medulla

Brain CT / MRI & MR Venography: High-risk detection of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST): superior sagittal or transverse sinus dense clot sign on non-contrast CT, 'empty delta sign' on contrast-enhanced CT, and loss of normal flow void on MRI
pathology_manifestations: Flow Cytometry (Gold-Standard Diagnostic Test): Multiparameter flow cytometry demonstrating complete absence (Type III cells) or partial deficiency (Type II cells) of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored regulatory proteins—specifically CD55 (decay-accelerating factor / DAF) and CD59 (membrane inhibitor of reactive lysis / MIRL / MAC-inhibitory protein)—on erythrocytes and granulocytes/monocytes using fluorescent aerolysin (FLAIR); identification of a distinct PNH clone size

Peripheral Blood & Urine Analysis: Normocytic or macrocytic anemia with prominent polychromasia and elevated reticulocyte count, with notable absence of spherocytes or mechanical schistocytes (distinguishing complement-mediated from mechanical hemolysis); markedly elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH often >5-10 times upper limit of normal) and undetectable haptoglobin; urinalysis demonstrates positive dipstick for blood with absence of intact red blood cells on microscopy, and pathognomonic Prussian blue staining of urinary sediment demonstrates massive blue hemosiderin granules within desquamated tubular cells (hemosiderinuria)

Bone Marrow Aspirate & Trephine Biopsy: Normocellular or hypercellular marrow showing prominent erythroid hyperplasia responding to peripheral hemolysis, or varying degrees of hypocellularity if presenting in the context of an aplastic anemia/PNH overlap syndrome

Molecular Genetics: Acquired somatic loss-of-function mutations in the X-linked PIGA (phosphatidylinositol glycan class A) gene in one or more hematopoietic stem cell clones, preventing the initial enzymatic step in GPI anchor biosynthesis
topics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic complement-mediated hematologic disorder displaying striking morning mahogany-colored hemoglobinuria and scleral icterus, imaged via pathognomonic 'black renal cortex' hemosiderosis on T2* MRI and Budd-Chiari hepatic thrombosis, and definitively confirmed by flow cytometric loss of CD55/CD59/FLAER.

topics.name: Polycythemia Vera
clinical_manifestations: Facial plethora ('ruddy cyanosis'): Deeply flushed, red-purple engorgement of the face, cheeks, ears, lips, and neck, contrasting with suffused, brick-red, congested conjunctival vessels ('bloodshot eyes') without inflammation

Aquagenic pruritus: Intense, intractable, prickling or stinging cutaneous itch devoid of rash, classically triggered within minutes of contact with warm water (taking a warm bath or shower), lasting 15-60 minutes and resistant to antihistamines

Erythromelalgia: Paroxysmal, intense burning pain, bright erythema, and increased skin temperature affecting the extremities (principally soles of feet and toes, occasionally palms), exacerbated by warmth and dramatically relieved by elevating the limbs or taking a single dose of aspirin
Retinal changes: Marked engorgement, tortuosity, and dark purple coloration of retinal veins on fundoscopy ('fundus polycythaemicus') with occasional retinal hemorrhages
Splenomegaly: Palpable, firm, non-tender spleen extending well below the left costal margin (in >70% of patients), sometimes crossing the midline and causing visible left upper quadrant fullness
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Doppler Ultrasound / Contrast-Enhanced CT: Massive, homogeneous splenomegaly (craniocaudal length often >16-20 cm); direct visualization of hepatic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari syndrome) or extrahepatic portal vein thrombosis, demonstrating non-visualized or truncated hepatic veins, intrahepatic comma-shaped collateral veins, patchy caudate lobe hypertrophy, and reduced peripheral hepatic perfusion; mesenteric and splenic vein thrombosis

Skeletal MRI: Marked diffuse conversion of fatty yellow marrow to cellular red marrow throughout the appendicular skeleton (proximal and distal femur and humerus), demonstrating diffuse low signal intensity on T1-weighted images and elevated signal on STIR
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow trephine core biopsy (WHO Major Criterion): Marked hypercellularity (often 90-100% cellularity) with panmyelosis (trilineage proliferation: prominent erythroid hyperplasia, granulocytic hyperplasia, and megakaryocytic hyperplasia); megakaryocytes form loose clusters, vary in size, and display hyperlobulated, pleomorphic nuclei without significant dysplasia; minimal reticulin fibrosis in early stages (grade 0-1/3), advancing to dense reticulin/collagen fibrosis in post-PV myelofibrosis

Peripheral blood smear: Striking polycythemia with packed red blood cells, mild leukocytosis (predominance of mature neutrophils), and thrombocytosis (large, hypergranulated platelets); absence of leucoerythroblastic features unless transformed to myelofibrosis

Molecular genetic testing: Pathognomonic somatic gain-of-function mutation in the JAK2 gene: JAK2 V617F (exon 14) detected in >95-97% of patients; JAK2 exon 12 mutations identified in 2-3% of remaining JAK2 V617F-negative cases; Serum erythropoietin (EPO) subnormal/suppressed
topics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic myeloproliferative disorder defined by bedside ruddy plethoric facies, suffused conjunctivae, aquagenic pruritus, and burning erythromelalgia, coupled with massive ultrasound splenomegaly, splanchnic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari), and panmyeloid hypercellular marrow harboring JAK2 V617F.

topics.name: Primary Myelofibrosis
clinical_manifestations: Colossal, rock-hard splenomegaly: Massive, non-tender or tender, firm splenomegaly frequently crossing the abdominal midline and descending into the right lower quadrant or pelvis; colossal abdominal asymmetry, early satiety, severe left upper quadrant pain (from splenic infarction or perisplenitis with friction rubs), and progressive moderate hepatomegaly

Extreme constitutional symptoms & cachexia: Severe profound unintentional weight loss, temporal and thenar muscle wasting ('bitemporal hollows'), sunken cheeks, drenching night sweats, low-grade fevers, and disabling generalized pruritus

Cutaneous & extramedullary hematopoietic signs: Extramedullary hematopoietic skin deposits (eruptive red-to-violaceous cutaneous plaques, nodules, or tumors), petechiae, ecchymoses, and mucosal purpura; diffuse pallor, resting tachycardia, and lower-extremity dependent pitting edema from portal hypertension and inferior vena cava compression by the massive spleen
Bone pain & arthropathies: Severe, deep, aching bone pain (especially in long bones and axial skeleton), exquisite localized sternal tenderness, and secondary gouty arthritis from purine turnover
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT / MRI: Giant, colossal splenomegaly (craniocaudal length often >25-35 cm) displacing stomach, bowel loops, and left kidney into the right hemiabdomen; frequent wedge-shaped, sharply demarcated, non-enhancing peripheral areas of splenic infarction; portal hypertension signs including dilated splenic vein, ascites, and splenorenal collaterals; marked hepatomegaly

Plain Skeletal Radiography / Skeletal CT: Diffuse, uniform or patchy osteosclerosis presenting in ~40-60% of advanced cases as increased bone density, coarsened thickened trabeculae, and cortical thickening without osteolysis, prominently involving the axial skeleton (spine, ribs, pelvis, proximal humeri, and femora); characteristic 'sandwich vertebrae' (dense sclerotic bands parallel to vertebral endplates)

18F-FDG PET/CT & Bone Scintigraphy: Diffuse, intense FDG uptake throughout the entire axial and appendicular skeletal marrow, extending down into distal extremities (distal tibiae and forearms) corresponding to peripheral expansion of active extramedullary and intramedullary hematopoiesis; bone scintigraphy reveals a 'super-scan' appearance with intense axial uptake and faint or absent renal visualization
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear (Pathognomonic Leukoerythroblastic Picture): Striking, classical tear-drop poikilocytes (dacrocytes) formed during mechanical extrusion through distorted, fibrotic marrow sinusoids; circulating immature myeloid cells (myelocytes, metamyelocytes, myeloblasts <10%) and nucleated red blood cells (normoblasts); anisopoikilocytosis; giant, hypogranular, dysplastic platelets and circulating megakaryocytic nuclei

Bone Marrow Aspirate & Trephine Core Biopsy (WHO Major Criterion): Marrow aspirate characteristically yields a 'dry tap' (punctio sicca) due to dense fibrosis. Trephine biopsy reveals marked hypercellularity with prominent megakaryocytic proliferation and atypia: tightly clustered, abnormally large megakaryocytes with hyperchromatic, bulbous, or 'cloud-like' nuclei with abnormal maturation (high N:C ratio); dense reticulin fibrosis (MF-2 or MF-3 on Silver Gomori stain) and extensive collagen fibrosis (blue on Masson trichrome stain); progressive osteosclerosis with neo-osteogenesis and dilated sinusoids containing intraluminal hematopoiesis

Molecular Genetics: Mutually exclusive driver mutations identifying constitutively active JAK-STAT signaling: JAK2 V617F (exon 14, in ~50-60% of patients), CALR (calreticulin exon 9 indels, in ~25-30%), or MPL (thrombopoietin receptor W515K/L, in ~5-10%); ~10% are 'triple-negative'
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic myeloproliferative neoplasm manifesting bedside with colossal spleen crossing the midline and profound cachectic muscle wasting, recognized radiologically by diffuse patchy osteosclerosis on CT and splenic infarcts, and diagnosed by blood smear dacrocytes (tear-drop cells) and marrow dry tap with dense silver-stained reticulin/collagen fibrosis.

topics.name: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
clinical_manifestations: Massive cervical lymphadenopathy ('bull neck'): Rapid, painless, bilateral, symmetric, grotesque enlargement of cervical lymph nodes forming huge, matted, confluent lobulated masses that obscure the angle of the jaw and sternocleidomastoid contours

Extranodal cutaneous lesions: Asymptomatic, firm, indurated, yellow-red, brownish, or violaceous papules, plaques, and solitary or grouped subcutaneous nodules (often xanthomatous in appearance), frequently on the face, nasal bridge, and trunk

Extranodal upper respiratory tract involvement: Exophytic mucosal masses and polypoid swelling of the nasal septum, turbinates, and paranasal sinuses causing chronic nasal obstruction, epistaxis, and 'saddle-nose' deformity
Extranodal orbital involvement: Painless, progressive, unilateral or bilateral exophthalmos (proptosis), eyelid edema, and periorbital soft tissue fullness from retro-orbital histiocytic deposition
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Neck and Chest CT: Massive, extensive, bilateral cervical, submandibular, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy with homogeneous soft-tissue density and moderate contrast enhancement, frequently coalescing into giant confluent lobulated nodal conglomerations; absence of central caseous necrosis or macroscopic calcification (distinguishing RDD from tuberculosis and necrotic metastatic carcinoma)

Contrast-Enhanced Brain / Spine MRI: Dural-based, intensely and homogeneously enhancing extra-axial masses with prominent 'dural tail' sign, closely mimicking meningioma, causing compressive myelopathy or mass effect on adjacent brain parenchyma
Sinonasal CT: Soft-tissue opacification of the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses with extensive remodeling and thinning of adjacent bony walls without frank aggressive bony destruction
Whole-Body 18F-FDG PET/CT: Symmetrical, intense hypermetabolism (SUVmax 5-15) throughout the cervical and mediastinal lymph node stations and extranodal skeletal/soft-tissue sites
pathology_manifestations: Lymph node / extranodal tissue biopsy: Massive sinus expansion and distension by large, pale, polygonal histiocytes possessing abundant clear-to-eosinophilic cytoplasm, round vesicular nuclei, and single prominent nucleoli; pathognomonic emperipolesis: intact, viable, non-degraded lymphocytes, plasma cells, and occasional erythrocytes traversing the cytoplasm of intact viable histiocytes; background interfollicular stroma exhibits marked sclerosis, polyclonal plasma cell infiltrate, and prominent lymphoid follicles; IHC: Histiocytes are intensely and diffusely positive for S100 protein and CD68 / CD163; negative for CD1a and Langerin (CD207) (distinguishing RDD from Langerhans cell histiocytosis)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Striking histiocytic disorder characterized by grotesque 'bull neck' cervical adenopathy and orbital exophthalmos, diagnosed by massive non-necrotic matted nodal conglomerations on CT and pathognomonic emperipolesis within S100-positive histiocytes.

topics.name: Sickle Cell Disease
clinical_manifestations: Dactylitis ('hand-foot syndrome'): Acute, exquisite, symmetric, painful, tender, tense, non-pitting soft tissue swelling of the dorsum of hands and feet in infants and young children (6-24 months) secondary to bone marrow infarction of the metacarpals and metatarsals

Craniofacial deformity ('chipmunk facies'): Prominent frontal and parietal bossing, maxillary hypertrophy, gnathopathy, malocclusion, and widening of the dental arch caused by profound extramedullary and intramedullary erythroid hyperplasia

Chronic lower extremity skin ulcers: Deep, sharply marginated, punched-out, painful, indolent ulcers with necrotic yellow fibrinous bases located over the medial and lateral malleoli, often surrounded by hyperpigmentation and atrophic skin

Ocular and systemic signs: Marked scleral icterus (conjugated/unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia from chronic hemolysis); pallor of conjunctivae and palmar creases; priapism; acute chest syndrome (tachypnea, chest pain, fever, hypoxia)
radiological_manifestations: Skull Radiography / CT: Marked widening and thickening of the diploic space with complete thinning of the outer cortical table, accompanied by vertical, fine, perpendicular trabecular striations producing the pathognomonic 'hair-on-end' (crew-cut) appearance of the calvarium

Spine Radiography / CT: Pathognomonic 'H-shaped vertebrae' (Reynolds sign): sharp, square, step-like central endplate depression of lumbar and thoracic vertebral bodies caused by microvascular ischemia and growth inhibition of the central growth plates with preserved peripheral vascular supply; 'fish-mouth' biconcave vertebrae

Musculoskeletal Radiography / MRI: Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) of the femoral and humeral heads demonstrating subchondral radiolucent crescent sign, structural flattening, sclerosis, and joint collapse; bone-within-bone appearance (endosteal bone formation following infarction); acute dactylitis showing initial soft-tissue swelling followed by patchy periosteal reaction and cortical resorption

Abdominal CT / Ultrasound: Progressive splenic autosplenectomy: childhood splenomegaly progressing to an exceedingly small, densely calcified, shrunken, non-functional fibrous splenic remnant; cholelithiasis (multiple radiopaque calcium bilirubinate gallstones)
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral blood smear: Striking red blood cell morphology featuring elongated, crescentic, sickle-shaped erythrocytes with pointed ends (drepanocytes / irreversible sickle cells); target cells (codocytes), Howell-Jolly bodies and Pappenheimer bodies (reflecting functional asplenia/autosplenectomy), polychromasia, nucleated red blood cells, and marked anisopoikilocytosis

Hemoglobin electrophoresis / High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC): Homozygous sickle cell disease (HbSS) demonstrates absent adult Hemoglobin A (HbA 0%), predominant Hemoglobin S (HbS 80-95%), elevated Hemoglobin F (HbF 5-20%), and normal/mildly elevated HbA2

Bone marrow aspirate/biopsy: Massive normoblastic erythroid hyperplasia (myeloid:erythroid ratio reversed to 1:1 or 1:2) with trabecular bone thinning, vascular engorgement, and prominent hemosiderin iron accumulation in reticuloendothelial macrophages
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential hemoglobinopathy with dramatic clinical phenotypes (infantile hand-foot dactylitis, malleolar leg ulcers, chipmunk facies) and unmistakable skeletal radiology: 'hair-on-end' skull, Reynolds 'H-shaped' vertebrae, and dense calcified autosplenectomy.

topics.name: Solitary Plasmacytoma
clinical_manifestations: Solitary Plasmacytoma of Bone (SPB): Severe, localized, persistent, deep bone pain corresponding to a focal skeletal site (most commonly thoracic/lumbar spine, pelvis, ribs, or proximal femur); localized palpable bony swelling or tenderness; neurologic deficits (radiculopathy, lower extremity weakness, sensory loss, or acute paraplegia) from epidural cord compression in vertebral lesions

Extramedullary Plasmacytoma (EMP): Solitary, fleshy, smooth, sessile or pedunculated, highly vascular, red-to-violaceous polypoid mass protruding from the mucosal surfaces of the upper aerodigestive tract (nasopharynx, nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses, or tonsils); symptoms of persistent unilateral nasal obstruction, epistaxis, hoarseness, dysphagia, or proptosis; subcutaneous extramedullary violaceous tumors
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography / Skeletal CT: Solitary, sharply demarcated, expansile osteolytic lesion with cortical thinning, ballooning, or frank cortical breach, typically devoid of sclerotic margins or periosteal reaction; in vertebral bodies, produces a classic 'mini-brain' appearance on axial CT (thickened cortical and trabecular struts radiating from the periphery resembling cerebral sulci/gyri) or vertebral collapse ('vertebra plana')

Contrast-Enhanced MRI: Essential modality demonstrating a single focal mass hypointense on T1, hyperintense on T2/STIR, with brisk homogeneous contrast enhancement; delineates epidural extension and spinal cord compression in SPB; confirms complete absence of occult lesions in the remainder of the spine and pelvis

Whole-Body 18F-FDG PET/CT (Mandatory Exclusionary Modality): Single, solitary intensely hypermetabolic focus (SUVmax typically >4-8) with definitive negative whole-body survey proving the strict solitary nature of the disease and ruling out systemic Multiple Myeloma
pathology_manifestations: Biopsy of solitary lesion: Monomorphic, sheet-like infiltration of mature or immature atypical plasma cells with eccentric, cartwheel ('clock-face') nuclear chromatin, abundant basophilic cytoplasm, and perinuclear pale hof; monoclonality confirmed by light chain restriction (kappa or lambda) on in situ hybridization or immunohistochemistry; CD138+, CD38+, CD56+ (often in SPB) or CD56- (often in EMP); absence of high-grade marrow plasma cell infiltration on blind bone marrow biopsy (<5% plasma cells) and absence of CRAB end-organ damage (hypercalcemia, renal failure, anemia) attributable to multiple myeloma
topics.inclusion_rationale: Focal plasma cell neoplasm presenting with localized violaceous mucosal nasopharyngeal masses or solitary destructive spine tumors, confirmed by unique 'mini-brain' expansile lytic lesions on CT/MRI and solitary PET avidity without disseminated myeloma.

topics.name: Systemic Mastocytosis
clinical_manifestations: Urticaria pigmentosa (maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis): Fixed, non-blanching, reddish-brown to hyperpigmented round or oval macules and papules scattered symmetrically across the trunk and extremities, sparing the face, palms, and soles

Pathognomonic Darier sign: Stroking, rubbing, or scratching a cutaneous lesion results within minutes in localized urtication, erythema, edema, and intense surrounding wheal-and-flare reaction due to local histamine and mast cell mediator degranulation

Systemic mediator flush: Sudden episodic intense fiery-red flushing of face, neck, and upper chest accompanied by tachycardia, hypotension/syncope, throbbing headache, and explosive diarrhea/abdominal cramping

Dermatographism: Exaggerated linear wheal formation after light blunt stroking of normal-appearing skin; telangiectasia macularis eruptiva perstans (TMEP) in older adults showing persistent telangiectatic brownish macules
radiological_manifestations: Skeletal Radiography / CT: Diffuse or focal osteosclerosis alternating with osteolytic lesions, producing a classic mottled 'peppered' or 'pagetoid' bone appearance, predominantly in axial skeleton (spine, pelvis, ribs, and proximal femora); thickened, sclerotic vertebral trabeculae with cortical thickening; pathological compression fractures and progressive generalized osteopenia/osteoporosis in young individuals

Abdominal Ultrasound / CT: Marked diffuse hepatomegaly and splenomegaly (frequent hypersplenism), extensive mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, diffuse bowel wall thickening (mast cell enteropathy), and ascites

99mTc Bone Scintigraphy: Heterogeneous, patchy, diffuse skeletal uptake ('super-scan'-like pattern in severe bone marrow mastocytosis) reflecting intense osteoblastic reaction adjacent to mast cell aggregates
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow trephine core biopsy (Major WHO Diagnostic Criterion): Multifocal, dense, compact aggregates of >=15 mast cells per infiltrate located in perivascular, paratrabecular, or intertrabecular marrow spaces; abnormal mast cells display elongated, spindle-shaped morphology with hypogranular cytoplasm, oval or bilobed nuclei (atypical mast cells type I and II); metachromatic cytoplasmic granules highlighted on Giemsa, toluidine blue, or Astra blue stains; IHC (Minor Criteria): Aberrant co-expression of CD25 and/or CD2 on neoplastic mast cells (alongside constitutive CD117/KIT and tryptase); Molecular: Activating KIT point mutation at codon 816 (most commonly KIT D816V, exon 17) present in >90% of cases; Serum total tryptase persistently elevated >20 ng/mL in absence of anaphylaxis
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic systemic mediator and infiltration disorder recognized clinically by Darier sign (urtication upon stroking reddish-brown papules) and episodic flushing, diagnosed on imaging by mottled diffuse osteosclerosis/osteolysis on CT and confirmed by spindle mast cell bone marrow aggregates with CD117/CD25 positivity and KIT D816V.

topics.name: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura
clinical_manifestations: Cutaneous & mucosal bleeding manifestations: Florid spontaneous purpuric eruption, extensive petechiae over extremities and torso, ecchymoses, subconjunctival hemorrhages, brisk epistaxis, and wet purpura of the buccal mucosa due to profound, consumptive peripheral thrombocytopenia (often platelet count <10,000-20,000/microL)

Severe, fluctuating neurological deficits: Strikingly waxing and waning neurological alterations ranging from acute confusion, agitation, expressive aphasia, transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), fluctuating hemiparesis, dysarthria, and headache to visual disturbances, seizures, stupor, and deep coma, reflecting transient microvascular platelet thrombi in the cerebral microcirculation

Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia signs: Marked porcelain-to-lemon-yellow skin pallor combined with vivid scleral icterus (unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia from intravascular mechanical erythrocyte fragmentation), dark cola-colored or tea-colored urine (hemoglobinuria)

Classic Diagnostic Pentad: The complete pentad—(1) thrombocytopenia with bleeding, (2) microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), (3) fluctuating neurologic deficits, (4) low-grade to high-grade fever, and (5) acute renal impairment—though present concurrently in only ~20-30% of patients, represents the iconic clinical hallmark
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (T2/FLAIR, DWI, and ADC): Multifocal, punctate or patchy hyperintensities in the subcortical white matter, basal ganglia, and cortex corresponding to acute microvascular platelet-rich ischemic microinfarctions; classic imaging pattern of Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES) with bilateral, symmetrical parieto-occipital subcortical hyperintensity on T2/FLAIR and elevated ADC representing reversible vasogenic edema

Abdominal / Renal Doppler Ultrasound: Kidneys usually appear normal in size with preserved parenchymal thickness but demonstrate increased cortical echogenicity and elevated resistive indices (RI >0.70-0.75) due to microvascular occlusion in the intrarenal arteriolar beds

CT Angiography / Brain MRA: Typically demonstrates normal large intracranial vessels (no major arterial trunk occlusion), highlighting that ischemic deficits are entirely microvascular and downstream of major bifurcations
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear (Cornerstone Microscopic Diagnosis): Marked microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with abundant red cell fragmentation: striking presence of schistocytes (helmet cells, triangular fragments, keratocytes, and microspherocytes) typically exceeding 1-2% of red blood cells (often 5-10+ per high-power field); marked polychromasia, nucleated red blood cells (normoblasts), severe thrombocytopenia with rare, giant stress platelets, and absence of platelet clumping

Histopathology (Skin, Gingival, or Organ Biopsy): Diagnostic disseminated platelet-rich, fibrin-poor microthrombi completely occluding arterioles and capillaries throughout multiple organs (brain, kidneys, heart, adrenals), with associated endothelial swelling and subendothelial hyaline deposition, without transmural inflammation, vessel wall necrosis, or leukocytoclasia (non-inflammatory microthrombosis)

Specialized Laboratory Hallmark: Severe deficiency of plasma ADAMTS13 metalloprotease activity (<10% of normal activity); detection of high-titer inhibitory anti-ADAMTS13 IgG autoantibodies in acquired immune TTP (or biallelic ADAMTS13 gene mutations in congenital Upshaw-Schulman syndrome); normal coagulation parameters (PT, aPTT, and fibrinogen normal, distinguishing TTP from disseminated intravascular coagulation)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening medical emergency recognized clinically by the classic pentad of petechiae/purpura, fluctuating focal aphasia/delirium, fever, and jaundice, verified radiologically by cerebral microvascular ischemic/PRES hyperintensities on brain MRI, and proved microscopically by sheets of schistocytes on blood smear and severe ADAMTS13 deficiency (<10%).

topics.name: Waldenström Macroglobulinemia
topics.subspecialty: Mature B-Cell Neoplasms / Plasma Cell Dyscrasias
clinical_manifestations: Hyperviscosity Retinopathy ('Fundus Macroglobulinemicus'): Dilated, hugely engorged, tortuous, segmented retinal veins displaying alternating narrowings and bulges resembling a string of sausages ('link-sausage' or 'boxcar' veins) on dilated fundoscopic examination; accompanied by diffuse flame-shaped retinal hemorrhages, soft exudates, microaneurysms, and bilateral papilledema, culminating in sudden painless visual loss

Mucocutaneous bleeding: Recurrent, profuse spontaneous epistaxis, persistent gingival bleeding, and prolonged oozing from minor trauma or surgical procedures caused by IgM coating of platelets and clotting factors

Cold-induced cutaneous changes: Acrocyanosis, Raynaud phenomenon, livedo reticularis, purpura, and cold urticaria affecting the fingertips, ears, and nose tip in patients with concomitant Type I IgM cryoglobulinemia or cold agglutinin disease

Neurologic & lymphoproliferative signs: Symmetrical, slowly progressive, distal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy ('numb feet' and ataxia); moderate non-tender peripheral lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT / Ultrasound: Moderate-to-marked homogeneous splenomegaly (in 30-40% of cases) and diffuse, smooth retroperitoneal, mesenteric, and celiac lymphadenopathy; absence of bulky conglomerations or necrotic nodal centers

Whole-Body Skeletal Radiography / CT: Absence of discrete punched-out osteolytic bone lesions (a critical negative radiological sign distinguishing Waldenström from Multiple Myeloma); diffuse osteopenia and mild vertebral demineralization without focal cortical destruction

Whole-Body MRI: Diffuse, homogenous or patchy bone marrow infiltration of the spine, pelvis, and proximal long bones, showing low signal on T1-weighted sequences and hyperintensity on T2/STIR, reflecting extensive lymphoplasmacytic marrow replacement
pathology_manifestations: Bone marrow trephine core biopsy & aspirate (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Intertrabecular infiltration (diffuse, interstitial, or nodular) by a clonal mixture of small B-lymphocytes, plasmacytoid lymphocytes, and mature plasma cells (lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, LPL); pathognomonic Dutcher bodies: intranuclear, Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive pseudoinclusions composed of invaginated cytoplasmic immunoglobulin (IgM); presence of cytoplasmic Russell bodies and increased background mast cells intimately admixed with the neoplastic lymphoid cells; IHC: Neoplastic B-cells are positive for CD19, CD20, CD22, and CD79a; plasma cells are CD138+ and CD38+; surface and cytoplasmic IgM monoclonal light chain restriction (predominantly kappa); negative for CD5, CD10, and CD23 (distinguishing from CLL and mantle cell lymphoma); Molecular Genetics: Pathognomonic somatic activating MYD88 L265P mutation detected in >90-95% of cases; CXCR4 mutations present in 30-40% of patients
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic lymphoplasmacytic IgM hyperviscosity neoplasm displaying striking 'sausage-link' retinal vein engorgement and cryoglobulinemic acrocyanosis, supported by diffuse marrow replacement without lytic bone lesions on MRI/CT, and Dutcher-body lymphoplasmacytic histology with MYD88 L265P.

topics.name: Actinomycosis
clinical_manifestations: Cervicofacial 'lumpy jaw': extremely hard, indurated, painless, dark-red or purplish 'wooden' swelling over the angle of the jaw or submandibular region
Multiple chronic draining cutaneous sinus tracts that erupt through the skin
Discharge containing macroscopic, gritty, yellowish-white particles known as 'sulfur granules'
Thoracic and abdominopelvic wall fistulous masses
radiological_manifestations: Head/Neck/Chest/Abdominal CT: Aggressive, infiltrative, expansile soft-tissue mass that ignores anatomical tissue planes and fascial boundaries, central areas of low-attenuation necrosis, prominent peripheral rim enhancement, adjacent bone periostitis or osteolysis (mandibular erosion)
Chest CT: Non-segmental airspace consolidation with multiple microcavities and chest wall invasion with rib periostitis
pathology_manifestations: Exudate / surgical biopsy: Characteristic 'sulfur granules' consisting of basophilic masses of tangled branching filamentous Gram-positive bacteria surrounded by an eosinophilic, radiating, club-like Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon; surrounding dense suppurative and xanthogranulomatous inflammation
topics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic 'lumpy jaw' presentation with woody induration and sulfur granule sinus drainage, matching infiltrative CT masses crossing tissue planes with adjacent bone periostitis.

topics.name: Alveolar Echinococcosis
clinical_manifestations: Hepatic Pseudomalignancy Presentation: Highly aggressive, chronically progressive, tumor-like invasive behavior resembling intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma or hepatocellular carcinoma; right upper quadrant heaviness, epigastric fullness, and hepatomegaly with a hard, irregular, rock-like liver mass

Biliary and Vascular Obstruction: Progressive obstructive jaundice, pruritus, dark urine, and pale stools from direct infiltration into the biliary confluence; secondary biliary cirrhosis and portal hypertension with ascites and bleeding esophageal varices from portal vein invasion (Budd-Chiari-like syndrome)
Distal Metastatic Dissemination: Infiltrative metastases to the lungs, brain, and regional retroperitoneal lymph nodes in advanced, untreated stages
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal CT (Diagnostic Hallmark): Large, ill-defined, infiltrative, heterogeneous hypoattenuating hepatic mass featuring an irregular, lobulated contour and a characteristic 'honeycomb' or multivesicular pattern composed of innumerable microcysts (1-10 mm); scattered amorphous, punctate, micronodular, or ring-like calcifications throughout the lesion ('geographic calcification' or 'stormy sky' appearance) with a central non-enhancing hypodense necrotic core and no peripheral vascular rim enhancement on contrast CT

Abdominal MRI: Heterogeneous mass with hypointense matrix on T1, heterogeneous T2 with innumerable hyperintense tiny microcysts ('bunch of grapes' microvesicles) embedded in a hypointense fibro-inflammatory background; direct invasion into the inferior vena cava, portal vein, and hepatic veins

PET/CT (18F-FDG): Distinct rim of intense metabolic activity surrounding the central cold necrotic cavity, corresponding to the active proliferating germinative metacestode layer at the outer advancing border (essential for monitoring response to albendazole)
pathology_manifestations: Gross Pathology of Hepatic Resection: Extremely firm, gritty, fibrous mass resembling scirrhous carcinoma, displaying a multivesicular spongy, honeycomb architecture with a central, ragged, yellowish-white necrotic liquefactive cavity

Histopathology of Cyst Wall: Microvesicles lined by a thin, folded, acellular, eosinophilic, Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive laminated layer enveloped by an outer proliferative germinal membrane; absence of a thick host fibrous pericyst (unlike Echinococcus granulosus), permitting unrestricted exogenous budding and aggressive contiguous tissue invasion into surrounding hepatic sinusoids

Surrounding Granulomatous Host Reaction: Dense necrotizing epithelioid granulomas, palisading histiocytes, foreign-body multinucleated giant cells, and extensive scirrhous collagenous fibrosis with dystrophic calcification; protoscolices are rarely observed in human tissue (sterile larvae)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Lethal parasitic pseudomalignancy of the liver characterized by the pathognomonic multivesicular honeycomb mass with 'stormy sky' calcifications on CT/MRI, metabolic rim on PET/CT, and invasively budding PAS-positive laminated microcysts on histology.

topics.name: Amebic Liver Abscess
clinical_manifestations: Hepatic Signs: Constant, dull, aching right upper quadrant (RUQ) abdominal pain, exquisite point tenderness over liver margins and lower right intercostal spaces (positive Murphy's percussion sign), and tender, firm, smooth hepatomegaly
Systemic Signs: High-spiking fevers, rigors, profuse nocturnal diaphoresis, malaise, weight loss, anorexia, and mild jaundice in large or multiple abscesses
Referred Diaphragmatic Pain: Dull aching pain referred to the right shoulder or neck from diaphragmatic irritation

Pathognomonic Pus Aspirate: Thick, odorless, reddish-brown or chocolate-colored viscous fluid traditionally described as 'anchovy paste' or chocolate sauce (consisting of liquefied necrotic hepatocytes rather than viable neutrophils)

Rupture Complications: Peritonitis from intraperitoneal rupture, empyema or hepatobronchial fistula with coughing of 'anchovy paste' sputum from transdiaphragmatic rupture, and pericardial tamponade from left-lobe abscess rupture
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound: Solitary, round or oval, well-defined hypoechoic mass located predominantly (70-80%) in the right hepatic lobe (subcapsular, posterosuperior aspect near the dome), with fine, low-level internal homogeneous echoes without wall calcification, and posterior acoustic enhancement

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Low-attenuation fluid cavity (10-30 HU) with a well-defined thick or thin enhancing capsule (2-5 mm) and a characteristic peripheral concentric hypodense surrounding zone ('halo sign' or 'double-rim sign') representing perilesional parenchymal edema and hyperemia

Abdominal MRI: Homogeneously hypointense on T1-weighted images and markedly hyperintense on T2-weighted images, surrounded by an inner rim that enhances early and an outer rim corresponding to compressed, edematous parenchyma that enhances on delayed phases
Chest Radiography: Elevation of the right hemidiaphragm with diminished excursion, reactive right-sided sympathetic pleural effusion, and right lower lobe basilar atelectasis or consolidation
pathology_manifestations: Gross Abscess Architecture: A central cavity containing amorphous reddish-brown liquefactive necrotic debris (lysed hepatocytes and liquefied tissue), surrounded by a middle zone of damaged and compressed hepatic parenchyma, and an outer zone of hyperemic, inflamed liver tissue

Trophozoite Microscopic Morphology: Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites (15-60 um) identified at the advancing margin of the abscess cavity / interface between necrotic and viable liver tissue (rarely in the central necrotic liquefied core); trophozoites possess a granular endoplasm, a clear ectoplasm, single spherical nucleus (3-5 um) with a pinpoint central karyosome and delicate, evenly distributed peripheral chromatin, and diagnostic ingested red blood cells (erythrophagocytosis)

Special Histochemical Stains: Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain stains trophozoite cytoplasm brilliant magenta-red (due to rich glycogen content) against a pale blue background; trichrome stain and Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stains delineate trophozoite nuclear and cytoplasmic detail
Real-Time PCR and Stool/Aspirate Antigen Detection: Confirms E. histolytica Gal/GalNAc lectin antigen or specific DNA, differentiating it definitively from commensal E. dispar
topics.inclusion_rationale: Most common extraintestinal manifestation of amebiasis, displaying hallmark bedside 'anchovy paste' aspirate, characteristic solitary round cystic abscess with peripheral halo on ultrasound/CT, and erythrophagocytic trophozoites on PAS histology.

topics.name: Blastomycosis
clinical_manifestations: Verrucous, crusted, violaceous, hyperkeratotic cutaneous plaques with sharply demarcated, sloping borders studded with pinpoint microabscesses (classic cutaneous blastomycosis)
Ulcerative cutaneous lesions with punched-out margins, undermined edges, and exuberant central granulation tissue
Subcutaneous fluctuating 'cold' abscesses that spontaneously rupture into chronic draining sinuses
Painful ulcerative mucosal lesions of the oral cavity, tongue, hard palate, and larynx mimicking squamous cell carcinoma
Osteoarticular swelling, warmth, and localized tenderness overlying infected long bones or septic arthritis (classically monoarticular in knees or ankles)
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT: Large mass-like consolidation with patent air bronchograms simulating bronchogenic carcinoma (predominantly in upper lobes); solitary or multiple pulmonary nodules or masses (1-4 cm) with irregular spicular margins and ground-glass halo sign; thick-walled cavitary lesions; tree-in-bud centrilobular opacities
Plain Radiography / Skeletal CT: Well-circumscribed osteolytic lesions with surrounding reactive sclerosis or periostitis involving long bone epiphyses/metaphyses, ribs, and skull

Spine CT / MRI (Blastomycotic Spondylodiscitis): Destructive vertebral body osteolysis with anterior subligamentous spread, relative early preservation of intervertebral disc spaces, and prominent paraspinal cold abscesses
pathology_manifestations: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) / Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) / Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain: Large (8-15 um, up to 30 um), spherical, thick-walled, doubly refractile yeasts demonstrating characteristic broad-based single budding (diameter of neck junction approaches daughter cell diameter)

Skin / Lung tissue biopsy: Mixed pyogranulomatous inflammatory infiltrate combining dense clusters of neutrophils (microabscesses) surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated Langhans giant cells; marked pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia of the epidermis mimicking well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic dimorphic endemic fungal infection presenting with hallmark verrucous crusted skin lesions studded with microabscesses, matching carcinoma-mimicking mass-like consolidations on chest CT and broad-based budding yeasts on histology.

topics.name: Buruli Ulcer
clinical_manifestations: Early pre-ulcerative stage: Painless, firm, mobile, non-erythematous subcutaneous nodule, well-demarcated indurated plaque, or diffuse non-pitting edema of an entire limb

Classic ulcerative stage: Large, indolent, necrotic ulcer with deeply undermined, violaceous, ragged edges and a yellowish-white necrotic slough base; remarkably painless relative to its catastrophic size (due to neurotoxic and immunosuppressive properties of mycolactone toxin)
Late healing/cicatricial stage: Severe contractures, fibrosis, joint ankylosis, and limb deformity causing permanent disability
radiological_manifestations: Soft-Tissue Ultrasound: Extensive thickening and diffuse hyperechogenicity of the subcutaneous adipose layer, necrosis of deep subcutaneous tissue planes, and absence of loculated purulent fluid or gas (distinguishing from acute pyogenic cellulitis/abscess)

Soft-Tissue Contrast MRI: Extensive high T2/STIR signal throughout the deep subcutis and deep fascia representing coalescent fat necrosis and edema, with characteristic lack of internal contrast enhancement in necrotic zones; marked peripheral soft-tissue enhancement
Plain Radiography (Late / Complicated Stage): Cortical irregularity, reactive periostitis, and contiguous osteolytic osteomyelitis of adjacent bone underlying the chronic ulcer bed
pathology_manifestations: Ulcer edge / punch biopsy (H&E stain): Massive, pathognomonic, contiguous coagulative necrosis of subcutaneous adipose tissue and deep dermis ('ghost adipocytes' or fat cell outlines devoid of nuclei), with striking absence or paucity of inflammatory cellular infiltration in necrotic areas (direct consequence of the cytotoxic, lipid-soluble polyketide toxin mycolactone)
Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) acid-fast stain: Abundant, massive extracellular clusters and clumps of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) located predominantly within the deep necrotic subcutaneous fat layers
topics.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive tropical mycobacterial disease presenting with giant, painless ulcers with deeply undermined violaceous borders, deep subcutaneous fat necrosis on ultrasound/MRI, and pathognomonic ghost-cell fat necrosis with extracellular AFB clumps on histology.

topics.name: Cat Scratch Disease
clinical_manifestations: Primary inoculation lesion: Solitary or small cluster of non-tender, erythematous, non-pruritic papules or pustules at the scratch/bite site, appearing 1-2 weeks after feline contact

Massive regional lymphadenopathy: Unilateral, dramatic enlargement of draining lymph nodes (axillary, epitrochlear, cervical, or inguinal); nodes are firm, warm, tender, often with overlying erythema, and become fluctuant/suppurative in 10-15% of cases
Parinaud oculoglandular syndrome: Unilateral granulomatous conjunctival nodule/folliculitis accompanied by dramatic, tender ipsilateral preauricular lymphadenopathy
Neuroretinitis: Sudden painless visual loss with optic disc swelling and a pathognomonic 'macular star' pattern of hard exudates radiating from the fovea
radiological_manifestations: Ultrasound / Contrast-Enhanced CT of Lymph Nodes: Markedly enlarged, conglomerate, hypervascular lymph nodes with central hypoechoic/hypodense areas of necrosis and microabscess formation, accompanied by prominent surrounding perinodal soft-tissue edema and inflammatory fat stranding

Abdominal CT / Ultrasound (Systemic / Hepatosplenic CSD): Multiple discrete, small (3-15 mm), round, well-demarcated, hypodense/hypoechoic microabscesses or granulomas distributed throughout the splenic parenchyma ('cat scratch spleen') and liver, often demonstrating peripheral rim enhancement

Fundus Photography / Fluorescein Angiography: Optic disc edema with leakage on angiography and classic radial lipid deposition forming a complete or incomplete star figure in the Henle fiber layer around the macula
pathology_manifestations: Lymph node excision / core biopsy (H&E stain): Characteristic triphasic histological progression: (1) follicular lymphoid hyperplasia with arteriolar proliferation, evolving to (2) multiple discrete epithelioid granulomas, culminating in (3) classic irregular, stellate necrotizing granulomas with central suppurative neutrophilic microabscesses surrounded by a palisade of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated Langhans giant cells

Warthin-Starry silver stain: Pleomorphic, small, dark brown-to-black, curved, rod-shaped bacilli (Bartonella henselae) arranged in dense clumps or clusters within areas of necrosis, along vessel walls, and within macrophage cytoplasm
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic zoonotic infection with hallmark inoculation papule, massive suppurative regional lymphadenopathy, Parinaud oculoglandular syndrome, splenic microabscesses on CT, and classic stellate necrotizing granulomas on Warthin-Starry stain.

topics.name: Chagas Disease (American Trypanosomiasis)
clinical_manifestations: Romaña Sign (Acute Phase Pathognomonic Sign): Unilateral, painless, bipalpebral edema and periocular swelling accompanied by conjunctivitis, dacryoadenitis, and ipsilateral preauricular lymphadenopathy, occurring when insect feces contaminate the ocular mucosa
Chagoma: Indurated, erythematous, non-tender inflammatory nodule or furunculoid plaque at the cutaneous site of vector inoculation
Chronic Dilated Cardiomyopathy: Severe heart failure, syncope, embolic strokes, and lethal ventricular arrhythmias (sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, complete AV block)
Chagasic Megaesophagus: Progressive dysphagia to both solids and liquids, regurgitation of undigested food, odynophagia, nocturnal coughing, and severe wasting

Chagasic Megacolon: Severe, chronic, intractable constipation (bowel movements spaced days to weeks apart), severe abdominal distension, palpable fecalomas, and acute sigmoid volvulus with bowel ischemia
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic Echocardiography & Cardiac MRI: Pathognomonic Apical Left Ventricular Aneurysm (thin-walled, dyskinetic or akinetic outpouching of the LV apex with preserved basal contractility, frequently containing a mural thrombus); biventricular dilation with severe systolic dysfunction; late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on MRI displaying transmural or midwall myocardial fibrosis

Barium Swallow (Esophagography): Marked, tortuous dilation of the entire thoracic esophagus with aperistalsis, retained food residue, and smooth, symmetric conical tapering at the gastroesophageal junction ('bird's-beak' or 'pencil-tip' appearance) mimicking idiopathic achalasia

Barium Enema / Abdominal CT: Massive, elongated dilation of the rectum and sigmoid colon (dolichomegacolon) with retention of huge calcified or rock-like fecal masses (fecalomas) and inverted 'coffee-bean' sign in sigmoid volvulus
pathology_manifestations: Acute Phase Peripheral Blood Wet Mount / Giemsa Smear: Motile, extracellular, slender, flagellated trypomastigotes measuring 20 um in length, featuring a characteristic C-shape or S-shape, a central round nucleus, an undulating membrane, a free anterior flagellum, and a large, subterminal, dark-staining posterior kinetoplast

Myocardial Histopathology (Endomyocardial Biopsy / Autopsy): Intense lymphohistiocytic myocarditis with extensive myocyte necrosis and interstitial fibrosis; hallmark intracellular amastigote pseudocysts (nests of round-to-oval amastigotes, 2-4 um in diameter, possessing a nucleus and rod-like kinetoplast tightly packed within ruptured or swollen cardiac myocytes)

Gastrointestinal Pathology: Marked denervation, severe reduction or complete destruction and fibrous loss of the myenteric (Auerbach's) and submucosal (Meissner's) neural plexuses, associated with chronic lymphocytic ganglionitis and smooth muscle hypertrophy
topics.inclusion_rationale: Visual prototype of American vector-borne parasitic disease featuring the pathognomonic Romaña sign on clinical exam, the classic apical LV aneurysm on echocardiography/MRI, 'bird's beak' megaesophagus on barium studies, and myocardial amastigote nests.

topics.name: Chromoblastomycosis
clinical_manifestations: Polymorphic, chronic, slowly progressive cutaneous lesions typically on lower extremities: Initial solitary pink papule or scaly macule progressing to nodular, verrucous, hyperkeratotic, papillomatous, or cauliflower-like vegetative plaques
Pathognomonic bedside finding: 'Black dots' (small, dark, cayenne-pepper-like specks on the surface of crusted verrucous plaques, representing transepidermal elimination of pigmented fungal elements)
Cicatricial form: Atrophic, shiny, sclerotic scarring plaques with centrifugal spread and creeping borders
Severe secondary lymphedema ('elephantiasis nostras') and chronic joint ankylosis/deformity of the affected extremity
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography / Soft-Tissue CT: Marked, irregular, nodular thickening and hypertrophy of the skin and subcutaneous soft tissues without primary osteolytic bony destruction; in advanced chronic cases with severe secondary lymphedema, secondary periostitis, cortical thickening, and pressure remodeling of adjacent long bones

Soft-Tissue MRI: Extensive subcutaneous nodular thickening with intermediate-to-low signal on T1-weighted images, heterogeneous hyperintensity on T2-weighted/STIR images, and intense patchy or nodular enhancement with deep fascial preservation
pathology_manifestations: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation / Direct biopsy histology: Pathognomonic 'muriform cells' (also called 'sclerotic cells', 'sclerotic bodies', 'Medlar bodies', or 'copper pennies'): thick-walled, single or clustered, chestnut-brown/golden-brown pigmented fungal structures (5-12 um in diameter) that divide by internal septation along longitudinal and transverse planes (resembling hot cross buns), without budding

Tissue architecture: Marked pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia of the epidermis (frequently mistaken for squamous cell carcinoma) with prominent transepidermal elimination of fungal sclerotic bodies; dense mixed dermal suppurative granulomas containing neutrophil microabscesses, epithelioid histiocytes, and multinucleated foreign body giant cells
topics.inclusion_rationale: Visual archetype of dematiaceous subcutaneous mycosis featuring pathognomonic cauliflower-like verrucous plaques with surface 'black dots', soft tissue elephantiasic thickening, and diagnostic golden-brown 'copper penny' Medlar bodies on pathology.

topics.name: Coccidioidomycosis
clinical_manifestations: Classic reactive immune skin manifestations: Erythema nodosum (tender, warm, erythematous, non-ulcerating subcutaneous nodules predominantly on pretibial surfaces) and Erythema multiforme (targetoid concentric papules and plaques on palms, soles, and extremities)
'Desert rheumatism': Classic triad of high fever, erythema nodosum, and severe polyarthralgias with periarticular soft tissue swelling (knees, ankles)
Disseminated cutaneous lesions: Papules, verrucous crusted plaques, pustules, subcutaneous cold abscesses, and ulcerated granulomas (predilection for the nasolabial fold and face)
Chronic coccidioidal meningitis: Basilar meningismus, cranial neuropathies, communicating hydrocephalus, and papilledema
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / High-Resolution CT: Pathognomonic thin-walled, sharply circumscribed, gas-filled cavitary lesions ('grape-skin' cavities, coccidioidal cavity) without surrounding consolidation; solitary or multiple discrete pulmonary nodules ('coccidioidoma'); dense lobar or segmental alveolar consolidation; diffuse micronodular miliary pattern; prominent ipsilateral hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy

Plain Radiography / CT / MRI of Bone: Punched-out, well-defined osteolytic lesions without surrounding reactive sclerosis involving the skull, spine, pelvis, and metaphyses of long bones; vertebral collapse with destruction of adjacent intervertebral discs and large paraspinal abscesses

Brain MRI (Coccidioidal Meningitis): Intense, thick, nodular contrast enhancement of the basal cisterns, sylvian fissures, and leptomeninges, accompanied by secondary acute vasculitic cerebral infarcts and progressive hydrocephalus
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology (H&E, GMS, PAS stains): Enormous, round, thick-walled spherules (20-100 um or larger, double-refractile wall) containing hundreds of small, round, non-budding endospores (2-5 um diameter)

Host tissue response: Rupture of spherules releases endospores, triggering intense suppurative neutrophilic microabscesses; intact spherules incite prominent granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans multinucleated giant cells, and peripheral fibrosis
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential Southwestern endemic mycosis presenting with classic erythema nodosum/multiforme ('desert rheumatism') and pathognomonic thin-walled pulmonary cavities on chest CT, confirmed by massive endospore-filled spherules on pathology.

topics.name: Cutaneous Anthrax
clinical_manifestations: Evolution from pruritic papule to hemorrhagic vesicle: Incubation of 1-7 days following contact with contaminated animal hides, wool, hair, or soil, beginning as a painless, pruritic macule or papule (often mistaken for an insect bite), which within 24-48 hours enlarges and develops a central ring of tiny secondary satellite hemorrhagic vesicles filled with dark, serosanguinous fluid

Pathognomonic depressed black necrotic eschar: Rupture and collapse of the central vesicle creating a painless, non-tender, sunken, central crater that hardens into a pathognomonic jet-black, thick, dry, coal-like necrotic eschar (Greek: 'anthrax' = coal) firmly adherent to the ulcer bed, typically measuring 1 to 3 cm in diameter

Non-pitting gelatinous surrounding edema: Disproportionately massive, non-pitting, gelatinous edema radiating widely from the black eschar across the entire affected limb, neck, or face, mediated by bacterial edema toxin (adenylate cyclase activity elevating intracellular cAMP)

Malignant edema and airway compromise (head and neck lesions): When involving the face, eyelid, or neck, severe malignant edema causes dramatic facial swelling, eyelid closure (orbital preseptal cellulitis), and descending submandibular/pharyngeal compression leading to acute upper airway compromise

Regional lymphadenopathy and systemic toxemia: Painful regional lymphadenitis (satellite buboes); systemic dissemination manifests with high fever, chills, tachycardia, diaphoresis, delirium, and progression to toxic shock
radiological_manifestations: Soft Tissue Ultrasound and Contrast-Enhanced CT (Affected Site): Demonstrates marked, diffuse, extensive subcutaneous gelatinous edema without frank purulent fluid collection or mature abscess formation (characteristic lack of frank pus despite extensive necrosis); regional reactive lymphadenomegaly

Chest Radiography and Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT (Systemic Dissemination / Inhalational or Bacteremic Spread): Pathognomonic symmetric, marked mediastinal widening (due to hemorrhagic mediastinal lymphadenitis and peribronchial edema), extensive hemorrhagic pleural effusions with dense dependent consolidation, perihilar cuffing, and absence of typical pulmonary parenchymal cavitations

Brain CT / MRI (in Anthrax Meningoencephalitis): Systemic hematogenous seeding produces hemorrhagic leptomeningitis ('cardinal's cap' sign on gross exam), appearing on non-contrast CT as striking hyperdense subarachnoid hemorrhage and on MRI as diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement with microhemorrhages and cerebral edema
pathology_manifestations: Cutaneous Histopathology: Marked epidermal and dermal coagulative necrosis with extensive ulceration; severe papillary and reticular dermal edema with vascular congestion; pathognomonic absence of a dense neutrophilic infiltration (leukocytolysis and edema predominate due to lethal toxin and edema toxin activity); abundant, large, blunt-ended, square-ended, boxcar-shaped Gram-positive bacilli arranged in long chains within the dermal vessels and interstitial fluid

Microbiological and Molecular Confirmation: Gram stain demonstrating large, encapsulated Gram-positive rods with central/subterminal spores (non-motile, non-hemolytic on sheep blood agar, forming 'Medusa-head' colonies with tenacity / beaten egg-white consistency); positive polychrome methylene blue stain (M'Fadyean reaction) highlighting the poly-D-glutamic acid capsule; definitive PCR detecting virulence plasmids pXO1 (encoding protective antigen, lethal factor, and edema factor) and pXO2 (encoding poly-D-glutamic acid capsule)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic zoonotic and biothreat infection featuring the unforgettable photographic coal-black necrotic eschar enveloped in massive gelatinous non-pitting edema, characteristic boxcar Gram-positive bacilli devoid of neutrophilic pus, and mediastinal widening on imaging.

topics.name: Cystic Echinococcosis
clinical_manifestations: Palpable, firm, smooth, non-tender abdominal mass in the right upper quadrant
Hepatomegaly, obstructive jaundice, and visible abdominal distension
Acute anaphylactic shock, intense pruritus, and widespread urticaria triggered by spontaneous or traumatic cyst rupture
Expectoration of salty hydatid fluid, hooklets, and membrane fragments ('hydatidoptysis') in lung cyst rupture
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Ultrasound (WHO-IWGE Classification CE1-CE5): Pathognomonic multilocular hydatid cysts with internal daughter cysts giving a 'spoke-wheel' or 'honeycomb' appearance; detached germinative endocyst membrane floating within fluid ('water lily sign'); heavy, curvilinear peripheral wall calcification (CE5 inactive stage)
Abdominal and Chest CT: Well-defined, spherical, water-density fluid collections with multiple daughter cysts, detached floating endocyst membranes, wall calcification
pathology_manifestations: Gross and microscopic cyst examination: Three-layered cyst wall comprising an outer host fibrous capsule (pericyst), middle acellular laminated chitinous membrane (ectocyst), and inner cellular germinal layer (endocyst); presence of broad capsules containing invaginated protoscolices with characteristic double-hooklet rings
topics.inclusion_rationale: Vivid parasitic disease presenting with palpable abdominal masses and anaphylactic urticaria, verified by pathognomonic ultrasound and CT imaging: 'water lily sign', daughter cysts, and calcified rims.

topics.name: Disseminated Cryptococcosis and Cryptococcal Meningitis
clinical_manifestations: Central Nervous System: Subacute headache, meningismus, nausea, vomiting, lethargy, confusion, altered mental status, and cranial nerve palsies (VI and VII); dramatically elevated opening pressure on lumbar puncture (>250-300 mm H2O) causing papilledema and optic atrophy

Hallmark Cutaneous Lesions (Second most common site after CNS in disseminated disease, affecting 10-15%): Characteristic umbilicated, translucent papules and nodules mimicking molluscum contagiosum, predominantly on the head and neck; ulcerated plaques, cellulitis-like phlegmons, and subcutaneous cold abscesses
Pulmonary Presentation: Dry cough, dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, and low-grade fevers in immunocompromised hosts (advanced HIV/AIDS with CD4 < 100/uL, solid organ transplant recipients)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Pathognomonic Imaging Signs): 'Gelatinous Pseudocysts' or 'Soap Bubble' Lesions (clustered, round or oval cystic lesions, 1-5 mm, in the basal ganglia, thalami, and midbrain along the perivascular Virchow-Robin spaces filled with mucoid capsular polysaccharide, hyperintense on T2/FLAIR and hypointense on T1 with minimal or no rim enhancement); 'Cryptococcomas' (parenchymal granulomatous masses with peripheral ring enhancement and surrounding vasogenic edema); and leptomeningeal enhancement with communicating hydrocephalus

High-Resolution Chest CT: Well-defined solitary or multiple non-calcified subpleural pulmonary nodules or masses (frequently cavitating in non-HIV hosts), segmental consolidations, and ground-glass halos
pathology_manifestations: Direct CSF Examination: India Ink Preparation demonstrates round-to-oval, encapsulated yeast cells (4-10 um) with narrow-based budding surrounded by a massive, clear, refractile, halo-like mucopolysaccharide capsule that completely excludes carbon particles

Histopathology of Tissue Biopsies (Skin, Lung, Brain): Abundant extracellular yeasts filling dilated Virchow-Robin spaces ('soap-bubble' appearance) with minimal inflammatory infiltrate in immunocompromised patients, or granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells in immunocompetent hosts

Pathognomonic Special Stains: Mayer's Mucicarmine stains the thick acidic mucopolysaccharide capsule brilliant rose-red/carmine-pink (pathognomonic differentiator from Histoplasma, Blastomyces, and Candida); Fontana-Masson stains melanin in the fungal cell wall dark brown-black; GMS and PAS stain the fungal cell wall intensely
topics.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening opportunistic mycosis defined by bedside molluscum-like umbilicated skin lesions, the pathognomonic 'soap-bubble' gelatinous pseudocysts on brain MRI, and India ink halo / mucicarmine-positive encapsulated yeasts on histology.

topics.name: Dracunculiasis (Guinea Worm Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Blister and Worm Emergence: Burning, painful blister that erupts typically on the lower extremity (foot, ankle, lower leg in >90% of cases) approximately one year after drinking copepod-contaminated water; upon immersion in cool water, the blister ruptures to form a painful, shallow, non-healing ulcer from which the milky-white, cord-like anterior end of a live adult female nematode (Dracunculus medinensis, up to 1 meter in length) visibly protrudes

Systemic Pre-Emergence Symptoms: Intense generalized urticaria, pruritus, severe erythema, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and syncope triggered by release of toxic nematode metabolic by-products during blister formation

Secondary Complications: Disabling secondary polymicrobial bacterial cellulitis, deep subcutaneous abscesses, tetanus, and permanent joint contractures or ankylosis if the emerging worm ruptures within deep fascial compartments
radiological_manifestations: Soft Tissue Plain Radiography: Pathognomonic appearance of dead, calcified adult worms: long, undulating, linear, curvilinear, serpentine, or coiled radio-opaque calcifications running parallel to muscle planes and fascial boundaries in the lower extremity; broken dead worms appear as segmented, beaded, or fragmented calcified tracks ('string-of-beads' calcification)

Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Non-invasive detection of uncalcified migrating female worm in subcutaneous tissues: tubular, non-vascular, elongated hyperechoic structure with a distinct double-line contour (parallel echogenic margins corresponding to the nematode cuticle) surrounded by a thin anechoic fluid halo within subcutaneous fascia
pathology_manifestations: Microscopic Fluid Examination: Diagnostic fluid discharged from the protruding worm's anterior uterine prolapse contains swarms of tens of thousands of active, motile, free-swimming rhabditiform larvae (measuring 500-700 um in length by 15-25 um in width) with rounded anterior ends and long, slender, whip-like pointed tails

Histopathology of Biopsied Ulcer / Subcutaneous Granuloma: Cross-sections of the adult gravid female worm reveal a thick, smooth, multi-layered cuticular wall, well-developed somatic musculature, and a massive paired uterus filled with countless coiled microfilariae; surrounded by dense eosinophilic necrosis, foreign-body granulomas, and extensive dystrophic calcification along dead worm segments
topics.inclusion_rationale: Historic eradication-target parasite with direct bedside photographic diagnosis of the emerging adult guinea worm from a lower extremity ulcer, pathognomonic serpentine/string-of-beads soft-tissue calcifications on X-ray, and larval microscopy.

topics.name: Fascioliasis (Hepatic Distomiasis / Sheep Liver Fluke)
clinical_manifestations: Acute Hepatic Phase (Larval Migration, 6-12 weeks post-ingestion of contaminated watercress): High-spiking undulating fever, acute severe right upper quadrant (RUQ) abdominal pain, hepatomegaly, striking allergic manifestations (generalized urticaria, pruritus, dermatographia, facial angioedema), and extreme, profound peripheral blood eosinophilia (>50-80% of total leukocytes)
Chronic Biliary Phase (Adult Flukes in Bile Ducts): Biliary colic, intermittent obstructive jaundice, ascending cholangitis, cholecystitis, and secondary sclerosing cholangitis

Halzoun / Marrara Syndrome: Acute pharyngeal and laryngeal edema with suffocating dyspnea and dysphagia caused by adult flukes attaching to the posterior pharyngeal mucosa after eating raw infected sheep/goat liver
radiological_manifestations: Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT (Pathognomonic Imaging Sign): Pathognomonic 'Burrow Tracks' or 'Tunnel Sign' (multiple branching, tortuous, serpentine, linear or cylindrical subcapsular hypodense tracts, 2-5 mm in diameter, tracking from the liver capsule toward the porta hepatis, representing necrosis and hemorrhage left behind by juvenile flukes burrowing through hepatic parenchyma); multiple small clustered microabscesses that cluster along portal tracts and fluctuate in position over serial CT scans ('wandering lesions')

Abdominal Ultrasound: Linear, elongated, non-shadowing, hyperechoic or leaf-like structures (20-30 mm in length) inside dilated intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts or gallbladder, exhibiting slow, subtle peristaltic undulating movement
Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) / MRCP: Irregular biliary ductal dilation with multiple mobile, radiolucent, flat, leaf-shaped filling defects without acoustic shadowing
pathology_manifestations: Stool and Duodenal Aspirate Microscopy: Detection of large, ellipsoidal, golden-yellow, operculated eggs measuring 130-150 um by 60-90 um, filled with unsegmented yolk cells, possessing an indistinct, small operculum at one pole

Histopathology of Liver Core Biopsy: Necrotizing eosinophilic tracts ('Charcot's tunnels') traversing the liver parenchyma, containing abundant necrotic debris, degenerate hepatocytes, intense eosinophilic infiltration with Charcot-Leyden crystals, and surrounding granulomatous rim with multinucleated giant cells and collagen deposition

Morphology of Adult Fluke: Large, flat, leaf-shaped trematode (Fasciola hepatica, 20-30 mm long by 13 mm wide) possessing a distinct conical anterior projection ('head cone') and branched digestive caeca
topics.inclusion_rationale: Visual hepatic trematode infection defined by acute allergic urticaria with profound eosinophilia, pathognomonic branching 'burrow tracks' on liver CT, real-time ultrasound detection of undulating flukes in bile ducts, and operculated eggs on microscopy.

topics.name: Histoplasmosis
clinical_manifestations: Painful, persistent mucosal ulcers of the hard and soft palate, tongue, buccal mucosa, and nasal septum with raised, indurated, rolled borders mimicking oral squamous cell carcinoma
Progressive disseminated histoplasmosis (PDH): Widespread polymorphic cutaneous lesions including umbilicated papules with necrotic centers (molluscum-like), pustules, and purpuric macules
Marked hepatosplenomegaly, generalized lymphadenopathy, and high spiking fevers
Signs of acute adrenal insufficiency (Addisonian crisis) with hyperpigmentation, hypotension, and profound asthenia due to bilateral adrenal destruction
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography / CT: Innumerable, uniform 1-3 mm micronodules symmetrically distributed throughout both lungs (classic miliary histoplasmosis); dense focal or patchy lobar consolidations with prominent hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy; multiple calcified pulmonary granulomas and calcified lymph nodes

Chest CT / MRI (Fibrosing Mediastinitis): Infiltrative, calcified, invasive soft-tissue mass in the middle/posterior mediastinum causing extrinsic compression, narrowing, or complete occlusion of the superior vena cava (SVC syndrome), pulmonary veins, or main pulmonary arteries

Abdominal CT / US: Symmetric, marked, bilateral adrenal gland enlargement with preservation of adrenal contour, central low-attenuation necrosis, and peripheral rim enhancement; scattered 'buckshot' parenchymal calcifications within spleen and liver
pathology_manifestations: GMS / PAS / Giemsa stain of bone marrow, liver, adrenal, or mucosal ulcer biopsy: Abundant small (2-4 um), uniform, round-to-oval yeasts with narrow-based budding, clustered densely inside the cytoplasm of histiocytes and macrophages (often creating an artifactual clear halo around each yeast simulating a capsule)

Tissue architecture: Range from discrete necrotizing (caseating) and non-caseating epithelioid granulomas with multinucleated giant cells in immunocompetent hosts, to sheet-like, unorganized macrophage infiltration packed with yeasts without granuloma formation in severe immunocompromise (AIDS)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic Ohio/Mississippi river valley endemic mycosis marked by painful oropharyngeal ulcers, bilateral necrotic adrenal enlargement causing adrenal failure on CT, miliary lung nodules, and intracellular narrow-based yeasts on silver stain.

topics.name: Infective Endocarditis
clinical_manifestations: Osler nodes: painful, tender, erythematous, raised nodules on the pads of fingers and toes (immunologic phenomenon)
Janeway lesions: painless, non-tender, erythematous or hemorrhagic macules on palms and soles (septic embolic phenomenon)
Splinter hemorrhages: linear dark red streaks beneath nail beds running longitudinally
Roth spots: retinal hemorrhages with pale or white centers on fundoscopic examination
Conjunctival petechiae and pallor
radiological_manifestations: Transthoracic / Transesophageal Echocardiography (TTE/TEE): Pathognomonic oscillating intracardiac valvular vegetations, perivalvular abscesses (aortic root), leaflet perforation, chordae tendineae rupture, new prosthetic valve dehiscence
Brain MRI: Multifocal septic embolic cerebral infarcts, microbleeds, cerebral mycotic aneurysms, meningitis
Abdominal / Chest CT: Wedge-shaped splenic and renal infarctions, septic pulmonary emboli with cavitation
pathology_manifestations: Explanted valve histology: Amorphous mass of dense fibrin, platelets, and bacterial colonies (Gram-positive cocci) invading and destroying the valve leaflet architecture, with surrounding acute and chronic neutrophilic inflammatory infiltrate
topics.inclusion_rationale: Textbook combination of physical exam peripheral stigmata (Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, splinter hemorrhages, Roth spots) and diagnostic echocardiographic vegetations and septic embolic imaging.

topics.name: Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis and Aspergilloma
clinical_manifestations: Acute Angioinvasive Aspergillosis (Neutropenic, Leukemia, or Transplant Patients): Refractory high fevers despite broad-spectrum antibacterial coverage, sharp pleuritic chest pain, tachypnea, dry cough, and acute hemoptysis

Chronic Cavitary Pulmonary Aspergillosis / Aspergilloma: Recurrent, often massive and life-threatening hemoptysis (from erosion into bronchial arterioles), chronic productive cough, low-grade fevers, night sweats, and severe progressive cachexia

Disseminated Extrapulmonary Manifestations: Necrotic cutaneous papules evolving into ulcerated plaques with central black necrotic eschar; epistaxis and necrotic black palatal/turbinate eschars in sinonasal extension
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Chest CT (HRCT) - Angioinvasive Stage: Pathognomonic 'CT Halo Sign' (macronodule >1 cm or mass surrounded by a perimeter of ground-glass attenuation corresponding to alveolar hemorrhage secondary to fungal angioinvasion and infarction); 'Hypoattenuating Center Sign' on contrast CT; and 'Vessel Cutoff Sign' on CT angiography

HRCT - Cavitation / Neutrophil Recovery Stage: Pathognomonic 'Air Crescent Sign' (crescent-shaped collection of gas appearing within or along the margin of a necrotic pulmonary nodule as the infarcted lung sequestrum separates from viable parenchyma)

Aspergilloma (Simple Fungus Ball): Well-defined pre-existing cavity containing a mobile, gravity-dependent, rounded, heterogeneously attenuating mass ('Monod Sign') that shifts position between supine and prone CT acquisitions, separated from the cavity wall by a crescent of air
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology of Lung Biopsy: Extensive coagulative ischemic necrosis, hemorrhagic infarction, and prominent vascular angioinvasion; fungal hyphae actively penetrating through elastica and endothelial walls of pulmonary arteries and arterioles, inducing intravascular thrombosis and localized tissue death

Fungal Hyphal Morphology: Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) and Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stains reveal uniform, slender, parallel-walled, septate hyphae (3-6 um in diameter) that branch characteristically at acute, progressive 45-degree dichotomous angles (V-shaped branching)

Aspergilloma Histopathology: Intertwined, dense, felt-like matted mass of degenerative fungal hyphae, conidiophores with biseriate sterigmata (in aerobic cavities), fibrin, degenerating erythrocytes, and cellular debris without tissue invasion of the surrounding thick fibrous cavity wall
topics.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening opportunistic mycosis defined by pathognomonic imaging signs on chest CT ('CT halo sign', 'air crescent sign', and mobile 'Monod sign' for aspergilloma), alongside hallmark acute-angle 45-degree branching septate hyphae with angioinvasion on histology.

topics.name: Leprosy
clinical_manifestations: Hypopigmented or erythematous anesthetic skin macules and plaques with loss of pain, temperature, and touch sensation
Leonine facies: diffuse facial skin thickening, infiltrated nodules, deep furrowing, and complete loss of eyebrows and eyelashes (madarosis)
Saddle nose deformity from destruction of nasal cartilage
Palpable, thickened, tender peripheral nerves (greater auricular, ulnar at elbow, common peroneal at fibular neck)
Neuropathic trophic claw hand, wrist drop, foot drop, and perforating plantar ulcers
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Nerve Ultrasound / MRI: Marked fusiform enlargement and thickening of peripheral nerves, loss of normal fascicular architecture, intraneural power Doppler hyperemia during lepra reactions

Hand and Foot Radiographs: Severe neurotrophic acro-osteolysis, concentric bone resorption leading to 'licked candy stick' or 'penciling' appearance of phalanges and metatarsals, neuropathic joint destruction (Charcot foot)
pathology_manifestations: Skin and nerve biopsy: In lepromatous leprosy: dermis packed with sheets of foamy, lipid-laden macrophages (Virchow cells / lepra cells) loaded with clumps and globi of acid-fast bacilli highlighted by Fite-Faraco stain; in tuberculoid leprosy: well-defined epithelioid granulomas invading dermal nerves
topics.inclusion_rationale: Legendary visual disease with unmistakable leonine facies, madarosis, and anesthetic skin plaques, coupled with high-resolution nerve ultrasound thickening and 'licked candy stick' acro-osteolysis on plain X-rays.

topics.name: Loiasis (Loa Loa Filariasis)
clinical_manifestations: Calabar Swellings (Fugitive Swellings): Pathognomonic transient, localized, non-pitting, migratory angioedema (typically 5-20 cm in diameter) occurring predominantly on extremities (wrist, dorsal hand, forearm, ankle), warm and pruritic, occasionally mildly painful, resolving spontaneously over 3 to 7 days before recurring elsewhere

Subconjunctival Worm Migration (Eyeworm): Spectacular, unmistakable bedside finding of an adult female or male worm (Loa loa, 30-70 mm in length) actively crawling across the bulbar subconjunctiva of the eye, producing foreign body sensation, extreme pruritus, lacrimation, photophobia, and periocular edema
Generalized pruritus, urticaria, maculopapular exanthem, fatigue, and myalgias

Post-treatment Encephalopathy: Acute severe neurological deterioration, coma, and retinal microhemorrhages triggered by mass microfilarial death following diethylcarbamazine (DEC) or ivermectin therapy in individuals with high microfilarial loads (>30,000 mf/mL)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Ocular and Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: Real-time dynamic visualization of a motile, coiled or serpentine, hyperechoic tubular structure measuring ~0.5 mm in diameter actively undulating within the subconjunctival space or subcutaneous tissue layers ('filarial dance sign')
Soft Tissue Radiographs: Fine, curvilinear, thread-like or coiled radio-opaque calcifications corresponding to dead, calcified adult worms in subcutaneous tissues of hands, wrists, or feet

Brain MRI (in Loa loa post-treatment encephalopathy): Multiple small punctate hyperintensities on T2/FLAIR throughout the deep cerebral white matter and basal ganglia, diffuse vasogenic cerebral edema, and microhemorrhages on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) from microvascular obstruction by dying microfilariae
pathology_manifestations: Peripheral Blood Smear Examination: Giemsa or hematoxylin-stained thick blood smear collected during peak diurnal hours (10:00 to 14:00, reflecting diurnal microfilarial periodicity); microfilariae measure 250-300 um by 6-8 um, possess a distinct hyaline sheath, and display somatic nuclei that extend in a continuous column to the absolute, rounded tip of the tail

Adult Worm Surgical Pathology: Intact cylindrical filarial nematode extracted from conjunctiva or skin; cuticle is distinctive, possessing numerous small, rounded, dome-shaped bosses or tubercles scattered over the surface; males measure 30-34 mm with unequal spicules, females measure 50-70 mm with vulva located anteriorly
Tissue Histology: Marked perivascular tissue infiltration with eosinophils, forming eosinophilic granulomas and Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon around degenerating worms in subcutaneous tissues
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic neglected filariasis with unforgettable bedside visual findings: the migrating subconjunctival 'eyeworm' and transient Calabar swellings, real-time ultrasound detection of motile worms, and diurnal sheathed microfilariae on blood smear.

topics.name: Ludwig's Angina
synonyms: phlegmon of the floor of the mouth
sublingual and submandibular space gangrenous cellulitis
