Renal Ultrasound: Solitary or multifocal ill-defined, hypoechoic or heterogeneous parenchymal masses with distortion of the central renal sinus complex, accompanied by hydroureteronephrosis
Fluoroscopic Retrograde / Antegrade Ureteropyelography: Irregular filling defects, strictures, and luminal nodularity in the distal ureters mimicking multifocal urothelial carcinoma
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Dense, confluent, chronic histiocytic infiltrate composed of sheets of large, polygonal macrophages with abundant, eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm known as von Hansemann cells

Pathognomonic Pathologic Structure: Michaelis-Gutmann bodies: round to oval, targetoid, basophilic, concentrically laminated, calcified intracytoplasmic (or extracellular) inclusion bodies; they represent defective phagolysosomes containing incompletely digested, calcified bacterial fragments (Escherichia coli)

Special Stains: Michaelis-Gutmann bodies are strongly positive for von Kossa stain (black, demonstrating calcium phosphate), Prussian blue stain (bright blue, demonstrating ferric iron), and Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) with diastase resistance; CD68 positive, confirming histiocytic lineage
topics.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive chronic granulomatous infection featuring cystoscopic yellowish-brown mucosal plaques with hyperemic halos, CT renal pseudotumors with hydronephrosis, and pathognomonic basophilic targetoid Michaelis-Gutmann bodies within von Hansemann histiocytes on pathology.

topics.name: Nail-Patella Syndrome
clinical_manifestations:
Tetrad of classic physical examination dysmorphic findings:
1) Dystrophic fingernails (pathognomonic bedside hallmark): Bilateral, symmetrical nail hypoplasia, aplasia, longitudinal ridging, spooning (koilonychia), triangular lunulae (pathognomonic sign where lunulae point distally like an arrowhead), most severe on the thumbs and progressively milder towards the fifth digit
2) Absent, hypoplastic, or dislocated patellae: easily palpated small, rudimentary, or absent kneecaps, associated with habitual recurrent patellar dislocations, genu valgum, and gait disturbances
3) Elbow dysplasias: prominent limitation of full extension, pronation, and supination of the forearms, with visible antecubital pterygia (webbing) and prominence of the radial head
4) Palpable posterior iliac horns: symmetric, firm, bony prominences palpated along the posterolateral surface of the iliac crests
Lester's sign: cloverleaf-shaped or irregular dark hyperpigmentation of the inner pupillary margin of the iris on slit-lamp ophthalmic examination

Renal manifestations: early asymptomatic microscopic hematuria and persistent, progressive non-nephrotic or nephrotic proteinuria developing in childhood or adolescence, progressing to end-stage kidney disease in 30-50%
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic Radiography (Pathognomonic Skeletal Hallmark): Pathognomonic bilateral, symmetrical, horn-like bony spurs or exostoses projecting posterolaterally from the posterior aspect of the iliac bones, known as iliac horns or Fong's sign (present in >80% of patients and pathognomonic for the syndrome)
Knee Radiography / MRI: Hypoplastic, small, asymmetrical, or completely absent patellae; lateral displacement/subluxation of the patella; hypoplastic lateral femoral condyle
Elbow Radiography: Hypoplasia of the capitellum, asymmetric enlargement of the medial epicondyle, and posterolateral subluxation or dislocation of the radial head
Renal Ultrasound: Non-specific findings of progressive glomerulopathy: bilateral normal-to-small kidneys with increased cortical echogenicity and loss of corticomedullary differentiation
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy Electron Microscopy (Diagnostic Gold Standard & Pathognomonic Hallmark): Pathognomonic 'moth-eaten' appearance of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) with diffuse irregular lucent areas throughout the lamina densa, containing embedded bundles of banded collagen fibrils showing characteristic 64 nm periodic striations (Type III collagen fibers, which are normally entirely absent from the glomerular basement membrane); accompanied by podocyte foot process effacement
Light Microscopy: Variable, non-specific changes ranging from mild mesangial matrix expansion to progressive focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and tubular atrophy

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous pathogenic loss-of-function mutations in the *LMX1B* gene on chromosome 9q34.1, encoding the LIM homeobox transcription factor 1-beta, critical for dorsoventral limb patterning, podocyte differentiation, and glomerular basement membrane collagen regulation
topics.inclusion_rationale: Premier hereditary pleiotropic nephropathy combining bedside triangular fingernail lunulae and absent patellae with pathognomonic bilateral iliac horns on pelvic radiography and pathognomonic banded collagen fibrils within a 'moth-eaten' GBM on electron microscopy.

topics.name: Nephropathic Cystinosis
topics.subspecialty: Metabolic and Lysosomal Storage Kidney Diseases
clinical_manifestations: Onset in early infancy (6-12 months) with complete renal Fanconi syndrome: extreme polyuria, polydipsia, recurrent episodes of severe dehydration, vomiting, failure to thrive, and growth arrest below the 3rd percentile

Hypophosphatemic Fanconi rickets: prominent rachitic rosary (beading of costochondral junctions), widening of wrists and ankles, severe lower limb bowing (genu varum/valgum), and craniotabes resistant to physiologic vitamin D

Pathognomonic ocular findings: severe photophobia, chronic blepharospasm, and eye rubbing; slit-lamp biomicroscopy reveals innumerable glistening, tinsel-like, needle-shaped and hexagonal cystine crystals deposited throughout the corneal stroma (appearing after 1 year of age, 100% pathognomonic)
Cutaneous pigmentary dilution: characteristic fair complexion, blond hair, and blue eyes (distinct hypopigmentation compared to unaffected family members due to altered melanogenesis)

Extrarenal storage manifestations in late childhood/adolescence: primary hypothyroidism (thyroid follicular atrophy), distal vacuolar myopathy, pancreatic exocrine and endocrine insufficiency (diabetes mellitus), and swallowing dysfunction
radiological_manifestations: Plain Skeletal Radiography: Severe, active hypophosphatemic rickets demonstrating pathognomonic cupping, widening, splaying, and ragged fraying of the metaphyseal margins at the distal radius, ulna, and tibia; wide, radiolucent growth plates (physes); severe generalized osteopenia and pseudofractures (Looser zones)

Renal Ultrasonography: Progressive bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis characterized by intensely hyperechoic renal pyramids with acoustic shadowing, loss of corticomedullary differentiation, and progressive symmetric renal volume loss leading to small, shrunken, echogenic kidneys
In Vivo Corneal Confocal Microscopy: Quantitative visualization of high-density hyperreflective, needle-shaped and fusiform crystal deposits in the anterior, middle, and posterior corneal stroma
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy Light Microscopy & Microdissection: Pathognomonic 'swan-neck' deformity of the proximal convoluted tubule (extreme atrophy and narrowing of the initial proximal tubule segment directly originating from the glomerulus, lined by flattened, atrophic epithelium); marked multinucleated podocytes; progressive focal segmental and global glomerulosclerosis with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy

Polarized Light Microscopy (Alcohol-Fixed Tissue): Innumerable iridescent, birefringent, hexagonal, rectangular, and needle-shaped cystine crystals packed within the lysosomes of interstitial histiocytes, mesangial cells, and proximal tubular cells (crystals dissolve in routine aqueous formalin fixation and require absolute ethanol fixation)

Electron Microscopy & Genetics: Intralysosomal crystalline voids within podocytes and interstitial macrophages; molecular testing demonstrates biallelic pathogenic loss-of-function variants in CTNS (such as the common 57-kb European founder deletion), resulting in defective lysosomal cystinosin transporter
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic lysosomal storage ciliopathy pairing infantile Fanconi rickets, blond hypopigmentation, and slit-lamp corneal crystals with metaphyseal fraying on X-ray, medullary nephrocalcinosis, and pathognomonic proximal tubular 'swan-neck' deformity on histology.

topics.name: Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1
topics.subspecialty: Metabolic and Genetic Renal Storage Diseases
clinical_manifestations: Early infantile or childhood presentation with recurrent, refractory calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis and urolithiasis, passing gravel or large calculi, leading to obstructive uropathy, renal colic, and rapid progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD)
Oxalate osteopathy: severe bone pain, joint deformities, pathological fractures of long bones, and painful swollen metaphyses mimicking intractable rickets

Cutaneous oxalosis (calciphylaxis-like ischemic necrosis): livedo reticularis, painful violaceous plaques, peripheral digital gangrene, Raynaud phenomenon, and ischemic acral ulcerations from systemic microvascular oxalate precipitation

Ocular oxalosis: pathognomonic 'crystalline retinopathy' characterized by white-to-yellow glistening birefringent flecks and crystalline deposits densely scattered across the posterior pole, macula, and retinal pigment epithelium on fundoscopy

Cardiac oxalosis: high-grade atrioventricular conduction blocks, bundle branch blocks, intractable ventricular arrhythmias, and restrictive cardiomyopathy resulting from diffuse myocardial oxalate crystal infiltration
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Abdominal CT / KUB Plain Radiography: Dense, diffuse, bilateral medullary and cortical nephrocalcinosis ('chalky-white kidneys') accompanied by bilateral radiopaque staghorn or multiple branched dendritic renal calculi (pure calcium oxalate monohydrate, >1200-1500 HU)

Renal Ultrasonography: Strikingly hyperechoic kidneys ('bright kidneys') with complete loss of corticomedullary differentiation and dense posterior acoustic shadowing caused by diffuse parenchymal crystal aggregation

Skeletal Radiographs (Pathognomonic Oxalate Osteopathy): Sclerotic transverse metaphyseal bands ('dense bone bands'), generalized axial osteosclerosis alternating with radiolucent submetaphyseal bands, Looser zones, cortical thinning, and pathological metaphyseal fractures

Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): Distinct hyperreflective punctate foci throughout the inner and outer retinal layers, with retinal pigment epithelial disruptions corresponding to crystalline deposits
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy (Diagnostic Polarized Light Microscopy): Innumerable birefringent, prismatic, wheatsheaf-shaped and radial rosette-shaped calcium oxalate monohydrate (whewellite) crystals packing tubular lumens, tubular epithelial cells, and the renal interstitium; under polarized light microscopy, crystals exhibit intense, bright polychromatic birefringence (multicolored glistening crystals)

Renal Biopsy Histopathology (H&E): Extensive foreign-body giant cell granulomatous reaction surrounding ruptured tubules with extruded crystals, marked interstitial fibrosis, profound tubular atrophy, and glomerulosclerosis

Hepatic Biopsy / Molecular Testing: Absent or markedly deficient alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase (AGT) catalytic activity in liver homogenates; biallelic pathogenic mutations in the AGXT gene (chromosome 2q37.3) confirming peroxisomal enzyme deficiency or mitochondrial mistargeting
topics.inclusion_rationale: Hallmark inborn error of glyoxylate metabolism causing childhood nephrocalcinosis, livedoid digital gangrene, crystalline retinopathy, dense metaphyseal bone bands, and intensely birefringent wheatsheaf calcium oxalate crystals on polarized microscopy.

topics.name: Renal Angiomyolipoma and Wunderlich Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Classic Lenk's triad of Wunderlich syndrome (spontaneous, non-traumatic acute retroperitoneal hemorrhage from ruptured AML): sudden severe unilateral flank/loin pain, palpable tender flank mass, and acute hypovolemic hemorrhagic shock (pallor, diaphoresis, tachycardia, and profound hypotension)

Cutaneous ecchymoses: delayed development (24-48 hours) of Grey Turner's sign (blue-red discoloration of the flank) and Cullen's sign (periumbilical ecchymosis) due to massive retroperitoneal blood tracking along fascial planes

Cutaneous stigmata of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (present in up to 80% of bilateral/multifocal AML cases): facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum—erythematous papules in a butterfly distribution across cheeks and nose), ungual/periungual fibromas (Koenen tumors), shagreen patches (leathery lumbosacral plaques), and hypomelanotic macules (ash-leaf spots under Wood's lamp)
Macroscopic gross hematuria, dull aching flank heaviness, and palpable ballotable flank mass in unruptured large lesions (>4 cm in diameter)
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Abdominal CT (Diagnostic Imaging Gold Standard): Pathognomonic identification of macroscopic intratumoral fat—well-demarcated exophytic cortical renal mass demonstrating regions of measurable negative attenuation values (typically -20 to -100 Hounsfield Units [HU]) intermixed with soft-tissue attenuation vascular and muscular components

Abdominal CT in Wunderlich Syndrome: Massive, hyperdense retroperitoneal hematoma (40-70 HU) dissecting into the perinephric and paranephric spaces, displacing the kidney and colon anteriorly, with active contrast extravasation ('contrast blush') on early arterial CTA phases

Abdominal MRI: Chemical shift imaging demonstrates the pathognomonic 'india-ink' boundary artifact (black etching line at fat-water interfaces) on out-of-phase T1-weighted gradient echo images; bright T1 and T2 signal with characteristic complete loss of signal on fat-saturated sequences

Catheter Renal Angiography: Hypervascular renal mass supplied by dilated, tortuous, dysplastic arterial branches displaying a 'sunburst' neovascular pattern with characteristic saccular or fusiform pseudoaneurysms (spontaneous rupture risk increases exponentially when pseudoaneurysms exceed 5 mm)
pathology_manifestations: Gross Nephrectomy / Embolization Specimen: Well-circumscribed, non-encapsulated, lobulated mass bulging from the renal parenchyma, displaying a variegated bright-yellow (adipose tissue), reddish-brown (hemorrhage), and grayish-white (smooth muscle) cut surface

Histopathology (Triphasic PEComa Architecture): Pathognomonic intermingling of three distinct tissue components: mature adipose tissue (adipocytes with variable lipid droplets), dysplastic, thick-walled, hyalinized, tortuous blood vessels completely lacking an internal elastic lamina, and sheets/fascicles of spindled and epithelioid smooth muscle cells radiating outward from vessel walls

Immunohistochemistry: Characteristic co-expression of melanocytic markers (diffuse positivity for HMB-45 and Melan-A) and myogenic markers (smooth muscle actin [SMA], Calponin); negative for epithelial markers (Cytokeratin AE1/AE3, Epithelial Membrane Antigen [EMA]), differentiating AML from clear cell RCC
topics.inclusion_rationale: Paramount renal mesenchymal neoplasm featuring TSC cutaneous stigmata and Lenk's triad in Wunderlich syndrome, confirmed by pathognomonic negative CT attenuation (<-20 HU) and triphasic HMB-45-positive histology.

topics.name: Renal Cell Carcinoma
clinical_manifestations: Classic Guyon's triad of locally advanced disease: palpable, firm, non-tender abdominal/flank mass, macroscopic gross hematuria (often with worm-like ureteral clot casts), and dull, persistent loin/flank pain (fully present in ~10% of cases)

Acute non-reducing left-sided scrotal varicocele ('bag of worms') that fails to decompress or empty in the supine/recumbent position, caused by left renal vein occlusion by tumor thrombus impeding left gonadal vein drainage

Bilateral lower extremity pitting edema, ascites, and dilated, tortuous superficial collateral veins on the anterior abdominal wall (caput medusae / IVC syndrome) resulting from inferior vena cava tumor thrombus extension

Paraneoplastic systemic signs: Stauffer syndrome (non-metastatic hepatic dysfunction presenting with hepatomegaly, jaundice, elevated serum alkaline phosphatase, and prolonged prothrombin time), severe erythrocytosis (plethoric facies from ectopic tumor erythropoietin production), and symptomatic hypercalcemia (PTHrP release)
Cachexia, marked unintentional weight loss, and prolonged fever of unknown origin (IL-6 mediated)
radiological_manifestations: Multiphase Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI of Abdomen (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Heterogeneous, solid, exophytic cortical renal mass showing intense, vivid early arterial phase enhancement (>80-100 HU increase over unenhanced baseline) with rapid washout in the nephrographic/excretory phase; prominent areas of central non-enhancing necrosis, internal cystic degeneration, and coarse dystrophic calcifications

CT Venography / Abdominal MRI with Gadolinium: Precise delineation and staging of intravenous tumor thrombus: non-enhancing filling defect expanding the main renal vein and advancing into the inferior vena cava (IVC) up to the retrohepatic space or right atrium (Neves/Zincke classification Levels I-IV)

Renal Doppler Ultrasound: Hypoechoic or heterogeneous vascular mass displaying disordered high-velocity internal vascularity, along with absent or reversed flow in the main renal vein indicating invasive tumor thrombus
pathology_manifestations: Gross Nephrectomy Specimen: Well-circumscribed, fleshy, golden-yellow to orange-tan lobulated cortical mass bulging from the renal contour, punctuated by geographic areas of red hemorrhage, grayish-white necrosis, and central cystic liquefaction

Histopathology (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Clear cell RCC (75-80%): Sheets, alveolar nests, and cords of uniform polygonal cells with abundant optical clear cytoplasm (secondary to dissolved cytoplasmic glycogen and neutral lipids during processing); bordered by an exquisite, delicate, arborizing network of thin-walled sinusoidal capillaries ('chicken-wire' vasculature); nucleolar prominence graded by the WHO/ISUP 4-tier grading system

Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong, circumferential 'box-like' membranous staining for Carbonic Anhydrase IX (CA-IX), along with positivity for CD10, Vimentin, and PAX8; typically negative for CK7, CD117, and AMACR (differentiating from chromophobe RCC, oncocytoma, and papillary RCC)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal primary renal neoplasm exhibiting Guyon's triad, an irreducible left-sided varicocele, and IVC syndrome, corroborated by multiphase CT/MRI showing a hypervascular necrotic cortical mass with venous thrombus and pathognomonic clear cells with 'chicken-wire' vascularity on histology.

topics.name: Retroperitoneal Fibrosis
clinical_manifestations: Deep-seated, dull, non-colicky, persistent lower back, lumbar, flank, or lower abdominal pain radiating into the groins, testicles, or thighs, worse at night and poorly responsive to position changes

Progressive bilateral lower extremity edema, scrotal swelling, and secondary deep vein thrombosis (DVT) resulting from extrinsic compression of the inferior vena cava and iliac veins by the retroperitoneal fibrous mass
Lower extremity claudication and diminished lower extremity pulses caused by encasement and constriction of the abdominal aorta and common iliac arteries
Oliguria, anuria, or fluctuating urine output secondary to extrinsic ureteral obstruction and progressive obstructive uropathy (post-renal acute kidney injury)
Constitutional symptoms: low-grade fever, anorexia, involuntary weight loss, and fatigue
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT / MRI (Diagnostic Imaging Gold Standard): Pathognomonic well-demarcated fibrous retroperitoneal plaque or soft-tissue mass centered over the anterior and lateral surface of the infrarenal abdominal aorta and common iliac vessels (between the renal arteries and the aortic bifurcation), characteristically entrapping both ureters and the IVC

Classic Urographic / CT Hallmark: Pathognomonic 'medial deviation of the middle third of both ureters' with proximal ureterohydronephrosis, smooth tapering of the obstructed ureteral segments, without displacement of the abdominal aorta anteriorly away from the spine (a vital imaging differentiator from retroperitoneal lymphoma or sarcoma, which elevate the aorta)

Contrast Enhancement / PET-CT: Active inflammatory phase demonstrates vivid contrast enhancement on CT/MRI and intense hypermetabolism on 18F-FDG PET-CT; late inactive fibrous phase shows low T1 and low T2 signal intensity on MRI with minimal contrast enhancement
pathology_manifestations: Surgical Biopsy Histopathology (Diagnostic Hallmark): Dense, hypocellular, collagenous connective tissue characterized by whorled, fascicular, or storiform fibrosis; prominent perivascular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate composed of mature B and T lymphocytes, plasma cells, and eosinophils; obliterative phlebitis (fibrotic occlusion and transmural inflammatory destruction of retroperitoneal veins)

Immunohistochemistry (IgG4-Related RPF): Abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells with >10 to 30 IgG4+ plasma cells per high-power field (HPF) and an elevated IgG4/IgG ratio exceeding 40%; negative for cytokeratins and sarcoma markers, confirming benign fibro-inflammatory proliferation
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic periaortitis and fibroinflammatory obstructive uropathy featuring lower back pain, lower limb edema/DVT, and pathognomonic CT/IVU medial deviation of ureters with an infrarenal periaortic fibrotic plaque, and storiform fibrosis with IgG4+ plasma cells and obliterative phlebitis on biopsy.

topics.name: Xanthogranulomatous Pyelonephritis
topics.subspecialty: Severe Renal Infections and Inflammatory Masses
clinical_manifestations: Large, firm, tender, ballotable unilateral flank mass that can mimic a huge malignant retroperitoneal neoplasm
Profound chronic constitutional wasting: marked unintentional weight loss, anorexia, severe cachexia, low-grade daily swinging fevers, and dull unilateral flank or abdominal pain
Draining nephrocutaneous fistula: discharging purulent or yellowish sinus tracts through the lumbar flank skin, buttock, or groin
Severe flank erythema, induration, and tenderness over the costovertebral angle, occasionally with psoas sign (pain on hip extension due to retroperitoneal and psoas abscess extension)
Recurrent recalcitrant urinary tract infections and urosepsis, predominantly caused by Proteus mirabilis or Escherichia coli
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Pathognomonic 'Bear's Paw Sign': massively enlarged, non-functioning kidney wherein normal renal parenchyma is completely replaced by multiple rounded, low-attenuation (-10 to +30 Hounsfield Units) fluid- and lipid-filled cavities (dilated calyces filled with pus and xanthomatous debris) radiating outward in a paw-like distribution around a central obstructing, contracted renal pelvis containing a large, dense staghorn calculus

CT Pelvis / Retroperitoneum: Marked inflammatory infiltration and thick stranding of the perirenal space, thickening of Gerota's fascia, and extrarenal invasion into the psoas muscle, retroperitoneal fat, colon, and lateral abdominal wall forming nephrocutaneous and nephrocolic fistulae

Renal Ultrasound: Massive renal enlargement with complete distortion of normal corticomedullary architecture, multiple hypoechoic fluid-debris filled calyces radiating outwards, and a brightly echogenic central staghorn stone producing sharp acoustic shadowing
pathology_manifestations: Gross Nephrectomy Specimen: Massively enlarged, distorted kidney, the parenchyma of which is obliterated and replaced by multiple nodular, circumscribed, bright golden-yellow, orange-tan, and yellow-brown lipid-rich masses surrounding the necrotic pelvicalyceal system and the central obstructive staghorn stone, frequently with extension through the renal capsule into perinephric adipose tissue

Histopathology (Diagnostic Hallmark): Extensive destruction of normal renal architecture by a dense, destructive granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate dominated by sheets of lipid-laden foamy histiocytes (xanthoma cells) with round vesicular nuclei and abundant pale granular vacuolated cytoplasm; interspersed with multinucleated Touton giant cells (lipid ring surrounding a central wreath of nuclei), plasma cells, lymphocytes, and neutrophils, bordered by extensive cholesterol clefts and dense fibrous encapsulation

Immunohistochemistry: Foamy xanthoma cells are strongly and diffusely positive for CD68 and CD163 (histiocytic markers), while negative for cytokeratin (AE1/AE3), EMA, and CD10, clearly distinguishing XGP from clear cell renal cell carcinoma
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic destructive chronic infection featuring chronic cachexia, draining cutaneous flank fistulae, and a ballotable flank mass, accompanied by the pathognomonic 'bear's paw sign' with staghorn calculus on CT and sheets of lipid-laden CD68+ xanthoma cells and Touton giant cells on pathology.

topics.name: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
clinical_manifestations: Acute monophasic encephalopathy: Abrupt onset of altered mental status (lethargy, confusion, delirium, stupor, or coma) occurring 1 to 3 weeks following a viral prodrome (e.g., exanthematous virus, upper respiratory infection) or immunization, primarily in children and young adults

Multifocal neurologic deficits: Bilateral optic neuritis, multiple cranial neuropathies (facial palsy, ocular dysmotility), ataxia, hemiparesis or quadriparesis, meningismus, and hyperreflexia with bilateral extensor plantar responses
Acute transverse myelitis signs: Rapidly ascending sensory deficits, paraplegia, and acute neurogenic urinary retention requiring catheterization
Fulminant variants (Acute Hemorrhagic Leukoencephalitis / Weston Hurst syndrome): Hyperacute deterioration with high fever, seizures, deep coma, signs of brain herniation, and decerebrate posturing
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial and Coronal T2/FLAIR and T1+Gd): Hallmark large, bilateral, asymmetrical, poorly marginated, fluffy or 'cloud-like' T2/FLAIR hyperintensities involving the subcortical and deep cerebral white matter, centrum semiovale, thalamus, and basal ganglia; deep gray matter involvement (thalamic/striatal) is frequent and helpful in distinguishing from classic MS; post-gadolinium T1 shows variable punctate, nodular, or incomplete ring enhancement; all lesions appear of the same chronological age
Spine MRI: Confluent, poorly demarcated, extensive intramedullary T2 hyperintensity spanning multiple vertebral segments with mild cord swelling and patchy enhancement
Head CT / MRI in Weston Hurst syndrome: Massive cerebral edema with focal petechial hemorrhages on CT and prominent gradient blooming on GRE/SWI sequences
pathology_manifestations: CNS histopathology / autopsy: Pathognomonic perivenular sleeves ('cuffs') of demyelination centered around small- and medium-sized parenchymal veins in cerebral and spinal white matter; dense infiltration of foamy lipid-laden macrophages engulfing myelin debris, accompanied by perivascular T-cell and B-cell infiltration; remarkable relative preservation of axons and absence of older, chronic astrogliotic plaques (monophasic single-age pathology)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Hallmark pediatric/young adult demyelinating encephalopathy with florid post-infectious presentation, classic bilateral fluffy/cloud-like white matter and deep gray MRI lesions of uniform age, and perivenular demyelinating sleeves on histopathology.

topics.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
clinical_manifestations: Widespread visible muscle fasciculations (rippling and flickering twitches beneath skin of limbs and trunk)
Tongue muscle atrophy, wrinkling, and continuous visible tongue fasciculations
'Split-hand' syndrome (preferential, marked wasting of the thenar complex [APB/FDI] with relative sparing of the hypothenar muscle [ADM])
Simultaneous upper motor neuron signs (spasticity, brisk hyperreflexia, extensor plantar response) and lower motor neuron signs (profound wasting, flaccidity, weakness)
Claw hand, wrist drop, and foot drop with steppage gait
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Cervical Spine MRI: Bilateral, symmetrical, continuous T2/FLAIR hyperintensity tracking along the corticospinal tracts from the corona radiata through the internal capsule and brainstem; 'motor band sign' (hypointensity of the precentral motor cortex on T2*/SWI due to excessive iron/macrophage deposition); spinal cord anterior horn atrophy
High-Frequency Muscle Ultrasound: High sensitivity for detection of silent, widespread muscle fasciculations and progressive muscle architecture atrophy
pathology_manifestations: Autopsy / muscle biopsy: Marked loss and degeneration of anterior horn alpha-motor neurons in the spinal cord and cortical Betz cells; reactive astrogliosis; characteristic TDP-43-positive ubiquitinated cytoplasmic inclusions within remaining motor neurons; muscle biopsy shows classic neurogenic group atrophy with target fibers
topics.inclusion_rationale: Combines striking physical signs (tongue fasciculations, 'split-hand' thenar wasting) with MRI corticospinal tract hyperintensity and muscle ultrasound fasciculation mapping.

topics.name: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
clinical_manifestations: Florid psychiatric prodrome: Acute-onset severe psychosis, agitation, paranoid delusions, visual and auditory hallucinations, mania, bizarre disinhibited behavior, and severe insomnia in previously healthy young females or children

Pathognomonic stereotypic dyskinesias: Continuous, involuntary, bizarre oro-facial-lingual dyskinesias (continuous lip-smacking, chewing, tongue protrusion, grimacing, teeth-grinding/bruxism), accompanied by choreoathetoid limb writhing, oculogyric crises, and pelvic thrusting
Catatonia, mutism, and memory collapse: Rapid progression to profound speech reduction, echolalia, complete mutism, waxy flexibility, catatonic posturing, and dense retrograde/anterograde amnesia

Autonomic instability and central hypoventilation: Life-threatening fluctuations in blood pressure, hyperpyrexia, sinus tachycardia, severe cardiac bradyarrhythmias/pauses, hypersalivation, and central respiratory hypoventilation requiring mechanical ventilation
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic Transvaginal Ultrasound and Contrast-Enhanced CT/MRI: High-sensitivity demonstration of an underlying mature cystic ovarian teratoma (dermoid cyst) containing calcified tooth/bone components, acoustic shadowing, cystic fat-fluid levels, and Rokitansky nodules in ~40-50% of young female cases

Brain MRI (T2/FLAIR and T1+Gd): Often normal or showing subtle, transient, non-specific T2/FLAIR hyperintensities within the medial temporal lobes, hippocampus, frontobasal cortex, basal ganglia, and periventricular white matter; faint meningeal or cortical gyral enhancement in ~20-30%

Continuous Video-EEG: Highly characteristic, pathognomonic 'extreme delta brush' (EDB) electrographic pattern: continuous, rhythmic, symmetrical 1-3 Hz delta waves with superimposed bursts of fast 20-30 Hz beta activity predominantly in frontal derivations
pathology_manifestations: Ovarian teratoma and neural tissue pathology: Mature cystic teratoma containing dysplastic neuroglial tissue infiltrated by prominent CD20+ B lymphocytes, CD138+ plasma cells, and microglial activation; confirmation of CSF and serum IgG antibodies (subclass IgG1) directed against the GluN1 (NR1) subunit of the NMDA receptor; immunofluorescence shows antibody-induced cross-linking, capping, and selective internalization of cell-surface NMDA receptors into endosomes, causing reversible loss of synaptic NMDA receptor clusters without neuronal death
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic autoimmune synaptic encephalitis featuring pathognomonic oro-facial-lingual dyskinesias, electrographic 'extreme delta brush', pelvic ultrasound/CT ovarian teratoma, and anti-GluN1 receptor-internalizing pathology.

topics.name: Carotid-Cavernous Fistula
clinical_manifestations: Pulsatile exophthalmos (proptosis): Unilateral forward ocular protrusion that visibly and synchronously pulsates with the arterial cardiac pulse, accompanied by palpable orbital thrill on gentle digital palpation of the globe

Auscultated ocular and cephalic bruit: Loud, continuous, whooshing subjective and objective cranial bruit heard loudest over the ipsilateral orbit, forehead, and temple, characteristically diminishing or abolished upon digital compression of the ipsilateral common carotid artery in the neck

Chemosis and 'corkscrew' arterialized episcleral vessels: Dramatic conjunctival edema (chemosis) with beefy red prolapse of the conjunctiva beyond the palpebral fissure, accompanied by pathognomonic corkscrew-like, dilated, tortuous, brightly arterialized episcleral and conjunctival vessels radiating outward towards the limbus ('caput medusae' of the eye)

Cranial nerve ophthalmoplegia: Variable combinations of third (oculomotor), fourth (trochlear), and sixth (abducens) cranial nerve palsies due to compressive engorgement or ischemia within the cavernous sinus wall, most frequently presenting as an early, isolated sixth nerve palsy (horizontal diplopia in lateral gaze) because CN VI runs free within the cavernous sinus lumen adjacent to the carotid artery

Secondary glaucoma and ocular hypertension: Severely elevated intraocular pressure (frequently >30-40 mmHg) with ocular pain, corneal edema, and venous stasis retinopathy (dilated tortuous retinal veins, flame hemorrhages, and optic disc edema) due to chronically elevated vortex and episcleral venous pressure
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Orbit and Brain CT / CTA: Prominent, pathognomonic enlargement and asymmetric dilatation of the ipsilateral superior ophthalmic vein (SOV, often >3-4 mm in diameter); outward convex bulging and expansion of the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus; asymmetric proptosis and marked enlargement of the extraocular muscle bellies (especially the superior rectus and medial rectus complexes) with sparing of the tendinous insertions

Orbit and Brain MRI / MRV: Markedly dilated, tortuous tubular flow voids in the superior ophthalmic vein and cavernous sinus on T1- and T2-weighted sequences; asymmetric expansion of the cavernous sinus with early post-contrast enhancement identical in timing to internal carotid artery transit; engorgement of cortical and dural draining veins with T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in adjacent brain parenchyma in high-risk retrograde cortical venous drainage

Catheter Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA, Gold Standard): Unequivocal demonstration of an abnormal high-flow or low-flow arteriovenous communication between the internal or external carotid artery and the cavernous sinus; Barrow classification: Type A (direct, high-flow shunt between the intracavernous internal carotid artery and cavernous sinus, classic post-traumatic or ruptured aneurysm), Type B (dural shunt from meningeal branches of the ICA), Type C (dural shunt from meningeal branches of the ECA), and Type D (dural shunt from meningeal branches of both ICA and ECA); immediate filling of the cavernous sinus during early arterial phase with retrograde opacification of the superior ophthalmic vein, inferior ophthalmic vein, and inferior petrosal sinus
pathology_manifestations: Vascular and Fistulous Histopathology: Direct laceration or defect in the muscularis and internal elastic lamina of the cavernous segment of the internal carotid artery connecting directly with the thin-walled, endothelially lined venous channels of the cavernous sinus; or complex plexiform nidus of microscopic arteriovenous communications within the dural wall of the sinus supplied by the meningohypophyseal trunk or inferolateral trunk; marked arterialization of the draining veins characterized by fibromuscular intimal hyperplasia, medial hypertrophy, fragmented elastic lamina, and microthrombosis
topics.inclusion_rationale: Definitive neurovascular and neuro-ophthalmic entity presenting with the unmistakable photographic triad of pulsatile proptosis, auscultable orbital bruit, and corkscrew arterialized conjunctival vessels, definitively staged on catheter DSA and orbit CT/MRI via superior ophthalmic vein enlargement.

topics.name: Cerebral Cavernous Malformation
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent unprovoked epileptic seizures: The most common initial presentation (50-70% of supratentorial cases), manifesting as focal seizures with or without impaired awareness or progression to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures, driven by recurrent microscopic subclinical hemorrhages that deposit epileptogenic hemosiderin into the surrounding perilesional cerebral cortex

Focal neurological deficits: Subacute or sudden motor weakness, sensory loss, cranial nerve palsies, dysmetria, or visual field deficits occurring in a 'stepwise' or episodic relapsing-remitting course caused by recurrent intralesional microhemorrhages, local mass effect, and perilesional edema

Brainstem cavernoma apoplexy: Severe acute headache, diplopia, internuclear ophthalmoplegia, facial numbness, dysarthria, dysphagia, ataxia, and quadriparesis resulting from acute hemorrhage within a brainstem cavernoma (pons, midbrain, medulla) causing catastrophic compression of compact cranial nerve nuclei and long tracts

Chronic intractable headaches: Persistent throbbing or dull localized head pain resulting from microvascular expansion, dural irritation, or intermittent microbleeding into neighboring parenchymal tissue

Familial multiple cavernoma cutaneous lesions: In patients with hereditary CCM (autosomal dominant loss-of-function mutations in CCM1/KRIT1, CCM2/MGC4607, or CCM3/PDCD10), presence of hyperkeratotic cutaneous capillary-venous malformations, facial angiofibromas, or vertebral hemangiomas accompanied by dozens of asymptomatic or symptomatic intracranial lesions
radiological_manifestations: Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI, Pathognomonic Popcorn Appearance): T2-weighted and FLAIR imaging unequivocally demonstrates the pathognomonic well-circumscribed 'popcorn' or 'mulberry' lesion characterized by a central heterogeneous core of reticulated mixed hyperintense and hypointense signal intensities representing hemorrhage of varying chronological stages (methemoglobin, intracellular and extracellular, and hemosiderin), completely enveloped by a continuous, well-defined hypointense rim of hemosiderin deposition

Gradient-Echo (GRE) T2* and Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging (SWI): Dramatic, exquisite 'blooming' artifact with intense signal drop-out resulting from magnetic susceptibility effects of perilesional hemosiderin; SWI is hypersensitive and detects dozens to hundreds of occult punctate micro-cavernomas in familial forms that are entirely invisible on conventional spin-echo T1/T2 imaging

Angiographically Occult / Normal Catheter Angiography (DSA): Cavernous malformations are classic 'angiographically occult vascular malformations' displaying complete non-visualization or faint avascular mass effect on conventional catheter cerebral angiography due to low internal blood flow, thrombosis, and absence of direct high-flow arterial feeding vessels; often accompanied by an adjacent, non-stenotic developmental venous anomaly (DVA) exhibiting a classic 'caput medusae' collection of medullary veins draining into a single dilated collector vein
pathology_manifestations: Gross and Microscopic Histopathology: Well-circumscribed, lobulated, purplish-red or dark bluish 'mulberry-like' vascular malformation composed of compact, back-to-back, closely packed, thin-walled, dilated capillary-like vascular sinusoids (caverns) lined by a single layer of attenuated, mature endothelial cells; pathognomonic absence of intervening mature brain parenchyma within the lesion core; walls lack smooth muscle and elastic tissue, consisting only of collagenous adventitia; lumen exhibits thrombosis in various stages of organization, recanalization, and calcification; surrounding brain tissue shows dense gliosis with abundant hemosiderin-laden macrophages (siderophages) and Rosenthal fibers
topics.inclusion_rationale: A cornerstone neurovascular disorder causing focal epilepsy and brainstem stroke, renowned for its pathognomonic MRI T2 'popcorn' core with complete hemosiderin blooming rim on SWI, angiographic occultness, and distinctive sinusoids devoid of intervening brain parenchyma.

topics.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 1A
synonyms: hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy type 1A
clinical_manifestations: Classic 'inverted champagne bottle' or 'stork leg' appearance of the lower extremities, produced by severe wasting and atrophy of the peroneal and anterior calf muscles contrasting sharply with preserved proximal thigh musculature
Bilateral rigid high-arched feet (pes cavus) with extensor claw toes / hammer toes and prominent plantar callosities beneath metatarsal heads
Bilateral foot drop resulting in a high-stepping, slapping steppage gait and frequent tripping over carpets or uneven ground
Intrinsic hand muscle wasting and weakness leading to flattened thenar/hypothenar eminences, interosseous guttering, and claw hand deformity ('main en griffe')

Palpably enlarged, hypertrophied, firm peripheral nerves (frequently identifiable along the greater auricular nerve in the neck, ulnar nerve at the elbow, and common peroneal nerve at the fibular head)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Neuromuscular Ultrasound: Marked, diffuse, symmetrical enlargement of peripheral nerve cross-sectional area (CSA) across both entrapment and non-entrapment sites (median, ulnar, radial, common fibular, and tibial nerves), showing hypoechoic fascicular enlargement without focal compression

Lower Extremity Muscle MRI (T1-weighted): Selective, symmetrical fatty infiltration and atrophy of the anterior and lateral compartment muscles of the lower leg (tibialis anterior, peroneus longus and brevis, extensor digitorum), with relative initial sparing of deep posterior flexors and intrinsic plantar foot muscles

Plain Radiographs of Feet: Structural pes cavus deformity showing elevated calcaneal pitch angle, acute angle of Hibbs, dorsal subluxation of the metatarsophalangeal joints, and flexion deformities of the interphalangeal joints
pathology_manifestations: Sural Nerve Biopsy Histopathology: Pathognomonic 'onion bulb' formations (concentric, redundant lamellae of proliferating Schwann cell cytoplasmic processes and basement membranes encircling demyelinated or thinly remyelinated axons), reflecting chronic, repeated cycles of segmental demyelination and remyelination; severe loss of large myelinated fibers with preserved unmyelinated fibers
Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic 1.4-Mb duplication of chromosome 17p11.2 containing the PMP22 gene (peripheral myelin protein 22), causing PMP22 protein overexpression and toxic dysmyelination
topics.inclusion_rationale: Most common inherited neuropathy, instantly identified by the 'stork leg' appearance, severe pes cavus, and palpably enlarged nerves, demonstrated objectively by diffuse nerve enlargement on ultrasound and pathognomonic 'onion bulb' Schwann formations.

topics.name: Corticobasal Degeneration
clinical_manifestations: 'Alien limb' phenomenon: pathognomonic sensory-motor dissociation where the patient's arm or leg exhibits autonomous, involuntary, purposeful-appearing complex movements (e.g., reaching, unbuttoning, groping) that the patient feels is completely outside their voluntary control and foreign to them
Extreme asymmetric limb apraxia: severe ideomotor apraxia (inability to execute learned skilled motor gestures, such as waving goodbye or using a key, despite normal primary muscle strength)
Cortical sensory loss: asymmetric astereognosis, agraphesthesia, two-point discrimination loss, and sensory extinction on double simultaneous stimulation
Fixed, asymmetric dystonic posturing of the affected upper extremity: clenched fist ('striatal limb'), flexion at wrist and elbow, and internal shoulder rotation
Focal stimulus-sensitive cortical myoclonus (reflex myoclonic jerks elicited by tapping or touch), levodopa-unresponsive parkinsonian rigidity, and progressive dynamic speech apraxia
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (3D T1-weighted and FLAIR): Marked, strikingly asymmetrical cortical atrophy predominantly localized to the peri-rolandic motor cortex, superior parietal lobule, and posterior frontal gyrus contralateral to the clinically affected limb, with widening of the central and postcentral sulci

Brain FDG-PET / SPECT: Markedly asymmetric hypometabolism / hypoperfusion in the contralateral cerebral cortex (superior parietal, peri-rolandic, and premotor regions) as well as the contralateral basal ganglia and thalamus

Tau-PET (18F-PI-2620 / 18F-AV-1451): Highly asymmetric tracer uptake localized to the contralateral peri-rolandic motor strip, superior parietal cortex, and basal ganglia, correlating with the spatial distribution of 4R tau pathology
Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI): Significant asymmetric reduction in fractional anisotropy (FA) along the corticospinal tracts and corpus callosum
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology Histopathology: 4-repeat (4R) tauopathy featuring pathognomonic 'astrocytic plaques' (annular, ring-like clusters of phosphorylated tau-positive fuzzy distal processes surrounding a tau-negative central astrocyte soma) in the neocortex and striatum; presence of swollen, achromatic, ballooned neurons (Pick cells / corticonigral degeneration) showing loss of Nissl substance in deep cortical layers; extensive tau-positive neuropil threads, neurofibrillary tangles, and coiled bodies in oligodendrocytes throughout the neocortex, striatum, and substantia nigra
topics.inclusion_rationale: Dramatically asymmetric neurodegenerative tauopathy showcasing the unmistakable 'alien limb' phenomenon, severe limb apraxia, and clenched dystonic fist, mapped precisely to asymmetric peri-rolandic cortical atrophy and astrocytic plaques.

topics.name: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease
clinical_manifestations: Dramatic startle-induced myoclonus: sudden, involuntary, widespread shock-like jerks of the trunk and limbs provoked by sudden auditory (clapping, dropped objects) or tactile stimuli
Fulminant, rapidly progressive dementia with global cognitive decline, memory impairment, and personality changes evolving over weeks to a few months
Prominent cerebellar ataxia: wide-based staggering gait, limb dysmetria, intention tremor, and nystagmus (often initial presentation in the Brownell-Oppenheimer variant)
Akinetic mutism in end stages: patient lies awake, eyes open and visually tracking or fixed, but completely immobile, unresponsive, and mute
Higher visual processing deficits: visual agnosia, metamorphopsia, and cortical blindness (Heidenhain variant), accompanied by severe extrapyramidal rigidity and spasticity
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Diffusion-Weighted Imaging DWI and ADC Maps): Pathognomonic 'cortical ribboning'—confluent, bright linear hyperintensity along the cerebral cortical gyri (predominantly involving the insula, cingulate gyrus, and frontoparietal cortex), with corresponding restricted diffusion (hypointensity on ADC map)

Brain MRI (Axial DWI/FLAIR): Marked, symmetric or asymmetric hyperintensity of the basal ganglia, particularly the caudate head and anterior putamen, often preceding or coexisting with cortical ribboning

Posterior Thalamus MRI Signs: 'Hockey-stick sign' (symmetric hyperintensity of the bilateral dorsomedial thalamus and pulvinar nuclei resembling a hockey stick) and 'Pulvinar sign' (bilateral symmetric hyperintensity of the pulvinar thalamic nuclei brighter than anterior putamen, pathognomonic for variant CJD)
Electroencephalography (EEG): Characteristic periodic sharp wave complexes (PSWCs) occurring at a frequency of 1 to 2 Hz on a slow background, present in >70% of sCJD patients
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology Histopathology: Definitive diagnostic triad of: (1) Spongiform change (fine, microvacuolar spongiform degeneration within the neuropil and neuronal cytoplasm of the cerebral cortex, striatum, and molecular layer of cerebellum); (2) Severe, extensive neuronal loss; (3) Dense reactive gemistocytic and fibrillary astrogliosis; absence of typical inflammatory infiltration

Immunohistochemistry / Western Blot: Abundant deposition of proteinase K-resistant abnormal prion protein (PrPSc) in synaptic, patchy, or perivacuolar patterns; presence of large multicentric amyloid plaques ('florid plaques' encircled by spongiform halos) in variant CJD; real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) ultrasensitive detection of prion seeds
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic fatal human prion encephalopathy combining startle myoclonus and akinetic mutism with pathognomonic DWI 'cortical ribboning' and 'hockey-stick sign' on brain MRI, verified by microscopic spongiform neuropil vacuolation and PrPSc deposits.

topics.name: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Gowers' sign: pathognomonic physical maneuver where child rises from floor to standing position by using hands to sequentially climb up thighs and knees due to profound pelvic girdle weakness
Prominent bilateral pseudohypertrophy of the calf muscles (enlarged, firm, rubbery gastrocnemius and soleus caused by extensive fibrofatty infiltration rather than true muscular hypertrophy)
Waddling, lordotic gait with exaggerated pelvic tilt, compensatory exaggerated lumbar hyperlordosis, and prominent Achilles tendon contractures forcing persistent toe-walking
Progressive symmetric proximal muscle weakness (pelvic girdle before pectoral girdle), loss of independent ambulation typically between ages 9 and 12 years
Wheelchair-bound phase complications: severe rapidly progressive neuromuscular scoliosis, restrictive respiratory insufficiency, and dilated cardiomyopathy
radiological_manifestations: Pelvic and Thigh Muscle MRI (T1-weighted and T2 Dixon): Bilateral, symmetrical, advanced fatty replacement and atrophy of hip extensors and knee muscles (striking involvement of gluteus maximus, adductor magnus, and quadriceps), with relative sparing of the gracilis, sartorius, and semitendinosus muscles ('thigh muscle preservation pattern')

High-Resolution Neuromuscular Ultrasound: Marked, diffuse, homogeneous hyperechogenicity of affected muscle bellies ('ground glass' appearance) with near-complete loss of normal muscular pennate architecture and complete acoustic shadowing of the underlying bone cortex

Cardiac MRI and Echocardiography: Progressive left ventricular dilation and eccentric remodeling, impaired ejection fraction, and characteristic late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) localized to the posterolateral left ventricular subepicardium
Spine Radiography: Rapidly progressive neuromuscular thoracolumbar C-shaped or S-shaped scoliosis with significant pelvic obliquity
pathology_manifestations: Muscle Biopsy Histopathology: Complete absence or profound deficiency of dystrophin protein on sarcolemmal immunohistochemistry and Western blot; marked fiber size variation with rounded atrophic and hypertrophic fibers; frequent hypercontracted ('opaque') degeneration fibers, active myonecrosis with phagocytosis, clusters of regenerating basophilic fibers, and relentless progressive endomysial and perimysial fibrofatty expansion replacing contractile parenchyma
Molecular Genetics: Out-of-frame mutations, deletions (exons 45-55 hotspot), or duplications in the DMD gene on chromosome Xp21.2 leading to complete truncation of dystrophin
topics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal pediatric muscular dystrophy featuring the classic Gowers sign, rubbery calf pseudohypertrophy, and waddling lordosis, validated by sarcolemmal dystrophin absence on histology and posterolateral subepicardial fibrosis on cardiac MRI.

topics.name: Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Facial weakness with transverse/horizontal smile, flat unexpressive facial contour, inability to bury eyelashes, whistle, purse lips, or sip through a straw
Severe, strikingly asymmetrical scapular winging and upward lateral scapular flaring on shoulder abduction, producing prominent trapezoid suprascapular humps and Poly-Hill sign
'Popeye arm' deformity characterized by severe, selective wasting of the biceps and triceps brachii with relative sparing of forearm musculature and deltoid bulk
Pectoralis major muscle atrophy producing a horizontal anterior axillary fold and sunken anterior chest wall
Beevor's sign: striking cephalic (upward) movement of the umbilicus during attempted neck flexion or sit-up caused by selective weakness of lower rectus abdominis muscles
Asymmetric foot drop (weakness of anterior compartment calf muscles) and compensatory lumbar hyperlordosis
radiological_manifestations: Shoulder and Upper Trunk Muscle MRI (T1-weighted and STIR): Highly characteristic, strikingly asymmetric patchy fatty infiltration and severe muscular atrophy involving the trapezius, serratus anterior, latissimus dorsi, and pectoralis major, with remarkable, pathognomonic preservation of deltoid muscles ('deltoid sparing sign')

Pelvis and Lower Extremity Muscle MRI: Asymmetric selective fatty replacement of hamstring muscles (semimembranosus and biceps femoris) and lower leg anterior compartment (tibialis anterior, medial gastrocnemius), with relative sparing of vastus lateralis and quadriceps femoris in early-to-moderate stages
Muscle Ultrasound: Increased echo intensity (fibrofatty replacement) with architectural degradation displaying stark right-to-left asymmetry in periscapular and arm muscles
pathology_manifestations: Muscle Biopsy Histopathology: Dystrophic and myopathic alterations including marked variation in muscle fiber diameter, scattered rounded atrophic fibers, hypertrophied fibers, internal/central nuclei, necrotic and regenerating fibers, and endomysial fibrosis; prominent perivascular and endomysial inflammatory lymphocytic infiltrates (predominantly CD8+ T cells) may be present, frequently mimicking inflammatory myopathy

Molecular Genetics: De-repression and aberrant toxic expression of DUX4 retrogene due to pathogenic contraction of D4Z4 macrosatellite repeat units (1-10 repeat units in FSHD1) on permissive chromosome 4qA (4q35 locus)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Stands out in neuromuscular medicine for instantly recognizable photographic exam signs (transverse smile, scapular winging, Popeye arms, Beevor sign) paired with distinctive asymmetric muscle MRI fatty replacement displaying pathognomonic deltoid sparing.

topics.name: Friedreich Ataxia
clinical_manifestations: Severe progressive sensory and cerebellar ataxia with broad-based uncoordinated gait, positive Romberg sign, and profound loss of vibration and joint position sense
Hallmark skeletal deformities: bilateral high-arched feet (pes cavus) with extensor hammer toes / claw toes, and progressive severe thoracolumbar kyphoscoliosis
Areflexia in lower extremities (loss of patellar and Achilles deep tendon reflexes) coexisting with extensor plantar responses (bilateral Babinski signs)
Ocular motor abnormalities including fixation instability with square-wave jerks and horizontal/vertical gaze-evoked nystagmus
Dysarthria (slow, jerky, scanning speech pattern) and late-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy symptoms (dyspnea, palpitations, heart failure)
radiological_manifestations: Spinal Cord and Brain MRI: Marked, progressive atrophy and anteroposterior thinning of the cervical spinal cord (particularly striking flattening of the posterior and lateral columns), with relative preservation of cerebral hemispheres and late-stage cerebellar vermian and dentate nucleus atrophy

Transthoracic Echocardiography and Cardiac MRI: Concentric or asymmetric septal left ventricular hypertrophy (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy pattern) mimicking HCM, with progressive diastolic dysfunction and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) indicating myocardial replacement fibrosis
Spine Radiography (Plain X-ray): Progressive neuromuscular thoracolumbar scoliosis with Cobb angles frequently exceeding 40-60 degrees requiring surgical stabilization
Foot Radiographs: Severe pes cavus deformity with high calcaneal pitch angle, clawing of metatarsophalangeal joints, and flexion deformities of interphalangeal joints
pathology_manifestations: Central and Peripheral Nervous System Histopathology: Severe degeneration and loss of large myelinated fibers in the posterior columns (fasciculus gracilis and cuneatus), corticospinal tracts, and spinocerebellar tracts of the spinal cord; profound loss of primary sensory pseudounipolar neurons in dorsal root ganglia (DRG) with proliferation of satellite cells (nodules of Nageotte); secondary loss of posterior root fibers

Cardiac Histopathology: Severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with cardiomyocyte enlargement, cellular pleomorphism, extensive diffuse interstitial fibrosis, and focal myocardial iron accumulation on Prussian blue staining due to frataxin deficiency (GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion in FXN gene on chromosome 9q21)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential hereditary neurodegenerative disorder uniting hallmark bedside skeletal signs (pes cavus, hammer toes, severe kyphoscoliosis) with diagnostic cervical spinal cord flattening on MRI, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on echocardiography, and posterior column degeneration on pathology.

topics.name: Huntington's Disease
clinical_manifestations: Chorea: rapid, involuntary, jerky, arrhythmic, dancelike movements flowing unpredictably from one muscle group to another
Motor impersistence (inability to sustain a voluntary action, e.g. 'darting tongue' or 'trombone tongue': inability to maintain tongue protrusion for >20 seconds)
'Milkmaid's grip' (rhythmic fluctuating grip squeezing during physical examination)
Saccadic eye movement dysfunction, paratonia, and dystonic posturing
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI / CT: Marked, bilateral, symmetrical atrophy of the caudate heads and putamen resulting in pathognomonic 'boxcar ventricles' (frontal horns of the lateral ventricles become squared and enlarged); increased bicaudate ratio and intercaudate distance
18F-FDG PET: Profound, bilateral hypometabolism within the caudate nuclei and putamen preceding marked structural volume loss
pathology_manifestations: Brain autopsy: Severe atrophy of the neostriatum (caudate nucleus and putamen) with loss of medium spiny GABAergic neurons (Vonsattel grading system 0-IV); intense reactive fibrillary astrogliosis; intranuclear inclusions of mutant huntingtin protein stained by anti-ubiquitin and anti-huntingtin antibodies
topics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield hereditary neurodegenerative disorder featuring classic involuntary chorea and 'darting tongue' matched with diagnostic caudate head atrophy ('boxcar ventricles') on brain MRI.

topics.name: Hypomelanosis of Ito
clinical_manifestations: Striking cutaneous hypopigmented streaks along Blaschko lines: Congenital or early infantile bizarre, whorled, marbled, reticular, and linear streaks of hypopigmented macules distributed strictly along the lines of Blaschko over the trunk, flanks, and limbs, representing the photographic negative of incontinentia pigmenti; mucous membranes, palms, and soles are characteristically spared
Intractable childhood epilepsy: Severe epileptic seizures (infantile spasms, West syndrome, refractory focal and generalized motor seizures) presenting in the first year of life
Severe developmental delay and cognitive disability: Profound intellectual impairment, global motor delay, and autism spectrum features
Musculoskeletal asymmetries: Marked hemihypertrophy (asymmetric limb overgrowth, leg length discrepancy), facial asymmetry, and progressive severe thoracolumbar scoliosis
Ocular abnormalities: Iris heterochromia, strabismus, microphthalmia, and patchy hypopigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium on fundoscopy
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial and Coronal T1, T2/FLAIR): Hemimegalencephaly (unilateral marked enlargement of an entire cerebral hemisphere), cortical malformations including polymicrogyria, pachygyria, and subcortical heterotopias; asymmetric ventriculomegaly; hypoplasia of the corpus callosum; patchy areas of subcortical white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensity
Skeletal Radiographs: Severe structural scoliosis, long-bone length discrepancy, and asymmetric bony overgrowth of the hypertrophic extremity
pathology_manifestations: Dermatopathology: Full-thickness skin punch biopsy from the hypopigmented macules stained with Fontana-Masson silver stain reveals a marked, quantitative reduction of melanin granules in the basal layer of the epidermis, with normal or slightly decreased numbers of melanocytes, reflecting functional hypomelanosis caused by chromosomal mosaicism; lack of dermal pigment incontinence, melanophages, or dermal inflammation (differentiating it from incontinentia pigmenti)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic neurocutaneous mosaic disorder displaying Blaschko-linear hypopigmented whorls, hemimegalencephaly and polymicrogyria on brain MRI, skeletal hemihypertrophy on radiographs, and basal layer hypomelanin pathology.

topics.name: Inclusion Body Myositis
clinical_manifestations: Distinctive asymmetrical finger flexor weakness and wasting: severe weakness of deep flexors (flexor digitorum profundus > flexor digitorum superficialis and flexor pollicis longus), rendering patients unable to form a tight fist, pinch keys, turn doorknobs, or grasp eating utensils

Severe, strikingly asymmetrical quadriceps femoris wasting and weakness, producing visible anterior thigh hollows ('scooped-out' thighs), frequent sudden knee buckling, and catastrophic falls while descending stairs
Bilateral or asymmetric foot drop caused by preferential involvement of the tibialis anterior muscle
Severe progressive pharyngeal dysphagia: high-esophageal obstruction, choking on solids and pills, and recurrent aspiration pneumonia caused by cricopharyngeal dysfunction
Relative sparing of deltoids, rotator cuff muscles, and hip adductors, contrasting sharply with polymyositis or dermatomyositis
radiological_manifestations: Thigh Muscle MRI (T1-weighted and STIR): Highly specific, asymmetrical fatty infiltration and severe atrophy of the quadriceps femoris (vastus lateralis, vastus intermedius, and vastus medialis), displaying the diagnostic 'rectus femoris sparing sign' (striking preservation or hypertrophic compensation of the rectus femoris relative to the vasti)

Forearm Muscle MRI: Severe, selective fatty degeneration and atrophy of the deep anterior flexor compartment of the forearm (flexor digitorum profundus and flexor pollicis longus), with relative sparing of superficial flexors, extensor compartment, and intrinsic hand musculature

Barium Swallow / Videofluoroscopy: Prominent cricopharyngeal bar (hypertrophied cricopharyngeus failing to open fully), extensive pooling of contrast in pyriform recesses, and tracheobronchial aspiration
pathology_manifestations: Muscle Biopsy Histopathology: Diagnostic triad of: (1) Rimmed vacuoles (multiple small round or oval autophagic vacuoles rimmed by granular basophilic/purplish material on modified Gomori trichrome staining); (2) Endomysial inflammatory infiltrates consisting of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells invading and surrounding non-necrotic muscle fibers expressing MHC class I; (3) Tubulofilamentous inclusions (15-21 nm diameter) within the cytoplasm and nuclei on transmission electron microscopy, with positive immunoreactivity for amyloid-beta, phosphorylated tau, p62, and TDP-43 aggregates
Serology: High specificity for circulating autoantibodies against cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase 1A (anti-cN1A / NT5C1A)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Most common acquired myopathy in patients over 50, featuring bedside deep finger flexor paralysis and scooped-out quadriceps, verified by the pathognomonic 'rectus femoris sparing sign' on thigh MRI and rimmed vacuoles with CD8+ T-cell invasion.

topics.name: Moyamoya Disease
synonyms: spontaneous occlusion of the circle of Willis
clinical_manifestations: Hyperventilation-triggered transient ischemic attacks (TIAs): Classic paroxysms of acute focal neurological deficits (hemiparesis, hemisensory loss, facial droop, dysphasia) provoked by hyperventilation (crying, blowing on hot food, playing wind instruments, vigorous exercise) due to hypocapnia-induced cerebral vasoconstriction superimposed on severe intracranial arterial stenosis

Childhood chorea and involuntary movements: Choreiform, athetoid, or hemiballistic involuntary movements in pediatric patients resulting from chronic basal ganglia hypoperfusion and ischemic irritation of striatal circuitry

Adult-onset intracranial hemorrhage: Sudden severe thunderclap headache, meningismus, vomiting, depressed consciousness, and focal deficits from spontaneous rupture of fragile, dilated, high-pressure basal perforating moyamoya collateral vessels or microaneurysms, presenting as intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), or intraparenchymal lobar hemorrhage

Cognitive impairment and intellectual decline: Progressive insidious decline in executive function, processing speed, memory, and school performance in children, often accompanied by chronic intractable headaches, secondary to persistent global frontal and hemispheric hypoperfusion

Recurrent ischemic strokes and focal seizures: Multifocal ischemic territorial infarctions manifesting as fluctuating motor deficits, recurrent focal motor or secondary generalized seizures, cortical blindness, and microvascular borderzone watershed infarctions
radiological_manifestations: Conventional Digital Subtraction Catheter Cerebral Angiography (Gold Standard): Diagnostic pathognomonic finding of bilateral (or unilateral in moyamoya syndrome) progressive stenosis or occlusion of the terminal supraclinoid internal carotid arteries (ICA) and proximal segments of the anterior (ACA) and middle cerebral arteries (MCA), surrounded by an elaborate, hazy, fine vascular network of dilated lenticulostriate and thalamoperforating collateral anastomoses at the skull base creating the unmistakable appearance of a 'puff of smoke' (Japanese: 'moyamoya'); staged according to Suzuki criteria from stage 1 (narrowing of carotid fork) to stage 6 (complete disappearance of circle of Willis with external carotid collateralization)

Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and MR Angiography (MRA): High-resolution T2/FLAIR demonstrating pathognomonic 'ivy sign' (prominent leptomeningeal high signal intensity along cortical sulci reflecting slow retrograde collateral blood flow through pial anastomoses); multiple flow voids at the basal ganglia and perimesencephalic cisterns on T1/T2; multiple acute and chronic watershed infarctions in deep white matter and borderzones; MRA shows marked flow attenuation/disappearance of terminal ICAs and proximal MCAs/ACAs

Perfusion Imaging (CT Perfusion / Dynamic Susceptibility Contrast MRI / SPECT / PET): Striking hemodynamic compromise characterized by markedly prolonged time to peak (TTP) and mean transit time (MTT), reduced cerebral blood flow (CBF), and exhausted cerebrovascular reserve capacity following acetazolamide (Diamox) challenge, confirming severe vascular steal and tissue at risk
pathology_manifestations: Arterial Histopathology and Genetics: Non-inflammatory, non-atherosclerotic fibrocellular intimal thickening and smooth muscle hyperplasia leading to marked luminal stenosis of the terminal internal carotid arteries; marked tortuosity, fragmentation, disruption, or duplication of the internal elastic lamina; thinning and attenuation of the muscular media with adventitial preservation; prominent proliferation and microaneurysmal dilation of fragile basal perforating collateral vessels with mural microthrombi and fibrinoid degeneration; strong genetic association with loss-of-function or missense variants in the ring finger protein 213 (RNF213) gene, particularly the p.R4810K founder variant in East Asian populations
topics.inclusion_rationale: Iconic cerebrovascular disease marked by hyperventilation-induced TIAs in children and catastrophic intraventricular hemorrhages in adults, defined radiologically by the pathognomonic catheter angiographic 'puff of smoke' basal collaterals and MRI 'ivy sign', underpinned by non-inflammatory intimal fibroplasia and RNF213 genetic mutations.

topics.name: Multiple Sclerosis
clinical_manifestations: Optic neuritis: unilateral painful loss of vision, afferent pupillary defect (Marcus Gunn pupil), swollen or pale optic disc on fundoscopy
Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO): impaired adduction of the ipsilateral eye with horizontal nystagmus of the abducting contralateral eye (damage to medial longitudinal fasciculus)
Lhermitte sign: electric-shock-like sensation shooting down the spine into the limbs upon neck flexion
Uhthoff phenomenon (transient worsening of neurologic symptoms with elevated body temperature)
Spastic paraparesis, intention tremor, scanning speech, and ataxia (Charcot neurologic triad)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Oval/ellipsoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense demyelinating plaques perpendicular to the lateral ventricles ('Dawson's fingers' along medullary veins); juxtacortical, infratentorial (pons/cerebellum), and periventricular lesions; T1 hypointense 'black holes' (permanent axonal loss); active lesions display incomplete 'open-ring' or nodular gadolinium enhancement
Spine MRI: Focal, peripherally located demyelinating lesions spanning <2 vertebral segments in length, occupying <50% of cord cross-section
pathology_manifestations: Brain autopsy / biopsy: Sharply demarcated, hypocellular demyelinating plaques with destruction of myelin sheaths and relative axonal sparing; abundant lipid-laden foamy macrophages (luxol fast blue myelin degradation products), perivenular cuffs of T lymphocytes and B cells, reactive astrogliosis
topics.inclusion_rationale: Core neurologic disorder with physical exam hallmarks (INO, optic disc pallor, Lhermitte sign) matching textbook 'Dawson's fingers' and open-ring enhancing lesions on brain/spine MRI.

topics.name: Multiple System Atrophy
clinical_manifestations: Profound, symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension (blood pressure drop >30 mmHg systolic or >15 mmHg diastolic without compensatory heart rate increase), often causing recurrent syncope
Nocturnal inspiratory stridor (high-pitched, harsh breathing during sleep caused by laryngeal abductor dystonia and vocal cord adductor paralysis), an ominous harbinger of sudden nocturnal death
Antecollis (severe, disproportionate flexion dystonia of the neck / 'dropped head' syndrome)

Severe, poorly levodopa-responsive parkinsonian rigidity and akinesia (MSA-P subtype) or progressive cerebellar ataxia with intention tremor, scanning dysarthria, and wide-based staggering gait (MSA-C subtype)

Disproportionate hand/foot posturing (striatal hands/toes), cold dusky violaceous extremities with impaired peripheral thermoregulation (autonomic circulatory dysfunction), and severe urinary urge incontinence or retention
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial T2 and FLAIR): Pathognomonic 'hot cross bun sign'—a striking cruciform T2 hyperintensity in the pontine tegmentum caused by selective degeneration and gliosis of transverse pontocerebellar fibers and the median pontine raphe

Brain MRI (Axial T2/SWI): 'Putaminal rim sign'—a distinct linear T2-hyperintense rim along the dorsolateral border of the putamen, accompanied by marked putaminal hypointensity (excessive iron deposition) and significant putaminal volume loss in MSA-P

Posterior Fossa MRI: Pronounced atrophy of the middle cerebellar peduncles (MCP) with bilateral T2/FLAIR hyperintensity ('MCP sign'), accompanied by severe olivopontocerebellar atrophy and marked enlargement of the fourth ventricle and prepontine cistern

Cardiovascular Autonomic Testing / 123I-MIBG Myocardial Scintigraphy: Normal or minimally decreased myocardial MIBG uptake (reflecting preserved postganglionic sympathetic fibers, unlike Lewy body Parkinson disease where MIBG uptake is profoundly reduced)
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology Histopathology: Alpha-synucleinopathy characterized by pathognomonic, widespread Glial Cytoplasmic Inclusions (GCIs, also known as Papp-Lantos bodies) located within the cytoplasm of oligodendrocytes, strongly positive for alpha-synuclein and ubiquitin; accompanied by severe neuronal loss, myelin pallor, and dense microglial activation in the striatonigral and olivopontocerebellar networks
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic neurodegenerative synucleinopathy displaying hallmark clinical autonomic collapse, laryngeal stridor, and antecollis, anchored by the iconic 'hot cross bun sign' on pontine MRI and putaminal rim hyperintensity.

topics.name: Myasthenia Gravis
clinical_manifestations: Asymmetric, fatigable ptosis worsening upon sustained upward gaze (>60 seconds)
Diplopia that changes with fatigue
'Myasthenic snarl' (retraction of the corners of the mouth without tooth exposure due to facial muscle weakness)
Dropped head syndrome (weakness of neck extensor muscles)
Bulbar fatigue with chewing and talking (dysphonia, nasal voice), proximal limb weakness
radiological_manifestations: Chest CT / MRI with Contrast: Anterior mediastinal mass demonstrating a thymoma (smooth or lobulated soft-tissue mass, calcification, cystic changes) or diffuse symmetric thymic hyperplasia
Orbit MRI: Useful to rule out structural compressive orbital/cavernous sinus lesions mimicking ocular MG
pathology_manifestations: Thymectomy surgical histology: Thymoma (WHO types A, AB, B1, B2, B3) showing neoplastic epithelial cells admixed with non-neoplastic immature T lymphocytes, or thymic follicular lymphoid hyperplasia with prominent ectopic germinal centers
topics.inclusion_rationale: Textbook neuromuscular disorder with visible fatigable ptosis and the 'myasthenic snarl' paired with diagnostic mediastinal thymoma imaging on chest CT.

topics.name: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease
clinical_manifestations: Severe acute bilateral optic neuritis: Profound decrease in visual acuity accompanied by excruciating orbital pain with eye movements; direct fundoscopy demonstrates marked, florid optic disc edema (papillitis) and peripapillary hemorrhages in >80% of eyes, with rapid steroid responsiveness

Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM)-like presentation: Common in children and adolescents, presenting with fever, encephalopathy, lethargy, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and multifocal cranial nerve palsies

Transverse myelitis and conus syndrome: Flaccid paraparesis, sensory ataxia, saddle anesthesia, early severe neurogenic bladder dysfunction (urinary retention), and erectile dysfunction due to preferential conus medullaris targeting
Steroid dependency and rapid remission: Dramatic, rapid clinical improvement following high-dose corticosteroids, with high risk of rebound relapses during tapering
radiological_manifestations: Orbital MRI (Coronal and Axial T1+Gd with Fat Suppression, T2/STIR): Longitudinally extensive optic nerve hyperintensity involving anterior optic nerve segments with marked swelling; pathognomonic prominent peri-optic nerve sheath and orbital fat enhancement (orbital perineuritis), extending along the sheath

Spine MRI: Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) often involving the lower thoracic cord and conus medullaris; axial T2-weighted MRI demonstrates the pathognomonic 'H-sign' (confined hyperintensity strictly mapped to the central spinal gray matter resembling the letter 'H', sparing surrounding white matter)

Brain MRI: Large, bilateral, hazy, fluffy, cloud-like, poorly demarcated T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions distributed in the deep white matter, brainstem, cerebellar peduncles, and cortical-subcortical junctions; cortical/subcortical FLAIR hyperintense lesions with seizures (FLICE pattern)
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology: Perivenular demyelination mediated by anti-MOG IgG1 autoantibodies targeting the extracellular domain of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein; distinct histopathologic preservation of oligodendrocytes and relative axonal sparing; macrophage-dominated inflammation with CD4+ T-cell infiltration and complement deposition, strictly lacking the astrocytic necrosis, AQP4 loss, and thick perivascular rosettes seen in NMOSD
topics.inclusion_rationale: Distinct antibody-mediated demyelinating syndrome featuring florid optic papillitis, pathognomonic orbital fat/nerve sheath perineuritis and conus spinal 'H-sign' on MRI, and perivenular demyelination with oligodendrocyte preservation on histology.

topics.name: Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1
clinical_manifestations: Distinctive 'hatchet' facies: long, narrow, haggard facial appearance caused by marked bilateral temporalis and masseter muscle wasting, facial diplegia, sagging jaw, and drooping lips
Premature frontal balding (androgenic alopecia) in both men and women, often initiating before age 30
Bilateral, symmetrical ptosis with hollowed temples, nasal speech, and swan-neck deformity of the cervical spine from severe sternocleidomastoid muscle atrophy

Active grip myotonia (dramatic inability to rapidly release hand grip after clenching) and percussion myotonia (percussion of thenar eminence with a reflex hammer elicits persistent abduction/flexion of thumb with slow relaxation)
Ophthalmic hallmark: polychromatic, iridescent 'Christmas tree' cataracts visible on slit-lamp biomicroscopy, and endocrine abnormalities (testicular atrophy, diabetes mellitus, hypogonadism)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial T2 and FLAIR): Highly characteristic, bilateral symmetrical white matter hyperintensities preferentially concentrated in the anterior temporal lobes and poles (a rare and specific distribution), along with diffuse white matter hyperintensities and ventriculomegaly

Lower Extremity Muscle MRI: Selective fatty degeneration and muscular atrophy demonstrating predilection for the anterior compartment of the lower leg (tibialis anterior, extensor digitorum longus) and medial gastrocnemius, with relative preservation of the posterior deep compartment

Chest Radiography and Fluoroscopy: Elevated hemidiaphragm (bilateral or unilateral) due to severe diaphragmatic weakness/myotonia, accompanied by basal atelectasis and chronic alveolar hypoventilation

Electrocardiography and Cardiac MRI: PR interval prolongation (first-degree AV block), intraventricular conduction delays (bundle branch block), and myocardial interstitial fibrosis on late gadolinium enhancement predisposing to sudden cardiac death
pathology_manifestations: Muscle Biopsy Histopathology: Striking, diagnostic profusion of internalized central nuclei forming long chains along the longitudinal axis of fibers (>20-50% of fibers contain central nuclei); severe selective atrophy of type 1 muscle fibers; presence of ring fibers (Ringbinden) with peripheral encircling myofibrils, sarcoplasmic masses, and pyknotic nuclear clumps
