Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic expansion of unstable (CTG)n trinucleotide repeats in the 3'-UTR of the DMPK gene on chromosome 19q13.3 (>50 to thousands of repeats), triggering toxic RNA foci that sequester MBNL1 splicing regulators
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential multisystem trinucleotide repeat disorder displaying the unmistakable 'hatchet' facies, frontal balding, and percussion myotonia, correlated with temporal pole white matter lesions on brain MRI and internal nuclear chains on muscle biopsy.

topics.name: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
clinical_manifestations: Café-au-lait macules: flat, uniform, light-brown patches with smooth borders (>=6 lesions >=5 mm prepubertal or >=15 mm postpubertal)
Axillary and inguinal freckling (Crowe sign)
Multiple cutaneous and subcutaneous neurofibromas (soft, flesh-colored, violaceous dome-shaped papules with 'buttonhole sign')
Plexiform neurofibromas: large, infiltrative, drooping, baggy subcutaneous masses feeling like a 'bag of worms'
Lisch nodules: pigmented, yellow-brown, raised melanocytic iris hamartomas on slit-lamp exam
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Orbit MRI: Optic pathway gliomas (thickening, tortuosity, and hyperintensity of optic nerves and chiasm); focal areas of signal intensity (FASI / unidentified bright objects [UBOs]) on T2/FLAIR in basal ganglia and cerebellum

Spine and Body MRI: Plexiform neurofibromas showing characteristic 'target sign' (central low T2 signal fibrocollagenous tissue rimmed by hyperintense myxoid tissue); dural ectasia with vertebral scalloping
Skeletal Radiographs: Sphenoid wing dysplasia (causing pulsating exophthalmos), congenital anterolateral bowing and pseudarthrosis of the tibia
pathology_manifestations: Neurofibroma biopsy: Benign, unencapsulated nerve sheath tumor composed of wavy Schwann cells with elongated comma-shaped nuclei, fibroblasts, perineurial-like cells, and mast cells embedded in an abundant myxoid and collagenous extracellular matrix
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic phakomatosis with distinct skin findings (café-au-lait, Crowe sign, Lisch nodules, plexiform neurofibromas) matched with MRI optic pathway gliomas and tibial pseudarthrosis on X-ray.

topics.name: Neurofibromatosis Type 2
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and vestibular dysfunction: Progressive, asymmetric hearing loss, tinnitus, and unsteadiness/disequilibrium in young adults (second to third decade) resulting from bilateral vestibulocochlear nerve schwannomas

Ocular abnormalities: Juvenile posterior subcapsular lenticular cataracts (early presenile cataracts) and combined hamartomas of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium (CRHRPE) visible on slit-lamp and dilated fundoscopy
Cutaneous schwannomas: Discrete, slightly raised, intracutaneous or subcutaneous plaque-like or nodular tumors along peripheral nerve courses, often hyperesthetic

Absence of NF1 hallmarks: Diagnostic absence of Lisch iris nodules, rarity or low number (<6) of pale cafe-au-lait macules, and lack of axillary/inguinal freckling (Crowe sign), distinguishing NF2 from NF1
Multiple cranial neuropathies: Facial weakness (CN VII), hoarseness and dysphagia (CN IX/X), and tongue atrophy (CN XII) from non-vestibular cranial nerve schwannomas
radiological_manifestations: Brain Contrast-Enhanced MRI: Pathognomonic bilateral vestibular schwannomas (acoustic neuromas) originating within the internal auditory canals (IAC) with 'ice cream cone' extension into the cerebellopontine angles (CPA), exhibiting intense, heterogeneous gadolinium enhancement and internal cystic changes; multiple intracranial meningiomas presenting as hyperostotic, intensely enhancing extra-axial masses with dural tails

Spine MRI (Sagittal and Axial T1+Gd and T2): Multiple intramedullary ependymomas (particularly in the cervical and upper thoracic cord) with central cystic components and hemosiderin 'cap sign'; multiple intradural extramedullary spinal schwannomas producing classic 'dumbbell' or 'hourglass' expansion through the neural exit foramina
CT of Temporal Bones: Symmetrical funnel-shaped widening and bony erosion of the internal acoustic canals bilaterally
pathology_manifestations: Schwannoma histopathology: Classic biphasic Antoni A and Antoni B architecture: Antoni A consists of dense, compact spindle-shaped cells with elongated nuclei aligned in parallel palisades around eosinophilic fibrillary zones (Verocay bodies); Antoni B consists of loose, hypocellular, microcystic myxoid stroma; strong, uniform, diffuse cytoplasmic and nuclear positivity for S100 and SOX10; molecular pathology demonstrates biallelic inactivating mutations in the NF2 gene on chromosome 22q12.2 encoding the tumor suppressor protein merlin (schwannomin)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic genetic phakomatosis with juvenile posterior subcapsular cataract, pathognomonic bilateral internal auditory canal 'ice cream cone' vestibular schwannomas on MRI, and classic Antoni A/B Verocay body histology.

topics.name: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
clinical_manifestations: Severe acute optic neuritis: Typically bilateral or rapidly sequential unilateral profound vision loss (frequently counting fingers or light perception only), severe ocular retrobulbar pain exacerbated by eye movement, and marked optic disc swelling (papillitis) on direct ophthalmoscopy evolving to chalky white optic atrophy

Area postrema syndrome: Intractable, persistent nausea, projectile vomiting, and continuous hiccups (singultus) lasting days to weeks, refractory to antiemetics, caused by medullary floor inflammation

Acute transverse myelitis: Sudden flaccid paraplegia or quadriplegia with a sharp, well-demarcated sensory level on the trunk, accompanied by painful paroxysmal tonic limb spasms, Lhermitte sign, and acute urinary retention/neurogenic bladder
Relative sparing of cognitive function: Unlike progressive forms of multiple sclerosis, cortical and cognitive functions are preserved in the majority of episodes
radiological_manifestations: Spine MRI (Sagittal and Axial T2/STIR and T1+Gd): Pathognomonic Longitudinally Extensive Transverse Myelitis (LETM) displaying continuous, uninterrupted T2 hyperintensity extending across >=3 contiguous vertebral segments; axial T2 images demonstrate central cord involvement occupying >50% of the cross-sectional spinal cord area, marked cord swelling, and heterogeneous patchy or ring gadolinium enhancement; late scans show central cord cavitation and atrophy

Brain MRI (FLAIR and T1+Gd): Distinctive non-MS lesions localized to aquaporin-4 (AQP4)-rich periependymal regions lining the ventricles: dorsal medulla/area postrema T2 hyperintensity, periaqueductal gray and third ventricle/hypothalamic lesions, and extensive splenium 'bridge-like' corpus callosum hyperintensities; absence of typical MS Dawson fingers

Orbital MRI: Longitudinally extensive T2 hyperintensity and marked gadolinium enhancement of the optic nerve, extending posteriorly into the optic chiasm and optic tracts over >50% of the optic nerve length
pathology_manifestations: CNS histopathology / autopsy: Vasocentric (perivascular) deposition of immunoglobulins (IgG and IgM) and activated complement components (membrane attack complex C9neo) forming characteristic perivascular rosettes around hyalinized vessels; profound, selective destruction of astrocytic foot processes with loss of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) immunoreactivity; secondary demyelination with extensive axonal injury, necrosis, and prominent perivascular infiltrates rich in neutrophils and eosinophils
topics.inclusion_rationale: Definitive neuroimmunologic entity with classic clinical area postrema hiccups/vomiting and profound optic neuritis, pathognomonic >=3 segment longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) on spine MRI, and AQP4 astrocytopathic complement rosette pathology.

topics.name: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus
clinical_manifestations: Classic Hakim-Adams clinical triad: gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and progressive cognitive impairment
Characteristic 'magnetic' gait: slow, wide-based, short-stepped, shuffling gait with feet appearing glued or magnetized to the floor; impaired postural reflexes and difficulty initiating steps
Significant immediate improvement in gait velocity and stride length following large-volume lumbar puncture (Miller Fisher CSF tap test)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI / CT: Marked symmetric ventriculomegaly out of proportion to high-convexity sulcal enlargement; Evans index >0.30; DESH sign (Disproportionately Enlarged Subarachnoid Space Hydrocephalus: tight high-convexity sulci with enlarged sylvian fissures); acute callosal angle (<90 degrees on coronal MRI); bulging of the lateral ventricular third ventricle into the chiasm; periventricular T2/FLAIR transependymal edema
pathology_manifestations: Brain biopsy / post-mortem: Patchy loss and disruption of ependymal lining along ventricular margins, periventricular subcortical interstitial edema, reactive subependymal astrogliosis, and absence of extensive primary cortical neuronal degeneration
topics.inclusion_rationale: Reversible neurological condition featuring the visible shuffling magnetic gait triad confirmed by pathognomonic DESH pattern, acute callosal angle, and Evans index >0.3 on coronal brain MRI.

topics.name: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy
clinical_manifestations: Bilateral, symmetrical, slowly progressive ptosis causing drooping eyelids that obstruct the visual axis, eliciting chronic compensatory contraction of the frontalis muscle (deep horizontal forehead furrows)
Characteristic 'astronomer posture' (retrocollis / head-tilt-back compensation to gaze beneath drooping ptotic eyelids)
Severe progressive pharyngeal dysphagia: early difficulty swallowing dry solid foods, progressing to liquids, with choking episodes, coughing during meals, and frequent nasal regurgitation
Progressive extraocular ophthalmoparesis with restricted upward and lateral gaze, typically without diplopia
Tongue atrophy, furrowing, and weakness with severe difficulty manipulating boluses within the oral cavity, leading to malnutrition, aspiration pneumonia, and weight loss
radiological_manifestations: Videofluoroscopic Swallowing Study (VFSS) / Barium Swallow: Severe pooling and stasis of barium contrast in the valleculae and pyriform sinuses, delayed trigger of pharyngeal swallow, prominent cricopharyngeal bar (achalasia of the upper esophageal sphincter failure to relax), and frequent laryngeal penetration or tracheal aspiration

Head and Neck Muscle MRI (T1-weighted and STIR): Advanced, symmetrical fatty infiltration and severe atrophy of the intrinsic and extrinsic tongue musculature (genioglossus, lingual muscles), pharyngeal constrictors, and masseters, with relative sparing of masticatory temporalis muscles

Pelvis and Thigh Muscle MRI: Late-stage selective fatty replacement in the lower limbs preferentially involving the adductor magnus, semimembranosus, and hamstrings, with relative preservation of rectus femoris
pathology_manifestations: Muscle Biopsy Histopathology and Electron Microscopy: Pathognomonic intranuclear tubulofilamentous inclusions (8.5 nm outer diameter filaments arranged in straight or tangled arrays within muscle fiber nuclei on transmission electron microscopy); light microscopy shows rimmed vacuoles (autophagic vacuoles rimmed by basophilic granular material on modified Gomori trichrome staining), muscle fiber size variation, and endomysial fibrosis

Molecular Genetics: Autosomal dominant or recessive (GCG)7-13 trinucleotide repeat expansion in the PABPN1 gene on chromosome 14q11.2, causing nuclear aggregation of mutant polyadenylate-binding protein nuclear 1
topics.inclusion_rationale: Distinctive late-onset myopathy presenting with the hallmark 'astronomer' tilted-head posture, bilateral ptosis, and cricopharyngeal bar on barium swallow, confirmed by pathognomonic 8.5 nm intranuclear tubulofilamentous inclusions.

topics.name: Pantothenate Kinase-Associated Neurodegeneration
synonyms: neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation type 1
clinical_manifestations: Severe progressive extrapyramidal movement disorder: striking cranial-orofacial dystonia characterized by blepharospasm, grimacing, forceful involuntary tongue protrusion, and severe jaw-opening dystonia that often leads to self-mutilating tongue and lip biting
Severe generalized limb dystonia: fixed equinovarus posturing of the feet, dystonic clenched fists with hyperextension of fingers, torticollis, and opisthotonic posturing of trunk
Progressive parkinsonian rigidity, bradykinesia, freezing of gait, and loss of postural reflexes leading to premature loss of independent walking
Corticospinal tract signs: spasticity, hyperreflexia, and bilateral extensor plantar responses (Babinski signs)
Ophthalmic hallmark: pigmentary retinopathy ('bone-spicule' retinal pigmentation / atypical retinitis pigmentosa) and optic atrophy causing progressive visual field constriction
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial T2-weighted and T2* / Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging SWI): Pathognomonic 'Eye of the Tiger' sign—marked, symmetrical, profound T2 hypointensity (striking signal loss due to massive iron deposition) throughout the globus pallidus, surrounding a well-circumscribed, central oval focus of hyperintensity (representing severe localized tissue necrosis, gliosis, and vacuolation)
Substantia Nigra MRI: Concomitant marked T2 hypointensity in the substantia nigra pars reticulata due to progressive iron accumulation, with sparing of the red nucleus and cerebral cortex

Gradient Echo / Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM): Markedly increased magnetic susceptibility confirming excessive ferrihydrite and non-heme iron load in the medial and lateral globus pallidus
pathology_manifestations: Brain Autopsy Gross Pathology: Striking rust-brown or dark chocolate-brown discoloration of the globus pallidus and substantia nigra caused by massive localized non-heme iron deposition (strongly positive on Perls Prussian blue stain)

Microscopic Histopathology: Abundant swollen, eosinophilic, degenerating axon spheroids (neuroaxonal dystrophy) throughout the pallidonigral system; marked loss of pallidal and nigral neurons accompanied by reactive astrocytic gliosis and macrophage infiltration with iron and ceroid-lipofuscin pigments; caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in PANK2 gene on chromosome 20p13
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic brain iron accumulation disorder featuring dramatic self-mutilating orofacial dystonia and equinovarus posturing, anchored by the pathognomonic MRI 'eye of the tiger' sign and rust-brown pallidonigral iron accumulation.

topics.name: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System
clinical_manifestations: Subacute progressive encephalopathy and intractable headache: Insidious, severe, unrelenting headache refractory to standard analgesics, accompanied by progressive cognitive deterioration, memory impairment, and personality changes in middle-aged adults

Recurrent multifocal cerebrovascular events: Multiple transient ischemic attacks and completed ischemic or hemorrhagic strokes in disparate vascular territories, producing fluctuating hemiparesis, aphasia, visual field cuts, and cerebellar ataxia
Absence of systemic vasculitis signs: Distinct lack of systemic symptoms (no rash, fever, weight loss, arthritis, or peripheral neuropathy) and normal or mildly elevated ESR/CRP
Intractable partial or generalized seizures: Refractory epileptic seizures resulting from cortical microvascular ischemia and leptomeningeal inflammation
radiological_manifestations: Catheter Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA): Classical pathognomonic 'string-of-beads' or 'beading' sign: multifocal, alternating areas of smooth arterial constriction (stenosis) and post-stenotic ectasia/dilatation across small and medium-sized intracranial arteries (anterior, middle, and posterior cerebral branches), associated with abrupt vascular tapering, occlusions, and collateral vessel development

High-Resolution Vessel Wall MRI (HR-VWMRI): Pathognomonic concentric, smooth, circumferential vessel wall thickening and vivid gadolinium enhancement of affected intracranial arterial segments, differentiating vasculitis from the eccentric, irregular enhancement of atherosclerosis or non-enhancing reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (RCVS)

Brain MRI (DWI, T2/FLAIR, SWI, T1+Gd): Multiple bilateral ischemic infarcts of differing ages involving both cortical gray and subcortical white matter territories; punctate microbleeds and superficial siderosis on SWI; linear and nodular leptomeningeal gadolinium enhancement in ~15-20% of cases
pathology_manifestations: Brain and Leptomeningeal Biopsy (Gold Standard): Transmural segmental inflammatory infiltration of small-to-medium-sized leptomeningeal and cortical arteries with destruction and fragmentation of the internal elastic lamina; three recognized histologic subtypes: 1) Granulomatous vasculitis (~60%): epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated Langerhans-type giant cells with vascular wall necrosis; 2) Lymphocytic vasculitis: dense CD3+ T-lymphocyte cuffs; 3) Necrotizing vasculitis: transmural fibrinoid necrosis mimicking polyarteritis nodosa; exclusion of infection, amyloid, and lymphoma
topics.inclusion_rationale: Prototypic isolated neurovascular inflammatory entity presenting with multi-territorial strokes, pathognomonic angiographic arterial 'beading' and vessel-wall MRI enhancement, and transmural elastic lamina granulomatous pathology on brain biopsy.

topics.name: Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
clinical_manifestations: Staring, unblinking facial appearance with widened palpebral fissures, infrequent blinking, and deep vertical/horizontal forehead furrowing ('astonished' or 'reptilian' facies)

Vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, characteristically affecting downward voluntary saccades early and selectively, with preservation of reflexive vertical eye movements during the doll's head maneuver (oculocephalic reflex)
Procerus sign: persistent contraction of the procerus muscle producing transverse wrinkling over the bridge of the nose and a worried/perplexed stare
Early severe postural instability with unexplained, precipitate backward falls within the first year of symptoms ('rocket sign' when attempting to stand)

Severe axial rigidity in extension with prominent retrocollis (neck extension dystonia), dysarthria (growling, spastic-hypokinetic speech), and applause sign (inability to stop clapping after three claps)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Midsagittal T1-weighted): Pathognomonic 'hummingbird sign' (also called 'penguin sign') created by severe selective midbrain tegmental atrophy with concavity of the superior midbrain contour, contrasting against a preserved, rounded pontine base

Brain MRI (Axial T2/T1-weighted): Marked midbrain tegmental atrophy producing the 'Mickey Mouse sign' (or 'morning glory flower sign') due to concavity of the lateral margins of the midbrain tegmentum; midbrain anteroposterior diameter reduced to <14 mm

Quantitative Magnetic Resonance Parkinsonism Index (MRPI): Midbrain area to pons area ratio multiplied by middle cerebellar peduncle (MCP) width to superior cerebellar peduncle (SCP) width ratio (MRPI > 13.5 reliably distinguishes PSP from Parkinson disease and MSA)
Tau-PET and FDG-PET: Symmetrical hyperaccumulation of 4-repeat tau tracers and hypometabolism in the midbrain tegmentum, subthalamic nucleus, thalamus, and medial frontal cortex
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology Histopathology: 4-repeat (4R) tauopathy defined by pathognomonic 'tufted astrocytes' (dense starburst-like radiating arrays of phosphorylated tau-immunoreactive filaments in proximal astrocytic processes) in motor cortex and striatum; globose neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) and neuropil threads in subthalamic nucleus, substantia nigra, globus pallidus, locus coeruleus, and oculomotor motor complex; severe neuronal loss and gliosis in substantia nigra and superior cerebellar peduncle
topics.inclusion_rationale: Exemplar neurodegenerative movement disorder defined clinically by the astonished facies, procerus sign, and downward gaze palsy, paired with the iconic 'hummingbird sign' and 'Mickey Mouse sign' of midbrain atrophy on brain MRI.

topics.name: Septic Cavernous Sinus Thrombosis
clinical_manifestations: Acute toxic febrile onset with severe periorbital and frontal headache: High spiking fevers, chills, severe retro-orbital and frontal cephalalgia, photophobia, and rapidly escalating toxic encephalopathy, typically following a mid-facial furuncle in the 'danger triangle of the face', sphenoid/ethmoid sinusitis, or dental infection

Severe chemosis and progressive proptosis: Striking, dramatic periorbital edema with violaceous discoloration, conjunctival chemosis (conjunctiva swelling and prolapsing between the eyelids), and prominent exophthalmos (proptosis) driven by obstructed venous return through the superior and inferior ophthalmic veins

Complete ophthalmoplegia and ptosis: Early abducens nerve (CN VI) palsy presenting as lateral rectus weakness and diplopia, rapidly followed by complete external and internal ophthalmoplegia involving oculomotor (CN III) and trochlear (CN IV) nerves, producing complete immobility of the eye, profound ptosis, and a dilated, sluggish or unreactive pupil

Trigeminal sensory loss and absent corneal reflex: Hyperesthesia or hypoesthesia in the ophthalmic (V1) and maxillary (V2) distribution of the trigeminal nerve, accompanied by an early loss of the ipsilateral corneal reflex

Rapid contralateral eye involvement: Hallmark pathognomonic progression of the periorbital edema, proptosis, and ophthalmoplegia to the contralateral eye within 24 to 48 hours, transmitted via the circular intercavernous sinuses across the midline
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Brain and Orbit MRI / Magnetic Resonance Venography (MRV): Pathognomonic asymmetric enlargement of the cavernous sinus with non-enhancing intraluminal filling defects (hypointense on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images) representing septic thrombus; pronounced lateral convexity of the normally concave or straight lateral wall of the cavernous sinus; dramatic dilatation, tortuosity, and thrombosis of the superior ophthalmic vein; narrowing or irregular contour of the intracavernous internal carotid artery; associated T2 hyperintensity and mucosal thickening in the adjacent sphenoid and ethmoid air cells

Contrast-Enhanced Orbit and Cranial CT / CT Venography (CTV): Demonstrates non-enhancing low-attenuation filling defects within an expanded cavernous sinus, lateral bulging of the lateral cavernous sinus margin, marked proptosis, marked enlargement of the superior ophthalmic vein, and fat stranding in the retrobulbar orbit, alongside frank opacification of the sphenoid/ethmoid sinuses

Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA): Used when carotico-cavernous fistula or internal carotid artery pseudoaneurysm / narrowing / occlusion is suspected; demonstrates non-filling of the cavernous sinus, delayed transit through the cavernous sinus tributaries, and segmental irregular stenosis or spasm of the cavernous ICA
pathology_manifestations: Vascular Histopathology and Microbiology: Acute suppurative thrombophlebitis within the trabeculated, endothelial-lined venous channels of the cavernous sinus; intraluminal septic thrombus densely packed with fibrin, necrotic debris, degenerate polymorphonuclear neutrophils, and clusters of bacteria; transmural inflammatory infiltration of the dural sinus wall extending into adjacent cranial nerves (CN III, IV, V1, V2, VI); potential adventitial and media necrosis of the internal carotid artery (septic arteritis) predisposing to catastrophic carotid rupture or mycotic aneurysm formation; Staphylococcus aureus is the predominant pathogen (>70% of cases, including methicillin-resistant S. aureus / MRSA), followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus pyogenes, Streptococcus anginosus group, Gram-negative bacilli, and anaerobes
topics.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening neuro-ophthalmologic infection marked by photographic bilateral chemosis, proptosis, and ophthalmoplegia rapidly crossing the midline, matched radiologically by contrast CT/MRI cavernous sinus filling defects and superior ophthalmic vein thrombosis.

topics.name: Spinal Muscular Atrophy
clinical_manifestations: Severe generalized hypotonia in infants ('floppy infant' syndrome) with characteristic 'frog-leg' resting posture of the lower extremities (hips abducted and externally rotated, knees flexed, resting flat against the examination table)

Bell-shaped thoracic deformity: narrow, constricted upper chest wall with flared lower ribs, accompanied by prominent paradoxical (see-saw) abdominal breathing due to severe intercostal muscle paralysis with preserved diaphragmatic strength
Continuous, fine, rippling fasciculations of the tongue, accompanied by progressive tongue atrophy
Profound, symmetric, flaccid proximal muscle weakness (lower limbs affected earlier and more severely than upper limbs) with complete loss of deep tendon reflexes (areflexia)
Alert, expressive, cognitively intact facial appearance ('bright, engaging eyes') contrasting starkly with an immobile, flaccid body; weakness of cry, weak suck, and progressive bulbar palsy
radiological_manifestations: Chest Radiography (Plain X-ray): Pathognomonic 'bell-shaped thorax' characterized by narrow apex, widening of the basal thoracic cage, thin slender ribs ('pencil ribs') due to severe intercostal muscle hypoplasia, and pectus excavatum

Whole-Body and Lower Extremity Muscle MRI: Severe, symmetric, widespread muscular atrophy and advanced fibrofatty replacement of pelvic girdle and thigh musculature (striking fatty degeneration of gluteus maximus, quadriceps, and hamstrings), with characteristic relative preservation of the diaphragm, rectus abdominis, and facial muscles
High-Resolution Spinal Cord Ultrasound and MRI: Marked volumetric thinning and caliber reduction of the cervical and lumbosacral anterior spinal cord, reflecting loss of anterior horn motor columns
Pelvic Radiography: Bilateral paralytic hip subluxation or dislocation and severe progressive neuromuscular C-shaped scoliosis
pathology_manifestations: Skeletal Muscle Biopsy Histopathology: Classic pan-fascicular / large group neurogenic atrophy: entire muscle fascicles are composed of small, rounded, atrophic myofibers with scattered or clustered massively hypertrophic type 1 muscle fibers (compensatory collateral reinnervation); endomysial connective tissue is preserved without active necrosis or inflammatory infiltration

Spinal Cord Neuropathology: Massive, selective loss and ballooning of large alpha-motor neurons in the anterior horns of the spinal cord and motor cranial nerve nuclei (CN VII, IX, X, XII); remaining neurons show central chromatolysis and neurofilament accumulation
Molecular Genetics: Biallelic homozygous deletion or loss-of-function mutation of exon 7 and/or 8 in the SMN1 gene on chromosome 5q13.2, with disease severity modulated by SMN2 copy number
topics.inclusion_rationale: Preeminent pediatric motor neuron disease displaying the unforgettable bell-shaped chest, frog-leg posture, and tongue fasciculations, confirmed by pencil-ribs on chest X-ray, pan-fascicular neurogenic atrophy on biopsy, and SMN1 deletions.

topics.name: Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy
synonyms: X-linked spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy
clinical_manifestations: Prominent perioral and chin fasciculations: rhythmic, involuntary flickering quivering of the chin and perioral muscles, dramatically exacerbated by speech, pursing lips, or swallowing
Marked tongue muscle atrophy with deep longitudinal furrowing ('scrotal tongue') and relentless, coarse, continuous tongue fasciculations
Systemic signs of partial androgen insensitivity in adult males: prominent, often tender, bilateral gynecomastia; testicular atrophy; reduced fertility; and early erectile dysfunction
Postural hand tremor (often fine, fast kinetic and postural tremor mimicking essential tremor) preceding overt proximal muscle weakness by decades
Slowly progressive proximal lower limb weakness (difficulty rising from chairs, climbing stairs), muscle cramping, diminished deep tendon reflexes, and preserved longevity
radiological_manifestations: Head and Neck Muscle MRI (T1-weighted): Advanced, symmetrical fatty infiltration and volumetric atrophy of intrinsic and extrinsic tongue musculature (genioglossus, vertical and longitudinal tongue muscles), producing a hollowed, fatty appearance on axial and coronal views
Pelvic and Thigh Muscle MRI: Symmetrical fatty infiltration and atrophy of the iliopsoas, gluteus maximus, and quadriceps muscles, with relative preservation of pelvic adductors
Spinal Cord and Brainstem MRI: Progressive volumetric thinning and atrophy of the cervical anterior spinal cord and anterior motor nuclei of the lower brainstem (hypoglossal and facial nuclei)
Breast and Scrotal Ultrasound: True gynecomastia with glandular ductal proliferation (subareolar hypoechoic tissue) and bilateral testicular volume reduction
pathology_manifestations: Histopathology of Spinal Cord and Brainstem: Severe, selective loss of lower motor neurons in the anterior horns of the spinal cord and motor cranial nerve nuclei (especially CN VII, IX, X, and XII); surviving motor neurons demonstrate diffuse cytoplasmic and pathognomonic nuclear inclusions containing mutant truncated androgen receptor protein

Skeletal Muscle Biopsy: Neurogenic muscular atrophy characterized by massive grouped atrophy of myofibers (large clusters of small, angulated fibers) interspersed with reinnervated, hypertrophic fibers displaying fiber type grouping and targetoid fibers
Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion (>38 repeats) in exon 1 of the androgen receptor (AR) gene on chromosome Xq12
topics.inclusion_rationale: Unique X-linked motor neuropathy combining lower motor neuron signs (quivering chin, scrotal tongue, fasciculations) with systemic androgen insensitivity (gynecomastia, testicular atrophy) and striking tongue MRI fatty replacement.

topics.name: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3
clinical_manifestations: Characteristic facial appearance: prominent, bulging, staring unblinking eyes with upper eyelid retraction and apparent exophthalmos ('Machado-Joseph staring facies')
Continuous, visible facial, perioral, and lingual fasciculations or undulating myokymia
Progressive cerebellar ataxia with severe broad-based staggering gait, dysmetria, intention tremor, and explosive scanning dysarthria
External ophthalmoplegia: progressive restriction of voluntary saccades, gaze-evoked horizontal and vertical nystagmus, and slow saccadic velocities
Pyramidal and extrapyramidal signs: lower limb spasticity, brisk hyperreflexia, extensor plantar responses (Babinski signs), and prominent dystonic limb posturing (equinovarus foot deformities)
Peripheral amyotrophy with distal wasting and sensory loss in the lower extremities
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Sagittal and Axial T1/T2-weighted): Severe, progressive olivopontocerebellar and brainstem atrophy: striking thinning of the basis pontis, severe atrophy of the superior cerebellar peduncles (SCP) and dentate nuclei, with marked enlargement of the fourth ventricle and prepontine cistern
Diffusion MRI: Microstructural degeneration with increased mean diffusivity and decreased fractional anisotropy in the cerebellar white matter, cerebellar peduncles, and spinocerebellar tracts

Proton MR Spectroscopy (1H-MRS): Significant reduction in N-acetylaspartate/creatine (NAA/Cr) ratio within the pontine tegmentum, cerebellar vermis, and cerebellar hemispheres, signifying neuronal loss
pathology_manifestations: Neuropathology Histopathology: Autosomal dominant polyglutamine (polyQ) neurodegeneration characterized by pathognomonic, widespread ubiquitin- and ataxin-3-positive neuronal intranuclear inclusions (NIIs) within degenerating neurons of the dentate nucleus, substantia nigra, subthalamic nucleus, and motor cranial nerve nuclei (CN III, IV, VI, VII, X, XII); striking loss of neurons in dentate nuclei and anterior horns of the spinal cord, with relative sparing of the inferior olive and Purkinje cells (distinguishing SCA3 from olivopontocerebellar atrophy)
Molecular Genetics: Pathogenic CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion (>60-87 repeats) in exon 10 of the ATXN3 gene on chromosome 14q32.1
topics.inclusion_rationale: Most prevalent autosomal dominant ataxia globally, presenting with the unmistakable staring proptotic facies, facial fasciculations, and severe gait ataxia, supported by marked pontine/superior cerebellar peduncle atrophy on MRI and intranuclear polyQ ataxin-3 inclusions.

topics.name: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Port-wine stain (nevus flammeus): unilateral, flat, pink, dark-red or violaceous vascular birthmark covering the ophthalmic (V1) and maxillary (V2) dermatomes of the trigeminal nerve, including upper eyelid
Congenital buphthalmos ('ox eye': enlarged cornea/globe from infantile glaucoma)
Contralateral focal motor seizures, hemiparesis, and hemianopia
Choroidal hemangioma on ophthalmoscopic exam ('tomato catsup' fundus)
radiological_manifestations: Brain CT (Non-contrast): Pathognomonic gyriform, serpentine, cortical calcification under the leptomeningeal angioma ('tram-track' or 'railroad-track' cortical calcification), ipsilateral calvarial thickening and hyperpneumatization of sinuses
Brain MRI with Contrast: Leptomeningeal capillary-venous angiomatosis with avid pial gadolinium enhancement, ipsilateral cerebral hemiatrophy, enlarged and hypervascular ipsilateral choroid plexus
pathology_manifestations: Brain/meningeal biopsy: Thin-walled, tortuous, dilated, non-neoplastic venous and capillary blood vessels packing the leptomeninges (pia-arachnoid); underlying cerebral cortex shows severe neuronal loss, marked astrogliosis, and extensive pericapillary calcification of cortical layers II and III
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic neurocutaneous disorder pairing the vivid facial port-wine stain and buphthalmos with pathognomonic gyriform 'tram-track' cortical calcifications on brain CT.

topics.name: Susac Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic clinical triad: 1) Subacute encephalopathy (cognitive dysfunction, confusion, severe memory loss, behavioral alterations, paranoia, and severe migraine-like headache); 2) Branch retinal artery occlusions (BRAO) presenting as dark scotomas, visual field cuts, or metamorphopsia; 3) Acute-onset bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, typically asymmetric with low-to-mid frequency loss, accompanied by tinnitus and severe vertigo

Fundoscopic Gass plaques: Direct ophthalmoscopy / fundus photography reveals characteristic small, discrete, yellow-white refractile or non-refractile atheromatous-like plaques (Gass plaques) located in retinal arterioles distant from bifurcations, accompanied by boxcar segmentation and localized retinal pallor/edema

Psychiatric and cognitive disturbances: Fluctuating abulia, confabulation, emotional lability, and catatonic-like states in young female patients, often misattributed to atypical psychosis or primary demyelinating disease
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI (Axial and Sagittal T2/FLAIR, DWI, T1+Gd): Pathognomonic 'snowball' lesions—small (3-7 mm), round, well-demarcated hyperintense lesions with restricted diffusion centered in the central fibers of the corpus callosum with strict sparing of the callosal-septal interface; sagittal T1-weighted images show evolution into 'punched-out' hypointense callosal holes ('Swiss cheese' or 'black holes'); 'spoke-wheel' lesions radiating perpendicularly through the callosum; leptomeningeal enhancement in up to 33% of patients

Retinal Fluorescein Angiography (FFA): Gold standard ophthalmologic modality: reveals multifocal branch retinal artery occlusions, delayed arterial filling, and pathognomonic segmental Arteriolar Wall Hyperfluorescence (AWH) affecting arteriolar segments remote from the actual occlusion sites

Pure Tone Audiometry: Diagnostic bilateral, asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss characteristically affecting the low-to-medium frequencies (250-2000 Hz), reflecting microinfarction of the apical turn of the cochlea
pathology_manifestations: Brain / leptomeningeal histopathology: CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell-mediated autoimmune endotheliopathy directed against endothelial cells of the precapillary arterioles; microvascular endothelial cell swelling, microvascular occlusion, and microinfarcts in the corpus callosum, cerebral white matter, and deep gray matter; absence of transmural necrotizing vasculitis, absence of fibrinoid necrosis, and absence of prominent perivascular lymphocytic cuffs
topics.inclusion_rationale: Visually striking neurovascular triad of encephalopathy, Gass plaques and BRAO, pathognomonic corpus callosum 'snowball' and 'punched-out hole' lesions on MRI, and diagnostic fluorescein arteriolar wall hyperfluorescence.

topics.name: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
clinical_manifestations: Hypomelanotic macules: polygonal or lanceolate ash-leaf spots (>=3 lesions highlighted by Wood's lamp) and confetti macules
Facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum): symmetrical, red-brown, telangiectatic papules over the nose, nasolabial folds, and cheeks in a butterfly distribution
Shagreen patch: leathery, pebbled, flesh-colored plaque (connective tissue nevus) on lumbosacral region
Periungual and subungual fibromas (Koenen tumors): smooth, firm nodules arising from nail folds
Dental enamel pits and gingival fibromas
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI / CT: Cortical and subcortical tubers (flair hyperintense widened gyri); subependymal nodules (calcified 'candle guttering' lining the ventricles on CT); Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytoma (SEGA: avidly enhancing mass at the Foramen of Monro causing hydrocephalus)
Abdominal CT / MRI: Multiple bilateral renal angiomyolipomas (AMLs) containing macroscopic fat density (<-20 HU)
Chest HRCT: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (thin-walled cystic lung disease in females)
Echocardiography: Cardiac rhabdomyomas (intracardiac tumors projecting into ventricles)
pathology_manifestations: Tissue biopsy: Cortical tubers display disordered cortical lamination, bizarre multinucleated giant cells, and balloon cells; angiofibromas display dermal vascular proliferation with perivascular fibrosis; renal AMLs exhibit triphasic histology (mature adipose tissue, thick-walled dysplastic blood vessels, and smooth muscle spindles)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Renowned visual triad (epilepsy, adenoma sebaceum, intellectual disability) with ash-leaf spots, Koenen tumors, and shagreen patches paired with ventricular 'candle-guttering' nodules, SEGA, and renal AMLs on imaging.

topics.name: Von Hippel-Lindau Disease
clinical_manifestations: Retinal capillary hemangioblastomas (von Hippel angiomas): Direct fundoscopy and color fundus photography demonstrate bright reddish-orange or pink spherical vascular lesions located in the peripheral or peripapillary retina, supplied by a conspicuously dilated, tortuous retinal feeder artery and drained by an engorged, tortuous vein, frequently surrounded by hard lipid exudates and macular star formation

Polycythemic ruddy cyanosis / plethora: Striking facial rubor, flushing, and conjunctival suffusion caused by secondary polycythemia resulting from tumor-driven ectopic erythropoietin (EPO) secretion by renal cell carcinomas or cerebellar hemangioblastomas

Pheochromocytoma paroxysms: Episodic severe hypertension accompanied by the classic symptomatic triad of profuse diaphoresis, headache, and episodic pallor/flushing, with postural orthostatic hypotension

Cerebellar and vestibular signs: Subacute truncal ataxia, appendicular intention tremor, dysmetria, past-pointing, and coarse horizontal/gaze-evoked nystagmus resulting from posterior fossa hemangioblastomas and obstructive hydrocephalus
Palpable scrotal or epididymal masses: Painless, firm, nodular scrotal swellings due to papillary cystadenomas of the epididymis in males or broad ligament cystadenomas in females
radiological_manifestations: Brain and Spinal Cord Contrast-Enhanced MRI: Pathognomonic hemangioblastomas appearing as well-demarcated cystic lesions with an intensely enhancing, vascular mural nodule abutting the pial surface; prominent serpiginous flow voids from dilated feeding vessels; characteristic predilection for the cerebellar hemispheres, vermis, medulla, and dorsal spinal cord; avid nodular enhancement on post-gadolinium T1-weighted images with high T2 signal in surrounding cystic fluid

Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT and MRI: Multicentric bilateral clear cell renal cell carcinomas (RCC) manifesting as heterogeneous enhancing cortical lesions with necrotic cystic components; innumerable simple pancreatic cysts, serous microcystic cystadenomas, and hypervascular pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNET); bilateral adrenal pheochromocytomas with intense arterial phase enhancement, heterogeneous central necrosis, and delayed wash-out

Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Immediate, intense hyperfluorescence of retinal capillary hemangioblastomas in the early arterial phase with late profuse fluorescein leakage into the vitreous and surrounding subretinal exudation
pathology_manifestations: Hemangioblastoma histopathology: Highly vascular neoplasm composed of an intricate meshwork of thin-walled, arborizing capillary blood vessels lined by normal endothelial cells, interspersed with abundant, distinctive vacuolated stromal cells containing lipid-rich, clear, lipid-laden cytoplasm; immunohistochemistry shows positive staining for inhibin-A, S100, neuron-specific enolase (NSE), and carbonic anhydrase IX (CA-IX); genetic confirmation demonstrates germline loss-of-function mutation or deletion of the VHL tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 3p25-26
topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic multi-system phakomatosis combining unmistakable fundoscopic retinal angiomas and polycythemic facies with pathognomonic MRI cystic lesions with enhancing mural nodules, abdominal CT renal cell carcinomas and pheochromocytomas, and characteristic lipid-laden stromal pathology.

topics.name: Wilson's Disease
clinical_manifestations: Kayser-Fleischer (KF) rings: golden-brown or greenish copper rings at the periphery of the cornea in Descemet's membrane on slit-lamp biomicroscopy
Sunflower cataracts (anterior subcapsular copper deposition)
Facial dystonia creating an involuntary fixed vacant smile ('risus sardonicus')
'Wing-beating' tremor (coarse, slow, high-amplitude postural tremor upon arm abduction)
Dysarthria, dystonia, choreoathetosis, and parkinsonian rigidity
Stigmata of chronic liver disease (spider angiomas, palmar erythema, jaundice)
radiological_manifestations: Brain MRI: Pathognomonic 'face of the giant panda' sign in the midbrain (normal red nuclei as 'eyes', normal substantia nigra as 'ears', and hypointense superior colliculus as 'chin' set against hyperintense tegmentum on T2); 'face of the miniature panda' in the pons; bilateral symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in lentiform and caudate nuclei, thalami, and brainstem
Abdominal Ultrasound / MRI: Micronodular or macronodular cirrhosis, splenomegaly, ascites
pathology_manifestations: Liver needle biopsy: Steatosis, glycogenated nuclei, chronic active hepatitis progressing to micronodular cirrhosis; marked elevation of hepatic copper concentration (>250 ug/g dry weight); rhodanine or rubeanic acid staining demonstrates coarse copper granules in periportal hepatocytes
topics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield neuro-metabolic entity with the unmistakable corneal Kayser-Fleischer ring paired with the textbook 'face of the giant panda' sign on brain MRI.

topics.name: Age-Related Macular Degeneration
clinical_manifestations: Progressive distortion of central vision (metamorphopsia, best detected on Amsler grid), central scotoma, and loss of reading vision in elderly patients

Dry (Non-neovascular) AMD: Funduscopy reveals soft, confluent, yellowish-white drusen at the macula, pigmentary changes, progressing to sharply demarcated, scalloped patches of geographic atrophy of the RPE exposing underlying large choroidal vessels

Wet (Neovascular) AMD: Sudden, rapid deterioration of central vision; funduscopic exam reveals a grayish-green elevated choroidal neovascular membrane (CNVM), subretinal or intraretinal hemorrhage, lipid/hard exudates, and exudative retinal elevation progressing to a dense, elevated fibrotic disciform scar
radiological_manifestations: Spectral-Domain OCT (SD-OCT): Subretinal fluid (SRF) and intraretinal cystoid fluid (IRF); pigment epithelial detachment (PED: serous, drusenoid, or fibrovascular); hyperreflective material in subretinal or sub-RPE spaces corresponding to CNVM; in geographic atrophy: complete loss of RPE and outer retinal layers with pathognomonic hypertransmission ('choroidal light show') into deep choroid

OCT Angiography (OCTA): High-resolution depth-resolved flow visualization of the abnormal choroidal vascular network in the choriocapillaris or outer retina (Type 1 sub-RPE 'sea-fan' or Type 2 subretinal 'glomerular/medusa' CNVM)

Fluorescein Angiography (FA) and Indocyanine Green Angiography (ICGA): Classic lacy early hyperfluorescence with progressive, intense late fluorescein leakage; occult CNVM with ill-defined stippled leakage; ICGA highlights polypoidal lesions and feeder vessels
pathology_manifestations: Macular Histopathology: Thickening and calcification of Bruch membrane with basal laminar and basal linear deposits; drusen composed of lipids, complement components (C3, C5b-9), amyloid-beta, and vitronectin; choriocapillaris atrophy; in neovascular AMD, capillary ingrowth from choriocapillaris breaks through Bruch membrane into sub-RPE/subretinal spaces with fibrovascular proliferation, myofibroblastic transformation, and dense disciform collagen scarring
topics.inclusion_rationale: Leading cause of blindness in elderly populations displaying unmistakable funduscopic soft drusen and subretinal hemorrhages, paired with multi-modal SD-OCT/OCTA choroidal neovascular network mapping.

topics.name: Aniridia
clinical_manifestations: Near-total or complete bilateral absence of the iris, appearing clinically as a massive, fully dilated black pupil occupying the entire anterior chamber diameter
Congenital pendular nystagmus, marked photophobia, and reduced visual acuity (typically 20/100 to 20/200) from foveal hypoplasia
Progressive Aniridic Keratopathy: Corneal limbal stem cell deficiency (LSCD) causing conjunctivalization, superficial corneal vascular pannus, chronic epithelial defects, and corneal opacification
Secondary Glaucoma (in 50-75% of patients) developing in late childhood/adolescence; early developmental cataract and ectopia lentis
WAGR Syndrome: Wilms tumor, Aniridia, Genitourinary anomalies, and intellectual disability
radiological_manifestations: High-Frequency Ultrasound Biomicroscopy (UBM) and Anterior Segment OCT (AS-OCT): Demonstrates the hidden, rudimentary, hypoplastic iris stump situated behind the corneoscleral limbus; progressive anterior rotation and synechial adherence of the rudimentary iris stump to the trabecular meshwork, causing secondary angle closure glaucoma

Spectral-Domain OCT (SD-OCT): Pathognomonic foveal hypoplasia: complete absence of the normal foveal pit/depression, persistent continuity of inner retinal layers across the center of the macula, and absence of photoreceptor outer segment elongation
Surveillance Abdominal Ultrasound and MRI (in WAGR / 11p13 deletion): Routine Q3-month screening for pediatric Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma) and genitourinary anomalies
pathology_manifestations: Ocular Histopathology: Arrest of neuroectodermal optic cup and neural crest mesenchymal migration during week 12 of embryogenesis; hypoplastic iris root remnant containing rudimentary stromal collagen and sparse sphincter muscle fibers; fovea reveals multi-layered ganglion cells across the foveola with absent rod-free zone

Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous mutations or haploinsufficiency of the master ocular transcription factor PAX6 on chromosome 11p13; contiguous gene deletion involving PAX6 and adjacent WT1 causes WAGR syndrome
topics.inclusion_rationale: Cardinal ocular genetic disorder featuring bedside black-iris absence, aniridic keratopathy, AS-OCT visualization of the hidden iris stump, and SD-OCT foveal hypoplasia.

topics.name: Central Serous Chorioretinopathy
clinical_manifestations: Idiopathic retinal disease characterized by serous detachment of the neurosensory retina at the macula, representing the prototypical pachychoroid spectrum disease; strongly predisposed to young and middle-aged adults (20-50 years, male-to-female ratio 6:1)

Strong clinical triggers: Exogenous corticosteroid use (any route: systemic, topical, inhaled, nasal spray, or intra-articular), elevated endogenous glucocorticoids (Cushing syndrome, pregnancy), intense emotional stress, type A personality traits, obstructive sleep apnea, and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor use

Patients present with sudden, painless, unilateral central visual blurring, micropsia (perceiving objects as smaller than actual size due to photoreceptor separation), metamorphopsia (straight lines appearing distorted on Amsler grid testing), central relative scotoma, delayed dark adaptation/recovery after photostress, and washed-out color saturation (dyschromatopsia)

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Hallmark: A well-demarcated, smooth, transparent, dome-shaped, blister-like circular or oval elevation of the neurosensory retina over the fovea/macular region, with loss of the crisp foveal light reflex

Associated Funduscopic Signs: Tiny yellowish-white subretinal fibrin deposits or subretinal lipid precipitants at the base of the detachment; one or more small, discreet, yellowish-orange elevations corresponding to focal pigment epithelial detachments (PEDs); in chronic cases, gravitation tracks ('guttering' or drip tracks) of RPE atrophic depigmentation extending downward from the macula toward the inferior retinal periphery
radiological_manifestations: Fluorescein Angiography (FA) Classic Pathognomonic Patterns: 1) 'Smoke-Stack' Phenomenon (~10-15% of cases): in early phases, a focal pinpoint hyperfluorescent leak at the RPE level appears, and as transit progresses, fluorescein ascends vertically in a thin stream (due to convection currents from protein gradients) before expanding laterally at the superior border of the detachment into an umbrella or mushroom shape; 2) 'Ink-Blot' / Expansile Dot Pattern (~80-90% of cases): focal pinpoint hyperfluorescent leak in early arteriovenous phases that gradually increases in size and intensity, symmetrically expanding radially to fill the entire serous subretinal space in late phases

Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Gold-standard cross-sectional diagnostic imaging: shows an optically clear, hypo-reflective space separating the elevated neurosensory retina from the underlying flat or minimally irregular RPE; elongation, swelling, and granular hyperreflectivity of outer photoreceptor segments ('shaggy' photoreceptors / photoreceptor outer segment elongation) due to lack of physiologic phagocytosis by detached RPE; small focal dome-shaped pigment epithelial detachments (PEDs) and hyperreflective subretinal fibrinous clumps

Enhanced-Depth Imaging OCT (EDI-OCT) & Swept-Source OCT (SS-OCT) Pachychoroid Features: Marked, diffuse thickening of the choroid beneath the detachment (subfoveal choroidal thickness often > 400-500 µm, compared to normal ~250 µm), accompanied by pathognomonic 'pachyvessels' (abnormally dilated, engorged outer choroidal venous channels in Haller's layer) with mechanical compression and thinning of the overlying Sattler's layer and choriocapillaris

Indocyanine Green Angiography (ICGA): Visualizes the primary choroidal pathophysiologic locus: early hypercyanescence with multifocal choroidal vascular hyperpermeability and delayed choroidal filling, mid-phase diffuse hyperfluorescent choroidal flush ('plumes' of leakage), and late hypofluorescent washout

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Acute subretinal fluid produces a masking effect with hypoautofluorescence, but as photoreceptors shed outer segments, accumulating fluorophores yield punctate hyperautofluorescence; chronic gravitation tracks display linear tracts of hypoautofluorescence with hyperautofluorescent margins
pathology_manifestations: Cellular and Hemodynamic Pathophysiology: Primary choroidal vascular hyperperfusion and choriocapillaris endothelial hyperpermeability mediated by excessive mineralocorticoid and glucocorticoid receptor activation; hydrostatic choroidal overload leads to focal breakdown and rupture of the tight junctions (zonula occludens) of the retinal pigment epithelium (the outer blood-retinal barrier), allowing proteinaceous choroidal fluid to escape into the subretinal space

Histopathology: Serous neurosensory retinal detachment without full-thickness retinal tears; accumulation of eosinophilic, protein-rich exudative fluid between the photoreceptor outer segments and the RPE; degenerative swelling, vacuolization, and elongation of photoreceptor outer segments; localized areas of RPE cell atrophy, RPE hyperplasia, and focal micro-dehiscences in the basement membrane of the RPE / Bruch's membrane; absent choroidal or retinal inflammatory cellular infiltrates (distinguishing it from inflammatory uveitis)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential pachychoroid retinal condition in young/middle-aged adults triggered by corticosteroids, displaying pathognomonic 'smoke-stack' leakage on FA, pachychoroid pachyvessels on EDI-OCT, and outer blood-retinal barrier breach.

topics.name: Coats' Disease
clinical_manifestations: Idiopathic, non-familial condition occurring predominantly in young males (peak presentation 6-8 years of age), presenting with unilateral leukocoria (white pupillary reflex), strabismus, or failing vision

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Findings: Massive yellowish-golden intraretinal and subretinal lipoprotein exudation ('exudative retinitis'), frequently forming a dense circinate lipid ring around the macula
Striking retinal vascular abnormalities: localized telangiectasias, aneurysmal tortuosity, and saccular dilatations ('lightbulb' aneurysms) located primarily in the retinal periphery and midperiphery
Bullous exudative (serous) retinal detachment without retinal breaks; cholesterol crystal deposits glittering within subretinal fluid
radiological_manifestations: Orbit Contrast-Enhanced CT: Subretinal exudate appears hyperdense relative to vitreous, with ABSENCE of intraocular calcification (the critical radiological feature differentiating Coats' disease from retinoblastoma!)

Orbit MRI: Subretinal fluid/exudate is hyperintense on both T1- and T2-weighted images (due to high protein and cholesterol content); linear contrast enhancement of the detached retina and abnormal telangiectatic retinal vessels; absence of solid enhancing tumor mass

Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Immediate hyperfluorescence of telangiectasias and aneurysmal saccular dilatations ('lightbulbs') in early phases, widespread capillary nonperfusion (ischemic zones), and massive progressive dye leakage in late phases
pathology_manifestations: Retinal Histopathology: Breakdown of the inner blood-retinal barrier due to loss of endothelial tight junctions and pericyte degeneration; dilated, thin-walled, aneurysmal retinal vessels with mural hyalinization and thrombosis; massive subretinal accumulation of proteinaceous fluid containing bipyramidal cholesterol crystals, lipid-laden foamy histiocytes (macrophages), and hemosiderin; complete absence of malignant neuroblastic cells
topics.inclusion_rationale: Essential pediatric ocular condition presenting with leukocoria and lightbulb aneurysms, where lack of CT calcification distinguishes it from retinoblastoma.

topics.name: Cytomegalovirus Retinitis
clinical_manifestations: Severe, sight-threatening opportunistic ocular infection occurring almost exclusively in profoundly immunocompromised individuals (HIV/AIDS with CD4+ T-cell count < 50 cells/uL, allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell or solid organ transplant recipients, or patients receiving potent immunosuppressive therapy)

Patients present with painless progressive visual blurring, expanding dark scotomas, sudden showers of floaters, and photopsias; may be asymptomatic initially if the peripheral retina is involved before extending into the macula or optic nerve

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Appearance: Classic 'pizza-pie' or 'cottage cheese and ketchup' retinopathy: extensive, dense, granular, yellowish-white full-thickness necrotizing retinal infiltrate with confluent, jagged superficial retinal flame hemorrhages and intraretinal blot hemorrhages distributed along retinal vascular arcades

Distinct clinical morphologic variants: 1) Fulminant / edematous / hemorrhagic pattern (classic pizza-pie appearance along arcades with massive hemorrhage and retinal edema); 2) Granular / indolent / brushfire pattern (peripherally located granular white infiltrate with minimal hemorrhage, expanding centrifugally with an active leading border leaving behind a thin, atrophic, scarred, hypocellular retina with granular RPE hyperpigmentation); 3) Frosted branch angiitis variant (severe perivascular sheathing resembling frosted tree branches)

Minimal to mild vitreous inflammation (vitritis) and anterior uveitis due to profound host immunosuppression ('quiet vitreous' compared to the intense vitritis seen in toxoplasmosis or acute retinal necrosis); late-stage complication of high-incidence rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) occurring through ragged necrotic atrophic retinal breaks (up to 30-50% of untreated eyes)
radiological_manifestations: Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Acute active phase reveals marked full-thickness retinal hyperreflectivity and architectural disorganization, prominent inner and outer retinal edema, hyperreflective intraretinal dots, and optical shadowing of the underlying choroid; chronic resolving phase reveals dramatic full-thickness retinal thinning, loss of all normal retinal laminae, necrotic retinal cavitations, and vitreoretinal traction bands predisposing to rhegmatogenous tears

Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Early phases show hypofluorescence corresponding to blockage from retinal hemorrhages and dense opaque necrotic retina; late phases demonstrate striking granular hyperfluorescence along the active advancing 'brushfire' border due to vascular leakage and capillary breakdown; retinal vascular staining and extensive capillary non-perfusion in ischemic necrotic zones

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Active leading edge exhibits prominent hyperautofluorescence reflecting intense lipofuscin accumulation from damaged photoreceptors and RPE cell stress; burned-out necrotic atrophic zones exhibit profound hypoautofluorescence due to complete RPE and photoreceptor cell death

B-Scan Ocular Ultrasonography: Indicated when media opacities or severe vitritis/cataract obscure direct visualization; demonstrates low-to-medium amplitude vitreous mobile echoes, focal retinochoroidal thickening at necrotizing sites, posterior vitreous detachment, and evaluates for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
pathology_manifestations: Retinal Histopathology: Coagulative, full-thickness cytolytic retinal necrosis with abrupt transition between completely necrotic retina and adjacent structurally preserved retina; extensive disruption of the internal limiting membrane, photoreceptor layer, and retinal pigment epithelium

Pathognomonic Cytomegalic Cells: Marked cytomegaly (cells enlarged up to 2-4 times normal size) with prominent, large, basophilic or amphophilic intranuclear inclusion bodies surrounded by a clear halo, imparting the classic 'owl's eye' appearance; granular, small, basophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions within retinal neurons, glial cells, and retinal vascular endothelial cells

Immunohistochemistry and Molecular Diagnostics: Strong cytoplasmic and nuclear immunoreactivity for CMV immediate-early (IE-1) and tegument (pp65) antigens; quantitative real-time PCR of aqueous humor or vitreous biopsy fluid demonstrates high viral copy loads of CMV DNA
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential opportunistic ocular infection in profound AIDS/immunosuppression characterized by pathognomonic 'pizza-pie' funduscopic retinopathy, full-thickness necrosis on SD-OCT, and pathognomonic cytomegalic 'owl's eye' viral inclusion pathology.

topics.name: Duane Retraction Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic retraction of the globe into the orbit on attempted adduction, accompanied by immediate narrowing of the palpebral fissure (pseudoptosis)
Widening of the palpebral fissure on attempted abduction
Frequent dramatic 'upshoot' or 'downshoot' of the adducted eye during vertical movement (bridle phenomenon / leaping eye)

Motility subtypes: Type 1 (most common, ~70%): marked limitation or complete absence of abduction with normal or slightly restricted adduction; Type 2: marked limitation of adduction with normal or slightly restricted abduction; Type 3: marked limitation of both abduction and adduction
Compensatory head turn (face turn) toward the side of the affected eye to maintain binocular single vision and prevent diplopia
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Contrast-Enhanced 3T Orbit and Brainstem MRI (thin-slice heavily T2-weighted CISS / FIESTA sequences): Pathognomonic complete absence (aplasia) or severe hypoplasia of the abducens nerve (CN VI) within the prepontine cistern and Dorello canal on the affected side

Paradoxical Innervation Imaging: Aberrant branches arising from the inferior division of the oculomotor nerve (CN III) entering the lateral rectus muscle belly; asymmetric hypoplasia and mild fibrous volume loss of the lateral rectus muscle compared to the contralateral normal eye
pathology_manifestations: Congenital Cranial Dysinnervation Disorder (CCDD): Primary developmental failure of abducens motor neurons in the abducens nucleus in the pons; secondary aberrant miswiring of oculomotor nerve axons to the lateral rectus muscle
Co-contraction phenomenon: Simultaneous firing of both the medial rectus and lateral rectus muscles during attempted adduction causes massive mechanical retraction of the globe into the orbital apex
Molecular Genetics: Heterozygous mutations in CHN1 (chimerin 1) in familial DRS, or SALL4 in Duane-radial ray syndrome (Okihiro syndrome)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential CCDD where globe retraction and palpebral fissure narrowing on adduction provide an immediate photographic exam finding matched with high-resolution 3T MRI demonstration of absent CN VI and paradoxical CN III innervation.

topics.name: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Papilledema)
synonyms: papilledema secondary to raised intracranial pressure
clinical_manifestations: Elevated intracranial pressure (ICP > 25 cm H2O on lumbar puncture in adults) of unknown etiology, overwhelmingly occurring in obese women of childbearing age (female-to-male ratio 8:1); strongly associated with rapid weight gain, hypervitaminosis A/retinoids, tetracycline antibiotics, and sleep apnea

Patients present with daily, severe, throbbing or holocephalic headaches (often worse in the morning or with Valsalva), pulse-synchronous tinnitus (rhythmic 'whooshing' sound in ears), and transient visual obscurations (TVOs: fleeting episodes of monocular or binocular vision graying out lasting seconds, typically triggered by bending or standing)

False-localizing Sixth Cranial Nerve (Abducens / CN VI) Palsy: Horizontal binocular diplopia worsening on lateral gaze due to mechanical stretching of the long, angulated intracranial course of the abducens nerve over Dorello's canal / petrous ridge

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Hallmark: Bilateral, symmetrical, severe optic disc swelling (Papilledema, Frisen staging grades 1 to 5): hyperemic swollen optic nerve heads with indistinct blurred margins, obliteration of the optic cup, elevation of the disc surface into the vitreous, and obscuration of major retinal vessels as they cross the disc margin

Specific Peripapillary Funduscopic Signs: Paton's lines (circumferential concentric retinal nerve fiber wrinkles and choroidal folds curving around the temporal disc border), radial retinal lines, flame-shaped peripapillary splinter hemorrhages, cotton-wool spots, and complete absence of spontaneous venous pulsations (SVP); central visual acuity remains preserved early, while perimetry reveals blind spot enlargement and progressive inferonasal visual field loss
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Brain and Orbit MRI (with Fat Suppression & Contrast) Pathognomonic Imaging Tetrad: 1) Partially empty or empty sella turcica (downward herniation of the suprasellar arachnoid space flattening the pituitary gland against the sellar floor); 2) Flattening of the posterior ocular globe / posterior sclera; 3) Prominent enlargement and distension of the perioptic subarachnoid space (increased optic nerve sheath diameter > 5.5-6.0 mm) with vertical tortuosity and kinking of the intraorbital optic nerve; 4) Intraocular protrusion / elevation of the optic nerve head into the vitreous cavity; lack of intracranial mass, ventricular enlargement, or dural enhancement
Magnetic Resonance Venography (MRV) / CT Venography (CTV): Demonstrates bilateral smooth, focal stenoses of the distal transverse cerebral venous sinuses (transverse sinus stenosis / TSS)

Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Quantitatively tracks papilledema: demonstrates marked, circumferential thickening of the peripapillary Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer (pRNFL) and total retinal volume, dome-shaped elevated contour of the optic disc, inward protrusion of Bruch's membrane / lamina cribrosa angle, and peripapillary subretinal fluid; in chronic untreated stages, progression to profound pRNFL thinning reflects optic nerve atrophy

B-Scan Ocular Ultrasonography: Demonstrates optic disc elevation, optic nerve sheath enlargement, and a positive '30-degree test' (decrease in optic nerve sheath diameter by >10% when gaze shifts 30 degrees away from primary position, confirming fluid distension within the subarachnoid sheath), with absence of optic disc calcification (ruling out optic disc drusen)
pathology_manifestations: Optic Nerve Pathophysiology: Transmission of markedly elevated cerebrospinal fluid hydrostatic pressure along the continuous subarachnoid space of the optic nerve sheath to the retrobulbar optic nerve; elevated pressure at the rigid scleral lamina cribrosa mechanically blocks both fast and slow axoplasmic transport in unmyelinated axons of retinal ganglion cells

Histopathology of Papilledema: Marked intracellular axoplasmic stasis and swelling of unmyelinated nerve fibers (cytoid bodies) in the prelaminar portion of the optic nerve head; compression of capillary microcirculation and peripapillary venous stasis with secondary extravasation of serous fluid and flame-shaped microhemorrhages; chronic pathology leads to irreversible loss of retinal ganglion cell axons, fibrous astrocytic proliferation (gliosis), and secondary optic disc pallor/atrophy

Sellar Histopathology: Herniation of the arachnoid membrane through an incompetent diaphragma sellae, leading to compression and thinning of the anterior pituitary parenchyma without adenomatous or neoplastic transformation
topics.inclusion_rationale: Quintessential neuro-ophthalmic disorder in young overweight females featuring pathognomonic bilateral papilledema with Paton lines, MRI empty sella and perioptic nerve distension, and axoplasmic stasis pathology.

topics.name: Keratoconus
clinical_manifestations: Progressive bilateral (often asymmetric) visual blurring, monocular polyopia, and rapid progression of irregular myopic astigmatism

Slit-Lamp Biomicroscopy Hallmark Signs: Fleischer Ring (partial or complete golden-brown ring of iron deposition in basal corneal epithelial cells encircling the cone base); Vogt Striae (fine, vertical stress lines in posterior stroma/Descemet membrane that disappear with gentle digital globe pressure)
Munson Sign: V-shaped conical indentation of the lower eyelid margin induced by the ectatic cornea on downgaze
Charleux Oil Droplet Sign on retroillumination; Acute Corneal Hydrops (sudden, painful profound stromal edema and visual drop due to spontaneous rupture of Descemet membrane)
radiological_manifestations: Scheimpflug Corneal Tomography (Pentacam / Sirius): Pathognomonic localized steepening with apex keratometry (Kmax >48-50 D), asymmetric bowtie pattern with skewed radial axes, elevation of anterior and posterior corneal elevation maps above best-fit sphere, and severe central/paracentral pachymetric thinning (<450 µm)

Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography (AS-OCT): Epithelial thickness mapping showing epithelial thinning ('doughnut pattern' with surrounding hyperplastic ring over the cone apex), hyperreflective stromal scarring, and acute breaks/coiling of Descemet membrane in hydrops
pathology_manifestations: Corneal Histopathology: Progressive central/inferotemporal stromal thinning with loss and disorganization of collagen lamellae; fragmentation and multiple micro-dehiscences in Bowman layer; keratocyte apoptosis in anterior stroma; basal epithelial iron accumulation visualized with Prussian blue stain (Fleischer ring)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Premier corneal ectatic disease characterized by unmistakable photographic signs (Fleischer ring, Vogt striae, Munson sign) and definitive Scheimpflug tomography and AS-OCT pachymetric mapping.

topics.name: Ocular Toxoplasmosis
clinical_manifestations: Most common cause of infectious posterior uveitis globally; caused by the obligate intracellular protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii, typically representing late reactivation of encysted parasites from congenital or acquired systemic infection
Patients typically present in the 2nd to 4th decade of life with unilateral floaters, hazy blurred vision, scotoma, and ocular redness/photophobia

Pathognomonic Funduscopic Hallmark: The classic 'Headlight in the Fog' sign: a focal, intensely elevated, fluffy, creamy-white or yellowish-white area of active necrotizing retinochoroiditis with ill-defined borders, obscured by dense overlying vitreous haze and inflammatory exudate (vitritis)

Pathognomonic Satellite Lesion: Active creamy-white retinitis lesion typically arises immediately adjacent to an old, heavily hyperpigmented, punched-out, atrophic chorioretinal scar (the site of encysted reactivation); lesions preferentially involve the posterior pole and macular region

Associated Ocular Signs: Kyrieleis plaques (segmental, glistening, yellowish-white, non-occlusive periarteriolar exudates located away from the primary retinitis focus); secondary anterior uveitis with granulomatous 'mutton-fat' keratic precipitates on the corneal endothelium and elevated intraocular pressure (hypertensive uveitis)
radiological_manifestations: Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT): Highly specific cross-sectional findings: acute active lesion shows massive full-thickness hyperreflectivity and localized thickening of the neurosensory retina, disruption of retinal layered architecture, localized posterior optical shadowing of the underlying choroid, subretinal fluid accumulation, hyperreflective inflammatory cells within the vitreous and preretinal space, and thickened posterior hyaloid membrane with vitreomacular traction; adjacent inactive chorioretinal scars show profound full-thickness retinal excavation/atrophy, loss of the RPE layer, and hypertransmission of OCT signal into the sclera

Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Early phases demonstrate pronounced hypofluorescence/blockage of choroidal and retinal background fluorescence caused by dense active retinal edema and infiltration; late phases show progressive, intense, fuzzy hyperfluorescence with extensive dye leakage along the margins of the active lesion; retinal vascular staining (periphlebitis and Kyrieleis arteriolitis); old adjacent inactive scars exhibit early window defects with late scleral staining

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Active retinochoroiditis exhibits patchy hypoautofluorescence surrounded by a hyperautofluorescent halo reflecting lipofuscin accumulation from dying RPE cells; old pigmented chorioretinal scars demonstrate deep hypoautofluorescence with rim hyperautofluorescence

B-Scan Ocular Ultrasonography: Crucial when dense vitritis ('fog') precludes clear ophthalmoscopic visualization; shows dense vitreous clumped echoes/membranes, posterior vitreous detachment (PVD), localized retinochoroidal thickening, and rules out rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
pathology_manifestations: Retinochoroidal Histopathology: Severe, full-thickness coagulative retinal necrosis with destruction of neural elements and photoreceptors, surrounded by dense non-caseating granulomatous and lymphoplasmacytic inflammatory infiltrates in the adjacent retina and underlying choroid; secondary disruption, pigment liberation, and reactive hyperplasia of the retinal pigment epithelium

Identification of Toxoplasma gondii Organisms: Pathognomonic identification of crescentic, basophilic tachyzoites (rapidly dividing active vegetative form, 2-6 µm) in necrotic tissue borders, and spherical or oval tissue cysts (bradyzoites, 10-100 µm) containing hundreds of densely packed, slowly metabolizing organisms with a well-defined cyst wall that stains intensely positive with Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Gomori methenamine silver (GMS)

Molecular Confirmation: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of aqueous humor or vitreous biopsy fluid demonstrating Toxoplasma gondii B1 or SAG1 gene sequences, and positive Goldmann-Witmer coefficient (GWC > 3) confirming local intraocular antibody synthesis
topics.inclusion_rationale: Foremost cause of infectious posterior uveitis worldwide, exhibiting the pathognomonic funduscopic 'headlight in the fog' sign adjacent to hyperpigmented scars, full-thickness hyperreflective necrosis on SD-OCT, and diagnostic PAS-positive bradyzoite tissue cysts.

topics.name: Optic Nerve Sheath Meningioma
clinical_manifestations: Middle-aged female predilection (3:1 female-to-male ratio); presents with slowly progressive, painless, monocular vision loss and visual field defects

Classic Hoyt-Spencer Triad: 1) Painless, progressive, long-standing visual loss; 2) Optic disc pallor (atrophy) or chronic optic disc swelling; 3) Retinochoroidal collateral vessels (optociliary shunt vessels) on the optic disc: enlarged, tortuous pre-existing capillaries that shunt blood from obstructed retinal venous circulation to the peripapillary choroidal circulation
Mild, painless axial proptosis and limitation of ocular motility (especially upgaze)
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Contrast-Enhanced Orbit MRI (with Fat Suppression): Pathognomonic 'Tram-Track' Sign on Axial T1 post-contrast images: Vivid, linear, homogeneous contrast enhancement of the expanded meningeal sheath surrounding the central, non-enhancing, hypointense optic nerve; Pathognomonic 'Doughnut' / 'Target' Sign on Coronal T1 post-contrast images: Circular ring of intensely enhancing meningeal tumor encasing the central non-enhancing circular optic nerve

Non-Contrast Orbit CT (Bone Window): Thickening of the optic nerve complex with pathognomonic fine, linear, punctate calcification along the optic nerve sheath (psammoma bodies), and apical expansion of the optic canal
pathology_manifestations: Meningioma Histopathology: Proliferation of uniform meningothelial cells arranged in tight syncytial lobules or concentric whorls with indistinct cell borders; abundant lamellated, concentric dystrophic calcifications (psammoma bodies); nuclear pseudoinclusions and longitudinal nuclear grooves
Immunohistochemistry: Diffuse, strong positivity for Epithelial Membrane Antigen (EMA), Progesterone Receptor (PR), and Vimentin; negative for S100 (ruling out schwannoma)
topics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield neuro-ophthalmic tumor displaying the Hoyt-Spencer triad of optic atrophy and optociliary shunt vessels, combined with pathognomonic MRI 'tram-track' sign and psammoma body pathology.

topics.name: Orbital Cellulitis and Subperiosteal Abscess
clinical_manifestations: Marked, tense, painful unilateral eyelid edema and violaceous erythema
Severe proptosis (axial or non-axial globe protrusion)
Painful limitation of extraocular movements (ophthalmoplegia)
Chemosis (intense swelling of bulbar conjunctiva bulging past eyelids)
Decreased visual acuity, relative afferent pupillary defect, and optic disc edema
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT of Orbit and Paranasal Sinuses (Emergency Gold Standard): Opacification of adjacent ethmoid or maxillary sinuses with bone erosion (lamina papyracea); subperiosteal abscess (well-defined lenticular or crescent-shaped fluid collection adjacent to the orbital wall with peripheral rim enhancement); post-septal intraconal/extraconal fat stranding; superior ophthalmic vein thrombosis
Brain and Orbit MRI: High-sensitivity detection of intracranial complications: cavernous sinus thrombosis, epidural/subdural abscess, and cerebritis
pathology_manifestations: Surgical drainage aspirate: Abundant degenerate polymorphonuclear neutrophils, necrotic debris, and bacterial pathogens (S. aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, or fungal hyphae in immunocompromised hosts)
topics.inclusion_rationale: Emergency orbital condition featuring striking eyelid edema, chemosis, and proptosis paired with diagnostic subperiosteal fluid collections and ethmoid sinus opacification on contrast CT.

topics.name: Persistent Fetal Vasculature
clinical_manifestations: Congenital developmental ocular malformation caused by the failure of the embryonic primary vitreous and hyaloid vascular system to undergo physiological programmed regression during the third trimester; typically sporadic and unilateral (>90% of cases)
Presents in full-term neonates or infants shortly after birth with leukocoria (white pupillary reflex), strabismus, microphthalmos, or failed red reflex screening

Pathognomonic Anterior PFV Hallmark on Slit-Lamp Biomicroscopy: Presence of a vascularized, dense, whitish-pink retrolental fibrovascular mass or membrane that adheres tightly to the posterior lens capsule; pathognomonic centripetal elongation and inward radial stretching of the ciliary processes visible through a dilated pupil around the margin of the small lens

Associated Anterior Segment Features: Microphthalmos (reduced corneal diameter and decreased axial length compared to contralateral eye), shallow anterior chamber, intumescent cataract due to posterior lens capsule dehiscence, and secondary angle-closure glaucoma

Pathognomonic Posterior PFV Features: Presence of a dense, opaque fibrovascular stalk or cord extending from the optic disc through the vitreous cavity to the posterior lens surface; associated with prominent falciform retinal folds, tractional retinal detachment, optic nerve hypoplasia, vitreous hemorrhage, and macular dragging
