excluded_topics.audit_reason: Postpartum pituitary failure without a photographic phenotype.

excluded_topics.name: Thyroid Eye Disease (Graves' Orbitopathy)
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark Axial Proptosis (Exophthalmos): Pathognomonic bilateral or markedly asymmetric forward protrusion of the globes (measured on Hertel exophthalmometer >20 mm in Caucasians, >22 mm in African Americans, or >2 mm interocular asymmetry) resulting from expansive retrobulbar autoimmune inflammation and lipogenesis

Eyelid Retraction and Dynamic Gaze Signs: Spontaneous upper eyelid retraction in primary gaze exposing sclera above the superior corneal limbus ('staring look' or Dalrymple sign); characteristic lagging of the upper eyelid behind the globe during downward saccadic movement (von Graefe sign); infrequent, sluggish blinking (Stellwag sign); and inability to maintain ocular convergence on near targets (Möbius sign)

Severe Inflammatory Orbital Signs: Dramatic periorbital edema and lower eyelid fat prolapse; marked caruncular and plical edema; intense bulbar conjunctival hyperemia (particularly prominent over extraocular muscle insertions); and chemosis with protruding gelatinous prolapse of conjunctiva over the lower eyelid margin

Sight-Threatening Complications: Severe lagophthalmos (inability to completely close the eyelids) causing exposure keratopathy, persistent corneal epithelial defects, corneal ulceration, and potential perforation; compressive dysthyroid optic neuropathy (DON) manifesting as reduced visual acuity, color desaturation (dyschromatopsia), relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD), and visual field scotomas from direct optic nerve compression at the orbital apex

Restrictive Extraocular Motility: Binocular diplopia with severe limitation of upward and lateral ocular excursion resulting from inflammatory swelling and secondary fibrotic contracture of the inferior rectus and medial rectus muscles
radiological_manifestations: High-Resolution Orbital CT / MRI: Pathognomonic fusiform, spindle-shaped enlargement of extraocular muscle bellies with characteristic, sharp sparing of the anterior tendinous insertions ('tendon-sparing enlargement'); classic pattern of muscular involvement follows the mnemonic 'I'M SLOw' (Inferior rectus > Medial rectus > Superior rectus > Lateral rectus > Obliques)

Apical Crowding Sign on Coronal MRI/CT: Severe expansion of extraocular muscle bellies within the tight bony orbital apex, compressing the intraorbital optic nerve against the optic canal, effacing the normal perineural fat ring, and stretching/straightening the optic nerve anteriorly, confirming dysthyroid optic neuropathy

Orbital MRI T2-Weighted and STIR Signal Intensity: Pronounced T2/STIR hyperintensity within swollen extraocular muscle bellies reflecting active interstitial edema and hydrophilic glycosaminoglycan accumulation; correlates directly with the Clinical Activity Score (CAS) and differentiates active inflammatory disease from chronic fibrotic inactive muscle hypertrophy

Retro-Orbital Fat Expansion and Venous Dilatation: Substantial increase in retrobulbar intraconal adipose volume causing anterior bowing and tension of the orbital septum, coupled with asymmetric enlargement and dilatation of the superior ophthalmic vein due to impaired orbital venous outflow
pathology_manifestations: Orbital Tissue Histopathology: Marked endomysial and perimysial inflammatory infiltration composed predominantly of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes, macrophages, mast cells, and plasma cells dissecting between separated muscle fibers; accompanied by massive accumulation of hydrophilic glycosaminoglycans (predominantly hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulfate) synthesized by activated CD34+ orbital fibroblasts

Immunopathologic Mechanism: Orbital fibroblasts expressing both the TSH receptor (TSHR) and insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor (IGF-1R) undergo synergistic activation by circulating autoantibodies (TRAb/TSI), stimulating de novo adipogenesis (orbital fat volume expansion) and excessive hyaluronic acid production, resulting in intense tissue edema, orbital compartment syndrome, and progressive endomysial fibrosis
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Visual autoimmune endocrine disorder displaying pathognomonic proptosis, Dalrymple/von Graefe eyelid retraction, and definitive orbital CT/MRI fusiform extraocular muscle enlargement with tendon sparing.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Orbitopathy is a manifestation of Graves disease, already indexed with dermopathy and eye disease.

excluded_topics.name: VIPoma Syndrome (WDHA / Verner-Morrison Syndrome)
synonyms: watery diarrhea, hypokalemia, and achlorhydria syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Hallmark 'Pancreatic Cholera' Watery Diarrhea: Massive, voluminous, secretory, tea-colored, odorless watery diarrhea persisting during strict fasting, commonly exceeding 3 to 10 liters daily (stool osmolality matching serum osmolality without an osmotic gap), leading to rapid life-threatening dehydration and electrolyte depletion

Profound Hypokalemic Muscular and Neurologic Signs: Severe, life-threatening hypokalemia (often serum potassium <2.0 mEq/L) producing generalized flaccid muscle weakness, profound lethargy, muscle cramps, diminished deep tendon reflexes, and paralytic ileus with abdominal distension and absent bowel sounds

Paroxysmal Cutaneous Vasodilatory Flushing: Episodic, bright red or violaceous cutaneous flushing affecting the face, neck, and upper chest occurring in 20–30% of patients, mediated by the potent vasodilatory action of vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)

Severe Dehydration and Metabolic Acidosis: Sunken eyes, dry cracked mucous membranes, loss of skin turgor, orthostatic hypotension, tachycardia, and deep Kussmaul respirations driven by massive enteric bicarbonate loss and non-anion gap metabolic hyperchloremic acidosis

Achlorhydria and Hypercalcemia: Hypochlorhydria or complete achlorhydria on gastric aspirate (due to VIP-induced inhibition of gastric acid secretion); mild to moderate hypercalcemia in up to 50% of patients (from coexisting parathyroid adenoma in MEN1 or tumor-induced osteoclast activation)
radiological_manifestations: Multiphasic Pancreatic Contrast-Enhanced CT: Solitary, large (median diameter 4–6 cm; >80% are >3 cm), well-circumscribed, highly vascular neoplasm situated predominantly in the body or tail of the pancreas, displaying avid heterogeneous contrast enhancement on late arterial phase with gradual washout; accurately detects regional lymphadenopathy

Detection of Hepatic Metastases on Abdominal MRI/CT: High rate of liver metastases present at diagnosis (>60–70%), appearing as multiple hypervascular nodular lesions with marked arterial phase rim enhancement and T2 hyperintensity, with restricted diffusion on DWI

68Ga-DOTATATE / 68Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT: Marked, avid focal radiotracer uptake localized to the primary pancreatic tumor and all metastatic sites, reflecting dense somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2) expression and facilitating targeted peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT)
Abdominal Plain Radiography: Diffuse, marked dilatation of small and large bowel loops with air-fluid levels consistent with extensive hypokalemic adynamic paralytic ileus
pathology_manifestations: Pancreatic Tumor Histology: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasm (PanNET G1 or G2) composed of uniform, cuboidal to polygonal cells arranged in trabecular, solid, or gyriform cords separated by delicate, highly vascularized stroma; round regular nuclei exhibiting classic finely speckled 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin and low mitotic activity

Immunohistochemistry: Diffusely and strongly positive for neuroendocrine markers synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and CD56; specific intense cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP); somatostatin receptor subtype 2A (SSTR2A) positivity on tumor cell membranes
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic endocrine emergency featuring massive 'pancreatic cholera' secretory diarrhea, cutaneous flushing, profound hypokalemic flaccid paralysis, and a large hypervascular pancreatic tail tumor on contrast CT and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Secretory-diarrhea syndrome without a disease-specific photograph.

excluded_topics.name: Adult Gastrointestinal Intussusception
clinical_manifestations: In contrast to idiopathic pediatric cases, >90% of adult intussusceptions are caused by a distinct pathological lead point (malignancy in ~60-70% of colonic cases, and benign or malignant neoplasms like lipoma, adenoma, GIST, or Meckel diverticulum in small bowel cases)

Palpable, tender, elongated, sausage-shaped or cylindrical abdominal mass, typically situated along the course of the colon or mid-abdomen, which may harden and become exquisitely painful during paroxysms of peristalsis

Dance's sign: Characteristic retraction, emptiness, and flattened sensation in the right lower quadrant in ileocecal intussusception, as the cecum and ascending colon invaginate distally into the transverse colon
Subacute or chronic, intermittent, episodic colicky abdominal pain accompanied by nausea, bilious vomiting, and visible peristaltic waves rippling across the thinned abdominal wall
Hematochezia or occult GI bleeding: Passage of dark red blood and mucus mixture resembling 'red currant jelly' stool or frank melena, with chronic microcytic anemia, fatigue, and weight loss
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Imaging Modality of Choice, sensitivity 98-100%): Pathognomonic 'target sign' or 'doughnut sign' on axial images, consisting of alternating concentric rings of bowel wall (intussusceptum and intussuscipiens) separated by high-attenuation mesenteric vessels and low-attenuation eccentric mesenteric fat; on longitudinal and oblique coronal reconstructions, displays the pathognomonic 'sausage sign' or 'pseudokidney sign' (reniform appearance with a central fatty and vascular core surrounded by thickened, edematous bowel wall); definitive identification of the inciting lead point (e.g., homogeneous fat-density submucosal lipoma, enhancing polypoid adenocarcinoma, or exophytic GIST); signs of strangulation include mural thickening, lack of mural enhancement, free fluid, and mesenteric congestion

Barium Enema / Small Bowel Follow-Through: Pathognomonic 'coiled-spring' appearance (spiral or accordion-like rings) created by thin layers of barium trapped in the mucosal crevices between the outer intussuscipiens and inner intussusceptum; cup-shaped intraluminal filling defect at the apex of invagination
Abdominal Ultrasound: Transverse views show the 'target' or 'multiple concentric rings' sign; longitudinal views show the 'hayfork' or 'sandwich' sign representing parallel layers of bowel wall
pathology_manifestations: Resected intestinal specimen: Telescoped bowel segment where the proximal inner bowel (intussusceptum) with its attached mesentery has prolapsed into the lumen of the distal receiving bowel (intussuscipiens); striking mucosal and serosal venous congestion, cyanosis, edema, and ischemic ulceration; identification of the underlying lead point neoplasm: in the colon, predominantly invasive adenocarcinoma (infiltrating malignant glands with nuclear pleomorphism, desmoplasia, and atypical mitoses) or lymphoma; in the small bowel, benign submucosal lipoma (lobules of mature adipocytes with fibrous capsule), adenomatous polyp, hamartoma (Peutz-Jeghers), or Meckel diverticulum
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: High-yield surgical condition featuring palpable sausage-shaped abdominal mass with Dance's sign, pathognomonic CT target/pseudokidney signs, barium coiled-spring pattern, and mandatory pathological search for malignant or benign lead points in adults.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Mechanical event, usually secondary to a lead-point tumor already covered elsewhere.

excluded_topics.name: Autoimmune Pancreatitis (IgG4-Related Pancreato-Biliary Disease)
clinical_manifestations: Painless obstructive jaundice with deep scleral icterus, dark tea-colored urine, acholic (clay-colored) stools, and generalized pruritus in an elderly male without severe constitutional cachexia
Bilateral, painless, firm, non-tender salivary gland swelling (Mikulicz syndrome: bilateral submandibular and parotid gland enlargement)
Bilateral lacrimal gland enlargement with painless eyelid swelling and fullness (dacryoadenitis / Küttner tumor)
Palpable epigastric fullness or dull deep abdominal discomfort without the agonizing, lancinating pain of acute pancreatitis; prominent weight loss mimicking pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
Cutaneous manifestations of systemic IgG4-related disease including prurigo nodularis-like lesions, erythematous indurated plaques, and subcutaneous nodules
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT / MRI: Diffusely enlarged, featureless, hypodense 'sausage-shaped' pancreas with loss of the normal lobular parenchymal architecture and clefts; pathognomonic capsule-like rim or 'halo' of low attenuation surrounding the pancreatic parenchyma on delayed contrast phases (representing a peripheral mantle of fibrous tissue and inflammatory infiltrate); patchy delayed homogeneous enhancement

Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) / ERCP: Diffuse or segmental smooth narrowing and attenuation of the main pancreatic duct (duct caliber <2 mm over a long segment) with conspicuous absence of marked upstream ductal dilation (distinguishing AIP from adenocarcinoma); smooth, tapered stricture of the intrapancreatic portion of the distal common bile duct with proximal extrahepatic/intrahepatic biliary dilation

Abdominal / Retroperitoneal CT: Soft-tissue rim thickening encasing the infrarenal abdominal aorta and iliac vessels (IgG4-related periaortitis / retroperitoneal fibrosis) with medial deviation of the ureters and hydronephrosis
pathology_manifestations: Pancreatic core biopsy / surgical resection (Type 1 AIP / LPSP): Dense, heavy lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate composed of mature lymphocytes and abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells (>10 to >50 IgG4+ plasma cells per high-power field, IgG4/IgG ratio >40%); pathognomonic 'storiform' (cartwheel or whorled) pattern of interlobular fibrosis; obliterative phlebitis (venous lumina occluded by inflammatory cells and collagen with sparing of adjacent arterioles on elastic stains); tissue eosinophilia; dramatic clinical and imaging resolution following corticosteroid therapy
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Premier systemic fibroinflammatory mimic of pancreatic cancer featuring painless jaundice and bilateral salivary gland swelling paired with the textbook 'sausage-shaped' pancreas with capsule-like rim halo on CT and storiform IgG4+ lymphoplasmacytic pathology.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Pancreatic manifestation of IgG4-related disease, already a rheumatology topic.

excluded_topics.name: Cecal Volvulus and Cecal Bascule
clinical_manifestations: Severe, acute, excruciating right lower quadrant or periumbilical colicky abdominal pain rapidly becoming constant and diffuse, accompanied by early, copious bilious and small-bowel emesis

Asymmetric abdominal distension with a visible and palpable, tensely tympanitic, resonant mass filling the epigastrium, left upper quadrant, or central abdomen, while the right lower quadrant feels strangely empty, flat, and hollow to palpation
Hyperactive, high-pitched borborygmi early in obstruction, which diminishes rapidly into silent, hypoperistaltic abdomen as strangulation and closed-loop ischemia progress

Peritoneal signs: Involuntary muscular guarding, localized or diffuse rebound tenderness (Blumberg's sign), abdominal wall rigidity, cutaneous diaphoresis, tachypnea, tachycardia, and fever denoting cecal strangulation and mucosal gangrene

High risk of rapid cecal perforation due to Laplace's law (the cecum having the largest luminal diameter of the colon generates highest wall tension at low intraluminal pressure, leading to ischemic rupture along the antimesenteric border)
radiological_manifestations: Plain Abdominal Radiography (Supine/Upright): Pathognomonic comma-shaped or kidney-shaped (embryo-shaped) gas-filled viscus with its convex contour oriented toward the left upper quadrant or mid-abdomen and its apex pointing to the right lower quadrant (the cecum twists and flips from RLQ into LUQ); pathognomonic single huge air-fluid level; complete absence of gas in the right iliac fossa and ascending colon, accompanied by multiple dilated small-bowel loops with central ladder-like air-fluid levels (small bowel obstruction); in cecal bascule (type III), the cecum folds anteriorly and superiorly over the ascending colon without axial torsion, sitting in the mid-abdomen

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Definitive diagnostic standard; pathognomonic 'whirl sign' in the right lower quadrant or mesentery formed by swirling mesenteric fat and engorged ileocolic vessels around the twist axis; huge distended cecum (often >9-10 cm in diameter) located in an ectopic position (LUQ, epigastrium); visualization of two compressed transition points forming an extreme closed-loop obstruction ('split-wall' or 'beak' sign at the afferent ileal and efferent colonic limbs); presence of pneumatosis intestinalis, cecal wall thinning or lack of mural enhancement indicates impending or established ischemic gangrene; pneumoperitoneum indicates cecal rupture

Water-Soluble Contrast Enema: Abrupt, sharp, smooth tapering of contrast column in the ascending colon terminating in a classic smooth, tapered beak ('bird's beak' or cone sign) pointing directly to the site of torsion, with non-filling of the cecum
pathology_manifestations: Surgical pathology of resected right hemicolectomy: Markedly dilated, thinned, cyanotic, plum-colored or frank black ischemic cecum and terminal ileum rotated on an abnormally mobile mesentery (developmental failure of retroperitoneal peritoneal fixation of the cecum and ascending colon to the posterior parietal peritoneum, persistency of mobile cecum / mesenterium commune); transmural hemorrhagic necrosis, extensive mucosal sloughing, severe submucosal hemorrhage, transmural inflammatory infiltrate, and microvascular venous thrombosis; frequent antimesenteric longitudinal serosal tears (diastatic perforation)
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Emergent surgical condition with striking asymmetric abdominal swelling and empty RLQ, pathognomonic kidney/comma-shaped LUQ cecal gas collection on plain film, CT mesenteric 'whirl' with closed-loop obstruction, and rapid progression to transmural gangrene via Laplace's law.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Radiographic emergency without a disease-specific clinical photograph.

excluded_topics.name: Focal Nodular Hyperplasia (FNH)
synonyms: focal nodular hyperplasia of the liver
clinical_manifestations: Second most common benign liver lesion (after hemangioma), predominantly occurring in young to middle-aged women (80-90% of cases, ages 20-50), arising as a hyperplastic polyclonal regenerative response to a pre-existing congenital arterial malformation/hyperperfusion

Presentation: predominantly asymptomatic and detected incidentally on routine imaging, but large lesions (>5-10 cm) present with a smooth, firm, non-tender palpable liver edge or mass in the right upper quadrant or epigastrium

Bedside physical examination: palpation reveals a non-tender, mobile right hypochondrial mass without friction rub; conspicuous absence of stigmata of chronic liver disease (no spider angiomas, palmar erythema, jaundice, or ascites) and absence of constitutional cachexia or weight loss

Symptoms in symptomatic cases: dull, dragging right upper quadrant or epigastric discomfort, postprandial fullness, or localized tenderness; catastrophic spontaneous rupture and hemoperitoneum are exceedingly rare (<1%, in marked contrast to hepatic adenoma)
radiological_manifestations: Multiphasic Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Non-contrast phase demonstrates a well-circumscribed, homogeneous, iso-to-slightly hypoattenuating/hypointense lesion with a central hypodense/hypointense stellate area; pathognomonic early arterial phase demonstrates intense, rapid, homogeneous hyperenhancement (except for the central scar which remains unenhanced); during portal venous and equilibrium delayed phases, the lesion parenchymal enhancement washes out rapidly to become isoattenuating/isointense to background liver ('stealth lesion'); the pathognomonic central fibrous stellate scar demonstrates marked, characteristic delayed hyperenhancement (due to contrast accumulation in the loose, myxoid fibrous connective tissue matrix)

Hepatobiliary MRI with Gd-EOB-DTPA (Primovist / Eovist): Key problem-solving modality; because FNH contains functioning hepatocytes and dysmorphic biliary ductules that take up hepatobiliary contrast via OATP1B1/3 transporters, FNH displays intense isointensity or hyperintensity on the 20-minute hepatobiliary phase with a hypointense central scar (100% specific differentiator from hepatocellular adenoma and metastases, which lack biliary excretion and appear as dark/hypointense defect 'holes')

Color and Spectral Doppler Ultrasound: Well-defined liver mass with the pathognomonic 'spoke-wheel' vascular pattern consisting of a central feeding artery with multiple branches radiating peripherally towards the margins; spectral Doppler shows high-velocity, low-resistance arterial waveforms (resistive index RI typically <0.50-0.65) with continuous turbulent diastolic flow

Tc-99m Sulfur Colloid Scintigraphy: In 60-70% of cases, normal or increased radiotracer uptake ('hot spot' or isointense to liver) due to the presence of functional, hyperplastic reticuloendothelial Kupffer cells (definitively ruling out hepatic adenoma or malignancy which fail to take up sulfur colloid)
pathology_manifestations: Surgical resection / explant: Solitary, well-circumscribed, unencapsulated multinodular mass (typically 3-8 cm) lighter in color (yellow-tan) than adjacent normal liver; cut surface reveals a pathognomonic central fibrous stellate scar with radiating fibrous septa dividing the parenchyma into numerous distinct nodular subunits, resembling focal cirrhosis ('focal cirrhosis')

Histology: Hyperplastic nodules of histologically benign, normal-appearing hepatocytes arranged in plates no more than 1-2 cells thick; central and radiating fibrous scars contain abnormally thick-walled, dystrophic, muscularized dysplastic arteries lacking an internal elastic lamina, with eccentric intimal hyperplasia; proliferating, anastomosing bile ductules at the interface of the fibrous septa and hepatocyte nodules (ductular reaction) without true formed portal triads (absence of portal veins and true bile ducts)

Immunohistochemistry: Pathognomonic, striking 'map-like' anastomosing geographic cytoplasmic immunostaining for Glutamine Synthetase (GS) throughout the lesion parenchyma (reflecting localized beta-catenin pathway activation secondary to altered arterial perfusion, in sharp contrast to the diffuse homogeneous staining of beta-catenin-mutated adenomas or the perivenular rim staining of normal liver); strongly positive for cytokeratin 7 (CK7) highlighting the prominent ductular reaction at fibrous boundaries
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Premier benign regenerative liver lesion featuring a palpable RUQ edge in young women, paired with the pathognomonic multiphasic MRI central stellate scar with delayed hyperenhancement, the 'spoke-wheel' color Doppler sign, Eovist retention, and 'map-like' glutamine synthetase histology.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Incidental liver imaging lesion. No clinical photograph.

excluded_topics.name: Gallstone Ileus and Bouveret Syndrome
clinical_manifestations: Elderly female presentation (peak age 70-80s) with a history of recurrent cholelithiasis presenting with intermittent, 'tumbling' or episodic mechanical small bowel obstruction (cramping abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, and obstipation) as a large ectopic gallstone rolls, impacts, temporarily dislodges, and moves distally

Bouveret syndrome (gastric outlet obstruction variant, ~1-3% of cases): A massive gallstone (>2.5 cm) erodes directly into the duodenal bulb or pylorus via a cholecystoduodenal fistula, creating sudden gastric outlet obstruction: intractable, profuse, foul-smelling or coffee-ground vomiting, epigastric fullness, visible gastric peristaltic waves, and a prominent succussion splash audible in the upper abdomen

Physical exam: Dehydrated, frail, elderly patient with diffuse abdominal distension, high-pitched metallic bowel sounds, mild localized tenderness in the right upper quadrant or epigastrium without frank rigidity unless perforation occurs; mild scleral icterus or jaundice in up to 15% of patients

Sepsis, peritonitis, and hemodynamic shock if delayed diagnosis leads to transmural pressure necrosis and bowel perforation at the site of stone impaction (most frequently the narrow terminal ileum, ~60-70%, followed by proximal jejunum and duodenum)
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Diagnostic Gold Standard, sensitivity >93%): Complete demonstration of the classic Rigler's Triad: (1) Pneumobilia (gas branching within the intrahepatic biliary tree or common bile duct and gallbladder), (2) Mechanical small bowel or gastric obstruction with sharp transition point and upstream dilated fluid-filled bowel, and (3) Ectopic, radio-opaque or laminated gallstone impacted within the bowel lumen (terminal ileum in classic gallstone ileus; duodenal bulb or pyloric channel in Bouveret syndrome); direct visualization of the cholecystoenteric / cholecystoduodenal fistula with air in a contracted, thick-walled gallbladder; Rigler's tetrad includes a change in position of a previously observed gallstone on sequential studies

Plain Abdominal Radiographs (Rigler's Triad on X-ray): Visualized in ~30-50% of cases: branching linear radiolucencies in the right upper quadrant liver shadow corresponding to pneumobilia; dilated small bowel loops with multiple air-fluid levels; and an ectopic calcified oval or faceted laminated gallstone in the right lower quadrant or pelvis

Upper Gastrointestinal Barium / Water-Soluble Swallow (Bouveret Syndrome): Huge, smooth, rounded or faceted intraluminal filling defect occupying the duodenal bulb or pylorus, with contrast tracing around the stone ('cupola' sign); massive gastric dilatation with retained food and fluid; contrast leakage into the gallbladder via the cholecystoduodenal fistula

Abdominal Ultrasound: Contracted, air-filled gallbladder with dense shadowing, obscured biliary anatomy, and an ectopic hyperreflective stone with acoustic shadow in the right lower quadrant or duodenum
pathology_manifestations: Surgical enterolithotomy / cholecystectomy specimen: Large, solid, faceted or barrel-shaped, laminated gallstone measuring 2.5 to 5 cm or greater, composed predominantly of cholesterol with concentric bilirubin and calcium carbonate laminations; cholecystoenteric fistula (cholecystoduodenal in 60-70%, cholecystocolonic in 10-15%, cholecystogastric in 5%); histopathology of the impacted bowel wall shows severe circumferential pressure ischemia, transmural coagulative necrosis, mucosal erosion, extensive submucosal edema and hemorrhage, and acute dense transmural neutrophilic infiltrate with impending decubitus ulcer perforation
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic surgical gem featuring the iconic Rigler's triad on imaging (pneumobilia, mechanical obstruction, ectopic gallstone), dramatic tumbling obstruction or Bouveret gastric outlet obstruction in elderly patients, and life-threatening pressure-necrosis fistula pathology.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Fistula complication of gallstone disease, not a primary disease.

excluded_topics.name: Gastric Volvulus
clinical_manifestations: Pathognomonic Borchardt's triad: (1) Severe, sudden-onset, agonizing epigastric pain and retrosternal oppression, (2) violent, persistent, intractable retching and dry heaving completely without production of vomitus, and (3) absolute inability to advance a nasogastric (NG) tube into the stomach due to mechanical obstruction at the gastroesophageal junction
Visible and palpable, exquisitely tender, tense epigastric or left upper quadrant fullness/distension with marked tympany, which may dramatically elevate the left hemidiaphragm

Sudden-onset dyspnea, tachypnea, and chest tightness from massive intrathoracic gastric herniation through a diaphragmatic hernia (large paraesophageal hernia, Bochdalek hernia, or post-traumatic diaphragmatic rupture) compressing the lung base and mediastinum

Rapid hemodynamic collapse: Tachycardia, hypotension, pallor, cold clammy extremities, and metabolic acidosis reflecting closed-loop gastric strangulation, transmural ischemia, shock, and risk of gastric rupture into the mediastinum or lesser sac
radiological_manifestations: Plain Chest and Abdominal Radiographs: Striking, pathognomonic appearance of a massive gas-filled and fluid-filled stomach occupying the lower left thorax or upper abdomen with two distinct air-fluid levels; in organoaxial volvulus (most common, ~60%), the stomach rotates along its long axis (cardio-pyloric line), causing the greater curvature to flip superiorly above the lesser curvature, with the gastroesophageal junction situated low and a horizontal double air-fluid level; in mesenteroaxial volvulus (~30%), the stomach rotates along its short axis (perpendicular to long axis, connecting lesser and greater curvatures), flipping the antrum and pylorus superior and anterior to the gastroesophageal junction, producing a spherical intrathoracic gas bubble with a vertical or high single air-fluid level

Contrast-Enhanced CT of the Chest and Abdomen (Modality of Choice): Massive gastric distension with abnormal anatomical displacement (antrum lying cephalad to the gastroesophageal junction or greater curvature lying superiorly); two transition points indicating closed-loop torsion; twisting of the gastric wall and swirling of the gastric vasculature (gastric 'whirl sign'); presence of diaphragmatic herniation with stomach in the posterior mediastinum; mural hypoenhancement, gastric pneumatosis (gas within the gastric wall), peri-gastric fluid or free air indicating transmural gastric infarction and perforation

Fluoroscopic Upper GI Series (Barium / Water-Soluble Swallow): Complete obstruction to the flow of contrast at the distal esophagus with a smooth, tapered bird-beak pointing into the obstructed stomach; or pathognomonic upside-down stomach configuration where the greater curvature forms the superior border and pylorus points downward or twisted
pathology_manifestations: Surgical resection / gastrectomy specimen: Greatly dilated, dusky red, mottled purple, or black necrotic stomach with severe transmural venous congestion and hemorrhagic infarction; twisting of the gastrosplenic, gastrocolic, and gastrohepatic ligaments; histopathology shows extensive mucosal necrosis, full-thickness coagulative ischemia of the gastric wall, massive submucosal edema, hemorrhage, acute diffuse neutrophilic infiltration, and microthrombi in intramural arterioles and venules; focal transmural perforation along the greater curvature
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Life-threatening surgical emergency defined by the historic Borchardt triad, classic pathognomonic inverted intrathoracic double-fluid viscus on radiograph, CT gastric whirl with closed-loop torsion, and fulminant transmural gastric gangrene.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Radiographic/endoscopic emergency without a disease phenotype.

excluded_topics.name: Giant Cavernous Hepatic Hemangioma
clinical_manifestations: Large benign liver neoplasm (>4-5 cm, frequently >10 cm in diameter): clinical manifestations caused by mechanical mass effect, stretching of Glisson's capsule, or vascular complications

Physical examination: palpable, smooth or nodular, non-tender or mildly tender right upper quadrant or epigastric abdominal mass; asymmetric hepatomegaly; audible continuous epigastric or right hypochondrial vascular bruit in high-flow lesions

Symptoms of compression: early satiety, postprandial fullness, anorexia, and weight loss from extrinsic gastric or duodenal compression; nausea, vomiting, and dull persistent right upper quadrant ache

Acute catastrophic presentation: sudden-onset severe right upper quadrant pain, guarding, rebound tenderness, and hypovolemic shock due to acute intratumoral thrombosis/infarction or spontaneous/traumatic rupture with life-threatening hemoperitoneum

Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon / consumptive coagulopathy: profound thrombocytopenia, hypofibrinogenemia, elevated D-dimer, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, widespread cutaneous petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, and systemic mucosal bleeding caused by platelet trapping, consumption, and activation within the vast cavernous vascular lake
radiological_manifestations: Multiphase Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Diagnostic Hallmark): Well-demarcated, lobulated, hypoattenuating mass on non-contrast CT; pathognomonic early arterial phase showing peripheral, nodular, discontinuous globular enhancement with attenuation matching that of the aorta ('peripheral puddling'); portal venous and delayed phases show progressive, gradual centripetal ('outside-in') fill-in of contrast toward the center; prolonged delayed retention of contrast becoming completely isoattenuating or hyperattenuating to surrounding liver parenchyma; central non-enhancing cleft or cleft-like zone may remain if thrombosis, fibrosis, or cystic necrosis is present

Multiphasic Contrast-Enhanced MRI (Imaging Gold Standard): Distinctly hypointense on T1-weighted sequences; pathognomonic intense, homogeneous or slightly heterogeneous hyperintensity on T2-weighted sequences ('lightbulb sign' or 'cotton-wool sign', with T2 signal intensity exceeding that of cerebrospinal fluid or spleen); dynamic gadolinium administration demonstrates the identical peripheral nodular puddling with progressive centripetal fill-in matching the CT pattern; high ADC values on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) reflecting free fluid diffusivity (distinguishing it from solid hypercellular malignancies)

Color Doppler Ultrasound: Typically well-circumscribed, lobulated, homogeneously hyperechoic mass with posterior acoustic enhancement; color and power Doppler demonstrate absent or low-velocity, continuous, monophasic peripheral venous flow signals within the cavernous spaces (due to extremely sluggish intravascular blood flow), distinguishing it from arterially hypervascular malignancies

Tc-99m labeled RBC Scintigraphy: Early dynamic phase demonstrates perfusion defect (photopenia / 'cold spot') followed on delayed 1-2 hour blood-pool images by intense, hot focal accumulation of radiolabeled red blood cells exceeding the surrounding liver activity (pathognomonic confirmation)
pathology_manifestations: Surgical resection / explant: Soft, sponge-like, compressible, dark reddish-purple or bluish-black well-circumscribed solitary mass with a lobulated subcapsular or parenchymal surface; cross-section displays a classic 'honeycomb' appearance of wide, blood-filled vascular spaces separated by fibrous trabeculae, often with a central stellate fibrous scar, organized thrombi, or gritty dystrophic calcifications (phleboliths)

Histology: Large, widely dilated, irregular, anastomosing cavernous vascular channels lined by a single, uniform, flat layer of mature, benign endothelial cells lacking cytological atypia, hyperchromasia, or mitoses; vascular spaces are filled with static erythrocytes and organized fibrin thrombi; intervening stroma consists of thin-to-dense collagenous fibrous septa containing elastic fibers; endothelial cells are strongly immunoreactive for CD31, CD34, and ERG, and strictly negative for GLUT-1 (distinguishing congenital cavernous hemangioma from infantile hemangioma)
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Paramount benign vascular liver tumor presenting with a palpable RUQ mass, early satiety, or consumptive coagulopathy (Kasabach-Merritt), featuring the unmistakable multiphasic CT/MRI peripheral nodular puddling with centripetal fill-in, the T2 'lightbulb sign', and cavernous endothelial histology.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Imaging lesion without a clinical photograph (distinct from cutaneous infantile hemangioma).

excluded_topics.name: Hepatocellular Adenoma (Hepatic Adenoma)
clinical_manifestations: Monoclonal benign epithelial liver neoplasm occurring overwhelmingly in young females (90%) with a history of long-term oral contraceptive pill (OCP) use (risk proportional to duration and estrogen dose), anabolic androgenic steroid use, glycogen storage disease (Types I and III), or metabolic syndrome/severe obesity
Clinical presentation: palpable, tender right upper quadrant mass or focal hepatomegaly discovered during evaluation of vague right hypochondrial fullness or chronic aching pain

Dramatic, life-threatening emergency presentation: spontaneous intratumoral hemorrhage and catastrophic rupture through Glisson's capsule into the peritoneal cavity in 20-30% of cases (especially lesions >5 cm); patients present with acute, knife-like, sudden-onset right upper quadrant/epigastric pain, marked peritoneal signs (involuntary abdominal guarding, board-like rigidity, rebound tenderness), profound pallor, diaphoresis, tachycardia, and severe hypovolemic shock / hemoperitoneum

Bedside physical examination: marked abdominal tenderness and distension; dullness to percussion in the flanks (fluid wave / hemoperitoneum); cool, clammy extremities and orthostatic hypotension during rupture; stigmata of metabolic syndrome or virilization/hirsutism in anabolic steroid users

Risk of malignant transformation: high propensity for malignant transformation into hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly in lesions >5 cm, in male patients, and in the beta-catenin-activated molecular subtype
radiological_manifestations: Multiphasic Contrast-Enhanced CT / MRI (Diagnostic Modality of Choice): Well-circumscribed, encapsulated or pseudocapsulated heterogeneous mass; heterogeneous, brisk hyperenhancement in the early arterial phase; on portal venous and delayed phases, enhancement is variable (may wash out to become iso- or hypoattenuating, mimicking HCC); T1-weighted MRI: hyperintense areas on T1 corresponding to acute or subacute methemoglobin from internal hemorrhage; HNF1A-inactivated adenomas (H-HCA, ~30-40%) display pathognomonic diffuse and homogeneous signal drop on out-of-phase chemical shift T1 MRI due to extensive intracellular lipid content ('chemical shift signal loss'); Inflammatory adenomas (I-HCA, ~40-50%) show the pathognomonic 'atoll sign' (hyperintense peripheral rim on T2-weighted MRI with persistent delayed phase rim enhancement)

Hepatobiliary-Specific Contrast MRI (Gd-EOB-DTPA / Eovist): Hallmark finding is failure to express OATP1B1/3 transporters and absent biliary excretion, resulting in marked, sharply demarcated hypointensity ('black hole' defect) on the 20-minute hepatobiliary phase (reliably differentiating HCA from focal nodular hyperplasia, which retains contrast)

Abdominal Ultrasound: Well-circumscribed, heterogeneous solid mass with hypoechoic or hyperechoic foci corresponding to acute hemorrhage or necrosis; color Doppler shows predominantly peripheral and chaotic internal vascularity with continuous venous flow and low-resistance arterial waveforms
pathology_manifestations: Surgical resection / explant: Soft, friable, fleshy, well-circumscribed, partially or completely pseudocapsulated mass (often >5 cm) with prominent mottled areas of reddish-brown hemorrhage, yellowish necrosis, and pale steatotic zones; sharp demarcation from adjacent non-cirrhotic liver parenchyma

Histology: Monotonous sheets and cords (1 to 2 cells thick) of well-differentiated hepatocytes with round, regular nuclei and abundant eosinophilic or vacuolated (lipid-rich) cytoplasm; total, conspicuous absence of portal tracts, central veins, and formed interlobular bile ducts; interspersed scattered, thin-walled, solitary, dysplastic arterioles without surrounding connective tissue ('naked arteries' / 'unaccompanied arteries') susceptible to spontaneous rupture; prominent sinusoidal dilatation and peliosis-like blood lakes

Molecular Subtyping & Immunohistochemistry: 1) HNF1A-inactivated (30-40%): complete loss of Liver Fatty Acid Binding Protein (LFABP) immunostaining; 2) Inflammatory HCA (40-50%): strong, diffuse overexpression of C-reactive protein (CRP) and Serum Amyloid A (SAA), dense perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate, dilated tortuous sinusoids; 3) Beta-catenin-activated HCA (10-15%, exons 3 or 7/8): nuclear and cytoplasmic beta-catenin accumulation, diffuse strong glutamine synthetase (GS) positivity, cellular atypia, and high risk of progression to hepatocellular carcinoma; 4) Unclassified HCA (<10%)
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Essential hepatic neoplasm in young females on oral contraceptives presenting with tender RUQ mass or catastrophic rupture with hypovolemic shock, featuring subtype-specific MRI (T1 chemical-shift fat dropout, 'atoll sign', Eovist black-hole defect), 'naked artery' histology, and LFABP/beta-catenin subtyping.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Imaging lesion. Rupture is a complication, not a visual disease phenotype.

excluded_topics.name: Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasm (IPMN) of the Pancreas
synonyms: intraductal papillary mucinous tumor of the pancreas
clinical_manifestations: Premalignant intraductal epithelial neoplasm of the exocrine pancreas characterized by mucin hypersecretion, intraductal papillary proliferation, and cystic ductal dilatation, typically occurring in elderly patients (ages 60-80, slight male predominance)

Recurrent acute pancreatitis: intermittent obstruction of the pancreatic ductal orifice by thick, tenacious, gelatinous mucin plugs produces recurrent bouts of acute pancreatitis (epigastric pain radiating to the mid-back, nausea, vomiting, and elevated serum lipase)

Chronic pancreatobiliary symptoms: persistent dull epigastric or back pain, progressive exocrine pancreatic insufficiency with steatorrhea (voluminous, greasy, floating stools), weight loss, cachexia, and new-onset or worsening diabetes mellitus

Physical examination: signs of biliary obstruction (deep scleral icterus, dark urine, pale stools) when a head lesion or copious mucin compresses/obstructs the intrapancreatic common bile duct; palpable epigastric fullness or fullness over a large branch-duct cyst; generalized cachexia in invasive transformation

Pathognomonic Endoscopic Hallmark (Side-Viewing Duodenoscopy): classic 'fish-mouth' or 'patulous' ampulla of Vater (widely dilated, gaping major duodenal papilla) with thick, clear, gelatinous, rope-like mucin actively extruding from the papillary orifice into the duodenal lumen
radiological_manifestations: Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP - Imaging Modality of Choice): 1) Main-Duct IPMN (MD-IPMN): diffuse or segmental marked dilatation of the main pancreatic duct (>5 mm, frequently >10-15 mm) without an obstructing parenchymal mass, with intraductal mucin globs (filling defects); 2) Branch-Duct IPMN (BD-IPMN): multilocular cystic lesion with a characteristic 'cluster of grapes' or pleomorphic lobulated appearance, with direct communication between the cystic lesion and the main pancreatic duct (the definitive pathognomonic diagnostic sign on thin-slice MRCP / 3D heavily T2-weighted reconstructions); 3) Mixed-Type IPMN: features of both main duct dilation and communicating branch-duct cysts

High-Resolution Contrast-Enhanced Multidetector CT: Evaluates International Fukuoka Consensus Criteria: 'High-Risk Stigmata' (mandating surgical resection: obstructive jaundice in a patient with a cystic lesion in the pancreatic head, enhancing mural nodule ≥5 mm, or main pancreatic duct diameter ≥10 mm); 'Worrisome Features' (cyst size ≥3 cm, enhancing mural nodule <5 mm, thickened enhancing cyst walls, main duct diameter 5-9 mm, abrupt caliber change with distal parenchymal atrophy, lymphadenopathy, or rapid cyst growth >5 mm in 2 years)

Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS) with Fine-Needle Aspiration (FNA): High-resolution imaging identifying subtle mural nodules, thickened internal septations, and ductal walls; cyst fluid analysis shows viscous fluid with a positive string test (>3-5 mm mucin string), markedly elevated Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA >192 ng/mL), extremely high fluid amylase (>250-1000 U/L confirming ductal communication), and absence of mucinous ovarian-type stroma
pathology_manifestations: Surgical resection (Pancreaticoduodenectomy / Whipple or Distal Pancreatectomy): Gross specimen shows markedly ectatic main pancreatic duct and/or dilated branch ducts filled with copious, thick, viscous, glistening, jelly-like mucin; lining displays friable, papillary, velvety mucosal projections, tan-pink polypoid mural nodules, or fine villous architecture

Histology: Intraductal proliferation of tall, columnar, mucin-rich neoplastic epithelial cells forming prominent, complex, branching, finger-like papillary projections supported by delicate fibrovascular cores; graded by architectural and cytological atypia according to the WHO classification: low-grade dysplasia, high-grade dysplasia (marked nuclear enlargement, pseudostratification, cribriforming, loss of polarity, and frequent mitoses), and IPMN with associated invasive adenocarcinoma (colloid/mucinous carcinoma or tubular ductal adenocarcinoma); conspicuous absence of ovarian-type stroma (strictly differentiating IPMN from mucinous cystic neoplasm / MCN)

Epithelial Subtypes: 1) Gastric type (predominantly in BD-IPMN, MUC5AC+, MUC6+, low malignant potential); 2) Intestinal type (predominantly in MD-IPMN, villous architecture, MUC2+, CDX2+, frequently develops into colloid carcinoma); 3) Pancreatobiliary type (complex arborizing papillae, MUC1+, high-grade dysplasia, aggressive tubular adenocarcinoma); 4) Oncocytic type (IOPN, eosinophilic mitochondria-rich cytoplasm, now recognized as distinct entity with PRKACA/PRKACB fusions)

Molecular Genetics: Characteristic somatic activating mutations in the GNAS oncogene (codon 201, detected in >60-70% of IPMNs, highly specific for IPMN among pancreatic cysts) and KRAS (codon 12/13, in >80%), followed by late inactivating mutations in RNF43, TP53, and SMAD4 during progression to invasive carcinoma
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Premier mucin-producing premalignant pancreatic neoplasm characterized by recurrent pancreatitis and the pathognomonic endoscopic 'fish-mouth' papilla with extruding mucin, paired with MRCP-demonstrated communicating 'cluster-of-grapes' cysts or diffuse main duct dilatation (Fukuoka criteria), and GNAS/KRAS-mutated mucinous papillary histology without ovarian stroma.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Pancreatic cyst diagnosis by MRI/EUS, without a clinical photograph.

excluded_topics.name: Mirizzi Syndrome (Extrinsic Bile Duct Compression and Cholecystobiliary Fistula)
clinical_manifestations: Uncommon and severe complication of chronic cholelithiasis (~0.5-1% of all gallstone patients) caused by a large gallstone impacted in the cystic duct or Hartmann's pouch of the gallbladder, producing extrinsic mechanical compression of the adjacent common hepatic duct (CHD), progressing via pressure necrosis to cholecystobiliary fistula

Hallmark presentation: recurrent episodes of acute obstructive jaundice (deep scleral icterus, dark tea-colored urine, light or acholic clay-colored stools) combined with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and high spiking fevers with shaking chills (Charcot's triad of acute cholangitis)

Bedside physical examination: marked right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness with involuntary guarding and a positive Murphy sign; deeply jaundiced skin and sclerae; palpable tender mass in the right hypochondrium (representing an intensely inflamed, hydropic gallbladder and surrounding phlegmon, although in long-standing disease the gallbladder may be small and contracted); cutaneous excoriations from severe cholestatic pruritus

Surgical importance: unrecognized Mirizzi syndrome is one of the leading causes of catastrophic intraoperative common bile duct transection and major biliary duct injury during laparoscopic cholecystectomy
radiological_manifestations: Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP - Preoperative Imaging Gold Standard): High-resolution demonstration of a large impacted gallstone (hypointense signal void >1-2 cm) in the neck of the gallbladder or cystic duct lying parallel to the common hepatic duct; marked dilatation of the intrahepatic bile ducts and the common hepatic duct down to the level of the cystic duct insertion, with an abrupt, smooth, concave extrinsic compression cutoff and completely normal caliber or collapsed distal common bile duct (CBD); direct visualization of a cholecystobiliary fistula tract between the gallbladder and CHD

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT: Thick-walled, contracted gallbladder containing a calcified or soft-tissue density gallstone in Hartmann's pouch or cystic duct directly abutting and compressing the common hepatic duct; severe proximal intrahepatic biliary dilatation; helps exclude perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (Klatskin tumor) by confirming the absence of an infiltrating soft-tissue periductal mass

Abdominal Ultrasound: Initial modality revealing a dilated intrahepatic biliary tree and dilated proximal common hepatic duct down to the site of an impacted acoustic-shadowing gallstone in the gallbladder neck, with a normal caliber common bile duct distally; contracted, thick-walled, stone-filled gallbladder intimately adherent to the common hepatic duct

ERCP / Percutaneous Transhepatic Cholangiography (PTC): Displays the Csendes Classification: Type I (extrinsic compression of CHD without fistula), Type II (cholecystobiliary fistula involving <1/3 of the CHD circumference), Type III (fistula involving 1/3 to 2/3 of the CHD circumference), Type IV (complete circumferential destruction of the CHD wall with loss of ductal continuity), and Type V (cholecystobiliary fistula combined with cholecystoenteric fistula, typically to duodenum [Va] or colon [Vb])
pathology_manifestations: Surgical resection specimen: Gallbladder is markedly distorted, thick-walled (often 5-15 mm), fibrotic, and contracted, containing a large solitary or faceted cholesterol/mixed calculus (>1.5-3 cm) firmly impacted in Hartmann's pouch or the cystic duct; chronic transmural cholecystitis with dense, dense collagenous mural fibrosis (porcelain-like or leathery wall); intense chronic inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and lipid-laden histiocytes (xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis overlap in up to 30% of cases)

Fistula tract and ductal histology: Focal pressure-induced ischemic necrosis, ulceration, and full-thickness perforation of the gallbladder neck and the adjacent common hepatic duct wall, leading to mucosal loss and fibrous fistulous bridging; extensive surrounding fibroblastic proliferation and obliterative periductal fibrosis; careful histological evaluation is mandatory to exclude coexisting occult gallbladder adenocarcinoma or perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (elevated in Mirizzi syndrome due to chronic inflammation)
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: High-risk surgical biliary disease featuring Charcot triad cholangitis and palpable RUQ mass, paired with MRCP-defined smooth common hepatic duct cutoff by an impacted cystic duct stone (Csendes types I-V) with distal CBD collapse, and transmural ischemic cholecystobiliary fistula histology.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Biliary compression complication of gallstone disease.

excluded_topics.name: Sigmoid Volvulus
clinical_manifestations: Extreme, asymmetrical abdominal distension (often described as a 'balloon-like' or 'drum-like' abdomen), with the left abdomen visibly towering over the right flank and chest wall

Marked, diffuse abdominal tympany on percussion over the distended sigmoid loop; high-pitched, metallic 'tinkling' bowel sounds or 'rushes' in early mechanical obstruction, progressing to ominous absolute silence (aperistalsis) with strangulation and ischemia

Classic triad of acute large bowel obstruction: profound obstipation (inability to pass flatus or stool), severe cramping lower abdominal pain, and marked abdominal distension, followed later by bilious or feculent vomiting

Signs of impending or established transmural bowel gangrene and peritonitis: involuntary abdominal wall guarding, rebound tenderness, cutaneous erythema or livedo over the distended abdominal wall, tachycardia, hypotension, and toxic shock facies
Digital rectal examination: Completely empty, collapsed, and dilated rectal vault ('empty ampulla'), with occasional palpable twisted sigmoid neck or blood-tinged mucus on the examining glove
radiological_manifestations: Plain Abdominal Radiography (Erect/Supine KUB): Pathognomonic 'coffee-bean' sign (also known as the 'bent inner-tube' sign or 'horseshoe' sign) formed by a massive, inverted U-shaped, afluid or air-fluid distended closed colonic loop arising from the pelvis with its apex projecting into the right upper quadrant or epigastrium; the three dense white lines forming the borders and the central thickened line (representing the apposed medial walls of the twisted loop) converge toward the left lower quadrant pelvis ('point of convergence' or 'pelvic junction'); absence of rectal gas

Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Imaging Modality of Choice): Pathognomonic 'whirl sign' / 'whirlpool sign' in the pelvis produced by the tightly twisted mesenteric vessels and collapsed bowel loops rotating around the point of volvulus torsion; huge closed-loop dilatation of the sigmoid colon with apposed walls, marked mural thinning ('paper-thin' wall), air-fluid levels, and upstream colonic dilatation; signs of strangulation/ischemia include mural hypoenhancement, intramural pneumatosis (pneumatosis intestinalis), mesenteric venous gas, pericolic fluid, and pneumoperitoneum in frank perforation

Water-Soluble Contrast Enema (Gastrografin Fluoroscopy): Smooth, progressive, beak-shaped tapering and complete obstruction of contrast at the level of the twisted sigmoid mesentery, forming the classic 'bird's beak' sign or 'ace-of-spades' sign
pathology_manifestations: Surgical resection specimen: Massive, markedly elongated, dark violaceous-to-black, gangrenous sigmoid loop rotated on its narrow, elongated mesosigmoid (often 180° to 540° clockwise or counterclockwise torsion around the mesenteric axis); gross serosal congestion, hemorrhagic infarction, mural thinned parchment-like necrosis, and serosanguinous peritoneal exudate; microscopic examination demonstrates transmural hemorrhagic infarction with complete mucosal coagulative necrosis, extensive submucosal hemorrhage and edema, microvascular thrombosis in mesenteric and intramural venules, and transmural neutrophilic infiltration with impending or focal transmural perforation
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Commonest and most lethal cause of colonic volvulus, presenting with dramatic asymmetric abdominal distension and obstipation, pathognomonic 'coffee-bean' sign on plain radiography, classic 'whirl sign' on CT, and transmural gangrenous infarction requiring emergency endoscopic detorsion or resective surgery.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Radiographic emergency without a disease-specific clinical photograph.

excluded_topics.name: Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome (Wilkie Syndrome)
clinical_manifestations: Profound, severe emaciation and rapid dramatic weight loss, typically occurring in the setting of anorexia nervosa, severe burns, major trauma, prolonged bed rest in a body cast ('cast syndrome'), rapid adolescent growth spurts, or corrective spinal surgery for scoliosis
Postprandial epigastric fullness, agonizing burning epigastric pain, and copious bilious vomiting containing partly digested food, occurring 15-45 minutes after meals

Pathognomonic postural relief (Busi position / knee-to-chest sign): Spontaneous, dramatic relief of symptoms when the patient assumes the prone position, left lateral decubitus position, or knee-to-chest (fetal) position, which pulls the mesenteric vascular root anteriorly and releases duodenal compression

Physical exam: Scaphoid, sunken lower abdomen with an acutely distended, bulging upper epigastrium; prominent epigastric succession splash audible hours after eating; cachectic temporal wasting, prominent ribs, loss of buccal fat pads (Bichat's fat pad), and severe orthostatic vitals
Metabolic alkalosis with severe hypokalemia and hypochloremia from recurrent persistent vomiting, complicated by prerenal azotemia and life-threatening electrolyte shifts (refeeding syndrome risk)
radiological_manifestations: Contrast-Enhanced CT / CT Angiography of Abdomen (Diagnostic Gold Standard): Sagittal reconstructions demonstrate severe acute narrowing of the aortomesenteric angle to <22° (normal angle 28°-65°) and reduction of the aortomesenteric distance to <8 mm (often 2-5 mm; normal distance 10-28 mm) at the level where the third (horizontal) part of the duodenum passes between the abdominal aorta and the superior mesenteric artery; massive dilatation of the stomach, first, and second parts of the duodenum, with an abrupt, sharp linear vascular cut-off at the 3rd duodenum; complete disappearance of the retroperitoneal mesenteric fat pad; sagittal maximum intensity projection (MIP) views provide definitive measurements

Upper Gastrointestinal Barium Series / Fluoroscopy: Pronounced, abrupt linear or vertical extrinsic compression defect across the third portion of the duodenum; vigorous, ineffective, hyperperistaltic reverse churning waves ('to-and-fro' peristalsis) in the proximal duodenal sweep trying to overcome the obstruction; pronounced retention of barium in the duodenal bulb and stomach (>4-6 hours); prompt, immediate relief and free passage of contrast into the jejunum when the patient is rolled into the prone or left lateral decubitus position
Abdominal Ultrasound / Color Doppler: Measurement of narrow aortomesenteric angle and visualization of distended, fluid-filled horizontal duodenum
pathology_manifestations: Clinical and operative pathology: Complete depletion and resorption of the retroperitoneal adipose cushion (mesenteric fat pad) normally encasing the superior mesenteric artery and protecting the third duodenum; operative findings demonstrate marked caliber mismatch between the grossly dilated, hypertrophic proximal duodenum and the collapsed distal jejunum at the crossing of the SMA root; histopathology of duodenal biopsies reveals marked mucosal congestion, chronic submucosal edema, microvascular venous stasis, and reactive duodenitis without primary intrinsic mural neoplasia or stricture
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal extrinsic compression disorder with severe cachectic wasting, pathognomonic postural relief (knee-to-chest), definitive CTA vascular angle/distance measurements (<22° and <8 mm), and characteristic 'to-and-fro' duodenal peristalsis.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Compression anatomy on barium/CT, not a photographic disease.

excluded_topics.name: Hemophilic Arthropathy
clinical_manifestations: Recurrent acute hemarthroses: Sudden, excruciating joint pain, dramatic tense intra-articular swelling, erythema, and localized skin warmth following minimal or no trauma; primarily targeting large hinge joints ('target joints'): knees (>45%), elbows (>30%), and ankles (>15%)

Chronic deforming arthropathy: Progressive irreversible joint destruction resulting in severe fixed flexion contractures (inability to fully extend knee or elbow), marked loss of joint motion, fibrous and bony ankylosis, and prominent joint enlargement with palpable 'boggy' synovial thickening

Severe periarticular muscle atrophy: Striking, disfiguring muscular wasting surrounding the involved joint (e.g., profound quadriceps muscle atrophy creating a 'knobby knee' appearance with bulging widened femoral condyles)

Hemophilic Pseudotumor: Slowly expanding, firm, tense, non-tender or painful subcutaneous, subperiosteal, or intraosseous mass (frequently in pelvis, femur, or calvarium) arising from recurrent encysted hematomas with fibrous encapsulation, causing skin necrosis, draining sinuses, or pathological fractures
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography (Arnold-Hilgartner Stages 0 to V): Pathognomonic structural remodeling signs including squaring of the inferior pole of the patella on lateral knee films; marked widening and deepening of the femoral intercondylar notch; overgrowth and 'ballooning' of the epiphyses with accelerated skeletal maturation due to chronic synovial hyperemia; multiple subchondral radiolucent cysts with sclerotic margins; progressive joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, and secondary osteophyte formation; end-stage complete bony ankylosis

Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI - Gold Standard): Massive hypertrophic synovial pannus demonstrating profound low signal intensity on both T1- and T2-weighted images due to dense hemosiderin iron accumulation within synovial lining cells; gradient-echo (GRE) or susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) sequences reveal striking 'blooming artifact' (exaggerated signal loss due to magnetic susceptibility of iron deposits); extensive articular cartilage loss and subchondral bone marrow edema

Musculoskeletal Ultrasound (HEAD-US protocol): Early detection of intra-articular hemarthrosis (hyperechoic bloody effusion), synovial hypertrophy (thickened hyperechoic/isoechoic synovium with Doppler hypervascularity in active synovitis), and cartilage thinning
pathology_manifestations: Synovial Biopsy & Histopathology: Intense, exuberant papillary and villous synovial hyperplasia; lining cells proliferate into multiple layers (pseudostratification); extensive intracellular hemosiderin deposition within synovial macrophages and fibroblasts, filling the cytoplasm with brown, coarsely granular iron pigment; dense subsynovial chronic lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, neovascularization, and extensive fibrous tissue deposition

Cartilage Pathology: Direct chondrotoxicity mediated by iron-induced free hydroxyl radicals, chondrocyte apoptosis, loss of matrix proteoglycans, and matrix metalloproteinase release, leading to full-thickness cartilage fissures, denudation, and eburnation of subchondral bone

Coagulation Studies & Genetics: Markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) with normal prothrombin time (PT) and normal platelet count; profound deficiency of functional Factor VIII activity (<1% in severe Hemophilia A) or Factor IX activity (<1% in severe Hemophilia B); genetic analysis identifies factor VIII gene inversions (intron 22 or intron 1 inversion in ~50% of severe Hemophilia A cases) or point mutations
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Premier musculoskeletal consequence of severe congenital coagulopathy displaying severe joint contractures, boggy synovitis, and profound quadriceps wasting, defined radiologically by patellar squaring and intercondylar notch widening on X-ray with pathognomonic dark blooming hemosiderin pannus on MRI, driven by iron-catalyzed synovial destruction.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Joint manifestation of hemophilia. Hemophilia A is added as the disease topic.

excluded_topics.name: Osteomyelitis
clinical_manifestations: Acute: localized exquisite bone tenderness, erythema, localized edema, and warmth over the affected limb
Chronic: persistent, foul-smelling, purulent draining cutaneous sinus tracts or fistulae tracking from deep bone
Visible, palpable, exposed necrotic bone at the base of chronic trophic ulcers ('probe-to-bone' sign)
Limb deformity, pathological fracture, and regional soft-tissue contractures
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography: Periosteal reaction (onion-skinning, elevation), cortical disruption, focal lytic bone destruction; in chronic osteomyelitis: pathognomonic triad of sequestrum (dense devitalized necrotic bone fragment), involucrum (sheath of reactive new periosteal bone), and cloaca (draining cortical defect)

Musculoskeletal MRI: Earliest and most sensitive modality: high-contrast bone marrow edema (hypointense on T1, hyperintense on T2/STIR), 'penumbra sign' (rim of vascularized granulation tissue hyperintense on T1), subperiosteal abscess collections
Thin-Slice CT: Superior detection of sequestra and cortical cloacae for surgical debridement planning
pathology_manifestations: Bone biopsy histology: Necrotic non-viable lamellar bone lacking osteocytes in lacunae (empty lacunae), sheets of degenerate neutrophils forming purulent exudate, vascular thrombosis, and surrounding reactive woven bone with osteoblastic rimming
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Features visible draining cutaneous fistulae and exposed bone matching the classic radiographic triad of sequestrum, involucrum, and cloaca, plus bone marrow edema on MRI.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Umbrella bone infection. Image search returns mixed organisms, implants, and diagrams rather than one disease phenotype.

excluded_topics.name: Septic Arthritis
clinical_manifestations: Acute, agonizing monoarthritis (most commonly knee, hip, shoulder, wrist) with joint locked in position of comfort (flexion)
Tense, warm, erythematous joint effusion with exquisite pain on minimal active or passive range of motion
In gonococcal arthritis: characteristic migratory polyarthralgias, tenosynovitis, and sparse pustular or necrotic skin lesions with violaceous halos on distal extremities
radiological_manifestations: Plain Radiography: Early capsular distension and soft tissue swelling; rapid progression within 7-14 days to severe, irregular joint space narrowing, subchondral bone erosions, and cortical demineralization
Joint Ultrasound: Hyperechoic or complex heterogeneous joint effusion with thick synovial hypertrophy and increased power Doppler signal; guidance for urgent needle arthrocentesis
Musculoskeletal MRI: Extensive synovial thickening and intense contrast enhancement, joint effusion, adjacent bone marrow edema, and periarticular soft-tissue abscess
pathology_manifestations: Synovial fluid analysis: Grossly purulent, turbid, yellow-green fluid with WBC count typically >50,000-100,000/uL (>90% neutrophils); identification of intracellular bacteria on Gram stain (e.g. Gram-positive clusters in S. aureus)
Synovial histology: Dense, diffuse suppurative neutrophilic infiltration, microabscess formation, fibrinopurulent exudate, and enzymatic destruction of articular cartilage matrix
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: High-urgency clinical picture of a locked, erythematous swollen joint and gonococcal purpuric pustules paired with ultrasound-guided effusion and rapid joint space destruction on plain X-rays and MRI.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Umbrella joint infection, not a single visual disease.

excluded_topics.name: Bartter Syndrome
synonyms: hereditary hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with hypercalciuria
clinical_manifestations: Severe antenatal presentation with profound polyhydramnios (maternal 'coconut abdomen') leading to premature delivery; neonatal presentation with life-threatening polyuria, severe hypovolemic dehydration, and failure to thrive
Characteristic dysmorphic facial features ('Bartter facies'): prominent triangular forehead, large protruding ears, wide-set bulging eyes, flat nasal bridge, and drooping corners of the mouth
In Bartter syndrome type 4 (BSND / CLCNKA+CLCNKB mutations): congenital sensorineural deafness combined with severe neonatal salt wasting
Severe hypokalemic, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis accompanied by marked hyperreninemic hyperaldosteronism with normal or low blood pressure (due to profound renal sodium and chloride wasting)
Severe hypercalciuria with recurrent renal colic, muscle weakness, carpopedal spasms, tetany, and salt craving
radiological_manifestations: Renal Ultrasonography: Early and profound bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis (appearing within the first weeks to months of life), characterized by diffusely hyperechoic medullary pyramids with sharp acoustic shadowing, normal cortical echogenicity, and preserved corticomedullary borders

Non-Contrast Abdominal CT: Symmetrical, dense radiopaque calcifications outlining every renal pyramid (pure medullary nephrocalcinosis composed of calcium oxalate and calcium phosphate), without parenchymal mass lesions
Plain Skeletal Radiography: Severe osteopenia, delayed skeletal bone age, and premature articular/periarticular chondrocalcinosis (calcium pyrophosphate deposition) in late childhood/adolescence
pathology_manifestations: Renal Biopsy Light Microscopy (Diagnostic Hallmark): Massive hypertrophy and hyperplasia of the juxtaglomerular apparatus (JGA)—concentric, multi-layered mantles of granular myoepithelial cells surrounding afferent arterioles, extending into the glomerulus and interlobular arteries

Medullary Histopathology: Hyperplasia of medullary interstitial cells (prostaglandin-producing cells); intraluminal calcium crystal aggregates in the thick ascending limb of Henle and medullary collecting ducts; secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and patchy interstitial fibrosis

Electron Microscopy & Molecular Genetics: Hypergranulated juxtaglomerular cells packed with renin-containing secretory granules; biallelic mutations in thick ascending limb transporters: SLC12A1 (NKCC2, Type 1), KCNJ1 (ROMK, Type 2), CLCNKB (ClC-Kb, Type 3), BSND (barttin, Type 4), or MAGED2 (transient X-linked antenatal Bartter)
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Definitive salt-wasting loop tubulopathy pairing polyhydramnios, triangular facies, and sensorineural deafness with dense infantile medullary nephrocalcinosis on renal ultrasound and massive juxtaglomerular apparatus hyperplasia on histology.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Electrolyte tubulopathy. Failure to thrive is not disease-specific imagery.

excluded_topics.name: Complete Ureteral Duplication with Ectopic Ureterocele
synonyms: duplex collecting system with ectopic ureterocele
clinical_manifestations: Intermittent or continuous vulvar / urethral mass in infant girls: smooth, pink, glistening, cystic intravesical mass prolapsing through the urethral meatus, causing acute bladder outlet obstruction, straining, and acute urinary retention

Pathognomonic incontinence pattern in females: continuous, involuntary, day-and-night urinary dribbling / constant wet underwear despite an otherwise completely normal voiding cycle (caused by an ectopic upper pole ureter terminating distal to the external urethral sphincter into the urethra, vestibule, or vagina)
Palpable, ballotable, smooth upper flank mass in neonates and infants representing a severely hydronephrotic, obstructed upper pole moiety

Recurrent, severe febrile urinary tract infections, pyelonephritis, and urosepsis in early childhood; in young males, recurrent epididymo-orchitis or perineal pain from ectopic ureteral drainage into the wolffian duct derivatives (seminal vesicle, vas deferens, or ejaculatory duct)
radiological_manifestations: Intravenous Urography (IVU) & Excretory CT Urography: Pathognomonic 'drooping lily' sign—inferior, outward, and lateral downward displacement and tilting of the opacified lower pole calyces resembling the flower of a drooping lily, caused by the non-functioning, massively hydronephrotic, unobstructed upper pole moiety pushing the lower pole downward

Voiding Cystourethrography (VCUG) & Excretory Urography: Pathognomonic 'cobra head' or 'spring onion' sign—round or oval contrast-filled dilatation of the distal ectopic ureter surrounded by a thin, smooth, radiolucent halo representing the stretched ureterocele wall bulging into the bladder base; demonstrates massive vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) into the lower pole moiety in ~50% of cases

Renal and Bladder Ultrasonography: Anatomical confirmation of duplex kidney with marked dilation and parenchymal thinning of the upper pole renal pelvis and calyces, a tortuous, aperistaltic, fluid-filled dilated upper pole megaureter, and a cystic, thin-walled, intravesical balloon-like mass at the bladder base

Validation of the Weigert-Meyer Law on CTU / MR Urography: Upper pole ureter inserts ectopically inferomedially into the bladder neck/urethra and ends in an obstructing ureterocele; lower pole ureter inserts superiorly and laterally into the normal bladder trigone, lacking an anti-reflux tunnel and predisposing to VUR
pathology_manifestations: Gross Nephroureterectomy Specimen: Bipartite kidney displaying a severely thinned, scarred, cystic, dysplastic upper pole moiety sharply demarcated from a well-preserved lower pole parenchyma; duplicate ureters enclosed within a common adventitial sheath

Renal Histopathology (Upper Pole Dysplasia): Classic features of renal dysplasia: primitive, disorganized collecting ducts lined by undifferentiated columnar epithelium and surrounded by concentric fibromuscular mantles ('collarettes'); metaplastic islands of hyaline cartilage; primitive embryonic glomeruli; extensive cystic tubular dilatation and dense interstitial fibrosis

Ureterocele Histopathology: Biopsy of the ureterocele wall reveals a thin fibroelastic membrane lined by transitional bladder epithelium on the external (vesical) surface and attenuated ureteral urothelium on the internal surface, with sparse, disorganized, fragmented smooth muscle bundles
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Classic congenital urologic malformation obeying the Weigert-Meyer rule, featuring prolapsing urethral cyst, continuous urinary dribbling, the pathognomonic 'drooping lily' and 'cobra head' signs on urography, and upper pole renal dysplasia on pathology.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Congenital imaging anatomy; the clinical clue (prolapsed ureterocele) is a finding, not the topic grain wanted here.

excluded_topics.name: Congenital Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus
excluded_topics.subspecialty: Inherited Tubulopathies and Water Balance Disorders
clinical_manifestations: Early infantile presentation (first weeks to months of life) with life-threatening hypernatremic dehydration, fever of unknown origin (dehydration fever), vomiting, failure to thrive, and severe irritability that is miraculously calmed only by offering water

Profound hyposthenuric polyuria (urine output exceeding 10-15 L/day in adults or >100-150 mL/kg/day in infants) and relentless unquenchable polydipsia with marked craving for cold water, leading to nocturnal enuresis and disrupted sleep
Physical signs of extreme chronic dehydration: dry oral mucosa, depressed anterior fontanelle, sunken eyeballs, loss of skin turgor, and delayed capillary refill
Severe hypernatremic neurologic sequelae if diagnosis is delayed: recurrent seizures, spastic diplegia, microcephaly, and permanent cognitive impairment
Refractory to exogenous desmopressin (dDAVP): complete lack of urinary concentrating response (<10% increase in urine osmolality, which remains persistently hyposthenuric <200 mOsm/kg H2O)
radiological_manifestations: Renal and Bladder Ultrasonography: Massive, bilateral, symmetric non-obstructive hydroureteronephrosis and giant megacystis—extreme dilation of the renal pelvis, calyces, and full length of both ureters ('functional megacystis-megaureter syndrome') resulting purely from tremendous high-volume urine flow through a physiologically overwhelmed lower urinary tract, without mechanical obstruction

Voiding Cystourethrography (VCUG) & Excretory Urography: Tremendous bladder enlargement with smooth, thin, trabeculation-free bladder walls (distinguishing it from anatomic posterior urethral valves), absence of vesicoureteral reflux, and widely dilated, tortuous, aperistaltic megaureters

Brain Non-Contrast CT / MRI: Bilateral, symmetrical, dense intracranial calcifications localized to the basal ganglia (globus pallidus, putamen), thalami, and subcortical white matter, representing dystrophic calcification from repeated episodes of severe hypernatremic brain dehydration
pathology_manifestations: Gross Renal & Urologic Morphology: Markedly enlarged, thin-walled, hyperdistended bladder (megacystis); massively dilated, tortuous ureters; dilated renal collecting systems with blunting of the renal papillae

Renal Biopsy Light Microscopy: Marked cystic dilation of collecting ducts and distal convoluted tubules; secondary focal tubular atrophy, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis due to prolonged backpressure from massive urine volumes

Immunohistochemistry & Molecular Genetics: Immunohistochemical staining for Aquaporin-2 (AQP2) shows complete absence or aberrant intracellular endoplasmic reticulum retention of AQP2 in principal cells of the collecting duct (in contrast to normal intense apical membrane brush-border staining following dDAVP); molecular testing identifies hemizygous pathogenic mutations in AVPR2 (Xq28, X-linked NDI, ~90%) or biallelic/heterozygous mutations in AQP2 (12q13, autosomal NDI, ~10%)
excluded_topics.inclusion_rationale: Archetypal water balance tubulopathy pairing infantile hypernatremic dehydration and relentless polyuria with massive non-obstructive megacystis-megaureter on ultrasound, basal ganglia calcifications on CT, and absent collecting duct AQP2 trafficking on immunohistochemistry.
excluded_topics.audit_reason: Water-balance disorder without disease-specific images. Same exclusion class as diabetes insipidus generally.

excluded_topics.name: Dent Disease
clinical_manifestations: Exclusively affects hemizygous males in early childhood or adolescence (X-linked recessive transmission), presenting with profound low-molecular-weight (LMW) proteinuria (>5-fold elevation of urinary beta-2-microglobulin and alpha-1-microglobulin)

Hypophosphatemic rickets / osteomalacia: prominent bowing deformities of the lower extremities (genu varum or genu valgum), rachitic rosary (beading of costochondral junctions), wrist and ankle widening, waddling gait, severe bone pain, and significant short stature
Recurrent episodes of calcium-based nephrolithiasis, renal colic, and painless gross or microscopic hematuria occurring in early childhood

Proximal renal tubular Fanconi syndrome manifestations: generalized aminoaciduria, renal glucosuria (normoglycemic glucosuria), uricosuria, and hypophosphatemic hypercalciuria (urinary calcium excretion >4 mg/kg/day)

In Dent disease type 2 (OCRL mutations): mild intellectual disability, subclinical congenital nuclear cataracts on slit-lamp exam, and generalized muscular hypotonia (representing an allelic variant of Lowe oculocerebrorenal syndrome)
radiological_manifestations: Non-Contrast Abdominal CT: Extensive, symmetrical medullary nephrocalcinosis characterized by dense radiopaque calcium aggregates localized throughout all renal medullary pyramids, accompanied by multiple bilateral renal calculi (calcium oxalate and calcium phosphate/apatite)

Renal Ultrasonography: Diffuse bilateral hyperechogenicity of the medullary pyramids with posterior acoustic shadowing ('echogenic pyramids'), progressive corticomedullary thinning, and eventual small, contracted kidneys with end-stage renal disease
